closing_issues.title: [MEDIUM] [BUG] untrackAgent() Never Called on Natural Agent Exit
closing_issues.body:
## Finding ID
LB-2

## Severity
MEDIUM

## Report Source
Latent Bugs - 04_LATENT_BUGS.md

## Files Affected
- `src/main/services/agent-system.ts`

## Found By
Claude

## Description
`untrackAgent` is only called by `killAgent`. If an agent exits naturally (process completes, PTY onExit fires), the five tracking Maps/Sets retain stale entries indefinitely.

## Impact
Memory leak in long-running sessions. Tracking maps grow without bound.

## Fix Suggestion
Call `untrackAgent` from the PTY `onExit` handler and any other natural exit paths to ensure tracking state is cleaned up.

closing_issues.title: [MEDIUM] [BUG] Fire-and-Forget killAgent in Auto-Exit Timer
closing_issues.body:
## Finding ID
LB-7

## Severity
MEDIUM

## Report Source
Latent Bugs - 04_LATENT_BUGS.md

## Files Affected
- `src/main/services/agent-system.ts`

## Found By
Claude

## Description
The stale sweep and auto-exit timer call `killAgent` without awaiting or catching. If `killAgent` rejects (process already dead), the rejection is unhandled.

## Impact
Unhandled promise rejections can crash the main process in strict environments or cause silent failures in agent cleanup.

## Fix Suggestion
Await `killAgent` calls and wrap in try/catch, or attach `.catch()` handlers to suppress expected rejections from already-dead processes.

closing_issues.title: [MEDIUM] [BUG] DELETE_SAVE_PATCH Uses win! Without Null Check
closing_issues.body:
## Finding ID
LB-10

## Severity
MEDIUM

## Report Source
Latent Bugs - 04_LATENT_BUGS.md

## Files Affected
- `src/main/ipc/agent-handlers.ts` (line 100)

## Found By
Claude

## Description
`BrowserWindow.getFocusedWindow()` can return `null` (e.g., popout window lost focus). The non-null assertion (`win!`) throws at runtime.

## Impact
Runtime crash when the delete save patch IPC handler is invoked while no window has focus.

## Fix Suggestion
Add a null check for the focused window and either fall back to the sender's window or return an error gracefully.

closing_issues.title: [MEDIUM] [BUG] Orchestrator Not Tracked When Inherited from Project Settings
closing_issues.body:
## Finding ID
LB-11

## Severity
MEDIUM

## Report Source
Latent Bugs - 04_LATENT_BUGS.md

## Files Affected
- `src/main/services/agent-system.ts`

## Found By
Claude

## Description
When the orchestrator is resolved from `.clubhouse/settings.json` rather than passed explicitly, the value in `agentOrchestratorMap` may differ from what was resolved. `killAgent` uses the caller-provided orchestrator, not the tracked one.

## Impact
Wrong exit command could be sent to the agent, potentially leaving processes orphaned or sending incompatible signals.

## Fix Suggestion
Store the resolved orchestrator in `agentOrchestratorMap` at spawn time (after resolution), and have `killAgent` read from the tracking map rather than accepting the orchestrator as a parameter.

closing_issues.title: [MEDIUM] [BUG] headlessStore.setDefaultMode Reads State After Async Call
closing_issues.body:
## Finding ID
LB-13

## Severity
MEDIUM

## Report Source
Latent Bugs - 04_LATENT_BUGS.md

## Files Affected
- `src/renderer/stores/headlessStore.ts` (lines 39-49)

## Found By
Claude

## Description
`get().projectOverrides` is read at time of IPC call, not when the function started. Concurrent `setProjectMode` could be overwritten.

## Impact
Race condition where project-specific headless mode overrides can be silently lost when default mode is changed concurrently.

## Fix Suggestion
Capture `projectOverrides` before the async IPC call, or use an atomic read-modify-write pattern.

closing_issues.title: [MEDIUM] [BUG] File Watcher Base-Path Extraction is POSIX-Only
closing_issues.body:
## Finding ID
LB-15

## Severity
MEDIUM

## Report Source
Latent Bugs - 04_LATENT_BUGS.md

## Files Affected
- `src/main/services/file-watch-service.ts` (lines 121-132)

## Found By
Codex

## Description
`glob.split('/')` and string assembly ignore platform separators. On Windows, watches wrong directory (`.` fallback) or silently misses files.

## Impact
File watching is broken on Windows -- plugins relying on file watchers will not receive expected events.

## Fix Suggestion
Use `path.sep` or `path.parse`/`path.join` for platform-independent path handling, or normalize globs to POSIX format before processing.

closing_issues.title: [LOW] [BUG] killAgent Takes Orchestrator from Caller, Not Tracking Map
closing_issues.body:
## Finding ID
LB-17

## Severity
LOW

## Report Source
Latent Bugs - 04_LATENT_BUGS.md

## Files Affected
- `src/main/services/agent-system.ts` (lines 297-312)

## Found By
Claude

## Description
The `orchestrator` parameter comes from the renderer. If renderer state is stale, wrong exit command sent.

## Impact
Agents may receive incorrect exit commands if the renderer's orchestrator state has drifted from the actual orchestrator used at spawn time.

## Fix Suggestion
Have `killAgent` look up the orchestrator from `agentOrchestratorMap` (set at spawn time) instead of accepting it as a parameter from the renderer.

closing_issues.title: [MEDIUM] [BUG] File Watcher Handles Leak on Window Close
closing_issues.body:
## Finding ID
LB-20

## Severity
MEDIUM

## Report Source
Latent Bugs - 04_LATENT_BUGS.md

## Files Affected
- `src/main/services/file-watch-service.ts` (lines 106-114)

## Found By
Claude, Codex, GPT

## Description
`cleanupWatchesForWindow` is a no-op. If a window closes while watches are active, watchers continue sending events to destroyed webContents.

## Impact
Handle leak and potential crashes when events are sent to destroyed renderer webContents after window close.

## Fix Suggestion
Implement `cleanupWatchesForWindow` to actually close/unwatch all watchers associated with the closing window, and remove them from the tracking data structures.

closing_issues.title: [HIGH] [BUG] File Watch Behavior Doesn't Match Glob Contract
closing_issues.body:
## Finding ID
LB-19

## Severity
HIGH

## Report Source
Latent Bugs - 04_LATENT_BUGS.md

## Files Affected
- `src/main/services/file-watch-service.ts` (lines 20-23, 29-45, 57-72)

## Found By
GPT

## Description
API claims to watch changes matching a glob, but implementation reduces to a base directory and watches recursively without applying the original glob filter. Plugins asking to watch a narrow glob receive unrelated events from the entire subtree.

## Impact
Correctness bug and performance issue -- every change under the tree wakes plugin code, regardless of whether the file matches the requested glob pattern.

## Fix Suggestion
Apply the original glob pattern as a filter on file change events before forwarding them to plugins. Use a library like `minimatch` or `picomatch` to test each changed path against the glob.

closing_issues.title: [LOW] [BUG] Settings Stores Read get() After Async Calls
closing_issues.body:
## Finding ID
LB-18

## Severity
LOW

## Report Source
Latent Bugs - 04_LATENT_BUGS.md

## Files Affected
- `src/renderer/stores/headlessStore.ts`
- `src/renderer/stores/clubhouseModeStore.ts`
- `src/renderer/stores/sessionSettingsStore.ts`

## Found By
Claude

## Description
All stores read current state after async operations complete. Concurrent updates could be overwritten.

## Impact
Race condition where settings changes made during an async operation are silently lost when the operation completes and overwrites with stale state.

## Fix Suggestion
Capture state before the async call, or use functional `set()` updates that read state at write time.

closing_issues.title: [HIGH] [CQ] Null Dereference in DELETE_SAVE_PATCH Handler
closing_issues.body:
## Finding ID
CQ-6

## Severity
HIGH

## Report Source
Code Quality - 02_CODE_QUALITY.md

## Files Affected
- `src/main/ipc/agent-handlers.ts:100`

## Found By
Claude

## Description
`dialog.showSaveDialog(win!, ...)` uses non-null assertion on `BrowserWindow.getFocusedWindow()`, which returns `null` when invoked from a popout window that lost focus.

## Impact
Causes a runtime crash (null dereference) when the user triggers the save dialog from a window that isn't focused.

## Fix Suggestion
Add a null check for the window, falling back to any available `BrowserWindow` or omitting the parent window parameter.

mentioned_issues.title: S6.0.1: Contrato de datos v1.0 (JSON/Schema)
mentioned_issues.body:
definir y publicar el modelo estándar para Talks/Speakers/Relaciones, con JSON Schema y convenciones de naming.

Pasos de implementación (Copilot-friendly):
Crear /schemas/talk.schema.json y /schemas/speaker.schema.json.

Campos obligatorios en Talk:
id, slug, title, abstract, track, room, day(YYYY-MM-DD), startTime(ISO8601), endTime(ISO8601), speakerIds[], updatedAt, version:"1.0".

Campos obligatorios en Speaker:
id, slug, name, bio, photoUrl, socials[], updatedAt, version:"1.0".
Script npm run validate:data que valida data/schedule.json contra los schemas (ajusta si schedule.json trae habla+speaker juntos, normaliza a tablas lógicas).
Documentar convenciones (camelCase, ISO8601, IDs inmutables).

Criterios de aceptación (G/W/T):
Given data/schedule.json When ejecuto npm run validate:data Then la validación pasa sin errores.
Given un Talk sin startTime When valido Then falla con mensaje claro del campo.

mentioned_issues.title: S6.0.2: DAL con origen intercambiable (JSON ↔ CMS)
mentioned_issues.body:
una única Data Access Layer que abstrae el origen de datos.
Pasos de implementación:
Crear /src/data/dal.ts con interfaz:
```typescript
getAgenda(filters): Promise<Talk[]>
getTalk(idOrSlug): Promise<Talk>
getSpeakers(filters?): Promise<Speaker[]>
getSpeaker(idOrSlug): Promise<Speaker>
```
Implementación A (default): lee data/schedule.json, normaliza y guarda en IndexedDB; responde desde IDB.

Implementación B (placeholder): fuente CMS (REST/GraphQL) activable por NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=cms.
Hooks useAgenda, useTalk, useSpeakers consumen solo la interfaz DAL.

Criterios:
Given NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=json When renderizo agenda Then carga datos desde schedule.json vía DAL/IDB.
Given NEXT_PUBLIC_DATA_SOURCE=cms When cambio env Then la UI sigue funcionando sin cambios de código.

Notas de implementación (rápidas)
Librerías sugeridas: Dexie/idb (IndexedDB), react-window, workbox, luxon/dayjs (TZ), zod/ajv (schema), web-push (server).
Archivos clave:
src/data/dal.ts, src/data/db.ts, src/hooks/useAgenda.ts, src/hooks/useSpeakers.ts
src/features/agenda/AgendaList.tsx, src/features/agenda/MyAgenda.tsx
public/data/schedule.json (hoy) / CMS (mañana)

## User Story

As an authenticated user, I want to view and interact with my GitHub Project Boards in a Kanban-style layout so that I can track project progress and issue details in real time within the app.

## UI/UX Description

Create a new /project-board route accessible from the sidebar navigation. The page displays a dropdown at the top listing all available GitHub Projects for the user. Upon selection, render a Kanban board with horizontal columns representing status fields, each showing a colored status dot, column name, item counts, aggregate estimates, and descriptions. Issue cards display repo name/issue number, title, assignee avatars, linked PR badge, priority, estimate, and size badges with color coding. Clicking an issue card opens a modal with expanded details and a link to github.com. The board auto-refreshes every 15 seconds and shows loading/error states. Tailwind CSS styling should match the app's design system (not GitHub's dark theme).

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST provide a new /project-board route accessible via the sidebar navigation.
- System MUST display a dropdown listing all available GitHub Projects for the authenticated user using the GitHub Projects V2 GraphQL API.
- System MUST render a Kanban-style board with columns representing status fields and display colored status dots, column names, item counts, aggregate estimates, and descriptions.
- System MUST display issue cards with repository name/issue number, issue title, assignee avatars, linked PR badge (if exists), priority, estimate, and size badges with color coding.
- System MUST open a detail modal when an issue card is clicked, containing expanded issue information and a link to open the issue/PR on github.com in a new tab.
- System MUST auto-refresh the board data every 15 seconds and display appropriate loading and error states.
- System MUST implement FastAPI endpoints that proxy GitHub Projects V2 GraphQL API requests, including listing projects, fetching board data, and retrieving linked PRs, authenticated via GITHUB_TOKEN.
- System MUST extend TypeScript types to support priority, size, estimate, linked PRs, assignee avatars, and repo name.

mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Add brown background to app

## User Story

As a user of @Boykai's Tech Connect app, I want the app to have a brown background so that the visual appearance aligns with my preference or branding needs and delivers a warmer, earthy aesthetic.

## UI/UX Description

The app should display a consistent brown background across all primary screens and components. The shade of brown should be visually appealing and provide sufficient contrast for legibility and accessibility. A recommended starting color is #8B5C2B (saddle brown), but designers should review and select a brown tone that complements existing UI elements, text, and interactive components. All backgrounds, including modals, pop-ups, and navigation panels, should inherit or override with the brown tone for visual consistency. Ensure that any gradients, overlays, or image backgrounds are either updated to harmonize with the brown or retain their intended effect without clashing. The brown background must be responsive, adjusting gracefully across all device sizes and orientations. Accessibility guidelines must be followed: text and icons should maintain at least WCAG AA contrast ratio against the brown background. Consider dark/light brown variants if the app supports theme toggling.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST set the primary app background color to a brown shade (suggested: #8B5C2B) across all main screens and layouts.
- System MUST ensure all text and UI elements over the brown background have sufficient contrast (minimum WCAG AA compliance).
- System MUST apply the brown background to modals, pop-ups, navigation bars, and any overlay components unless their design intentionally differs.
- System SHOULD update existing gradients or image backgrounds to harmonize with the brown background color or retain their intended effect without visual conflict.
- System MUST make the brown background responsive, ensuring it scales and displays correctly on all devices (mobile, tablet, desktop) and screen orientations.
- System SHOULD provide fallback color values for browsers or devices that do not support custom CSS variables.
- System MUST validate that the brown background does not introduce UI rendering errors or break any interactive elements.
- System SHOULD offer a configuration option for theme color adjustment if theme toggling is supported in the app.

## Technical Notes

Implement the brown background using global CSS styles or theme configuration files, depending on the app's architecture (e.g., CSS, SCSS, styled-components, or a theme provider in React/Vue/Angular). Use CSS variables for easy future color adjustments and to support theming if required. Review all screens/components to ensure the background change is applied universally, including edge cases like modals or overlays. Test across common browsers and devices for visual consistency and accessibility. Use automated tools (like axe or Lighthouse) to verify color contrast. If gradients/images are used, adjust their tones or overlays to avoid clashing with the brown background. Document the new color scheme in the app's style guide. No database or backend changes required unless theme management is stored in user settings.

The app's background should consistently display a solid red color (#FF0000) across all main views, including login, dashboard, navigation, and any modal overlays. The red background must fully cover the viewport, including scrollable areas, and should not be obstructed by other UI elements unless specifically intended. ## Original Request

> Add green background to app

## User Story

As a user of @Boykai's Tech Connect app, I want the app to have a green background so that the visual experience is more vibrant and cohesive with the desired color scheme.

## UI/UX Description

The app should display a consistent green background across all screens, including landing pages, main dashboard, modals, and any pop-up dialogs. The background color should be set using a HEX value such as #00FF00 (bright green), but designers may select a green shade that ensures sufficient contrast with text and interactive elements for legibility. The green background should not interfere with existing UI components; all buttons, cards, input fields, and other widgets must remain clearly visible and accessible. For accessibility, ensure that text and icons provide high contrast against the green background. If the app supports light/dark mode, the green background should adapt accordingly (e.g., a darker green for dark mode). The background must scale responsively across all devices and screen sizes. Transitions between screens should retain the green background without visible flicker. If any overlays or modal dialogs are used, their background should respect the green theme or use a suitable overlay opacity to maintain the visual consistency.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST apply a green background to all app screens, including landing, dashboard, settings, and modal dialogs.
- System MUST use a consistent green color (e.g., HEX #00FF00) for the background, or select an appropriate green shade that meets WCAG AA contrast requirements.
- System MUST ensure that all text, icons, buttons, and input fields maintain sufficient contrast and legibility against the green background.
- System MUST ensure that the green background renders correctly on all supported devices and screen sizes, including mobile, tablet, and desktop.
- System SHOULD adapt the green background for light and dark mode, using lighter or darker green shades as appropriate.
- System MUST handle transitions between screens so that the green background is persistent and does not flicker or disappear.
- System MUST ensure that overlays and modal dialogs either maintain a green background or use an appropriate overlay that harmonizes with the green theme.
- System MUST not interfere with the existing layout or functionality of UI components when applying the green background.
- System SHOULD provide fallback styles in case the green color fails to render, defaulting to a neutral background.
- System MUST comply with all accessibility standards, including keyboard and screen reader navigation.

## Technical Notes

Apply the green background using a global CSS selector (e.g., body { background-color: #00FF00; }) or via theme provider in React/Vue/Angular. Review all screens for component contrast and update styles as needed to ensure accessibility. If the app supports theming or dark mode, use CSS variables or theme context to switch green shades dynamically. Test on major browsers and devices for compatibility. For modal overlays, use semi-transparent green backgrounds (e.g., rgba(0,255,0,0.2)) to ensure visual harmony. Consider using CSS transitions to avoid flicker during navigation. If the app uses existing themes, integrate the green background as a new theme option or as the default. Ensure that the background color does not break layout or cause overflow issues. Validate compliance with WCAG AA/AAA contrast ratios.

mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Add brown background to app

## User Story

As a developer/stakeholder on Boykai's Tech Connect project, I want a brown background applied to the app so that the visual aesthetic matches the desired color scheme and brand identity.

## UI/UX Description

Apply a brown background color across the app's primary surfaces (e.g., main layout wrapper, body, or root container). The brown tone should be chosen to ensure sufficient contrast against foreground text and UI elements per WCAG accessibility guidelines. Consider using a warm, rich brown (e.g., #5C3317, #795548, or similar Material/brand-aligned brown) consistently across light-mode surfaces. All existing text, icons, and interactive elements must remain legible against the new background. If the app supports dark mode, ensure the brown background integrates gracefully or is scoped appropriately to the intended theme.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST apply a brown background color to the app's root or primary layout container so it is visible across all pages/views.
- System MUST define the brown color as a reusable CSS variable or design token (e.g., --color-bg-primary: #795548) to ensure consistency and ease of future updates.
- System MUST ensure a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 (WCAG AA) between the brown background and all foreground text elements.
- System MUST update or override any existing background-color declarations (e.g., white or gray defaults on body or app shell) so no conflicting styles override the brown background.
- System SHOULD apply the brown background consistently across all route-level views and modal/overlay backdrops where a page background is visible.
- System SHOULD verify the brown background renders correctly on all major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) and on both mobile and desktop viewport sizes.
- System SHOULD document the chosen brown hex/RGB value in the project's design tokens or style guide file for designer-developer alignment.

## Technical Notes

Implement the brown background by setting a CSS custom property on the :root or body selector (e.g., background-color: var(--color-bg-primary)) and applying it to the top-level app shell component. If the project uses a CSS framework like Tailwind CSS, add a custom brown color to the theme config and apply the utility class to the root layout. If using a component library (e.g., Material UI, Chakra), update the theme's background palette token. Ensure global stylesheet specificity does not conflict with scoped component styles that may override the background.

## User Story

As a user of Boykai's Tech Connect app, I want the application to have a blue background so that the visual appearance is updated to reflect a cohesive, branded color scheme. This change should apply consistently across the app to create a unified look and feel.

## UI/UX Description

Apply a blue background color globally across the application. The specific shade of blue should align with the existing brand palette (e.g., a primary blue such as #1E3A5F, #1A73E8, or a similarly appropriate tone determined by the design system). The background should be applied to the root/body level so all screens and pages inherit it. Ensure sufficient contrast between the blue background and foreground text/content elements to meet WCAG AA accessibility standards (minimum 4.5:1 ratio for normal text). On screens with cards, modals, or panels, those surface elements should use a lighter or neutral color to visually separate content layers from the background. The blue background should render correctly on all screen sizes (mobile, tablet, desktop) and should not interfere with existing UI components such as navigation bars, footers, buttons, or input fields.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST apply a blue background color to the root/body element of the application so all pages and screens display the blue background by default.
- System MUST use a specific blue color value (hex, RGB, or CSS variable) that is defined in the app's design system or theme configuration to ensure consistency and maintainability.
- System MUST ensure the blue background provides sufficient color contrast (WCAG AA minimum 4.5:1 ratio) against all primary text and interactive elements rendered on top of it.
- System MUST preserve the appearance of overlay surfaces (modals, cards, dropdowns, tooltips) by ensuring they use a contrasting background color that visually separates them from the blue app background.
- System MUST apply the blue background responsively across all breakpoints (mobile, tablet, desktop) without visual artifacts, overflow, or layout shifts.
- System SHOULD define the blue background color as a CSS variable or theme token (e.g., --color-app-bg) to allow easy future updates and support for theming or dark mode.
- System MUST verify that existing UI components (navigation bars, sidebars, footers, buttons, forms, icons) remain fully visible and functional against the new blue background.
- System SHOULD update or add relevant Storybook stories, snapshot tests, or visual regression tests to reflect the new background color.

## Technical Notes

Implement the blue background by updating the global stylesheet or theme configuration file (e.g., index.css, App.css, tailwind.config.js, or a CSS-in-JS theme provider). If the project uses a design token system or theming library (e.g., MUI, Tailwind, Styled Components), the change should be made at the theme level rather than inline styles to ensure scalability. Confirm the exact blue hex value with the design team or default to a strong primary blue (e.g., #1A73E8 or #1E3A5F) if no brand guideline exists. Run accessibility contrast checks using a tool like Lighthouse or axe-core after the change to catch any contrast failures introduced by the new background.

mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> add black background to app

## User Story

As a user of Boykai's Tech Connect app, I want the application to have a black background so that the visual experience is modern, sleek, and easier on the eyes in low-light environments.

## UI/UX Description

The entire app background should be updated to use a true black (#000000) or near-black (#0A0A0A / #121212) color across all screens, pages, and components. All existing UI elements — text, icons, cards, modals, sidebars, navbars, and containers — must be audited to ensure proper contrast ratios (WCAG AA minimum 4.5:1) against the new black background. Text colors should be updated to light/white tones if not already compatible. Scrollable areas, drawers, overlays, and popups should consistently inherit or apply the black background. The transition should feel cohesive and intentional — no white flashes, unthemed containers, or legacy light backgrounds remaining visible anywhere in the app.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST apply a black or near-black background color (e.g., #000000 or #121212) globally across all app pages and views
- System MUST update all component-level background styles (cards, modals, drawers, sidebars, navbars, footers) to be consistent with the black theme
- System MUST ensure all text, icons, and interactive elements maintain a WCAG AA-compliant contrast ratio (minimum 4.5:1) against the black background
- System MUST prevent any white or light background flash during page loads, route transitions, or component mounting
- System SHOULD use a centralized CSS variable (e.g., --bg-primary: #000000) or theme token so the black background is maintainable from a single source of truth
- System MUST audit and update any hardcoded light background values (e.g., #fff, #ffffff, white, background: #f5f5f5) found throughout stylesheets or inline styles
- System SHOULD verify the black background renders correctly on both mobile and desktop breakpoints across all supported browsers
- System MUST ensure third-party embedded components or iframes visually blend with or are contained within the black background where possible

## Technical Notes

Apply the global black background via the root CSS selector (html, body) and/or a top-level app wrapper class using a CSS custom property (--bg-primary: #000000 or #121212) to allow easy future theming. Audit all component stylesheets, Tailwind config (if used), or CSS-in-JS theme objects for hardcoded light background values and replace them with the centralized token. If the project uses a design system or theme provider (e.g., MUI, Chakra UI, Tailwind dark mode), update the theme config at the source rather than overriding per-component. Run a visual regression pass across major routes after implementation to catch any missed light-background containers.

- System MUST update all component-level background styles (cards, modals, drawers, sidebars, navbars, footers) to be consistent with the black theme
- System MUST ensure all text, icons, and interactive elements maintain a WCAG AA-compliant contrast ratio (minimum 4.5:1) against the black background
- System MUST prevent any white or light background flash during page loads, route transitions, or component mounting
- System SHOULD use a centralized CSS variable (e.g., --bg-primary: #000000) or theme token so the black background is maintainable from a single source of truth
- System MUST audit and update any hardcoded light background values (e.g., #fff, #ffffff, white, background: #f5f5f5) found throughout stylesheets or inline styles

- System MUST ensure third-party embedded components or iframes visually blend with or are contained within the black background where possible

## Technical Notes

Audit all component stylesheets, Tailwind config (if used), or CSS-in-JS theme objects for hardcoded light background values and replace them with the centralized token. mentioned_issues.title: Improve Test Coverage to 85% and Fix Discovered Bugs
mentioned_issues.body:
## Overview
Audit and expand the test suite for **Tech Connect** to achieve a minimum of **85% code coverage** across the codebase. During this process, identify and resolve any bugs or errors uncovered by the new or existing tests, following established best practices for testing.

## Technical Details
- Use the project's existing test framework (e.g., Jest, Vitest, PyTest, etc.) to measure and report current coverage baselines before making changes
- Write unit, integration, and/or edge-case tests for any untested or under-tested modules, components, and utilities
- Follow the Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) pattern for test structure and ensure tests are isolated, deterministic, and meaningful
- Avoid writing tests purely to inflate coverage — focus on testing real behaviors and user flows
- Any bugs discovered during testing should be fixed in the same branch with clear commit messages distinguishing bug fixes from test additions
- Run the full test suite locally before submitting to confirm no regressions are introduced

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Overall test coverage meets or exceeds **85%** as reported by the project's coverage tool
- [ ] All newly written tests follow best practices (AAA pattern, isolated, no flaky tests)
- [ ] Any bugs or errors discovered during testing are identified, documented, and fixed
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass with no regressions
- [ ] A brief summary of coverage changes and bugs fixed is included in the pull request description

- Use the project's existing test framework (e.g., Jest, Vitest, PyTest, etc.) to measure and report current coverage baselines before making changes
- Write unit, integration, and/or edge-case tests for any untested or under-tested modules, components, and utilities
- Follow the Arrange-Act-Assert (AAA) pattern for test structure and ensure tests are isolated, deterministic, and meaningful
- Avoid writing tests purely to inflate coverage — focus on testing real behaviors and user flows
- Any bugs discovered during testing should be fixed in the same branch with clear commit messages distinguishing bug fixes from test additions
- Run the full test suite locally before submitting to confirm no regressions are introduced

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Overall test coverage meets or exceeds **85%** as reported by the project's coverage tool
- [ ] All newly written tests follow best practices (AAA pattern, isolated, no flaky tests)
- [ ] Any bugs or errors discovered during testing are identified, documented, and fixed
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass with no regressions
- [ ] A brief summary of coverage changes and bugs fixed is included in the pull request description

closing_issues.title: Codebase Cleanup & Refactor: DRY, Single-Responsibility Modules, Unified Error Handling, Shared Frontend Client, and Test Coverage
closing_issues.body:
## Original Request

> # Feature Specification: Codebase Cleanup & Refactor
> 
> **Input**: User description: "refactor codebase to clean-up codebase. Keep it simple. Keep it DRY. Use best practices."
> 
> ## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
> 
> ### User Story 1 - Break Apart Oversized Modules (Priority: P1)
> 
> As a developer working on this codebase, I need the two largest service files — `github_projects.py` (~4,400 lines) and `copilot_polling.py` (~4,000 lines) — split into focused, single-responsibility modules so that I can understand, navigate, and modify them without context-switching through thousands of lines.
> 
> **Why this priority**: These two files are the biggest barrier to maintainability. Their size makes code review difficult, merge conflicts frequent, and onboarding slow. Every other refactoring effort becomes easier once these are manageable.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by verifying all existing unit and integration tests pass after the split, and that each new module has a clear, documented responsibility.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** the existing `github_projects.py` service, **When** refactored, **Then** it is split into focused modules (e.g., repository resolution, issue/PR management, project board operations, label/status management) each under ~500 lines, with no change in external behavior.
> 2. **Given** the existing `copilot_polling.py` service, **When** refactored, **Then** it is split into focused modules (e.g., polling lifecycle, event processing, response parsing, status tracking) each under ~500 lines, with no change in external behavior.
> 3. **Given** any module that imports from `github_projects` or `copilot_polling`, **When** the split is complete, **Then** all imports resolve correctly and the application starts and serves requests identically.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 2 - Eliminate Duplicated Code Patterns (Priority: P1)
> 
> As a developer, I need duplicated logic consolidated into shared utilities so that bug fixes and behavior changes only need to happen in one place.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Duplicated code is the root cause of inconsistent behavior and wasted effort. Fixing a bug in one copy but not another leads to subtle production issues.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by searching the codebase for previously-duplicated patterns and confirming each exists in exactly one location, with all callers using the shared version.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** repository resolution logic appears in three separate locations (GitHub projects service, webhook handler, and copilot polling), **When** refactored, **Then** a single shared utility handles repository resolution and all three callers use it.
> 2. **Given** polling start/initialization logic is repeated in multiple places, **When** refactored, **Then** a single entry point manages polling lifecycle.
> 3. **Given** session reconstruction logic is duplicated across request handlers, **When** refactored, **Then** a shared session-management utility is used consistently.
> 4. **Given** cache key construction is scattered with inline string formatting, **When** refactored, **Then** cache keys are built through a centralized helper with consistent naming conventions.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 3 - Standardize Error Handling (Priority: P2)
> 
> As a developer, I need a single, consistent error-handling strategy across the entire backend so that errors are reported predictably and debugging is straightforward.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Currently, some modules raise `HTTPException` directly, others use custom `AppException` classes, and some silently swallow errors. This inconsistency makes it hard to trace failures and deliver reliable error messages to users.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by triggering known error conditions in each API endpoint and verifying the response format, status code, and logged output follow the same pattern.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** the backend has mixed error-handling patterns, **When** refactored, **Then** all API route handlers use a unified error-handling approach where domain exceptions are translated to HTTP responses in one place (e.g., a middleware or exception handler).
> 2. **Given** some service functions silently catch and ignore exceptions, **When** refactored, **Then** all exceptions are either handled explicitly with appropriate logging or propagated to the caller.
> 3. **Given** error responses vary in shape across endpoints, **When** refactored, **Then** all error responses follow a consistent structure (status code, error message, optional detail).
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 4 - Consolidate Hardcoded Values and Magic Numbers (Priority: P2)
> 
> As a developer, I need all magic numbers, hardcoded strings, and configuration values moved to a central location so that tuning behavior doesn't require hunting through source code.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Hardcoded values scattered throughout the codebase (timeouts, retry counts, cache TTLs, default limits) make it impossible to adjust behavior without risk of missing an occurrence.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by searching the codebase for numeric literals and string constants in business logic and confirming they reference named constants or configuration values.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** timeout values, retry counts, and polling intervals are hardcoded in service files, **When** refactored, **Then** they are defined as named constants in the configuration or constants module.
> 2. **Given** cache TTL values are embedded inline, **When** refactored, **Then** all cache durations reference a single configuration source.
> 3. **Given** default pagination limits, batch sizes, and similar operational values are scattered, **When** refactored, **Then** they are centralized and documented.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 5 - Unify Frontend API Communication Layer (Priority: P2)
> 
> As a frontend developer, I need a single, consistent approach to calling backend APIs so that error handling, authentication headers, and retry logic are handled uniformly.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Currently the frontend mixes raw `fetch()` calls with inconsistent patterns across hooks. This leads to duplicated auth header logic, inconsistent error handling, and makes it easy to forget edge cases.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by verifying all API calls route through a shared client, with consistent error handling and auth header injection.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** frontend hooks make direct `fetch()` calls with manually constructed headers, **When** refactored, **Then** all API calls use a shared HTTP client that automatically handles authentication headers and base URL configuration.
> 2. **Given** error handling in API calls varies across hooks, **When** refactored, **Then** the shared client provides consistent error parsing and notification.
> 3. **Given** the frontend has no centralized response interceptor, **When** refactored, **Then** common concerns (401 redirect, network errors, response parsing) are handled in one place.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 6 - Improve Frontend State Management and Resilience (Priority: P3)
> 
> As a user, I need the application to handle page refreshes, errors, and edge cases gracefully so that I don't lose context or encounter blank screens.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Currently, in-memory state is lost on page refresh, there are no error boundaries, and redundant polling alongside WebSocket connections wastes resources. These are quality-of-life improvements that make the app feel robust.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by refreshing the page mid-workflow and verifying state is preserved, and by simulating API failures and verifying error boundaries display helpful messages.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** critical application state (selected project, board filters) is stored only in memory, **When** refactored, **Then** essential state is persisted to `sessionStorage` so that a page refresh restores the user's context within the same tab.
> 2. **Given** no error boundaries exist in the component tree, **When** refactored, **Then** error boundaries catch rendering failures and display fallback UI instead of a blank screen.
> 3. **Given** some views use both polling and WebSocket for the same data, **When** refactored, **Then** WebSocket is the primary real-time channel per data stream, with automatic polling fallback on disconnect that ceases when WebSocket reconnects.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 7 - Increase Test Coverage for Untested Modules (Priority: P3)
> 
> As a developer, I need test coverage for currently-untested services and hooks so that refactoring can proceed safely with a regression safety net.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Several backend services and most frontend hooks lack any test coverage. Without tests, the refactoring work in P1 and P2 stories carries higher risk of silent regressions.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by running the test suite and verifying coverage reports show tests exist for previously-untested modules.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** backend services `completion_providers.py`, `session_store.py`, `settings_store.py`, `agent_tracking.py`, and `workflow_orchestrator.py` have no dedicated tests, **When** tests are added, **Then** each service has unit tests covering its primary functions and edge cases.
> 2. **Given** frontend hooks `useSettings`, `useWorkflow`, `useAgentConfig`, `useChat`, `useProjectBoard`, and `useAppTheme` are untested, **When** tests are added, **Then** each hook has tests verifying its core behavior.
> 3. **Given** no frontend component tests exist, **When** basic component tests are added, **Then** key user-facing components (board view, chat panel, settings page) have rendering and interaction tests.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### Edge Cases
> 
> - What happens if a refactored module is imported by a third-party integration or script outside the main application? Thin re-export facades at the original module paths ensure backward compatibility. Internal code imports directly from new sub-modules.
> - How does the system handle in-progress WebSocket connections during a deployment that includes the refactored modules? Existing connections should gracefully degrade.
> - What happens when the centralized error handler encounters an unexpected exception type? It must fall back to a generic 500 response with appropriate logging rather than crashing.
> - What if removing duplicate code reveals that the copies had diverged in subtle ways? The refactoring must reconcile differences explicitly, choosing the correct behavior and documenting the decision.
> 
> ## Clarifications
> 
> ### Session 2026-02-19
> 
> - Q: Should error responses include internal details (stack traces, exception class names) or only sanitized user-safe messages? → A: Sanitized user-safe messages always; full details logged server-side only.
> - Q: Which browser storage mechanism should be used for persisting navigation state across page refreshes? → A: `sessionStorage` (per-tab, clears on tab close, no cross-tab leakage).
> - Q: When the WebSocket connection drops, what should the fallback behavior be? → A: WebSocket primary + automatic polling fallback on disconnect; polling stops when WS reconnects.
> - Q: Should original service file paths remain as re-export facades after the module split? → A: Yes — keep thin re-export facades at original paths; internal code imports from new sub-modules.
> - Q: Where should the shared frontend HTTP client obtain the auth token from? → A: Client reads from a centralized auth context/store at request time (lazy lookup).
> 
> ## Requirements *(mandatory)*
> 
> ### Functional Requirements
> 
> - **FR-001**: System MUST maintain identical external API behavior (request/response contracts) after all refactoring — no endpoint signatures, response shapes, or status codes may change.
> - **FR-002**: System MUST split `github_projects.py` into focused sub-modules with single responsibilities, each no larger than ~500 lines. The original module path MUST remain as a thin re-export facade preserving the existing public API for backward compatibility.
> - **FR-003**: System MUST split `copilot_polling.py` into focused sub-modules with single responsibilities, each no larger than ~500 lines. The original module path MUST remain as a thin re-export facade preserving the existing public API for backward compatibility.
> - **FR-004**: System MUST consolidate duplicate repository-resolution logic into a single shared utility used by all callers.
> - **FR-005**: System MUST consolidate duplicate polling-initialization logic into a single entry point.
> - **FR-006**: System MUST consolidate duplicate session-reconstruction logic into a shared utility.
> - **FR-007**: System MUST centralize all cache key construction through a shared helper with consistent naming.
> - **FR-008**: System MUST use a unified error-handling strategy where domain exceptions map to HTTP responses through a single mechanism (middleware or handler).
> - **FR-009**: System MUST ensure all error responses follow a consistent, sanitized structure across all endpoints — no internal details (stack traces, exception class names, database info) are ever returned to the client. Full diagnostic details MUST be logged server-side only.
> - **FR-010**: System MUST move all hardcoded magic numbers, timeouts, retry counts, TTLs, and default limits to named constants or configuration.
> - **FR-011**: Frontend MUST route all API calls through a shared HTTP client with automatic base URL configuration. The client MUST obtain the auth token via lazy lookup from a centralized auth context/store at request time, avoiding stale tokens.
> - **FR-012**: Frontend MUST implement error boundaries to prevent blank screens on component rendering failures.
> - **FR-013**: Frontend MUST persist essential navigation state (selected project, board context) across page refreshes using `sessionStorage`, scoped per browser tab.
> - **FR-014**: Frontend MUST use WebSocket as the primary real-time update channel with automatic polling fallback when the WebSocket connection is lost. Polling MUST stop automatically once the WebSocket reconnects. No data stream may use both channels simultaneously.
> - **FR-015**: System MUST have unit tests for all backend services that currently lack coverage (`completion_providers`, `session_store`, `settings_store`, `agent_tracking`, `workflow_orchestrator`).
> - **FR-016**: Frontend MUST have tests for all hooks that currently lack coverage (`useSettings`, `useWorkflow`, `useAgentConfig`, `useChat`, `useProjectBoard`, `useAppTheme`).
> 
> ### Key Entities
> 
> - **Service Module**: A focused backend module with a single responsibility, defined public interface, and clear dependency boundaries. Replaces the current monolithic service files.
> - **Shared Utility**: A reusable function or class extracted from duplicated code, consumed by multiple callers. Lives in a dedicated utilities layer.
> - **HTTP Client**: A frontend abstraction over `fetch()` that centralizes base URL, error handling, and response parsing for all API communication. Obtains the auth token via lazy lookup from a centralized auth context/store at each request time, ensuring tokens are never stale.
> - **Error Response**: A standardized, sanitized structure returned by all API endpoints on failure, containing status code, error type, and user-facing message. Internal diagnostic details (stack traces, exception classes) are never included in the response body; they are logged server-side only.
> - **Named Constant**: A configuration value or operational parameter defined in a central location with a descriptive name, replacing inline magic numbers.
> 
> ## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
> 
> ### Measurable Outcomes
> 
> - **SC-001**: No backend source file exceeds 500 lines of code (excluding tests and generated files).
> - **SC-002**: Zero instances of duplicated logic patterns — each business operation (repo resolution, polling init, session construction, cache key building) exists in exactly one location.
> - **SC-003**: All API error responses conform to a single documented structure, verifiable by running the full test suite.
> - **SC-004**: All operational parameters (timeouts, retries, TTLs, limits) are traceable to named constants — zero magic numbers in business logic.
> - **SC-005**: 100% of frontend API calls route through the shared HTTP client — zero direct `fetch()` calls outside the client module.
> - **SC-006**: Application state survives a page refresh for all primary workflows (project selection, board view, active chat) via `sessionStorage`, without leaking state across tabs.
> - **SC-007**: All existing tests pass without modification to test assertions (test infrastructure changes are acceptable).
> - **SC-008**: Backend test coverage increases to include all five currently-untested service modules.
> - **SC-009**: Frontend test coverage increases to include all six currently-untested hooks.
> - **SC-010**: Developer onboarding time for understanding a single module decreases — measured by each module having a clear, single-sentence description of its responsibility in its docstring.
> 
> ## Assumptions
> 
> - The existing test suite is trusted as the correctness baseline. If all tests pass after refactoring, behavior is considered preserved.
> - "No larger than ~500 lines" is a guideline, not a hard rule — a module may slightly exceed this if splitting further would harm cohesion.
> - Backend database schema and migration files are out of scope for this refactoring effort.
> - Third-party API contracts (GitHub API, Copilot API) are unchanged and the refactoring only affects internal code organization.
> - The frontend build toolchain (Vite, TypeScript, ESLint) and backend framework (FastAPI) remain unchanged.
> - Performance characteristics should remain unchanged or improve — no refactoring should introduce additional latency or resource consumption.

## User Story

As a developer working on this codebase, I need the two largest service files (`github_projects.py` ~4,400 lines and `copilot_polling.py` ~4,000 lines) split into focused single-responsibility modules under ~500 lines each, all duplicated logic (repository resolution, polling initialization, session reconstruction, cache key construction) consolidated into shared utilities, a unified backend error-handling strategy, all magic numbers moved to named constants, a shared frontend HTTP client with lazy auth-token lookup, sessionStorage-backed state persistence, error boundaries, and WebSocket-primary/polling-fallback real-time updates — so that the codebase is maintainable, onboarding is fast, bugs are fixed in one place, and the application behaves predictably. As a frontend developer, I also need all six currently-untested hooks and five untested backend services covered by tests so that future refactoring can proceed safely without silent regressions.

## UI/UX Description

This is a backend and frontend engineering refactor with no new user-visible UI surfaces, but several UX-resilience improvements. Error boundaries must replace blank screens with a helpful fallback UI (e.g., a card with an error message and a 'Retry' or 'Reload' option) when any component in the React tree throws a rendering error — covering at minimum the board view, chat panel, and settings page. Essential navigation state (selected project, active board filters, board context) must be written to `sessionStorage` at every state change and rehydrated on mount, scoped per browser tab with no cross-tab leakage; state must survive F5/hard refresh for all primary workflows (project selection, board view, active chat). The real-time data layer must transparently switch between WebSocket (primary) and polling (fallback on disconnect) with no visible loading interruption; polling must cease automatically once WebSocket reconnects, and no data stream may use both channels simultaneously. All API error responses seen by the frontend must use a consistent sanitized structure (status code, error type, user-facing message) — no stack traces, exception class names, or database details are ever surfaced in the UI. The shared frontend HTTP client must be invisible to end users but must handle 401 redirects, network errors, and response parsing in one place, ensuring auth headers are never stale via lazy lookup from the centralized auth context/store at each request time.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST split `github_projects.py` (~4,400 lines) into focused sub-modules with single responsibilities (e.g., repository resolution, issue/PR management, project board operations, label/status management), each no larger than ~500 lines, while retaining a thin re-export facade at the original `github_projects` module path that preserves the full existing public API for backward compatibility.
- System MUST split `copilot_polling.py` (~4,000 lines) into focused sub-modules with single responsibilities (e.g., polling lifecycle, event processing, response parsing, status tracking), each no larger than ~500 lines, while retaining a thin re-export facade at the original `copilot_polling` module path that preserves the full existing public API for backward compatibility.
- System MUST consolidate the duplicate repository-resolution logic currently present in three locations (GitHub projects service, webhook handler, copilot polling) into a single shared utility consumed by all three callers, with zero residual copies of the logic elsewhere.
- System MUST consolidate duplicate polling-initialization logic into a single entry point, duplicate session-reconstruction logic into a shared session-management utility, and all inline cache-key string formatting into a centralized cache-key helper with consistent naming conventions.
- System MUST implement a unified backend error-handling strategy (middleware or exception handler) that translates domain exceptions (`AppException`, `HTTPException`, and unexpected types) into HTTP responses in one place; all error responses MUST follow a consistent sanitized structure (status code, error type, user-facing message) with no stack traces, exception class names, or database details in the response body — full diagnostic details MUST be logged server-side only. The centralized handler MUST fall back to a generic 500 response with logging for unexpected exception types rather than crashing.
- System MUST move all hardcoded magic numbers, timeout values, retry counts, cache TTLs, polling intervals, default pagination limits, and batch sizes out of business logic and into named constants or a configuration module, making them traceable and documented.
- Frontend MUST route 100% of API calls through a shared HTTP client (zero direct `fetch()` calls outside the client module) that automatically handles base URL configuration, authentication header injection via lazy lookup from the centralized auth context/store at request time (never stale tokens), consistent error parsing, 401 redirect handling, network error handling, and response parsing in one place.
- Frontend MUST persist essential navigation state (selected project, board context, board filters) to `sessionStorage` (per-tab, clears on tab close, no cross-tab leakage) at every state change and rehydrate on mount, so that page refreshes restore the user's context within the same tab for all primary workflows.
- Frontend MUST implement error boundaries around the board view, chat panel, and settings page (at minimum) to catch rendering failures and display a helpful fallback UI instead of a blank screen.
- Frontend MUST use WebSocket as the primary real-time update channel per data stream, with automatic polling fallback triggered on WebSocket disconnect; polling MUST stop automatically once the WebSocket reconnects, and no single data stream may use both channels simultaneously.
- System MUST have unit tests covering primary functions and edge cases for all five currently-untested backend services: `completion_providers.py`, `session_store.py`, `settings_store.py`, `agent_tracking.py`, and `workflow_orchestrator.py`.
- Frontend MUST have tests covering core behavior for all six currently-untested hooks: `useSettings`, `useWorkflow`, `useAgentConfig`, `useChat`, `useProjectBoard`, and `useAppTheme`; key user-facing components (board view, chat panel, settings page) MUST have rendering and interaction tests.
- System MUST maintain identical external API behavior after all refactoring — no endpoint signatures, response shapes, or HTTP status codes may change — and all existing tests MUST pass without modification to test assertions (test infrastructure changes are acceptable).
- System MUST ensure divergent copies of duplicated logic are explicitly reconciled during consolidation, choosing the correct behavior, documenting the decision, and providing thin re-export facades at original module paths for any third-party integrations or scripts that import from the old paths.
- System MUST ensure every new sub-module and shared utility has a single-sentence docstring describing its sole responsibility, supporting SC-010 (measurable reduction in developer onboarding time per module).
- System SHOULD ensure performance characteristics remain unchanged or improve after refactoring — no additional latency or resource consumption may be introduced by the new module boundaries or shared utilities.

## Technical Notes

Backend is FastAPI; frontend uses Vite, TypeScript, and ESLint — neither build toolchain nor framework changes are in scope. Start with `github_projects.py` and `copilot_polling.py` splits (P1) since all other refactoring becomes easier once these monoliths are decomposed; use Python packages (directories with `__init__.py` re-export facades) so existing `from github_projects import X` call sites require zero changes. For the unified error handler, implement a FastAPI `@app.exception_handler` or middleware that catches `AppException`, `HTTPException`, and `Exception` base class in priority order, maps them to a `{ status, error, message }` JSON shape, and always logs `exc_info=True` server-side before responding. ## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.specify`

Write a detailed specification for this feature. Analyze requirements, define acceptance criteria, and document the technical approach.

## Parent Issue Context

## Original Request

> # Feature Specification: Codebase Cleanup & Refactor
> 
> **Input**: User description: "refactor codebase to clean-up codebase. Keep it simple. Keep it DRY. Use best practices."
> 
> ## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
> 
> ### User Story 1 - Break Apart Oversized Modules (Priority: P1)
> 
> As a developer working on this codebase, I need the two largest service files — `github_projects.py` (~4,400 lines) and `copilot_polling.py` (~4,000 lines) — split into focused, single-responsibility modules so that I can understand, navigate, and modify them without context-switching through thousands of lines.
> 
> **Why this priority**: These two files are the biggest barrier to maintainability. Their size makes code review difficult, merge conflicts frequent, and onboarding slow. Every other refactoring effort becomes easier once these are manageable.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by verifying all existing unit and integration tests pass after the split, and that each new module has a clear, documented responsibility.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** the existing `github_projects.py` service, **When** refactored, **Then** it is split into focused modules (e.g., repository resolution, issue/PR management, project board operations, label/status management) each under ~500 lines, with no change in external behavior.
> 2. **Given** the existing `copilot_polling.py` service, **When** refactored, **Then** it is split into focused modules (e.g., polling lifecycle, event processing, response parsing, status tracking) each under ~500 lines, with no change in external behavior.
> 3. **Given** any module that imports from `github_projects` or `copilot_polling`, **When** the split is complete, **Then** all imports resolve correctly and the application starts and serves requests identically.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 2 - Eliminate Duplicated Code Patterns (Priority: P1)
> 
> As a developer, I need duplicated logic consolidated into shared utilities so that bug fixes and behavior changes only need to happen in one place.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Duplicated code is the root cause of inconsistent behavior and wasted effort. Fixing a bug in one copy but not another leads to subtle production issues.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by searching the codebase for previously-duplicated patterns and confirming each exists in exactly one location, with all callers using the shared version.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** repository resolution logic appears in three separate locations (GitHub projects service, webhook handler, and copilot polling), **When** refactored, **Then** a single shared utility handles repository resolution and all three callers use it.
> 2. **Given** polling start/initialization logic is repeated in multiple places, **When** refactored, **Then** a single entry point manages polling lifecycle.
> 3. **Given** session reconstruction logic is duplicated across request handlers, **When** refactored, **Then** a shared session-management utility is used consistently.
> 4. **Given** cache key construction is scattered with inline string formatting, **When** refactored, **Then** cache keys are built through a centralized helper with consistent naming conventions.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 3 - Standardize Error Handling (Priority: P2)
> 
> As a developer, I need a single, consistent error-handling strategy across the entire backend so that errors are reported predictably and debugging is straightforward.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Currently, some modules raise `HTTPException` directly, others use custom `AppException` classes, and some silently swallow errors. This inconsistency makes it hard to trace failures and deliver reliable error messages to users.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by triggering known error conditions in each API endpoint and verifying the response format, status code, and logged output follow the same pattern.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** the backend has mixed error-handling patterns, **When** refactored, **Then** all API route handlers use a unified error-handling approach where domain exceptions are translated to HTTP responses in one place (e.g., a middleware or exception handler).
> 2. **Given** some service functions silently catch and ignore exceptions, **When** refactored, **Then** all exceptions are either handled explicitly with appropriate logging or propagated to the caller.
> 3. **Given** error responses vary in shape across endpoints, **When** refactored, **Then** all error responses follow a consistent structure (status code, error message, optional detail).
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 4 - Consolidate Hardcoded Values and Magic Numbers (Priority: P2)
> 
> As a developer, I need all magic numbers, hardcoded strings, and configuration values moved to a central location so that tuning behavior doesn't require hunting through source code.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Hardcoded values scattered throughout the codebase (timeouts, retry counts, cache TTLs, default limits) make it impossible to adjust behavior without risk of missing an occurrence.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by searching the codebase for numeric literals and string constants in business logic and confirming they reference named constants or configuration values.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** timeout values, retry counts, and polling intervals are hardcoded in service files, **When** refactored, **Then** they are defined as named constants in the configuration or constants module.
> 2. **Given** cache TTL values are embedded inline, **When** refactored, **Then** all cache durations reference a single configuration source.
> 3. **Given** default pagination limits, batch sizes, and similar operational values are scattered, **When** refactored, **Then** they are centralized and documented.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 5 - Unify Frontend API Communication Layer (Priority: P2)
> 
> As a frontend developer, I need a single, consistent approach to calling backend APIs so that error handling, authentication headers, and retry logic are handled uniformly.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Currently the frontend mixes raw `fetch()` calls with inconsistent patterns across hooks. This leads to duplicated auth header logic, inconsistent error handling, and makes it easy to forget edge cases.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by verifying all API calls route through a shared client, with consistent error handling and auth header injection.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** frontend hooks make direct `fetch()` calls with manually constructed headers, **When** refactored, **Then** all API calls use a shared HTTP client that automatically handles authentication headers and base URL configuration.
> 2. **Given** error handling in API calls varies across hooks, **When** refactored, **Then** the shared client provides consistent error parsing and notification.
> 3. **Given** the frontend has no centralized response interceptor, **When** refactored, **Then** common concerns (401 redirect, network errors, response parsing) are handled in one place.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 6 - Improve Frontend State Management and Resilience (Priority: P3)
> 
> As a user, I need the application to handle page refreshes, errors, and edge cases gracefully so that I don't lose context or encounter blank screens.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Currently, in-memory state is lost on page refresh, there are no error boundaries, and redundant polling alongside WebSocket connections wastes resources. These are quality-of-life improvements that make the app feel robust.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by refreshing the page mid-workflow and verifying state is preserved, and by simulating API failures and verifying error boundaries display helpful messages.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** critical application state (selected project, board filters) is stored only in memory, **When** refactored, **Then** essential state is persisted to `sessionStorage` so that a page refresh restores the user's context within the same tab.
> 2. **Given** no error boundaries exist in the component tree, **When** refactored, **Then** error boundaries catch rendering failures and display fallback UI instead of a blank screen.
> 3. **Given** some views use both polling and WebSocket for the same data, **When** refactored, **Then** WebSocket is the primary real-time channel per data stream, with automatic polling fallback on disconnect that ceases when WebSocket reconnects.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### User Story 7 - Increase Test Coverage for Untested Modules (Priority: P3)
> 
> As a developer, I need test coverage for currently-untested services and hooks so that refactoring can proceed safely with a regression safety net.
> 
> **Why this priority**: Several backend services and most frontend hooks lack any test coverage. Without tests, the refactoring work in P1 and P2 stories carries higher risk of silent regressions.
> 
> **Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by running the test suite and verifying coverage reports show tests exist for previously-untested modules.
> 
> **Acceptance Scenarios**:
> 
> 1. **Given** backend services `completion_providers.py`, `session_store.py`, `settings_store.py`, `agent_tracking.py`, and `workflow_orchestrator.py` have no dedicated tests, **When** tests are added, **Then** each service has unit tests covering its primary functions and edge cases.
> 2. **Given** frontend hooks `useSettings`, `useWorkflow`, `useAgentConfig`, `useChat`, `useProjectBoard`, and `useAppTheme` are untested, **When** tests are added, **Then** each hook has tests verifying its core behavior.
> 3. **Given** no frontend component tests exist, **When** basic component tests are added, **Then** key user-facing components (board view, chat panel, settings page) have rendering and interaction tests.
> 
> ---
> 
> ### Edge Cases
> 
> - What happens if a refactored module is imported by a third-party integration or script outside the main application? Thin re-export facades at the original module paths ensure backward compatibility. Internal code imports directly from new sub-modules.
> - How does the system handle in-progress WebSocket connections during a deployment that includes the refactored modules? Existing connections should gracefully degrade.
> - What happens when the centralized error handler encounters an unexpected exception type? It must fall back to a generic 500 response with appropriate logging rather than crashing.
> - What if removing duplicate code reveals that the copies had diverged in subtle ways? The refactoring must reconcile differences explicitly, choosing the correct behavior and documenting the decision.
> 
> ## Clarifications
> 
> ### Session 2026-02-19
> 
> - Q: Should error responses include internal details (stack traces, exception class names) or only sanitized user-safe messages? → A: Sanitized user-safe messages always; full details logged server-side only.
> - Q: Which browser storage mechanism should be used for persisting navigation state across page refreshes? → A: `sessionStorage` (per-tab, clears on tab close, no cross-tab leakage).
> - Q: When the WebSocket connection drops, what should the fallback behavior be? → A: WebSocket primary + automatic polling fallback on disconnect; polling stops when WS reconnects.
> - Q: Should original service file paths remain as re-export facades after the module split? → A: Yes — keep thin re-export facades at original paths; internal code imports from new sub-modules.
> - Q: Where should the shared frontend HTTP client obtain the auth token from? → A: Client reads from a centralized auth context/store at request time (lazy lookup).
> 
> ## Requirements *(mandatory)*

> - **FR-003**: System MUST split `copilot_polling.py` into focused sub-modules with single responsibilities, each no larger than ~500 lines. The original module path MUST remain as a thin re-export facade preserving the existing public API for backward compatibility.
> - **FR-004**: System MUST consolidate duplicate repository-resolution logic into a single shared utility used by all callers.
> - **FR-005**: System MUST consolidate duplicate polling-initialization logic into a single entry point.
> - **FR-006**: System MUST consolidate duplicate session-reconstruction logic into a shared utility.
> - **FR-007**: System MUST centralize all cache key construction through a shared helper with consistent naming.
> - **FR-008**: System MUST use a unified error-handling strategy where domain exceptions map to HTTP responses through a single mechanism (middleware or handler).
> - **FR-009**: System MUST ensure all error responses follow a consistent, sanitized structure across all endpoints — no internal details (stack traces, exception class names, database info) are ever returned to the client. Full diagnostic details MUST be logged server-side only.
> - **FR-010**: System MUST move all hardcoded magic numbers, timeouts, retry counts, TTLs, and default limits to named constants or configuration.
> - **FR-011**: Frontend MUST route all API calls through a shared HTTP client with automatic base URL configuration. The client MUST obtain the auth token via lazy lookup from a centralized auth context/store at request time, avoiding stale tokens.
> - **FR-012**: Frontend MUST implement error boundaries to prevent blank screens on component rendering failures.
> - **FR-013**: Frontend MUST persist essential navigation state (selected project, board context) across page refreshes using `sessionStorage`, scoped per browser tab.
> - **FR-014**: Frontend MUST use WebSocket as the primary real-time update channel with automatic polling fallback when the WebSocket connection is lost. Polling MUST stop automatically once the WebSocket reconnects. No data stream may use both channels simultaneously.
> - **FR-015**: System MUST have unit tests for all backend services that currently lack coverage (`completion_providers`, `session_store`, `settings_store`, `agent_tracking`, `workflow_orchestrator`).
> - **FR-016**: Frontend MUST have tests for all hooks that currently lack coverage (`useSettings`, `useWorkflow`, `useAgentConfig`, `useChat`, `useProjectBoard`, `useAppTheme`).
> 
> ### Key Entities
> 
> - **Service Module**: A focused backend module with a single responsibility, defined public interface, and clear dependency boundaries. Replaces the current monolithic service files.
> - **Shared Utility**: A reusable function or class extracted from duplicated code, consumed by multiple callers. Lives in a dedicated utilities layer.
> - **HTTP Client**: A frontend abstraction over `fetch()` that centralizes base URL, error handling, and response parsing for all API communication. Obtains the auth token via lazy lookup from a centralized auth context/store at each request time, ensuring tokens are never stale.
> - **Error Response**: A standardized, sanitized structure returned by all API endpoints on failure, containing status code, error type, and user-facing message. Internal diagnostic details (stack traces, exception classes) are never included in the response body; they are logged server-side only.
> - **Named Constant**: A configuration value or operational parameter defined in a central location with a descriptive name, replacing inline magic numbers.

> - **SC-003**: All API error responses conform to a single documented structure, verifiable by running the full test suite.
> - **SC-004**: All operational parameters (timeouts, retries, TTLs, limits) are traceable to named constants — zero magic numbers in business logic.
> - **SC-005**: 100% of frontend API calls route through the shared HTTP client — zero direct `fetch()` calls outside the client module.
> - **SC-006**: Application state survives a page refresh for all primary workflows (project selection, board view, active chat) via `sessionStorage`, without leaking state across tabs.
> - **SC-007**: All existing tests pass without modification to test assertions (test infrastructure changes are acceptable).

>

mentioned_issues.title: Add Blue Background Color to App
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> add blue background to app

## User Story

As a user of Boykai's Tech Connect app, I want the application to display a blue background so that the visual design is more aligned with the desired branding and aesthetic. This change should apply consistently across the app for a cohesive look and feel.

## UI/UX Description

The app's background should be updated to a blue color across all screens and views. The specific shade of blue should align with the project's design system or brand palette (e.g., a primary blue such as #1E90FF, #2563EB, or a similarly appropriate hue). The blue background must maintain sufficient contrast with all existing text, icons, buttons, and UI elements to meet WCAG AA accessibility standards. The transition should feel intentional and polished — consider whether a flat solid blue, a subtle gradient (e.g., light blue to deep blue), or a themed CSS variable is most appropriate. All foreground elements (cards, modals, inputs) should remain legible and visually distinct against the new background.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST apply a blue background color to the root/app-level container so it is visible across all pages and views of the application.
- System MUST use a specific, consistent blue color value (hex, RGB, or CSS variable) that aligns with the project's existing design tokens or brand guidelines.
- System MUST ensure all text elements maintain a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 against the blue background in compliance with WCAG AA accessibility standards.
- System MUST NOT break any existing UI components (buttons, cards, modals, inputs, navigation) when the background color is applied.
- System SHOULD define the blue background color as a reusable CSS variable or theme token (e.g., --color-bg-primary) to allow easy future updates.
- System SHOULD apply the background color responsively so it renders correctly on mobile, tablet, and desktop screen sizes.
- System SHOULD ensure the blue background is compatible with both light and dark mode variants if the app supports theme switching.
- System MUST be tested across major modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) to confirm consistent rendering of the blue background.

## Technical Notes

Apply the blue background at the highest-level layout component or global stylesheet (e.g., body, #root, or App.css) to ensure full coverage. Use a CSS custom property such as --app-bg-color: #2563EB and reference it via background-color throughout the app for maintainability. If the project uses a CSS framework like Tailwind CSS, apply a utility class (e.g., bg-blue-600) to the root element or extend the theme config. Review all child components for hardcoded white or transparent backgrounds that may conflict with the new global background color.
