mentioned_issues.title: Security Review
mentioned_issues.body: Plan: Security, Privacy & Vulnerability Audit 3 Critical · 8 High · 9 Medium · 2 Low — across OWASP Top 10. Findings describe the vulnerable pattern/behavior, not tied to specific function or line numbers. Phase 1 — Critical (Fix Immediately) 1. Session token passed in URL — OWASP A02 (Critical) The OAuth flow redirects the browser to the frontend with ?session_token=... in the URL. Tokens in URLs are recorded in browser history, server/proxy/CDN access logs, and HTTP Referer headers. Correct behavior: Backend sets an HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Secure cookie directly on the OAuth callback response and redirects with no credentials in the URL. Frontend must never read credentials from URL params. Files: auth.py, useAuth.ts 2. At-rest encryption not enforced — OWASP A02 (Critical) ENCRYPTION_KEY is optional; when absent the app logs a warning and stores OAuth tokens in plaintext SQLite. Correct behavior: On startup in non-debug mode, the application must refuse to start if ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set. Also apply the same mandatory rule to GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Files: config.py, encryption.py 3. Frontend container runs as root — OWASP A05 (Critical) The frontend Dockerfile has no USER directive; nginx runs as uid=0. The backend already runs non-root. Correct behavior: All containers must run as a dedicated non-root system user. Files: Dockerfile Phase 2 — High (This Week) 4. Project resources not scoped to authenticated user — OWASP A01 (High) Endpoints that accept a project_id (task creation, WebSocket subscription, project settings, workflow operations) do not verify the authenticated user owns that project. Any authenticated user can target any project by guessing its ID. Correct behavior: Every endpoint accepting a project identifier must verify the session has access to that project before performing any action. Centralize this check as a shared dependency. Files: tasks.py, projects.py, settings.py, workflow.py 5. Timing attack on Signal webhook — OWASP A07 (High) Signal webhook secret comparison uses standard string equality (!=), which leaks timing information. The GitHub webhook already uses hmac.compare_digest correctly. Correct behavior: All secret/token comparisons throughout the codebase must use constant-time comparison. Files: signal.py 6. Missing HTTP security headers in nginx — OWASP A05 (High) Only basic headers are set. Missing: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. The present X-XSS-Protection is deprecated in modern browsers. Correct behavior: Add all five headers; remove X-XSS-Protection; set server_tokens off to hide nginx version. Files: nginx.conf 7. Dev endpoint accepts GitHub PAT in URL — OWASP A02 (High) The dev login endpoint receives a GitHub Personal Access Token as a URL query parameter. Correct behavior: All credential inputs, even dev-only, must arrive in the POST request body (JSON), never in the URL. Files: auth.py 8. OAuth requests overly broad repo scope — OWASP A01 (High) The app requests the repo scope, which grants full read/write access to all private repositories. Only project management access is needed. Correct behavior: Request minimum necessary scopes. Test that all write operations work with narrower scopes before removing repo. Files: github_auth.py 9. Session secret key has no minimum entropy check — OWASP A07 (High) SESSION_SECRET_KEY is accepted at any length with no validation. Correct behavior: Startup must reject keys shorter than 64 characters. Files: config.py 10. Docker services bound to all network interfaces — OWASP A05 (High) Backend and frontend ports are bound to 0.0.0.0, exposing them on all interfaces. Correct behavior: Development: bind to 127.0.0.1 only. Production: expose only via a reverse proxy, not directly via container ports. Files: docker-compose.yml Phase 3 — Medium (Next Sprint) 11. No rate limiting on expensive/sensitive endpoints — OWASP A04 (Medium) Chat, agent invocation, workflow, and OAuth callback endpoints have no per-user or per-IP rate limits. A single user can exhaust shared AI/GitHub quotas. Correct behavior: Per-user limits on write/AI endpoints; per-IP limit on OAuth callback. slowapi (FastAPI-compatible) is the recommended library. Files: chat.py, agents.py, workflow.py, auth.py 12. Cookie Secure flag not enforced in production — OWASP A02 (Medium) cookie_secure defaults to False and relies on indirect URL-prefix detection to enable it — fragile and silently misconfigures. Correct behavior: Startup in non-debug mode must fail if cookies are not configured as Secure. Files: config.py 13. Debug mode bypasses webhook signature verification — OWASP A05 (Medium) When DEBUG=true and no webhook secret is set, signature verification is skipped. If debug mode is accidentally on in production, unauthenticated callers can trigger workflows. Correct behavior: Webhook verification must never be conditional on debug mode. Developers use a locally configured test secret. Files: webhooks.py 14. API docs exposed when debug is enabled — OWASP A05 (Medium) Swagger/ReDoc availability is gated on DEBUG, not a dedicated toggle. If debug is on in production, full API schema is public. Correct behavior: Gate on a separate ENABLE_DOCS environment variable, independent of DEBUG. Files: main.py 15. SQLite database directory is world-readable — OWASP A02 (Medium) Database directory is created with default 0755 permissions; any process on the container can read the DB file. Correct behavior: Create directory with 0700, database file with 0600. Only the application user needs access. Files: database.py 16. CORS origins configuration not validated — OWASP A05 (Medium) The comma-separated CORS origins env var is parsed with no URL format validation. Typos silently pass. Correct behavior: Config startup validates each origin is a well-formed URL with scheme and hostname. Fail on any malformed value. Files: config.py 17. Data volume mounted inside application directory — OWASP A05 (Medium) The SQLite volume is mounted at data, commingling runtime data with application code. Correct behavior: Mount data volumes outside the application root (e.g., /var/lib/ghchat/data). Files: docker-compose.yml 18. Chat history stored unencrypted and indefinitely in localStorage — Privacy / OWASP A02 (Medium) Full message content is persisted to localStorage with no expiration, survives logout, and is readable by any XSS. Correct behavior: Store only lightweight references (message IDs) locally with a TTL. Load content from backend on demand. Clear all local data on logout. Files: useChatHistory.ts 19. GraphQL error messages expose internal details — OWASP A09 (Medium) Raw error messages from the GitHub GraphQL API are surfaced as internal exceptions without sanitization, potentially leaking query structure or token scope details. Correct behavior: Log full error internally; raise only a generic sanitized message toward the API response. Files: service.py Phase 4 — Low (Backlog) 20. GitHub Actions workflow has broad issues: write permission — Supply Chain (Low) Correct behavior: Scope to minimum permission needed; add a justification comment. Files: branch-issue-link.yml 21. Avatar URLs rendered without domain validation — OWASP A03 (Low) External avatar URLs from the GitHub API are used in without validating protocol or hostname. Correct behavior: Validate URLs use https: and originate from a known GitHub avatar domain. Fall back to a placeholder on validation failure. Files: IssueCard.tsx Verification (Behavior-Based) # Check 1 After login, no credentials appear in browser URL bar, history, or access logs 2 Backend refuses to start in non-debug mode without ENCRYPTION_KEY set 3 docker exec into frontend container — id must return non-root UID 4 Authenticated request with unowned project_id returns 403, not success 5 WebSocket connection to an unowned project ID is rejected before any data is sent 6 All webhook secret comparisons use constant-time function (code review) 7 curl -I frontend returns Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy; no nginx version in Server: header 8 After rate limit threshold, expensive endpoints return 429 Too Many Requests 9 After logout, localStorage contains no message content (browser devtools) 10 DB directory permissions are 0700; file permissions are 0600 Key Decisions OAuth scope removal (step 8): May break write operations. Test in staging; users must re-authorize after scope change. Encryption enforcement (step 2): Breaking change for deployments without a key. Migration path for existing plaintext rows must be included in the same change. Rate limiting: Per-user limits preferred over per-IP to avoid penalizing shared NAT/VPN users. Out of scope: GitHub API security, MCP server internals, network-layer infrastructure. --- ## 🤖 Agent Pipeline | # | Status | Agent | State | |---|--------|-------|-------| | 1 | Backlog | `speckit.specify` | ✅ Done | | 2 | Ready | `speckit.plan` | ✅ Done | | 3 | Ready | `speckit.tasks` | ✅ Done | | 4 | In Progress | `speckit.implement` | ✅ Done | | 5 | In Review | `copilot-review` | ✅ Done | | 6 | In Review | `linter` | ✅ Done | | 7 | In Review | `judge` | ✅ Done | | 8 | In Review | `human` | 🔄 Active |

mentioned_issues.body:
## Bug Bash: Full Codebase Review & Fix

### Objective
Perform a comprehensive bug bash code review of the **entire codebase**. Identify bugs, fix them, and ensure fixes are validated by tests.

### Scope — Review Categories
Audit every file in the repository for the following bug categories, in priority order:

1. **Security vulnerabilities** — auth bypasses, injection risks, secrets/tokens exposed in code or config, insecure defaults, improper input validation
2. **Runtime errors** — unhandled exceptions, race conditions, null/None references, missing imports, type errors, file handle leaks, database connection leaks
3. **Logic bugs** — incorrect state transitions, wrong API calls, off-by-one errors, data inconsistencies, broken control flow, incorrect return values
4. **Test gaps & test quality** — untested code paths, tests that pass for the wrong reason, mock leaks (e.g., `MagicMock` objects leaking into production paths like database file paths), assertions that never fail, missing edge case coverage
5. **Code quality issues** — dead code, unreachable branches, duplicated logic, hardcoded values that should be configurable, missing error messages, silent failures

### Actions Required

**For obvious/clear bugs:**
- Fix the bug directly in the source code.
- Update any existing tests that are affected by the fix.
- Add at least one new regression test per bug to ensure it does not reoccur.
- Write a clear commit message explaining: what the bug was, why it's a bug, and how the fix resolves it.

**For ambiguous or trade-off situations:**
- Do NOT make the change.
- Instead, add a `# TODO(bug-bash):` comment at the relevant location describing the issue, the options, and why it needs a human decision.
- Include these in a summary (see Output below).

### Validation
After all fixes are applied:
1. Run `pytest` and ensure the full test suite passes (including all new regression tests).
2. Run any existing linting/formatting checks if configured (e.g., `flake8`, `black`, `ruff`).
3. Do not commit if tests fail — iterate on the fix until green.

### Output
At the end, provide a single summary comment with:

| # | File | Line(s) | Category | Description | Status |
|---|------|---------|----------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | `path/to/file.py` | 42-45 | Security | Description of bug | ✅ Fixed |
| 2 | `path/to/file.py` | 100 | Logic | Description of ambiguity | ⚠️ Flagged (TODO) |

- **✅ Fixed** — bug was resolved, tests added, all passing
- **⚠️ Flagged (TODO)** — ambiguous issue left as `TODO(bug-bash)` comment for human review

### Constraints
- Do not change the project's architecture or public API surface.
- Do not add new dependencies.
- Preserve existing code style and patterns.
- Each fix should be minimal and focused — no drive-by refactors.
- If a file has no bugs, skip it — don't mention it in the summary.

mentioned_issues.title: Security Review
mentioned_issues.body: Plan: Security, Privacy & Vulnerability Audit 3 Critical · 8 High · 9 Medium · 2 Low — across OWASP Top 10. Findings describe the vulnerable pattern/behavior, not tied to specific function or line numbers. Phase 1 — Critical (Fix Immediately) 1. Session token passed in URL — OWASP A02 (Critical) The OAuth flow redirects the browser to the frontend with ?session_token=... in the URL. Tokens in URLs are recorded in browser history, server/proxy/CDN access logs, and HTTP Referer headers. Correct behavior: Backend sets an HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Secure cookie directly on the OAuth callback response and redirects with no credentials in the URL. Frontend must never read credentials from URL params. Files: auth.py, useAuth.ts 2. At-rest encryption not enforced — OWASP A02 (Critical) ENCRYPTION_KEY is optional; when absent the app logs a warning and stores OAuth tokens in plaintext SQLite. Correct behavior: On startup in non-debug mode, the application must refuse to start if ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set. Also apply the same mandatory rule to GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Files: config.py, encryption.py 3. Frontend container runs as root — OWASP A05 (Critical) The frontend Dockerfile has no USER directive; nginx runs as uid=0. The backend already runs non-root. Correct behavior: All containers must run as a dedicated non-root system user. Files: Dockerfile Phase 2 — High (This Week) 4. Project resources not scoped to authenticated user — OWASP A01 (High) Endpoints that accept a project_id (task creation, WebSocket subscription, project settings, workflow operations) do not verify the authenticated user owns that project. Any authenticated user can target any project by guessing its ID. Correct behavior: Every endpoint accepting a project identifier must verify the session has access to that project before performing any action. Centralize this check as a shared dependency. Files: tasks.py, projects.py, settings.py, workflow.py 5. Timing attack on Signal webhook — OWASP A07 (High) Signal webhook secret comparison uses standard string equality (!=), which leaks timing information. The GitHub webhook already uses hmac.compare_digest correctly. Correct behavior: All secret/token comparisons throughout the codebase must use constant-time comparison. Files: signal.py 6. Missing HTTP security headers in nginx — OWASP A05 (High) Only basic headers are set. Missing: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. The present X-XSS-Protection is deprecated in modern browsers. Correct behavior: Add all five headers; remove X-XSS-Protection; set server_tokens off to hide nginx version. Files: nginx.conf 7. Dev endpoint accepts GitHub PAT in URL — OWASP A02 (High) The dev login endpoint receives a GitHub Personal Access Token as a URL query parameter. Correct behavior: All credential inputs, even dev-only, must arrive in the POST request body (JSON), never in the URL. Files: auth.py 8. OAuth requests overly broad repo scope — OWASP A01 (High) The app requests the repo scope, which grants full read/write access to all private repositories. Only project management access is needed. Correct behavior: Request minimum necessary scopes. Test that all write operations work with narrower scopes before removing repo. Files: github_auth.py 9. Session secret key has no minimum entropy check — OWASP A07 (High) SESSION_SECRET_KEY is accepted at any length with no validation. Correct behavior: Startup must reject keys shorter than 64 characters. Files: config.py 10. Docker services bound to all network interfaces — OWASP A05 (High) Backend and frontend ports are bound to 0.0.0.0, exposing them on all interfaces. Correct behavior: Development: bind to 127.0.0.1 only. Production: expose only via a reverse proxy, not directly via container ports. Files: docker-compose.yml Phase 3 — Medium (Next Sprint) 11. No rate limiting on expensive/sensitive endpoints — OWASP A04 (Medium) Chat, agent invocation, workflow, and OAuth callback endpoints have no per-user or per-IP rate limits. A single user can exhaust shared AI/GitHub quotas. Correct behavior: Per-user limits on write/AI endpoints; per-IP limit on OAuth callback. slowapi (FastAPI-compatible) is the recommended library. Files: chat.py, agents.py, workflow.py, auth.py 12. Cookie Secure flag not enforced in production — OWASP A02 (Medium) cookie_secure defaults to False and relies on indirect URL-prefix detection to enable it — fragile and silently misconfigures. Correct behavior: Startup in non-debug mode must fail if cookies are not configured as Secure. Files: config.py 13. Debug mode bypasses webhook signature verification — OWASP A05 (Medium) When DEBUG=true and no webhook secret is set, signature verification is skipped. If debug mode is accidentally on in production, unauthenticated callers can trigger workflows. Correct behavior: Webhook verification must never be conditional on debug mode. Developers use a locally configured test secret. Files: webhooks.py 14. API docs exposed when debug is enabled — OWASP A05 (Medium) Swagger/ReDoc availability is gated on DEBUG, not a dedicated toggle. If debug is on in production, full API schema is public. Correct behavior: Gate on a separate ENABLE_DOCS environment variable, independent of DEBUG. Files: main.py 15. SQLite database directory is world-readable — OWASP A02 (Medium) Database directory is created with default 0755 permissions; any process on the container can read the DB file. Correct behavior: Create directory with 0700, database file with 0600. Only the application user needs access. Files: database.py 16. CORS origins configuration not validated — OWASP A05 (Medium) The comma-separated CORS origins env var is parsed with no URL format validation. Typos silently pass. Correct behavior: Config startup validates each origin is a well-formed URL with scheme and hostname. Fail on any malformed value. Files: config.py 17. Data volume mounted inside application directory — OWASP A05 (Medium) The SQLite volume is mounted at data, commingling runtime data with application code. Correct behavior: Mount data volumes outside the application root (e.g., /var/lib/ghchat/data). Files: docker-compose.yml 18. Chat history stored unencrypted and indefinitely in localStorage — Privacy / OWASP A02 (Medium) Full message content is persisted to localStorage with no expiration, survives logout, and is readable by any XSS. Correct behavior: Store only lightweight references (message IDs) locally with a TTL. Load content from backend on demand. Clear all local data on logout. Files: useChatHistory.ts 19. GraphQL error messages expose internal details — OWASP A09 (Medium) Raw error messages from the GitHub GraphQL API are surfaced as internal exceptions without sanitization, potentially leaking query structure or token scope details. Correct behavior: Log full error internally; raise only a generic sanitized message toward the API response. Files: service.py Phase 4 — Low (Backlog) 20. GitHub Actions workflow has broad issues: write permission — Supply Chain (Low) Correct behavior: Scope to minimum permission needed; add a justification comment. Files: branch-issue-link.yml 21. Avatar URLs rendered without domain validation — OWASP A03 (Low) External avatar URLs from the GitHub API are used in without validating protocol or hostname. Correct behavior: Validate URLs use https: and originate from a known GitHub avatar domain. Fall back to a placeholder on validation failure. Files: IssueCard.tsx Verification (Behavior-Based) # Check 1 After login, no credentials appear in browser URL bar, history, or access logs 2 Backend refuses to start in non-debug mode without ENCRYPTION_KEY set 3 docker exec into frontend container — id must return non-root UID 4 Authenticated request with unowned project_id returns 403, not success 5 WebSocket connection to an unowned project ID is rejected before any data is sent 6 All webhook secret comparisons use constant-time function (code review) 7 curl -I frontend returns Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy; no nginx version in Server: header 8 After rate limit threshold, expensive endpoints return 429 Too Many Requests 9 After logout, localStorage contains no message content (browser devtools) 10 DB directory permissions are 0700; file permissions are 0600 Key Decisions OAuth scope removal (step 8): May break write operations. Test in staging; users must re-authorize after scope change. Encryption enforcement (step 2): Breaking change for deployments without a key. Migration path for existing plaintext rows must be included in the same change. Rate limiting: Per-user limits preferred over per-IP to avoid penalizing shared NAT/VPN users. Out of scope: GitHub API security, MCP server internals, network-layer infrastructure. --- ## 🤖 Agent Pipeline | # | Status | Agent | State | |---|--------|-------|-------| | 1 | Backlog | `speckit.specify` | ✅ Done | | 2 | Ready | `speckit.plan` | ✅ Done | | 3 | Ready | `speckit.tasks` | ✅ Done | | 4 | In Progress | `speckit.implement` | ✅ Done | | 5 | In Review | `copilot-review` | ✅ Done | | 6 | In Review | `linter` | ✅ Done | | 7 | In Review | `judge` | ✅ Done | | 8 | In Review | `human` | 🔄 Active |

5. **Code quality issues** — dead code, unreachable branches, duplicated logic, hardcoded values that should be configurable, missing error messages, silent failures

### Actions Required

**For obvious/clear bugs:**
- Fix the bug directly in the source code.
- Update any existing tests that are affected by the fix.
- Add at least one new regression test per bug to ensure it does not reoccur.
- Write a clear commit message explaining: what the bug was, why it's a bug, and how the fix resolves it.

**For ambiguous or trade-off situations:**
- Do NOT make the change.
- Instead, add a `# TODO(bug-bash):` comment at the relevant location describing the issue, the options, and why it needs a human decision.
- Include these in a summary (see Output below).

### Validation
After all fixes are applied:
1. Run `pytest` and ensure the full test suite passes (including all new regression tests).
2. Run any existing linting/formatting checks if configured (e.g., `flake8`, `black`, `ruff`).
3. Do not commit if tests fail — iterate on the fix until green.

### Output
At the end, provide a single summary comment with:

| # | File | Line(s) | Category | Description | Status |
|---|------|---------|----------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | `path/to/file.py` | 42-45 | Security | Description of bug | ✅ Fixed |
| 2 | `path/to/file.py` | 100 | Logic | Description of ambiguity | ⚠️ Flagged (TODO) |

- **✅ Fixed** — bug was resolved, tests added, all passing
- **⚠️ Flagged (TODO)** — ambiguous issue left as `TODO(bug-bash)` comment for human review

- Do not change the project's architecture or public API surface.
- Do not add new dependencies.
- Preserve existing code style and patterns.
- Each fix should be minimal and focused — no drive-by refactors.
- If a file has no bugs, skip it — don't mention it in the summary.

mentioned_issues.title: Security Review
mentioned_issues.body: Plan: Security, Privacy & Vulnerability Audit 3 Critical · 8 High · 9 Medium · 2 Low — across OWASP Top 10. Findings describe the vulnerable pattern/behavior, not tied to specific function or line numbers. Phase 1 — Critical (Fix Immediately) 1. Session token passed in URL — OWASP A02 (Critical) The OAuth flow redirects the browser to the frontend with ?session_token=... in the URL. Tokens in URLs are recorded in browser history, server/proxy/CDN access logs, and HTTP Referer headers. Correct behavior: Backend sets an HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Secure cookie directly on the OAuth callback response and redirects with no credentials in the URL. Frontend must never read credentials from URL params. Files: auth.py, useAuth.ts 2. At-rest encryption not enforced — OWASP A02 (Critical) ENCRYPTION_KEY is optional; when absent the app logs a warning and stores OAuth tokens in plaintext SQLite. Correct behavior: On startup in non-debug mode, the application must refuse to start if ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set. Also apply the same mandatory rule to GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Files: config.py, encryption.py 3. Frontend container runs as root — OWASP A05 (Critical) The frontend Dockerfile has no USER directive; nginx runs as uid=0. The backend already runs non-root. Correct behavior: All containers must run as a dedicated non-root system user. Files: Dockerfile Phase 2 — High (This Week) 4. Project resources not scoped to authenticated user — OWASP A01 (High) Endpoints that accept a project_id (task creation, WebSocket subscription, project settings, workflow operations) do not verify the authenticated user owns that project. Any authenticated user can target any project by guessing its ID. Correct behavior: Every endpoint accepting a project identifier must verify the session has access to that project before performing any action. Centralize this check as a shared dependency. Files: tasks.py, projects.py, settings.py, workflow.py 5. Timing attack on Signal webhook — OWASP A07 (High) Signal webhook secret comparison uses standard string equality (!=), which leaks timing information. The GitHub webhook already uses hmac.compare_digest correctly. Correct behavior: All secret/token comparisons throughout the codebase must use constant-time comparison. Files: signal.py 6. Missing HTTP security headers in nginx — OWASP A05 (High) Only basic headers are set. Missing: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. The present X-XSS-Protection is deprecated in modern browsers. Correct behavior: Add all five headers; remove X-XSS-Protection; set server_tokens off to hide nginx version. Files: nginx.conf 7. Dev endpoint accepts GitHub PAT in URL — OWASP A02 (High) The dev login endpoint receives a GitHub Personal Access Token as a URL query parameter. Correct behavior: All credential inputs, even dev-only, must arrive in the POST request body (JSON), never in the URL. Files: auth.py 8. OAuth requests overly broad repo scope — OWASP A01 (High) The app requests the repo scope, which grants full read/write access to all private repositories. Only project management access is needed. Correct behavior: Request minimum necessary scopes. Test that all write operations work with narrower scopes before removing repo. Files: github_auth.py 9. Session secret key has no minimum entropy check — OWASP A07 (High) SESSION_SECRET_KEY is accepted at any length with no validation. Correct behavior: Startup must reject keys shorter than 64 characters. Files: config.py 10. Docker services bound to all network interfaces — OWASP A05 (High) Backend and frontend ports are bound to 0.0.0.0, exposing them on all interfaces. Correct behavior: Development: bind to 127.0.0.1 only. Production: expose only via a reverse proxy, not directly via container ports. Files: docker-compose.yml Phase 3 — Medium (Next Sprint) 11. No rate limiting on expensive/sensitive endpoints — OWASP A04 (Medium) Chat, agent invocation, workflow, and OAuth callback endpoints have no per-user or per-IP rate limits. A single user can exhaust shared AI/GitHub quotas. Correct behavior: Per-user limits on write/AI endpoints; per-IP limit on OAuth callback. slowapi (FastAPI-compatible) is the recommended library. Files: chat.py, agents.py, workflow.py, auth.py 12. Cookie Secure flag not enforced in production — OWASP A02 (Medium) cookie_secure defaults to False and relies on indirect URL-prefix detection to enable it — fragile and silently misconfigures. Correct behavior: Startup in non-debug mode must fail if cookies are not configured as Secure. Files: config.py 13. Debug mode bypasses webhook signature verification — OWASP A05 (Medium) When DEBUG=true and no webhook secret is set, signature verification is skipped. If debug mode is accidentally on in production, unauthenticated callers can trigger workflows. Correct behavior: Webhook verification must never be conditional on debug mode. Developers use a locally configured test secret. Files: webhooks.py 14. API docs exposed when debug is enabled — OWASP A05 (Medium) Swagger/ReDoc availability is gated on DEBUG, not a dedicated toggle. If debug is on in production, full API schema is public. Correct behavior: Gate on a separate ENABLE_DOCS environment variable, independent of DEBUG. Files: main.py 15. SQLite database directory is world-readable — OWASP A02 (Medium) Database directory is created with default 0755 permissions; any process on the container can read the DB file. Correct behavior: Create directory with 0700, database file with 0600. Only the application user needs access. Files: database.py 16. CORS origins configuration not validated — OWASP A05 (Medium) The comma-separated CORS origins env var is parsed with no URL format validation. Typos silently pass. Correct behavior: Config startup validates each origin is a well-formed URL with scheme and hostname. Fail on any malformed value. Files: config.py 17. Data volume mounted inside application directory — OWASP A05 (Medium) The SQLite volume is mounted at data, commingling runtime data with application code. Correct behavior: Mount data volumes outside the application root (e.g., /var/lib/ghchat/data). Files: docker-compose.yml 18. Chat history stored unencrypted and indefinitely in localStorage — Privacy / OWASP A02 (Medium) Full message content is persisted to localStorage with no expiration, survives logout, and is readable by any XSS. Correct behavior: Store only lightweight references (message IDs) locally with a TTL. Load content from backend on demand. Clear all local data on logout. Files: useChatHistory.ts 19. GraphQL error messages expose internal details — OWASP A09 (Medium) Raw error messages from the GitHub GraphQL API are surfaced as internal exceptions without sanitization, potentially leaking query structure or token scope details. Correct behavior: Log full error internally; raise only a generic sanitized message toward the API response. Files: service.py Phase 4 — Low (Backlog) 20. GitHub Actions workflow has broad issues: write permission — Supply Chain (Low) Correct behavior: Scope to minimum permission needed; add a justification comment. Files: branch-issue-link.yml 21. Avatar URLs rendered without domain validation — OWASP A03 (Low) External avatar URLs from the GitHub API are used in without validating protocol or hostname. Correct behavior: Validate URLs use https: and originate from a known GitHub avatar domain. Fall back to a placeholder on validation failure. Files: IssueCard.tsx Verification (Behavior-Based) # Check 1 After login, no credentials appear in browser URL bar, history, or access logs 2 Backend refuses to start in non-debug mode without ENCRYPTION_KEY set 3 docker exec into frontend container — id must return non-root UID 4 Authenticated request with unowned project_id returns 403, not success 5 WebSocket connection to an unowned project ID is rejected before any data is sent 6 All webhook secret comparisons use constant-time function (code review) 7 curl -I frontend returns Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy; no nginx version in Server: header 8 After rate limit threshold, expensive endpoints return 429 Too Many Requests 9 After logout, localStorage contains no message content (browser devtools) 10 DB directory permissions are 0700; file permissions are 0600 Key Decisions OAuth scope removal (step 8): May break write operations. Test in staging; users must re-authorize after scope change. Encryption enforcement (step 2): Breaking change for deployments without a key. Migration path for existing plaintext rows must be included in the same change. Rate limiting: Per-user limits preferred over per-IP to avoid penalizing shared NAT/VPN users. Out of scope: GitHub API security, MCP server internals, network-layer infrastructure. --- ## 🤖 Agent Pipeline | # | Status | Agent | State | |---|--------|-------|-------| | 1 | Backlog | `speckit.specify` | ✅ Done | | 2 | Ready | `speckit.plan` | ✅ Done | | 3 | Ready | `speckit.tasks` | ✅ Done | | 4 | In Progress | `speckit.implement` | ✅ Done | | 5 | In Review | `copilot-review` | ✅ Done | | 6 | In Review | `linter` | ✅ Done | | 7 | In Review | `judge` | ✅ Done | | 8 | In Review | `human` | 🔄 Active |

mentioned_issues.body: > **Parent Issue:** #1905 — Security Review ## 🤖 Agent Task: `linter` Complete the work assigned to the `linter` agent. --- ## Parent Issue Context Plan: Security, Privacy & Vulnerability Audit 3 Critical · 8 High · 9 Medium · 2 Low — across OWASP Top 10. Findings describe the vulnerable pattern/behavior, not tied to specific function or line numbers. Phase 1 — Critical (Fix Immediately) 1. Session token passed in URL — OWASP A02 (Critical) The OAuth flow redirects the browser to the frontend with ?session_token=... in the URL. Tokens in URLs are recorded in browser history, server/proxy/CDN access logs, and HTTP Referer headers. Correct behavior: Backend sets an HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Secure cookie directly on the OAuth callback response and redirects with no credentials in the URL. Frontend must never read credentials from URL params. Files: auth.py, useAuth.ts 2. At-rest encryption not enforced — OWASP A02 (Critical) ENCRYPTION_KEY is optional; when absent the app logs a warning and stores OAuth tokens in plaintext SQLite. Correct behavior: On startup in non-debug mode, the application must refuse to start if ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set. Also apply the same mandatory rule to GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Files: config.py, encryption.py 3. Frontend container runs as root — OWASP A05 (Critical) The frontend Dockerfile has no USER directive; nginx runs as uid=0. The backend already runs non-root. Correct behavior: All containers must run as a dedicated non-root system user. Files: Dockerfile Phase 2 — High (This Week) 4. Project resources not scoped to authenticated user — OWASP A01 (High) Endpoints that accept a project_id (task creation, WebSocket subscription, project settings, workflow operations) do not verify the authenticated user owns that project. Any authenticated user can target any project by guessing its ID. Correct behavior: Every endpoint accepting a project identifier must verify the session has access to that project before performing any action. Centralize this check as a shared dependency. Files: tasks.py, projects.py, settings.py, workflow.py 5. Timing attack on Signal webhook — OWASP A07 (High) Signal webhook secret comparison uses standard string equality (!=), which leaks timing information. The GitHub webhook already uses hmac.compare_digest correctly. Correct behavior: All secret/token comparisons throughout the codebase must use constant-time comparison. Files: signal.py 6. Missing HTTP security headers in nginx — OWASP A05 (High) Only basic headers are set. Missing: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. The present X-XSS-Protection is deprecated in modern browsers. Correct behavior: Add all five headers; remove X-XSS-Protection; set server_tokens off to hide nginx version. Files: nginx.conf 7. Dev endpoint accepts GitHub PAT in URL — OWASP A02 (High) The dev login endpoint receives a GitHub Personal Access Token as a URL query parameter. Correct behavior: All credential inputs, even dev-only, must arrive in the POST request body (JSON), never in the URL. Files: auth.py 8. OAuth requests overly broad repo scope — OWASP A01 (High) The app requests the repo scope, which grants full read/write access to all private repositories. Only project management access is needed. Correct behavior: Request minimum necessary scopes. Test that all write operations work with narrower scopes before removing repo. Files: github_auth.py 9. Session secret key has no minimum entropy check — OWASP A07 (High) SESSION_SECRET_KEY is accepted at any length with no validation. Correct behavior: Startup must reject keys shorter than 64 characters. Files: config.py 10. Docker services bound to all network interfaces — OWASP A05 (High) Backend and frontend ports are bound to 0.0.0.0, exposing them on all interfaces. Correct behavior: Development: bind to 127.0.0.1 only. Production: expose only via a reverse proxy, not directly via container ports. Files: docker-compose.yml Phase 3 — Medium (Next Sprint) 11. No rate limiting on expensive/sensitive endpoints — OWASP A04 (Medium) Chat, agent invocation, workflow, and OAuth callback endpoints have no per-user or per-IP rate limits. A single user can exhaust shared AI/GitHub quotas. Correct behavior: Per-user limits on write/AI endpoints; per-IP limit on OAuth callback. slowapi (FastAPI-compatible) is the recommended library. Files: chat.py, agents.py, workflow.py, auth.py 12. Correct behavior: Startup in non-debug mode must fail if cookies are not configured as Secure. Files: config.py 13. Debug mode bypasses webhook signature verification — OWASP A05 (Medium) When DEBUG=true and no webhook secret is set, signature verification is skipped. If debug mode is accidentally on in production, unauthenticated callers can trigger workflows. Correct behavior: Webhook verification must never be conditional on debug mode. Developers use a locally configured test secret. Files: webhooks.py 14. API docs exposed when debug is enabled — OWASP A05 (Medium) Swagger/ReDoc availability is gated on DEBUG, not a dedicated toggle. If debug is on in production, full API schema is public. Correct behavior: Gate on a separate ENABLE_DOCS environment variable, independent of DEBUG. Files: main.py 15. SQLite database directory is world-readable — OWASP A02 (Medium) Database directory is created with default 0755 permissions; any process on the container can read the DB file. Correct behavior: Create directory with 0700, database file with 0600. Only the application user needs access. Files: database.py 16. Correct behavior: Config startup validates each origin is a well-formed URL with scheme and hostname. Fail on any malformed value. Files: config.py 17. Data volume mounted inside application directory — OWASP A05 (Medium) The SQLite volume is mounted at data, commingling runtime data with application code. Correct behavior: Mount data volumes outside the application root (e.g., /var/lib/ghchat/data). Files: docker-compose.yml 18. Chat history stored unencrypted and indefinitely in localStorage — Privacy / OWASP A02 (Medium) Full message content is persisted to localStorage with no expiration, survives logout, and is readable by any XSS. Correct behavior: Store only lightweight references (message IDs) locally with a TTL. Load content from backend on demand. Clear all local data on logout. Files: useChatHistory.ts 19. mentioned_issues.title: Security Review
mentioned_issues.body: Plan: Security, Privacy & Vulnerability Audit 3 Critical · 8 High · 9 Medium · 2 Low — across OWASP Top 10. Session token passed in URL — OWASP A02 (Critical) The OAuth flow redirects the browser to the frontend with ?session_token=... in the URL. Tokens in URLs are recorded in browser history, server/proxy/CDN access logs, and HTTP Referer headers. Correct behavior: Backend sets an HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Secure cookie directly on the OAuth callback response and redirects with no credentials in the URL. Frontend must never read credentials from URL params. Files: auth.py, useAuth.ts 2. At-rest encryption not enforced — OWASP A02 (Critical) ENCRYPTION_KEY is optional; when absent the app logs a warning and stores OAuth tokens in plaintext SQLite. Correct behavior: On startup in non-debug mode, the application must refuse to start if ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set. Also apply the same mandatory rule to GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Files: config.py, encryption.py 3. Frontend container runs as root — OWASP A05 (Critical) The frontend Dockerfile has no USER directive; nginx runs as uid=0. The backend already runs non-root. Correct behavior: All containers must run as a dedicated non-root system user. Files: Dockerfile Phase 2 — High (This Week) 4. closing_issues.title: Fix #help Command Auto-Repeat Bug & Add Optimistic Message Rendering in Chat UI
closing_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Debug chat. I entered #help once and now it keeps sending it automatically as a reply to the chat agent.
> 
> Also, when a user sends a chat message, it should be displayed immediately in the chat UI, then the chat agent can "think" if processing time is needed.

## User Story

As a Solune chat user, I want the `#help` command (and any special commands) to send only once without being replayed automatically on subsequent messages, and I want my sent messages to appear in the chat UI immediately upon submission so that the conversation feels responsive and I'm not left wondering if my message was received while the agent is processing.

## UI/UX Description

The chat input area must clear and display the user's message in the conversation thread the instant they hit send — before any agent response or thinking state begins. A visual 'thinking' indicator (e.g., animated ellipsis or spinner bubble) should appear below the user's message to signal the agent is processing. For the #help bug: the special `#help` command (and any slash/hash commands) must be treated as one-time actions that do not persist in any input state, reply context, or message queue. There should be no residual state from a previously sent command that causes it to be re-injected into future messages. If a command is pending or being replayed erroneously, the UI should not show stale command text in the input field or as a pre-filled reply.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST clear any stored command state (including `#help` and all hash/slash commands) immediately after the command is dispatched, preventing it from being re-sent or auto-appended to subsequent messages.
- System MUST audit and reset the chat input field, reply context, and any message queue state upon successful message dispatch to eliminate stale command replay.
- System MUST display the user's sent message in the chat conversation UI immediately upon submission (optimistic rendering), before awaiting any response from the chat agent.
- System MUST show a 'thinking' or processing indicator (e.g., animated typing bubble) in the chat UI after the user's message appears, persisting until the agent response is received.
- System MUST remove the thinking indicator and render the agent's response once the processing is complete, replacing the placeholder without causing layout shifts.
- System SHOULD handle failure cases for optimistic messages — if the message fails to send, it must be visually marked as failed with a retry option, not silently dropped.
- System MUST ensure that special commands like `#help` do not get injected into the reply-to or context payload of any subsequent chat message after their initial dispatch.
- System SHOULD include regression test coverage for the `#help` auto-repeat scenario to prevent recurrence of command state leaking across message sends.

## Technical Notes

The `#help` auto-repeat bug is likely caused by command state (or a reply/context reference) not being cleared after dispatch — inspect the chat state manager, message composer reducer, and any reply-context or pending-command queues for stale references that survive after send. For optimistic UI, implement an optimistic message append pattern: add the user's message to the local chat state immediately on submit with a `pending` status, then update to `sent` or `failed` upon server acknowledgment. Ensure the chat agent 'thinking' state is triggered only after the optimistic message is rendered. Use a unique temporary ID for the optimistic message to reconcile it with the server-confirmed message. Review any middleware or interceptors that process outgoing messages for unintentional command re-injection.

closing_issues.title: Pipeline Page: CRUD for Agent Pipeline Configurations with Model Selection and Saved Workflow Management
closing_issues.body:
## Original Request

> On the pipeline page, I want the user to be able to CRUD Agent Pipeline configurations.
> 
> They should also be able to select the agent model for each agent, be smart with the UI/UX here.
> 
> Saved Agent workflows should be displayed on the bottom, when selected it goes into edit mode for the user, populating the Agent Pipeline board and stages.

## User Story

As a user on the pipeline page, I want to create, read, update, and delete Agent Pipeline configurations — including selecting the specific agent model for each individual agent in the pipeline — so that I can build, save, and revisit customized agent workflows. I also want my saved workflows listed at the bottom of the page so I can quickly select one to load it into the pipeline board in edit mode, with all stages and agent settings fully restored.

## UI/UX Description

The pipeline page consists of two primary zones: (1) an interactive Agent Pipeline Board at the top/center where users configure a pipeline by adding, arranging, and editing stages and agents; each agent node/card on the board exposes a model selector (e.g., a compact dropdown or popover with a model list) inline or via a side panel — model selection UI should be context-aware, grouping models by provider or capability and showing relevant metadata (e.g., context size, cost tier) to aid decision-making. A persistent toolbar provides Create/Save/Delete/Discard actions with clear enabled/disabled states. (2) A Saved Workflows section at the bottom of the page displays previously saved pipeline configurations as cards or rows (showing pipeline name, last modified date, agent count, and a brief description if available); clicking a saved workflow card transitions the board into Edit Mode, loading all pipeline stages, agent assignments, and model selections into the board — a visual indicator (e.g., banner or highlighted header) communicates that the user is editing an existing workflow. Unsaved changes should trigger a confirmation dialog before navigating away or loading another workflow. The board should support drag-and-drop stage reordering and inline renaming. Empty states for both the board and the saved workflows list should include clear CTAs.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST allow users to create a new Agent Pipeline configuration from the pipeline page, including naming the pipeline and adding one or more stages with assigned agents.
- System MUST allow users to select an agent model for each individual agent within a pipeline stage, presenting a model picker UI that displays available models grouped logically (e.g., by provider or capability tier).
- System MUST allow users to save (persist) a configured Agent Pipeline, updating an existing record on edit or creating a new record on first save.
- System MUST allow users to update/edit any previously saved Agent Pipeline configuration by selecting it from the Saved Workflows section, which loads the full pipeline board and all stage/agent/model data into edit mode.
- System MUST allow users to delete a saved Agent Pipeline configuration, with a confirmation prompt before permanent removal.
- System MUST display all saved Agent Pipeline workflows in a dedicated section at the bottom of the pipeline page, showing at minimum the pipeline name, last modified date, and agent/stage count per entry.
- System MUST populate the Agent Pipeline board and all its stages, agents, and model selections when a saved workflow is selected, transitioning the UI into edit mode with a clear visual indicator.
- System MUST prompt the user to confirm or discard unsaved changes when they attempt to load a different saved workflow or navigate away from an in-progress configuration.
- System SHOULD display an empty state with a call-to-action in the Saved Workflows section when no pipelines have been saved yet.
- System SHOULD disable or hide destructive actions (e.g., Delete) contextually when no workflow is selected or when the board is in a pristine new-pipeline state.

## Technical Notes

The Agent Pipeline board likely needs a graph or stage-based state model (e.g., a list of stage objects, each containing an array of agent objects with agentId, modelId, and config fields); this state should be serializable to JSON for persistence. Model selection per agent should fetch available models from an existing models API or config and cache results to avoid redundant requests — consider a reusable ModelSelector component that can be embedded inline on agent cards. The Saved Workflows section should paginate or virtualize if the list grows large; use optimistic UI updates for delete/save actions with rollback on failure. Edit mode vs. new mode should be tracked in local/component state (e.g., editingWorkflowId: string | null), and route or URL state may be used to deep-link to a specific workflow. Ensure CRUD operations map to well-defined API endpoints (e.g., GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/pipelines/:id) and that the agent-config label scope is respected for any configuration schema changes.

mentioned_issues.title: Security Review
mentioned_issues.body: Plan: Security, Privacy & Vulnerability Audit 3 Critical · 8 High · 9 Medium · 2 Low — across OWASP Top 10. Findings describe the vulnerable pattern/behavior, not tied to specific function or line numbers. Phase 1 — Critical (Fix Immediately) 1. Session token passed in URL — OWASP A02 (Critical) The OAuth flow redirects the browser to the frontend with ?session_token=... in the URL. Tokens in URLs are recorded in browser history, server/proxy/CDN access logs, and HTTP Referer headers. Correct behavior: Backend sets an HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Secure cookie directly on the OAuth callback response and redirects with no credentials in the URL. Frontend must never read credentials from URL params. Files: auth.py, useAuth.ts 2. At-rest encryption not enforced — OWASP A02 (Critical) ENCRYPTION_KEY is optional; when absent the app logs a warning and stores OAuth tokens in plaintext SQLite. Correct behavior: On startup in non-debug mode, the application must refuse to start if ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set. Also apply the same mandatory rule to GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Files: config.py, encryption.py 3. Frontend container runs as root — OWASP A05 (Critical) The frontend Dockerfile has no USER directive; nginx runs as uid=0. The backend already runs non-root. Correct behavior: All containers must run as a dedicated non-root system user. Files: Dockerfile Phase 2 — High (This Week) 4. Project resources not scoped to authenticated user — OWASP A01 (High) Endpoints that accept a project_id (task creation, WebSocket subscription, project settings, workflow operations) do not verify the authenticated user owns that project. Any authenticated user can target any project by guessing its ID. Correct behavior: Every endpoint accepting a project identifier must verify the session has access to that project before performing any action. Centralize this check as a shared dependency. Files: tasks.py, projects.py, settings.py, workflow.py 5. Timing attack on Signal webhook — OWASP A07 (High) Signal webhook secret comparison uses standard string equality (!=), which leaks timing information. The GitHub webhook already uses hmac.compare_digest correctly. Correct behavior: All secret/token comparisons throughout the codebase must use constant-time comparison. Files: signal.py 6. Missing HTTP security headers in nginx — OWASP A05 (High) Only basic headers are set. Missing: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. The present X-XSS-Protection is deprecated in modern browsers. Correct behavior: Add all five headers; remove X-XSS-Protection; set server_tokens off to hide nginx version. Files: nginx.conf 7. Dev endpoint accepts GitHub PAT in URL — OWASP A02 (High) The dev login endpoint receives a GitHub Personal Access Token as a URL query parameter. Correct behavior: All credential inputs, even dev-only, must arrive in the POST request body (JSON), never in the URL. Files: auth.py 8. OAuth requests overly broad repo scope — OWASP A01 (High) The app requests the repo scope, which grants full read/write access to all private repositories. Only project management access is needed. Correct behavior: Request minimum necessary scopes. Test that all write operations work with narrower scopes before removing repo. Files: github_auth.py 9. Session secret key has no minimum entropy check — OWASP A07 (High) SESSION_SECRET_KEY is accepted at any length with no validation. Correct behavior: Startup must reject keys shorter than 64 characters. Files: config.py 10. Docker services bound to all network interfaces — OWASP A05 (High) Backend and frontend ports are bound to 0.0.0.0, exposing them on all interfaces. Correct behavior: Development: bind to 127.0.0.1 only. Production: expose only via a reverse proxy, not directly via container ports. Files: docker-compose.yml Phase 3 — Medium (Next Sprint) 11. No rate limiting on expensive/sensitive endpoints — OWASP A04 (Medium) Chat, agent invocation, workflow, and OAuth callback endpoints have no per-user or per-IP rate limits. A single user can exhaust shared AI/GitHub quotas. Correct behavior: Per-user limits on write/AI endpoints; per-IP limit on OAuth callback. slowapi (FastAPI-compatible) is the recommended library. Files: chat.py, agents.py, workflow.py, auth.py 12. Cookie Secure flag not enforced in production — OWASP A02 (Medium) cookie_secure defaults to False and relies on indirect URL-prefix detection to enable it — fragile and silently misconfigures. Correct behavior: Startup in non-debug mode must fail if cookies are not configured as Secure. Files: config.py 13. Debug mode bypasses webhook signature verification — OWASP A05 (Medium) When DEBUG=true and no webhook secret is set, signature verification is skipped. If debug mode is accidentally on in production, unauthenticated callers can trigger workflows. Correct behavior: Webhook verification must never be conditional on debug mode. Developers use a locally configured test secret. Files: webhooks.py 14. API docs exposed when debug is enabled — OWASP A05 (Medium) Swagger/ReDoc availability is gated on DEBUG, not a dedicated toggle. If debug is on in production, full API schema is public. Correct behavior: Gate on a separate ENABLE_DOCS environment variable, independent of DEBUG. Files: main.py 15. SQLite database directory is world-readable — OWASP A02 (Medium) Database directory is created with default 0755 permissions; any process on the container can read the DB file. Correct behavior: Create directory with 0700, database file with 0600. Only the application user needs access. Files: database.py 16. CORS origins configuration not validated — OWASP A05 (Medium) The comma-separated CORS origins env var is parsed with no URL format validation. Typos silently pass. Correct behavior: Config startup validates each origin is a well-formed URL with scheme and hostname. Fail on any malformed value. Files: config.py 17. Data volume mounted inside application directory — OWASP A05 (Medium) The SQLite volume is mounted at data, commingling runtime data with application code. Correct behavior: Mount data volumes outside the application root (e.g., /var/lib/ghchat/data). Files: docker-compose.yml 18. Chat history stored unencrypted and indefinitely in localStorage — Privacy / OWASP A02 (Medium) Full message content is persisted to localStorage with no expiration, survives logout, and is readable by any XSS. Correct behavior: Store only lightweight references (message IDs) locally with a TTL. Load content from backend on demand. Clear all local data on logout. Files: useChatHistory.ts 19. GraphQL error messages expose internal details — OWASP A09 (Medium) Raw error messages from the GitHub GraphQL API are surfaced as internal exceptions without sanitization, potentially leaking query structure or token scope details. Correct behavior: Log full error internally; raise only a generic sanitized message toward the API response. Files: service.py Phase 4 — Low (Backlog) 20. GitHub Actions workflow has broad issues: write permission — Supply Chain (Low) Correct behavior: Scope to minimum permission needed; add a justification comment. Files: branch-issue-link.yml 21. Avatar URLs rendered without domain validation — OWASP A03 (Low) External avatar URLs from the GitHub API are used in without validating protocol or hostname. Correct behavior: Validate URLs use https: and originate from a known GitHub avatar domain. Fall back to a placeholder on validation failure. Files: IssueCard.tsx Verification (Behavior-Based) # Check 1 After login, no credentials appear in browser URL bar, history, or access logs 2 Backend refuses to start in non-debug mode without ENCRYPTION_KEY set 3 docker exec into frontend container — id must return non-root UID 4 Authenticated request with unowned project_id returns 403, not success 5 WebSocket connection to an unowned project ID is rejected before any data is sent 6 All webhook secret comparisons use constant-time function (code review) 7 curl -I frontend returns Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy; no nginx version in Server: header 8 After rate limit threshold, expensive endpoints return 429 Too Many Requests 9 After logout, localStorage contains no message content (browser devtools) 10 DB directory permissions are 0700; file permissions are 0600 Key Decisions OAuth scope removal (step 8): May break write operations. Test in staging; users must re-authorize after scope change. Encryption enforcement (step 2): Breaking change for deployments without a key. Migration path for existing plaintext rows must be included in the same change. Rate limiting: Per-user limits preferred over per-IP to avoid penalizing shared NAT/VPN users. Out of scope: GitHub API security, MCP server internals, network-layer infrastructure. --- ## 🤖 Agent Pipeline | # | Status | Agent | State | |---|--------|-------|-------| | 1 | Backlog | `speckit.specify` | ✅ Done | | 2 | Ready | `speckit.plan` | ✅ Done | | 3 | Ready | `speckit.tasks` | ✅ Done | | 4 | In Progress | `speckit.implement` | ✅ Done | | 5 | In Review | `copilot-review` | 🔄 Active | | 6 | In Review | `linter` | ✅ Done | | 7 | In Review | `judge` | ✅ Done | | 8 | In Review | `human` | 🔄 Active |

mentioned_issues.title: Fix #help Command Auto-Repeat Bug & Add Optimistic Message Rendering in Chat UI
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Debug chat. I entered #help once and now it keeps sending it automatically as a reply to the chat agent.
> 
> Also, when a user sends a chat message, it should be displayed immediately in the chat UI, then the chat agent can "think" if processing time is needed.

## User Story

As a Solune chat user, I want the `#help` command (and any special commands) to send only once without being replayed automatically on subsequent messages, and I want my sent messages to appear in the chat UI immediately upon submission so that the conversation feels responsive and I'm not left wondering if my message was received while the agent is processing.

## UI/UX Description

The chat input area must clear and display the user's message in the conversation thread the instant they hit send — before any agent response or thinking state begins. A visual 'thinking' indicator (e.g., animated ellipsis or spinner bubble) should appear below the user's message to signal the agent is processing. For the #help bug: the special `#help` command (and any slash/hash commands) must be treated as one-time actions that do not persist in any input state, reply context, or message queue. There should be no residual state from a previously sent command that causes it to be re-injected into future messages. If a command is pending or being replayed erroneously, the UI should not show stale command text in the input field or as a pre-filled reply.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST clear any stored command state (including `#help` and all hash/slash commands) immediately after the command is dispatched, preventing it from being re-sent or auto-appended to subsequent messages.
- System MUST audit and reset the chat input field, reply context, and any message queue state upon successful message dispatch to eliminate stale command replay.
- System MUST display the user's sent message in the chat conversation UI immediately upon submission (optimistic rendering), before awaiting any response from the chat agent.
- System MUST show a 'thinking' or processing indicator (e.g., animated typing bubble) in the chat UI after the user's message appears, persisting until the agent response is received.
- System MUST remove the thinking indicator and render the agent's response once the processing is complete, replacing the placeholder without causing layout shifts.
- System SHOULD handle failure cases for optimistic messages — if the message fails to send, it must be visually marked as failed with a retry option, not silently dropped.
- System MUST ensure that special commands like `#help` do not get injected into the reply-to or context payload of any subsequent chat message after their initial dispatch.
- System SHOULD include regression test coverage for the `#help` auto-repeat scenario to prevent recurrence of command state leaking across message sends.

## Technical Notes

The `#help` auto-repeat bug is likely caused by command state (or a reply/context reference) not being cleared after dispatch — inspect the chat state manager, message composer reducer, and any reply-context or pending-command queues for stale references that survive after send. For optimistic UI, implement an optimistic message append pattern: add the user's message to the local chat state immediately on submit with a `pending` status, then update to `sent` or `failed` upon server acknowledgment. Ensure the chat agent 'thinking' state is triggered only after the optimistic message is rendered. Use a unique temporary ID for the optimistic message to reconcile it with the server-confirmed message. Review any middleware or interceptors that process outgoing messages for unintentional command re-injection.

mentioned_issues.title: Pipeline Page: CRUD for Agent Pipeline Configurations with Model Selection and Saved Workflow Management
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> On the pipeline page, I want the user to be able to CRUD Agent Pipeline configurations.
> 
> They should also be able to select the agent model for each agent, be smart with the UI/UX here.
> 
> Saved Agent workflows should be displayed on the bottom, when selected it goes into edit mode for the user, populating the Agent Pipeline board and stages.

## User Story

As a user on the pipeline page, I want to create, read, update, and delete Agent Pipeline configurations — including selecting the specific agent model for each individual agent in the pipeline — so that I can build, save, and revisit customized agent workflows. I also want my saved workflows listed at the bottom of the page so I can quickly select one to load it into the pipeline board in edit mode, with all stages and agent settings fully restored.

## UI/UX Description

The pipeline page consists of two primary zones: (1) an interactive Agent Pipeline Board at the top/center where users configure a pipeline by adding, arranging, and editing stages and agents; each agent node/card on the board exposes a model selector (e.g., a compact dropdown or popover with a model list) inline or via a side panel — model selection UI should be context-aware, grouping models by provider or capability and showing relevant metadata (e.g., context size, cost tier) to aid decision-making. A persistent toolbar provides Create/Save/Delete/Discard actions with clear enabled/disabled states. (2) A Saved Workflows section at the bottom of the page displays previously saved pipeline configurations as cards or rows (showing pipeline name, last modified date, agent count, and a brief description if available); clicking a saved workflow card transitions the board into Edit Mode, loading all pipeline stages, agent assignments, and model selections into the board — a visual indicator (e.g., banner or highlighted header) communicates that the user is editing an existing workflow. Unsaved changes should trigger a confirmation dialog before navigating away or loading another workflow. The board should support drag-and-drop stage reordering and inline renaming. Empty states for both the board and the saved workflows list should include clear CTAs.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST allow users to create a new Agent Pipeline configuration from the pipeline page, including naming the pipeline and adding one or more stages with assigned agents.
- System MUST allow users to select an agent model for each individual agent within a pipeline stage, presenting a model picker UI that displays available models grouped logically (e.g., by provider or capability tier).
- System MUST allow users to save (persist) a configured Agent Pipeline, updating an existing record on edit or creating a new record on first save.
- System MUST allow users to update/edit any previously saved Agent Pipeline configuration by selecting it from the Saved Workflows section, which loads the full pipeline board and all stage/agent/model data into edit mode.
- System MUST allow users to delete a saved Agent Pipeline configuration, with a confirmation prompt before permanent removal.
- System MUST display all saved Agent Pipeline workflows in a dedicated section at the bottom of the pipeline page, showing at minimum the pipeline name, last modified date, and agent/stage count per entry.
- System MUST populate the Agent Pipeline board and all its stages, agents, and model selections when a saved workflow is selected, transitioning the UI into edit mode with a clear visual indicator.
- System MUST prompt the user to confirm or discard unsaved changes when they attempt to load a different saved workflow or navigate away from an in-progress configuration.
- System SHOULD display an empty state with a call-to-action in the Saved Workflows section when no pipelines have been saved yet.

closing_issues.title: Recent Interactions: Filter Deleted Items & Display Only Parent Issues with Project Board Status Colors
closing_issues.body:
## Original Request

> If items are deleted from Clean Up or otherwise, Recent Interactions should removed the any deleted items and display only current items. These should ONLY be GitHub Issue PARENT ISSUES. Display them in themed colors to show their current status from project board.

## User Story

As a user managing GitHub Issues, I want the Recent Interactions panel to automatically remove any deleted items (whether deleted via Clean Up or any other method) and exclusively display active GitHub Issue Parent Issues so that my Recent Interactions view always reflects accurate, current data without stale or orphaned entries. I also want each displayed Parent Issue to be visually color-coded according to its current status on the project board so that I can immediately understand each issue's workflow state at a glance.

## UI/UX Description

The Recent Interactions panel must dynamically reflect the live state of the project. Deleted issues — regardless of whether they were removed through the Clean Up feature or via any other deletion mechanism — must be purged from the list immediately or on next render, with no ghost/stale entries remaining. The list must be strictly filtered to show ONLY GitHub Issue Parent Issues; sub-issues, pull requests, commits, or any other item types must be excluded entirely. Each Parent Issue entry in the list should be rendered with a distinct themed color (background chip, left border accent, or badge) that maps to its current status column on the project board (e.g., 'Todo' → neutral/grey, 'In Progress' → blue, 'In Review' → yellow/amber, 'Done' → green, 'Blocked' → red). Color tokens should align with the existing design system. Status colors should update if an issue's project board status changes. Empty state messaging should appear when no valid Parent Issues exist in Recent Interactions.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST remove any issue from Recent Interactions that has been deleted, regardless of whether deletion originated from the Clean Up feature or any other deletion pathway.
- System MUST filter Recent Interactions to display ONLY GitHub Issue Parent Issues — sub-issues, pull requests, commits, and all other item types must be excluded from the list.
- System MUST fetch and display the current project board status for each Parent Issue shown in Recent Interactions.
- System MUST apply a distinct themed color to each Recent Interactions entry corresponding to the issue's current project board status column (e.g., Todo, In Progress, In Review, Done, Blocked).
- System MUST update status colors in Recent Interactions if an issue's project board column/status changes after initial load.
- System MUST display an empty state UI with appropriate messaging when Recent Interactions contains no valid, non-deleted Parent Issues.
- System SHOULD handle the edge case where a Parent Issue's project board status is undefined or unavailable by rendering a neutral/default fallback color.
- System MUST ensure that stale or orphaned references to deleted issues do not persist in Recent Interactions across page refreshes or session reloads.

## Technical Notes

Recent Interactions likely maintains a local list or cache of recently viewed/interacted issue IDs — this cache must be validated against live GitHub API data (e.g., GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number}) to detect deletions (404 responses) and filter them out before rendering. To enforce Parent Issue-only display, check that each issue does NOT contain a 'sub_issues_summary' parent reference or is not listed as a sub-issue via the GitHub Issues API. Project board status should be queried via the GitHub Projects V2 GraphQL API (projectV2Items) to retrieve the current status field value per issue, and a color map should be defined in the theme layer (e.g., a STATUS_COLOR_MAP constant) to translate status labels to design tokens. Consider debouncing or caching project board status lookups to avoid excessive API calls on repeated renders. The branch 'copilot/audit-update-ui-components' is the recommended development target as this is a UI component update.

mentioned_issues.title: Fix #help Command Auto-Repeat Bug & Add Optimistic Message Rendering in Chat UI
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Debug chat. I entered #help once and now it keeps sending it automatically as a reply to the chat agent.
> 
> Also, when a user sends a chat message, it should be displayed immediately in the chat UI, then the chat agent can "think" if processing time is needed.

## User Story

As a Solune chat user, I want the `#help` command (and any special commands) to send only once without being replayed automatically on subsequent messages, and I want my sent messages to appear in the chat UI immediately upon submission so that the conversation feels responsive and I'm not left wondering if my message was received while the agent is processing.

## UI/UX Description

The chat input area must clear and display the user's message in the conversation thread the instant they hit send — before any agent response or thinking state begins. A visual 'thinking' indicator (e.g., animated ellipsis or spinner bubble) should appear below the user's message to signal the agent is processing. For the #help bug: the special `#help` command (and any slash/hash commands) must be treated as one-time actions that do not persist in any input state, reply context, or message queue. There should be no residual state from a previously sent command that causes it to be re-injected into future messages. If a command is pending or being replayed erroneously, the UI should not show stale command text in the input field or as a pre-filled reply.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST clear any stored command state (including `#help` and all hash/slash commands) immediately after the command is dispatched, preventing it from being re-sent or auto-appended to subsequent messages.
- System MUST audit and reset the chat input field, reply context, and any message queue state upon successful message dispatch to eliminate stale command replay.
- System MUST display the user's sent message in the chat conversation UI immediately upon submission (optimistic rendering), before awaiting any response from the chat agent.
- System MUST show a 'thinking' or processing indicator (e.g., animated typing bubble) in the chat UI after the user's message appears, persisting until the agent response is received.
- System MUST remove the thinking indicator and render the agent's response once the processing is complete, replacing the placeholder without causing layout shifts.
- System SHOULD handle failure cases for optimistic messages — if the message fails to send, it must be visually marked as failed with a retry option, not silently dropped.
- System MUST ensure that special commands like `#help` do not get injected into the reply-to or context payload of any subsequent chat message after their initial dispatch.
- System SHOULD include regression test coverage for the `#help` auto-repeat scenario to prevent recurrence of command state leaking across message sends.

## Technical Notes

The `#help` auto-repeat bug is likely caused by command state (or a reply/context reference) not being cleared after dispatch — inspect the chat state manager, message composer reducer, and any reply-context or pending-command queues for stale references that survive after send. For optimistic UI, implement an optimistic message append pattern: add the user's message to the local chat state immediately on submit with a `pending` status, then update to `sent` or `failed` upon server acknowledgment. Ensure the chat agent 'thinking' state is triggered only after the optimistic message is rendered. Use a unique temporary ID for the optimistic message to reconcile it with the server-confirmed message. Review any middleware or interceptors that process outgoing messages for unintentional command re-injection.
