mentioned_issues.title: Add Tools Page with MCP Configuration Upload and Agent Tool Selection via Grid Modal
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Add a Tools page right under Agents page on the left nav bar. This page should look almost exactly like Agents. Except this should support a user uploading MCP configurations to be synced/added to GitHub repo/project for GitHub Custom Agents to use. Agents should then be able to have tools added, similar to how models are selected. Except, pop up a tile module in a grid pattern of MCPs for the user to select 0-to-many to add to an agent while creating. 
> 
> Check current documentation for how to integrate this into GitHub

## User Story

As a developer building GitHub Custom Agents, I want a dedicated Tools page (positioned directly below the Agents page in the left nav bar) where I can upload and manage MCP (Model Context Protocol) configurations that sync to a GitHub repo/project, and then assign those MCP tools to agents during creation via a tile-grid selection modal, so that my agents can leverage custom MCP-powered tools in a structured, discoverable way — just like selecting models today.

## UI/UX Description

The Tools page must be placed immediately below the Agents entry in the left navigation bar and must visually mirror the Agents page layout (same card structure, header style, action buttons, empty states, and list/grid view). Each MCP configuration is represented as a card showing its name, description, and sync status (e.g., 'Synced to GitHub', 'Pending', 'Error'). An 'Upload MCP Config' button opens a file/JSON upload modal allowing users to paste or upload an MCP configuration file; on successful upload, the config is automatically pushed/synced to the connected GitHub repo/project. On the Agent creation/edit form, a 'Add Tools' section mirrors the 'Select Model' interaction: clicking it opens a full overlay modal displaying all available MCPs in a responsive tile grid (card-per-MCP with icon, name, and short description). Users can select zero or many MCP tiles (multi-select with a visible checkmark or highlight state), then confirm to attach them to the agent. Selected tools appear as removable chips/tags on the agent form. Deselecting inside the modal or removing chips on the form both work. Empty state for the Tools page should mirror the Agents page empty state pattern.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST add a 'Tools' navigation item to the left sidebar positioned directly below the 'Agents' navigation item, using the same styling and icon pattern as the Agents nav item.
- System MUST render the Tools page with a layout and component structure that mirrors the Agents page, including header, action bar, card/list views, and empty state components.
- System MUST allow users to upload an MCP configuration (JSON or supported format) via an upload modal, and automatically sync/push that configuration to the connected GitHub repository or project for use by GitHub Custom Agents.
- System MUST display each uploaded MCP configuration as a card on the Tools page, showing at minimum: name, description, and current sync status (e.g., Synced, Pending, Error) with the GitHub repo/project.
- System MUST provide a re-sync or refresh action per MCP card to allow users to manually trigger a re-push of a configuration to the GitHub repo/project.
- System MUST surface an 'Add Tools' selector in the Agent creation and Agent edit forms, allowing users to select zero or more MCP tools to associate with an agent — analogous to the existing model selection interaction.
- System MUST render the MCP tool selector as a modal overlay containing a responsive tile grid (one tile per MCP), where each tile shows the MCP icon/logo, name, and short description, and supports multi-select with a clear visual active/selected state (e.g., checkmark overlay or highlighted border).
- System MUST persist the selected MCP tools on the agent record and display them as removable chips or tags on the agent form and agent detail view.
- System MUST validate uploaded MCP configuration files for correct schema/format before syncing to GitHub and display actionable error messages for invalid uploads.
- System SHOULD check and follow the official GitHub documentation for integrating MCP configurations with GitHub Custom Agents during implementation to ensure API compatibility and required file structure/placement in the repo.
- System MUST handle sync failures gracefully, showing an error status on the affected MCP card with a user-readable reason and a retry option.
- System SHOULD support deleting an MCP configuration from the Tools page, with a confirmation prompt, which also removes or flags the config in the connected GitHub repo/project.

## Technical Notes

Review the official GitHub Custom Agents and GitHub MCP integration documentation (https://docs.github.com) to determine the required MCP config file format, target file path within the repo (e.g., `.github/` directory), and the appropriate GitHub API endpoints (Contents API or Copilot Extensions API) for pushing configurations. The Tools page should reuse existing Agents page components (cards, headers, empty states, modals) to minimize duplication — consider abstracting shared layout into a generic resource page wrapper. The MCP tile-grid selection modal on the Agent form should mirror the model-selection interaction pattern already in the codebase; multi-select state can be managed locally with a controlled set of selected IDs committed on modal confirm. Store MCP configs in the existing data layer with fields for: id, name, description, raw config JSON, syncStatus, syncedAt, and githubRepoTarget. Ensure the GitHub sync operation uses authenticated API calls and reports status back to the UI via optimistic updates with error rollback.

mentioned_issues.title: Performance Review
mentioned_issues.body:
## Performance Review

Perform a balanced first pass focused on measurable, low-risk performance gains across backend and frontend. Start by capturing baselines and instrumentation, then fix the highest-value issues already surfaced by the codebase: backend GitHub API churn around board refreshes and polling, and frontend board responsiveness issues caused by broad query invalidation, full-list rerenders, and hot event listeners. Defer broader architectural refactors like virtualization and large service decomposition unless the first pass fails to meet targets.

**Steps**
1. Phase 1 — Baseline and guardrails. Capture current backend and frontend performance baselines before changing behavior. Measure idle API activity for an open board, board endpoint request cost, WebSocket/polling refresh behavior, and frontend render hot spots. Reuse existing tests around cache, polling, WebSocket fallback, and board refresh to define a before/after checklist. This phase blocks all optimization work because the success criteria and regression guardrails depend on it.
2. Phase 1 — Confirm current backend state against Spec 022. Verify whether WebSocket change detection, board cache TTL alignment, and sub-issue cache invalidation are fully implemented or only partially landed. The current board endpoint already appears to set a 300-second TTL and clears sub-issue cache on manual refresh, so the remaining work should target any still-missing pieces rather than redoing completed items. This step can run in parallel with frontend baseline inspection once the measurement checklist is defined.
3. Phase 2 — Backend API consumption fixes. Prioritize the highest-value remaining server-side issues: WebSocket subscription refresh logic in the projects API, sub-issue caching behavior for board data, and any remaining unnecessary GitHub calls in polling or repository resolution. Explicitly validate that idle board viewing no longer emits repeated refreshes when data is unchanged, that warm sub-issue caches materially reduce board refresh call count, and that fallback polling does not trigger expensive board refreshes unintentionally. This depends on Phase 1 baselines.
4. Phase 2 — Frontend refresh-path fixes. Update the real-time and fallback refresh paths so lightweight task updates stay decoupled from the expensive board data query except on manual refresh. Review the interaction between WebSocket updates, fallback polling, auto-refresh, and manual refresh to ensure they use a single coherent policy and do not recreate the prior polling storm. This can proceed in parallel with backend API work once the desired refresh contract is confirmed.
5. Phase 3 — Frontend render optimization. Target low-risk rendering costs in board and chat surfaces: reduce repeated derived-data work in page components and hooks, stabilize props where useful, memoize heavy card/list components when it actually reduces rerenders, and throttle or rationalize hot event listeners such as drag and popover positioning. Keep this phase intentionally low-risk; avoid introducing new dependencies or virtualization in the first pass unless baseline results show large boards still regress after the lighter fixes.
6. Phase 3 — Verification and regression coverage. Extend or adjust unit/integration coverage around backend cache behavior, WebSocket change detection, fallback polling, and frontend board refresh logic. Validate with backend tests, frontend tests, and at least one manual network/profile pass to confirm the target improvements are real rather than inferred. This depends on Phases 2 and 3.
7. Phase 4 — Optional second-wave work. If the first pass still leaves material UI lag on large boards or excessive backend complexity, prepare a follow-on plan for structural changes: board virtualization, deeper service decomposition around GitHub project fetching/polling, bounded cache policies, and stronger instrumentation around request budgets and render timings. This phase is explicitly out of scope for the first implementation unless measurements prove it is necessary.

**Relevant files**
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/specs/022-api-rate-limit-protection/spec.md` — primary acceptance criteria for idle-rate-limit reduction, sub-issue caching, refresh behavior, and cache TTL alignment.

- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/services/github_projects/service.py` — board/project fetching path and candidate reuse points for sub-issue caching or batching.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/services/cache.py` — cache TTLs, cache-key helpers, and any bounded-cache improvements if needed.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/utils.py` — shared repository resolution logic to reuse instead of duplicated fallback flows.

2. If backend API churn remains high after Spec 022-aligned fixes, the next recommended option is deeper consolidation in the GitHub projects service and polling pipeline rather than more cache-layer patching.

mentioned_issues.title: Add Tools Page with MCP Configuration Upload and Agent Tool Selection via Grid Modal
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Add a Tools page right under Agents page on the left nav bar. This page should look almost exactly like Agents. Except this should support a user uploading MCP configurations to be synced/added to GitHub repo/project for GitHub Custom Agents to use. Agents should then be able to have tools added, similar to how models are selected. Except, pop up a tile module in a grid pattern of MCPs for the user to select 0-to-many to add to an agent while creating. 
> 
> Check current documentation for how to integrate this into GitHub

## User Story

As a developer building GitHub Custom Agents, I want a dedicated Tools page (positioned directly below the Agents page in the left nav bar) where I can upload and manage MCP (Model Context Protocol) configurations that sync to a GitHub repo/project, and then assign those MCP tools to agents during creation via a tile-grid selection modal, so that my agents can leverage custom MCP-powered tools in a structured, discoverable way — just like selecting models today.

## UI/UX Description

The Tools page must be placed immediately below the Agents entry in the left navigation bar and must visually mirror the Agents page layout (same card structure, header style, action buttons, empty states, and list/grid view). Each MCP configuration is represented as a card showing its name, description, and sync status (e.g., 'Synced to GitHub', 'Pending', 'Error'). An 'Upload MCP Config' button opens a file/JSON upload modal allowing users to paste or upload an MCP configuration file; on successful upload, the config is automatically pushed/synced to the connected GitHub repo/project. On the Agent creation/edit form, a 'Add Tools' section mirrors the 'Select Model' interaction: clicking it opens a full overlay modal displaying all available MCPs in a responsive tile grid (card-per-MCP with icon, name, and short description). Users can select zero or many MCP tiles (multi-select with a visible checkmark or highlight state), then confirm to attach them to the agent. Selected tools appear as removable chips/tags on the agent form. Deselecting inside the modal or removing chips on the form both work. Empty state for the Tools page should mirror the Agents page empty state pattern.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST add a 'Tools' navigation item to the left sidebar positioned directly below the 'Agents' navigation item, using the same styling and icon pattern as the Agents nav item.
- System MUST render the Tools page with a layout and component structure that mirrors the Agents page, including header, action bar, card/list views, and empty state components.
- System MUST allow users to upload an MCP configuration (JSON or supported format) via an upload modal, and automatically sync/push that configuration to the connected GitHub repository or project for use by GitHub Custom Agents.
- System MUST display each uploaded MCP configuration as a card on the Tools page, showing at minimum: name, description, and current sync status (e.g., Synced, Pending, Error) with the GitHub repo/project.
- System MUST provide a re-sync or refresh action per MCP card to allow users to manually trigger a re-push of a configuration to the GitHub repo/project.
- System MUST surface an 'Add Tools' selector in the Agent creation and Agent edit forms, allowing users to select zero or more MCP tools to associate with an agent — analogous to the existing model selection interaction.
- System MUST render the MCP tool selector as a modal overlay containing a responsive tile grid (one tile per MCP), where each tile shows the MCP icon/logo, name, and short description, and supports multi-select with a clear visual active/selected state (e.g., checkmark overlay or highlighted border).
- System MUST persist the selected MCP tools on the agent record and display them as removable chips or tags on the agent form and agent detail view.
- System MUST validate uploaded MCP configuration files for correct schema/format before syncing to GitHub and display actionable error messages for invalid uploads.
- System SHOULD check and follow the official GitHub documentation for integrating MCP configurations with GitHub Custom Agents during implementation to ensure API compatibility and required file structure/placement in the repo.
- System MUST handle sync failures gracefully, showing an error status on the affected MCP card with a user-readable reason and a retry option.
- System SHOULD support deleting an MCP configuration from the Tools page, with a confirmation prompt, which also removes or flags the config in the connected GitHub repo/project.

## Technical Notes

Review the official GitHub Custom Agents and GitHub MCP integration documentation (https://docs.github.com) to determine the required MCP config file format, target file path within the repo (e.g., `.github/` directory), and the appropriate GitHub API endpoints (Contents API or Copilot Extensions API) for pushing configurations. The Tools page should reuse existing Agents page components (cards, headers, empty states, modals) to minimize duplication — consider abstracting shared layout into a generic resource page wrapper. The MCP tile-grid selection modal on the Agent form should mirror the model-selection interaction pattern already in the codebase; multi-select state can be managed locally with a controlled set of selected IDs committed on modal confirm. Store MCP configs in the existing data layer with fields for: id, name, description, raw config JSON, syncStatus, syncedAt, and githubRepoTarget. Ensure the GitHub sync operation uses authenticated API calls and reports status back to the UI via optimistic updates with error rollback.

mentioned_issues.title: Chat UX Enhancements: AI Enhance Toggle, Markdown Input Support, File Upload, and Voice Chat
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> In the app user chat,
> - Similar to "+ Add Agent" pop-out on Agents page, add a feature to allow the user to "AI Enhance" toggle on/off. If "AI Enhance" is enabled - keep the flow the same. If the "AI Enhance" is disabled, use the user's exact chat input for the GitHub Parent Issue description but, use the Chat Agent to generate all the metadata needed for GitHub Issue creation (labels, estimates, title, etc) and add Agent Pipeline configuration information to description.
> - Allow for a user to enter in markdown without triggering something like "not recognized command"
> - Add support for user file upload. The file should be attached to the GitHub Parent Issue.
> - Add support for user to voice chat with microphone to Chat Agent

## User Story

As a user of the app chat interface, I want granular control over how my chat input is processed — including an 'AI Enhance' toggle to optionally bypass AI rewriting of my issue description while still generating metadata, the ability to write raw Markdown without triggering unrecognized command errors, the ability to attach files directly to GitHub Parent Issues from the chat, and the ability to speak to the Chat Agent via microphone — so that I have full flexibility in how I communicate and what gets submitted to GitHub without friction or unintended transformations of my content.

## UI/UX Description

The chat input area should include a persistent toolbar or popout controls panel — styled similarly to the existing '+ Add Agent' pop-out on the Agents page — containing an 'AI Enhance' toggle (on/off). When 'AI Enhance' is ON (default), the existing flow remains unchanged. When 'AI Enhance' is OFF, the user's exact verbatim chat input is used as the GitHub Parent Issue description body without any AI rewriting, but the Chat Agent still runs in the background to generate all required GitHub Issue metadata (title, labels, estimates, assignees, milestones, etc.) and appends Agent Pipeline configuration information to the description. The toggle should have a clear visual ON/OFF state (e.g., colored pill toggle with label). The Markdown input support means the chat input field must render or at minimum accept raw Markdown syntax (headers, bold, lists, code blocks, etc.) without misinterpreting them as chat commands — the system should only treat explicit command prefixes (e.g., '/command') as commands, not Markdown characters like '#', '*', '-', or backticks. A file upload affordance (paperclip icon or 'Attach File' button) should appear in the chat toolbar; when a file is selected, a preview chip/thumbnail should appear above the input field with a remove (×) option, and upon submission the file is attached to the resulting GitHub Parent Issue. A microphone button in the toolbar should activate voice-to-text transcription, populating the chat input field with transcribed speech in real time; a visual indicator (pulsing mic icon, waveform animation) should show active recording state, with a clear stop/cancel control.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST provide an 'AI Enhance' toggle control in the chat UI, visually consistent with the '+ Add Agent' pop-out pattern on the Agents page, defaulting to the ON state.
- System MUST, when 'AI Enhance' is OFF, pass the user's exact verbatim chat input as the GitHub Parent Issue description body without any AI transformation or rewriting of the content.
- System MUST, when 'AI Enhance' is OFF, still invoke the Chat Agent to auto-generate all GitHub Issue metadata (title, labels, size/effort estimates, assignees, milestones) and append Agent Pipeline configuration details to the issue description.
- System MUST accept raw Markdown syntax in the chat input field (including '#', '*', '-', '`', '>', '[]()' etc.) without triggering 'unrecognized command' errors or misinterpreting Markdown tokens as chat commands — only explicit slash-prefixed strings (e.g., '/commandName') should be treated as commands.
- System MUST provide a file upload control (e.g., paperclip/attach button) in the chat toolbar that allows users to select one or more files, displays an inline preview chip with filename and a remove option before submission, and attaches the uploaded file(s) to the generated GitHub Parent Issue upon submission.
- System MUST display an error or unsupported-format message when a file type or size exceeds defined limits, and prevent submission of invalid attachments.
- System MUST provide a microphone/voice input button in the chat toolbar that activates real-time speech-to-text transcription, populates the chat input field with the transcribed text, and shows a clear active-recording visual indicator (e.g., pulsing mic icon or waveform animation) with a stop/cancel control.
- System SHOULD persist the user's 'AI Enhance' toggle preference across sessions or at minimum within the current session so users do not need to re-set it on every chat open.
- System MUST gracefully handle microphone permission denial by displaying an informative error message and falling back to manual text input without breaking the chat flow.
- System SHOULD allow the user to edit voice-transcribed text in the input field before submitting, giving full control over the final content sent to the Chat Agent.

## Technical Notes

The 'AI Enhance' toggle should integrate with the existing Chat Agent pipeline; when OFF, the pipeline must short-circuit the description-generation step and substitute the raw input string, while still executing metadata inference (labels, estimates, title) and appending Agent Pipeline config as a structured section in the issue body. Markdown parsing conflict with command detection should be resolved by scoping the command parser to only match tokens that begin at the start of a message with a '/' prefix, leaving all other special characters as plain text content. File upload should use the GitHub REST API's issue attachment or comment attachment endpoint (or upload via blob/asset if supported), with client-side validation for file type (images, PDFs, text files, etc.) and size limits (e.g., max 10MB per GitHub constraints); consider a pre-upload step before issue creation and embed the file URL in the issue body if direct attachment is unsupported. Voice input should leverage the Web Speech API (SpeechRecognition) for in-browser transcription with a fallback notice for unsupported browsers, or integrate a third-party STT service (e.g., Whisper API) for broader compatibility and accuracy.

As a user of the app chat interface, I want granular control over how my chat input is processed — including an 'AI Enhance' toggle to optionally bypass AI rewriting of my issue description while still generating metadata, the ability to write raw Markdown without triggering unrecognized command errors, the ability to attach files directly to GitHub Parent Issues from the chat, and the ability to speak to the Chat Agent via microphone — so that I have full flexibility in how I communicate and what gets submitted to GitHub without friction or unintended transformations of my content.

## UI/UX Description

The chat input area should include a persistent toolbar or popout controls panel — styled similarly to the existing '+ Add Agent' pop-out on the Agents page — containing an 'AI Enhance' toggle (on/off). When 'AI Enhance' is ON (default), the existing flow remains unchanged. When 'AI Enhance' is OFF, the user's exact verbatim chat input is used as the GitHub Parent Issue description body without any AI rewriting, but the Chat Agent still runs in the background to generate all required GitHub Issue metadata (title, labels, estimates, assignees, milestones, etc.) and appends Agent Pipeline configuration information to the description. The toggle should have a clear visual ON/OFF state (e.g., colored pill toggle with label). The Markdown input support means the chat input field must render or at minimum accept raw Markdown syntax (headers, bold, lists, code blocks, etc.) without misinterpreting them as chat commands — the system should only treat explicit command prefixes (e.g., '/command') as commands, not Markdown characters like '#', '*', '-', or backticks. A file upload affordance (paperclip icon or 'Attach File' button) should appear in the chat toolbar; when a file is selected, a preview chip/thumbnail should appear above the input field with a remove (×) option, and upon submission the file is attached to the resulting GitHub Parent Issue. A microphone button in the toolbar should activate voice-to-text transcription, populating the chat input field with transcribed speech in real time; a visual indicator (pulsing mic icon, waveform animation) should show active recording state, with a clear stop/cancel control.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST provide an 'AI Enhance' toggle control in the chat UI, visually consistent with the '+ Add Agent' pop-out pattern on the Agents page, defaulting to the ON state.
- System MUST, when 'AI Enhance' is OFF, pass the user's exact verbatim chat input as the GitHub Parent Issue description body without any AI transformation or rewriting of the content.
- System MUST, when 'AI Enhance' is OFF, still invoke the Chat Agent to auto-generate all GitHub Issue metadata (title, labels, size/effort estimates, assignees, milestones) and append Agent Pipeline configuration details to the issue description.
- System MUST accept raw Markdown syntax in the chat input field (including '#', '*', '-', '`', '>', '[]()' etc.) without triggering 'unrecognized command' errors or misinterpreting Markdown tokens as chat commands — only explicit slash-prefixed strings (e.g., '/commandName') should be treated as commands.
- System MUST provide a file upload control (e.g., paperclip/attach button) in the chat toolbar that allows users to select one or more files, displays an inline preview chip with filename and a remove option before submission, and attaches the uploaded file(s) to the generated GitHub Parent Issue upon submission.
- System MUST display an error or unsupported-format message when a file type or size exceeds defined limits, and prevent submission of invalid attachments.
- System MUST provide a microphone/voice input button in the chat toolbar that activates real-time speech-to-text transcription, populates the chat input field with the transcribed text, and shows a clear active-recording visual indicator (e.g., pulsing mic icon or waveform animation) with a stop/cancel control.
- System SHOULD persist the user's 'AI Enhance' toggle preference across sessions or at minimum within the current session so users do not need to re-set it on every chat open.
- System MUST gracefully handle microphone permission denial by displaying an informative error message and falling back to manual text input without breaking the chat flow.
- System SHOULD allow the user to edit voice-transcribed text in the input field before submitting, giving full control over the final content sent to the Chat Agent.

## Technical Notes

The 'AI Enhance' toggle should integrate with the existing Chat Agent pipeline; when OFF, the pipeline must short-circuit the description-generation step and substitute the raw input string, while still executing metadata inference (labels, estimates, title) and appending Agent Pipeline config as a structured section in the issue body. File upload should use the GitHub REST API's issue attachment or comment attachment endpoint (or upload via blob/asset if supported), with client-side validation for file type (images, PDFs, text files, etc.) and size limits (e.g., max 10MB per GitHub constraints); consider a pre-upload step before issue creation and embed the file URL in the issue body if direct attachment is unsupported. > - When creating a new Pipeline configuration, the Status tiles should not be moveable. The Agent tiles should be moveable.
> - When in Creating new Pipeline, add a "clone" button to agents - so it creates a copy of the agent definition to be used on the Pipeline.
> - In the Pipeline Creation, remove "Add Stage"

## User Story

As a Solune pipeline builder, I want the Pipeline Creation page to correctly reflect available GitHub models per user account, render the Tools module above all other elements, restrict drag-and-drop to Agent tiles only, provide a clone button for agent definitions, and remove the unused 'Add Stage' control — so that the pipeline configuration experience is accurate, visually correct, and free of confusing or broken interactions.

## UI/UX Description

The Pipeline page requires five targeted fixes: (1) The 'Pipeline Model' dropdown in '+ Add Agent → Select model' must be dynamically populated from the authenticated user's available GitHub models for Custom GitHub Agents rather than a static/mismatched list — since this list varies per account, it must be fetched at runtime. (2) When a user opens '+ Add Agent → + Tools', the Tools module/popover must render at the highest z-index layer (above all cards, panels, and overlays) so it is never obscured by adjacent or parent elements. (3) On the pipeline canvas, Status tiles must be locked in place (no drag interaction, no move cursor) while Agent tiles remain fully draggable and repositionable; visual affordance (e.g., grab cursor) should only appear on Agent tiles. (4) Each Agent tile must display a 'Clone' button that, when clicked, creates a full deep copy of that agent's configuration (model, tools, parameters) as a new Agent tile on the pipeline, ready for independent editing. (5) The 'Add Stage' button/control must be removed entirely from the Pipeline Creation UI, cleaning up the interface.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST fetch the list of available GitHub models for Custom GitHub Agents dynamically from the authenticated user's GitHub account and populate the 'Select model' dropdown in '+ Add Agent' with that list, replacing any current static or mismatched model list.
- System MUST ensure the Tools module rendered via '+ Add Agent → + Tools' has a CSS z-index (or equivalent stacking context) higher than all surrounding pipeline canvas elements, panels, and overlays, so it is never hidden or clipped by other UI elements.
- System MUST disable drag-and-drop interactions entirely on Status tiles within the Pipeline Creation canvas — Status tiles must not be moveable, must not display a grab/move cursor, and must not respond to drag events.
- System MUST preserve full drag-and-drop reordering and repositioning functionality exclusively on Agent tiles within the Pipeline Creation canvas, with appropriate visual affordance (e.g., grab cursor on hover).
- System MUST provide a 'Clone' button on each Agent tile in the Pipeline Creation view that creates a complete deep copy of the agent definition — including its selected model, configured tools, and all other parameters — and inserts the cloned Agent tile into the pipeline as an independently editable instance.
- System MUST remove the 'Add Stage' button and all associated stage-creation logic from the Pipeline Creation UI.
- System SHOULD handle the case where the GitHub model list API call fails or returns an empty list gracefully, displaying a user-friendly error or fallback state in the 'Select model' dropdown rather than crashing or showing stale data.
- System SHOULD visually differentiate Status tiles from Agent tiles (e.g., locked icon, distinct border or cursor) to clearly communicate to users that Status tiles cannot be moved while Agent tiles can.

## Technical Notes

The dynamic GitHub model list for 'Select model' should be fetched from the GitHub API (e.g., GitHub Models endpoint or equivalent Custom GitHub Agents model availability API) using the current user's auth token at pipeline load time or when '+ Add Agent' is opened; responses should be cached per session to avoid redundant calls. The Tools module z-index bug is likely a CSS stacking context issue caused by a parent element with overflow:hidden, transform, or an explicit z-index — investigate the component hierarchy for '+ Add Agent' and ensure the Tools popover/modal is portaled to the document body or given a sufficiently high z-index (e.g., 9999). For drag-and-drop tile locking, check the existing DnD library (e.g., react-dnd, dnd-kit, or similar) used in the pipeline canvas and apply a `canDrag: () => false` guard or `disabled` prop specifically to Status tile drag sources. Agent cloning should perform a deep clone of the agent config object (avoid shallow copy pitfalls with nested tool arrays/objects) and assign a new unique ID to the cloned tile before adding it to the pipeline state.

closing_issues.title: Fix: Use Exact User Input + Chat Agent Metadata When AI Enhance Is Disabled
closing_issues.body:
## Original Request

> On the app user chat,
> - When the AI Enhance is disabled I receive an error. If the "AI Enhance" is disabled, use the user's exact chat input for the GitHub Parent Issue description but, use the Chat Agent to generate all the metadata needed for GitHub Issue creation (labels, estimates, title, etc) and add Agent Pipeline configuration information to description.
>  Error: I couldn't generate a task from your description. Please try again with more detail.

## User Story

As a Solune app user submitting a chat request with AI Enhance disabled, I want my exact chat input used as the GitHub Parent Issue description while the Chat Agent still generates all required metadata (title, labels, estimates, etc.) and Agent Pipeline configuration, so that I can create well-structured GitHub issues without needing AI content enhancement and without encountering the 'I couldn't generate a task from your description' error.

## UI/UX Description

When the user submits a chat message with AI Enhance toggled off, the system should silently bypass the AI enhancement step and proceed with a two-track pipeline: (1) use the user's verbatim chat input as the GitHub Parent Issue description body — no paraphrasing, summarizing, or reformatting — and (2) invoke the Chat Agent independently to generate all GitHub Issue metadata (title, labels, size estimates, assignees, priority, etc.) and append Agent Pipeline configuration details to the issue description. The user should never see the error message 'I couldn't generate a task from your description. Please try again with more detail.' when AI Enhance is disabled. The submission flow should feel seamless — no visible errors, no stalled states — and the resulting issue should reflect the raw user input in the description alongside fully AI-generated metadata fields.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST detect when the AI Enhance toggle is disabled before invoking any content generation pipeline and branch into the fallback metadata-only path.
- System MUST use the user's exact, unmodified chat input as the GitHub Parent Issue description body when AI Enhance is disabled — no summarization, paraphrasing, or reformatting of the description.
- System MUST invoke the Chat Agent to generate all required GitHub Issue metadata (title, labels, size estimate, priority, assignees, and any other structured fields) even when AI Enhance is disabled.
- System MUST append Agent Pipeline configuration information to the GitHub Parent Issue description when AI Enhance is disabled, in addition to the verbatim user input.
- System MUST NOT display the error message 'I couldn't generate a task from your description. Please try again with more detail.' when AI Enhance is disabled and the user has provided any non-empty chat input.
- System MUST suppress or reroute any error thrown by the AI enhancement step when the toggle is off, ensuring the fallback path completes successfully and creates the GitHub issue.
- System SHOULD validate that the Chat Agent metadata generation step succeeded independently of the AI Enhance step, and surface a specific, actionable error only if the metadata generation itself fails.
- System MUST ensure the final GitHub issue created with AI Enhance disabled is structurally identical to one created with AI Enhance enabled, differing only in that the description body is the raw user input rather than AI-enhanced content.

## Technical Notes

The root cause is likely that the issue creation pipeline assumes AI Enhance is always active and throws a generic catch-all error when the enhancement step returns nothing or fails silently — the error handler should check the AI Enhance flag before surfacing user-facing errors. Refactor the pipeline into two explicit branches: a full pipeline (AI Enhance on: enhance content → generate metadata → build issue) and a metadata-only pipeline (AI Enhance off: pass-through raw input → invoke Chat Agent for metadata → append Agent Pipeline config → build issue). The Chat Agent metadata generation call should be decoupled from the AI Enhance step so it can run independently in both paths. Ensure the Agent Pipeline configuration block appended to the description is clearly delimited (e.g., a markdown section) so it does not visually blend with the user's raw input.

closing_issues.title: Project Board: Parent Issue Hierarchy, Sub-Issue Display Improvements, Agent Pipeline Fixes & Functional Filters
closing_issues.body:
## Original Request

> On project page,
> - Only show Parent GitHub Issues on the Project Board
> - The GitHub Sub Issue list should be collapsible, in the GitHub Parent card
> - The assigned Agent and Model should be on each GitHub Sub Issue tile shown in the GitHub Parent card
> - The GitHub Parent Issue labels should be displayed on the card
> - Some models are missing from being displayed on the agents in the Agent Pipeline
> - Some tool counts are missing from being displayed on the agents in the Agent Pipeline
> - 'Custom' on the Agent Pipeline, should update it's name to a "saved pipeline configuration's name" if the user selects a saved configuration.
> - The columns in the Project Board should be scrollable
> - Update the Filter, Sort, and Group By buttons to actually function - this should be in relation to the GitHub Parent Issues on the Project Board

## User Story

As a project manager using the Project Board, I want parent GitHub Issues to be the primary unit of display with collapsible sub-issue lists inside each parent card — showing agent assignments, model names, and labels — so that I can maintain a clean, organized board view while still accessing granular sub-issue detail on demand. I also need the Agent Pipeline to correctly display all model names and tool counts, rename 'Custom' to the saved configuration name when applicable, and have fully functional Filter, Sort, and Group By controls so I can navigate and prioritize work efficiently.

## UI/UX Description

The Project Board columns must only render GitHub Parent Issues as top-level cards; sub-issues are nested within each parent card in a collapsible section (collapsed by default, toggleable via a chevron/arrow icon). Each sub-issue tile inside the collapsed panel displays the assigned Agent name and Model name prominently. Parent Issue cards display all associated GitHub labels as colored label chips (matching GitHub label colors). Columns must be independently vertically scrollable (overflow-y: auto) so long columns do not overflow the viewport. The Agent Pipeline panel must render every available model name without omission and show accurate tool counts on each agent tile — both are likely data-binding bugs requiring audit. The 'Custom' label on the Agent Pipeline header/selector must dynamically update to reflect the name of any saved pipeline configuration the user selects, reverting to 'Custom' only when no named configuration is active. The Filter, Sort, and Group By toolbar buttons must open functional control panels that operate exclusively on GitHub Parent Issues: Filter by label, assignee, status, or milestone; Sort by created date, updated date, priority, or title; Group By label, assignee, or milestone, reorganizing cards into named column groups accordingly.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST render only GitHub Parent Issues as top-level cards on the Project Board columns, excluding standalone sub-issues from the primary board view.
- System MUST display a collapsible sub-issue list section within each GitHub Parent Issue card, collapsed by default, expandable via a visible toggle control (e.g., chevron icon with sub-issue count badge).
- System MUST show the assigned Agent name and Model name on each sub-issue tile rendered inside the parent card's expanded sub-issue panel.
- System MUST display all GitHub labels associated with a Parent Issue as colored label chips on the parent card, using the label's configured color and name.
- System MUST make each Project Board column independently vertically scrollable (overflow-y: auto or scroll) so cards in tall columns remain accessible without page-level scrolling issues.
- System MUST audit and fix the Agent Pipeline to ensure all available model names are correctly bound and displayed on every agent tile, with no models missing from the UI.
- System MUST audit and fix the Agent Pipeline to ensure accurate tool counts are displayed on every agent tile, resolving any missing or zero-count rendering bugs.
- System MUST dynamically replace the 'Custom' label in the Agent Pipeline with the name of the currently active saved pipeline configuration when the user selects one, and revert to 'Custom' only when no named configuration is selected.
- System MUST implement functional Filter controls on the Project Board that filter the displayed GitHub Parent Issue cards by one or more criteria including label, assignee, status, and milestone.
- System MUST implement functional Sort controls on the Project Board that reorder GitHub Parent Issue cards within columns by created date, updated date, priority, or title (ascending/descending).
- System MUST implement functional Group By controls on the Project Board that reorganize GitHub Parent Issue cards into named groups (e.g., by label, assignee, or milestone), visually separating groups within or across columns.
- System SHOULD persist the user's active Filter, Sort, and Group By selections across page refreshes using local storage or URL query params.
- System SHOULD display a visual indicator (e.g., active state highlight or badge) on the Filter, Sort, and Group By buttons when any non-default configuration is active.

## Technical Notes

Audit the data pipeline feeding the Project Board to ensure sub-issues are correctly identified via GitHub API parent/child relationships (using the sub_issues or tracked-in metadata) and excluded from the top-level card render loop. The collapsible sub-issue panel can be implemented with a local component state toggle; sub-issue tiles should receive agent and model data from the existing assignment store/context. closing_issues.body:
## Original Request

> On Agents page,
> - Agents should have unique sun/moon themed avatars/icons
> - "Featured Agents" should show the top 3 used agents, or any agents created in the past 3 days
> - The user should be able to edit the agent definition directly. They must save the page before leaving. If they save, create a PR with updated file changes to agents.
> - Add an option to update all Agent models at once, ensure confirmation from the user
> - Repository - should be the repo name, not the owner. Fit text to background bubble dynamically
> - The user should be able to easily edit/update the tools an Agent has defined in it's configuration

## User Story

As a user managing agents on the Agents page, I want a polished and fully interactive agent management experience — including unique sun/moon themed avatars, a 'Featured Agents' section surfacing the top 3 most-used or recently created agents, the ability to directly edit agent definitions inline (with a mandatory save gate that auto-creates a PR with file changes on save), a one-click option to update all agent models at once with a confirmation step, a repository display that shows only the repo name (not the owner) with dynamically fitted text, and an easy-to-use tools editor within each agent's configuration — so that I can efficiently create, discover, and maintain agents without leaving the page or relying on manual file edits.

## UI/UX Description

Each agent card should display a unique avatar built from a sun/moon visual theme — e.g., assigned deterministically based on agent name or ID using a palette of sun and moon icon variants (full moon, crescent, sun with rays, eclipse, etc.). The 'Featured Agents' section sits prominently at the top of the Agents page and shows up to 3 cards: prioritizing the top 3 most-used agents by invocation count, and supplementing with any agents created within the past 3 days if fewer than 3 high-usage agents exist. Inline editing of the agent definition should be accessible via an 'Edit' button on the agent detail view; the editor should support structured form fields (not raw file text) and show a persistent unsaved-changes banner/warning. If the user attempts to navigate away with unsaved changes, a blocking modal must confirm intent ('You have unsaved changes — save before leaving?'). On save, the system creates a GitHub PR with the updated agent config file changes and displays a link to the PR. A 'Update All Models' button (e.g., in a settings/actions toolbar on the page) triggers a confirmation dialog listing which agents and what model will be applied, requiring explicit user confirmation before proceeding. The Repository field on each agent card/detail should display only the repository name (e.g., 'my-repo') — not the full owner/repo path — and the text must dynamically scale or truncate with an ellipsis to fit within the styled background bubble/chip, using CSS techniques like `fit-content`, `text-overflow`, or dynamic font scaling. The tools section within each agent's configuration should render as an editable list — users can add, remove, or reorder tools via UI controls (checkboxes, drag-and-drop, or a multi-select dropdown), with changes reflected immediately in the unsaved-changes state.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST assign each agent a unique sun/moon themed avatar or icon, deterministically derived from the agent's identifier, selecting from a predefined set of sun and moon variants (e.g., full moon, crescent, sun, eclipse, sunrise).
- System MUST display a 'Featured Agents' section at the top of the Agents page showing up to 3 agents, prioritizing the top 3 agents by usage/invocation count; if fewer than 3 high-usage agents exist, the section MUST supplement with agents created within the past 3 days.
- System MUST allow users to edit agent definitions inline on the Agents page via a structured editor, and MUST display a persistent unsaved-changes indicator whenever the form has been modified but not yet saved.
- System MUST present a blocking confirmation modal when the user attempts to navigate away from an agent with unsaved changes, offering options to save or discard before leaving.
- System MUST create a GitHub Pull Request containing the updated agent configuration file changes when the user successfully saves an edited agent definition, and MUST display a link to the created PR in the UI.
- System MUST provide an 'Update All Models' action that, when triggered, displays a confirmation dialog listing all affected agents and the target model to be applied, and MUST only proceed with the bulk update upon explicit user confirmation.
- System MUST display the Repository field on agent cards and detail views using only the repository name (not the owner prefix), and MUST dynamically fit or scale the text to fill the styled background bubble/chip without overflow, using ellipsis truncation as a fallback.
- System MUST render the tools section of each agent's configuration as an interactive, editable list allowing users to add, remove, and reorder tools, with all modifications tracked as part of the agent's unsaved-changes state.
- System SHOULD validate that at least one tool remains assigned to an agent before allowing the user to save, displaying an inline error if the tools list is empty.
- System SHOULD show a success toast or notification after a PR is successfully created, including a clickable link to the PR URL.

## Technical Notes

Sun/moon avatars can be implemented using a deterministic hash of the agent ID mapped to an index in a curated SVG icon set (10–20 variants); consider a library like `boring-avatars` or a custom SVG sprite sheet. The inline editor should read and write agent config files (likely YAML/JSON) via a backend API; on save, the backend should use the GitHub REST API (Octokit) to create a new branch, commit the changed file, and open a PR against the default branch — store the GitHub token in server-side env vars. 'Update All Models' should call a batch API endpoint that accepts a target model ID and patches all agent configs; the confirmation dialog should be populated by fetching current agent metadata before display. For the dynamic repository name bubble, use CSS `max-width` + `text-overflow: ellipsis` with `overflow: hidden` and `white-space: nowrap`, or a JavaScript-based text-fit library for scaling; ensure the display name is parsed by splitting on '/' and taking the last segment. The tools editor state should be managed in local component state (or a form library like React Hook Form/Formik) and merged into the agent definition payload at save time.

mentioned_issues.title: Pipeline Page: Fix Model List, Tools Z-Index, Tile Dragging, Agent Clone, and Remove Add Stage
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> On the pipeline page,
> - The list of "Pipeline Model" is different than what is available in the Create Pipeline, "+ Add Agent", "Select model" dropdown. This list should be the available models from GitHub for running Custom GitHub Agents. This varies by user account.
> - When in Creating new Pipeline, "+ Add Agent", "+ Tools" the Tools module is hidden by other elements. It should be the top layer. 
> - When creating a new Pipeline configuration, the Status tiles should not be moveable. The Agent tiles should be moveable.
> - When in Creating new Pipeline, add a "clone" button to agents - so it creates a copy of the agent definition to be used on the Pipeline.
> - In the Pipeline Creation, remove "Add Stage"

## User Story

As a Solune pipeline builder, I want the Pipeline Creation page to correctly reflect available GitHub models per user account, render the Tools module above all other elements, restrict drag-and-drop to Agent tiles only, provide a clone button for agent definitions, and remove the unused 'Add Stage' control — so that the pipeline configuration experience is accurate, visually correct, and free of confusing or broken interactions.

## UI/UX Description

The Pipeline page requires five targeted fixes: (1) The 'Pipeline Model' dropdown in '+ Add Agent → Select model' must be dynamically populated from the authenticated user's available GitHub models for Custom GitHub Agents rather than a static/mismatched list — since this list varies per account, it must be fetched at runtime. (2) When a user opens '+ Add Agent → + Tools', the Tools module/popover must render at the highest z-index layer (above all cards, panels, and overlays) so it is never obscured by adjacent or parent elements. (3) On the pipeline canvas, Status tiles must be locked in place (no drag interaction, no move cursor) while Agent tiles remain fully draggable and repositionable; visual affordance (e.g., grab cursor) should only appear on Agent tiles. (4) Each Agent tile must display a 'Clone' button that, when clicked, creates a full deep copy of that agent's configuration (model, tools, parameters) as a new Agent tile on the pipeline, ready for independent editing. (5) The 'Add Stage' button/control must be removed entirely from the Pipeline Creation UI, cleaning up the interface.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST fetch the list of available GitHub models for Custom GitHub Agents dynamically from the authenticated user's GitHub account and populate the 'Select model' dropdown in '+ Add Agent' with that list, replacing any current static or mismatched model list.
- System MUST ensure the Tools module rendered via '+ Add Agent → + Tools' has a CSS z-index (or equivalent stacking context) higher than all surrounding pipeline canvas elements, panels, and overlays, so it is never hidden or clipped by other UI elements.
- System MUST disable drag-and-drop interactions entirely on Status tiles within the Pipeline Creation canvas — Status tiles must not be moveable, must not display a grab/move cursor, and must not respond to drag events.
- System MUST preserve full drag-and-drop reordering and repositioning functionality exclusively on Agent tiles within the Pipeline Creation canvas, with appropriate visual affordance (e.g., grab cursor on hover).
- System MUST provide a 'Clone' button on each Agent tile in the Pipeline Creation view that creates a complete deep copy of the agent definition — including its selected model, configured tools, and all other parameters — and inserts the cloned Agent tile into the pipeline as an independently editable instance.
- System MUST remove the 'Add Stage' button and all associated stage-creation logic from the Pipeline Creation UI.
- System SHOULD handle the case where the GitHub model list API call fails or returns an empty list gracefully, displaying a user-friendly error or fallback state in the 'Select model' dropdown rather than crashing or showing stale data.
- System SHOULD visually differentiate Status tiles from Agent tiles (e.g., locked icon, distinct border or cursor) to clearly communicate to users that Status tiles cannot be moved while Agent tiles can.

## Technical Notes

The dynamic GitHub model list for 'Select model' should be fetched from the GitHub API (e.g., GitHub Models endpoint or equivalent Custom GitHub Agents model availability API) using the current user's auth token at pipeline load time or when '+ Add Agent' is opened; responses should be cached per session to avoid redundant calls. The Tools module z-index bug is likely a CSS stacking context issue caused by a parent element with overflow:hidden, transform, or an explicit z-index — investigate the component hierarchy for '+ Add Agent' and ensure the Tools popover/modal is portaled to the document body or given a sufficiently high z-index (e.g., 9999). For drag-and-drop tile locking, check the existing DnD library (e.g., react-dnd, dnd-kit, or similar) used in the pipeline canvas and apply a `canDrag: () => false` guard or `disabled` prop specifically to Status tile drag sources. Agent cloning should perform a deep clone of the agent config object (avoid shallow copy pitfalls with nested tool arrays/objects) and assign a new unique ID to the cloned tile before adding it to the pipeline state.

mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> On the app user chat,
> - When the AI Enhance is disabled I receive an error. If the "AI Enhance" is disabled, use the user's exact chat input for the GitHub Parent Issue description but, use the Chat Agent to generate all the metadata needed for GitHub Issue creation (labels, estimates, title, etc) and add Agent Pipeline configuration information to description.
>  Error: I couldn't generate a task from your description. Please try again with more detail.

## User Story

As a Solune app user submitting a chat request with AI Enhance disabled, I want my exact chat input used as the GitHub Parent Issue description while the Chat Agent still generates all required metadata (title, labels, estimates, etc.) and Agent Pipeline configuration, so that I can create well-structured GitHub issues without needing AI content enhancement and without encountering the 'I couldn't generate a task from your description' error.

## UI/UX Description

When the user submits a chat message with AI Enhance toggled off, the system should silently bypass the AI enhancement step and proceed with a two-track pipeline: (1) use the user's verbatim chat input as the GitHub Parent Issue description body — no paraphrasing, summarizing, or reformatting — and (2) invoke the Chat Agent independently to generate all GitHub Issue metadata (title, labels, size estimates, assignees, priority, etc.) and append Agent Pipeline configuration details to the issue description. The user should never see the error message 'I couldn't generate a task from your description. Please try again with more detail.' when AI Enhance is disabled. The submission flow should feel seamless — no visible errors, no stalled states — and the resulting issue should reflect the raw user input in the description alongside fully AI-generated metadata fields.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST detect when the AI Enhance toggle is disabled before invoking any content generation pipeline and branch into the fallback metadata-only path.
- System MUST use the user's exact, unmodified chat input as the GitHub Parent Issue description body when AI Enhance is disabled — no summarization, paraphrasing, or reformatting of the description.
- System MUST invoke the Chat Agent to generate all required GitHub Issue metadata (title, labels, size estimate, priority, assignees, and any other structured fields) even when AI Enhance is disabled.
- System MUST append Agent Pipeline configuration information to the GitHub Parent Issue description when AI Enhance is disabled, in addition to the verbatim user input.
- System MUST NOT display the error message 'I couldn't generate a task from your description. Please try again with more detail.' when AI Enhance is disabled and the user has provided any non-empty chat input.
- System MUST suppress or reroute any error thrown by the AI enhancement step when the toggle is off, ensuring the fallback path completes successfully and creates the GitHub issue.
- System SHOULD validate that the Chat Agent metadata generation step succeeded independently of the AI Enhance step, and surface a specific, actionable error only if the metadata generation itself fails.
- System MUST ensure the final GitHub issue created with AI Enhance disabled is structurally identical to one created with AI Enhance enabled, differing only in that the description body is the raw user input rather than AI-enhanced content.

## Technical Notes

The root cause is likely that the issue creation pipeline assumes AI Enhance is always active and throws a generic catch-all error when the enhancement step returns nothing or fails silently — the error handler should check the AI Enhance flag before surfacing user-facing errors. Refactor the pipeline into two explicit branches: a full pipeline (AI Enhance on: enhance content → generate metadata → build issue) and a metadata-only pipeline (AI Enhance off: pass-through raw input → invoke Chat Agent for metadata → append Agent Pipeline config → build issue). The Chat Agent metadata generation call should be decoupled from the AI Enhance step so it can run independently in both paths. Ensure the Agent Pipeline configuration block appended to the description is clearly delimited (e.g., a markdown section) so it does not visually blend with the user's raw input.

closing_issues.title: Chores Page: Counter Fixes, Featured Rituals Panel, Inline Editing, AI Enhance Toggle, Agent Pipeline Config & Auto-Merge PR Flow
closing_issues.body:
## Original Request

> On chores page,
> - Ensure that the counters for Chores with "Every x issues" is counting down how many GitHub Parent Issues have been created since the last time that particular Chore has run. This is the counter on the tile and the trigger event
> - In the Featured Rituals panel, show the next run, most recently run, and most run Chores
> - The user should be able to edit the Chore definition directly. They must save the page before leaving. If they save, create a PR with updated file changes to Chores.
> - Similar to "+ Add Agent" pop-out on Agents page, add a feature to allow the user to "AI Enhance" toggle on/off. If "AI Enhance" is enabled - keep the flow the same. If the "AI Enhance" is disabled, use the user's exact chat input for the GitHub Issue Template creation but, use the Chat Agent to generate all the metadata needed for GitHub Template creation (name, about, title, labels, etc)
> - Chores should be able to configure a selected saved Agent Pipeline configuration or "Auto". Auto, will use the currently selected Agent Pipeline configuration for a given Project.
> - The PR created for a new Chore being created, should prompt the user with a double confirmation when saving. To inform the user the Chore will be automatically added to the code repo. After creating the GitHub Issue and PR - automatically merge the PR into main to create a new Chore.

## User Story

As a project maintainer using the Chores page, I want accurate 'Every x issues' countdown counters based on GitHub Parent Issue creation, a Featured Rituals panel surfacing next/recent/most-run Chores, inline editable Chore definitions that generate PRs on save with auto-merge, an 'AI Enhance' toggle that controls whether user chat input or AI-generated content drives GitHub Issue Template creation, and per-Chore Agent Pipeline configuration (saved config or Auto), so that Chores are reliably triggered, discoverable, configurable, and self-managing within the codebase with minimal manual overhead.

## UI/UX Description

The Chores page receives several layered UX enhancements: (1) Each Chore tile's counter badge must visually reflect the count of GitHub Parent Issues created since that Chore last ran — not a generic global counter — updating in real time or on page refresh. The tile counter and the trigger evaluation logic must both use this same scoped count. (2) A 'Featured Rituals' panel (sidebar or top section) displays three highlighted Chores: 'Next Run' (soonest to trigger), 'Most Recently Run' (last execution timestamp), and 'Most Run' (highest all-time execution count), each shown as a card with Chore name, relevant stat, and a quick-action link. (3) Chore definitions are directly editable inline on the page — fields render as editable inputs/textareas rather than read-only text. A persistent 'Save' button and unsaved-changes indicator (e.g., dirty-state banner or asterisk in the page title) must appear when edits are detected. Navigation away without saving prompts a 'You have unsaved changes' confirmation modal. On save, a PR is created containing the updated Chore definition file changes. (4) An 'AI Enhance' toggle is added to the Chore creation/editing flow, styled and positioned similarly to the '+ Add Agent' pop-out on the Agents page. When ON (default), the existing AI-driven GitHub Issue Template generation flow is preserved. When OFF, the user's exact chat input is used verbatim as the Issue Template body, but the Chat Agent is still invoked to generate all GitHub Issue Template metadata (name, about, title, labels, assignees, etc.) without modifying the body content. (5) A per-Chore 'Agent Pipeline' selector (dropdown or segmented control) allows choosing a saved Agent Pipeline configuration or 'Auto'. 'Auto' inherits the currently active Agent Pipeline configuration for the given Project. (6) When a user saves a brand-new Chore, a double-confirmation modal appears: first confirmation warns that the Chore will be automatically committed to the code repository; second confirmation is a final 'Yes, create Chore' action. After both confirmations, the system creates a GitHub Issue, opens a PR with the new Chore file, and automatically merges that PR into main.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST recalculate each Chore's 'Every x issues' counter by querying the number of GitHub Parent Issues created since the timestamp of that Chore's last execution, scoping the count per-Chore rather than globally
- System MUST use this per-Chore Parent Issue count as both the displayed counter on the tile UI and as the condition evaluated when determining if the Chore's trigger threshold has been met
- System MUST display a 'Featured Rituals' panel on the Chores page containing three distinct Chore highlight cards: 'Next Run' (lowest remaining issues until trigger), 'Most Recently Run' (most recent last_run_at timestamp), and 'Most Run' (highest total execution count)
- System MUST render Chore definition fields as editable inputs/textareas and display a dirty-state indicator (unsaved changes banner or title asterisk) whenever any field value differs from the last saved state
- System MUST prompt the user with a 'You have unsaved changes — are you sure you want to leave?' confirmation dialog when navigating away from the Chores page with unsaved edits
- System MUST, upon saving an edited Chore definition, open a Pull Request against the repository containing the updated Chore definition file(s) with an auto-generated PR title and description summarizing the changes
- System MUST provide an 'AI Enhance' toggle on the Chore creation/edit form, co-located with the flow controls similarly to the '+ Add Agent' pop-out on the Agents page; when toggled OFF, the user's exact chat input MUST be used verbatim as the GitHub Issue Template body while the Chat Agent is still invoked to generate all template metadata (name, about, title, labels, etc.) without altering the body
- System MUST provide a per-Chore 'Agent Pipeline' configuration selector with options for each saved Agent Pipeline configuration and an 'Auto' option; 'Auto' MUST resolve to the currently active Agent Pipeline configuration for the associated Project at execution time
- System MUST display a two-step confirmation modal when saving a new Chore: step 1 informs the user the Chore file will be automatically added to the code repository and asks for acknowledgment; step 2 presents a final 'Yes, Create Chore' confirmation before proceeding
- System MUST, after both confirmations are accepted for a new Chore, sequentially: create a GitHub Issue for the Chore, open a PR containing the new Chore definition file, and automatically merge that PR into the main branch
- System SHOULD surface merge status (success/failure) of the auto-merge PR back to the user via a toast notification or status indicator on the Chores page
- System SHOULD handle PR merge conflicts or CI failures on the auto-merge gracefully by notifying the user and leaving the PR open for manual resolution rather than silently failing

## Technical Notes

The per-Chore issue counter requires a query filtered by Chore ID and bounded by the Chore's last_run_at timestamp — store last_run_at and execution_count on each Chore record in the database and index on chore_id + created_at for performance. The 'AI Enhance' toggle OFF path should call the Chat Agent with a structured prompt requesting only metadata fields (name, about, title, labels) while injecting the raw user input as a pre-filled, locked body field before constructing the GitHub Issue Template payload. Agent Pipeline resolution for 'Auto' should be a runtime lookup against the Project's active pipeline config, not a cached value stored on the Chore, to ensure it always reflects the current project setting. PR creation and auto-merge for new/edited Chores should use the GitHub API (octokit or equivalent) with merge method 'squash' or 'merge' per project convention; auto-merge failures must be caught and surfaced as actionable errors without blocking the Chore record from being persisted locally.

mentioned_issues.title: Project Board: Parent Issue Hierarchy, Sub-Issue Display Improvements, Agent Pipeline Fixes & Functional Filters
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> On project page,
> - Only show Parent GitHub Issues on the Project Board
> - The GitHub Sub Issue list should be collapsible, in the GitHub Parent card
> - The assigned Agent and Model should be on each GitHub Sub Issue tile shown in the GitHub Parent card
> - The GitHub Parent Issue labels should be displayed on the card
> - Some models are missing from being displayed on the agents in the Agent Pipeline
> - Some tool counts are missing from being displayed on the agents in the Agent Pipeline
> - 'Custom' on the Agent Pipeline, should update it's name to a "saved pipeline configuration's name" if the user selects a saved configuration.
> - The columns in the Project Board should be scrollable
> - Update the Filter, Sort, and Group By buttons to actually function - this should be in relation to the GitHub Parent Issues on the Project Board

## User Story

As a project manager using the Project Board, I want parent GitHub Issues to be the primary unit of display with collapsible sub-issue lists inside each parent card — showing agent assignments, model names, and labels — so that I can maintain a clean, organized board view while still accessing granular sub-issue detail on demand. I also need the Agent Pipeline to correctly display all model names and tool counts, rename 'Custom' to the saved configuration name when applicable, and have fully functional Filter, Sort, and Group By controls so I can navigate and prioritize work efficiently.

## UI/UX Description

The Project Board columns must only render GitHub Parent Issues as top-level cards; sub-issues are nested within each parent card in a collapsible section (collapsed by default, toggleable via a chevron/arrow icon). Each sub-issue tile inside the collapsed panel displays the assigned Agent name and Model name prominently. Parent Issue cards display all associated GitHub labels as colored label chips (matching GitHub label colors). Columns must be independently vertically scrollable (overflow-y: auto) so long columns do not overflow the viewport. The Agent Pipeline panel must render every available model name without omission and show accurate tool counts on each agent tile — both are likely data-binding bugs requiring audit. The 'Custom' label on the Agent Pipeline header/selector must dynamically update to reflect the name of any saved pipeline configuration the user selects, reverting to 'Custom' only when no named configuration is active. mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> On Agents page,
> - Agents should have unique sun/moon themed avatars/icons
> - "Featured Agents" should show the top 3 used agents, or any agents created in the past 3 days
> - The user should be able to edit the agent definition directly. They must save the page before leaving. If they save, create a PR with updated file changes to agents.
> - Add an option to update all Agent models at once, ensure confirmation from the user
> - Repository - should be the repo name, not the owner. Fit text to background bubble dynamically
> - The user should be able to easily edit/update the tools an Agent has defined in it's configuration

## User Story

As a user managing agents on the Agents page, I want a polished and fully interactive agent management experience — including unique sun/moon themed avatars, a 'Featured Agents' section surfacing the top 3 most-used or recently created agents, the ability to directly edit agent definitions inline (with a mandatory save gate that auto-creates a PR with file changes on save), a one-click option to update all agent models at once with a confirmation step, a repository display that shows only the repo name (not the owner) with dynamically fitted text, and an easy-to-use tools editor within each agent's configuration — so that I can efficiently create, discover, and maintain agents without leaving the page or relying on manual file edits.

## UI/UX Description

Each agent card should display a unique avatar built from a sun/moon visual theme — e.g., assigned deterministically based on agent name or ID using a palette of sun and moon icon variants (full moon, crescent, sun with rays, eclipse, etc.). The 'Featured Agents' section sits prominently at the top of the Agents page and shows up to 3 cards: prioritizing the top 3 most-used agents by invocation count, and supplementing with any agents created within the past 3 days if fewer than 3 high-usage agents exist. Inline editing of the agent definition should be accessible via an 'Edit' button on the agent detail view; the editor should support structured form fields (not raw file text) and show a persistent unsaved-changes banner/warning. If the user attempts to navigate away with unsaved changes, a blocking modal must confirm intent ('You have unsaved changes — save before leaving?'). On save, the system creates a GitHub PR with the updated agent config file changes and displays a link to the PR. A 'Update All Models' button (e.g., in a settings/actions toolbar on the page) triggers a confirmation dialog listing which agents and what model will be applied, requiring explicit user confirmation before proceeding. The Repository field on each agent card/detail should display only the repository name (e.g., 'my-repo') — not the full owner/repo path — and the text must dynamically scale or truncate with an ellipsis to fit within the styled background bubble/chip, using CSS techniques like `fit-content`, `text-overflow`, or dynamic font scaling. The tools section within each agent's configuration should render as an editable list — users can add, remove, or reorder tools via UI controls (checkboxes, drag-and-drop, or a multi-select dropdown), with changes reflected immediately in the unsaved-changes state.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST assign each agent a unique sun/moon themed avatar or icon, deterministically derived from the agent's identifier, selecting from a predefined set of sun and moon variants (e.g., full moon, crescent, sun, eclipse, sunrise).
- System MUST display a 'Featured Agents' section at the top of the Agents page showing up to 3 agents, prioritizing the top 3 agents by usage/invocation count; if fewer than 3 high-usage agents exist, the section MUST supplement with agents created within the past 3 days.
- System MUST allow users to edit agent definitions inline on the Agents page via a structured editor, and MUST display a persistent unsaved-changes indicator whenever the form has been modified but not yet saved.
- System MUST present a blocking confirmation modal when the user attempts to navigate away from an agent with unsaved changes, offering options to save or discard before leaving.
- System MUST create a GitHub Pull Request containing the updated agent configuration file changes when the user successfully saves an edited agent definition, and MUST display a link to the created PR in the UI.
- System MUST provide an 'Update All Models' action that, when triggered, displays a confirmation dialog listing all affected agents and the target model to be applied, and MUST only proceed with the bulk update upon explicit user confirmation.
- System MUST display the Repository field on agent cards and detail views using only the repository name (not the owner prefix), and MUST dynamically fit or scale the text to fill the styled background bubble/chip without overflow, using ellipsis truncation as a fallback.
- System MUST render the tools section of each agent's configuration as an interactive, editable list allowing users to add, remove, and reorder tools, with all modifications tracked as part of the agent's unsaved-changes state.
- System SHOULD validate that at least one tool remains assigned to an agent before allowing the user to save, displaying an inline error if the tools list is empty.
- System SHOULD show a success toast or notification after a PR is successfully created, including a clickable link to the PR URL.

## Technical Notes

Sun/moon avatars can be implemented using a deterministic hash of the agent ID mapped to an index in a curated SVG icon set (10–20 variants); consider a library like `boring-avatars` or a custom SVG sprite sheet. The inline editor should read and write agent config files (likely YAML/JSON) via a backend API; on save, the backend should use the GitHub REST API (Octokit) to create a new branch, commit the changed file, and open a PR against the default branch — store the GitHub token in server-side env vars. 'Update All Models' should call a batch API endpoint that accepts a target model ID and patches all agent configs; the confirmation dialog should be populated by fetching current agent metadata before display. For the dynamic repository name bubble, use CSS `max-width` + `text-overflow: ellipsis` with `overflow: hidden` and `white-space: nowrap`, or a JavaScript-based text-fit library for scaling; ensure the display name is parsed by splitting on '/' and taking the last segment. The tools editor state should be managed in local component state (or a form library like React Hook Form/Formik) and merged into the agent definition payload at save time.
