mentioned_issues.title: Fix 'Every X Issues' Chore Counter to Only Count GitHub Parent Issues (Excluding Chores and Sub-Issues)
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Ensure that the counters for Chores with "Every x issues" is counting down how many GitHub Parent Issues have been created since the last time that particular Chore has run. This is the counter on the tile and the trigger event. Other Chores do not count towards the counter. Sub Issues do not count towards the counter. ONLY GitHub Parent Issues that are not Chores count towards the counter.

## User Story

As a Solune user managing Chores with an 'Every X Issues' trigger, I want the countdown counter — shown on the Chore tile and used as the trigger evaluation — to accurately reflect only the number of GitHub Parent Issues created since that specific Chore last ran, so that Chores fire at the correct cadence without being skewed by unrelated Chores or Sub-Issues inflating the count.

## UI/UX Description

The Chore tile displays a counter representing progress toward the 'Every X Issues' threshold. This counter must visually reflect only qualifying GitHub Parent Issues — issues that are not Chores and not Sub-Issues — created since the last execution of that specific Chore. The counter on the tile and the internal trigger evaluation logic must both derive from the same filtered dataset. No other issue type (Chores or Sub-Issues) should appear to increment the counter. The counter should reset after the Chore runs and begin accumulating again from zero based only on new qualifying Parent Issues.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST count only GitHub Parent Issues created after the last run timestamp of a given Chore when evaluating the 'Every X Issues' trigger condition.
- System MUST exclude all issues tagged or classified as Chores from the 'Every X Issues' counter, regardless of whether they are parent or child issues.
- System MUST exclude all Sub-Issues (GitHub child/sub issues) from the 'Every X Issues' counter — only top-level, non-Chore GitHub issues qualify.
- System MUST use the same filtered issue count for both the visual counter displayed on the Chore tile and the internal trigger evaluation logic, ensuring consistency between what the user sees and when the Chore fires.
- System MUST scope the counter independently per Chore — each Chore tracks its own count from its own last-run timestamp, so one Chore running does not affect another Chore's counter.
- System MUST reset the qualifying issue counter for a Chore to zero (or re-anchor the baseline timestamp) immediately after that Chore successfully executes.
- System SHOULD accurately identify Sub-Issues using GitHub's issue relationship metadata (e.g., parent/child linkage via 'sub_issues' or tracked-in relationships) to reliably exclude them from the count.
- System MUST NOT count the same GitHub Parent Issue toward multiple Chore counters in a way that would cause double-triggering — each Chore independently evaluates against its own last-run baseline.

## Technical Notes

The fix requires auditing the issue-fetching or counter-aggregation logic tied to the 'Every X Issues' Chore trigger. The query or filter that populates the counter must apply three exclusions: (1) filter out issues whose type/label/classification marks them as a Chore, (2) filter out Sub-Issues by checking GitHub's parent-issue linkage (e.g., absence of a parent issue ID, or checking the 'sub_issues_summary' field on the GitHub Issues API), and (3) anchor the count window to the specific Chore's last-run timestamp rather than a global or shared baseline. The Chore tile UI counter and the trigger evaluation should share a single source-of-truth function to avoid drift. Branch 'copilot/fix-chores-page-counters' appears directly relevant and should be used as the development base.

closing_issues.title: feat: Blocking Queue — Serial Issue Activation & Branch Ancestry Control via Chores, Pipelines, and #block Chat Command
closing_issues.body:
## Original Request

> # Plan: Blocking Feature for Issue Activation & Branching
> 
> ## TL;DR
> Add a "Blocking" toggle to Chores, Pipelines, and a `#block` magic word in chat. When blocking issues exist, they serialize issue activation and control branch ancestry — only one issue runs agents at a time, and subsequent issues branch from the oldest open blocking issue's branch instead of `main`. When all blocking issues complete, branching returns to `main`.
> 
> ## Confirmed Decisions
> - **Scope**: Per-repository blocking queue (not per-project)
> - **Pipeline-level toggle**: ALL issues from a blocking pipeline are blocking
> - **Non-blocking concurrency**: When no blocking issues exist, multiple non-blocking issues can be active simultaneously (current behavior preserved)
> - **Branch target**: When blocking issues activate, they ALL branch from the oldest open blocking issue's branch (not chained)
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Phase 1: Database & Models
> 
> ### Step 1.1 — New migration: `017_blocking_queue.sql`
> - New table `blocking_queue`:
>   - `id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT
>   - `repo_key` TEXT NOT NULL (formatted as `owner/repo`)
>   - `issue_number` INTEGER NOT NULL
>   - `project_id` TEXT NOT NULL
>   - `is_blocking` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
>   - `queue_status` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK IN ('pending','active','in_review','completed')
>   - `parent_branch` TEXT (the branch this issue targets as base_ref)
>   - `blocking_source_issue` INTEGER (which blocking issue provided the parent branch)
>   - `created_at` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
>   - `activated_at` TEXT
>   - `completed_at` TEXT
>   - UNIQUE(repo_key, issue_number)
> - Add `blocking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` column to `pipeline_configs` table
> - Add `blocking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` column to `chores` table
> 
> ### Step 1.2 — Backend models
> - New file: `backend/src/models/blocking.py`
>   - `BlockingQueueEntry` — Pydantic model mirroring the DB row
>   - `BlockingQueueStatus` — StrEnum: pending, active, in_review, completed
> - Update `backend/src/models/pipeline.py`: add `blocking: bool = False` to `PipelineConfig`
> - Update `backend/src/models/chores.py`: add `blocking: bool = False` to `Chore`, `ChoreCreate`, `ChoreUpdate`
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Phase 2: Blocking Queue Service (Core Engine)
> 
> ### Step 2.1 — New service: `backend/src/services/blocking_queue.py`
> Central service managing the blocking queue state machine. Key functions:
> 
> | Function | Purpose |
> |----------|---------|
> | `enqueue_issue(repo_key, issue_number, project_id, is_blocking)` | Insert into blocking_queue table, determine initial activation |
> | `get_base_ref_for_issue(repo_key, issue_number)` | Return oldest open blocking issue's branch, or `"main"` |
> | `mark_active(repo_key, issue_number, parent_branch)` | Update queue_status to active, set parent_branch, activated_at |
> | `mark_in_review(repo_key, issue_number)` | Update queue_status to in_review, trigger `try_activate_next()` |
> | `mark_completed(repo_key, issue_number)` | Update queue_status to completed, recalculate base branch, trigger activation |
> | `try_activate_next(repo_key)` | **Core logic** — activate next pending issue(s) per the rules |
> | `get_current_base_branch(repo_key)` | Returns oldest open blocking issue's branch, or `"main"` |
> | `has_open_blocking_issues(repo_key)` | Quick boolean check for gating |
> 
> **Activation rules** (matching the user's 8-issue example):
> - Non-blocking issues with no open blocking issues → activate immediately (current behavior)
> - Any blocking issue open → serial activation, one at a time
> - When active issue(s) → "In review": activate next batch:
>   - Non-blocking issues activate together up to the next blocking entry
>   - Blocking entries activate alone
> - Activated issues branch from the oldest open blocking issue's branch
> - When a blocking issue completes: base branch shifts to next oldest open blocking issue, or `"main"` if none remain
> 
> ### Step 2.2 — Persistence layer: `backend/src/services/blocking_queue_store.py`
> - SQLite CRUD operations using existing `get_db()` pattern from chores/pipelines
> - Methods: insert, update_status, get_by_repo, get_by_issue, get_pending, get_open_blocking
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Phase 3: Backend Integration
> 
> ### Step 3.1 — Modify orchestrator base_ref resolution (*depends on Phase 2*)
> **File**: `backend/src/services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py` (~line 800-1000)
> - Before the existing base_ref logic, call `blocking_queue.get_base_ref_for_issue(repo_key, issue_number)`
> - If the issue is the FIRST agent assignment (no existing main branch), use the blocking queue's base_ref instead of hardcoded `"main"`
> - If a main branch already exists (subsequent agents), keep current behavior (branch from main branch name)
> 
> ### Step 3.2 — Modify orchestrator issue creation flow (*depends on Phase 2*)
> **File**: `backend/src/services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py` (`execute_full_workflow()` ~line 2002)
> - After issue creation, call `blocking_queue.enqueue_issue()`
> - Check if issue should activate immediately
> - If NOT activated: skip agent assignment, store issue as "pending" in queue, return WorkflowResult with pending status
> - If activated: proceed with current flow (assign first agent, start polling)
> 
> ### Step 3.3 — Modify pipeline polling for activation (*depends on Phase 2*)
> **File**: `backend/src/services/copilot_polling/pipeline.py`
> - In status transition handler (when an issue moves to "In review"):
>   - Call `blocking_queue.mark_in_review(repo_key, issue_number)`
>   - Get list of newly activated issues from `try_activate_next()`
>   - For each activated issue: trigger `assign_agent_for_status()`
> - In completion handler (when an issue is done):
>   - Call `blocking_queue.mark_completed(repo_key, issue_number)`
>   - Get list of newly activated issues from `try_activate_next()`
>   - For each activated issue: trigger agent assignment
> 
> ### Step 3.4 — Chat `#block` parsing (*parallel with steps 3.1-3.3*)
> **File**: `backend/src/api/chat.py`
> - Add new Priority 0.5 (between `#agent` and feature request):
>   - Detect `#block` anywhere in message content (not just prefix)
>   - Strip `#block` from content before passing to downstream intent processing
>   - Set `is_blocking=True` flag on the resulting issue recommendation / task proposal
>   - Pass `is_blocking` through `confirm_proposal()` → `execute_full_workflow()`
> 
> ### Step 3.5 — Modify chore trigger (*parallel with steps 3.1-3.3*)
> **Files**: `backend/src/api/chores.py` / `backend/src/services/chores/service.py`
> - In `trigger_chore()`: read `chore.blocking` flag
> - Pass `is_blocking` to orchestrator's `execute_full_workflow()`
> - Also check the assigned pipeline's blocking flag if chore doesn't have its own
> 
> ### Step 3.6 — Modify pipeline config API (*parallel with steps 3.1-3.3*)
> **Files**: `backend/src/api/pipelines.py` / `backend/src/services/pipelines/service.py`
> - Add `blocking` field to create/update pipeline endpoints
> - Store in `pipeline_configs.blocking` column
> - Return `blocking` in pipeline config responses
> 
> ### Step 3.7 — Modify chore config API (*parallel with steps 3.1-3.3*)
> **Files**: `backend/src/api/chores.py` / `backend/src/services/chores/service.py`
> - Add `blocking` field to `ChoreUpdate` model
> - Store in `chores.blocking` column
> - Return `blocking` in chore responses
> 
> ### Step 3.8 — WebSocket notifications (*depends on 3.3*)
> - Broadcast `blocking_queue_updated` event when issues activate/complete
> - Include: repo_key, activated_issues, completed_issues, current_base_branch
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Phase 4: Frontend Integration
> 
> ### Step 4.1 — TypeScript types (*parallel with Phase 3*)
> - Update pipeline types to include `blocking: boolean`
> - Update chore types to include `blocking: boolean`
> - Add `BlockingQueueEntry` type
> - Add `isBlocking` option to chat message send
> 
> ### Step 4.2 — Pipeline blocking toggle (*depends on 4.1*)
> **File**: `frontend/src/components/pipeline/PipelineBoard.tsx` or `SavedWorkflowsList.tsx`
> - Add a toggle switch for `blocking` on pipeline config
> - Use `usePipelineConfig` hook's mutation to persist
> 
> ### Step 4.3 — Chore blocking toggle (*depends on 4.1*)
> **File**: `frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx`
> - Add a toggle switch for `blocking` (follow `ai_enhance_enabled` toggle pattern)
> - Use `useUpdateChore` mutation to persist
> 
> ### Step 4.4 — Chat `#block` support (*depends on 4.1*)

- System MUST create a new SQLite migration `017_blocking_queue.sql` with table `blocking_queue` containing columns: `id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, `repo_key` TEXT NOT NULL (formatted `owner/repo`), `issue_number` INTEGER NOT NULL, `project_id` TEXT NOT NULL, `is_blocking` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, `queue_status` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK IN ('pending','active','in_review','completed'), `parent_branch` TEXT, `blocking_source_issue` INTEGER, `created_at` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')), `activated_at` TEXT, `completed_at` TEXT, and UNIQUE(repo_key, issue_number); and MUST add `blocking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` to both `pipeline_configs` and `chores` tables.
- System MUST implement `backend/src/models/blocking.py` with a `BlockingQueueEntry` Pydantic model mirroring all DB columns and a `BlockingQueueStatus` StrEnum with values: pending, active, in_review, completed; and MUST add `blocking: bool = False` to `PipelineConfig` in `pipeline.py` and to `Chore`, `ChoreCreate`, and `ChoreUpdate` in `chores.py`.
- System MUST implement `backend/src/services/blocking_queue.py` with functions: `enqueue_issue(repo_key, issue_number, project_id, is_blocking)`, `get_base_ref_for_issue(repo_key, issue_number)` returning the oldest open blocking issue's branch or `'main'`, `mark_active(repo_key, issue_number, parent_branch)`, `mark_in_review(repo_key, issue_number)`, `mark_completed(repo_key, issue_number)`, `try_activate_next(repo_key)` (the core state machine), `get_current_base_branch(repo_key)`, and `has_open_blocking_issues(repo_key)`; activation rules: non-blocking issues with no open blocking issues activate immediately (preserving existing concurrency), any open blocking issue enforces serial activation one at a time, when active issues move to 'in_review' the next batch activates (non-blocking issues together up to the next blocking entry, blocking entries alone), and all newly activated issues branch from the oldest open blocking issue's branch.
- System MUST implement `backend/src/services/blocking_queue_store.py` using the existing `get_db()` SQLite pattern with methods: insert, update_status, get_by_repo, get_by_issue, get_pending, and get_open_blocking.
- System MUST modify `workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py` so that: (a) in `execute_full_workflow()` after issue creation, `enqueue_issue()` is called and if the issue is not immediately activated the function returns a WorkflowResult with pending status and skips agent assignment; (b) in base_ref resolution (lines ~800-1000), for the FIRST agent assignment `blocking_queue.get_base_ref_for_issue()` is used instead of hardcoded `'main'`, while subsequent agents on an already-branched issue retain current behavior.

- System MUST add `blocking` boolean field to pipeline create/update/read endpoints (`api/pipelines.py`, `services/pipelines/service.py`) and to chore trigger and CRUD endpoints (`api/chores.py`, `services/chores/service.py`); chore trigger MUST also inherit the blocking flag from its assigned pipeline if the chore's own flag is not set.

This is a 4-phase implementation: Phase 1 (DB + models), Phase 2 (blocking_queue service — the state machine core), Phase 3 (backend integration across orchestrator, polling, chat, chores, pipelines APIs), Phase 4 (frontend toggles, indicators, WebSocket-driven UI). > - **Scope**: Per-repository blocking queue (not per-project)

- System MUST create a new SQLite migration `017_blocking_queue.sql` with table `blocking_queue` containing columns: `id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, `repo_key` TEXT NOT NULL (formatted `owner/repo`), `issue_number` INTEGER NOT NULL, `project_id` TEXT NOT NULL, `is_blocking` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, `queue_status` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK IN ('pending','active','in_review','completed'), `parent_branch` TEXT, `blocking_source_issue` INTEGER, `created_at` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')), `activated_at` TEXT, `completed_at` TEXT, and UNIQUE(repo_key, issue_number); and MUST add `blocking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` to both `pipeline_configs` and `chores` tables.
- System MUST implement `backend/src/models/blocking.py` with a `BlockingQueueEntry` Pydantic model mirroring all DB columns and a `BlockingQueueStatus` StrEnum with values: pending, active, in_review, completed; and MUST add `blocking: bool = False` to `PipelineConfig` in `pipeline.py` and to `Chore`, `ChoreCreate`, and `ChoreUpdate` in `chores.py`.
- System MUST implement `backend/src/services/blocking_queue.py` with functions: `enqueue_issue(repo_key, issue_number, project_id, is_blocking)`, `get_base_ref_for_issue(repo_key, issue_number)` returning the oldest open blocking issue's branch or `'main'`, `mark_active(repo_key, issue_number, parent_branch)`, `mark_in_review(repo_key, issue_number)`, `mark_completed(repo_key, issue_number)`, `try_activate_next(repo_key)` (the core state machine), `get_current_base_branch(repo_key)`, and `has_open_blocking_issues(repo_key)`; activation rules: non-blocking issues with no open blocking issues activate immediately (preserving existing concurrency), any open blocking issue enforces serial activation one at a time, when active issues move to 'in_review' the next batch activates (non-blocking issues together up to the next blocking entry, blocking entries alone), and all newly activated issues branch from the oldest open blocking issue's branch.
- System MUST implement `backend/src/services/blocking_queue_store.py` using the existing `get_db()` SQLite pattern with methods: insert, update_status, get_by_repo, get_by_issue, get_pending, and get_open_blocking.
- System MUST modify `workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py` so that: (a) in `execute_full_workflow()` after issue creation, `enqueue_issue()` is called and if the issue is not immediately activated the function returns a WorkflowResult with pending status and skips agent assignment; (b) in base_ref resolution (lines ~800-1000), for the FIRST agent assignment `blocking_queue.get_base_ref_for_issue()` is used instead of hardcoded `'main'`, while subsequent agents on an already-branched issue retain current behavior.
- System MUST modify `copilot_polling/pipeline.py` and `completion.py` so that on 'In review' transition `mark_in_review()` is called and each newly activated issue from `try_activate_next()` triggers `assign_agent_for_status()`; on issue completion `mark_completed()` is called and the same activation cascade runs.
- System MUST detect `#block` anywhere (not just as a prefix) in chat message content in `backend/src/api/chat.py`, strip it before passing to downstream intent processing (Priority 0.5, between `#agent` handling and feature-request handling), and propagate `is_blocking=True` through `confirm_proposal()` to `execute_full_workflow()`.
- System MUST add `blocking` boolean field to pipeline create/update/read endpoints (`api/pipelines.py`, `services/pipelines/service.py`) and to chore trigger and CRUD endpoints (`api/chores.py`, `services/chores/service.py`); chore trigger MUST also inherit the blocking flag from its assigned pipeline if the chore's own flag is not set.
- System MUST broadcast a `blocking_queue_updated` WebSocket event containing `repo_key`, `activated_issues`, `completed_issues`, and `current_base_branch` whenever issues activate or complete; and MUST surface a user-facing toast notification reading 'Issue #X is now active — agents starting' for newly activated previously-pending issues.
- System MUST use SQLite transactions and a per-repo service-layer lock in `blocking_queue.py` to prevent double-activation race conditions; and on container/polling-loop startup MUST call `try_activate_next()` for all repos with non-completed queue entries to recover from any missed activations during downtime.
- System MUST include unit tests for the blocking queue state machine validating an 8-issue activation scenario (creation order, activation order, branch sources, completion cascades); unit tests for `#block` detection and stripping in `chat.py`; integration tests for chore trigger with `blocking=True` and pipeline-level blocking; and the `blocking` field MUST be returned in all pipeline and chore API responses so frontend toggles reflect persisted state.
- System SHOULD add `#block` to ChatInterface command autocomplete and render a visual badge when `#block` is present in the composer; SHOULD display a 🔒 icon or 'Blocking' badge on blocking issue cards and 'Pending (blocked)' status on queued issues; and SHOULD provide a tooltip or sidebar visualization of the current per-repo blocking chain including ordered queue and current base branch.

## Technical Notes

This is a 4-phase implementation: Phase 1 (DB + models), Phase 2 (blocking_queue service — the state machine core), Phase 3 (backend integration across orchestrator, polling, chat, chores, pipelines APIs), Phase 4 (frontend toggles, indicators, WebSocket-driven UI). Phase 3 steps 3.4–3.7 are parallelizable with 3.1–3.3 but all depend on Phase 2 being complete. The `try_activate_next()` function is the most critical and risk-prone piece — it must handle the exact activation rules: non-blocking issues batch together when no blocking issues are open, blocking issues activate one-at-a-time, and all activated issues receive `get_current_base_branch()` (oldest open blocking issue's branch or `'main'`) as their base_ref, NOT a chained approach. SQLite transactions with a per-repo advisory lock (e.g., a threading.Lock keyed by repo_key held in the service layer) are required to prevent race conditions on concurrent status transitions. The recovery path on startup (calling `try_activate_next()` for all repos with pending queue entries) is mandatory for correctness after container restarts. Frontend blocking toggles should follow the `ai_enhance_enabled` toggle pattern already present in ChoreCard; `#block` parsing in chat.py must be case-insensitive and strip the token regardless of position in the message. Scope exclusions to enforce: no UI for reordering the queue, no cross-repo blocking, no retroactive blocking of existing open issues, no blocking for draft items, no admin force-activate override.

mentioned_issues.title: Implement Confirmation Dialog for Critical User Actions
mentioned_issues.body:
## Overview
Add a confirmation step to safeguard critical or destructive user actions (e.g., deletions, submissions, irreversible changes) within Project Solune. This ensures users are prompted to verify their intent before the action is executed, reducing accidental data loss or unintended operations.

## Technical Details
- Identify all critical user actions across the application that require a confirmation step
- Design and implement a reusable confirmation dialog/modal component
- Ensure the dialog clearly communicates the action being confirmed and its consequences
- Handle both confirm and cancel outcomes gracefully, including any async operations
- Ensure accessibility compliance (keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, focus management)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All critical/destructive actions trigger a confirmation prompt before execution
- [ ] Confirmation dialog displays a clear, human-readable description of the action and its impact
- [ ] Cancelling the dialog aborts the action with no side effects
- [ ] The confirmation component is reusable and can be applied across different parts of the application
- [ ] Dialog meets accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA) including keyboard and screen reader support

mentioned_issues.title: DRY Logging & Error Handling Modernization: Activate Dead Helpers, Migrate HTTPException → AppException, Add Frontend Toast/Logger/ErrorAlert
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> # Plan: DRY Logging & Error Handling Modernization
> 
> The backend has solid foundations (structured logging, redaction, AppException hierarchy, correlation IDs) but **26+ endpoints use raw `HTTPException`** instead of `AppException`, and the existing `handle_service_error()` helper is **dead code** despite 18 places manually replicating its pattern. The frontend has **no shared error component**, **no toast system**, 7+ silent catches, and mutations missing `onError`. This plan standardizes both sides with targeted, DRY changes.
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Phase 1: Backend — Adopt Existing Helpers & Eliminate HTTPException
> 
> ### Step 1: Activate `handle_service_error` across API routes
> - Replace all 18 manual `logger.error(..., exc_info=True)` + `raise SomeException(...)` patterns with `handle_service_error(exc, operation, ErrorClass)`
> - Files: `backend/src/api/cleanup.py`, `backend/src/api/workflow.py`, `backend/src/api/board.py`, `backend/src/api/agents.py`, `backend/src/api/chores.py`, `backend/src/api/chat.py`
> - Reference: `handle_service_error()` in `backend/src/logging_utils.py` — already defined, zero callers
> 
> ### Step 2: Migrate HTTPException → AppException subclasses *(parallel with Step 1)*
> - Replace all 26+ `HTTPException` usages across `backend/src/api/agents.py` (14), `backend/src/api/chores.py` (18+), `backend/src/api/auth.py` (5), `backend/src/api/signal.py` (9+), `backend/src/api/tools.py`, `backend/src/api/pipelines.py`, `backend/src/api/webhooks.py`, `backend/dependencies.py` (5)
> - Map: 400→`ValidationError`, 401→`AuthenticationError`, 403→`AuthorizationError`, 404→`NotFoundError`, 409→`ConflictError` (new), 500→`GitHubAPIError`
> - Add `ConflictError(AppException)` with `status_code=409` to `backend/src/exceptions.py`
> - Reference: `backend/src/api/board.py` as the exemplar (already uses AppException correctly)
> 
> ### Step 3: Fix silent catch blocks *(parallel with Steps 1-2)*
> - `backend/src/api/settings.py` L156: `except Exception: pass` → add `logger.debug()`
> - Audit any other bare `except` blocks
> 
> ### Step 4: Add correlation context to background tasks *(depends on Steps 1-2)*
> - In `backend/src/main.py` background tasks (`_polling_watchdog_loop`, `_session_cleanup_loop`, `_auto_start_copilot_polling`): set a synthetic `request_id_var` so their log lines include traceable correlation IDs (e.g., `bg-polling-<uuid>`)
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Phase 2: Frontend — Shared Error Components, Toast System & Centralized Logging
> 
> ### Step 5: Create minimal `logger` utility
> - Create `frontend/src/utils/logger.ts` — `logger.error()`, `logger.warn()`, `logger.info()` wrapping console, respecting `import.meta.env.DEV`
> - Replace all `console.error()` / `console.warn()` calls (6 instances)
> - Add logging in currently silent catches: `frontend/src/hooks/useBoardControls.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/useSidebarState.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/useAppTheme.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/useMetadata.ts`, `frontend/src/hooks/useRealTimeSync.ts`
> 
> ### Step 6: Create shared `<ErrorAlert>` component *(parallel with Step 5)*
> - Create `frontend/src/components/common/ErrorAlert.tsx` with standardized styling
> - Props: `message`, `onRetry?`, `onDismiss?`, `className?`
> - Replace inline error displays across: ChatInterface, IssueRecommendationPreview, VoiceInputButton, ProjectsPage, AgentPresetSelector, McpSettings
> 
> ### Step 7: Add toast notification system (sonner) *(depends on Step 5)*
> - Install `sonner`, add `<Toaster />` to `frontend/src/App.tsx`
> - Configure default error/success/info toast styles matching the design system
> - Wire into TanStack QueryClient default `onError` to auto-toast unhandled mutation errors
> 
> ### Step 8: Add global unhandled error handlers *(parallel with Step 7)*
> - In `frontend/src/main.tsx`: `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', ...)` and `window.onerror` calling `logger.error()`
> 
> ### Step 9: Standardize mutation error surfacing *(depends on Steps 5, 7)*
> - Add centralized mutation error handling via `QueryClient` default `onError` callback in `frontend/src/App.tsx`
> - Default: logs via `logger.error()` + shows toast with error message
> - Individual `onError` overrides still respected
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Phase 3: Verification
> 
> ### Step 10: Backend tests
> - Run existing backend test suite — confirm no regressions from HTTPException→AppException migration
> - Grep for zero remaining `HTTPException` imports in API routes
> - Verify `handle_service_error` is now actually called
> 
> ### Step 11: Frontend tests *(parallel with Step 10)*
> - Run vitest + playwright suites — confirm no regressions
> - Verify ErrorAlert renders, logger works, toast shows on mutation failure
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Relevant Files
> 
> ### Backend
> - `backend/src/logging_utils.py` — `handle_service_error()` and `safe_error_response()` to activate (L241-287)
> - `backend/src/exceptions.py` — AppException hierarchy (add ConflictError)
> - `backend/src/main.py` — Global handlers (L440-475) + background tasks (L18-248)
> - `backend/src/api/agents.py` — 14 HTTPException usages, heaviest migration
> - `backend/src/api/chores.py` — 18+ HTTPException usages
> - `backend/src/api/auth.py` — 5 HTTPException usages
> - `backend/src/api/signal.py` — 9+ HTTPException usages
> - `backend/src/api/board.py` — Exemplar of correct AppException usage
> - `backend/src/api/cleanup.py` — 3 manual logger+raise patterns
> - `backend/src/api/workflow.py` — 2 manual logger+raise patterns
> - `backend/src/api/chat.py` — 3 manual logger+raise patterns
> - `backend/src/api/settings.py` — Silent catch at L156
> - `backend/src/api/tools.py` — HTTPException usages
> - `backend/src/api/pipelines.py` — HTTPException usages
> - `backend/src/api/webhooks.py` — HTTPException usages
> - `backend/dependencies.py` — 5 HTTPException usages
> - `backend/src/middleware/request_id.py` — request_id_var for background task context
> 
> ### Frontend
> - `frontend/src/services/api.ts` — ApiError class, normalizeApiError (reference)
> - `frontend/src/components/common/ErrorBoundary.tsx` — Existing error boundary (reference)
> - `frontend/src/App.tsx` — QueryClient config (Steps 7, 9)
> - `frontend/src/main.tsx` — Entry point for global handlers (Step 8)
> - `frontend/src/hooks/useBoardControls.ts` — Silent catch
> - `frontend/src/hooks/useSidebarState.ts` — Silent catch
> - `frontend/src/hooks/useAppTheme.ts` — Silent catch
> - `frontend/src/hooks/useMetadata.ts` — Silent catch
> - `frontend/src/hooks/useRealTimeSync.ts` — Silent catch
> - `frontend/src/components/chat/ChatInterface.tsx` — Inline error display to replace
> - `frontend/src/components/chat/IssueRecommendationPreview.tsx` — Inline error display
> - `frontend/src/pages/ProjectsPage.tsx` — Inline error display to replace
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Decisions
> - **No new logging library on backend** — existing infrastructure is production-grade
> - **Add sonner for toasts** — lightweight, modern, integrates with TanStack Query
> - **Add `ConflictError`** — clean single-purpose exception for 409 responses
> - **`board.py` is the reference** for backend error handling
> - **`handle_service_error` stays as-is** — just needs callers
> - **Background task correlation IDs use `bg-` prefix** to distinguish from HTTP request IDs
> 
> ## Further Considerations
> 1. **Log sampling**: Existing `setup_logging(debug=)` toggle covers this. Low priority.
> 2. **Frontend error tracking (Sentry, etc.)**: Once the logger utility is in place, integrating is a drop-in enhancement for a future plan.

## User Story

As a backend and frontend engineer on this project, I want to eliminate the 26+ raw HTTPException usages across API routes, activate the currently dead `handle_service_error()` helper that 18 places manually replicate, add `ConflictError` to the AppException hierarchy, fix 7+ silent frontend catches with a shared logger utility, introduce a `sonner`-based toast system wired to TanStack QueryClient, and replace scattered inline error UI with a shared `<ErrorAlert>` component — so that both layers share a single, traceable, DRY error contract that is easy to extend, debug with correlation IDs (including background tasks), and surface clearly to users without duplicating boilerplate.

## UI/UX Description

Frontend error surfaces should be unified through two channels: (1) a reusable `<ErrorAlert>` component (`frontend/src/components/common/ErrorAlert.tsx`) accepting `message`, `onRetry?`, `onDismiss?`, and `className?` props with standardized styling consistent with the existing design system — replacing inline error displays in ChatInterface, IssueRecommendationPreview, VoiceInputButton, ProjectsPage, AgentPresetSelector, and McpSettings; and (2) a `sonner` `<Toaster />` mounted in `App.tsx` for transient toast notifications on mutation errors, styled to match the design system. TanStack QueryClient's default `onError` callback auto-toasts unhandled mutation errors while individual `onError` overrides remain respected. Global unhandled promise rejections and `window.onerror` events are captured in `main.tsx` and routed through `logger.error()`. All `console.error()`/`console.warn()` calls (6 instances) are replaced with the new `frontend/src/utils/logger.ts` utility that wraps console and respects `import.meta.env.DEV`. No visible UI changes are expected for the backend phase; improved error response shapes and structured log lines with correlation IDs (HTTP requests and background tasks prefixed `bg-polling-<uuid>`, `bg-cleanup-<uuid>`, etc.) are the observable artifacts.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST replace all 18 manual `logger.error(..., exc_info=True)` + `raise SomeException(...)` patterns in `cleanup.py`, `workflow.py`, `board.py`, `agents.py`, `chores.py`, and `chat.py` with calls to the existing `handle_service_error(exc, operation, ErrorClass)` in `backend/src/logging_utils.py` (currently zero callers)
- System MUST migrate all 26+ raw `HTTPException` usages across `agents.py` (14), `chores.py` (18+), `auth.py` (5), `signal.py` (9+), `tools.py`, `pipelines.py`, `webhooks.py`, and `dependencies.py` (5) to the appropriate AppException subclass: 400→ValidationError, 401→AuthenticationError, 403→AuthorizationError, 404→NotFoundError, 409→ConflictError, 500→GitHubAPIError
- System MUST add `ConflictError(AppException)` with `status_code=409` to `backend/src/exceptions.py` — no other changes to the AppException hierarchy are required
- System MUST fix the silent `except Exception: pass` block at `backend/src/api/settings.py` L156` by adding at minimum a `logger.debug()` call; a full audit of all bare `except` blocks across API routes MUST be performed and any additional silent swallows addressed
- System MUST inject a synthetic `request_id_var` context variable into the three background task loops in `backend/src/main.py` (`_polling_watchdog_loop`, `_session_cleanup_loop`, `_auto_start_copilot_polling`) using a `bg-<task-name>-<uuid>` prefix so background log lines carry traceable correlation IDs, using `backend/src/middleware/request_id.py` as the reference
- System MUST create `frontend/src/utils/logger.ts` exposing `logger.error()`, `logger.warn()`, and `logger.info()` wrapping console methods and gating non-error output behind `import.meta.env.DEV`; all 6 existing `console.error()`/`console.warn()` call sites and the 5 silent catches in `useBoardControls.ts`, `useSidebarState.ts`, `useAppTheme.ts`, `useMetadata.ts`, and `useRealTimeSync.ts` MUST be updated to use this utility
- System MUST create `frontend/src/components/common/ErrorAlert.tsx` accepting `message`, `onRetry?`, `onDismiss?`, and `className?` props with design-system-consistent styling, and replace all inline error displays in ChatInterface, IssueRecommendationPreview, VoiceInputButton, ProjectsPage, AgentPresetSelector, and McpSettings with this component
- System MUST install `sonner`, mount `<Toaster />` in `frontend/src/App.tsx`, configure default error/success/info styles matching the design system, and wire TanStack QueryClient's default `onError` to call `logger.error()` and display a sonner toast; individual mutation `onError` overrides MUST still take precedence
- System MUST register `window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', ...)` and `window.onerror` in `frontend/src/main.tsx` routing to `logger.error()`
- System MUST verify zero remaining `HTTPException` imports in API route files post-migration (grep check), confirm `handle_service_error` has callers, run the existing backend test suite with no regressions, and run vitest + Playwright suites confirming ErrorAlert renders, logger operates correctly, and toasts appear on mutation failure

## Technical Notes

Backend: use `backend/src/api/board.py` as the sole reference implementation for correct AppException usage; `handle_service_error()` signature is defined at `backend/src/logging_utils.py` L241–287 and `safe_error_response()` at the same module — no changes to these helpers are needed, only callers must be added. For background task correlation IDs, import `request_id_var` from `backend/src/middleware/request_id.py` and call `request_id_var.set(f'bg-{task_name}-{uuid4().hex[:8]}')` at the start of each loop iteration. Frontend: `frontend/src/services/api.ts` contains `ApiError` and `normalizeApiError` as reference for error shape normalization; `frontend/src/components/common/ErrorBoundary.tsx` is the existing boundary reference. Sonner integrates with TanStack Query v5 via `queryClient`'s `defaultOptions.mutations.onError`; ensure the `<Toaster />` is placed above all route providers in `App.tsx` to guarantee global availability. No new backend logging library is introduced — existing structured logging infrastructure is production-grade. Sentry or other frontend error tracking is explicitly out of scope but the new `logger.ts` is designed as a drop-in integration point for a future plan.

mentioned_issues.title: Use Selected Agent Pipeline Config from Project Page When Creating GitHub Issues via Chat
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> The chat should use the currently selected Agent Pipeline configuration from Project page, when defining the Agent Pipeline for new GitHub Issues created via user chat

## User Story

As a user interacting with the chat interface, I want new GitHub Issues created through my chat to automatically use the currently selected Agent Pipeline configuration from the Project page, so that the Agent Pipeline defined for each issue accurately reflects my intended pipeline without requiring manual re-selection per issue.

## UI/UX Description

The chat interface should silently inherit the active Agent Pipeline configuration chosen on the Project page when generating a new GitHub Issue. No additional user input should be required — the pipeline selection should be resolved automatically at issue-creation time. If no Agent Pipeline is currently selected on the Project page, the chat should either display an inline warning/prompt nudging the user to select one, or fall back to a clearly defined default. A read-only indicator in the chat or issue-creation confirmation step could optionally surface which Agent Pipeline was applied, giving the user confidence that the correct configuration was used.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST read the currently selected Agent Pipeline configuration from the Project page at the time a new GitHub Issue is created via user chat.
- System MUST pass the resolved Agent Pipeline configuration as part of the GitHub Issue creation payload, populating the Agent Pipeline field on the new issue.
- System MUST NOT default to a hardcoded or previously used Agent Pipeline when a valid Project-page selection exists.
- System SHOULD display a warning or prompt in the chat UI if no Agent Pipeline is currently selected on the Project page at the time of issue creation, preventing silent misconfiguration.
- System MUST fall back to a defined default Agent Pipeline (or surface an explicit error) when no pipeline is selected and the user proceeds with issue creation.
- System SHOULD surface the applied Agent Pipeline name in the chat's issue-creation confirmation or summary message so the user can verify the correct pipeline was used.
- System MUST keep the Agent Pipeline selection state in sync between the Project page and the chat context, reflecting any changes the user makes without requiring a page reload or chat restart.
- System SHOULD handle the case where the previously selected Agent Pipeline configuration is deleted or becomes unavailable, notifying the user and prompting re-selection.

## Technical Notes

The chat's issue-creation logic must access shared application state (e.g., a global store, context, or URL-persisted param) that holds the Project page's currently active Agent Pipeline selection — likely the same state used by the `feat/agent-tools-pipeline-ux` or `copilot/speckit-specify-agents-page-features` branches. Ensure the Agent Pipeline ID/config reference is passed through the issue-creation service or API call rather than being resolved only on the frontend, to avoid stale-state bugs. Consider adding a selector hook (e.g., `useSelectedAgentPipeline`) that both the Project page and chat can consume from the same source of truth. Edge cases to guard: null/undefined pipeline selection, pipeline deleted mid-session, and multi-project contexts where the wrong project's pipeline could bleed in.

closing_issues.title: Support @<agent-pipeline-name> Mention in Chat to Select Agent Pipeline Configuration for GitHub Issue Creation
closing_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Add support to allow the user to @<agent-pipeline-name> to call any saved Agent Pipeline configuration. This is the configuration that should be used when creating the GitHub Issues for the user's chat input description

## User Story

As a user composing a chat input description, I want to type @<agent-pipeline-name> to reference and activate a saved Agent Pipeline configuration so that the selected pipeline's settings are automatically applied when generating GitHub Issues from my chat input — giving me precise control over which AI agent workflow handles the issue creation.

## UI/UX Description

In the chat input field, typing '@' should trigger an autocomplete/typeahead dropdown listing all saved Agent Pipeline configurations by name. As the user continues typing after '@', the list should filter in real-time to match the pipeline name. Selecting a pipeline from the dropdown (via keyboard arrow keys + Enter, or mouse click) inserts a styled @mention chip/tag (e.g., highlighted token) inline in the chat input, visually distinguishing the pipeline reference from plain text. If a valid pipeline is mentioned, the GitHub Issue creation flow should visibly indicate which pipeline configuration is active (e.g., a badge or label near the submit button reading 'Using pipeline: <name>'). If an unknown or deleted pipeline name is typed, the mention should render with a warning state (e.g., red/orange underline or icon) and the system should alert the user before submission. The autocomplete dropdown should show each pipeline's name and optionally a short description or last-modified date to help distinguish configurations.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST detect when the user types '@' in the chat input field and display an autocomplete dropdown listing all saved Agent Pipeline configurations.
- System MUST filter the autocomplete dropdown in real-time as the user types characters after '@', matching against pipeline names case-insensitively.
- System MUST allow the user to select a pipeline from the dropdown via keyboard navigation (arrow keys + Enter) or mouse click, inserting a resolved @mention token into the chat input.
- System MUST use the Agent Pipeline configuration associated with the @mentioned pipeline name as the active configuration when the user submits their chat input to create a GitHub Issue.
- System MUST support only one active @agent-pipeline-name mention per chat submission; if multiple @mentions are present, the system SHOULD either use the last valid one or surface a validation error.
- System MUST validate that the @mentioned pipeline name corresponds to an existing saved Agent Pipeline configuration at submission time and MUST prevent GitHub Issue creation with a clear error message if the pipeline cannot be resolved.
- System SHOULD render the @mention as a distinct inline chip or styled token within the chat input to visually differentiate it from regular text.
- System SHOULD display the active pipeline name as a contextual indicator near the GitHub Issue creation submit action (e.g., 'Using pipeline: <name>') so the user can confirm their selection before submitting.
- System SHOULD gracefully handle edge cases where a previously valid pipeline is deleted or renamed after being mentioned, surfacing a recoverable error with guidance to re-select a valid pipeline.

## Technical Notes

Implement a mention-parsing utility that intercepts keystrokes in the chat input and triggers a pipeline lookup query against the saved Agent Pipeline configurations store (likely an existing API or state slice). The autocomplete dropdown should be a reusable component (similar to any existing @mention or typeahead UI in the codebase) positioned relative to the cursor. On submission, extract the resolved pipeline ID/config from the parsed mention token and pass it as a parameter to the GitHub Issue creation workflow — referencing the patterns in the 'copilot/create-github-issues-with-selected-pipeline' branch for how pipeline config is plumbed into the issue creation flow. Ensure the mention token stores the pipeline ID internally (not just display name) to guard against rename edge cases. Consider debouncing the autocomplete query to avoid excessive lookups on rapid keystrokes.

mentioned_issues.title: Fix 'Every X Issues' Chore Counter to Only Count GitHub Parent Issues (Excluding Chores and Sub-Issues)
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Ensure that the counters for Chores with "Every x issues" is counting down how many GitHub Parent Issues have been created since the last time that particular Chore has run. This is the counter on the tile and the trigger event. Other Chores do not count towards the counter. Sub Issues do not count towards the counter. ONLY GitHub Parent Issues that are not Chores count towards the counter.

## User Story

As a Solune user managing Chores with an 'Every X Issues' trigger, I want the countdown counter — shown on the Chore tile and used as the trigger evaluation — to accurately reflect only the number of GitHub Parent Issues created since that specific Chore last ran, so that Chores fire at the correct cadence without being skewed by unrelated Chores or Sub-Issues inflating the count.

## UI/UX Description

The Chore tile displays a counter representing progress toward the 'Every X Issues' threshold. This counter must visually reflect only qualifying GitHub Parent Issues — issues that are not Chores and not Sub-Issues — created since the last execution of that specific Chore. The counter on the tile and the internal trigger evaluation logic must both derive from the same filtered dataset. No other issue type (Chores or Sub-Issues) should appear to increment the counter. The counter should reset after the Chore runs and begin accumulating again from zero based only on new qualifying Parent Issues.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST count only GitHub Parent Issues created after the last run timestamp of a given Chore when evaluating the 'Every X Issues' trigger condition.

## Overview
Users are experiencing an intermittent issue where scrolling (both up and down) becomes unresponsive or "stuck" on the screen. This affects usability and needs to be investigated and resolved.

- Issue appears to be intermittent, making it potentially related to a race condition, event listener conflict, or state management problem
- Investigate scroll event handlers for any blocking logic or missing cleanup
- Check for CSS properties that may interfere with scrolling (e.g., `overflow`, `pointer-events`, `touch-action`)
- Review any third-party libraries or components that may be capturing or suppressing scroll events
- Test across different browsers and devices to determine if the issue is platform-specific
- Check if the issue is tied to specific user interactions or app states that precede the freeze

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause of the scroll freeze is identified and documented
- [ ] Scrolling works reliably in both directions without getting stuck
- [ ] Fix is verified across major browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) and on mobile devices
- [ ] No regression introduced to other scroll-dependent UI components
- [ ] Fix handles edge cases such as rapid scrolling or switching between views

mentioned_issues.title: Display Models Used in Agent Pipeline Section of Parent Issue Description
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> The GitHub Parent Issue description - Agent Pipeline section, should also list the models to be used for the Agent Pipeline

## User Story

As a developer or project stakeholder viewing a GitHub Parent Issue for Project Solune, I want the Agent Pipeline section of the issue description to list the specific AI models assigned to each agent in the pipeline so that I can quickly understand the full configuration of the pipeline without navigating to separate agent config pages.

## UI/UX Description

The Agent Pipeline section within the GitHub Parent Issue description should be enhanced to include model information alongside each agent entry. Each agent listed in the pipeline should display its associated model name (e.g., 'gpt-4o', 'claude-3-5-sonnet', etc.) in a clear, readable format — such as inline next to the agent name, or as a sub-item/badge beneath it. The model display should follow the existing formatting conventions used in the issue description (Markdown-compatible), ensuring it renders cleanly on GitHub's issue view. If a model is not yet assigned to an agent in the pipeline, a placeholder such as 'No model assigned' or 'TBD' should be shown to maintain visual consistency. The layout should remain scannable and not add excessive verbosity to the issue body.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST include the model name associated with each agent when rendering the Agent Pipeline section of the GitHub Parent Issue description.
- System MUST update the Agent Pipeline section dynamically whenever agent model assignments are changed, so that the Parent Issue description stays in sync.
- System MUST display a clear placeholder (e.g., 'No model assigned' or 'TBD') for any pipeline agent that does not yet have a model configured.
- System MUST format model information in valid GitHub-flavored Markdown so it renders correctly in the GitHub issue description view.
- System SHOULD display the model name inline with or directly beneath the corresponding agent entry to maintain a clear visual association.
- System SHOULD preserve all existing Agent Pipeline section content and formatting when adding model information, ensuring no regression in current issue description structure.
- System MUST handle pipelines with one or more agents, correctly listing model information for each agent in order.
- System SHOULD reflect the model label or identifier consistently with how models are referenced elsewhere in Project Solune (e.g., agent-config pages).

## Technical Notes

This change involves updating the logic that generates or writes the GitHub Parent Issue description — likely in an issue-creation or issue-update utility/script within the codebase. The Agent Pipeline section renderer should be extended to query each agent's model field and append it to the Markdown output. Review the 'agent-config' and 'copilot/speckit-specify-agents-page-features' branch for existing agent model data structures to ensure consistent field naming. If the issue description is generated via a GitHub API call (e.g., using Octokit or a REST call), ensure the body string construction for the pipeline section is updated and that the issue is re-patched on config changes.

mentioned_issues.title: feat: Blocking Queue — Serial Issue Activation & Branch Ancestry Control via Chores, Pipelines, and #block Chat Command
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> # Plan: Blocking Feature for Issue Activation & Branching
> 
> ## TL;DR
> Add a "Blocking" toggle to Chores, Pipelines, and a `#block` magic word in chat. When blocking issues exist, they serialize issue activation and control branch ancestry — only one issue runs agents at a time, and subsequent issues branch from the oldest open blocking issue's branch instead of `main`. When all blocking issues complete, branching returns to `main`.
> 
> ## Confirmed Decisions
> - **Scope**: Per-repository blocking queue (not per-project)
> - **Pipeline-level toggle**: ALL issues from a blocking pipeline are blocking
> - **Non-blocking concurrency**: When no blocking issues exist, multiple non-blocking issues can be active simultaneously (current behavior preserved)
> - **Branch target**: When blocking issues activate, they ALL branch from the oldest open blocking issue's branch (not chained)
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Phase 1: Database & Models
> 
> ### Step 1.1 — New migration: `017_blocking_queue.sql`
> - New table `blocking_queue`:
>   - `id` INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT
>   - `repo_key` TEXT NOT NULL (formatted as `owner/repo`)
>   - `issue_number` INTEGER NOT NULL
>   - `project_id` TEXT NOT NULL
>   - `is_blocking` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
>   - `queue_status` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK IN ('pending','active','in_review','completed')
>   - `parent_branch` TEXT (the branch this issue targets as base_ref)
>   - `blocking_source_issue` INTEGER (which blocking issue provided the parent branch)
>   - `created_at` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
>   - `activated_at` TEXT
>   - `completed_at` TEXT
>   - UNIQUE(repo_key, issue_number)
> - Add `blocking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` column to `pipeline_configs` table
> - Add `blocking INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` column to `chores` table
> 
> ### Step 1.2 — Backend models
> - New file: `backend/src/models/blocking.py`
>   - `BlockingQueueEntry` — Pydantic model mirroring the DB row
>   - `BlockingQueueStatus` — StrEnum: pending, active, in_review, completed
> - Update `backend/src/models/pipeline.py`: add `blocking: bool = False` to `PipelineConfig`
> - Update `backend/src/models/chores.py`: add `blocking: bool = False` to `Chore`, `ChoreCreate`, `ChoreUpdate`
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Phase 2: Blocking Queue Service (Core Engine)
> 
> ### Step 2.1 — New service: `backend/src/services/blocking_queue.py`
> Central service managing the blocking queue state machine. Key functions:
> 
> | Function | Purpose |
> |----------|---------|
> | `enqueue_issue(repo_key, issue_number, project_id, is_blocking)` | Insert into blocking_queue table, determine initial activation |
> | `get_base_ref_for_issue(repo_key, issue_number)` | Return oldest open blocking issue's branch, or `"main"` |
> | `mark_active(repo_key, issue_number, parent_branch)` | Update queue_status to active, set parent_branch, activated_at |
> | `mark_in_review(repo_key, issue_number)` | Update queue_status to in_review, trigger `try_activate_next()` |
> | `mark_completed(repo_key, issue_number)` | Update queue_status to completed, recalculate base branch, trigger activation |
> | `try_activate_next(repo_key)` | **Core logic** — activate next pending issue(s) per the rules |
> | `get_current_base_branch(repo_key)` | Returns oldest open blocking issue's branch, or `"main"` |
> | `has_open_blocking_issues(repo_key)` | Quick boolean check for gating |
> 
> **Activation rules** (matching the user's 8-issue example):
> - Non-blocking issues with no open blocking issues → activate immediately (current behavior)
> - Any blocking issue open → serial activation, one at a time
> - When active issue(s) → "In review": activate next batch:
>   - Non-blocking issues activate together up to the next blocking entry
>   - Blocking entries activate alone
> - Activated issues branch from the oldest open blocking issue's branch
> - When a blocking issue completes: base branch shifts to next oldest open blocking issue, or `"main"` if none remain
> 
> ### Step 2.2 — Persistence layer: `backend/src/services/blocking_queue_store.py`
> - SQLite CRUD operations using existing `get_db()` pattern from chores/pipelines
> - Methods: insert, update_status, get_by_repo, get_by_issue, get_pending, get_open_blocking
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Phase 3: Backend Integration
> 
> ### Step 3.1 — Modify orchestrator base_ref resolution (*depends on Phase 2*)
> **File**: `backend/src/services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py` (~line 800-1000)
> - Before the existing base_ref logic, call `blocking_queue.get_base_ref_for_issue(repo_key, issue_number)`
> - If the issue is the FIRST agent assignment (no existing main branch), use the blocking queue's base_ref instead of hardcoded `"main"`
> - If a main branch already exists (subsequent agents), keep current behavior (branch from main branch name)
> 
> ### Step 3.2 — Modify orchestrator issue creation flow (*depends on Phase 2*)
> **File**: `backend/src/services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py` (`execute_full_workflow()` ~line 2002)
> - After issue creation, call `blocking_queue.enqueue_issue()`
> - Check if issue should activate immediately
> - If NOT activated: skip agent assignment, store issue as "pending" in queue, return WorkflowResult with pending status
> - If activated: proceed with current flow (assign first agent, start polling)
> 
> ### Step 3.3 — Modify pipeline polling for activation (*depends on Phase 2*)
> **File**: `backend/src/services/copilot_polling/pipeline.py`
> - In status transition handler (when an issue moves to "In review"):
>   - Call `blocking_queue.mark_in_review(repo_key, issue_number)`
>   - Get list of newly activated issues from `try_activate_next()`
>   - For each activated issue: trigger `assign_agent_for_status()`
> - In completion handler (when an issue is done):
>   - Call `blocking_queue.mark_completed(repo_key, issue_number)`
>   - Get list of newly activated issues from `try_activate_next()`
>   - For each activated issue: trigger agent assignment
> 
> ### Step 3.4 — Chat `#block` parsing (*parallel with steps 3.1-3.3*)
> **File**: `backend/src/api/chat.py`
> - Add new Priority 0.5 (between `#agent` and feature request):
>   - Detect `#block` anywhere in message content (not just prefix)
>   - Strip `#block` from content before passing to downstream intent processing
>   - Set `is_blocking=True` flag on the resulting issue recommendation / task proposal
>   - Pass `is_blocking` through `confirm_proposal()` → `execute_full_workflow()`
> 
> ### Step 3.5 — Modify chore trigger (*parallel with steps 3.1-3.3*)
> **Files**: `backend/src/api/chores.py` / `backend/src/services/chores/service.py`
> - In `trigger_chore()`: read `chore.blocking` flag
> - Pass `is_blocking` to orchestrator's `execute_full_workflow()`
> - Also check the assigned pipeline's blocking flag if chore doesn't have its own
> 
> ### Step 3.6 — Modify pipeline config API (*parallel with steps 3.1-3.3*)
> **Files**: `backend/src/api/pipelines.py` / `backend/src/services/pipelines/service.py`
> - Add `blocking` field to create/update pipeline endpoints
> - Store in `pipeline_configs.blocking` column
> - Return `blocking` in pipeline config responses
> 
> ### Step 3.7 — Modify chore config API (*parallel with steps 3.1-3.3*)
> **Files**: `backend/src/api/chores.py` / `backend/src/services/chores/service.py`
> - Add `blocking` field to `ChoreUpdate` model
> - Store in `chores.blocking` column
> - Return `blocking` in chore responses
> 
> ### Step 3.8 — WebSocket notifications (*depends on 3.3*)
> - Broadcast `blocking_queue_updated` event when issues activate/complete
> - Include: repo_key, activated_issues, completed_issues, current_base_branch
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Phase 4: Frontend Integration
> 
> ### Step 4.1 — TypeScript types (*parallel with Phase 3*)
> - Update pipeline types to include `blocking: boolean`
> - Update chore types to include `blocking: boolean`
> - Add `BlockingQueueEntry` type
> - Add `isBlocking` option to chat message send
> 
> ### Step 4.2 — Pipeline blocking toggle (*depends on 4.1*)
> **File**: `frontend/src/components/pipeline/PipelineBoard.tsx` or `SavedWorkflowsList.tsx`
> - Add a toggle switch for `blocking` on pipeline config
> - Use `usePipelineConfig` hook's mutation to persist
> 
> ### Step 4.3 — Chore blocking toggle (*depends on 4.1*)
> **File**: `frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx`
> - Add a toggle switch for `blocking` (follow `ai_enhance_enabled` toggle pattern)
> - Use `useUpdateChore` mutation to persist
> 
> ### Step 4.4 — Chat `#block` support (*depends on 4.1*)
> **File**: `frontend/src/components/chat/ChatInterface.tsx`
> - Add `#block` to command autocomplete suggestions
> - Visual indicator when `#block` is detected in the message (e.g., small badge)
> - Pass `isBlocking` flag in message options to backend
> 
> ### Step 4.5 — Board blocking indicators (*depends on 4.1*)
> - Show 🔒 icon or "Blocking" badge on issue cards that are blocking
> - Show "Pending (blocked)" status for queued issues
> - Show current blocking chain in a tooltip or sidebar
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Relevant Files
> 
> **Backend — New files:**
> - `backend/src/migrations/017_blocking_queue.sql` — DB schema
> - `backend/src/models/blocking.py` — Pydantic models
> - `backend/src/services/blocking_queue.py` — Core blocking logic
> - `backend/src/services/blocking_queue_store.py` — SQLite persistence
> 
> **Backend — Modified files:**
> - `backend/src/models/pipeline.py` — add `blocking` field to `PipelineConfig`
> - `backend/src/models/chores.py` — add `blocking` field to `Chore`, `ChoreUpdate`
> - `backend/src/services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py` — base_ref resolution + activation gating
> - `backend/src/services/copilot_polling/pipeline.py` — status transition hooks for activation
> - `backend/src/services/copilot_polling/completion.py` — completion hooks for activation
> - `backend/src/api/chat.py` — `#block` parsing
> - `backend/src/api/chores.py` — pass blocking flag on trigger
> - `backend/src/services/chores/service.py` — read blocking from chore/pipeline
> - `backend/src/api/pipelines.py` — blocking in CRUD
> - `backend/src/services/pipelines/service.py` — blocking in CRUD
> 
> **Frontend — Modified files:**
> - `frontend/src/components/pipeline/PipelineBoard.tsx` or `SavedWorkflowsList.tsx` — toggle
> - `frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx` — toggle
> - `frontend/src/components/chat/ChatInterface.tsx` — `#block` autocomplete + indicator
> - `frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts` — blocking field in types/mutations
> - `frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts` — blocking field in types/mutations
> 
> ---
> 
> ## Verification
> 
> 1. **Unit tests** for `blocking_queue.py`: Test the activation state machine with the exact 8-issue example from requirements — verify creation order, activation order, branch sources, and completion cascades
> 2. **Unit tests** for `#block` parsing in `chat.py`: Verify `#block` is detected and stripped from message content

> - **Scope**: Per-repository blocking queue (not per-project)

>   - `created_at` TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
>   - `activated_at` TEXT
>   - `completed_at` TEXT
>   - UNIQUE(repo_key, issue_number)

> ---

> | `mark_in_review(repo_key, issue_number)` | Update queue_status to in_review, trigger `try_activate_next()` |
> | `mark_completed(repo_key, issue_number)` | Update queue_status to completed, recalculate base branch, trigger activation |

> | `get_current_base_branch(repo_key)` | Returns oldest open blocking issue's branch, or `"main"` |
> | `has_open_blocking_issues(repo_key)` | Quick boolean check for gating |
>

> - Non-blocking issues with no open blocking issues → activate immediately (current behavior)

>   - Non-blocking issues activate together up to the next blocking entry
>   - Blocking entries activate alone
> - Activated issues branch from the oldest open blocking issue's branch
> - When a blocking issue completes: base branch shifts to next oldest open blocking issue, or `"main"` if none remain

- System MUST detect `#block` anywhere (not just as a prefix) in chat message content in `backend/src/api/chat.py`, strip it before passing to downstream intent processing (Priority 0.5, between `#agent` handling and feature-request handling), and propagate `is_blocking=True` through `confirm_proposal()` to `execute_full_workflow()`.
- System MUST add `blocking` boolean field to pipeline create/update/read endpoints (`api/pipelines.py`, `services/pipelines/service.py`) and to chore trigger and CRUD endpoints (`api/chores.py`, `services/chores/service.py`); chore trigger MUST also inherit the blocking flag from its assigned pipeline if the chore's own flag is not set.
- System MUST broadcast a `blocking_queue_updated` WebSocket event containing `repo_key`, `activated_issues`, `completed_issues`, and `current_base_branch` whenever issues activate or complete; and MUST surface a user-facing toast notification reading 'Issue #X is now active — agents starting' for newly activated previously-pending issues.
- System MUST use SQLite transactions and a per-repo service-layer lock in `blocking_queue.py` to prevent double-activation race conditions; and on container/polling-loop startup MUST call `try_activate_next()` for all repos with non-completed queue entries to recover from any missed activations during downtime.
- System MUST include unit tests for the blocking queue state machine validating an 8-issue activation scenario (creation order, activation order, branch sources, completion cascades); unit tests for `#block` detection and stripping in `chat.py`; integration tests for chore trigger with `blocking=True` and pipeline-level blocking; and the `blocking` field MUST be returned in all pipeline and chore API responses so frontend toggles reflect persisted state.
- System SHOULD add `#block` to ChatInterface command autocomplete and render a visual badge when `#block` is present in the composer; SHOULD display a 🔒 icon or 'Blocking' badge on blocking issue cards and 'Pending (blocked)' status on queued issues; and SHOULD provide a tooltip or sidebar visualization of the current per-repo blocking chain including ordered queue and current base branch.

## Technical Notes

This is a 4-phase implementation: Phase 1 (DB + models), Phase 2 (blocking_queue service — the state machine core), Phase 3 (backend integration across orchestrator, polling, chat, chores, pipelines APIs), Phase 4 (frontend toggles, indicators, WebSocket-driven UI). Phase 3 steps 3.4–3.7 are parallelizable with 3.1–3.3 but all depend on Phase 2 being complete. The `try_activate_next()` function is the most critical and risk-prone piece — it must handle the exact activation rules: non-blocking issues batch together when no blocking issues are open, blocking issues activate one-at-a-time, and all activated issues receive `get_current_base_branch()` (oldest open blocking issue's branch or `'main'`) as their base_ref, NOT a chained approach. SQLite transactions with a per-repo advisory lock (e.g., a threading.Lock keyed by repo_key held in the service layer) are required to prevent race conditions on concurrent status transitions. The recovery path on startup (calling `try_activate_next()` for all repos with pending queue entries) is mandatory for correctness after container restarts. Frontend blocking toggles should follow the `ai_enhance_enabled` toggle pattern already present in ChoreCard; `#block` parsing in chat.py must be case-insensitive and strip the token regardless of position in the message. Scope exclusions to enforce: no UI for reordering the queue, no cross-repo blocking, no retroactive blocking of existing open issues, no blocking for draft items, no admin force-activate override.

mentioned_issues.title: Add Comprehensive Tooltips Across App UI for Feature Explainability and UX Guidance
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Add comprehensive tooltips to the app UI to provide the user with easy UX and explainable understanding of all the features, decision consequences, and functionality.

## User Story

As an app user, I want comprehensive tooltips on all interactive UI elements, features, and decision points so that I can easily understand what each feature does, what consequences my choices may have, and how to use the app's full functionality without needing external documentation.

## UI/UX Description

Tooltips should appear on hover (desktop) and long-press (mobile/touch) for all interactive elements including buttons, toggles, form fields, dropdowns, icons, configuration options, and pipeline steps. Each tooltip should use a consistent design language: a dark or theme-aware floating popover with a subtle arrow pointing to the trigger element, legible font size (min 13px), max-width of ~280px, and a short delay (~300ms) before appearing to avoid accidental triggers. Tooltip copy should be concise but informative — explaining not just what an element is, but why it matters and what happens when the user interacts with it (i.e., decision consequences). For complex features, tooltips may include a bolded title line followed by 1–2 sentences of explanation. Tooltips must not obstruct adjacent UI and should reposition intelligently based on available viewport space (flip from top to bottom, left to right as needed). Dismiss on mouse-out, touch-end, or Escape key. Consider progressive disclosure: simple label on first hover, with an optional 'Learn more' link for deeply complex features.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST display a tooltip on hover (desktop) and long-press (mobile) for every interactive UI element including buttons, icons, toggles, dropdowns, form fields, sliders, and pipeline/agent configuration controls.
- System MUST ensure each tooltip communicates not only the name/label of the element but also its functional purpose and any decision consequences or downstream effects of interacting with it.
- System MUST implement intelligent tooltip positioning so that popovers automatically reposition (flip vertically and/or horizontally) when they would otherwise overflow or be clipped by the viewport edge.
- System MUST enforce a consistent visual design for all tooltips — dark or theme-aware background, white/light text, directional arrow indicator, max-width ~280px, and minimum font size of 13px — aligned with the app's existing design system.
- System MUST apply a short trigger delay (~300ms on hover) to prevent accidental tooltip display during normal cursor movement across the UI.
- System MUST allow tooltips to be dismissed via mouse-out, touch-end, or pressing the Escape key, and MUST ensure open tooltips do not block or overlap adjacent interactive elements.
- System SHOULD support a two-tier progressive disclosure pattern — a concise summary on first hover and an optional 'Learn more' affordance for features with deeper complexity.
- System MUST ensure all tooltips meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards, including keyboard focusability (tooltips trigger on focus for keyboard users), sufficient color contrast, and aria-describedby or role='tooltip' attributes on all tooltip targets.

## Technical Notes

Use a battle-tested tooltip/popover library such as Floating UI (formerly Popper.js) or Radix UI Tooltip primitive to handle positioning, flip behavior, and accessibility semantics out of the box — avoid reinventing placement logic. Create a centralized tooltip content registry (e.g., a JSON/TS constants file) mapping UI element keys to their tooltip strings, making copy easy to audit, update, and localize in the future. Implement a reusable Tooltip wrapper component that can be dropped around any element with a single `content` prop, keeping adoption consistent and low-friction across the codebase. Pay special attention to agent configuration controls, pipeline decision nodes, and any settings with irreversible or high-impact consequences — these should have the most descriptive tooltip copy and may warrant the 'Learn more' progressive disclosure tier.
