mentioned_issues.title: Frontend Style Audit & Celestial/Cosmic Theme Animation Enhancement
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Analyze every frontend component to ensure style and theme alignment. Also proper casing of text for best UI/UX. Use modern approaches and best practices. Make app more animated around the theme of sun/moon/stars/celestial/cosmic. @Expert

## User Story

As a frontend developer and end user, I want every UI component to be audited for visual consistency, proper text casing, and modern best practices, and for the app to be enriched with fluid animations inspired by a sun/moon/stars/celestial/cosmic theme, so that the application feels cohesive, polished, visually immersive, and thematically aligned throughout every screen.

## UI/UX Description

Conduct a full sweep of all frontend components to enforce style and theme alignment: consistent use of design tokens (spacing, typography, color palette), proper title/sentence casing across all labels, headings, buttons, tooltips, and placeholders per UX best practices. Introduce a rich celestial/cosmic animation layer — including subtle star-field backgrounds, glowing sun/moon iconography transitions, orbital particle effects, twinkling star micro-animations on hover/focus states, and smooth gradient shifts mimicking day-to-night/cosmic transitions. Animations should respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. All motion should feel purposeful, not distracting — reinforcing the solar theme already present (see `feat/solar-theme-agent-icon-catalog` branch). Use CSS custom properties and/or a consistent animation library (e.g., Framer Motion or CSS keyframes) to ensure maintainability. Every component — cards, buttons, modals, sidebars, navigation, tooltips, inputs, loaders — must be visited and assessed.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST audit every frontend component for adherence to the established design token system (colors, typography, spacing, border-radius, shadows) and flag or correct any deviations.
- System MUST enforce proper text casing (title case for headings/nav items, sentence case for body copy/descriptions, ALL CAPS only for labels/badges per UX convention) across all UI text elements including buttons, tooltips, placeholders, and page titles.
- System MUST introduce celestial/cosmic-themed animations including: star-field or particle background effects, sun/moon glow transitions, twinkling star hover/focus micro-interactions, and orbital or shimmer loading states.
- System MUST ensure all new and existing animations respect the `prefers-reduced-motion` CSS media query, disabling or minimizing motion for users who have opted out.
- System MUST apply modern CSS best practices (CSS custom properties, logical properties, clamp() for fluid typography, container queries where applicable) during the component audit and refactor.
- System MUST ensure all animated and restyled components remain fully accessible — maintaining WCAG AA contrast ratios under all animation states, focus-visible outlines, and ARIA attributes.
- System SHOULD standardize animation duration and easing curves via shared design tokens (e.g., `--transition-cosmic-slow: 800ms ease-in-out`) to ensure motion consistency across the app.
- System SHOULD align the celestial animation palette with the existing solar theme established in the `feat/solar-theme-agent-icon-catalog` branch, reusing or extending existing icon and color assets.
- System SHOULD ensure all components are responsive and that animations degrade gracefully on mobile/low-power devices.
- System MUST produce a brief style alignment report or inline code comments documenting what was changed per component for future maintainability.

## Technical Notes

Base all animation and theming work on the existing solar theme foundation in `feat/solar-theme-agent-icon-catalog`; coordinate to avoid conflicts or redundant design token definitions. Use Framer Motion (if already in the dependency tree) or CSS `@keyframes` + `animation` for celestial effects — prefer CSS-native where possible for performance. Implement a shared `animations.css` or `theme/motion.ts` token file so durations, easing, and keyframes are centralized and not scattered per-component. For the star/particle effects, consider a lightweight canvas or SVG-based background component to avoid heavy DOM overhead; lazy-load it to protect initial page performance.

mentioned_issues.title: Documentation Sweep
mentioned_issues.body:
# Recurring Documentation Update Process

## Overview

A structured cadence for keeping all project documentation accurate, complete, and helpful across the full stack — backend API, frontend components, architecture, configuration, and developer guides.

---

## Cadence

| Review Type            | Frequency     | Trigger                                              |
|------------------------|---------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| Inline doc check       | Every PR      | Author + reviewer responsibility                     |
| Staleness sweep        | Weekly        | Dev rotation (same person as security spot check)    |
| Full doc review        | Monthly       | Sprint planning item                                 |
| Architecture audit     | Quarterly     | After major feature milestones                       |
| New contributor review | On demand     | Before onboarding a new team member                  |

---

## Phase 1 — PR-Level Checks (Every Pull Request)

The PR author is responsible. Reviewers must not approve if these are unmet.

- [ ] Any new endpoint added to `api/` has a corresponding entry in `docs/api-reference.md`
- [ ] Any new environment variable added to `config.py` is documented in `docs/configuration.md`
- [ ] Any change to startup behavior, Docker setup, or prerequisites is reflected in `docs/setup.md`
- [ ] Any new agent, workflow module, or AI provider change is reflected in `docs/agent-pipeline.md`
- [ ] Any schema or data model change is reflected in relevant API or architecture docs
- [ ] PR description references which doc files were updated (or explicitly states "no doc changes needed")

**Add to PR template checklist:**
```
- [ ] Documentation updated (or confirmed not needed)
```

---

## Phase 2 — Weekly Staleness Sweep (~30 minutes, dev rotation)

A quick pass to catch docs that have drifted from the codebase.

### API Reference (`docs/api-reference.md`)
- [ ] Scan `backend/src/api/` — confirm every route file has matching API table entries
- [ ] Confirm all path prefixes, methods, and path params are still accurate
- [ ] Flag any endpoints removed or deprecated but still listed

### Configuration (`docs/configuration.md`)
- [ ] Compare documented env vars against `backend/src/config.py` — add any missing, remove any deleted
- [ ] Confirm default values and required/optional status are still correct

### Setup Guide (`docs/setup.md`)
- [ ] Confirm Docker Compose and manual setup steps still match project state
- [ ] Confirm prerequisite versions (Python, Node, Docker) still match `pyproject.toml` and `package.json`
- [ ] Confirm Codespaces badge and quick start flow still work end-to-end

---

## Phase 3 — Monthly Full Documentation Review (~2–3 hours)

### Coverage Audit

Walk every file in `docs/` and verify it is:
- [ ] **Accurate** — reflects current code behavior, not aspirational or outdated state
- [ ] **Complete** — no major features or workflows are undocumented
- [ ] **Consistent** — terminology, naming, and formatting are uniform across files

| File | Ownership | Key Things to Verify |
|------|-----------|----------------------|
| `docs/setup.md` | Infra/DX | Prerequisites, Codespaces flow, env var list, Docker Compose steps |
| `docs/configuration.md` | Backend | All env vars, types, defaults, and validation rules |
| `docs/api-reference.md` | Backend | All routes, methods, params, auth requirements, and response shapes |
| `docs/architecture.md` | Full stack | Service diagram, data flow, WebSocket flow, AI provider list |
| `docs/agent-pipeline.md` | Backend | Workflow orchestrator modules, Copilot polling, task/issue generation |
| `docs/custom-agents-best-practices.md` | Backend | Agent authoring patterns, extension points |
| `docs/signal-integration.md` | Backend | Signal sidecar setup, webhook flow, delivery logic |
| `docs/testing.md` | Full stack | Test commands, coverage targets, Playwright setup, CI behavior |
| `docs/troubleshooting.md` | Full stack | Common errors and resolutions — remove fixed issues, add new ones |
| `docs/project-structure.md` | Full stack | Directory layout — update after any structural refactor |
| `frontend/docs/` | Frontend | Component patterns, findings log, any frontend-specific guides |

### Cross-Reference Check
- [ ] All internal `docs/` links are valid and resolve to existing headings
- [ ] Code snippets in docs compile or run without error against current codebase
- [ ] README.md top-level links to correct doc files
- [ ] Any external links (GitHub docs, library docs) still resolve to relevant pages

### Readability & Usability
- [ ] Each page has a clear purpose statement at the top
- [ ] Step-by-step guides use numbered lists and include expected outcomes
- [ ] Configuration tables include: variable name, type, required/optional, default, description
- [ ] API tables include: method, path, auth required, brief description
- [ ] Troubleshooting entries follow the format: **Symptom → Cause → Fix**

---

## Phase 4 — Quarterly Architecture Audit (~half day)

Run after major feature milestones (new integrations, significant refactors, new agent types).

### Architecture Document (`docs/architecture.md`)
- [ ] Service diagram reflects current Docker Compose topology
- [ ] All backend service modules are represented (Workflow Orchestrator, Copilot Polling, GitHub Projects Service, Signal Bridge, AI providers)
- [ ] Data flow arrows are accurate — especially WebSocket paths and GitHub API interactions
- [ ] AI provider list is current (Copilot SDK, OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)

### Decision Records
- [ ] Any significant architectural decision made this quarter is captured as an ADR (Architecture Decision Record) in `docs/decisions/` (create if it doesn't exist)
- [ ] ADR format: **Context → Decision → Consequences**

### Developer Experience Audit
- [ ] Have a team member (or new contributor) follow `docs/setup.md` from scratch — note any friction
- [ ] Time the full local setup end-to-end; document in setup guide
- [ ] Review `docs/troubleshooting.md` — add any issues encountered during the audit

### Docs Gaps Analysis
- [ ] List all features shipped in the last quarter — confirm each has adequate documentation
- [ ] Identify docs that exist but no one references — consider consolidating or removing
- [ ] Check if a public-facing changelog or `CHANGELOG.md` should be started or updated

---

## Phase 5 — Standards & Tooling

### Formatting Standards
- All docs use ATX-style headings (`#`, `##`, `###`)
- Code blocks specify language for syntax highlighting (` ```python `, ` ```bash `, ` ```typescript `)
- Tables used for: env vars, API endpoints, config options
- Numbered lists for sequential steps; bullet lists for non-ordered items
- Filenames referenced in docs use inline code formatting (e.g., `config.py`)

### Linting & Automation
- [ ] Add `markdownlint` to CI — enforce consistent formatting on all `docs/` and `*.md` files
- [ ] Add `markdown-link-check` to CI — catch broken internal and external links automatically
- [ ] Consider `vale` for prose style linting (consistent tone, no passive voice, etc.)

### Doc Ownership
Each doc file should have a designated owner listed in a `docs/OWNERS.md` file:

```
docs/setup.md                   → infra/DX lead
docs/api-reference.md           → backend lead
docs/architecture.md            → tech lead
docs/agent-pipeline.md          → backend lead
docs/configuration.md           → backend lead
docs/signal-integration.md      → backend lead
docs/testing.md                 → QA / full stack lead
docs/troubleshooting.md         → rotating (whoever fixes the bug documents the fix)
docs/custom-agents-best-practices.md → backend lead
```

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|---------------|
| PR author | Update docs for any code change that affects behavior, config, or APIs |
| PR reviewer | Reject PRs that change behavior without updating relevant docs |
| Dev (rotation) | Weekly staleness sweep |
| Tech lead | Monthly review sign-off; quarterly architecture audit |
| All contributors | Follow formatting standards; flag stale docs when encountered |

---

## Definition of "Good Documentation"

A doc is considered current and complete when:

1. **Accurate** — Every step, command, variable, and path matches the current codebase
2. **Minimal** — No redundant content; each fact appears in exactly one place
3. **Actionable** — Readers can accomplish the documented task without needing to read source code
4. **Discoverable** — The correct doc is easy to find from the README or table of contents
5. **Maintained** — Last-reviewed date is within the current quarter

---

## 🤖 Agents Pipelines

| # | Status | Agent | Model | State |
|---|--------|-------|-------|-------|
| 1 | Backlog | `speckit.specify` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 2 | Ready | `speckit.plan` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 3 | Ready | `speckit.tasks` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 4 | In Progress | `speckit.implement` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 5 | In Progress | `copilot-review` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 6 | In Progress | `judge` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 7 | In Progress | `linter` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 8 | In Review | `human` | TBD | 🔄 Active |

docs/configuration.md           → backend lead
docs/signal-integration.md      → backend lead
docs/testing.md                 → QA / full stack lead
docs/troubleshooting.md         → rotating (whoever fixes the bug documents the fix)
docs/custom-agents-best-practices.md → backend lead
```

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|---------------|
| PR author | Update docs for any code change that affects behavior, config, or APIs |
| PR reviewer | Reject PRs that change behavior without updating relevant docs |
| Dev (rotation) | Weekly staleness sweep |
| Tech lead | Monthly review sign-off; quarterly architecture audit |
| All contributors | Follow formatting standards; flag stale docs when encountered |

---

## Definition of "Good Documentation"

A doc is considered current and complete when:

1. **Accurate** — Every step, command, variable, and path matches the current codebase
2. **Minimal** — No redundant content; each fact appears in exactly one place
3. **Actionable** — Readers can accomplish the documented task without needing to read source code
4. **Discoverable** — The correct doc is easy to find from the README or table of contents
5. **Maintained** — Last-reviewed date is within the current quarter

## Original Request

> On the Projects page. Add support for a user to upload a GitHub Parent Issue description directly and select the Agent Pipeline Config.

## User Story

As a user on the Projects page, I want to upload a GitHub Parent Issue description directly and select an associated Agent Pipeline Config so that I can quickly bootstrap agent workflows from existing GitHub issue context without manual re-entry of issue details.

## UI/UX Description

On the Projects page, introduce a dedicated upload/input section that allows users to paste or upload a GitHub Parent Issue description. Alongside this, provide a dropdown or selection component for choosing an Agent Pipeline Config from the available configurations. The UI should clearly associate the uploaded issue description with the selected pipeline config, presenting both inputs in a cohesive form layout. Include a submission/confirm action button that triggers the pipeline with the provided inputs. Provide inline validation feedback if the issue description is empty or no pipeline config is selected. On success, display a confirmation state or redirect to the relevant project/agent run view. The design should match the existing Projects page aesthetic and component patterns used in Project Solune.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST provide an input mechanism on the Projects page that allows users to upload or paste a GitHub Parent Issue description directly into the interface.
- System MUST provide a selection control (e.g., dropdown or list) on the Projects page for users to choose from available Agent Pipeline Configs.
- System MUST validate that both a GitHub Parent Issue description and an Agent Pipeline Config are provided before allowing submission; display clear inline error messages if either is missing.
- System MUST associate the uploaded GitHub Parent Issue description with the selected Agent Pipeline Config upon submission and pass both to the downstream agent pipeline execution logic.
- System MUST display a success confirmation state or navigate the user to the relevant project or agent run view after a successful submission.
- System SHOULD support both text paste and file upload (e.g., .md or .txt) as input methods for the GitHub Parent Issue description.
- System SHOULD dynamically populate the Agent Pipeline Config selection list from existing configurations available in the system, keeping the list current without requiring a page reload.
- System SHOULD preserve the entered issue description and selected config in form state if a validation error occurs, preventing data loss on failed submission attempts.

## Technical Notes

This feature extends the existing Projects page UI — identify the current Projects page component(s) in the frontend codebase and add the new upload form as a composable section or modal. The Agent Pipeline Config selector should fetch available configs from the existing agent-config data source or API endpoint; ensure the fetch is reactive and handles empty/error states gracefully. When the form is submitted, wire the GitHub Parent Issue description and selected Agent Pipeline Config ID into the agent pipeline invocation layer, preserving any existing pipeline execution contracts. Consider storing the raw issue description as a text field and linking the config by ID/slug in the relevant data model.

closing_issues.title: [speckit.specify] Update Tools Page: Replace 'Configure GitHub Toolset' with GitHub.com MCP Configuration Generator
closing_issues.body:
> **Parent Issue:** #3039 — Update Tools Page: Replace 'Configure GitHub Toolset' with GitHub.com MCP Configuration Generator

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.specify`

Write a detailed specification for this feature. Analyze requirements, define acceptance criteria, and document the technical approach.

---

## Parent Issue Context

## Original Request

> Update Tools page, for "Configure GitHub toolset" this should instead provide the user with the GitHub.com MCP configuration they need to copy/paste into GitHub.com.
> 
> This should be based on the active MCPs the user has.
> 
> Ensure "Built-In" MCPs, like Context7 and Code Graph Context - are labeled as such and included in the GitHub.com MCP definition.
> 
> The GitHub.com MCP definition is to run remote Custom GitHub Agents

## User Story

As a Solune user configuring GitHub integrations, I want the 'Configure GitHub Toolset' section on the Tools page to generate and display the GitHub.com MCP configuration I can copy/paste directly into GitHub.com — dynamically built from my active MCPs (including Built-In MCPs like Context7 and Code Graph Context) — so that I can seamlessly enable remote Custom GitHub Agents on GitHub.com without manually constructing the configuration myself.

## UI/UX Description

The Tools page 'Configure GitHub Toolset' section should be redesigned to present a ready-to-use GitHub.com MCP configuration block instead of its current behavior. The configuration output should be displayed in a styled, read-only code block with a one-click 'Copy to Clipboard' button. The configuration is generated dynamically based on the user's currently active MCPs. Built-In MCPs (e.g., Context7, Code Graph Context) must be visually distinguished with a 'Built-In' badge/label both in the MCP list and within the rendered configuration output. A brief contextual description should explain that this configuration is used to run remote Custom GitHub Agents on GitHub.com. If no MCPs are active, the UI should display an empty-state message guiding the user to activate MCPs first. The section should update in real time as the user toggles MCPs on or off.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST replace the existing 'Configure GitHub Toolset' UI with a GitHub.com MCP configuration generator panel on the Tools page.
- System MUST dynamically generate the GitHub.com MCP configuration JSON/YAML block based solely on the user's currently active MCPs at the time of viewing.
- System MUST include Built-In MCPs (Context7, Code Graph Context, and any future Built-In MCPs) in the generated GitHub.com MCP configuration definition automatically.
- System MUST visually label Built-In MCPs (e.g., Context7, Code Graph Context) with a 'Built-In' badge or tag wherever they appear in the Tools page MCP list and in the configuration output.
- System MUST display the generated GitHub.com MCP configuration in a read-only, syntax-highlighted code block with a functional 'Copy to Clipboard' button.
- System MUST re-generate the MCP configuration in real time whenever the user activates or deactivates an MCP, reflecting the updated active set immediately.
- System MUST display a clear empty-state message and actionable guidance when the user has no active MCPs and the configuration cannot be generated.
- System SHOULD include inline contextual help text clarifying that the generated configuration is intended for use with remote Custom GitHub Agents on GitHub.com.

## Technical Notes

The configuration generator should query the active MCP list from the existing MCP state/store and merge in all Built-In MCPs (Context7, Code Graph Context) unconditionally, flagging them with a 'builtin: true' or equivalent property. The output format must conform to the GitHub.com remote Custom GitHub Agents MCP configuration schema — verify against the GitHub.com MCP spec on the 'update-mcp-support' branch which may already contain relevant structures. Consider a dedicated utility function (e.g., buildGitHubMCPConfig(activeMCPs, builtins)) that is unit-testable and decoupled from the UI layer. The copy-to-clipboard interaction should use the Clipboard API with a fallback, and the code block should support syntax highlighting appropriate for the config format (JSON or YAML).

| Target Date | 2026-03-11 |

mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Update Tools page, for "Configure GitHub toolset" this should instead provide the user with the GitHub.com MCP configuration they need to copy/paste into GitHub.com.
> 
> This should be based on the active MCPs the user has.
> 
> Ensure "Built-In" MCPs, like Context7 and Code Graph Context - are labeled as such and included in the GitHub.com MCP definition.
> 
> The GitHub.com MCP definition is to run remote Custom GitHub Agents

## User Story

As a Solune user configuring GitHub integrations, I want the 'Configure GitHub Toolset' section on the Tools page to generate and display the GitHub.com MCP configuration I can copy/paste directly into GitHub.com — dynamically built from my active MCPs (including Built-In MCPs like Context7 and Code Graph Context) — so that I can seamlessly enable remote Custom GitHub Agents on GitHub.com without manually constructing the configuration myself.

## UI/UX Description

The Tools page 'Configure GitHub Toolset' section should be redesigned to present a ready-to-use GitHub.com MCP configuration block instead of its current behavior. The configuration output should be displayed in a styled, read-only code block with a one-click 'Copy to Clipboard' button. The configuration is generated dynamically based on the user's currently active MCPs. Built-In MCPs (e.g., Context7, Code Graph Context) must be visually distinguished with a 'Built-In' badge/label both in the MCP list and within the rendered configuration output. A brief contextual description should explain that this configuration is used to run remote Custom GitHub Agents on GitHub.com. If no MCPs are active, the UI should display an empty-state message guiding the user to activate MCPs first. The section should update in real time as the user toggles MCPs on or off.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST replace the existing 'Configure GitHub Toolset' UI with a GitHub.com MCP configuration generator panel on the Tools page.
- System MUST dynamically generate the GitHub.com MCP configuration JSON/YAML block based solely on the user's currently active MCPs at the time of viewing.
- System MUST include Built-In MCPs (Context7, Code Graph Context, and any future Built-In MCPs) in the generated GitHub.com MCP configuration definition automatically.
- System MUST visually label Built-In MCPs (e.g., Context7, Code Graph Context) with a 'Built-In' badge or tag wherever they appear in the Tools page MCP list and in the configuration output.
- System MUST display the generated GitHub.com MCP configuration in a read-only, syntax-highlighted code block with a functional 'Copy to Clipboard' button.
- System MUST re-generate the MCP configuration in real time whenever the user activates or deactivates an MCP, reflecting the updated active set immediately.
- System MUST display a clear empty-state message and actionable guidance when the user has no active MCPs and the configuration cannot be generated.
- System SHOULD include inline contextual help text clarifying that the generated configuration is intended for use with remote Custom GitHub Agents on GitHub.com.

## Technical Notes

The configuration generator should query the active MCP list from the existing MCP state/store and merge in all Built-In MCPs (Context7, Code Graph Context) unconditionally, flagging them with a 'builtin: true' or equivalent property. The output format must conform to the GitHub.com remote Custom GitHub Agents MCP configuration schema — verify against the GitHub.com MCP spec on the 'update-mcp-support' branch which may already contain relevant structures. Consider a dedicated utility function (e.g., buildGitHubMCPConfig(activeMCPs, builtins)) that is unit-testable and decoupled from the UI layer. The copy-to-clipboard interaction should use the Clipboard API with a fallback, and the code block should support syntax highlighting appropriate for the config format (JSON or YAML).

closing_issues.title: Pipelines: Support Side-by-Side (Parallel) Agent Layout When Creating or Editing Agent Pipelines
closing_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Update Pipelines page, to allow the user to put Agents side-by-side in a single column while Creating or Editing Agent Pipelines.
> 
> When Agents are side-by-side, they trigger/run at the same time (in parallel) all of these must complete before moving onto the next set of Agent(s).
> 
> When Agents are stack on top of each other, they trigger/run in series. (the only way the app currently allows)

## User Story

As a pipeline builder in Project Solune, I want to arrange Agents side-by-side within a single column stage so that those Agents execute in parallel simultaneously, all completing before the pipeline advances to the next sequential stage or Agent. Currently, the Pipelines page only supports stacked (series) Agent execution, and I need the flexibility to design pipelines with both parallel and sequential stages in a single workflow.

## UI/UX Description

The Pipelines page Create/Edit canvas must support two distinct Agent layout modes within a pipeline column/stage: (1) Stacked (series) — Agents arranged vertically, one after another, executing sequentially as today; and (2) Side-by-side (parallel) — multiple Agents arranged horizontally within the same column/stage, all firing simultaneously, with the pipeline gating forward progress until every parallel Agent in that stage has completed. Users should be able to drag-and-drop or use an 'Add Parallel Agent' affordance (e.g., a '+' button on the side of an existing Agent card) to place an Agent alongside another within the same stage. Parallel Agents within a stage should be visually grouped — e.g., enclosed in a shared container/band with a clear 'Runs in Parallel' label or icon (such as two-arrow or split-lane icon) to distinguish them from sequential stages. A vertical connector line or arrow between stages should only appear between stage groups, not between parallel siblings. On hover or selection, tooltips should clarify 'These agents run at the same time' vs. 'This agent runs after the previous completes'. The layout should be responsive and remain readable with 2–4+ parallel Agents in a single stage.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST allow users to add two or more Agents into the same pipeline stage/column so they are designated as parallel (side-by-side) during Create and Edit pipeline workflows.
- System MUST execute all Agents within a parallel stage simultaneously at runtime, triggering them at the same time regardless of individual Agent duration.
- System MUST NOT advance the pipeline to the next stage or Agent until every Agent within the current parallel stage has completed successfully.
- System MUST visually differentiate parallel stage groups from sequential (stacked) stages on the pipeline canvas using distinct layout, iconography, or container styling.
- System MUST preserve the existing sequential (stacked/series) execution behavior so that Agents not grouped in a parallel stage continue to run in order, one after another.
- System MUST handle partial failure within a parallel stage — defining and surfacing clear error state behavior (e.g., halt pipeline and mark stage as failed) when one or more parallel Agents fail.
- System MUST persist the parallel vs. sequential layout configuration as part of the pipeline definition when saving a Create or Edit operation.
- System SHOULD allow users to remove an Agent from a parallel stage (reverting it to its own sequential stage) without disrupting other Agents in the pipeline.
- System SHOULD support reordering of parallel Agents within a stage and reordering of stages (parallel or sequential) via drag-and-drop on the pipeline canvas.
- System SHOULD display a visual status indicator per parallel Agent during pipeline execution, showing which Agents in a parallel stage are running, completed, or failed in real time.

## Technical Notes

The pipeline data model must be updated to support a stage-based structure where each stage contains an ordered array of Agents (one Agent = sequential stage, multiple Agents = parallel stage), replacing or extending any flat ordered-list schema currently used. At runtime, the pipeline execution engine must fan out all Agents in a parallel stage using concurrent dispatch (e.g., Promise.all, parallel task queue, or equivalent async mechanism) and implement a join/barrier step that waits for all to resolve before proceeding. Frontend pipeline canvas likely built with a drag-and-drop library (e.g., React DnD, dnd-kit) — the drop logic must distinguish between dropping 'onto' an existing Agent (creating a parallel group) vs. dropping 'between' stages (inserting a new sequential stage). API contracts for pipeline CRUD endpoints must be versioned or backward-compatible to avoid breaking existing serial pipelines. Consider using a directed acyclic graph (DAG) representation internally for maximum future flexibility.

mentioned_issues.title: Update Tools Page: Replace 'Configure GitHub Toolset' with GitHub.com MCP Configuration Generator
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Update Tools page, for "Configure GitHub toolset" this should instead provide the user with the GitHub.com MCP configuration they need to copy/paste into GitHub.com.
> 
> This should be based on the active MCPs the user has.
> 
> Ensure "Built-In" MCPs, like Context7 and Code Graph Context - are labeled as such and included in the GitHub.com MCP definition.
> 
> The GitHub.com MCP definition is to run remote Custom GitHub Agents

## User Story

As a Solune user configuring GitHub integrations, I want the 'Configure GitHub Toolset' section on the Tools page to generate and display the GitHub.com MCP configuration I can copy/paste directly into GitHub.com — dynamically built from my active MCPs (including Built-In MCPs like Context7 and Code Graph Context) — so that I can seamlessly enable remote Custom GitHub Agents on GitHub.com without manually constructing the configuration myself.

## UI/UX Description

The Tools page 'Configure GitHub Toolset' section should be redesigned to present a ready-to-use GitHub.com MCP configuration block instead of its current behavior. The configuration output should be displayed in a styled, read-only code block with a one-click 'Copy to Clipboard' button. The configuration is generated dynamically based on the user's currently active MCPs. Built-In MCPs (e.g., Context7, Code Graph Context) must be visually distinguished with a 'Built-In' badge/label both in the MCP list and within the rendered configuration output. A brief contextual description should explain that this configuration is used to run remote Custom GitHub Agents on GitHub.com. If no MCPs are active, the UI should display an empty-state message guiding the user to activate MCPs first. The section should update in real time as the user toggles MCPs on or off.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST replace the existing 'Configure GitHub Toolset' UI with a GitHub.com MCP configuration generator panel on the Tools page.
- System MUST dynamically generate the GitHub.com MCP configuration JSON/YAML block based solely on the user's currently active MCPs at the time of viewing.
- System MUST include Built-In MCPs (Context7, Code Graph Context, and any future Built-In MCPs) in the generated GitHub.com MCP configuration definition automatically.
- System MUST visually label Built-In MCPs (e.g., Context7, Code Graph Context) with a 'Built-In' badge or tag wherever they appear in the Tools page MCP list and in the configuration output.
- System MUST display the generated GitHub.com MCP configuration in a read-only, syntax-highlighted code block with a functional 'Copy to Clipboard' button.
- System MUST re-generate the MCP configuration in real time whenever the user activates or deactivates an MCP, reflecting the updated active set immediately.
- System MUST display a clear empty-state message and actionable guidance when the user has no active MCPs and the configuration cannot be generated.
- System SHOULD include inline contextual help text clarifying that the generated configuration is intended for use with remote Custom GitHub Agents on GitHub.com.

## Technical Notes

The configuration generator should query the active MCP list from the existing MCP state/store and merge in all Built-In MCPs (Context7, Code Graph Context) unconditionally, flagging them with a 'builtin: true' or equivalent property. The output format must conform to the GitHub.com remote Custom GitHub Agents MCP configuration schema — verify against the GitHub.com MCP spec on the 'update-mcp-support' branch which may already contain relevant structures. Consider a dedicated utility function (e.g., buildGitHubMCPConfig(activeMCPs, builtins)) that is unit-testable and decoupled from the UI layer. The copy-to-clipboard interaction should use the Clipboard API with a fallback, and the code block should support syntax highlighting appropriate for the config format (JSON or YAML).

## Original Request

> Analyze entire frontend. Every component, every page, every menu. Ensure App is responsive and dynamic. Ensure it is mobile friendly. @Expert

## User Story

As an expert frontend engineer on Project Solune, I want every component, page, and menu in the application to be fully responsive, dynamic, and mobile-friendly so that users on all device sizes and orientations receive a seamless, high-quality experience without layout breakage, overflow issues, or inaccessible interactions.

## UI/UX Description

Conduct a comprehensive audit and remediation pass across the entire frontend — every page, every component, every navigation menu, every modal, drawer, tooltip, sidebar, and interactive element. All layouts must fluidly adapt from small mobile screens (320px) through tablet (768px) to large desktop (1440px+). Touch targets must be appropriately sized (minimum 44x44px per WCAG). Menus and navigation must collapse or transform gracefully on small screens (e.g., hamburger/drawer pattern). Typography, spacing, and iconography must scale proportionally. No horizontal scroll should appear on any viewport. Dynamic content (agent pipelines, chat panels, lists, tables, cards) must reflow without clipping or overflow. Sticky or fixed elements must not obscure content on any screen size. All interactive states (hover, focus, active) must be touch-compatible. The overall visual language must remain consistent across breakpoints — colors, spacing rhythm, and component hierarchy should not degrade on mobile.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST audit every page, component, and menu in the frontend codebase and document any element that fails to respond correctly to viewport changes between 320px and 1440px+.
- System MUST ensure no horizontal scrollbar appears at any standard breakpoint (320px, 375px, 390px, 768px, 1024px, 1280px, 1440px) on any page or component.
- System MUST ensure all interactive touch targets (buttons, links, menu items, icons) meet a minimum size of 44x44px on mobile viewports.
- System MUST ensure all navigation menus collapse or transform into a mobile-appropriate pattern (e.g., hamburger menu, bottom nav, or slide-out drawer) on viewports below 768px.
- System MUST ensure all page layouts, cards, grids, and list components use fluid/responsive CSS (flexbox, CSS Grid, or equivalent) and avoid fixed pixel widths that break on small screens.
- System MUST ensure agent pipeline views, chat panels, and data-heavy components reflow gracefully on tablet and mobile without content clipping, text overflow, or z-index collisions.
- System MUST ensure fixed or sticky UI elements (headers, footers, toolbars, tooltips) do not obscure primary content on any viewport size or orientation (portrait/landscape).
- System MUST ensure all form inputs, dropdowns, and interactive controls are fully usable via touch on mobile devices and pass basic cross-browser mobile testing (iOS Safari, Android Chrome).
- System SHOULD apply consistent responsive breakpoint tokens/variables across the codebase to avoid ad-hoc media query values and ensure maintainability.

mentioned_issues.title: Frontend Style Audit & Celestial/Cosmic Theme Animation Enhancement
mentioned_issues.body:
## Original Request

> Analyze every frontend component to ensure style and theme alignment. Also proper casing of text for best UI/UX. Use modern approaches and best practices. Make app more animated around the theme of sun/moon/stars/celestial/cosmic. @Expert

## User Story

As a frontend developer and end user, I want every UI component to be audited for visual consistency, proper text casing, and modern best practices, and for the app to be enriched with fluid animations inspired by a sun/moon/stars/celestial/cosmic theme, so that the application feels cohesive, polished, visually immersive, and thematically aligned throughout every screen.

## UI/UX Description

Conduct a full sweep of all frontend components to enforce style and theme alignment: consistent use of design tokens (spacing, typography, color palette), proper title/sentence casing across all labels, headings, buttons, tooltips, and placeholders per UX best practices. Introduce a rich celestial/cosmic animation layer — including subtle star-field backgrounds, glowing sun/moon iconography transitions, orbital particle effects, twinkling star micro-animations on hover/focus states, and smooth gradient shifts mimicking day-to-night/cosmic transitions. Animations should respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. All motion should feel purposeful, not distracting — reinforcing the solar theme already present (see `feat/solar-theme-agent-icon-catalog` branch). Use CSS custom properties and/or a consistent animation library (e.g., Framer Motion or CSS keyframes) to ensure maintainability. Every component — cards, buttons, modals, sidebars, navigation, tooltips, inputs, loaders — must be visited and assessed.

## Functional Requirements

- System MUST audit every frontend component for adherence to the established design token system (colors, typography, spacing, border-radius, shadows) and flag or correct any deviations.
- System MUST enforce proper text casing (title case for headings/nav items, sentence case for body copy/descriptions, ALL CAPS only for labels/badges per UX convention) across all UI text elements including buttons, tooltips, placeholders, and page titles.
- System MUST introduce celestial/cosmic-themed animations including: star-field or particle background effects, sun/moon glow transitions, twinkling star hover/focus micro-interactions, and orbital or shimmer loading states.
- System MUST ensure all new and existing animations respect the `prefers-reduced-motion` CSS media query, disabling or minimizing motion for users who have opted out.
- System MUST apply modern CSS best practices (CSS custom properties, logical properties, clamp() for fluid typography, container queries where applicable) during the component audit and refactor.
- System MUST ensure all animated and restyled components remain fully accessible — maintaining WCAG AA contrast ratios under all animation states, focus-visible outlines, and ARIA attributes.
- System SHOULD standardize animation duration and easing curves via shared design tokens (e.g., `--transition-cosmic-slow: 800ms ease-in-out`) to ensure motion consistency across the app.
- System SHOULD align the celestial animation palette with the existing solar theme established in the `feat/solar-theme-agent-icon-catalog` branch, reusing or extending existing icon and color assets.
- System SHOULD ensure all components are responsive and that animations degrade gracefully on mobile/low-power devices.
- System MUST produce a brief style alignment report or inline code comments documenting what was changed per component for future maintainability.

## Technical Notes

Base all animation and theming work on the existing solar theme foundation in `feat/solar-theme-agent-icon-catalog`; coordinate to avoid conflicts or redundant design token definitions. Use Framer Motion (if already in the dependency tree) or CSS `@keyframes` + `animation` for celestial effects — prefer CSS-native where possible for performance. Implement a shared `animations.css` or `theme/motion.ts` token file so durations, easing, and keyframes are centralized and not scattered per-component. For the star/particle effects, consider a lightweight canvas or SVG-based background component to avoid heavy DOM overhead; lazy-load it to protect initial page performance.

- System MUST apply modern CSS best practices (CSS custom properties, logical properties, clamp() for fluid typography, container queries where applicable) during the component audit and refactor.
- System MUST ensure all animated and restyled components remain fully accessible — maintaining WCAG AA contrast ratios under all animation states, focus-visible outlines, and ARIA attributes.
- System SHOULD standardize animation duration and easing curves via shared design tokens (e.g., `--transition-cosmic-slow: 800ms ease-in-out`) to ensure motion consistency across the app.

- System SHOULD ensure all components are responsive and that animations degrade gracefully on mobile/low-power devices.
- System MUST produce a brief style alignment report or inline code comments documenting what was changed per component for future maintainability.

Base all animation and theming work on the existing solar theme foundation in `feat/solar-theme-agent-icon-catalog`; coordinate to avoid conflicts or redundant design token definitions. mentioned_issues.title: Documentation Sweep
mentioned_issues.body:
# Recurring Documentation Update Process

## Overview

A structured cadence for keeping all project documentation accurate, complete, and helpful across the full stack — backend API, frontend components, architecture, configuration, and developer guides.

---

## Cadence

| Review Type            | Frequency     | Trigger                                              |
|------------------------|---------------|------------------------------------------------------|
| Inline doc check       | Every PR      | Author + reviewer responsibility                     |
| Staleness sweep        | Weekly        | Dev rotation (same person as security spot check)    |
| Full doc review        | Monthly       | Sprint planning item                                 |
| Architecture audit     | Quarterly     | After major feature milestones                       |
| New contributor review | On demand     | Before onboarding a new team member                  |

---

## Phase 1 — PR-Level Checks (Every Pull Request)

The PR author is responsible. Reviewers must not approve if these are unmet.

- [ ] Any new endpoint added to `api/` has a corresponding entry in `docs/api-reference.md`
- [ ] Any new environment variable added to `config.py` is documented in `docs/configuration.md`
- [ ] Any change to startup behavior, Docker setup, or prerequisites is reflected in `docs/setup.md`
- [ ] Any new agent, workflow module, or AI provider change is reflected in `docs/agent-pipeline.md`
- [ ] Any schema or data model change is reflected in relevant API or architecture docs
- [ ] PR description references which doc files were updated (or explicitly states "no doc changes needed")

**Add to PR template checklist:**
```
- [ ] Documentation updated (or confirmed not needed)
```

---

## Phase 2 — Weekly Staleness Sweep (~30 minutes, dev rotation)

A quick pass to catch docs that have drifted from the codebase.

### API Reference (`docs/api-reference.md`)
- [ ] Scan `backend/src/api/` — confirm every route file has matching API table entries
- [ ] Confirm all path prefixes, methods, and path params are still accurate
- [ ] Flag any endpoints removed or deprecated but still listed

### Configuration (`docs/configuration.md`)
- [ ] Compare documented env vars against `backend/src/config.py` — add any missing, remove any deleted
- [ ] Confirm default values and required/optional status are still correct

### Setup Guide (`docs/setup.md`)
- [ ] Confirm Docker Compose and manual setup steps still match project state
- [ ] Confirm prerequisite versions (Python, Node, Docker) still match `pyproject.toml` and `package.json`
- [ ] Confirm Codespaces badge and quick start flow still work end-to-end

---

## Phase 3 — Monthly Full Documentation Review (~2–3 hours)

### Coverage Audit

Walk every file in `docs/` and verify it is:
- [ ] **Accurate** — reflects current code behavior, not aspirational or outdated state
- [ ] **Complete** — no major features or workflows are undocumented
- [ ] **Consistent** — terminology, naming, and formatting are uniform across files

| File | Ownership | Key Things to Verify |
|------|-----------|----------------------|
| `docs/setup.md` | Infra/DX | Prerequisites, Codespaces flow, env var list, Docker Compose steps |
| `docs/configuration.md` | Backend | All env vars, types, defaults, and validation rules |
| `docs/api-reference.md` | Backend | All routes, methods, params, auth requirements, and response shapes |
| `docs/architecture.md` | Full stack | Service diagram, data flow, WebSocket flow, AI provider list |
| `docs/agent-pipeline.md` | Backend | Workflow orchestrator modules, Copilot polling, task/issue generation |
| `docs/custom-agents-best-practices.md` | Backend | Agent authoring patterns, extension points |
| `docs/signal-integration.md` | Backend | Signal sidecar setup, webhook flow, delivery logic |
| `docs/testing.md` | Full stack | Test commands, coverage targets, Playwright setup, CI behavior |
| `docs/troubleshooting.md` | Full stack | Common errors and resolutions — remove fixed issues, add new ones |
| `docs/project-structure.md` | Full stack | Directory layout — update after any structural refactor |
| `frontend/docs/` | Frontend | Component patterns, findings log, any frontend-specific guides |

### Cross-Reference Check
- [ ] All internal `docs/` links are valid and resolve to existing headings
- [ ] Code snippets in docs compile or run without error against current codebase
- [ ] README.md top-level links to correct doc files
- [ ] Any external links (GitHub docs, library docs) still resolve to relevant pages

### Readability & Usability
- [ ] Each page has a clear purpose statement at the top
- [ ] Step-by-step guides use numbered lists and include expected outcomes
- [ ] Configuration tables include: variable name, type, required/optional, default, description
- [ ] API tables include: method, path, auth required, brief description
- [ ] Troubleshooting entries follow the format: **Symptom → Cause → Fix**

---

## Phase 4 — Quarterly Architecture Audit (~half day)

Run after major feature milestones (new integrations, significant refactors, new agent types).

### Architecture Document (`docs/architecture.md`)
- [ ] Service diagram reflects current Docker Compose topology
- [ ] All backend service modules are represented (Workflow Orchestrator, Copilot Polling, GitHub Projects Service, Signal Bridge, AI providers)
- [ ] Data flow arrows are accurate — especially WebSocket paths and GitHub API interactions
- [ ] AI provider list is current (Copilot SDK, OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.)

### Decision Records
- [ ] Any significant architectural decision made this quarter is captured as an ADR (Architecture Decision Record) in `docs/decisions/` (create if it doesn't exist)
- [ ] ADR format: **Context → Decision → Consequences**

### Developer Experience Audit
- [ ] Have a team member (or new contributor) follow `docs/setup.md` from scratch — note any friction
- [ ] Time the full local setup end-to-end; document in setup guide
- [ ] Review `docs/troubleshooting.md` — add any issues encountered during the audit

### Docs Gaps Analysis
- [ ] List all features shipped in the last quarter — confirm each has adequate documentation
- [ ] Identify docs that exist but no one references — consider consolidating or removing
- [ ] Check if a public-facing changelog or `CHANGELOG.md` should be started or updated

---

## Phase 5 — Standards & Tooling

### Formatting Standards
- All docs use ATX-style headings (`#`, `##`, `###`)
- Code blocks specify language for syntax highlighting (` ```python `, ` ```bash `, ` ```typescript `)
- Tables used for: env vars, API endpoints, config options
- Numbered lists for sequential steps; bullet lists for non-ordered items
- Filenames referenced in docs use inline code formatting (e.g., `config.py`)

### Linting & Automation
- [ ] Add `markdownlint` to CI — enforce consistent formatting on all `docs/` and `*.md` files
- [ ] Add `markdown-link-check` to CI — catch broken internal and external links automatically
- [ ] Consider `vale` for prose style linting (consistent tone, no passive voice, etc.)

### Doc Ownership
Each doc file should have a designated owner listed in a `docs/OWNERS.md` file:

```
docs/setup.md                   → infra/DX lead
docs/api-reference.md           → backend lead
docs/architecture.md            → tech lead
docs/agent-pipeline.md          → backend lead
docs/configuration.md           → backend lead
docs/signal-integration.md      → backend lead
docs/testing.md                 → QA / full stack lead
docs/troubleshooting.md         → rotating (whoever fixes the bug documents the fix)
docs/custom-agents-best-practices.md → backend lead
```

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|---------------|
| PR author | Update docs for any code change that affects behavior, config, or APIs |
| PR reviewer | Reject PRs that change behavior without updating relevant docs |
| Dev (rotation) | Weekly staleness sweep |
| Tech lead | Monthly review sign-off; quarterly architecture audit |
| All contributors | Follow formatting standards; flag stale docs when encountered |

---

## Definition of "Good Documentation"

A doc is considered current and complete when:

1. **Accurate** — Every step, command, variable, and path matches the current codebase
2. **Minimal** — No redundant content; each fact appears in exactly one place
3. **Actionable** — Readers can accomplish the documented task without needing to read source code
4. **Discoverable** — The correct doc is easy to find from the README or table of contents
5. **Maintained** — Last-reviewed date is within the current quarter

---

## 🤖 Agents Pipelines

| # | Status | Agent | Model | State |
|---|--------|-------|-------|-------|
| 1 | Backlog | `speckit.specify` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 2 | Ready | `speckit.plan` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 3 | Ready | `speckit.tasks` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 4 | In Progress | `speckit.implement` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 5 | In Progress | `copilot-review` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 6 | In Progress | `judge` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 7 | In Progress | `linter` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 8 | In Review | `human` | TBD | 🔄 Active |

- All docs use ATX-style headings (`#`, `##`, `###`)
- Code blocks specify language for syntax highlighting (` ```python `, ` ```bash `, ` ```typescript `)
- Tables used for: env vars, API endpoints, config options
- Numbered lists for sequential steps; bullet lists for non-ordered items
- Filenames referenced in docs use inline code formatting (e.g., `config.py`)

### Linting & Automation
- [ ] Add `markdownlint` to CI — enforce consistent formatting on all `docs/` and `*.md` files
- [ ] Add `markdown-link-check` to CI — catch broken internal and external links automatically
- [ ] Consider `vale` for prose style linting (consistent tone, no passive voice, etc.)

### Doc Ownership
Each doc file should have a designated owner listed in a `docs/OWNERS.md` file:

```
docs/setup.md                   → infra/DX lead
docs/api-reference.md           → backend lead
docs/architecture.md            → tech lead
docs/agent-pipeline.md          → backend lead
docs/configuration.md           → backend lead
docs/signal-integration.md      → backend lead
docs/testing.md                 → QA / full stack lead
docs/troubleshooting.md         → rotating (whoever fixes the bug documents the fix)
docs/custom-agents-best-practices.md → backend lead
```

---

## Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibility |
|------|---------------|
| PR author | Update docs for any code change that affects behavior, config, or APIs |
| PR reviewer | Reject PRs that change behavior without updating relevant docs |
| Dev (rotation) | Weekly staleness sweep |
| Tech lead | Monthly review sign-off; quarterly architecture audit |
| All contributors | Follow formatting standards; flag stale docs when encountered |

---

## Definition of "Good Documentation"

A doc is considered current and complete when:

1. **Accurate** — Every step, command, variable, and path matches the current codebase
2. **Minimal** — No redundant content; each fact appears in exactly one place
3. **Actionable** — Readers can accomplish the documented task without needing to read source code
4. **Discoverable** — The correct doc is easy to find from the README or table of contents
5. **Maintained** — Last-reviewed date is within the current quarter

mentioned_issues.body:
## Performance Review

Perform a balanced first pass focused on measurable, low-risk performance gains across backend and frontend. Start by capturing baselines and instrumentation, then fix the highest-value issues already surfaced by the codebase: backend GitHub API churn around board refreshes and polling, and frontend board responsiveness issues caused by broad query invalidation, full-list rerenders, and hot event listeners. Defer broader architectural refactors like virtualization and large service decomposition unless the first pass fails to meet targets.

**Steps**
1. Phase 1 — Baseline and guardrails. Capture current backend and frontend performance baselines before changing behavior. Measure idle API activity for an open board, board endpoint request cost, WebSocket/polling refresh behavior, and frontend render hot spots. Reuse existing tests around cache, polling, WebSocket fallback, and board refresh to define a before/after checklist. This phase blocks all optimization work because the success criteria and regression guardrails depend on it.
2. Phase 1 — Confirm current backend state against Spec 022. Verify whether WebSocket change detection, board cache TTL alignment, and sub-issue cache invalidation are fully implemented or only partially landed. The current board endpoint already appears to set a 300-second TTL and clears sub-issue cache on manual refresh, so the remaining work should target any still-missing pieces rather than redoing completed items. This step can run in parallel with frontend baseline inspection once the measurement checklist is defined.
3. Phase 2 — Backend API consumption fixes. Prioritize the highest-value remaining server-side issues: WebSocket subscription refresh logic in the projects API, sub-issue caching behavior for board data, and any remaining unnecessary GitHub calls in polling or repository resolution. Explicitly validate that idle board viewing no longer emits repeated refreshes when data is unchanged, that warm sub-issue caches materially reduce board refresh call count, and that fallback polling does not trigger expensive board refreshes unintentionally. This depends on Phase 1 baselines.
4. Phase 2 — Frontend refresh-path fixes. Update the real-time and fallback refresh paths so lightweight task updates stay decoupled from the expensive board data query except on manual refresh. Review the interaction between WebSocket updates, fallback polling, auto-refresh, and manual refresh to ensure they use a single coherent policy and do not recreate the prior polling storm. This can proceed in parallel with backend API work once the desired refresh contract is confirmed.
5. Phase 3 — Frontend render optimization. Target low-risk rendering costs in board and chat surfaces: reduce repeated derived-data work in page components and hooks, stabilize props where useful, memoize heavy card/list components when it actually reduces rerenders, and throttle or rationalize hot event listeners such as drag and popover positioning. Keep this phase intentionally low-risk; avoid introducing new dependencies or virtualization in the first pass unless baseline results show large boards still regress after the lighter fixes.
6. Phase 3 — Verification and regression coverage. Extend or adjust unit/integration coverage around backend cache behavior, WebSocket change detection, fallback polling, and frontend board refresh logic. Validate with backend tests, frontend tests, and at least one manual network/profile pass to confirm the target improvements are real rather than inferred. This depends on Phases 2 and 3.
7. Phase 4 — Optional second-wave work. If the first pass still leaves material UI lag on large boards or excessive backend complexity, prepare a follow-on plan for structural changes: board virtualization, deeper service decomposition around GitHub project fetching/polling, bounded cache policies, and stronger instrumentation around request budgets and render timings. This phase is explicitly out of scope for the first implementation unless measurements prove it is necessary.

**Relevant files**
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/specs/022-api-rate-limit-protection/spec.md` — primary acceptance criteria for idle-rate-limit reduction, sub-issue caching, refresh behavior, and cache TTL alignment.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/api/projects.py` — projects tasks endpoints and WebSocket subscription flow; likely location for change-detection verification and refresh semantics.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/api/board.py` — board-data cache behavior, manual refresh semantics, and sub-issue cache invalidation path.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/services/copilot_polling/polling_loop.py` — polling hot path and expensive background work that can still consume rate limit budget.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/services/github_projects/service.py` — board/project fetching path and candidate reuse points for sub-issue caching or batching.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/services/cache.py` — cache TTLs, cache-key helpers, and any bounded-cache improvements if needed.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/utils.py` — shared repository resolution logic to reuse instead of duplicated fallback flows.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/api/workflow.py` — known duplicate repository-resolution path that may add inconsistency and avoidable work.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/hooks/useRealTimeSync.ts` — current WebSocket/fallback polling behavior; today it still invalidates board data during polling fallback.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/hooks/useBoardRefresh.ts` — board auto-refresh policy and manual refresh coordination.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/hooks/useProjectBoard.ts` — board query ownership and invalidation/refetch strategy.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/components/board/BoardColumn.tsx` — full column list rendering without memoization or virtualization.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/components/board/IssueCard.tsx` — likely high-frequency rerender unit for board interactions.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/pages/ProjectsPage.tsx` — render-time sorting/aggregation and board-level derived state.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPopup.tsx` — hot drag listener path worth throttling.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/components/agents/AddAgentPopover.tsx` — positioning listeners and update frequency.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/tests/unit/test_cache.py` — backend cache TTL and stale fallback coverage to extend.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/tests/unit/test_api_board.py` — board cache and board endpoint behavior to reuse for regression tests.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/tests/unit/test_copilot_polling.py` — polling behavior and rate-limit-aware logic to reuse.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/hooks/useRealTimeSync.test.tsx` — refresh invalidation and WebSocket fallback coverage to extend.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/hooks/useBoardRefresh.test.tsx` — refresh timer and deduplication behavior to reuse.

**Verification**
1. Backend baseline: measure idle API activity for an open board over a fixed interval and compare against Spec 022 targets; confirm no repeated unchanged refreshes are sent.
2. Backend automated checks: run Ruff, Pyright, and the targeted pytest files covering cache, board, projects/WebSocket, and polling behavior.
3. Frontend baseline: profile board load and interaction on a representative project size, inspect network activity for WebSocket, fallback polling, and board query invalidation, and identify repeated rerender sources.
4. Frontend automated checks: run ESLint, type-checking, Vitest coverage for real-time sync and board refresh hooks, and a build check.
5. Manual end-to-end check: verify that WebSocket updates refresh task data quickly, fallback polling remains safe, manual refresh still bypasses caches when intended, and board interactions remain responsive.

**Decisions**
- Selected approach: balanced pass across backend and frontend rather than a single-area optimization.
- Recommended implementation scope for the first pass: low-risk optimizations first, even though the user left the aggressiveness undecided.
- Included scope: measurement, idle API reduction, refresh-path cleanup, low-risk render optimization, and regression coverage.
- Excluded from the first pass unless metrics justify it: board virtualization, major service decomposition, dependency changes, and larger architectural rewrites.
- Baseline measurement is mandatory before code changes so the improvements can be proven and not just assumed.

**Further Considerations**
1. If large boards still feel slow after the low-risk frontend fixes, the next recommended option is virtualization rather than additional scattered memoization.
2. If backend API churn remains high after Spec 022-aligned fixes, the next recommended option is deeper consolidation in the GitHub projects service and polling pipeline rather than more cache-layer patching.
3. If repeated performance work is expected in this repo, add lightweight instrumentation or logging around board refresh cost, sub-issue cache hit rate, and refresh-source attribution so regressions are visible earlier.

---

## 🤖 Agents Pipelines

| # | Status | Agent | Model | State |
|---|--------|-------|-------|-------|
| 1 | Backlog | `speckit.specify` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 2 | Ready | `speckit.plan` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 3 | Ready | `speckit.tasks` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 4 | In Progress | `speckit.implement` | TBD | 🔄 Active |
| 5 | In Progress | `copilot-review` | TBD | ⏳ Pending |
| 6 | In Progress | `judge` | TBD | ⏳ Pending |
| 7 | In Progress | `linter` | TBD | ⏳ Pending |
| 8 | In Review | `human` | TBD | ⏳ Pending |

> **Parent Issue:** #2691 — Performance Review

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.plan`

Create a detailed implementation plan. Break down the specification into actionable steps, identify dependencies, and define the order of execution.

---

## Parent Issue Context

## Performance Review

Perform a balanced first pass focused on measurable, low-risk performance gains across backend and frontend. Start by capturing baselines and instrumentation, then fix the highest-value issues already surfaced by the codebase: backend GitHub API churn around board refreshes and polling, and frontend board responsiveness issues caused by broad query invalidation, full-list rerenders, and hot event listeners. Defer broader architectural refactors like virtualization and large service decomposition unless the first pass fails to meet targets.

**Steps**
1. Phase 1 — Baseline and guardrails. Capture current backend and frontend performance baselines before changing behavior. Measure idle API activity for an open board, board endpoint request cost, WebSocket/polling refresh behavior, and frontend render hot spots. Reuse existing tests around cache, polling, WebSocket fallback, and board refresh to define a before/after checklist. This phase blocks all optimization work because the success criteria and regression guardrails depend on it.
2. Phase 1 — Confirm current backend state against Spec 022. Verify whether WebSocket change detection, board cache TTL alignment, and sub-issue cache invalidation are fully implemented or only partially landed. The current board endpoint already appears to set a 300-second TTL and clears sub-issue cache on manual refresh, so the remaining work should target any still-missing pieces rather than redoing completed items. This step can run in parallel with frontend baseline inspection once the measurement checklist is defined.
3. Phase 2 — Backend API consumption fixes. Prioritize the highest-value remaining server-side issues: WebSocket subscription refresh logic in the projects API, sub-issue caching behavior for board data, and any remaining unnecessary GitHub calls in polling or repository resolution. Explicitly validate that idle board viewing no longer emits repeated refreshes when data is unchanged, that warm sub-issue caches materially reduce board refresh call count, and that fallback polling does not trigger expensive board refreshes unintentionally. This depends on Phase 1 baselines.
4. Phase 2 — Frontend refresh-path fixes. Update the real-time and fallback refresh paths so lightweight task updates stay decoupled from the expensive board data query except on manual refresh. Review the interaction between WebSocket updates, fallback polling, auto-refresh, and manual refresh to ensure they use a single coherent policy and do not recreate the prior polling storm. This can proceed in parallel with backend API work once the desired refresh contract is confirmed.
5. Phase 3 — Frontend render optimization. Target low-risk rendering costs in board and chat surfaces: reduce repeated derived-data work in page components and hooks, stabilize props where useful, memoize heavy card/list components when it actually reduces rerenders, and throttle or rationalize hot event listeners such as drag and popover positioning. Keep this phase intentionally low-risk; avoid introducing new dependencies or virtualization in the first pass unless baseline results show large boards still regress after the lighter fixes.
6. Phase 3 — Verification and regression coverage. Extend or adjust unit/integration coverage around backend cache behavior, WebSocket change detection, fallback polling, and frontend board refresh logic. Validate with backend tests, frontend tests, and at least one manual network/profile pass to confirm the target improvements are real rather than inferred. This depends on Phases 2 and 3.
7. Phase 4 — Optional second-wave work. If the first pass still leaves material UI lag on large boards or excessive backend complexity, prepare a follow-on plan for structural changes: board virtualization, deeper service decomposition around GitHub project fetching/polling, bounded cache policies, and stronger instrumentation around request budgets and render timings. - `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/services/github_projects/service.py` — board/project fetching path and candidate reuse points for sub-issue caching or batching.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/services/cache.py` — cache TTLs, cache-key helpers, and any bounded-cache improvements if needed.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/utils.py` — shared repository resolution logic to reuse instead of duplicated fallback flows.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/backend/src/api/workflow.py` — known duplicate repository-resolution path that may add inconsistency and avoidable work.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/hooks/useRealTimeSync.ts` — current WebSocket/fallback polling behavior; today it still invalidates board data during polling fallback.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/hooks/useBoardRefresh.ts` — board auto-refresh policy and manual refresh coordination.

- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/components/board/IssueCard.tsx` — likely high-frequency rerender unit for board interactions.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/pages/ProjectsPage.tsx` — render-time sorting/aggregation and board-level derived state.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPopup.tsx` — hot drag listener path worth throttling.
- `/root/repos/github-projects-chat/github-workflows/frontend/src/components/agents/AddAgentPopover.tsx` — positioning listeners and update frequency.
