closing_issues.title: [speckit.specify] Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
closing_issues.body:
> **Parent Issue:** #4791 — Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.specify`

Write a detailed specification for this feature. Analyze requirements, define acceptance criteria, and document the technical approach.

---

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
Destructive actions (delete agent, pipeline, chore, tool) use a confirmation dialog but offer no recovery after confirmation. The standard modern pattern — an "undo toast" with a timed grace period — is missing entirely. The pipeline editor already has an undo/redo stack (usePipelineConfig.ts) but it resets completely on delete, and no other entity has any undo capability.

The fix: replace immediate hard-deletes with a soft-delete + undo toast pattern. During a grace window (~5s), the item is hidden from the UI but not yet deleted server-side. Clicking "Undo" in the toast cancels the pending delete. If the timer expires, the real DELETE fires.

Phase 1 — Generic Undo Toast Infrastructure
Create useUndoableDelete hook — New file frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts. Encapsulates:
Accepts: { onDelete: () => Promise<void>, undoTimeoutMs?: number, entityLabel: string }
On trigger: immediately hides item via optimistic cache removal (from Plan #3's onMutate pattern), then shows sonner toast with action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: cancelDelete } and duration: 5000
Internally: starts a setTimeout that fires the real API delete when the timer expires
Undo handler: clears timeout, restores cache snapshot, shows "Restored" toast
Cleanup: clears pending timeout on unmount
Returns { undoableDelete: (id) => void, pendingIds: Set<string> }
Toast configuration — In frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx, ensure <Toaster /> has closeButton enabled and supports action buttons (sonner does this natively via toast('message', { action: { label, onClick } })). No library change needed — sonner v1+ supports this out of the box.
Phase 2 — Chore Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts, frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx)
Replace confirmation + immediate delete — In ChoreCard.tsx, remove the confirm() dialog for delete. Instead call undoableDelete(choreId) from the new hook. Depends on step 1.
Optimistic removal — useDeleteChore gets onMutate to remove chore from choreKeys.list(projectId) cache instantly (same pattern as Plan #3 step 7), but the actual mutationFn is deferred by the undo hook.
Backend: no changes needed — Chore delete is already a hard delete (DELETE /chores/{project_id}/{chore_id}). The undo window is purely client-side; the API call simply doesn't fire until the grace period ends.
Phase 3 — Pipeline Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts)
Replace confirmation dialog — Currently useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts shows "This action cannot be undone." Replace with undo toast pattern. The pipeline is removed from pipelineKeys.list(projectId) cache immediately, real DELETE fires after grace period. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phase 2.
Preserve undo/redo stacks — The existing pipeline editor undo/redo (undoStackRef, redoStackRef, Ctrl+Z) is scoped to field edits inside the editor. This is orthogonal to delete-undo — keep both. The delete-undo is a toast-based grace period; the editor undo is a state history stack.
Phase 4 — Tool Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts, frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx)
Replace two-step confirm — Tool delete currently does a pre-flight check (confirm=false) to show affected agents, then a confirmation dialog. Change to: show affected agents inline (tooltip/popover on delete button), then fire undoableDelete(toolId). The undo toast provides the safety net instead of the dialog. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–3.
Deferred delete with confirm=true — The real DELETE /tools/{project_id}/{tool_id}?confirm=true fires only after grace period expires.
Phase 5 — Agent Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts, frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx)
Agent delete is already soft — Backend marks agent as pending_deletion and opens a PR. The undo pattern here is simpler: on "Undo", call a restore endpoint (or cancel the PR). If no restore endpoint exists, keep the confirmation dialog for agents but add an undo toast that re-enables the agent before the PR merges. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–4.
Backend: Add agent restore endpoint (optional) — POST /agents/{project_id}/{agent_id}/restore that flips status back from pending_deletion to active and closes the deletion PR. Only needed if we want full undo for agents.

mentioned_issues.title: Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
mentioned_issues.body:
Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
Destructive actions (delete agent, pipeline, chore, tool) use a confirmation dialog but offer no recovery after confirmation. The standard modern pattern — an "undo toast" with a timed grace period — is missing entirely. The pipeline editor already has an undo/redo stack (usePipelineConfig.ts) but it resets completely on delete, and no other entity has any undo capability.

The fix: replace immediate hard-deletes with a soft-delete + undo toast pattern. During a grace window (~5s), the item is hidden from the UI but not yet deleted server-side. Clicking "Undo" in the toast cancels the pending delete. If the timer expires, the real DELETE fires.

Phase 1 — Generic Undo Toast Infrastructure
Create useUndoableDelete hook — New file frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts. Encapsulates:
Accepts: { onDelete: () => Promise<void>, undoTimeoutMs?: number, entityLabel: string }
On trigger: immediately hides item via optimistic cache removal (from Plan #3's onMutate pattern), then shows sonner toast with action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: cancelDelete } and duration: 5000
Internally: starts a setTimeout that fires the real API delete when the timer expires
Undo handler: clears timeout, restores cache snapshot, shows "Restored" toast
Cleanup: clears pending timeout on unmount
Returns { undoableDelete: (id) => void, pendingIds: Set<string> }
Toast configuration — In frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx, ensure <Toaster /> has closeButton enabled and supports action buttons (sonner does this natively via toast('message', { action: { label, onClick } })). No library change needed — sonner v1+ supports this out of the box.
Phase 2 — Chore Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts, frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx)
Replace confirmation + immediate delete — In ChoreCard.tsx, remove the confirm() dialog for delete. Instead call undoableDelete(choreId) from the new hook. Depends on step 1.
Optimistic removal — useDeleteChore gets onMutate to remove chore from choreKeys.list(projectId) cache instantly (same pattern as Plan #3 step 7), but the actual mutationFn is deferred by the undo hook.
Backend: no changes needed — Chore delete is already a hard delete (DELETE /chores/{project_id}/{chore_id}). The undo window is purely client-side; the API call simply doesn't fire until the grace period ends.
Phase 3 — Pipeline Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts)
Replace confirmation dialog — Currently useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts shows "This action cannot be undone." Replace with undo toast pattern. The pipeline is removed from pipelineKeys.list(projectId) cache immediately, real DELETE fires after grace period. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phase 2.
Preserve undo/redo stacks — The existing pipeline editor undo/redo (undoStackRef, redoStackRef, Ctrl+Z) is scoped to field edits inside the editor. This is orthogonal to delete-undo — keep both. The delete-undo is a toast-based grace period; the editor undo is a state history stack.

closing_issues.title: [speckit.specify] Plan: Activity Log / Audit Trail
closing_issues.body:
> **Parent Issue:** #4802 — Plan: Activity Log / Audit Trail

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.specify`

Write a detailed specification for this feature. Analyze requirements, define acceptance criteria, and document the technical approach.

---

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: Activity Log / Audit Trail
The backend already persists pipeline runs (pipeline_runs + pipeline_stage_states tables) and cleanup operations (cleanup_audit_logs table) with GET endpoints, but the frontend has zero UI to view them. Workflow transitions are in-memory only. Chore triggers and agent executions have no history at all. The notification bell (useNotifications.ts) returns an empty array — it's a placeholder.

The fix: add a unified activity events table in the backend, persist all trackable actions into it, expose a paginated API, and build an Activity page + feed component in the frontend.

Phase 1 — Backend: Unified Activity Events Table
New migration — backend/src/migrations/ — Create activity_events table:
id INTEGER PK, event_type TEXT (pipeline_run | pipeline_stage | chore_trigger | chore_crud | agent_crud | agent_execution | cleanup | app_crud | tool_crud | status_change | webhook), entity_type TEXT (pipeline | chore | agent | app | tool | issue), entity_id TEXT, project_id TEXT, actor TEXT (user or "system"), action TEXT (created | updated | deleted | triggered | started | completed | failed | cancelled | moved), summary TEXT (human-readable one-liner), detail TEXT (JSON blob — old/new values, error messages, metadata), created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
Index on (project_id, created_at DESC) for feed queries
Index on (entity_type, entity_id) for entity-scoped history
New model — backend/src/models/activity.py — Pydantic models: ActivityEvent, ActivityEventCreate, ActivityFeedResponse (items + total + cursor for pagination).
New service — backend/src/services/activity_logger.py — Thin write-through service:
log_event(event_type, entity_type, entity_id, project_id, actor, action, summary, detail=None) — inserts row
Injected as a dependency (like get_db), called from existing API routes and services
Async-safe, fire-and-forget (activity logging should never block the primary operation)
Phase 2 — Backend: Instrument Existing Flows
Pipeline runs — In services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py and api/pipelines.py: call log_event() on run create, status transitions (running → completed/failed/cancelled), and stage completions. Reuse data already in pipeline_runs table — the activity event is a denormalized summary row, not a replacement. Depends on step 3.
Workflow transitions — In orchestrator.py, persist WorkflowTransition data via log_event() instead of (or in addition to) the in-memory _transitions list. Fields: from_status, to_status, triggered_by, success, error_message. Depends on step 3. Parallel with step 4.
Chore triggers — In api/chores.py evaluate_triggers() and trigger_chore(): log each trigger event with chore name, trigger type (cron/manual), result count. Parallel with steps 4–5.
CRUD operations — In api/chores.py, api/agents.py, api/apps.py, api/tools.py: log create/update/delete events with entity name and actor. Keep it lightweight — one log_event() call per endpoint handler. Parallel with steps 4–6.
Webhook events — In api/webhooks.py: log inbound GitHub webhook events (PR opened, issue status changed) with summary. Parallel.
Cleanup operations — In api/cleanup.py: log start/completion with branch/PR counts from existing CleanupAuditLogRow. Parallel.
Phase 3 — Backend: Activity Feed API
New router — backend/src/api/activity.py — Two GET endpoints:
GET /activity?project_id=X&limit=50&cursor=TIMESTAMP&event_type=pipeline_run,chore_trigger — paginated feed, filterable by type, scoped to project
GET /activity/{entity_type}/{entity_id} — history for a specific entity (e.g., all events for pipeline "abc-123")
Register in main.py router. Depends on steps 1–2.
Phase 4 — Frontend: API Layer + Hook
Add activityApi — In frontend/src/services/api.ts:
activityApi.feed(projectId, { limit, cursor, eventTypes? }) → GET /activity
activityApi.entityHistory(entityType, entityId) → GET /activity/{type}/{id}
Depends on step 10.
Add useActivityFeed hook — frontend/src/hooks/useActivityFeed.ts:
useInfiniteQuery with cursor-based pagination (load more on scroll)
Query key: ['activity', projectId, filters]
Stale time: 30s (activity data is append-only, light polling is fine)
Returns { events, fetchNextPage, hasNextPage, isLoading }
Depends on step 11.
Phase 5 — Frontend: Activity Page
New page — frontend/src/pages/ActivityPage.tsx:
Filter bar: event type chips (pipeline, chore, agent, app, tool, webhook), date range
Infinite-scroll timeline: each event as a compact row with icon (by type), summary text, relative timestamp, entity link
Click event → expand inline detail (JSON detail rendered as key-value pairs, or link to entity page)
Empty state when no events
Depends on step 12.
Add route — In frontend/src/App.tsx: add /activity route → ActivityPage. Depends on step 13.
Add nav link — In sidebar/navigation component: add "Activity" link with clock/history icon between existing nav items. Parallel with step 14.
Phase 6 — Frontend: Wire Notification Bell
Implement useNotifications.ts — Replace the empty placeholder:
Query activityApi.feed(projectId, { limit: 20 }) for recent events
Filter to high-signal types: pipeline_run (completed/failed), chore_trigger, agent_execution
Map to existing Notification type: { id, type, title: summary, timestamp, read, source }
Read tracking stays in localStorage (existing pattern)
"View all" link in bell dropdown → navigates to /activity
Depends on step 12. Parallel with Phase 5.
Phase 7 — Frontend: Entity-Scoped History Panels
Pipeline run history — Add pipelinesApi.listRuns(projectId, pipelineId) and pipelinesApi.getRun(projectId, pipelineId, runId) to frontend/src/services/api.ts (backend endpoints already exist at GET /{pipeline_id}/runs). Add a "Run History" tab/panel in the pipeline editor view showing past runs with status, duration, stage breakdown. Parallel with Phase 6.
Entity history sidebar — In detail views for chores, agents, apps: add a collapsible "History" section that calls activityApi.entityHistory(type, id) and shows a mini-timeline. Depends on step 12. Parallel with step 17.
Relevant Files
File	Action
backend/src/migrations/03X_activity_events.sql	New — activity_events table + indexes
backend/src/models/activity.py	New — ActivityEvent, ActivityFeedResponse models
backend/src/services/activity_logger.py	New — log_event() service
backend/src/api/activity.py	New — GET /activity feed + entity history endpoints
backend/src/main.py	Register activity router
backend/src/api/pipelines.py	Add log_event() calls on run transitions
backend/src/api/chores.py	Add log_event() calls on trigger/CRUD
backend/src/api/agents.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD
backend/src/api/apps.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD/start/stop
backend/src/api/tools.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD
backend/src/api/webhooks.py	Add log_event() calls on webhook processing
backend/src/api/cleanup.py	Add log_event() calls on cleanup operations
backend/src/services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py	Persist transitions via log_event()
frontend/src/services/api.ts	Add activityApi + pipelinesApi.listRuns/getRun
frontend/src/hooks/useActivityFeed.ts	New — useInfiniteQuery for activity feed
frontend/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts	Replace placeholder with real activity query
frontend/src/pages/ActivityPage.tsx	New — full activity timeline page
frontend/src/App.tsx	Add /activity route
frontend/src/layout/ (nav component)	Add "Activity" nav link
frontend/src/types/index.ts	Add ActivityEvent type
Verification
Backend: trigger a pipeline run, create/delete a chore, trigger a webhook → query GET /activity?project_id=X → all events appear in chronological order with correct types and summaries
Pagination: insert 100+ events → GET /activity?limit=20 returns 20 with cursor → next page returns next 20
Entity history: GET /activity/pipeline/{id} returns only events for that pipeline
Frontend Activity page: load page → events render in timeline → scroll down → next page loads → filter by type → list narrows
Notification bell: after pipeline completes → bell shows unread badge → click → notification appears with summary → "View all" navigates to /activity
Pipeline run history panel: open pipeline editor → "Run History" tab shows past runs with status badges and durations
Performance: activity_events table with 10K rows → feed query returns in <100ms (verify with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on indexed query)
Run existing test suites to confirm no regressions
Decisions
Single table (activity_events) over per-entity history tables — simpler to query for a unified feed, denormalized summaries avoid JOINs
Cursor-based pagination (timestamp cursor) over offset — better for append-only data, no skipped/duplicated rows on new inserts
Fire-and-forget logging — activity logging failures are silently caught; they must never break the primary operation
Scope included: pipeline runs, stage transitions, workflow transitions, chore triggers, CRUD for all entities, webhooks, cleanup operations
Scope excluded: chat messages (already have their own table/UI), real-time WebSocket events (ephemeral by design), login/session events
Retention: no automatic cleanup initially; add a TTL-based purge (e.g., 90 days) as a follow-up if table grows large
Further Considerations
WebSocket push for new events — The existing connection_manager.broadcast_to_project() could push activity_event messages so the feed updates in real-time without polling. Recommend deferring to a follow-up since 30s stale time is acceptable for v1.
Export/download — An "Export CSV" button on the Activity page would be useful for audit compliance. Low effort to add as a follow-up endpoint.
Retention policy — With aggressive pipeline usage, the table could grow to 100K+ rows over months. A background cleanup job (keep last 90 days or last 10K rows per project) should be planned but doesn't block v1.

---

mentioned_issues.title: Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
mentioned_issues.body:
Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
Destructive actions (delete agent, pipeline, chore, tool) use a confirmation dialog but offer no recovery after confirmation. The standard modern pattern — an "undo toast" with a timed grace period — is missing entirely. The pipeline editor already has an undo/redo stack (usePipelineConfig.ts) but it resets completely on delete, and no other entity has any undo capability.

The fix: replace immediate hard-deletes with a soft-delete + undo toast pattern. During a grace window (~5s), the item is hidden from the UI but not yet deleted server-side. Clicking "Undo" in the toast cancels the pending delete. If the timer expires, the real DELETE fires.

Phase 1 — Generic Undo Toast Infrastructure
Create useUndoableDelete hook — New file frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts. Encapsulates:
Accepts: { onDelete: () => Promise<void>, undoTimeoutMs?: number, entityLabel: string }
On trigger: immediately hides item via optimistic cache removal (from Plan #3's onMutate pattern), then shows sonner toast with action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: cancelDelete } and duration: 5000
Internally: starts a setTimeout that fires the real API delete when the timer expires
Undo handler: clears timeout, restores cache snapshot, shows "Restored" toast
Cleanup: clears pending timeout on unmount
Returns { undoableDelete: (id) => void, pendingIds: Set<string> }
Toast configuration — In frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx, ensure <Toaster /> has closeButton enabled and supports action buttons (sonner does this natively via toast('message', { action: { label, onClick } })). No library change needed — sonner v1+ supports this out of the box.
Phase 2 — Chore Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts, frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx)
Replace confirmation + immediate delete — In ChoreCard.tsx, remove the confirm() dialog for delete. Instead call undoableDelete(choreId) from the new hook. Depends on step 1.
Optimistic removal — useDeleteChore gets onMutate to remove chore from choreKeys.list(projectId) cache instantly (same pattern as Plan #3 step 7), but the actual mutationFn is deferred by the undo hook.
Backend: no changes needed — Chore delete is already a hard delete (DELETE /chores/{project_id}/{chore_id}). The undo window is purely client-side; the API call simply doesn't fire until the grace period ends.
Phase 3 — Pipeline Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts)
Replace confirmation dialog — Currently useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts shows "This action cannot be undone." Replace with undo toast pattern. The pipeline is removed from pipelineKeys.list(projectId) cache immediately, real DELETE fires after grace period. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phase 2.
Preserve undo/redo stacks — The existing pipeline editor undo/redo (undoStackRef, redoStackRef, Ctrl+Z) is scoped to field edits inside the editor. This is orthogonal to delete-undo — keep both. The delete-undo is a toast-based grace period; the editor undo is a state history stack.
Phase 4 — Tool Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts, frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx)
Replace two-step confirm — Tool delete currently does a pre-flight check (confirm=false) to show affected agents, then a confirmation dialog. Change to: show affected agents inline (tooltip/popover on delete button), then fire undoableDelete(toolId). The undo toast provides the safety net instead of the dialog. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–3.
Deferred delete with confirm=true — The real DELETE /tools/{project_id}/{tool_id}?confirm=true fires only after grace period expires.
Phase 5 — Agent Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts, frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx)
Agent delete is already soft — Backend marks agent as pending_deletion and opens a PR. The undo pattern here is simpler: on "Undo", call a restore endpoint (or cancel the PR). If no restore endpoint exists, keep the confirmation dialog for agents but add an undo toast that re-enables the agent before the PR merges. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–4.
Backend: Add agent restore endpoint (optional) — POST /agents/{project_id}/{agent_id}/restore that flips status back from pending_deletion to active and closes the deletion PR. Only needed if we want full undo for agents.
Phase 6 — App Delete (Keep Confirmation — No Undo Toast)
No change — App deletion is intentionally heavyweight (type-to-confirm, multi-asset cleanup, GitHub repo/project deletion). An undo toast is inappropriate here — the blast radius is too large and some operations (repo deletion) are irreversible on GitHub's side. Keep the existing two-step confirmation.
Relevant Files
File	Action
frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts	New — generic undo toast + deferred delete hook
frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx	Verify <Toaster /> supports action buttons (likely no change)
frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx	Replace confirm() → undoableDelete()
frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into useDeleteChore
frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts	Wire undo toast into pipeline delete flow
frontend/src/hooks/useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts	Remove "cannot be undone" confirmation for delete
frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx	Replace two-step confirm → undo toast
frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into tool delete
frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx	Replace confirm → undo toast (if restore endpoint added)
frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts	Wire undo toast for agent delete
backend/src/api/agents.py	(Optional) Add POST /agents/{id}/restore endpoint
frontend/src/hooks/useConfirmation.tsx	No change — still used by app delete and other non-delete confirmations
Verification
Chore delete: click delete → chore disappears instantly → toast with "Undo" button appears → click Undo → chore reappears → no API call made. Let toast expire → chore stays gone → API call fires → onSettled invalidation confirms server state.
Pipeline delete: same flow, verify editor state clears only after grace period, not on undo.
Tool delete: delete tool with agent associations → affected agent names shown in toast body → Undo restores tool and associations.
Unmount safety: navigate away during grace period → pending delete still fires (timeout persists via ref or is cleaned up with explicit cancel-on-unmount policy — decide per entity).
Multiple deletes: delete 3 chores rapidly → 3 independent undo toasts → undo middle one → only that chore restores.
Run Vitest + Playwright to confirm no regressions.
Decisions
Pattern: client-side deferred delete with undo toast (not server-side soft-delete) for chores, pipelines, tools. The API call is simply delayed, not changed.
Grace period: 5 seconds (industry standard — Gmail, Slack, Notion all use 5–10s).
App delete excluded: too destructive for undo toast; keep type-to-confirm.
Agent delete: depends on whether a restore endpoint is added. If not, keep confirmation dialog (agent delete is already soft/reversible via PR).
Unmount behavior: if user navigates away during grace period, fire the delete immediately (don't leave zombie timeouts). This matches Gmail's behavior.
Further Considerations
Agent restore endpoint — Adding POST /agents/{id}/restore is low effort (flip DB status, close PR) but requires backend work. Recommend including it. Without it, agents keep the confirmation dialog.
Keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Z for global undo — The pipeline editor already captures Ctrl+Z. A global Ctrl+Z that undoes the last toast-based delete would be powerful but could conflict. Recommend deferring this to a follow-up.

---

| 6 | In Progress | G2 (parallel) | `copilot-review` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 7 | In Progress | G2 (parallel) | `linter` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |

mentioned_issues.title: Plan: Activity Log / Audit Trail
mentioned_issues.body:
Plan: Activity Log / Audit Trail
The backend already persists pipeline runs (pipeline_runs + pipeline_stage_states tables) and cleanup operations (cleanup_audit_logs table) with GET endpoints, but the frontend has zero UI to view them. Workflow transitions are in-memory only. Chore triggers and agent executions have no history at all. The notification bell (useNotifications.ts) returns an empty array — it's a placeholder.

The fix: add a unified activity events table in the backend, persist all trackable actions into it, expose a paginated API, and build an Activity page + feed component in the frontend.

Phase 1 — Backend: Unified Activity Events Table
New migration — backend/src/migrations/ — Create activity_events table:
id INTEGER PK, event_type TEXT (pipeline_run | pipeline_stage | chore_trigger | chore_crud | agent_crud | agent_execution | cleanup | app_crud | tool_crud | status_change | webhook), entity_type TEXT (pipeline | chore | agent | app | tool | issue), entity_id TEXT, project_id TEXT, actor TEXT (user or "system"), action TEXT (created | updated | deleted | triggered | started | completed | failed | cancelled | moved), summary TEXT (human-readable one-liner), detail TEXT (JSON blob — old/new values, error messages, metadata), created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
Index on (project_id, created_at DESC) for feed queries
Index on (entity_type, entity_id) for entity-scoped history
New model — backend/src/models/activity.py — Pydantic models: ActivityEvent, ActivityEventCreate, ActivityFeedResponse (items + total + cursor for pagination).
New service — backend/src/services/activity_logger.py — Thin write-through service:
log_event(event_type, entity_type, entity_id, project_id, actor, action, summary, detail=None) — inserts row
Injected as a dependency (like get_db), called from existing API routes and services
Async-safe, fire-and-forget (activity logging should never block the primary operation)
Phase 2 — Backend: Instrument Existing Flows
Pipeline runs — In services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py and api/pipelines.py: call log_event() on run create, status transitions (running → completed/failed/cancelled), and stage completions. Reuse data already in pipeline_runs table — the activity event is a denormalized summary row, not a replacement. Depends on step 3.
Workflow transitions — In orchestrator.py, persist WorkflowTransition data via log_event() instead of (or in addition to) the in-memory _transitions list. Fields: from_status, to_status, triggered_by, success, error_message. Depends on step 3. Parallel with step 4.
Chore triggers — In api/chores.py evaluate_triggers() and trigger_chore(): log each trigger event with chore name, trigger type (cron/manual), result count. Parallel with steps 4–5.
CRUD operations — In api/chores.py, api/agents.py, api/apps.py, api/tools.py: log create/update/delete events with entity name and actor. Keep it lightweight — one log_event() call per endpoint handler. Parallel with steps 4–6.
Webhook events — In api/webhooks.py: log inbound GitHub webhook events (PR opened, issue status changed) with summary. Parallel.
Cleanup operations — In api/cleanup.py: log start/completion with branch/PR counts from existing CleanupAuditLogRow. Parallel.
Phase 3 — Backend: Activity Feed API
New router — backend/src/api/activity.py — Two GET endpoints:
GET /activity?project_id=X&limit=50&cursor=TIMESTAMP&event_type=pipeline_run,chore_trigger — paginated feed, filterable by type, scoped to project
GET /activity/{entity_type}/{entity_id} — history for a specific entity (e.g., all events for pipeline "abc-123")
Register in main.py router. Depends on steps 1–2.
Phase 4 — Frontend: API Layer + Hook
Add activityApi — In frontend/src/services/api.ts:
activityApi.feed(projectId, { limit, cursor, eventTypes? }) → GET /activity
activityApi.entityHistory(entityType, entityId) → GET /activity/{type}/{id}
Depends on step 10.
Add useActivityFeed hook — frontend/src/hooks/useActivityFeed.ts:
useInfiniteQuery with cursor-based pagination (load more on scroll)
Query key: ['activity', projectId, filters]
Stale time: 30s (activity data is append-only, light polling is fine)
Returns { events, fetchNextPage, hasNextPage, isLoading }
Depends on step 11.
Phase 5 — Frontend: Activity Page
New page — frontend/src/pages/ActivityPage.tsx:
Filter bar: event type chips (pipeline, chore, agent, app, tool, webhook), date range
Infinite-scroll timeline: each event as a compact row with icon (by type), summary text, relative timestamp, entity link
Click event → expand inline detail (JSON detail rendered as key-value pairs, or link to entity page)
Empty state when no events
Depends on step 12.
Add route — In frontend/src/App.tsx: add /activity route → ActivityPage. Depends on step 13.
Add nav link — In sidebar/navigation component: add "Activity" link with clock/history icon between existing nav items. Parallel with step 14.
Phase 6 — Frontend: Wire Notification Bell
Implement useNotifications.ts — Replace the empty placeholder:
Query activityApi.feed(projectId, { limit: 20 }) for recent events
Filter to high-signal types: pipeline_run (completed/failed), chore_trigger, agent_execution
Map to existing Notification type: { id, type, title: summary, timestamp, read, source }
Read tracking stays in localStorage (existing pattern)
"View all" link in bell dropdown → navigates to /activity
Depends on step 12. Parallel with Phase 5.
Phase 7 — Frontend: Entity-Scoped History Panels
Pipeline run history — Add pipelinesApi.listRuns(projectId, pipelineId) and pipelinesApi.getRun(projectId, pipelineId, runId) to frontend/src/services/api.ts (backend endpoints already exist at GET /{pipeline_id}/runs). Add a "Run History" tab/panel in the pipeline editor view showing past runs with status, duration, stage breakdown. Parallel with Phase 6.
Entity history sidebar — In detail views for chores, agents, apps: add a collapsible "History" section that calls activityApi.entityHistory(type, id) and shows a mini-timeline. Depends on step 12. Parallel with step 17.
Relevant Files
File	Action
backend/src/migrations/03X_activity_events.sql	New — activity_events table + indexes
backend/src/models/activity.py	New — ActivityEvent, ActivityFeedResponse models
backend/src/services/activity_logger.py	New — log_event() service
backend/src/api/activity.py	New — GET /activity feed + entity history endpoints
backend/src/main.py	Register activity router
backend/src/api/pipelines.py	Add log_event() calls on run transitions
backend/src/api/chores.py	Add log_event() calls on trigger/CRUD
backend/src/api/agents.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD
backend/src/api/apps.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD/start/stop
backend/src/api/tools.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD
backend/src/api/webhooks.py	Add log_event() calls on webhook processing
backend/src/api/cleanup.py	Add log_event() calls on cleanup operations
backend/src/services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py	Persist transitions via log_event()
frontend/src/services/api.ts	Add activityApi + pipelinesApi.listRuns/getRun
frontend/src/hooks/useActivityFeed.ts	New — useInfiniteQuery for activity feed
frontend/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts	Replace placeholder with real activity query
frontend/src/pages/ActivityPage.tsx	New — full activity timeline page
frontend/src/App.tsx	Add /activity route
frontend/src/layout/ (nav component)	Add "Activity" nav link
frontend/src/types/index.ts	Add ActivityEvent type
Verification
Backend: trigger a pipeline run, create/delete a chore, trigger a webhook → query GET /activity?project_id=X → all events appear in chronological order with correct types and summaries
Pagination: insert 100+ events → GET /activity?limit=20 returns 20 with cursor → next page returns next 20
Entity history: GET /activity/pipeline/{id} returns only events for that pipeline
Frontend Activity page: load page → events render in timeline → scroll down → next page loads → filter by type → list narrows

mentioned_issues.title: Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
mentioned_issues.body:
Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
Destructive actions (delete agent, pipeline, chore, tool) use a confirmation dialog but offer no recovery after confirmation. The standard modern pattern — an "undo toast" with a timed grace period — is missing entirely. The pipeline editor already has an undo/redo stack (usePipelineConfig.ts) but it resets completely on delete, and no other entity has any undo capability.

The fix: replace immediate hard-deletes with a soft-delete + undo toast pattern. During a grace window (~5s), the item is hidden from the UI but not yet deleted server-side. Clicking "Undo" in the toast cancels the pending delete. If the timer expires, the real DELETE fires.

Phase 1 — Generic Undo Toast Infrastructure
Create useUndoableDelete hook — New file frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts. Encapsulates:
Accepts: { onDelete: () => Promise<void>, undoTimeoutMs?: number, entityLabel: string }
On trigger: immediately hides item via optimistic cache removal (from Plan #3's onMutate pattern), then shows sonner toast with action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: cancelDelete } and duration: 5000
Internally: starts a setTimeout that fires the real API delete when the timer expires
Undo handler: clears timeout, restores cache snapshot, shows "Restored" toast
Cleanup: clears pending timeout on unmount
Returns { undoableDelete: (id) => void, pendingIds: Set<string> }
Toast configuration — In frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx, ensure <Toaster /> has closeButton enabled and supports action buttons (sonner does this natively via toast('message', { action: { label, onClick } })). No library change needed — sonner v1+ supports this out of the box.
Phase 2 — Chore Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts, frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx)
Replace confirmation + immediate delete — In ChoreCard.tsx, remove the confirm() dialog for delete. Instead call undoableDelete(choreId) from the new hook. Depends on step 1.
Optimistic removal — useDeleteChore gets onMutate to remove chore from choreKeys.list(projectId) cache instantly (same pattern as Plan #3 step 7), but the actual mutationFn is deferred by the undo hook.
Backend: no changes needed — Chore delete is already a hard delete (DELETE /chores/{project_id}/{chore_id}). The undo window is purely client-side; the API call simply doesn't fire until the grace period ends.
Phase 3 — Pipeline Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts)
Replace confirmation dialog — Currently useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts shows "This action cannot be undone." Replace with undo toast pattern. The pipeline is removed from pipelineKeys.list(projectId) cache immediately, real DELETE fires after grace period. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phase 2.
Preserve undo/redo stacks — The existing pipeline editor undo/redo (undoStackRef, redoStackRef, Ctrl+Z) is scoped to field edits inside the editor. This is orthogonal to delete-undo — keep both. The delete-undo is a toast-based grace period; the editor undo is a state history stack.
Phase 4 — Tool Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts, frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx)
Replace two-step confirm — Tool delete currently does a pre-flight check (confirm=false) to show affected agents, then a confirmation dialog. Change to: show affected agents inline (tooltip/popover on delete button), then fire undoableDelete(toolId). The undo toast provides the safety net instead of the dialog. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–3.
Deferred delete with confirm=true — The real DELETE /tools/{project_id}/{tool_id}?confirm=true fires only after grace period expires.
Phase 5 — Agent Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts, frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx)
Agent delete is already soft — Backend marks agent as pending_deletion and opens a PR. The undo pattern here is simpler: on "Undo", call a restore endpoint (or cancel the PR). If no restore endpoint exists, keep the confirmation dialog for agents but add an undo toast that re-enables the agent before the PR merges. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–4.
Backend: Add agent restore endpoint (optional) — POST /agents/{project_id}/{agent_id}/restore that flips status back from pending_deletion to active and closes the deletion PR. Only needed if we want full undo for agents.
Phase 6 — App Delete (Keep Confirmation — No Undo Toast)
No change — App deletion is intentionally heavyweight (type-to-confirm, multi-asset cleanup, GitHub repo/project deletion). An undo toast is inappropriate here — the blast radius is too large and some operations (repo deletion) are irreversible on GitHub's side. Keep the existing two-step confirmation.
Relevant Files
File	Action
frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts	New — generic undo toast + deferred delete hook
frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx	Verify <Toaster /> supports action buttons (likely no change)
frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx	Replace confirm() → undoableDelete()
frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into useDeleteChore
frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts	Wire undo toast into pipeline delete flow
frontend/src/hooks/useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts	Remove "cannot be undone" confirmation for delete
frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx	Replace two-step confirm → undo toast
frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into tool delete
frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx	Replace confirm → undo toast (if restore endpoint added)
frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts	Wire undo toast for agent delete
backend/src/api/agents.py	(Optional) Add POST /agents/{id}/restore endpoint
frontend/src/hooks/useConfirmation.tsx	No change — still used by app delete and other non-delete confirmations
Verification
Chore delete: click delete → chore disappears instantly → toast with "Undo" button appears → click Undo → chore reappears → no API call made. Let toast expire → chore stays gone → API call fires → onSettled invalidation confirms server state.
Pipeline delete: same flow, verify editor state clears only after grace period, not on undo.
Tool delete: delete tool with agent associations → affected agent names shown in toast body → Undo restores tool and associations.
Unmount safety: navigate away during grace period → pending delete still fires (timeout persists via ref or is cleaned up with explicit cancel-on-unmount policy — decide per entity).
Multiple deletes: delete 3 chores rapidly → 3 independent undo toasts → undo middle one → only that chore restores.
Run Vitest + Playwright to confirm no regressions.
Decisions
Pattern: client-side deferred delete with undo toast (not server-side soft-delete) for chores, pipelines, tools. The API call is simply delayed, not changed.
Grace period: 5 seconds (industry standard — Gmail, Slack, Notion all use 5–10s).
App delete excluded: too destructive for undo toast; keep type-to-confirm.
Agent delete: depends on whether a restore endpoint is added. If not, keep confirmation dialog (agent delete is already soft/reversible via PR).
Unmount behavior: if user navigates away during grace period, fire the delete immediately (don't leave zombie timeouts). This matches Gmail's behavior.
Further Considerations
Agent restore endpoint — Adding POST /agents/{id}/restore is low effort (flip DB status, close PR) but requires backend work. Recommend including it. Without it, agents keep the confirmation dialog.
Keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Z for global undo — The pipeline editor already captures Ctrl+Z. A global Ctrl+Z that undoes the last toast-based delete would be powerful but could conflict. Recommend deferring this to a follow-up.

| 6 | In Progress | G2 (parallel) | `copilot-review` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 7 | In Progress | G2 (parallel) | `linter` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |

mentioned_issues.title: Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
mentioned_issues.body:
Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
Destructive actions (delete agent, pipeline, chore, tool) use a confirmation dialog but offer no recovery after confirmation. The standard modern pattern — an "undo toast" with a timed grace period — is missing entirely. The pipeline editor already has an undo/redo stack (usePipelineConfig.ts) but it resets completely on delete, and no other entity has any undo capability.

The fix: replace immediate hard-deletes with a soft-delete + undo toast pattern. During a grace window (~5s), the item is hidden from the UI but not yet deleted server-side. Clicking "Undo" in the toast cancels the pending delete. If the timer expires, the real DELETE fires.

Phase 1 — Generic Undo Toast Infrastructure
Create useUndoableDelete hook — New file frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts. Encapsulates:
Accepts: { onDelete: () => Promise<void>, undoTimeoutMs?: number, entityLabel: string }
On trigger: immediately hides item via optimistic cache removal (from Plan #3's onMutate pattern), then shows sonner toast with action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: cancelDelete } and duration: 5000
Internally: starts a setTimeout that fires the real API delete when the timer expires
Undo handler: clears timeout, restores cache snapshot, shows "Restored" toast
Cleanup: clears pending timeout on unmount
Returns { undoableDelete: (id) => void, pendingIds: Set<string> }
Toast configuration — In frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx, ensure <Toaster /> has closeButton enabled and supports action buttons (sonner does this natively via toast('message', { action: { label, onClick } })). No library change needed — sonner v1+ supports this out of the box.
Phase 2 — Chore Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts, frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx)
Replace confirmation + immediate delete — In ChoreCard.tsx, remove the confirm() dialog for delete. Instead call undoableDelete(choreId) from the new hook. Depends on step 1.
Optimistic removal — useDeleteChore gets onMutate to remove chore from choreKeys.list(projectId) cache instantly (same pattern as Plan #3 step 7), but the actual mutationFn is deferred by the undo hook.
Backend: no changes needed — Chore delete is already a hard delete (DELETE /chores/{project_id}/{chore_id}). The undo window is purely client-side; the API call simply doesn't fire until the grace period ends.
Phase 3 — Pipeline Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts)
Replace confirmation dialog — Currently useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts shows "This action cannot be undone." Replace with undo toast pattern. The pipeline is removed from pipelineKeys.list(projectId) cache immediately, real DELETE fires after grace period. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phase 2.
Preserve undo/redo stacks — The existing pipeline editor undo/redo (undoStackRef, redoStackRef, Ctrl+Z) is scoped to field edits inside the editor. This is orthogonal to delete-undo — keep both. The delete-undo is a toast-based grace period; the editor undo is a state history stack.
Phase 4 — Tool Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts, frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx)
Replace two-step confirm — Tool delete currently does a pre-flight check (confirm=false) to show affected agents, then a confirmation dialog. Change to: show affected agents inline (tooltip/popover on delete button), then fire undoableDelete(toolId). The undo toast provides the safety net instead of the dialog. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–3.
Deferred delete with confirm=true — The real DELETE /tools/{project_id}/{tool_id}?confirm=true fires only after grace period expires.
Phase 5 — Agent Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts, frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx)
Agent delete is already soft — Backend marks agent as pending_deletion and opens a PR. The undo pattern here is simpler: on "Undo", call a restore endpoint (or cancel the PR). If no restore endpoint exists, keep the confirmation dialog for agents but add an undo toast that re-enables the agent before the PR merges. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–4.
Backend: Add agent restore endpoint (optional) — POST /agents/{project_id}/{agent_id}/restore that flips status back from pending_deletion to active and closes the deletion PR. Only needed if we want full undo for agents.
Phase 6 — App Delete (Keep Confirmation — No Undo Toast)
No change — App deletion is intentionally heavyweight (type-to-confirm, multi-asset cleanup, GitHub repo/project deletion). An undo toast is inappropriate here — the blast radius is too large and some operations (repo deletion) are irreversible on GitHub's side. Keep the existing two-step confirmation.
Relevant Files
File	Action
frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts	New — generic undo toast + deferred delete hook
frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx	Verify <Toaster /> supports action buttons (likely no change)
frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx	Replace confirm() → undoableDelete()
frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into useDeleteChore
frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts	Wire undo toast into pipeline delete flow
frontend/src/hooks/useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts	Remove "cannot be undone" confirmation for delete
frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx	Replace two-step confirm → undo toast
frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into tool delete
frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx	Replace confirm → undo toast (if restore endpoint added)
frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts	Wire undo toast for agent delete
backend/src/api/agents.py	(Optional) Add POST /agents/{id}/restore endpoint
frontend/src/hooks/useConfirmation.tsx	No change — still used by app delete and other non-delete confirmations
Verification
Chore delete: click delete → chore disappears instantly → toast with "Undo" button appears → click Undo → chore reappears → no API call made. Let toast expire → chore stays gone → API call fires → onSettled invalidation confirms server state.
Pipeline delete: same flow, verify editor state clears only after grace period, not on undo.
Tool delete: delete tool with agent associations → affected agent names shown in toast body → Undo restores tool and associations.
Unmount safety: navigate away during grace period → pending delete still fires (timeout persists via ref or is cleaned up with explicit cancel-on-unmount policy — decide per entity).
Multiple deletes: delete 3 chores rapidly → 3 independent undo toasts → undo middle one → only that chore restores.
Run Vitest + Playwright to confirm no regressions.
Decisions
Pattern: client-side deferred delete with undo toast (not server-side soft-delete) for chores, pipelines, tools. The API call is simply delayed, not changed.
Grace period: 5 seconds (industry standard — Gmail, Slack, Notion all use 5–10s).
App delete excluded: too destructive for undo toast; keep type-to-confirm.
Agent delete: depends on whether a restore endpoint is added. If not, keep confirmation dialog (agent delete is already soft/reversible via PR).
Unmount behavior: if user navigates away during grace period, fire the delete immediately (don't leave zombie timeouts). This matches Gmail's behavior.
Further Considerations
Agent restore endpoint — Adding POST /agents/{id}/restore is low effort (flip DB status, close PR) but requires backend work. Recommend including it. Without it, agents keep the confirmation dialog.
Keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Z for global undo — The pipeline editor already captures Ctrl+Z. A global Ctrl+Z that undoes the last toast-based delete would be powerful but could conflict. Recommend deferring this to a follow-up.

mentioned_issues.title: [speckit.analyze] Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
mentioned_issues.body:
> **Parent Issue:** #4791 — Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.analyze`

Complete the work assigned to the `speckit.analyze` agent.

---

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
Destructive actions (delete agent, pipeline, chore, tool) use a confirmation dialog but offer no recovery after confirmation. The standard modern pattern — an "undo toast" with a timed grace period — is missing entirely. The pipeline editor already has an undo/redo stack (usePipelineConfig.ts) but it resets completely on delete, and no other entity has any undo capability.

The fix: replace immediate hard-deletes with a soft-delete + undo toast pattern. During a grace window (~5s), the item is hidden from the UI but not yet deleted server-side. Clicking "Undo" in the toast cancels the pending delete. If the timer expires, the real DELETE fires.

Phase 1 — Generic Undo Toast Infrastructure
Create useUndoableDelete hook — New file frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts. Encapsulates:
Accepts: { onDelete: () => Promise<void>, undoTimeoutMs?: number, entityLabel: string }
On trigger: immediately hides item via optimistic cache removal (from Plan #3's onMutate pattern), then shows sonner toast with action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: cancelDelete } and duration: 5000
Internally: starts a setTimeout that fires the real API delete when the timer expires
Undo handler: clears timeout, restores cache snapshot, shows "Restored" toast
Cleanup: clears pending timeout on unmount
Returns { undoableDelete: (id) => void, pendingIds: Set<string> }
Toast configuration — In frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx, ensure <Toaster /> has closeButton enabled and supports action buttons (sonner does this natively via toast('message', { action: { label, onClick } })). No library change needed — sonner v1+ supports this out of the box.
Phase 2 — Chore Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts, frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx)
Replace confirmation + immediate delete — In ChoreCard.tsx, remove the confirm() dialog for delete. Instead call undoableDelete(choreId) from the new hook. Depends on step 1.
Optimistic removal — useDeleteChore gets onMutate to remove chore from choreKeys.list(projectId) cache instantly (same pattern as Plan #3 step 7), but the actual mutationFn is deferred by the undo hook.
Backend: no changes needed — Chore delete is already a hard delete (DELETE /chores/{project_id}/{chore_id}). The undo window is purely client-side; the API call simply doesn't fire until the grace period ends.
Phase 3 — Pipeline Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts)
Replace confirmation dialog — Currently useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts shows "This action cannot be undone." Replace with undo toast pattern. The pipeline is removed from pipelineKeys.list(projectId) cache immediately, real DELETE fires after grace period. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phase 2.
Preserve undo/redo stacks — The existing pipeline editor undo/redo (undoStackRef, redoStackRef, Ctrl+Z) is scoped to field edits inside the editor. This is orthogonal to delete-undo — keep both. The delete-undo is a toast-based grace period; the editor undo is a state history stack.
Phase 4 — Tool Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts, frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx)
Replace two-step confirm — Tool delete currently does a pre-flight check (confirm=false) to show affected agents, then a confirmation dialog. Change to: show affected agents inline (tooltip/popover on delete button), then fire undoableDelete(toolId). The undo toast provides the safety net instead of the dialog. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–3.
Deferred delete with confirm=true — The real DELETE /tools/{project_id}/{tool_id}?confirm=true fires only after grace period expires.
Phase 5 — Agent Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts, frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx)
Agent delete is already soft — Backend marks agent as pending_deletion and opens a PR. The undo pattern here is simpler: on "Undo", call a restore endpoint (or cancel the PR). If no restore endpoint exists, keep the confirmation dialog for agents but add an undo toast that re-enables the agent before the PR merges. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–4.
Backend: Add agent restore endpoint (optional) — POST /agents/{project_id}/{agent_id}/restore that flips status back from pending_deletion to active and closes the deletion PR. Only needed if we want full undo for agents.
Phase 6 — App Delete (Keep Confirmation — No Undo Toast)
No change — App deletion is intentionally heavyweight (type-to-confirm, multi-asset cleanup, GitHub repo/project deletion). An undo toast is inappropriate here — the blast radius is too large and some operations (repo deletion) are irreversible on GitHub's side. Keep the existing two-step confirmation.
Relevant Files
File	Action
frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts	New — generic undo toast + deferred delete hook
frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx	Verify <Toaster /> supports action buttons (likely no change)
frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx	Replace confirm() → undoableDelete()
frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into useDeleteChore
frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts	Wire undo toast into pipeline delete flow
frontend/src/hooks/useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts	Remove "cannot be undone" confirmation for delete
frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx	Replace two-step confirm → undo toast
frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into tool delete
frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx	Replace confirm → undo toast (if restore endpoint added)
frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts	Wire undo toast for agent delete
backend/src/api/agents.py	(Optional) Add POST /agents/{id}/restore endpoint
frontend/src/hooks/useConfirmation.tsx	No change — still used by app delete and other non-delete confirmations
Verification
Chore delete: click delete → chore disappears instantly → toast with "Undo" button appears → click Undo → chore reappears → no API call made. Let toast expire → chore stays gone → API call fires → onSettled invalidation confirms server state.
Pipeline delete: same flow, verify editor state clears only after grace period, not on undo.
Tool delete: delete tool with agent associations → affected agent names shown in toast body → Undo restores tool and associations.
Unmount safety: navigate away during grace period → pending delete still fires (timeout persists via ref or is cleaned up with explicit cancel-on-unmount policy — decide per entity).
Multiple deletes: delete 3 chores rapidly → 3 independent undo toasts → undo middle one → only that chore restores.
Run Vitest + Playwright to confirm no regressions.
Decisions
Pattern: client-side deferred delete with undo toast (not server-side soft-delete) for chores, pipelines, tools. The API call is simply delayed, not changed.
Grace period: 5 seconds (industry standard — Gmail, Slack, Notion all use 5–10s).
App delete excluded: too destructive for undo toast; keep type-to-confirm.
Agent delete: depends on whether a restore endpoint is added. If not, keep confirmation dialog (agent delete is already soft/reversible via PR).
Unmount behavior: if user navigates away during grace period, fire the delete immediately (don't leave zombie timeouts). This matches Gmail's behavior.
Further Considerations
Agent restore endpoint — Adding POST /agents/{id}/restore is low effort (flip DB status, close PR) but requires backend work. Recommend including it. Without it, agents keep the confirmation dialog.
Keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Z for global undo — The pipeline editor already captures Ctrl+Z. A global Ctrl+Z that undoes the last toast-based delete would be powerful but could conflict. Recommend deferring this to a follow-up.

---

mentioned_issues.title: Plan: Activity Log / Audit Trail
mentioned_issues.body:
Plan: Activity Log / Audit Trail
The backend already persists pipeline runs (pipeline_runs + pipeline_stage_states tables) and cleanup operations (cleanup_audit_logs table) with GET endpoints, but the frontend has zero UI to view them. Workflow transitions are in-memory only. Chore triggers and agent executions have no history at all. The notification bell (useNotifications.ts) returns an empty array — it's a placeholder.

The fix: add a unified activity events table in the backend, persist all trackable actions into it, expose a paginated API, and build an Activity page + feed component in the frontend.

Phase 1 — Backend: Unified Activity Events Table
New migration — backend/src/migrations/ — Create activity_events table:
id INTEGER PK, event_type TEXT (pipeline_run | pipeline_stage | chore_trigger | chore_crud | agent_crud | agent_execution | cleanup | app_crud | tool_crud | status_change | webhook), entity_type TEXT (pipeline | chore | agent | app | tool | issue), entity_id TEXT, project_id TEXT, actor TEXT (user or "system"), action TEXT (created | updated | deleted | triggered | started | completed | failed | cancelled | moved), summary TEXT (human-readable one-liner), detail TEXT (JSON blob — old/new values, error messages, metadata), created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
Index on (project_id, created_at DESC) for feed queries
Index on (entity_type, entity_id) for entity-scoped history
New model — backend/src/models/activity.py — Pydantic models: ActivityEvent, ActivityEventCreate, ActivityFeedResponse (items + total + cursor for pagination).
New service — backend/src/services/activity_logger.py — Thin write-through service:
log_event(event_type, entity_type, entity_id, project_id, actor, action, summary, detail=None) — inserts row
Injected as a dependency (like get_db), called from existing API routes and services
Async-safe, fire-and-forget (activity logging should never block the primary operation)
Phase 2 — Backend: Instrument Existing Flows
Pipeline runs — In services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py and api/pipelines.py: call log_event() on run create, status transitions (running → completed/failed/cancelled), and stage completions. Reuse data already in pipeline_runs table — the activity event is a denormalized summary row, not a replacement. Depends on step 3.
Workflow transitions — In orchestrator.py, persist WorkflowTransition data via log_event() instead of (or in addition to) the in-memory _transitions list. Fields: from_status, to_status, triggered_by, success, error_message. Depends on step 3. Parallel with step 4.
Chore triggers — In api/chores.py evaluate_triggers() and trigger_chore(): log each trigger event with chore name, trigger type (cron/manual), result count. Parallel with steps 4–5.
CRUD operations — In api/chores.py, api/agents.py, api/apps.py, api/tools.py: log create/update/delete events with entity name and actor. Keep it lightweight — one log_event() call per endpoint handler. Parallel with steps 4–6.
Webhook events — In api/webhooks.py: log inbound GitHub webhook events (PR opened, issue status changed) with summary. Parallel.
Cleanup operations — In api/cleanup.py: log start/completion with branch/PR counts from existing CleanupAuditLogRow. Parallel.
Phase 3 — Backend: Activity Feed API
New router — backend/src/api/activity.py — Two GET endpoints:
GET /activity?project_id=X&limit=50&cursor=TIMESTAMP&event_type=pipeline_run,chore_trigger — paginated feed, filterable by type, scoped to project
GET /activity/{entity_type}/{entity_id} — history for a specific entity (e.g., all events for pipeline "abc-123")
Register in main.py router. Depends on steps 1–2.
Phase 4 — Frontend: API Layer + Hook
Add activityApi — In frontend/src/services/api.ts:
activityApi.feed(projectId, { limit, cursor, eventTypes? }) → GET /activity
activityApi.entityHistory(entityType, entityId) → GET /activity/{type}/{id}
Depends on step 10.
Add useActivityFeed hook — frontend/src/hooks/useActivityFeed.ts:
useInfiniteQuery with cursor-based pagination (load more on scroll)
Query key: ['activity', projectId, filters]
Stale time: 30s (activity data is append-only, light polling is fine)
Returns { events, fetchNextPage, hasNextPage, isLoading }
Depends on step 11.
Phase 5 — Frontend: Activity Page
New page — frontend/src/pages/ActivityPage.tsx:
Filter bar: event type chips (pipeline, chore, agent, app, tool, webhook), date range
Infinite-scroll timeline: each event as a compact row with icon (by type), summary text, relative timestamp, entity link
Click event → expand inline detail (JSON detail rendered as key-value pairs, or link to entity page)
Empty state when no events
Depends on step 12.
Add route — In frontend/src/App.tsx: add /activity route → ActivityPage. Depends on step 13.
Add nav link — In sidebar/navigation component: add "Activity" link with clock/history icon between existing nav items. Parallel with step 14.
Phase 6 — Frontend: Wire Notification Bell
Implement useNotifications.ts — Replace the empty placeholder:
Query activityApi.feed(projectId, { limit: 20 }) for recent events
Filter to high-signal types: pipeline_run (completed/failed), chore_trigger, agent_execution
Map to existing Notification type: { id, type, title: summary, timestamp, read, source }
Read tracking stays in localStorage (existing pattern)
"View all" link in bell dropdown → navigates to /activity
Depends on step 12. Parallel with Phase 5.
Phase 7 — Frontend: Entity-Scoped History Panels
Pipeline run history — Add pipelinesApi.listRuns(projectId, pipelineId) and pipelinesApi.getRun(projectId, pipelineId, runId) to frontend/src/services/api.ts (backend endpoints already exist at GET /{pipeline_id}/runs). Add a "Run History" tab/panel in the pipeline editor view showing past runs with status, duration, stage breakdown. Parallel with Phase 6.
Entity history sidebar — In detail views for chores, agents, apps: add a collapsible "History" section that calls activityApi.entityHistory(type, id) and shows a mini-timeline. Depends on step 12. Parallel with step 17.
Relevant Files
File	Action
backend/src/migrations/03X_activity_events.sql	New — activity_events table + indexes
backend/src/models/activity.py	New — ActivityEvent, ActivityFeedResponse models
backend/src/services/activity_logger.py	New — log_event() service
backend/src/api/activity.py	New — GET /activity feed + entity history endpoints
backend/src/main.py	Register activity router
backend/src/api/pipelines.py	Add log_event() calls on run transitions
backend/src/api/chores.py	Add log_event() calls on trigger/CRUD
backend/src/api/agents.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD
backend/src/api/apps.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD/start/stop
backend/src/api/tools.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD
backend/src/api/webhooks.py	Add log_event() calls on webhook processing
backend/src/api/cleanup.py	Add log_event() calls on cleanup operations
backend/src/services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py	Persist transitions via log_event()
frontend/src/services/api.ts	Add activityApi + pipelinesApi.listRuns/getRun
frontend/src/hooks/useActivityFeed.ts	New — useInfiniteQuery for activity feed
frontend/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts	Replace placeholder with real activity query
frontend/src/pages/ActivityPage.tsx	New — full activity timeline page
frontend/src/App.tsx	Add /activity route
frontend/src/layout/ (nav component)	Add "Activity" nav link
frontend/src/types/index.ts	Add ActivityEvent type
Verification
Backend: trigger a pipeline run, create/delete a chore, trigger a webhook → query GET /activity?project_id=X → all events appear in chronological order with correct types and summaries
Pagination: insert 100+ events → GET /activity?limit=20 returns 20 with cursor → next page returns next 20
Entity history: GET /activity/pipeline/{id} returns only events for that pipeline
Frontend Activity page: load page → events render in timeline → scroll down → next page loads → filter by type → list narrows
Notification bell: after pipeline completes → bell shows unread badge → click → notification appears with summary → "View all" navigates to /activity
Pipeline run history panel: open pipeline editor → "Run History" tab shows past runs with status badges and durations
Performance: activity_events table with 10K rows → feed query returns in <100ms (verify with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on indexed query)
Run existing test suites to confirm no regressions
Decisions
Single table (activity_events) over per-entity history tables — simpler to query for a unified feed, denormalized summaries avoid JOINs
Cursor-based pagination (timestamp cursor) over offset — better for append-only data, no skipped/duplicated rows on new inserts
Fire-and-forget logging — activity logging failures are silently caught; they must never break the primary operation
Scope included: pipeline runs, stage transitions, workflow transitions, chore triggers, CRUD for all entities, webhooks, cleanup operations
Scope excluded: chat messages (already have their own table/UI), real-time WebSocket events (ephemeral by design), login/session events
Retention: no automatic cleanup initially; add a TTL-based purge (e.g., 90 days) as a follow-up if table grows large
Further Considerations
WebSocket push for new events — The existing connection_manager.broadcast_to_project() could push activity_event messages so the feed updates in real-time without polling. Recommend deferring to a follow-up since 30s stale time is acceptable for v1.
Export/download — An "Export CSV" button on the Activity page would be useful for audit compliance. Low effort to add as a follow-up endpoint.
Retention policy — With aggressive pipeline usage, the table could grow to 100K+ rows over months. A background cleanup job (keep last 90 days or last 10K rows per project) should be planned but doesn't block v1.

---

mentioned_issues.title: Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
mentioned_issues.body:
Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
Destructive actions (delete agent, pipeline, chore, tool) use a confirmation dialog but offer no recovery after confirmation. The standard modern pattern — an "undo toast" with a timed grace period — is missing entirely. The pipeline editor already has an undo/redo stack (usePipelineConfig.ts) but it resets completely on delete, and no other entity has any undo capability.

The fix: replace immediate hard-deletes with a soft-delete + undo toast pattern. During a grace window (~5s), the item is hidden from the UI but not yet deleted server-side. Clicking "Undo" in the toast cancels the pending delete. If the timer expires, the real DELETE fires.

Phase 1 — Generic Undo Toast Infrastructure
Create useUndoableDelete hook — New file frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts. Encapsulates:
Accepts: { onDelete: () => Promise<void>, undoTimeoutMs?: number, entityLabel: string }
On trigger: immediately hides item via optimistic cache removal (from Plan #3's onMutate pattern), then shows sonner toast with action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: cancelDelete } and duration: 5000
Internally: starts a setTimeout that fires the real API delete when the timer expires
Undo handler: clears timeout, restores cache snapshot, shows "Restored" toast
Cleanup: clears pending timeout on unmount
Returns { undoableDelete: (id) => void, pendingIds: Set<string> }
Toast configuration — In frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx, ensure <Toaster /> has closeButton enabled and supports action buttons (sonner does this natively via toast('message', { action: { label, onClick } })). No library change needed — sonner v1+ supports this out of the box.
Phase 2 — Chore Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts, frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx)
Replace confirmation + immediate delete — In ChoreCard.tsx, remove the confirm() dialog for delete. Instead call undoableDelete(choreId) from the new hook. Depends on step 1.
Optimistic removal — useDeleteChore gets onMutate to remove chore from choreKeys.list(projectId) cache instantly (same pattern as Plan #3 step 7), but the actual mutationFn is deferred by the undo hook.
Backend: no changes needed — Chore delete is already a hard delete (DELETE /chores/{project_id}/{chore_id}). The undo window is purely client-side; the API call simply doesn't fire until the grace period ends.
Phase 3 — Pipeline Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts)
Replace confirmation dialog — Currently useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts shows "This action cannot be undone." Replace with undo toast pattern. The pipeline is removed from pipelineKeys.list(projectId) cache immediately, real DELETE fires after grace period. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phase 2.
Preserve undo/redo stacks — The existing pipeline editor undo/redo (undoStackRef, redoStackRef, Ctrl+Z) is scoped to field edits inside the editor. This is orthogonal to delete-undo — keep both. The delete-undo is a toast-based grace period; the editor undo is a state history stack.
Phase 4 — Tool Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts, frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx)
Replace two-step confirm — Tool delete currently does a pre-flight check (confirm=false) to show affected agents, then a confirmation dialog. Change to: show affected agents inline (tooltip/popover on delete button), then fire undoableDelete(toolId). The undo toast provides the safety net instead of the dialog. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–3.
Deferred delete with confirm=true — The real DELETE /tools/{project_id}/{tool_id}?confirm=true fires only after grace period expires.
Phase 5 — Agent Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts, frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx)
Agent delete is already soft — Backend marks agent as pending_deletion and opens a PR. The undo pattern here is simpler: on "Undo", call a restore endpoint (or cancel the PR). If no restore endpoint exists, keep the confirmation dialog for agents but add an undo toast that re-enables the agent before the PR merges. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–4.
Backend: Add agent restore endpoint (optional) — POST /agents/{project_id}/{agent_id}/restore that flips status back from pending_deletion to active and closes the deletion PR. Only needed if we want full undo for agents.
Phase 6 — App Delete (Keep Confirmation — No Undo Toast)
No change — App deletion is intentionally heavyweight (type-to-confirm, multi-asset cleanup, GitHub repo/project deletion). An undo toast is inappropriate here — the blast radius is too large and some operations (repo deletion) are irreversible on GitHub's side. Keep the existing two-step confirmation.
Relevant Files
File	Action
frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts	New — generic undo toast + deferred delete hook
frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx	Verify <Toaster /> supports action buttons (likely no change)
frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx	Replace confirm() → undoableDelete()
frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into useDeleteChore
frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts	Wire undo toast into pipeline delete flow
frontend/src/hooks/useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts	Remove "cannot be undone" confirmation for delete
frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx	Replace two-step confirm → undo toast
frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into tool delete
frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx	Replace confirm → undo toast (if restore endpoint added)
frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts	Wire undo toast for agent delete
backend/src/api/agents.py	(Optional) Add POST /agents/{id}/restore endpoint
frontend/src/hooks/useConfirmation.tsx	No change — still used by app delete and other non-delete confirmations
Verification
Chore delete: click delete → chore disappears instantly → toast with "Undo" button appears → click Undo → chore reappears → no API call made. Let toast expire → chore stays gone → API call fires → onSettled invalidation confirms server state.
Pipeline delete: same flow, verify editor state clears only after grace period, not on undo.
Tool delete: delete tool with agent associations → affected agent names shown in toast body → Undo restores tool and associations.
Unmount safety: navigate away during grace period → pending delete still fires (timeout persists via ref or is cleaned up with explicit cancel-on-unmount policy — decide per entity).
Multiple deletes: delete 3 chores rapidly → 3 independent undo toasts → undo middle one → only that chore restores.
Run Vitest + Playwright to confirm no regressions.
Decisions
Pattern: client-side deferred delete with undo toast (not server-side soft-delete) for chores, pipelines, tools. The API call is simply delayed, not changed.
Grace period: 5 seconds (industry standard — Gmail, Slack, Notion all use 5–10s).
App delete excluded: too destructive for undo toast; keep type-to-confirm.
Agent delete: depends on whether a restore endpoint is added. If not, keep confirmation dialog (agent delete is already soft/reversible via PR).
Unmount behavior: if user navigates away during grace period, fire the delete immediately (don't leave zombie timeouts). This matches Gmail's behavior.
Further Considerations
Agent restore endpoint — Adding POST /agents/{id}/restore is low effort (flip DB status, close PR) but requires backend work. Recommend including it. Without it, agents keep the confirmation dialog.
Keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Z for global undo — The pipeline editor already captures Ctrl+Z. A global Ctrl+Z that undoes the last toast-based delete would be powerful but could conflict. Recommend deferring this to a follow-up.
