mentioned_issues.title: Plan: Activity Log / Audit Trail
mentioned_issues.body:
Plan: Activity Log / Audit Trail
The backend already persists pipeline runs (pipeline_runs + pipeline_stage_states tables) and cleanup operations (cleanup_audit_logs table) with GET endpoints, but the frontend has zero UI to view them. Workflow transitions are in-memory only. Chore triggers and agent executions have no history at all. The notification bell (useNotifications.ts) returns an empty array — it's a placeholder.

The fix: add a unified activity events table in the backend, persist all trackable actions into it, expose a paginated API, and build an Activity page + feed component in the frontend.

Phase 1 — Backend: Unified Activity Events Table
New migration — backend/src/migrations/ — Create activity_events table:
id INTEGER PK, event_type TEXT (pipeline_run | pipeline_stage | chore_trigger | chore_crud | agent_crud | agent_execution | cleanup | app_crud | tool_crud | status_change | webhook), entity_type TEXT (pipeline | chore | agent | app | tool | issue), entity_id TEXT, project_id TEXT, actor TEXT (user or "system"), action TEXT (created | updated | deleted | triggered | started | completed | failed | cancelled | moved), summary TEXT (human-readable one-liner), detail TEXT (JSON blob — old/new values, error messages, metadata), created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
Index on (project_id, created_at DESC) for feed queries
Index on (entity_type, entity_id) for entity-scoped history
New model — backend/src/models/activity.py — Pydantic models: ActivityEvent, ActivityEventCreate, ActivityFeedResponse (items + total + cursor for pagination).
New service — backend/src/services/activity_logger.py — Thin write-through service:
log_event(event_type, entity_type, entity_id, project_id, actor, action, summary, detail=None) — inserts row
Injected as a dependency (like get_db), called from existing API routes and services
Async-safe, fire-and-forget (activity logging should never block the primary operation)
Phase 2 — Backend: Instrument Existing Flows
Pipeline runs — In services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py and api/pipelines.py: call log_event() on run create, status transitions (running → completed/failed/cancelled), and stage completions. Reuse data already in pipeline_runs table — the activity event is a denormalized summary row, not a replacement. Depends on step 3.
Workflow transitions — In orchestrator.py, persist WorkflowTransition data via log_event() instead of (or in addition to) the in-memory _transitions list. Fields: from_status, to_status, triggered_by, success, error_message. Depends on step 3. Parallel with step 4.
Chore triggers — In api/chores.py evaluate_triggers() and trigger_chore(): log each trigger event with chore name, trigger type (cron/manual), result count. Parallel with steps 4–5.
CRUD operations — In api/chores.py, api/agents.py, api/apps.py, api/tools.py: log create/update/delete events with entity name and actor. Keep it lightweight — one log_event() call per endpoint handler. Parallel with steps 4–6.
Webhook events — In api/webhooks.py: log inbound GitHub webhook events (PR opened, issue status changed) with summary. Parallel.
Cleanup operations — In api/cleanup.py: log start/completion with branch/PR counts from existing CleanupAuditLogRow. Parallel.
Phase 3 — Backend: Activity Feed API
New router — backend/src/api/activity.py — Two GET endpoints:
GET /activity?project_id=X&limit=50&cursor=TIMESTAMP&event_type=pipeline_run,chore_trigger — paginated feed, filterable by type, scoped to project
GET /activity/{entity_type}/{entity_id} — history for a specific entity (e.g., all events for pipeline "abc-123")
Register in main.py router. Depends on steps 1–2.
Phase 4 — Frontend: API Layer + Hook
Add activityApi — In frontend/src/services/api.ts:
activityApi.feed(projectId, { limit, cursor, eventTypes? }) → GET /activity
activityApi.entityHistory(entityType, entityId) → GET /activity/{type}/{id}
Depends on step 10.
Add useActivityFeed hook — frontend/src/hooks/useActivityFeed.ts:
useInfiniteQuery with cursor-based pagination (load more on scroll)
Query key: ['activity', projectId, filters]
Stale time: 30s (activity data is append-only, light polling is fine)
Returns { events, fetchNextPage, hasNextPage, isLoading }
Depends on step 11.
Phase 5 — Frontend: Activity Page
New page — frontend/src/pages/ActivityPage.tsx:
Filter bar: event type chips (pipeline, chore, agent, app, tool, webhook), date range
Infinite-scroll timeline: each event as a compact row with icon (by type), summary text, relative timestamp, entity link
Click event → expand inline detail (JSON detail rendered as key-value pairs, or link to entity page)
Empty state when no events
Depends on step 12.
Add route — In frontend/src/App.tsx: add /activity route → ActivityPage. Depends on step 13.
Add nav link — In sidebar/navigation component: add "Activity" link with clock/history icon between existing nav items. Parallel with step 14.
Phase 6 — Frontend: Wire Notification Bell
Implement useNotifications.ts — Replace the empty placeholder:
Query activityApi.feed(projectId, { limit: 20 }) for recent events
Filter to high-signal types: pipeline_run (completed/failed), chore_trigger, agent_execution
Map to existing Notification type: { id, type, title: summary, timestamp, read, source }
Read tracking stays in localStorage (existing pattern)
"View all" link in bell dropdown → navigates to /activity
Depends on step 12. Parallel with Phase 5.
Phase 7 — Frontend: Entity-Scoped History Panels
Pipeline run history — Add pipelinesApi.listRuns(projectId, pipelineId) and pipelinesApi.getRun(projectId, pipelineId, runId) to frontend/src/services/api.ts (backend endpoints already exist at GET /{pipeline_id}/runs). Add a "Run History" tab/panel in the pipeline editor view showing past runs with status, duration, stage breakdown. Parallel with Phase 6.
Entity history sidebar — In detail views for chores, agents, apps: add a collapsible "History" section that calls activityApi.entityHistory(type, id) and shows a mini-timeline. Depends on step 12. Parallel with step 17.
Relevant Files
File	Action
backend/src/migrations/03X_activity_events.sql	New — activity_events table + indexes
backend/src/models/activity.py	New — ActivityEvent, ActivityFeedResponse models
backend/src/services/activity_logger.py	New — log_event() service
backend/src/api/activity.py	New — GET /activity feed + entity history endpoints
backend/src/main.py	Register activity router
backend/src/api/pipelines.py	Add log_event() calls on run transitions
backend/src/api/chores.py	Add log_event() calls on trigger/CRUD
backend/src/api/agents.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD
backend/src/api/apps.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD/start/stop
backend/src/api/tools.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD
backend/src/api/webhooks.py	Add log_event() calls on webhook processing
backend/src/api/cleanup.py	Add log_event() calls on cleanup operations
backend/src/services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py	Persist transitions via log_event()
frontend/src/services/api.ts	Add activityApi + pipelinesApi.listRuns/getRun
frontend/src/hooks/useActivityFeed.ts	New — useInfiniteQuery for activity feed
frontend/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts	Replace placeholder with real activity query
frontend/src/pages/ActivityPage.tsx	New — full activity timeline page
frontend/src/App.tsx	Add /activity route
frontend/src/layout/ (nav component)	Add "Activity" nav link
frontend/src/types/index.ts	Add ActivityEvent type
Verification
Backend: trigger a pipeline run, create/delete a chore, trigger a webhook → query GET /activity?project_id=X → all events appear in chronological order with correct types and summaries
Pagination: insert 100+ events → GET /activity?limit=20 returns 20 with cursor → next page returns next 20
Entity history: GET /activity/pipeline/{id} returns only events for that pipeline
Frontend Activity page: load page → events render in timeline → scroll down → next page loads → filter by type → list narrows
Notification bell: after pipeline completes → bell shows unread badge → click → notification appears with summary → "View all" navigates to /activity
Pipeline run history panel: open pipeline editor → "Run History" tab shows past runs with status badges and durations
Performance: activity_events table with 10K rows → feed query returns in <100ms (verify with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on indexed query)
Run existing test suites to confirm no regressions
Decisions
Single table (activity_events) over per-entity history tables — simpler to query for a unified feed, denormalized summaries avoid JOINs
Cursor-based pagination (timestamp cursor) over offset — better for append-only data, no skipped/duplicated rows on new inserts
Fire-and-forget logging — activity logging failures are silently caught; they must never break the primary operation
Scope included: pipeline runs, stage transitions, workflow transitions, chore triggers, CRUD for all entities, webhooks, cleanup operations
Scope excluded: chat messages (already have their own table/UI), real-time WebSocket events (ephemeral by design), login/session events
Retention: no automatic cleanup initially; add a TTL-based purge (e.g., 90 days) as a follow-up if table grows large
Further Considerations
WebSocket push for new events — The existing connection_manager.broadcast_to_project() could push activity_event messages so the feed updates in real-time without polling. Recommend deferring to a follow-up since 30s stale time is acceptable for v1.
Export/download — An "Export CSV" button on the Activity page would be useful for audit compliance. Low effort to add as a follow-up endpoint.
Retention policy — With aggressive pipeline usage, the table could grow to 100K+ rows over months. A background cleanup job (keep last 90 days or last 10K rows per project) should be planned but doesn't block v1.

New service — backend/src/services/activity_logger.py — Thin write-through service:

mentioned_issues.title: Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
mentioned_issues.body:
Plan: Undo/Redo Support for Destructive Actions
Destructive actions (delete agent, pipeline, chore, tool) use a confirmation dialog but offer no recovery after confirmation. The standard modern pattern — an "undo toast" with a timed grace period — is missing entirely. The pipeline editor already has an undo/redo stack (usePipelineConfig.ts) but it resets completely on delete, and no other entity has any undo capability.

The fix: replace immediate hard-deletes with a soft-delete + undo toast pattern. During a grace window (~5s), the item is hidden from the UI but not yet deleted server-side. Clicking "Undo" in the toast cancels the pending delete. If the timer expires, the real DELETE fires.

Phase 1 — Generic Undo Toast Infrastructure
Create useUndoableDelete hook — New file frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts. Encapsulates:
Accepts: { onDelete: () => Promise<void>, undoTimeoutMs?: number, entityLabel: string }
On trigger: immediately hides item via optimistic cache removal (from Plan #3's onMutate pattern), then shows sonner toast with action: { label: 'Undo', onClick: cancelDelete } and duration: 5000
Internally: starts a setTimeout that fires the real API delete when the timer expires
Undo handler: clears timeout, restores cache snapshot, shows "Restored" toast
Cleanup: clears pending timeout on unmount
Returns { undoableDelete: (id) => void, pendingIds: Set<string> }
Toast configuration — In frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx, ensure <Toaster /> has closeButton enabled and supports action buttons (sonner does this natively via toast('message', { action: { label, onClick } })). No library change needed — sonner v1+ supports this out of the box.
Phase 2 — Chore Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts, frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx)
Replace confirmation + immediate delete — In ChoreCard.tsx, remove the confirm() dialog for delete. Instead call undoableDelete(choreId) from the new hook. Depends on step 1.
Optimistic removal — useDeleteChore gets onMutate to remove chore from choreKeys.list(projectId) cache instantly (same pattern as Plan #3 step 7), but the actual mutationFn is deferred by the undo hook.
Backend: no changes needed — Chore delete is already a hard delete (DELETE /chores/{project_id}/{chore_id}). The undo window is purely client-side; the API call simply doesn't fire until the grace period ends.
Phase 3 — Pipeline Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts)
Replace confirmation dialog — Currently useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts shows "This action cannot be undone." Replace with undo toast pattern. The pipeline is removed from pipelineKeys.list(projectId) cache immediately, real DELETE fires after grace period. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phase 2.
Preserve undo/redo stacks — The existing pipeline editor undo/redo (undoStackRef, redoStackRef, Ctrl+Z) is scoped to field edits inside the editor. This is orthogonal to delete-undo — keep both. The delete-undo is a toast-based grace period; the editor undo is a state history stack.
Phase 4 — Tool Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts, frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx)
Replace two-step confirm — Tool delete currently does a pre-flight check (confirm=false) to show affected agents, then a confirmation dialog. Change to: show affected agents inline (tooltip/popover on delete button), then fire undoableDelete(toolId). The undo toast provides the safety net instead of the dialog. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–3.
Deferred delete with confirm=true — The real DELETE /tools/{project_id}/{tool_id}?confirm=true fires only after grace period expires.
Phase 5 — Agent Delete with Undo (frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts, frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx)
Agent delete is already soft — Backend marks agent as pending_deletion and opens a PR. The undo pattern here is simpler: on "Undo", call a restore endpoint (or cancel the PR). If no restore endpoint exists, keep the confirmation dialog for agents but add an undo toast that re-enables the agent before the PR merges. Depends on step 1. Parallel with Phases 2–4.
Backend: Add agent restore endpoint (optional) — POST /agents/{project_id}/{agent_id}/restore that flips status back from pending_deletion to active and closes the deletion PR. Only needed if we want full undo for agents.
Phase 6 — App Delete (Keep Confirmation — No Undo Toast)
No change — App deletion is intentionally heavyweight (type-to-confirm, multi-asset cleanup, GitHub repo/project deletion). An undo toast is inappropriate here — the blast radius is too large and some operations (repo deletion) are irreversible on GitHub's side. Keep the existing two-step confirmation.
Relevant Files
File	Action
frontend/src/hooks/useUndoableDelete.ts	New — generic undo toast + deferred delete hook
frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx	Verify <Toaster /> supports action buttons (likely no change)
frontend/src/components/chores/ChoreCard.tsx	Replace confirm() → undoableDelete()
frontend/src/hooks/useChores.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into useDeleteChore
frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineConfig.ts	Wire undo toast into pipeline delete flow
frontend/src/hooks/useUnsavedPipelineGuard.ts	Remove "cannot be undone" confirmation for delete
frontend/src/components/tools/ToolsPanel.tsx	Replace two-step confirm → undo toast
frontend/src/hooks/useTools.ts	Wire useUndoableDelete into tool delete
frontend/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx	Replace confirm → undo toast (if restore endpoint added)
frontend/src/hooks/useAgents.ts	Wire undo toast for agent delete
backend/src/api/agents.py	(Optional) Add POST /agents/{id}/restore endpoint
frontend/src/hooks/useConfirmation.tsx	No change — still used by app delete and other non-delete confirmations
Verification
Chore delete: click delete → chore disappears instantly → toast with "Undo" button appears → click Undo → chore reappears → no API call made. Let toast expire → chore stays gone → API call fires → onSettled invalidation confirms server state.
Pipeline delete: same flow, verify editor state clears only after grace period, not on undo.
Tool delete: delete tool with agent associations → affected agent names shown in toast body → Undo restores tool and associations.
Unmount safety: navigate away during grace period → pending delete still fires (timeout persists via ref or is cleaned up with explicit cancel-on-unmount policy — decide per entity).
Multiple deletes: delete 3 chores rapidly → 3 independent undo toasts → undo middle one → only that chore restores.
Run Vitest + Playwright to confirm no regressions.
Decisions
Pattern: client-side deferred delete with undo toast (not server-side soft-delete) for chores, pipelines, tools. The API call is simply delayed, not changed.
Grace period: 5 seconds (industry standard — Gmail, Slack, Notion all use 5–10s).
App delete excluded: too destructive for undo toast; keep type-to-confirm.
Agent delete: depends on whether a restore endpoint is added. If not, keep confirmation dialog (agent delete is already soft/reversible via PR).
Unmount behavior: if user navigates away during grace period, fire the delete immediately (don't leave zombie timeouts). This matches Gmail's behavior.
Further Considerations
Agent restore endpoint — Adding POST /agents/{id}/restore is low effort (flip DB status, close PR) but requires backend work. Recommend including it. Without it, agents keep the confirmation dialog.
Keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Z for global undo — The pipeline editor already captures Ctrl+Z. A global Ctrl+Z that undoes the last toast-based delete would be powerful but could conflict. Recommend deferring this to a follow-up.

---

|---|--------|-------|-------|-------|-------|
| 1 | Backlog | G1 (series) | `speckit.specify` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |
| 2 | Backlog | G1 (series) | `speckit.plan` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |

| 4 | Ready | G1 (series) | `speckit.analyze` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |
| 5 | In Progress | G1 (series) | `speckit.implement` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |
| 6 | In Progress | G2 (parallel) | `copilot-review` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 7 | In Progress | G2 (parallel) | `linter` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |
| 8 | In Progress | G3 (series) | `judge` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |

mentioned_issues.title: Plan: Activity Log / Audit Trail
mentioned_issues.body:
Plan: Activity Log / Audit Trail
The backend already persists pipeline runs (pipeline_runs + pipeline_stage_states tables) and cleanup operations (cleanup_audit_logs table) with GET endpoints, but the frontend has zero UI to view them. Workflow transitions are in-memory only. Chore triggers and agent executions have no history at all. The notification bell (useNotifications.ts) returns an empty array — it's a placeholder.

The fix: add a unified activity events table in the backend, persist all trackable actions into it, expose a paginated API, and build an Activity page + feed component in the frontend.

Phase 1 — Backend: Unified Activity Events Table
New migration — backend/src/migrations/ — Create activity_events table:
id INTEGER PK, event_type TEXT (pipeline_run | pipeline_stage | chore_trigger | chore_crud | agent_crud | agent_execution | cleanup | app_crud | tool_crud | status_change | webhook), entity_type TEXT (pipeline | chore | agent | app | tool | issue), entity_id TEXT, project_id TEXT, actor TEXT (user or "system"), action TEXT (created | updated | deleted | triggered | started | completed | failed | cancelled | moved), summary TEXT (human-readable one-liner), detail TEXT (JSON blob — old/new values, error messages, metadata), created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
Index on (project_id, created_at DESC) for feed queries
Index on (entity_type, entity_id) for entity-scoped history
New model — backend/src/models/activity.py — Pydantic models: ActivityEvent, ActivityEventCreate, ActivityFeedResponse (items + total + cursor for pagination).
New service — backend/src/services/activity_logger.py — Thin write-through service:
log_event(event_type, entity_type, entity_id, project_id, actor, action, summary, detail=None) — inserts row
Injected as a dependency (like get_db), called from existing API routes and services
Async-safe, fire-and-forget (activity logging should never block the primary operation)
Phase 2 — Backend: Instrument Existing Flows
Pipeline runs — In services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py and api/pipelines.py: call log_event() on run create, status transitions (running → completed/failed/cancelled), and stage completions. Reuse data already in pipeline_runs table — the activity event is a denormalized summary row, not a replacement. Depends on step 3.
Workflow transitions — In orchestrator.py, persist WorkflowTransition data via log_event() instead of (or in addition to) the in-memory _transitions list. Fields: from_status, to_status, triggered_by, success, error_message. Depends on step 3. Parallel with step 4.
Chore triggers — In api/chores.py evaluate_triggers() and trigger_chore(): log each trigger event with chore name, trigger type (cron/manual), result count. Parallel with steps 4–5.
CRUD operations — In api/chores.py, api/agents.py, api/apps.py, api/tools.py: log create/update/delete events with entity name and actor. Keep it lightweight — one log_event() call per endpoint handler. Parallel with steps 4–6.
Webhook events — In api/webhooks.py: log inbound GitHub webhook events (PR opened, issue status changed) with summary. Parallel.
Cleanup operations — In api/cleanup.py: log start/completion with branch/PR counts from existing CleanupAuditLogRow. Parallel.
Phase 3 — Backend: Activity Feed API
New router — backend/src/api/activity.py — Two GET endpoints:
GET /activity?project_id=X&limit=50&cursor=TIMESTAMP&event_type=pipeline_run,chore_trigger — paginated feed, filterable by type, scoped to project
GET /activity/{entity_type}/{entity_id} — history for a specific entity (e.g., all events for pipeline "abc-123")
Register in main.py router. Depends on steps 1–2.
Phase 4 — Frontend: API Layer + Hook
Add activityApi — In frontend/src/services/api.ts:
activityApi.feed(projectId, { limit, cursor, eventTypes? }) → GET /activity
activityApi.entityHistory(entityType, entityId) → GET /activity/{type}/{id}
Depends on step 10.
Add useActivityFeed hook — frontend/src/hooks/useActivityFeed.ts:
useInfiniteQuery with cursor-based pagination (load more on scroll)
Query key: ['activity', projectId, filters]
Stale time: 30s (activity data is append-only, light polling is fine)
Returns { events, fetchNextPage, hasNextPage, isLoading }
Depends on step 11.
Phase 5 — Frontend: Activity Page
New page — frontend/src/pages/ActivityPage.tsx:
Filter bar: event type chips (pipeline, chore, agent, app, tool, webhook), date range
Infinite-scroll timeline: each event as a compact row with icon (by type), summary text, relative timestamp, entity link
Click event → expand inline detail (JSON detail rendered as key-value pairs, or link to entity page)
Empty state when no events
Depends on step 12.
Add route — In frontend/src/App.tsx: add /activity route → ActivityPage. Depends on step 13.
Add nav link — In sidebar/navigation component: add "Activity" link with clock/history icon between existing nav items. Parallel with step 14.
Phase 6 — Frontend: Wire Notification Bell
Implement useNotifications.ts — Replace the empty placeholder:
Query activityApi.feed(projectId, { limit: 20 }) for recent events
Filter to high-signal types: pipeline_run (completed/failed), chore_trigger, agent_execution
Map to existing Notification type: { id, type, title: summary, timestamp, read, source }
Read tracking stays in localStorage (existing pattern)
"View all" link in bell dropdown → navigates to /activity
Depends on step 12. Parallel with Phase 5.
Phase 7 — Frontend: Entity-Scoped History Panels
Pipeline run history — Add pipelinesApi.listRuns(projectId, pipelineId) and pipelinesApi.getRun(projectId, pipelineId, runId) to frontend/src/services/api.ts (backend endpoints already exist at GET /{pipeline_id}/runs). Add a "Run History" tab/panel in the pipeline editor view showing past runs with status, duration, stage breakdown. Parallel with Phase 6.
Entity history sidebar — In detail views for chores, agents, apps: add a collapsible "History" section that calls activityApi.entityHistory(type, id) and shows a mini-timeline. Depends on step 12. Parallel with step 17.
Relevant Files
File	Action
backend/src/migrations/03X_activity_events.sql	New — activity_events table + indexes
backend/src/models/activity.py	New — ActivityEvent, ActivityFeedResponse models
backend/src/services/activity_logger.py	New — log_event() service
backend/src/api/activity.py	New — GET /activity feed + entity history endpoints
backend/src/main.py	Register activity router
backend/src/api/pipelines.py	Add log_event() calls on run transitions
backend/src/api/chores.py	Add log_event() calls on trigger/CRUD
backend/src/api/agents.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD
backend/src/api/apps.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD/start/stop
backend/src/api/tools.py	Add log_event() calls on CRUD
backend/src/api/webhooks.py	Add log_event() calls on webhook processing
backend/src/api/cleanup.py	Add log_event() calls on cleanup operations
backend/src/services/workflow_orchestrator/orchestrator.py	Persist transitions via log_event()
frontend/src/services/api.ts	Add activityApi + pipelinesApi.listRuns/getRun
frontend/src/hooks/useActivityFeed.ts	New — useInfiniteQuery for activity feed
frontend/src/hooks/useNotifications.ts	Replace placeholder with real activity query
frontend/src/pages/ActivityPage.tsx	New — full activity timeline page
frontend/src/App.tsx	Add /activity route
frontend/src/layout/ (nav component)	Add "Activity" nav link
frontend/src/types/index.ts	Add ActivityEvent type
Verification
Backend: trigger a pipeline run, create/delete a chore, trigger a webhook → query GET /activity?project_id=X → all events appear in chronological order with correct types and summaries
Pagination: insert 100+ events → GET /activity?limit=20 returns 20 with cursor → next page returns next 20
Entity history: GET /activity/pipeline/{id} returns only events for that pipeline
Frontend Activity page: load page → events render in timeline → scroll down → next page loads → filter by type → list narrows
Notification bell: after pipeline completes → bell shows unread badge → click → notification appears with summary → "View all" navigates to /activity
Pipeline run history panel: open pipeline editor → "Run History" tab shows past runs with status badges and durations
Performance: activity_events table with 10K rows → feed query returns in <100ms (verify with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on indexed query)
Run existing test suites to confirm no regressions
Decisions
Single table (activity_events) over per-entity history tables — simpler to query for a unified feed, denormalized summaries avoid JOINs
Cursor-based pagination (timestamp cursor) over offset — better for append-only data, no skipped/duplicated rows on new inserts
Fire-and-forget logging — activity logging failures are silently caught; they must never break the primary operation
Scope included: pipeline runs, stage transitions, workflow transitions, chore triggers, CRUD for all entities, webhooks, cleanup operations
Scope excluded: chat messages (already have their own table/UI), real-time WebSocket events (ephemeral by design), login/session events
Retention: no automatic cleanup initially; add a TTL-based purge (e.g., 90 days) as a follow-up if table grows large
Further Considerations
WebSocket push for new events — The existing connection_manager.broadcast_to_project() could push activity_event messages so the feed updates in real-time without polling. Recommend deferring to a follow-up since 30s stale time is acceptable for v1.
Export/download — An "Export CSV" button on the Activity page would be useful for audit compliance. Low effort to add as a follow-up endpoint.
Retention policy — With aggressive pipeline usage, the table could grow to 100K+ rows over months. A background cleanup job (keep last 90 days or last 10K rows per project) should be planned but doesn't block v1.

---

## 🤖 Agents Pipelines

| # | Status | Group | Agent | Model | State |
|---|--------|-------|-------|-------|-------|

| 2 | Backlog | G1 (series) | `speckit.plan` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |
| 3 | Ready | G1 (series) | `speckit.tasks` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |
| 4 | Ready | G1 (series) | `speckit.analyze` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |
| 5 | In Progress | G1 (series) | `speckit.implement` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |
| 6 | In Progress | G2 (parallel) | `copilot-review` | TBD | ✅ Done |
| 7 | In Progress | G2 (parallel) | `linter` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |
| 8 | In Progress | G3 (series) | `judge` | claude-opus-4.6 | ✅ Done |
| 9 | In Review | G1 (series) | `human` | TBD | 🔄 Active |

closing_issues.title: [speckit.specify] Plan: Breadcrumb Doesn't Handle Deep Routes
closing_issues.body:
> **Parent Issue:** #4840 — Plan: Breadcrumb Doesn't Handle Deep Routes

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.specify`

Write a detailed specification for this feature. Analyze requirements, define acceptance criteria, and document the technical approach.

---

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: Breadcrumb Doesn't Handle Deep Routes
The Breadcrumb component matches the current pathname against the flat NAV_ROUTES array and always renders exactly two segments: "Home" + the matched route label. At /apps/my-cool-app, it finds the apps route via pathname.startsWith(r.path) and shows Home > Apps — the :appName param is ignored. There's no mechanism for dynamic segments, route metadata, or depth beyond 2.

closing_issues.title: [speckit.specify] Plan: Fix Premature Copilot Review Completion in Agent Pipeline
closing_issues.body:
> **Parent Issue:** #4857 — Plan: Fix Premature Copilot Review Completion in Agent Pipeline

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.specify`

Write a detailed specification for this feature. Analyze requirements, define acceptance criteria, and document the technical approach.

---

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: Fix Premature Copilot Review Completion in Agent Pipeline
The pipeline marks copilot-review as "Done!" before it's actually copilot-review's turn because of three compounding issues: the webhook unconditionally moves issues to "In Review", the completion detection function has no pipeline-position guard, and the review-request timestamp is lost on server restart. Fix with layered guards + durable state.

Root Causes
Webhook blindly moves to "In Review" — webhooks.py:417 calls update_item_status_by_name("In Review") whenever ANY Copilot PR becomes ready, regardless of pipeline stage. When speckit.implement finishes and its PR is ready, the webhook fires and the board shows "In Review" before the pipeline has actually advanced to copilot-review.

No pipeline-position guard in _check_copilot_review_done() — helpers.py:152 checks timestamps, stale markers, and confirmation delays — but never verifies that copilot-review is the current pipeline agent. It trusts callers, but callers can get it wrong after pipeline reconstruction.

Reconstruction falsely sets current_agent to "copilot-review" — After server restart/cache eviction, pipeline.py:318 is called with status="In Review" and agents=["copilot-review"]. With no "Done!" marker found, it sets current_agent_index=0 → current_agent="copilot-review" — even if speckit.implement is still pending.

In-memory timestamp lost on restart — _copilot_review_requested_at is a BoundedDict in memory. Server restart clears it. Recovery from issue body HTML comments is best-effort and can fail.

Steps
Phase 1: Pipeline Position Guards (blocks Phase 2)
Add pipeline-position guard to _check_copilot_review_done()

File: helpers.py
Add optional pipeline param. If pipeline.current_agent != "copilot-review", return False immediately with a warning log — before ANY API calls.
This is the innermost defense: even if all other guards fail, this prevents false completion.
Pass pipeline through from _check_agent_done_on_sub_or_parent() (depends on 1)

File: helpers.py
At helpers.py:113, pass the existing pipeline parameter through to _check_copilot_review_done().
Add pipeline-position guard to check_in_review_issues() (parallel with 1–2)

File: pipeline.py
After pipeline retrieval at pipeline.py:2327, if pipeline.current_agent != "copilot-review" AND pipeline.status is earlier than "In Review", log a warning and let _process_pipeline_completion() handle advancing the current (non-copilot-review) agent only.
Phase 2: Webhook Guard (parallel with Phase 3, depends on Phase 1)
Guard webhook status move with pipeline validation
File: webhooks.py
In update_issue_status_for_copilot_pr(), before webhooks.py:466, check pipeline state:
If pipeline exists AND pipeline.current_agent != "copilot-review" AND pipeline.status != "In Review" → do NOT move the issue. Log and return a "skipped" result.

mentioned_issues.title: [linter] Plan: Breadcrumb Doesn't Handle Deep Routes
mentioned_issues.body:
> **Parent Issue:** #4840 — Plan: Breadcrumb Doesn't Handle Deep Routes

## 🤖 Agent Task: `linter`

Complete the work assigned to the `linter` agent.

---

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: Breadcrumb Doesn't Handle Deep Routes
The Breadcrumb component matches the current pathname against the flat NAV_ROUTES array and always renders exactly two segments: "Home" + the matched route label. At /apps/my-cool-app, it finds the apps route via pathname.startsWith(r.path) and shows Home > Apps — the :appName param is ignored. There's no mechanism for dynamic segments, route metadata, or depth beyond 2.

The fix: make the breadcrumb parse all path segments, resolve params against route data, and support a useBreadcrumb context so pages can inject dynamic labels (e.g., the actual app name).

Phase 1 — Breadcrumb Context for Dynamic Labels
Create BreadcrumbContext — New file frontend/src/hooks/useBreadcrumb.ts:
Context holds a Map<string, string> of path-segment overrides (e.g., { "my-cool-app": "My Cool App" })
useBreadcrumbLabel(segment: string, label: string) — hook that registers a dynamic label on mount and clears on unmount. Pages call this to inject entity names.
useBreadcrumbOverrides() — consumed by Breadcrumb.tsx to resolve dynamic labels
Provider wraps the app in AppLayout.tsx (alongside existing providers)
Wire provider — In frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx, wrap content with <BreadcrumbProvider>. Depends on step 1.
Phase 2 — Rewrite Breadcrumb Component
Rewrite Breadcrumb.tsx — In frontend/src/layout/Breadcrumb.tsx:
Split pathname into segments: /apps/my-cool-app → ["apps", "my-cool-app"]
For each segment, build cumulative path: apps, /apps/my-cool-app
Resolve label: first check BreadcrumbContext overrides, then check NAV_ROUTES lookup (keyed by path), then fallback to decodeURIComponent(segment) title-cased
Render N segments (not capped at 2): Home > Apps > My Cool App
Last segment remains non-interactive (<span>), all prior segments are <Link>
Keep existing styling (ChevronRight separator, text-muted-foreground, hover effects)
Depends on step 1.
Phase 3 — Pages Register Dynamic Labels
AppsPage — In frontend/src/pages/AppsPage.tsx:
When appName param exists, call useBreadcrumbLabel(appName, app.display_name ?? appName) using the fetched app data. This makes /apps/my-cool-app render as Home > Apps > My Cool App.
The label cleans up automatically on unmount (navigating away).
Depends on steps 1, 3.
Any future parameterized routes (e.g., /activity/:eventId, /pipeline/:pipelineId) can call useBreadcrumbLabel() in the same pattern. No changes to the breadcrumb component needed — it's generic. Parallel with step 4.
Phase 4 — Handle Edge Cases
Trailing slashes — Strip trailing slashes from pathname before splitting. Part of step 3.
Unknown segments — If a segment doesn't match NAV_ROUTES and has no context override, display it as title-cased decoded URI (e.g., my-cool-app → My Cool App). Part of step 3.
404 routes — The catch-all * route maps to NotFoundPage. Breadcrumb should show Home > Not Found or just Home. The current behavior of falling back to "Home" alone is fine. Part of step 3.
/help and /settings — No params, no change — they continue to show 2-segment breadcrumbs as before. No action.
Relevant Files
File	Action
frontend/src/hooks/useBreadcrumb.ts	New — BreadcrumbContext + useBreadcrumbLabel hook
frontend/src/layout/Breadcrumb.tsx	Rewrite to parse all path segments + consume context overrides
frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx	Wrap with <BreadcrumbProvider>
frontend/src/pages/AppsPage.tsx	Call useBreadcrumbLabel(appName, displayName)
frontend/src/constants.ts	Reference: NAV_ROUTES array (no change, used as lookup)
Verification
apps → shows Home > Apps (unchanged)
/apps/my-cool-app → shows Home > Apps > My Cool App (new third crumb with app display name)
Click "Apps" crumb at /apps/my-cool-app → navigates to apps list view
Navigate away from /apps/my-cool-app → dynamic label cleaned up from context, no stale crumbs
Unknown deep path (e.g., manually typed /apps/nonexistent) → shows Home > Apps > Nonexistent (title-cased fallback) until data loads or 404 renders
All flat routes (/projects, /pipeline, /agents, etc.) → unchanged 2-segment breadcrumbs
/ (home) → shows only Home (unchanged)
Run Vitest to confirm no regressions
Decisions
Context-based over react-router handle metadata — avoids coupling breadcrumb labels to route definitions and supports async data (entity names from API responses)
Fallback to title-cased segment — ensures breadcrumb never shows raw URL slugs like "my-cool-app"; renders "My Cool App" even before API data loads
No NAV_ROUTES restructuring — the flat array stays as-is; breadcrumb path-segment parsing replaces the startsWith matching
Scope: only /apps/:appName benefits today, but the pattern is generic for any future parameterized route

---
*Sub-issue created for agent `linter` — see parent issue #4840 for full context*

mentioned_issues.title: [speckit.tasks] Plan: Breadcrumb Doesn't Handle Deep Routes
mentioned_issues.body:
> **Parent Issue:** #4840 — Plan: Breadcrumb Doesn't Handle Deep Routes

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.tasks`

Generate granular implementation tasks from the plan. Each task should be a well-defined unit of work with clear inputs, outputs, and acceptance criteria.

---

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: Breadcrumb Doesn't Handle Deep Routes
The Breadcrumb component matches the current pathname against the flat NAV_ROUTES array and always renders exactly two segments: "Home" + the matched route label. At /apps/my-cool-app, it finds the apps route via pathname.startsWith(r.path) and shows Home > Apps — the :appName param is ignored. There's no mechanism for dynamic segments, route metadata, or depth beyond 2.

The fix: make the breadcrumb parse all path segments, resolve params against route data, and support a useBreadcrumb context so pages can inject dynamic labels (e.g., the actual app name).

Phase 1 — Breadcrumb Context for Dynamic Labels
Create BreadcrumbContext — New file frontend/src/hooks/useBreadcrumb.ts:
Context holds a Map<string, string> of path-segment overrides (e.g., { "my-cool-app": "My Cool App" })
useBreadcrumbLabel(segment: string, label: string) — hook that registers a dynamic label on mount and clears on unmount. Pages call this to inject entity names.
useBreadcrumbOverrides() — consumed by Breadcrumb.tsx to resolve dynamic labels
Provider wraps the app in AppLayout.tsx (alongside existing providers)
Wire provider — In frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx, wrap content with <BreadcrumbProvider>. Depends on step 1.
Phase 2 — Rewrite Breadcrumb Component
Rewrite Breadcrumb.tsx — In frontend/src/layout/Breadcrumb.tsx:
Split pathname into segments: /apps/my-cool-app → ["apps", "my-cool-app"]
For each segment, build cumulative path: apps, /apps/my-cool-app
Resolve label: first check BreadcrumbContext overrides, then check NAV_ROUTES lookup (keyed by path), then fallback to decodeURIComponent(segment) title-cased
Render N segments (not capped at 2): Home > Apps > My Cool App
Last segment remains non-interactive (<span>), all prior segments are <Link>
Keep existing styling (ChevronRight separator, text-muted-foreground, hover effects)
Depends on step 1.
Phase 3 — Pages Register Dynamic Labels
AppsPage — In frontend/src/pages/AppsPage.tsx:
When appName param exists, call useBreadcrumbLabel(appName, app.display_name ?? appName) using the fetched app data. This makes /apps/my-cool-app render as Home > Apps > My Cool App.
The label cleans up automatically on unmount (navigating away).
Depends on steps 1, 3.
Any future parameterized routes (e.g., /activity/:eventId, /pipeline/:pipelineId) can call useBreadcrumbLabel() in the same pattern. No changes to the breadcrumb component needed — it's generic. Parallel with step 4.
Phase 4 — Handle Edge Cases
Trailing slashes — Strip trailing slashes from pathname before splitting. Part of step 3.
Unknown segments — If a segment doesn't match NAV_ROUTES and has no context override, display it as title-cased decoded URI (e.g., my-cool-app → My Cool App). Part of step 3.
404 routes — The catch-all * route maps to NotFoundPage. Breadcrumb should show Home > Not Found or just Home. The current behavior of falling back to "Home" alone is fine. Part of step 3.
/help and /settings — No params, no change — they continue to show 2-segment breadcrumbs as before. No action.
Relevant Files
File	Action
frontend/src/hooks/useBreadcrumb.ts	New — BreadcrumbContext + useBreadcrumbLabel hook
frontend/src/layout/Breadcrumb.tsx	Rewrite to parse all path segments + consume context overrides
frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx	Wrap with <BreadcrumbProvider>
frontend/src/pages/AppsPage.tsx	Call useBreadcrumbLabel(appName, displayName)
frontend/src/constants.ts	Reference: NAV_ROUTES array (no change, used as lookup)
Verification
apps → shows Home > Apps (unchanged)
/apps/my-cool-app → shows Home > Apps > My Cool App (new third crumb with app display name)
Click "Apps" crumb at /apps/my-cool-app → navigates to apps list view
Navigate away from /apps/my-cool-app → dynamic label cleaned up from context, no stale crumbs
Unknown deep path (e.g., manually typed /apps/nonexistent) → shows Home > Apps > Nonexistent (title-cased fallback) until data loads or 404 renders
All flat routes (/projects, /pipeline, /agents, etc.) → unchanged 2-segment breadcrumbs
/ (home) → shows only Home (unchanged)
Run Vitest to confirm no regressions
Decisions
Context-based over react-router handle metadata — avoids coupling breadcrumb labels to route definitions and supports async data (entity names from API responses)
Fallback to title-cased segment — ensures breadcrumb never shows raw URL slugs like "my-cool-app"; renders "My Cool App" even before API data loads
No NAV_ROUTES restructuring — the flat array stays as-is; breadcrumb path-segment parsing replaces the startsWith matching
Scope: only /apps/:appName benefits today, but the pattern is generic for any future parameterized route

---
*Sub-issue created for agent `speckit.tasks` — see parent issue #4840 for full context*

> **Parent Issue:** #4857 — Plan: Fix Premature Copilot Review Completion in Agent Pipeline

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.implement`

Implement the feature based on the specification, plan, and tasks. Write production-quality code with tests.

---

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: Fix Premature Copilot Review Completion in Agent Pipeline
The pipeline marks copilot-review as "Done!" before it's actually copilot-review's turn because of three compounding issues: the webhook unconditionally moves issues to "In Review", the completion detection function has no pipeline-position guard, and the review-request timestamp is lost on server restart. Fix with layered guards + durable state.

Root Causes
Webhook blindly moves to "In Review" — webhooks.py:417 calls update_item_status_by_name("In Review") whenever ANY Copilot PR becomes ready, regardless of pipeline stage. When speckit.implement finishes and its PR is ready, the webhook fires and the board shows "In Review" before the pipeline has actually advanced to copilot-review.

No pipeline-position guard in _check_copilot_review_done() — helpers.py:152 checks timestamps, stale markers, and confirmation delays — but never verifies that copilot-review is the current pipeline agent. It trusts callers, but callers can get it wrong after pipeline reconstruction.

Reconstruction falsely sets current_agent to "copilot-review" — After server restart/cache eviction, pipeline.py:318 is called with status="In Review" and agents=["copilot-review"]. With no "Done!" marker found, it sets current_agent_index=0 → current_agent="copilot-review" — even if speckit.implement is still pending.

In-memory timestamp lost on restart — _copilot_review_requested_at is a BoundedDict in memory. Server restart clears it. Recovery from issue body HTML comments is best-effort and can fail.

Phase 1: Pipeline Position Guards (blocks Phase 2)
Add pipeline-position guard to _check_copilot_review_done()

File: helpers.py
Add optional pipeline param. If pipeline.current_agent != "copilot-review", return False immediately with a warning log — before ANY API calls.
This is the innermost defense: even if all other guards fail, this prevents false completion.
Pass pipeline through from _check_agent_done_on_sub_or_parent() (depends on 1)

File: helpers.py
At helpers.py:113, pass the existing pipeline parameter through to _check_copilot_review_done().
Add pipeline-position guard to check_in_review_issues() (parallel with 1–2)

Persist timestamp on review request (depends on 5)

Write to both in-memory dict AND SQLite.
Recover timestamp from DB on restart (depends on 5, 6)

mentioned_issues.title: [linter] Plan: Fix Premature Copilot Review Completion in Agent Pipeline
mentioned_issues.body:
> **Parent Issue:** #4857 — Plan: Fix Premature Copilot Review Completion in Agent Pipeline

## 🤖 Agent Task: `linter`

Complete the work assigned to the `linter` agent.

---

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: Fix Premature Copilot Review Completion in Agent Pipeline
The pipeline marks copilot-review as "Done!" before it's actually copilot-review's turn because of three compounding issues: the webhook unconditionally moves issues to "In Review", the completion detection function has no pipeline-position guard, and the review-request timestamp is lost on server restart. Fix with layered guards + durable state.

Root Causes
Webhook blindly moves to "In Review" — webhooks.py:417 calls update_item_status_by_name("In Review") whenever ANY Copilot PR becomes ready, regardless of pipeline stage. When speckit.implement finishes and its PR is ready, the webhook fires and the board shows "In Review" before the pipeline has actually advanced to copilot-review.

No pipeline-position guard in _check_copilot_review_done() — helpers.py:152 checks timestamps, stale markers, and confirmation delays — but never verifies that copilot-review is the current pipeline agent. It trusts callers, but callers can get it wrong after pipeline reconstruction.

Reconstruction falsely sets current_agent to "copilot-review" — After server restart/cache eviction, pipeline.py:318 is called with status="In Review" and agents=["copilot-review"]. With no "Done!" marker found, it sets current_agent_index=0 → current_agent="copilot-review" — even if speckit.implement is still pending.

In-memory timestamp lost on restart — _copilot_review_requested_at is a BoundedDict in memory. Server restart clears it. Recovery from issue body HTML comments is best-effort and can fail.

Steps
Phase 1: Pipeline Position Guards (blocks Phase 2)
Add pipeline-position guard to _check_copilot_review_done()

File: helpers.py
Add optional pipeline param. If pipeline.current_agent != "copilot-review", return False immediately with a warning log — before ANY API calls.
This is the innermost defense: even if all other guards fail, this prevents false completion.
Pass pipeline through from _check_agent_done_on_sub_or_parent() (depends on 1)

File: helpers.py
At helpers.py:113, pass the existing pipeline parameter through to _check_copilot_review_done().
Add pipeline-position guard to check_in_review_issues() (parallel with 1–2)

File: pipeline.py
After pipeline retrieval at pipeline.py:2327, if pipeline.current_agent != "copilot-review" AND pipeline.status is earlier than "In Review", log a warning and let _process_pipeline_completion() handle advancing the current (non-copilot-review) agent only.
Phase 2: Webhook Guard (parallel with Phase 3, depends on Phase 1)
Guard webhook status move with pipeline validation
File: webhooks.py
In update_issue_status_for_copilot_pr(), before webhooks.py:466, check pipeline state:
If pipeline exists AND pipeline.current_agent != "copilot-review" AND pipeline.status != "In Review" → do NOT move the issue. Log and return a "skipped" result.
If no pipeline exists → still move (backward compat for non-pipeline issues).
The pipeline's own _transition_after_pipeline_complete() handles status transitions at the correct time.
Phase 3: Durable Review-Request Timestamp (parallel with Phase 2)
Add migration for durable timestamp storage

New migration in migrations
Table: copilot_review_requests(issue_number INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, requested_at TIMESTAMP, project_id TEXT)
Persist timestamp on review request (depends on 5)

File: helpers.py, function _record_copilot_review_request_timestamp()
Write to both in-memory dict AND SQLite.
Recover timestamp from DB on restart (depends on 5, 6)

File: helpers.py, inside _check_copilot_review_done()
When _copilot_review_requested_at.get(issue_number) is None, query SQLite before falling back to issue body HTML comment.
Phase 4: Reconstruction Safety (depends on Phase 1)
Harden _get_or_reconstruct_pipeline() for "In Review"
File: pipeline.py
Verify the existing tracking-table guard (lines ~410-444) correctly handles "In Progress agents pending but board says In Review". Add test coverage for this specific scenario.
Relevant Files
helpers.py — _check_copilot_review_done(), _check_agent_done_on_sub_or_parent(), _record_copilot_review_request_timestamp()
pipeline.py — check_in_review_issues(), _get_or_reconstruct_pipeline(), _process_pipeline_completion()
webhooks.py — update_issue_status_for_copilot_pr(), handle_pull_request_event()
state.py — _copilot_review_requested_at, _copilot_review_first_detected
completion.py — ensure_copilot_review_requested() (already has _pipeline_allows_copilot_review_request — good)
New migration file in migrations
Verification
Unit test: Pipeline at "In Progress" with current_agent="speckit.implement" → call _check_copilot_review_done(pipeline=pipeline) → returns False without API calls
Unit test: Webhook ready_for_review fires with pipeline at current_agent="speckit.implement" → update_issue_status_for_copilot_pr() does NOT move to "In Review"
Unit test: Clear _copilot_review_requested_at, insert timestamp in SQLite → _check_copilot_review_done() recovers from DB
Integration test: Full pipeline run — speckit.implement finishes, GitHub auto-triggers a review → pipeline does NOT mark copilot-review done; only marks done when pipeline reaches copilot-review step, Solune requests review, and Copilot completes it
Regression test: When copilot-review IS the current agent → existing flow still works correctly
Reconstruction test: Issue body has "In Progress" agents pending, call _get_or_reconstruct_pipeline(status="In Review") → reconstructs for "In Progress"
Decisions
Webhook still moves status for non-pipeline issues (backward compat); only pipeline-tracked issues are guarded
Review-request timestamp persisted to SQLite (not just in-memory + HTML comment)
The _pipeline_allows_copilot_review_request() guard in completion.py is sufficient for review requests — the missing piece was review completion detection
Scope excludes: refactoring polling loop order, changing confirmation delay timing, modifying _advance_pipeline() (already correct once called with the right agent)

---
*Sub-issue created for agent `linter` — see parent issue #4857 for full context*

closing_issues.title: [speckit.specify] Performance Review
closing_issues.body:
> **Parent Issue:** #4882 — Performance Review

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.specify`

Write a detailed specification for this feature. Analyze requirements, define acceptance criteria, and document the technical approach.

---

## Parent Issue Context

## Performance Review

Perform a balanced first pass focused on measurable, low-risk performance gains across backend and frontend. Start by capturing baselines and instrumentation, then fix the highest-value issues already surfaced by the codebase: backend GitHub API churn around board refreshes and polling, and frontend board responsiveness issues caused by broad query invalidation, full-list rerenders, and hot event listeners. Defer broader architectural refactors like virtualization and large service decomposition unless the first pass fails to meet targets.

**Steps**
1. Phase 1 — Baseline and guardrails. Capture current backend and frontend performance baselines before changing behavior. Measure idle API activity for an open board, board endpoint request cost, WebSocket/polling refresh behavior, and frontend render hot spots. Reuse existing tests around cache, polling, WebSocket fallback, and board refresh to define a before/after checklist. This phase blocks all optimization work because the success criteria and regression guardrails depend on it.
2. Phase 1 — Confirm current backend state against Spec 022. Verify whether WebSocket change detection, board cache TTL alignment, and sub-issue cache invalidation are fully implemented or only partially landed. The current board endpoint already appears to set a 300-second TTL and clears sub-issue cache on manual refresh, so the remaining work should target any still-missing pieces rather than redoing completed items. This step can run in parallel with frontend baseline inspection once the measurement checklist is defined.
3. Phase 2 — Backend API consumption fixes. Prioritize the highest-value remaining server-side issues: WebSocket subscription refresh logic in the projects API, sub-issue caching behavior for board data, and any remaining unnecessary GitHub calls in polling or repository resolution. Explicitly validate that idle board viewing no longer emits repeated refreshes when data is unchanged, that warm sub-issue caches materially reduce board refresh call count, and that fallback polling does not trigger expensive board refreshes unintentionally. This depends on Phase 1 baselines.
4. Phase 2 — Frontend refresh-path fixes. Update the real-time and fallback refresh paths so lightweight task updates stay decoupled from the expensive board data query except on manual refresh. Review the interaction between WebSocket updates, fallback polling, auto-refresh, and manual refresh to ensure they use a single coherent policy and do not recreate the prior polling storm. This can proceed in parallel with backend API work once the desired refresh contract is confirmed.
5. Phase 3 — Frontend render optimization. Target low-risk rendering costs in board and chat surfaces: reduce repeated derived-data work in page components and hooks, stabilize props where useful, memoize heavy card/list components when it actually reduces rerenders, and throttle or rationalize hot event listeners such as drag and popover positioning. Keep this phase intentionally low-risk; avoid introducing new dependencies or virtualization in the first pass unless baseline results show large boards still regress after the lighter fixes.
6. Phase 3 — Verification and regression coverage. Extend or adjust unit/integration coverage around backend cache behavior, WebSocket change detection, fallback polling, and frontend board refresh logic. Validate with backend tests, frontend tests, and at least one manual network/profile pass to confirm the target improvements are real rather than inferred. This depends on Phases 2 and 3.
7. Phase 4 — Optional second-wave work. If the first pass still leaves material UI lag on large boards or excessive backend complexity, prepare a follow-on plan for structural changes: board virtualization, deeper service decomposition around GitHub project fetching/polling, bounded cache policies, and stronger instrumentation around request budgets and render timings. This phase is explicitly out of scope for the first implementation unless measurements prove it is necessary.

**Relevant files**
- `solune/specs/022-api-rate-limit-protection/spec.md` — primary acceptance criteria for idle-rate-limit reduction, sub-issue caching, refresh behavior, and cache TTL alignment.
- `solune/backend/src/api/projects.py` — projects tasks endpoints and WebSocket subscription flow; likely location for change-detection verification and refresh semantics.
- `solune/backend/src/api/board.py` — board-data cache behavior, manual refresh semantics, and sub-issue cache invalidation path.
- `solune/backend/src/services/copilot_polling/polling_loop.py` — polling hot path and expensive background work that can still consume rate limit budget.
- `solune/backend/src/services/github_projects/service.py` — board/project fetching path and candidate reuse points for sub-issue caching or batching.
- `solune/backend/src/services/cache.py` — cache TTLs, cache-key helpers, and any bounded-cache improvements if needed.
- `solune/backend/src/utils.py` — shared repository resolution logic to reuse instead of duplicated fallback flows.
- `solune/backend/src/api/workflow.py` — known duplicate repository-resolution path that may add inconsistency and avoidable work.
- `solune/frontend/src/hooks/useRealTimeSync.ts` — current WebSocket/fallback polling behavior; today it still invalidates board data during polling fallback.
- `solune/frontend/src/hooks/useBoardRefresh.ts` — board auto-refresh policy and manual refresh coordination.
- `solune/frontend/src/hooks/useProjectBoard.ts` — board query ownership and invalidation/refetch strategy.
- `solune/frontend/src/components/board/BoardColumn.tsx` — full column list rendering without memoization or virtualization.
- `solune/frontend/src/components/board/IssueCard.tsx` — likely high-frequency rerender unit for board interactions.
- `solune/frontend/src/pages/ProjectsPage.tsx` — render-time sorting/aggregation and board-level derived state.
- `solune/frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPopup.tsx` — hot drag listener path worth throttling.
- `solune/frontend/src/components/agents/AddAgentPopover.tsx` — positioning listeners and update frequency.
- `solune/backend/tests/unit/test_cache.py` — backend cache TTL and stale fallback coverage to extend.
- `solune/backend/tests/unit/test_api_board.py` — board cache and board endpoint behavior to reuse for regression tests.
- `solune/backend/tests/unit/test_copilot_polling.py` — polling behavior and rate-limit-aware logic to reuse.
- `solune/frontend/src/hooks/useRealTimeSync.test.tsx` — refresh invalidation and WebSocket fallback coverage to extend.
- `solune/frontend/src/hooks/useBoardRefresh.test.tsx` — refresh timer and deduplication behavior to reuse.

**Verification**
1. Backend baseline: measure idle API activity for an open board over a fixed interval and compare against Spec 022 targets; confirm no repeated unchanged refreshes are sent.
2. Backend automated checks: run Ruff, Pyright, and the targeted pytest files covering cache, board, projects/WebSocket, and polling behavior.
3. Frontend baseline: profile board load and interaction on a representative project size, inspect network activity for WebSocket, fallback polling, and board query invalidation, and identify repeated rerender sources.
4. Frontend automated checks: run ESLint, type-checking, Vitest coverage for real-time sync and board refresh hooks, and a build check.
5. Manual end-to-end check: verify that WebSocket updates refresh task data quickly, fallback polling remains safe, manual refresh still bypasses caches when intended, and board interactions remain responsive.

**Decisions**
- Selected approach: balanced pass across backend and frontend rather than a single-area optimization.
- Recommended implementation scope for the first pass: low-risk optimizations first, even though the user left the aggressiveness undecided.
- Included scope: measurement, idle API reduction, refresh-path cleanup, low-risk render optimization, and regression coverage.
- Excluded from the first pass unless metrics justify it: board virtualization, major service decomposition, dependency changes, and larger architectural rewrites.
- Baseline measurement is mandatory before code changes so the improvements can be proven and not just assumed.

**Further Considerations**
1. If large boards still feel slow after the low-risk frontend fixes, the next recommended option is virtualization rather than additional scattered memoization.
2. If backend API churn remains high after Spec 022-aligned fixes, the next recommended option is deeper consolidation in the GitHub projects service and polling pipeline rather than more cache-layer patching.
3. If repeated performance work is expected in this repo, add lightweight instrumentation or logging around board refresh cost, sub-issue cache hit rate, and refresh-source attribution so regressions are visible earlier.

---

closing_issues.title: [speckit.specify] Plan: ChoresPanel Pagination Migration
closing_issues.body:
> **Parent Issue:** #4894 — Plan: ChoresPanel Pagination Migration

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.specify`

Write a detailed specification for this feature. Analyze requirements, define acceptance criteria, and document the technical approach.

---

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: ChoresPanel Pagination Migration
The gap is narrower than described — ChoresPanel is the only remaining unpaginated list. Agents, Tools, Apps, Activity, and Board columns all already use cursor-based infinite scroll via useInfiniteList + InfiniteScrollContainer. The infrastructure is fully built; ChoresPanel just hasn't been wired up yet.

The complication: ChoresPanel does client-side filtering (search, status, schedule) and sorting. Switching to paginated data means filtering only the loaded pages, missing items on later pages. This requires moving filters server-side.

Steps

Phase 1: Backend — Add server-side filtering (no dependencies)
Add query parameters status, schedule_type, search, sort, order to GET /chores/{project_id} in chores.py — apply filtering before calling apply_pagination()
Phase 2: Frontend — Wire up paginated hook (steps 3-4 parallel with Phase 1; step 5+ sequential)
Update choresApi.listPaginated() in api.ts to accept optional filter params (status, scheduleType, search, sort, order) and append to query string
Update useChoresListPaginated() in useChores.ts to accept filter/sort params and include them in the query key so changing a filter triggers a fresh fetch (depends on 2)
Switch ChoresPanel.tsx from useChoresList() to useChoresListPaginated() — pass filter state as hook params, remove the client-side filter/sort useMemo, pass hasNextPage/isFetchingNextPage/fetchNextPage to ChoresGrid (depends on 3)
Call resetPagination() when filters change so pagination restarts from page 1 (depends on 4)
Phase 3: Cleanup
Check if useChoresList() and choresApi.list() are used elsewhere — if not, remove the non-paginated variants (depends on 4)
Relevant files

chores.py — add filter query params, apply before apply_pagination()
api.ts — update choresApi.listPaginated() signature
useChores.ts — update useChoresListPaginated() to accept/forward filters
ChoresPanel.tsx — swap hooks, remove client-side filter useMemo, pass pagination props to ChoresGrid
ChoresGrid.tsx — no changes needed (already supports pagination props + InfiniteScrollContainer)
Reference implementations (patterns to follow):

AgentsPanel.tsx — useAgentsListPaginated() + InfiniteScrollContainer wiring
ActivityPage.tsx — working infinite scroll template
Verification

Add pytest tests for GET /chores/{project_id} with filter combos — verify correct items + cursor behavior with active filters
Update vitest tests for useChoresListPaginated with filter params in query key
Manual: load ChoresPanel with 50+ chores — confirm 25 load initially, scrolling loads more, filter changes reset and re-fetch from server
Verify rapid filter toggling doesn't cause issues (search is already debounced via useDeferredValue)
Decisions

Server-side filtering is required — client-side filtering on paginated data would only filter loaded pages
Sorting also moves server-side (client-side sort of partial data is meaningless)
Keep useDeferredValue for search debouncing — the deferred value becomes a query param
Default limit stays at 25 (consistent with all other paginated hooks)

---

mentioned_issues.body:
## Performance Review

Perform a balanced first pass focused on measurable, low-risk performance gains across backend and frontend. Start by capturing baselines and instrumentation, then fix the highest-value issues already surfaced by the codebase: backend GitHub API churn around board refreshes and polling, and frontend board responsiveness issues caused by broad query invalidation, full-list rerenders, and hot event listeners. Defer broader architectural refactors like virtualization and large service decomposition unless the first pass fails to meet targets.

**Steps**
1. Phase 1 — Baseline and guardrails. Capture current backend and frontend performance baselines before changing behavior. Measure idle API activity for an open board, board endpoint request cost, WebSocket/polling refresh behavior, and frontend render hot spots. Reuse existing tests around cache, polling, WebSocket fallback, and board refresh to define a before/after checklist. This phase blocks all optimization work because the success criteria and regression guardrails depend on it.
2. Phase 1 — Confirm current backend state against Spec 022. Verify whether WebSocket change detection, board cache TTL alignment, and sub-issue cache invalidation are fully implemented or only partially landed. The current board endpoint already appears to set a 300-second TTL and clears sub-issue cache on manual refresh, so the remaining work should target any still-missing pieces rather than redoing completed items. This step can run in parallel with frontend baseline inspection once the measurement checklist is defined.
3. Phase 2 — Backend API consumption fixes. Prioritize the highest-value remaining server-side issues: WebSocket subscription refresh logic in the projects API, sub-issue caching behavior for board data, and any remaining unnecessary GitHub calls in polling or repository resolution. Explicitly validate that idle board viewing no longer emits repeated refreshes when data is unchanged, that warm sub-issue caches materially reduce board refresh call count, and that fallback polling does not trigger expensive board refreshes unintentionally. This depends on Phase 1 baselines.
4. Phase 2 — Frontend refresh-path fixes. Update the real-time and fallback refresh paths so lightweight task updates stay decoupled from the expensive board data query except on manual refresh. Review the interaction between WebSocket updates, fallback polling, auto-refresh, and manual refresh to ensure they use a single coherent policy and do not recreate the prior polling storm. This can proceed in parallel with backend API work once the desired refresh contract is confirmed.
5. Phase 3 — Frontend render optimization. Target low-risk rendering costs in board and chat surfaces: reduce repeated derived-data work in page components and hooks, stabilize props where useful, memoize heavy card/list components when it actually reduces rerenders, and throttle or rationalize hot event listeners such as drag and popover positioning. Keep this phase intentionally low-risk; avoid introducing new dependencies or virtualization in the first pass unless baseline results show large boards still regress after the lighter fixes.
6. Phase 3 — Verification and regression coverage. Extend or adjust unit/integration coverage around backend cache behavior, WebSocket change detection, fallback polling, and frontend board refresh logic. Validate with backend tests, frontend tests, and at least one manual network/profile pass to confirm the target improvements are real rather than inferred. This depends on Phases 2 and 3.
7. Phase 4 — Optional second-wave work. If the first pass still leaves material UI lag on large boards or excessive backend complexity, prepare a follow-on plan for structural changes: board virtualization, deeper service decomposition around GitHub project fetching/polling, bounded cache policies, and stronger instrumentation around request budgets and render timings. This phase is explicitly out of scope for the first implementation unless measurements prove it is necessary.

**Relevant files**
- `solune/specs/022-api-rate-limit-protection/spec.md` — primary acceptance criteria for idle-rate-limit reduction, sub-issue caching, refresh behavior, and cache TTL alignment.
- `solune/backend/src/api/projects.py` — projects tasks endpoints and WebSocket subscription flow; likely location for change-detection verification and refresh semantics.
- `solune/backend/src/api/board.py` — board-data cache behavior, manual refresh semantics, and sub-issue cache invalidation path.
- `solune/backend/src/services/copilot_polling/polling_loop.py` — polling hot path and expensive background work that can still consume rate limit budget.
- `solune/backend/src/services/github_projects/service.py` — board/project fetching path and candidate reuse points for sub-issue caching or batching.
- `solune/backend/src/services/cache.py` — cache TTLs, cache-key helpers, and any bounded-cache improvements if needed.
- `solune/backend/src/utils.py` — shared repository resolution logic to reuse instead of duplicated fallback flows.
- `solune/backend/src/api/workflow.py` — known duplicate repository-resolution path that may add inconsistency and avoidable work.
- `solune/frontend/src/hooks/useRealTimeSync.ts` — current WebSocket/fallback polling behavior; today it still invalidates board data during polling fallback.
- `solune/frontend/src/hooks/useBoardRefresh.ts` — board auto-refresh policy and manual refresh coordination.
- `solune/frontend/src/hooks/useProjectBoard.ts` — board query ownership and invalidation/refetch strategy.
- `solune/frontend/src/components/board/BoardColumn.tsx` — full column list rendering without memoization or virtualization.
- `solune/frontend/src/components/board/IssueCard.tsx` — likely high-frequency rerender unit for board interactions.
- `solune/frontend/src/pages/ProjectsPage.tsx` — render-time sorting/aggregation and board-level derived state.
- `solune/frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPopup.tsx` — hot drag listener path worth throttling.
- `solune/frontend/src/components/agents/AddAgentPopover.tsx` — positioning listeners and update frequency.
- `solune/backend/tests/unit/test_cache.py` — backend cache TTL and stale fallback coverage to extend.
- `solune/backend/tests/unit/test_api_board.py` — board cache and board endpoint behavior to reuse for regression tests.
- `solune/backend/tests/unit/test_copilot_polling.py` — polling behavior and rate-limit-aware logic to reuse.
- `solune/frontend/src/hooks/useRealTimeSync.test.tsx` — refresh invalidation and WebSocket fallback coverage to extend.
- `solune/frontend/src/hooks/useBoardRefresh.test.tsx` — refresh timer and deduplication behavior to reuse.

**Verification**
1. Backend baseline: measure idle API activity for an open board over a fixed interval and compare against Spec 022 targets; confirm no repeated unchanged refreshes are sent.
2. Backend automated checks: run Ruff, Pyright, and the targeted pytest files covering cache, board, projects/WebSocket, and polling behavior.
3. Frontend baseline: profile board load and interaction on a representative project size, inspect network activity for WebSocket, fallback polling, and board query invalidation, and identify repeated rerender sources.
4. Frontend automated checks: run ESLint, type-checking, Vitest coverage for real-time sync and board refresh hooks, and a build check.
5. Manual end-to-end check: verify that WebSocket updates refresh task data quickly, fallback polling remains safe, manual refresh still bypasses caches when intended, and board interactions remain responsive.

**Decisions**
- Selected approach: balanced pass across backend and frontend rather than a single-area optimization.
- Recommended implementation scope for the first pass: low-risk optimizations first, even though the user left the aggressiveness undecided.
- Included scope: measurement, idle API reduction, refresh-path cleanup, low-risk render optimization, and regression coverage.
- Excluded from the first pass unless metrics justify it: board virtualization, major service decomposition, dependency changes, and larger architectural rewrites.
- Baseline measurement is mandatory before code changes so the improvements can be proven and not just assumed.

**Further Considerations**
1. If large boards still feel slow after the low-risk frontend fixes, the next recommended option is virtualization rather than additional scattered memoization.
2. If backend API churn remains high after Spec 022-aligned fixes, the next recommended option is deeper consolidation in the GitHub projects service and polling pipeline rather than more cache-layer patching.
3. If repeated performance work is expected in this repo, add lightweight instrumentation or logging around board refresh cost, sub-issue cache hit rate, and refresh-source attribution so regressions are visible earlier.

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: Optimistic Updates for Mutations
Add optimistic UI updates to the 4 mutations missing them, and fix the paginated cache gap where existing optimistic updates only target flat array caches while the UI has migrated to useInfiniteQuery.

Current State
Already optimistic (but only flat array cache): create/update/delete chore, create/update/delete/start/stop app, delete tool, board drag-and-drop

useCreateAgent — useAgents.ts:63 — no onMutate
useDeleteAgent — useAgents.ts:99 — no onMutate
uploadTool — useTools.ts:49 — no onMutate, no error toast
useCreateProject — useProjects.ts:74 — no onMutate

useCreateAgent — add onMutate: insert placeholder with _optimistic: true into both agentKeys.list(projectId) and paginated cache; add onError rollback
useDeleteAgent — add onMutate: remove agent from both cache structures; add onError rollback
uploadTool — add onMutate: insert placeholder tool; add onError rollback + error toast
useCreateProject — add onMutate: insert placeholder project; add onError rollback

Update useCreateApp, useDeleteApp, useUpdateApp, useStartApp, useStopApp in useApps.ts — extend onMutate to also modify paginated cache key
Update useDeleteTool in useTools.ts — extend onMutate to also modify paginated cache key
Relevant files

New: solune/frontend/src/hooks/queryUtils.ts — shared cache helpers
Modify: useAgents.ts — useCreateAgent, useDeleteAgent
Modify: useTools.ts — uploadTool, useDeleteTool
Modify: useProjects.ts — useCreateProject
Modify: useChores.ts — 4 mutations
Modify: useApps.ts — 5 mutations
Reference: useUndoableDelete.ts — removeEntityFromCache pattern to generalize
Verification

Unit test queryUtils helpers: flat array add/remove/update, InfiniteData add/remove/update, graceful no-op when cache is empty/undefined
Update existing mutation tests to assert both cache keys are modified in onMutate
Manual: create agent → card appears instantly; delete agent → card vanishes instantly, reappears on error
Manual: with paginated view active, delete an item → no flash/stale state before onSettled invalidation
Kill backend, perform a mutation → verify onError properly restores snapshots

Shared queryUtils.ts avoids duplicating InfiniteData logic across 5+ files
Placeholder items use _optimistic: true flag (existing convention)
useUndoableDelete.ts stays untouched — already handles both cache structures

mentioned_issues.title: Plan: ChoresPanel Pagination Migration
mentioned_issues.body:
Plan: ChoresPanel Pagination Migration
The gap is narrower than described — ChoresPanel is the only remaining unpaginated list. Agents, Tools, Apps, Activity, and Board columns all already use cursor-based infinite scroll via useInfiniteList + InfiniteScrollContainer. The infrastructure is fully built; ChoresPanel just hasn't been wired up yet.

The complication: ChoresPanel does client-side filtering (search, status, schedule) and sorting. Switching to paginated data means filtering only the loaded pages, missing items on later pages. This requires moving filters server-side.

Steps

Phase 1: Backend — Add server-side filtering (no dependencies)
Add query parameters status, schedule_type, search, sort, order to GET /chores/{project_id} in chores.py — apply filtering before calling apply_pagination()
Phase 2: Frontend — Wire up paginated hook (steps 3-4 parallel with Phase 1; step 5+ sequential)
Update choresApi.listPaginated() in api.ts to accept optional filter params (status, scheduleType, search, sort, order) and append to query string
Update useChoresListPaginated() in useChores.ts to accept filter/sort params and include them in the query key so changing a filter triggers a fresh fetch (depends on 2)
Switch ChoresPanel.tsx from useChoresList() to useChoresListPaginated() — pass filter state as hook params, remove the client-side filter/sort useMemo, pass hasNextPage/isFetchingNextPage/fetchNextPage to ChoresGrid (depends on 3)
Call resetPagination() when filters change so pagination restarts from page 1 (depends on 4)
Phase 3: Cleanup
Check if useChoresList() and choresApi.list() are used elsewhere — if not, remove the non-paginated variants (depends on 4)
Relevant files

chores.py — add filter query params, apply before apply_pagination()
api.ts — update choresApi.listPaginated() signature
useChores.ts — update useChoresListPaginated() to accept/forward filters
ChoresPanel.tsx — swap hooks, remove client-side filter useMemo, pass pagination props to ChoresGrid
ChoresGrid.tsx — no changes needed (already supports pagination props + InfiniteScrollContainer)
Reference implementations (patterns to follow):

AgentsPanel.tsx — useAgentsListPaginated() + InfiniteScrollContainer wiring
ActivityPage.tsx — working infinite scroll template
Verification

Add pytest tests for GET /chores/{project_id} with filter combos — verify correct items + cursor behavior with active filters
Update vitest tests for useChoresListPaginated with filter params in query key
Manual: load ChoresPanel with 50+ chores — confirm 25 load initially, scrolling loads more, filter changes reset and re-fetch from server
Verify rapid filter toggling doesn't cause issues (search is already debounced via useDeferredValue)
Decisions

Server-side filtering is required — client-side filtering on paginated data would only filter loaded pages
Sorting also moves server-side (client-side sort of partial data is meaningless)
Keep useDeferredValue for search debouncing — the deferred value becomes a query param
Default limit stays at 25 (consistent with all other paginated hooks)

---
