closing_issues.title: [BUG] Normal usage results in rate limiting error.
closing_issues.body: **Describe the bug** While experimenting with features in the UI (sending messages, changing setting values, ...) the rate limiting is getting active. This is not obvious and results in error messages, logging out and showing a connection error message. Clicking on 'Retry Connection' is not successful. The rate limiting is also not obvious in the container logs. (Are there other logs to get this information?) I have tried to get some info about the error situation and tried the health endpoint (http://meshmonitor.lan:3001/api/health). Here i got the message 'Too many requests from this IP, please try again later' **First:** Maybe it is better to configure a rate limit in the default configuration which is not as aggressive, that i can trigger it with normal usage. **Second:** Please show a hint so i can get a info about the cause of this error, maybe in a log or other place visible for an admin. **Third:** The behavior in showing the retry button (connection, see screenshot) in case of a triggered rate limit may lead a user to click more often and trigger the rate limit again.

mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary
Project foundation for jellow-app: Next.js 15 scaffold, CI pipeline, **and** the full design token layer (colors, typography, spacing, shadows) from the Penpot design system.

> Consolidates former #1 (scaffold) + #2 (design tokens).

## Acceptance Criteria

### Scaffold & CI
- [ ] Project structure at `projects/jellow-app/` follows §stack:jellow
- [ ] `pnpm install` succeeds with no errors
- [ ] `pnpm dev` starts development server
- [ ] `pnpm build` completes without errors
- [ ] `pnpm typecheck` passes
- [ ] CI workflow `jellow-copilot-setup-steps.yml` runs on push
- [ ] Basic landing page renders at `/`

### Design Tokens
- [ ] CSS variables defined in `src/app/globals.css` for all Jellow tokens
- [ ] Token map: Primary colors (green/yellow/red verdicts), neutrals, background (#FFFBF0)
- [ ] Typography scale matching iOS HIG (11pt-34pt range)
- [ ] 8pt spacing grid (4px, 8px, 12px, 16px, 20px, 24px, 32px, 40px, 48px)
- [ ] Shadow elevation ladder (4 levels: subtle, card, elevated, modal)
- [ ] `design-tokens.json` exported to `docs/design-tokens.json`
- [ ] Tailwind config extended with Jellow tokens

**Repo:** `abhishek-mittal/jellow-app`
**Path:** `projects/jellow-app/`
**Branch to create:** `feat/jellow-foundation`
**Base branch:** `main`
**Tier:** `atom`
**Blocked By:** None

### §stack:jellow

**Framework:** Next.js 15 App Router
**Pattern:** Pages under `src/app/`; lib utilities in `src/lib/`; components in `src/components/`

**Penpot:** Jellow Design System board
**Penpot Design System ID:** `b8eb142a-1c57-8083-8007-b1852639bf10`
**Design Tokens:** [design-tokens.json](https://github.com/abhishek-mittal/jellow-app/blob/main/src/config/design-tokens.json)

| Token | CSS Variable | Value |

| Background | `--jellow-bg` | `#FFFBF0` |
| Gray 50-900 | `--jellow-gray-*` | Standard neutral scale |

- [ ] No hardcoded secrets or API keys
- [ ] Tokens match Penpot design system exactly
- [ ] ESLint passes
- [ ] TypeScript compiles without errors

mentioned_issues.title: jellow-7: Home Dashboard (+ StatsCard, HealthScoreRing)
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary
Home Dashboard screen — compose shared atoms into the main landing page, **build** StatsCard and HealthScoreRing atoms (unique to this screen cluster), wire mock data, and connect navigation.

> Consolidates former #7 (screen) + #15 (StatsCard) + #16 (HealthScoreRing).

## Acceptance Criteria

### StatsCard component (`src/components/ui/stats-card.tsx`)
- [ ] Props: label (string), value (string or number), icon (ReactNode), trend (up | down | flat), trendValue (string)
- [ ] Rounded card with soft shadow, white background
- [ ] Icon (left) + value (bold, large) + label (muted, small) + optional trend indicator
- [ ] Trend: green arrow up / red arrow down / gray flat
- [ ] Uses design tokens for colors, spacing, radii
- [ ] Pure component: props in, JSX out, no side effects
- [ ] Unit test at `tests/components/stats-card.test.tsx`
- [ ] **Exported** — also used by #10 (Rewards)

### HealthScoreRing component (`src/components/ui/health-score-ring.tsx`)
- [ ] Props: score (number 0-10), size (sm | md | lg), showLabel (boolean), verdict (good | moderate | bad)
- [ ] SVG circle with animated stroke-dasharray progress
- [ ] Color: green (7-10), yellow (4-6.9), red (0-3.9) — from design tokens
- [ ] Center: score number (bold) + optional label text below
- [ ] Sizes: sm (48px), md (80px), lg (120px)
- [ ] Smooth animation on mount (CSS transition or framer-motion)

mentioned_issues.title: [P1] dispatch_batch/3 misattributes :task_exit error index when ordered: false
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary
While reviewing #77 (head `3997911a8a0e0c62d95b89b42cafd725a07c38b6`), `Dispatch.dispatch_batch/3` can associate `{:exit, reason}` results with the wrong original config index when streaming with `ordered: false`.

## Evidence
- `lib/jido_signal/dispatch.ex` uses `ordered: false` in `Task.Supervisor.async_stream/5`.
- The next step zips `stream_results` against the original input list.
- The `{:exit, reason}` branch uses the zipped `original_idx`, which may not belong to the exited task.

Code reference:
- https://github.com/agentjido/jido_signal/blob/3997911a8a0e0c62d95b89b42cafd725a07c38b6/lib/jido_signal/dispatch.ex#L438-L467

## Impact
Error tuples can point to the wrong dispatch target, making retries, telemetry, and debugging unreliable under concurrency or timeout pressure.

## Expected Behavior
Each dispatch result (including task exits/timeouts) should be reported with the index of the config that actually produced that result.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `dispatch_batch/3` returns `{:error, {idx, {:task_exit, reason}}}` with the correct original config index.
2. Index mapping remains correct under out-of-order completion.
3. Existing success-path behavior remains unchanged.

## Required Tests
1. Regression test with mixed fast/slow adapters where at least one task exits or times out.
2. Assertion that returned `idx` matches the failing config position.
3. Deterministic synchronization or repeated runs to cover nondeterministic completion order.

## Context
- Found during #76 / #77 review.

mentioned_issues.title: [P1] Stream.filter correlation filtering is broken for standard %Jido.Signal{} entries
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary
`Bus.Stream.filter/4` in PR #77 head uses `signal.correlation_id` for correlation filtering, which is not a standard field on `%Jido.Signal{}`. This can raise and fall into the rescue path, returning `{:error, :filter_failed}` for valid inputs.

## Evidence
- Current code path checks correlation with `signal.correlation_id == correlation_id`.
- `%Jido.Signal{}` correlation context is carried via extensions, not a direct `correlation_id` field.
- `origin/main` previously used extension-based extraction (`correlation_id_for/1`) in this path.

Code references:
- Current: https://github.com/agentjido/jido_signal/blob/3997911a8a0e0c62d95b89b42cafd725a07c38b6/lib/jido_signal/bus/bus_stream.ex#L27-L107
- Prior baseline (`origin/main`): https://github.com/agentjido/jido_signal/blob/main/lib/jido_signal/bus/bus_stream.ex

## Impact
Replay and snapshot flows that rely on `correlation_id` filtering can fail unexpectedly or produce incorrect filtering behavior for standard signals.

## Expected Behavior
`correlation_id` filtering should work for normal `%Jido.Signal{}` entries by reading canonical correlation metadata from signal extensions (with explicit fallback policy).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Correlation filtering is extension-based and does not crash on standard signal structs.
2. `Stream.filter/4` returns filtered results (not `{:error, :filter_failed}`) for valid correlation metadata.
3. Behavior is documented for missing/invalid correlation metadata.

## Required Tests
1. Regression test for `correlation_id` filtering using signals with correlation metadata in extensions.
2. Negative test where correlation metadata is missing (explicitly defined expected result).
3. Snapshot/replay coverage confirming correlation filter parity.

## Context
- Found during #76 / #77 review.

mentioned_issues.title: [P2] SnapshotStore fallback lookup/delete can cross bus boundaries
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary
`SnapshotStore` fallback behavior can cross bus boundaries when exact `{jido, bus_name, snapshot_id}` lookup misses and code falls back to lookup/delete by `snapshot_id` across any bus in the same `jido` scope.

## Evidence
- `handle_call({:get, key}, ...)` falls back to `lookup_by_snapshot_id/2` on exact-key miss.
- `lookup_by_snapshot_id/2` matches `{{jido, :_, snapshot_id}, :_}`.
- `handle_call({:delete, key}, ...)` similarly falls back to `delete_by_snapshot_id/2`.

Code reference:
- https://github.com/agentjido/jido_signal/blob/3997911a8a0e0c62d95b89b42cafd725a07c38b6/lib/jido_signal/bus/snapshot_store.ex#L67-L126

## Impact
A stale/mismatched bus-scoped key can read/delete snapshot payloads belonging to another bus, which violates isolation expectations and creates data integrity risk.

## Expected Behavior
Snapshot read/delete should be strictly scoped to the provided `{jido, bus_name, snapshot_id}` key unless explicitly opting into cross-bus lookup semantics via a separate API.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `get` and `delete` paths are strict to bus scope by default.
2. No cross-bus payload access/deletion occurs from stale/mismatched keys.
3. Any opt-in cross-bus lookup is explicit and separately documented.

## Required Tests
1. Multi-bus test with identical `snapshot_id` values proving read isolation.
2. Multi-bus test proving delete isolation under stale key input.
3. Optional explicit-lookup test if a separate API is introduced.

## Context
- Found during #76 / #77 review.

mentioned_issues.title: [P2] RecordedSignal.serialize/1 contract changed but docs still advertise binary return
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary
`RecordedSignal.serialize/1` now returns `{:ok, binary()} | {:error, Error.t()}`, but module docs/examples still describe and demonstrate a direct `binary()` return.

## Evidence
- Docs/examples show:
  - `json = ...serialize(recorded)`
  - `is_binary(json) == true`
- Spec now declares tuple return:
  - `@spec serialize(...) :: {:ok, binary()} | {:error, Error.t()}`

Code reference:
- https://github.com/agentjido/jido_signal/blob/3997911a8a0e0c62d95b89b42cafd725a07c38b6/lib/jido_signal/bus/recorded_signal.ex#L35-L80

## Impact
This is a migration/compatibility hazard for callers and documentation consumers. Existing integrations that assumed direct binary return may break silently or mis-handle return values.

## Expected Behavior
Either:
1. Restore legacy binary-return behavior for `serialize/1`, or
2. Keep tuple return and provide clear migration guidance (`serialize!/1` vs safe tuple API), with docs/tests updated accordingly.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Public docs/examples exactly match implemented return contract.
2. Changelog/release notes include explicit migration guidance.
3. Compatibility behavior is covered by tests.

## Required Tests
1. Serialization contract tests for successful tuple return and error return path.
2. Tests/examples aligned with docs for both `serialize/1` and `serialize!/1`.
3. Backward-compatibility expectations are explicitly asserted.

## Context
- Found during #76 / #77 review.

mentioned_issues.title: [P2] Unknown persistent ack identifiers are silently treated as success
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary
Persistent ack handling treats unknown ack identifiers as `{:ok, :noop}` and the public `Bus.ack/3` path still returns `:ok`. This can hide invalid/mistyped ack IDs from callers.

## Evidence
- `do_ack/2` returns success on `{:ok, :noop}`.
- `resolve_unknown_ack/1` maps unknown binary/non-negative integer IDs to `{:ok, :noop}`.
- Public API contract remains `@spec ack(...) :: :ok | {:error, term()}`.

Code references:
- https://github.com/agentjido/jido_signal/blob/3997911a8a0e0c62d95b89b42cafd725a07c38b6/lib/jido_signal/bus/persistent_subscription.ex#L630-L635
- https://github.com/agentjido/jido_signal/blob/3997911a8a0e0c62d95b89b42cafd725a07c38b6/lib/jido_signal/bus/persistent_subscription.ex#L722-L729
- https://github.com/agentjido/jido_signal/blob/3997911a8a0e0c62d95b89b42cafd725a07c38b6/lib/jido_signal/bus.ex#L623-L626

## Impact
Client bugs and ID mismatches can be silently ignored, making ack reliability difficult to reason about and reducing observability of data-loss conditions.

## Expected Behavior
Unknown ack identifiers should return explicit errors by default, or best-effort noop should be an explicit mode with telemetry and clear documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Unknown ack IDs are not silently acknowledged in default mode.
2. If noop behavior is retained, it is opt-in and emits telemetry.
3. API docs clearly define ack behavior for valid, unknown, and malformed IDs.

## Required Tests
1. Ack behavior for valid log ID.
2. Ack behavior for unknown ID (default failure path).
3. Ack behavior for malformed ID.
4. Mixed batch ack input coverage.

## Context
- Found during #76 / #77 review.

closing_issues.title: CLI-002: Watch Mode for Development
closing_issues.body:
## Summary
Add `--watch` flag to CLI commands for continuous validation and formatting during development.

## Problem
No watch mode - developers must manually re-run commands after each file change.

## Action Items
1. Add file watcher library: `fsnotify`
2. Implement watch mode for all commands:
   ```bash
   gosqlx format --watch src/**/*.sql
   gosqlx validate --watch queries/
   gosqlx lint --watch migrations/
   ```

3. Features:
   - Debounce file changes (500ms)
   - Show change notifications
   - Handle errors gracefully (don't exit)
   - Clear screen between runs (optional)
   - Color-coded output (green/red)

4. Test on macOS, Linux, Windows
5. Handle Ctrl+C gracefully

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Watch mode works on macOS, Linux, Windows
- [ ] Debouncing prevents rapid re-runs (500ms)
- [ ] Clear status output with timestamps
- [ ] Ctrl+C exits gracefully
- [ ] File system events handled correctly

## Technical Details
**Priority**: Medium  
**Effort**: Small (8h)  
**Phase**: Phase 3 - UX & Documentation  
**Dependencies**: None

## Example Output
```
[14:23:45] Watching for changes in src/**/*.sql
[14:23:52] ✓ query.sql - Valid
[14:24:15] ✗ complex.sql - Line 5: unexpected token
[14:24:20] ✓ complex.sql - Valid
```

closing_issues.title: CLI-003: Stdin/Stdout Pipeline Support
closing_issues.body:
## Summary
Add full stdin/stdout support for Unix pipeline composition.

## Problem
Stdin/stdout not fully implemented - can't use GoSQLX in Unix pipelines.

## Action Items
1. Full stdin support:
   ```bash
   cat query.sql | gosqlx format
   echo "SELECT * FROM users" | gosqlx validate
   ```

2. Pipeline composition:
   ```bash
   gosqlx format query.sql | gosqlx validate
   cat *.sql | gosqlx format | gosqlx validate
   ```

3. Auto-detect input source (pipe vs file vs arg)
4. Add explicit `--stdin` flag for clarity
5. Proper exit codes (0 = success, 1 = error)
6. Handle binary output for --format json

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Stdin/stdout work correctly in all commands
- [ ] Pipelines compose properly
- [ ] Exit codes correct (0 for success)
- [ ] Auto-detection works (pipe vs file)
- [ ] Examples in CLI documentation

## Technical Details
**Priority**: Medium  
**Effort**: Small (4h)  
**Phase**: Phase 3 - UX & Documentation  
**Dependencies**: None

## Example Usage
```bash
# Format from stdin
echo "SELECT * FROM users" | gosqlx format

# Chain commands
cat queries/*.sql | gosqlx format | gosqlx validate

# Use in scripts
if gosqlx validate < query.sql; then
    echo "Valid SQL"
fi
```

closing_issues.title: FEAT-007: Multi-Column USING Clause in JOINs
closing_issues.body:
## Summary
Extend USING clause to support multiple columns - currently limited to single column.

## Problem
**Current**: `JOIN table USING (col1)`  
**Needed**: `JOIN table USING (col1, col2, col3)`

This is SQL-92 standard but not implemented.

## Action Items
1. Update parser to handle column list in USING clause
2. Modify AST to store list of columns instead of single column
3. Add tests for 1-10 columns in USING clause
4. Update documentation with examples
5. Ensure backward compatibility with single-column USING

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Multi-column USING works correctly
- [ ] Tests cover 1-10 columns
- [ ] SQL-92 compliance improved
- [ ] Backward compatible with existing single-column usage
- [ ] Documentation updated

## Technical Details
**Priority**: Medium  
**Effort**: Small (8h)  
**Phase**: Phase 4 - Feature Development  
**Dependencies**: None

## Example SQL
```sql
-- Current (works)
SELECT * FROM users u
JOIN profiles p USING (user_id);

-- Needed (doesn't work yet)
SELECT * FROM orders o
JOIN shipments s USING (order_id, warehouse_id);
```

closing_issues.title: CLI-007: Output Format Options
closing_issues.body:
## Summary
Add multiple output format options for better CI/IDE integration.

## Problem
Limited output formats - only human-readable text, no machine-readable or CI-friendly formats.

## Action Items
1. Add `--format` flag with options:
   - `text` - human-readable (default)
   - `json` - machine-readable, structured
   - `yaml` - human-friendly structured
   - `junit` - CI integration (JUnit XML)
   - `checkstyle` - IDE integration (Checkstyle XML)

2. Apply to all commands (validate, format, analyze, lint)

3. Document JSON/YAML schemas:
   ```json
   {
     "status": "error",
     "errors": [{
       "file": "query.sql",
       "line": 3,
       "column": 15,
       "message": "unexpected token",
       "code": "E001"
     }]
   }
   ```

4. Add examples for CI/IDE integration

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 5 output formats implemented
- [ ] JSON schema documented
- [ ] YAML schema documented
- [ ] CI integration examples (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI)
- [ ] IDE integration examples (VSCode problem matcher)
- [ ] Tests for all formats

Add collector to track how often apps are switched during the day.

**Output:**
- Total app switches
- Average time between switches
- Switches per hour

**Example:** "You switched apps 127 times (avg every 3.5 min)"

This helps identify context fragmentation and distraction patterns.

**Implementation notes:**

- Calculate deltas between app focus changes
- Add to main output and quiet mode

closing_issues.title: Calculate context fragmentation score
closing_issues.body:
Combined metric to measure how fragmented your work context is throughout the day.

**Inputs:**
- Number of unique apps used
- Tab switches across browsers
- Unique domains visited
- App switches per hour

**Output:** 0-100 score where:
- 0-30 = Focused 🎯
- 31-60 = Moderate ⚖️
- 61-100 = Fragmented 🔀

**Example:** "Context fragmentation: 67/100 (fragmented)"

**Implementation notes:**
- Weighted algorithm combining multiple factors
- Thresholds should be configurable
- Display in summary section with emoji indicator

- Total notifications today

closing_issues.title: Track screen lock/unlock events
closing_issues.body:
Count how many times the screen was locked/unlocked today by parsing pmset logs or screen on/off events.

**Output:**
- Total lock/unlock count
- Average time between locks (break frequency)

- Security consciousness

- Or track screen on/off transitions
- Filter out very short locks (<1 min)

closing_issues.title: Add browser history analysis for visited URLs
closing_issues.body:
Extend browser tab collector to also parse browser history databases for today's browsing activity.

**Features:**
- Track all URLs visited today (not just open tabs)
- Identify issue/ticket URLs (Jira, GitHub, Linear, etc.)
- Domain visit frequency
- Most-visited pages

**Privacy model:**
- Only today's data (respects privacy-first approach)
- Never stored
- All processing local
- No external calls

**Supported browsers:**
- Chrome: `~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default/History`
- Safari: `~/Library/Safari/History.db`
- Edge: `~/Library/Application Support/Microsoft Edge/Default/History`

**Output example:**
```
📊 Browser Activity:
  • 147 URLs visited
  • Top: github.com (34 visits)
  • Issues viewed: PROJ-123, PROJ-456, github.com/org/repo/issues/89
```

closing_issues.title: Categorize domains as work/distraction/neutral
closing_issues.body:
Add configurable domain categorization with sensible defaults to calculate work/distraction ratio.

**Default work domains:**
- github.com, gitlab.com, bitbucket.org
- stackoverflow.com, stackexchange.com
- docs.*, developer.*, api.*
- atlassian.net (Jira, Confluence)
- linear.app, asana.com, notion.so
- aws.amazon.com, console.cloud.google.com, portal.azure.com

**Default distraction domains:**
- twitter.com, x.com, reddit.com
- facebook.com, instagram.com
- youtube.com (non-work content)
- tiktok.com, twitch.tv
- news sites (optional)

**Configuration override:**
```yaml
domains:
  work:
    - mycompany.atlassian.net
    - internal.company.com
  distraction:
    - news.ycombinator.com  # personal preference
  neutral:
    - gmail.com  # could be work or personal
```

**Output:**
```
📊 Domain breakdown:
  • Work: 147 visits (78%)
  • Distraction: 23 visits (12%)
  • Neutral: 19 visits (10%)
```

closing_issues.title: Detect and track issue/ticket URLs from browser history
closing_issues.body:
Parse browser history for common issue tracker patterns to show what issues/tickets were worked on today.

**Supported patterns:**
- **GitHub:** `github.com/{org}/{repo}/issues/{number}`
- **Jira:** `*.atlassian.net/browse/{KEY-123}`
- **Linear:** `linear.app/issue/{id}`
- **GitLab:** `gitlab.com/{org}/{repo}/-/issues/{number}`
- **Azure DevOps:** `dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_workitems/edit/{id}`

**Output:**
```
🎫 Issues/Tickets viewed today:
  • PROJ-123 (Jira, 8 visits)
  • github.com/org/repo/issues/456 (5 visits)
  • linear.app/issue/ABC-789 (3 visits)
```

**Use case:**
Helps answer "What did I work on today?" by showing which tickets/issues you actually looked at.

**Implementation notes:**
- Regex patterns for each tracker type
- Group by issue ID, count visits
- Sort by visit frequency
- Link to existing browser history collector

closing_issues.title: Add smart burnout warning heuristics
closing_issues.body: Detect burnout: >10h days, >50 app switches/hour, >100 tabs, midnight work, no breaks 4h+. Show subtle warnings.

closing_issues.title: Detect and warn about context overload
closing_issues.body:
Alert when too many contexts are active simultaneously.

**Triggers:**
- >5 apps actively used (not just open)
- >30 browser tabs open
- >10 unique domains visited in last hour

**Example output:**
"⚠️ Context overload: 7 apps + 45 tabs active"

**Implementation:** Simple threshold checks, display warning in output.

closing_issues.title: Add --accessible flag for color-blind friendly output
closing_issues.body:
Add accessibility mode for color-blind users and high contrast needs.

**Features:**
- Use patterns/symbols instead of relying on colors
- High contrast output
- No color-only information conveyed
- Configurable via flag and config file

**Config:**
```yaml
accessibility:
  enabled: true
  high_contrast: true
  no_emoji: false
```

**Usage:** `rekap --accessible`

**Implementation:** Modify UI renderer to support alternate style mode.

closing_issues.title: Add custom themes support
closing_issues.body:
## Description
Allow users to create and share custom color themes for rekap output.

## Features
- Define themes in config file or separate theme files
- Built-in themes (default, minimal, hacker, pastel, etc.)
- Community theme sharing
- Preview themes with demo mode

## Theme Format
```yaml
# ~/.config/rekap/themes/ocean.yaml
name: "Ocean"
author: "username"
colors:
  primary: "#0077be"
  secondary: "#00a8e8"
  accent: "#00c9ff"
  success: "#00ffa3"
  error: "#ff6b6b"
  muted: "#6c757d"
  text: "#ffffff"
```

## Usage
```bash
rekap --theme ocean
rekap --theme ~/.config/rekap/themes/custom.yaml
rekap demo --theme minimal
```

## Built-in Themes Ideas
- **default** - Current magenta/cyan theme
- **minimal** - Grayscale with minimal color
- **hacker** - Matrix-style green
- **pastel** - Soft, muted colors
- **nord** - Nord color scheme
- **dracula** - Dracula theme
- **solarized** - Solarized dark/light

## Labels
enhancement, ui, good first issue

closing_issues.title: Add Claude-powered issue analyzer workflow
closing_issues.body:
## Summary

Integrate GitHub Actions workflow that automatically analyzes new issues using Claude API and provides helpful comments.

## Feature

When a new issue is created:
1. Claude API analyzes the issue content
2. Automatically classifies as Bug / Feature / Question
3. Posts a summary and suggested approach as a comment
4. Optionally applies labels

## Analysis Output

| Item | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Classification** | 🐛 Bug / ✨ Feature / ❓ Question |
| **Summary** | 2-3 sentence summary of the issue |
| **Suggested Approach** | Concrete steps to address the issue |

## Implementation

### Files to Add

\`\`\`
.github/
├── workflows/
│   └── issue-analyzer.yml
└── scripts/
    └── analyze_issue.py
\`\`\`

### Requirements

- [ ] Add \`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\` to repository secrets
- [ ] Create labels: bug, enhancement, question
- [ ] Add workflow and script files

## Reference

Based on the issue-analyzer template at \`temp/issue-analyzer/\`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Workflow triggers on issue creation
- [ ] Claude API analyzes issue content
- [ ] Analysis comment is posted within 2 minutes
- [ ] Labels are applied based on classification

closing_issues.title: Integrate CodeRabbit for automated PR reviews
closing_issues.body:
## Summary

Integrate [CodeRabbit](https://coderabbit.ai/) for AI-powered automated code reviews on pull requests.

## What is CodeRabbit?

CodeRabbit is an AI code reviewer that:
- Automatically reviews PRs with detailed feedback
- Identifies bugs, security issues, and code quality problems
- Provides actionable suggestions
- Learns from codebase patterns over time

## Benefits

| Benefit | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Consistent Reviews** | Every PR gets thorough, consistent review |
| **Faster Feedback** | Immediate feedback without waiting for human reviewers |
| **Security Focus** | Catches potential security vulnerabilities |
| **Code Quality** | Enforces best practices and coding standards |

## Implementation

### Option A: GitHub App (Recommended)

1. Install CodeRabbit GitHub App from marketplace
2. Configure \`.coderabbit.yaml\` for project-specific settings
3. Done - it will auto-review PRs

### Option B: GitHub Actions

1. Add CodeRabbit action to workflow
2. Configure API key
3. Set up review triggers

## Configuration

Create \`.coderabbit.yaml\`:

\`\`\`yaml
# CodeRabbit configuration
language: "en"
early_access: false
reviews:
  profile: "assertive"
  request_changes_workflow: true
  high_level_summary: true
  poem: true
  auto_title_placeholder: "[WIP]"
chat:
  auto_reply: true
\`\`\`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] CodeRabbit installed and configured
- [ ] Test PR reviewed successfully
- [ ] Configuration tuned for project needs

## References

- [CodeRabbit Documentation](https://docs.coderabbit.ai/)
- [GitHub Marketplace](https://github.com/marketplace/coderabbit)

closing_issues.title: Add documentation validator workflow (DOCS_VALIDATOR)
closing_issues.body:
## Summary

Add a GitHub Actions workflow that uses Claude API to validate that documentation (README, CONTRIBUTING, etc.) matches the actual implementation.

## Background

Documentation can easily drift from implementation:
- Agent/skill counts in README may not match actual counts
- CLI command documentation may be outdated
- Feature descriptions may not reflect current behavior

## Proposal

### Workflow: `.github/workflows/docs-validator.yml`

**Triggers:**
- Push to develop (when docs or src change)
- Weekly schedule
- Manual dispatch

**Process:**
1. Collect current implementation stats (agent count, skill count, CLI commands)
2. Extract documentation claims from README.md, README_ko.md
3. Send both to Claude API for comparison
4. Report discrepancies as PR comment or issue

### Script: `.github/scripts/validate_docs.py`

Validates:
| Check | Source | Documentation |
|-------|--------|---------------|
| Agent count | \`templates/.claude/agents/*.md\` | README "34 agents" |
| Skill count | \`templates/.claude/skills/*/\` | README "42 skills" |
| Rule count | \`templates/.claude/rules/*.md\` | README "18 rules" |
| CLI commands | \`src/cli/*.ts\` exports | README CLI table |
| Slash commands | \`templates/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md\` | README commands table |

### Secret Required

- \`DOCS_VALIDATOR\` - Anthropic API key (already configured)

### Prompt Design

The Claude prompt should:
1. Receive implementation facts (counts, command names)
2. Receive documentation excerpts
3. Compare and identify discrepancies
4. Output structured report

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Workflow triggers on relevant file changes
- [ ] Script collects implementation stats accurately
- [ ] Claude API compares docs vs implementation
- [ ] Clear report of discrepancies
- [ ] Non-blocking (warning only, not failing CI)

closing_issues.title: Add automated release notes workflow (RELEASE_BOT)
closing_issues.body:
## Summary

Add a GitHub Actions workflow that uses Claude API to automatically generate release notes and manage release workflows.

## Background

Manual release note writing is:
- Time-consuming
- Inconsistent in format and detail
- Prone to missing important changes

## Proposal

### Workflow: `.github/workflows/release-notes.yml`

**Triggers:**
- When a release branch is created (`release/*`)
- When a tag is pushed (`v*`)
- Manual dispatch for draft releases

**Process:**
1. Collect commits since last release tag
2. Categorize changes (feat, fix, docs, chore, etc.)
3. Send to Claude API for release note generation
4. Create/update GitHub Release draft
5. Optionally trigger npm publish

### Script: `.github/scripts/generate_release_notes.py`

**Input:**
- Commit messages since last tag
- PR titles and descriptions (if available)
- Changed files summary

**Output (Claude generates):**
- Release title suggestion
- Categorized changelog:
  - ✨ New Features
  - 🐛 Bug Fixes
  - 📚 Documentation
  - 🔧 Maintenance
- Breaking changes warning (if any)
- Upgrade instructions (if needed)
- Contributors list

### Secret Required

- \`RELEASE_BOT\` - Anthropic API key (already configured)

### Prompt Design

The Claude prompt should:
1. Receive structured commit/PR data
2. Understand semantic versioning context
3. Generate user-friendly release notes
4. Highlight breaking changes prominently
5. Follow conventional changelog format

### Integration with Git Workflow

```
develop
  │
  └── release/x.y.z (trigger: branch created)
        │
        ├── Claude generates release notes draft
        │
        └── tag vx.y.z (trigger: tag pushed)
              │
              ├── Create GitHub Release with notes
              └── Trigger npm publish
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Workflow triggers on release branch/tag
- [ ] Script collects commit history accurately
- [ ] Claude generates well-formatted release notes
- [ ] GitHub Release draft is created/updated
- [ ] Breaking changes are clearly highlighted
- [ ] Works with existing Git branching strategy

## Example Output

```markdown
# v0.3.0

## ✨ New Features
- Add Claude-powered issue analyzer (#13)
- Add GitHub Wiki with auto-sync (#11)

## 🐛 Bug Fixes
- Fix wiki push permission issue

## 📚 Documentation
- Add comprehensive Git branching strategy (#12)

## 🔧 Maintenance
- Update CodeRabbit configuration (#14)

---
**Full Changelog**: v0.2.0...v0.3.0
```

closing_issues.title: feat: parent-child workflow architecture (baekgom-agents → oh-my-customcode dependency)
closing_issues.body:
## Overview

Establish oh-my-customcode as the **parent** that provides reusable CI/CD workflows, and baekgom-agents as a **child** that depends on them. This pattern should be easily replicable for future child projects.

## Current State

### baekgom-agents workflows (to migrate)
| Workflow | Trigger | Purpose | API Key |
|----------|---------|---------|---------|
| `claude-native-check.yml` | Weekly (Mon 09:00 KST) | Check Claude docs changes, create issue | None |
| `claude-native-verification.yml` | Daily (04:00 KST) | Verify agent compliance with Claude docs | `BAEKGOM_AGENTS` |
| `issue-analyzer.yml` | On issue opened | Analyze issues with Claude API | `BAEKGOM_AGENTS` |
| `daily-issue-report.yml` | Daily (09:00 KST) | Email report of open issues | `OMCUSTOM_MASTER` + `GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD` |

### baekgom-agents TS scripts (to migrate)
| Script | Lines | Dependencies |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| `src/scripts/verify-claude-native.ts` | 705 | @anthropic-ai/sdk, js-yaml |
| `src/scripts/analyze-issue.ts` | 345 | @anthropic-ai/sdk |
| `src/scripts/send-report.ts` | 272 | nodemailer |

### oh-my-customcode Python scripts (to convert to TS)
| Script | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `.github/scripts/analyze_issue.py` | Issue analysis (duplicate of baekgom-agents version) |
| `.github/scripts/generate_release_notes.py` | Release notes generation |
| `.github/scripts/validate_docs.py` | Documentation validation |

## Proposed Architecture

### Phase 1: Centralize Scripts in oh-my-customcode
- Convert 3 Python scripts to TS/Bun
- Move 3 baekgom-agents TS scripts to oh-my-customcode
- Merge `claude-native-check` + `claude-native-verification` into one unified workflow/script

### Phase 2: Create Reusable Workflows
oh-my-customcode provides reusable workflows that any child project can call:

```yaml
# oh-my-customcode/.github/workflows/reusable-issue-analyzer.yml
on:
  workflow_call:
    secrets:
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:
        required: true

# baekgom-agents/.github/workflows/issue-analyzer.yml  
jobs:
  analyze:
    uses: baekenough/oh-my-customcode/.github/workflows/reusable-issue-analyzer.yml@develop
    secrets:
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.BAEKGOM_AGENTS }}
```

### Phase 3: Simplify baekgom-agents
- Replace 4 local workflows with thin callers to oh-my-customcode
- Remove `src/scripts/*.ts`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, `js-yaml`, `nodemailer` dependencies
- Keep only `bun test` for structural validation

## Key Design Decisions

1. **Reusable workflows** (not composite actions) - simpler, full job control
2. **`secrets: inherit` or explicit** - TBD based on security needs
3. **Versioning**: callers reference `@develop` or `@v1.0.0` tag
4. **`workflow_call` can coexist with `schedule`/`issues`** triggers in same file

## Benefits

- Single source of truth for CI/CD automation scripts
- Easy to add new child projects (just create thin caller workflows)
- Centralized Claude API version management
- Reduced maintenance burden on child repos

## Scope

- [ ] Convert oh-my-customcode Python scripts to TS
- [ ] Merge claude-native-check + verification
- [ ] Create reusable workflows (issue-analyzer, claude-native, daily-report)
- [ ] Migrate baekgom-agents to use reusable workflows
- [ ] Clean up baekgom-agents (remove scripts, simplify package.json)
- [ ] Document the parent-child pattern for future projects

closing_issues.title: feat: Add rule to leverage Agent Teams when locally enabled
closing_issues.body:
## Summary

When the user's local machine has Claude Code Agent Teams feature enabled (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`), the harness should actively leverage this capability for complex collaborative tasks instead of only relying on the traditional Task tool approach.

## Background

- Claude Code (Opus 4.6) introduced native Agent Teams as an experimental feature
- Agent Teams provide peer-to-peer messaging, shared task lists, and collaborative workflows
- Currently, baekgom-agents (and by extension oh-my-customcode) treats Agent Teams as "research preview" and defaults to the Task tool + routing skills approach
- The Task tool approach remains the stable default, but when Agent Teams is available, it can provide superior coordination for certain task types

## Proposed Changes

1. **New Rule**: Add a SHOULD-level rule (e.g., `SHOULD-agent-teams.md`) that:
   - Detects if `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS` is enabled
   - When enabled, actively uses Agent Teams for tasks that benefit from:
     - Multi-agent collaboration with inter-agent communication
     - Shared state management across agents
     - Complex research/review/debugging tasks requiring coordination
   - Falls back to Task tool approach when Agent Teams is not available
   
2. **Update existing rules**:
   - `MUST-orchestrator-coordination.md` (R010): Add Agent Teams as a first-class coordination option when enabled
   - `MUST-parallel-execution.md` (R009): Document when Agent Teams is preferred over parallel Task spawning
   
3. **CLAUDE.md template updates**:
   - Add Agent Teams section with detection and activation guidance
   - Update the Experimental Features section to reflect active usage (not just evaluation)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New SHOULD-level rule for Agent Teams adoption
- [ ] R010 updated with Agent Teams coordination path
- [ ] R009 updated with Agent Teams parallel execution guidance  
- [ ] CLAUDE.md.en and CLAUDE.md.ko templates updated
- [ ] Detection mechanism for `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS` documented
- [ ] Clear guidelines on when to use Agent Teams vs Task tool

## Decision Matrix

| Scenario | Task Tool | Agent Teams |
|----------|-----------|-------------|
| Simple independent subtasks | Preferred | Overkill |
| Multi-step with shared state | Possible | Preferred |
| Research requiring agent discussion | Limited | Preferred |
| Cost-sensitive batch operations | Preferred | Higher cost |
| Complex debugging across modules | Limited | Preferred |

## Notes

- Agent Teams is still experimental - the rule should gracefully handle feature removal
- The Task tool approach must remain the stable fallback
- Sync this change back to baekgom-agents after implementation

closing_issues.title: feat: Add project migration/update command for initialized projects
closing_issues.body:
## Summary

Projects initialized with `omcc init` at an older version have no way to update their `.claude/` configuration to match newer oh-my-customcode templates. We need a migration command that safely updates existing projects.

## Problem

When a user runs `omcc init` on a project, it scaffolds `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.claude/rules/`, and `guides/` from the current template version. Over time, oh-my-customcode evolves with:
- New agents added
- Existing agent definitions updated (new fields, improved descriptions)
- New skills and rules
- Updated guides with latest best practices

Currently there is no way to bring an already-initialized project up to date. Users must manually diff and merge changes.

## Proposed Solution

### `omcc update` command

```bash
# Update all templates to latest version
omcc update

# Dry-run to preview changes
omcc update --dry-run

# Update only specific categories
omcc update --agents
omcc update --skills
omcc update --rules
omcc update --guides

# Update from a specific version
omcc update --from v0.2.0
```

### Behavior

1. **Version tracking**: Store the installed template version in `.claude/.omcc-version` (or similar)
2. **Diff detection**: Compare current files against the template version they were installed from
3. **Safe merge strategy**:
   - **New files**: Add automatically
   - **Deleted templates**: Warn but don't remove (user may have customized)
   - **Modified templates**: Show diff and ask user to confirm (interactive merge)
   - **User-customized files**: Detect local modifications and skip or offer 3-way merge
4. **Rollback**: Create backup before update, allow `omcc update --rollback`

### Version File (`.claude/.omcc-version`)

```json
{
  "version": "0.3.2",
  "installedAt": "2026-02-05T10:30:00Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-02-10T14:00:00Z",
  "customized": [
    ".claude/agents/custom-agent.md",
    ".claude/rules/MUST-custom-rule.md"
  ]
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `omcc update` detects version differences between installed and latest templates
- [ ] New template files are added to the project
- [ ] Modified template files show diffs and allow user confirmation
- [ ] User-customized files are preserved (not overwritten without consent)
- [ ] `--dry-run` flag shows what would change without modifying files
- [ ] Version tracking file is maintained
- [ ] Integration tests cover update scenarios

## Labels

enhancement, feature-request

closing_issues.title: fix: entry-merger false positive on markers inside fenced code blocks
closing_issues.body:
## Problem

The `parseEntryDoc()` function in `entry-merger.ts` treats `<!-- omcustom:start -->` and `<!-- omcustom:end -->` markers as section boundaries regardless of context. If these markers appear inside fenced code blocks (e.g., in documentation examples), they will be incorrectly parsed as real section markers.

## Example

```markdown
# My Documentation

<!-- omcustom:start -->
Real managed section
<!-- omcustom:end -->

## Examples

\`\`\`markdown
<!-- omcustom:start -->
This is an example of markers, not a real section
<!-- omcustom:end -->
\`\`\`
```

The parser would incorrectly find 2 managed sections instead of 1.

## Proposed Solution

Track fenced code block state (` \`\`\` `) during line scanning and skip marker detection inside code blocks.

## Impact

Low — this edge case only occurs when users document omcustom marker syntax inside their CLAUDE.md file. Unlikely in practice but should be handled for correctness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Markers inside fenced code blocks are ignored
- [ ] Markers inside inline code are ignored
- [ ] All existing entry-merger tests pass
- [ ] New tests cover code block edge case

closing_issues.title: perf: reduce redundant loadConfig() calls in list and updater modules
closing_issues.body:
## Problem

`loadConfig()` is called redundantly in multiple places:

- **list.ts**: Each getter (`getAgents`, `getSkills`, `getGuides`, `getRules`) calls `loadConfig()` independently. When `listCommand` calls all 4 in parallel via `handleListAll`, this results in 4 separate file reads of `.omcustomrc.json`.
- **updater.ts**: `updateComponent()` calls `loadConfig()` on every invocation (once per component). With 6 components, this means 6 redundant reads plus 1 in `update()` itself = 7 total.

## Proposed Solution

- **list.ts**: Load config once in `handleListAll` and pass it down to each getter function as an optional parameter.
- **updater.ts**: Load config once in `update()` and pass it to `updateComponent()`.

## Impact

Performance improvement only. No functional change. Each `loadConfig()` does a filesystem read + JSON parse, so eliminating ~10 redundant calls per operation reduces I/O.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `loadConfig()` called at most once per `listCommand` execution
- [ ] `loadConfig()` called at most once per `update()` execution
- [ ] All existing tests pass
- [ ] No API changes to public functions (optional parameter only)

closing_issues.title: fix: clarify preserveCustomizations option semantics
closing_issues.body:
## Problem

The `preserveCustomizations: false` option in `UpdateOptions` only disables the `.omcustom-customizations.json` manifest-based preservation. It does NOT disable `.omcustomrc.json` config-based `preserveFiles`.

This creates a semantic ambiguity: users expect `preserveCustomizations: false` to mean "don't preserve anything", but config-based preservation still occurs.

## Current Behavior

```typescript
// preserveCustomizations: false
const manifestCustomizations = options.preserveCustomizations !== false
  ? await loadCustomizationManifest(options.targetDir)
  : null;  // manifest disabled

const configPreserveFiles = config.preserveFiles || [];  // still active!
```

## Proposed Options

1. **Option A**: `preserveCustomizations: false` disables BOTH sources (breaking change)
2. **Option B**: Add separate `ignoreConfigPreserveFiles` option
3. **Option C (recommended)**: Document current behavior clearly, add `--force-overwrite-all` flag that bypasses both

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Behavior is clearly documented
- [ ] Users have a way to bypass all preservation if needed
- [ ] No silent data loss

closing_issues.title: security: add path traversal validation for preserveFiles
closing_issues.body:
## Problem

The `preserveFiles` configuration field accepts arbitrary relative paths without validation. A malicious or misconfigured `.omcustomrc.json` could contain paths like `../../etc/passwd` or `../other-project/secrets.env`.

While `preserveFiles` is used for skip-path logic (preventing files from being overwritten during update, not reading/copying them), a lack of validation could lead to unexpected behavior.

## Current Behavior

```json
{
  "preserveFiles": ["../../etc/passwd", "../other-project/.env"]
}
```

These paths are passed directly to `shouldSkipPath()` without validation.

## Proposed Solution

Add path normalization and validation in `resolveCustomizations()`:

1. Normalize all paths with `path.normalize()`
2. Reject paths that resolve outside the project root (contain `..` that escapes)
3. Log a warning for rejected paths

## Impact

Low — this is a local CLI tool where the user controls the config file. However, defense-in-depth is good practice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Paths resolving outside project root are rejected with warning
- [ ] Normalized paths work correctly (e.g., `./foo/../bar` → `bar`)
- [ ] Validation applied to both config and manifest sources
- [ ] Tests cover path traversal rejection

closing_issues.title: feat: Git workflow in CLAUDE.md template should adapt to target project
closing_issues.body:
## Description

The `CLAUDE.md` template hardcodes a specific Git workflow (develop-based branching strategy) that may not match the target project's actual branch structure. When installed into a project that uses `main` as its sole branch, the template creates a mismatch.

## Current Behavior

The CLAUDE.md template always includes:

```markdown
## Git Workflow (MUST follow)

| Branch | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `develop` | Main development branch (default) |
| `feature/*` | New features -> PR to develop |
| `release/*` | Release preparation |
| `hotfix/*` | Critical fixes |
```

This is installed regardless of the target project's actual branching strategy.

## Problem

- A project using `main`-only workflow gets instructions for a `develop`-based flow
- The agent (and mgr-gitnerd) will try to follow the template workflow, not the project's actual workflow
- Creates confusion between what CLAUDE.md says and what the project actually does
- Example: wasm-video-player has only `main` branch, but CLAUDE.md tells agents to use `develop`

## Expected Behavior

One of:

1. **Detection**: `omcustom init` detects the project's default branch and branch structure, then generates an appropriate Git workflow section
2. **Configurable**: Allow users to choose their Git workflow during init (e.g., "trunk-based", "git-flow", "github-flow")
3. **Placeholder**: Use a generic template that users customize, rather than prescribing a specific workflow
4. **Project override section**: Add a clearly marked section in CLAUDE.md where project-specific Git workflow overrides the template default

## Suggested Approach

During `omcustom init`:
```
? Git workflow strategy:
  > Detect from repository (recommended)
    Git Flow (develop/feature/release/hotfix)
    GitHub Flow (main + feature branches)
    Trunk-based (main only)
    Custom
```

Then generate the appropriate CLAUDE.md Git Workflow section.

## Impact

- Every project installed with oh-my-customcode gets the same Git workflow regardless of actual needs
- Agents may create wrong branches or follow incorrect PR targets
- Users must manually edit CLAUDE.md after every init/update to fix the workflow section

closing_issues.title: fix: omcustom update shows 'Updated from 0.2.0 to 0.2.0' when only components are synced
closing_issues.body:
## Problem

`omcustom update` shows misleading version message when only component-level updates occur:

```
✓ Updated from 0.2.0 to 0.2.0
```

Both `previousVersion` (from `.omcustomrc.json`) and `newVersion` (from `manifest.json`) are the same.

## Root Cause

In `src/core/updater.ts`:
- Line 429: `result.previousVersion = config.version` → `0.2.0`
- Line 432: `result.newVersion = updateCheck.latestVersion` → `0.2.0`
- Line 475: `success('update.success', { from: result.previousVersion, to: result.newVersion })`

The update proceeds because `componentHasUpdate()` (line 588-590) returns `true` when `componentVersions` entries are missing, but the overall version is unchanged.

## Expected Behavior

When versions are identical, show something like:
- `✓ Components synced (version 0.2.0)` 
- Or suppress the version message entirely and only show component-level updates

## Suggested Fix

In `update()` function, differentiate between:
1. Version upgrade (0.1.0 → 0.2.0): Show "Updated from X to Y"
2. Component sync within same version: Show "Components synced" or similar
3. No changes at all: Show "Already up to date"

closing_issues.title: fix: Release workflow fails when CHANGELOG.md entry is missing
closing_issues.body:
## Problem

The release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) has a critical failure mode when CHANGELOG.md entries are missing. This breaks the entire release pipeline in the following ways:

1. **Hard failure on missing entry**: The "Extract Release Notes" step (L134-160) exits with `exit 1` when it cannot find a version section in CHANGELOG.md
2. **Post-publish failure**: This step runs AFTER npm publish (L62-75), meaning the package is already published to npm but GitHub Release creation fails
3. **Cascade failure**: The Release Notes Generator workflow (`release-notes.yml`) depends on the Release workflow completing successfully (`workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`, L26), so it gets skipped entirely
4. **Result**: Missing CHANGELOG entry causes incomplete releases with no GitHub Release and no AI-generated notes

This pattern has occurred in v0.12.2 and v0.12.3 releases.

## Current Behavior

```yaml
# release.yml L149-153
if [ -z "$NOTES" ]; then
  echo "::error::No changelog entry found for version ${VERSION}."
  echo "::error::Please add a '## [${VERSION}]' section to CHANGELOG.md before releasing."
  exit 1  # ← Hard failure
fi
```

**Timeline when CHANGELOG is missing:**
1. ✅ npm publish succeeds
2. ❌ Extract Release Notes fails (exit 1)
3. ⏭️  GitHub Release creation skipped
4. ⏭️  Release Notes Generator workflow skipped

## Proposed Solutions

### Option A: Graceful Fallback (Recommended)

Allow the workflow to continue with auto-generated notes when CHANGELOG entry is missing:

```yaml
- name: Extract Release Notes
  id: changelog
  run: |
    VERSION=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/v}
    echo "version=$VERSION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    
    if [ ! -f CHANGELOG.md ]; then
      echo "::warning::CHANGELOG.md not found. Will use auto-generated notes."
      echo "notes=" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      exit 0
    fi
    
    NOTES=$(awk "/^## \[${VERSION}\]/{flag=1; next} /^## \[/{flag=0} flag" CHANGELOG.md)
    
    if [ -z "$NOTES" ]; then
      echo "::warning::No changelog entry found for version ${VERSION}. Will use auto-generated notes."
      echo "notes=" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
    else
      echo "notes<<EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      echo "$NOTES" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      echo "EOF" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      echo "::notice::Found changelog entry for v${VERSION}"
    fi

- name: Create GitHub Release
  uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
  with:
    body: |
      ## What's Changed
      
      ${{ steps.changelog.outputs.notes || 'See commit history for changes.' }}
      
      <!-- Release Notes Generator will update this -->
    generate_release_notes: ${{ steps.changelog.outputs.notes == '' }}
```

**Pros**: Resilient, allows Release Notes Generator to always run, maintains existing CHANGELOG-first workflow when available
**Cons**: None significant

### Option B: Auto-update CHANGELOG

Add a step to automatically update CHANGELOG.md before extraction:

```yaml
- name: Update CHANGELOG
  run: |
    VERSION=${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/v}
    if ! grep -q "## \[${VERSION}\]" CHANGELOG.md 2>/dev/null; then
      # Generate entry from commits
      gh api repos/${{ github.repository }}/releases/generate-notes \
        -f tag_name="${GITHUB_REF#refs/tags/}" \
        --jq '.body' > /tmp/notes.md
      
      # Insert into CHANGELOG
      sed -i "/^# Changelog/a \\\n## [${VERSION}] - $(date +%Y-%m-%d)\\\n\\\n$(cat /tmp/notes.md)" CHANGELOG.md
      
      git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
      git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
      git add CHANGELOG.md
      git commit -m "chore: auto-update CHANGELOG for v${VERSION}"
      git push
    fi
```

**Pros**: Ensures CHANGELOG.md is always complete
**Cons**: Creates extra commits, may conflict with manual CHANGELOG workflow

### Option C: Non-blocking Extraction

Make the extraction step non-blocking:

```yaml
- name: Extract Release Notes
  id: changelog
  continue-on-error: true
  run: |
    # existing logic with exit 1

- name: Release Notes Generator
  if: always()  # Change from workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
```

**Pros**: Simple change
**Cons**: Doesn't fix the root issue, just masks it

## Recommendation

**Option A** is the best balance of resilience and maintaining existing workflows. It:
- Prevents release pipeline failures
- Allows Release Notes Generator to always run
- Preserves CHANGELOG-first workflow when available
- Provides clear warnings for missing entries

## Impact

**Current releases affected**: v0.12.2, v0.12.3 (potentially others)
**Severity**: High - breaks release automation and user-facing release notes
**Workaround**: Manual `gh release create` or re-running Release Notes Generator via `workflow_dispatch`

## Related Files

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (L134-160)
- `.github/workflows/release-notes.yml` (L24-26)
- `CHANGELOG.md`

closing_issues.title: fix: `omcustom init` fails with "ontology-rag was not found in the package registry"
closing_issues.body:
## Bug Description

`omcustom init` fails when trying to setup the MCP environment because `mcp-config.ts` attempts to install `ontology-rag` from PyPI via `uv pip install ontology-rag`, but the package is not published on PyPI.

## Error Message

```
Warning: Failed to setup MCP environment: Failed to setup Python environment: Command failed: uv pip install ontology-rag
  × No solution found when resolving dependencies:
  ╰─▶ Because ontology-rag was not found in the package registry and you
      require ontology-rag, we can conclude that your requirements are
      unsatisfiable.
```

## Root Cause

`src/core/mcp-config.ts:41` runs `uv pip install ontology-rag` which looks up PyPI, but `ontology-rag` is a local package in `packages/ontology-rag/` and has never been published to PyPI.

## Fix

Change the install command to use a Git URL:
```
uv pip install "ontology-rag @ git+https://github.com/baekenough/oh-my-customcode.git#subdirectory=packages/ontology-rag"
```

## Affected Version

v0.14.0

closing_issues.body:
# Critical Security: SSL Certificate Verification Disabled

## 🔴 Severity: CRITICAL

## Description
SSL certificate verification is disabled in the database connection pool configuration (`rejectUnauthorized: false`), creating a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attack vulnerability.

## Location
- **File:** `src/server/db/pool.ts`
- **Lines:** 30-33, 54-57

## Warning Message
```
WARNING: SSL is configured with rejectUnauthorized: false
This is insecure and should only be used in development
```

## Impact
- ⚠️ Database connections are vulnerable to MITM attacks
- ⚠️ Encrypted traffic can be intercepted and modified
- ⚠️ Production data can be compromised
- ⚠️ Violates security compliance requirements

## Recommended Fix
1. Enable SSL certificate verification in production (`rejectUnauthorized: true`)
2. Use proper CA certificates for production databases
3. Only allow `rejectUnauthorized: false` in development environment
4. Fail startup if insecure SSL configuration detected in production
5. Add environment-based SSL configuration

## Example Fix
```typescript
const sslConfig = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production'
  ? { rejectUnauthorized: true }
  : { rejectUnauthorized: false };
```

## Priority
🔴 **CRITICAL** - Fix before production deployment

closing_issues.body:
# High Priority: CSP Configuration Allows Unsafe-Inline and Unsafe-Eval

## 🟠 Severity: HIGH

## Description
Content Security Policy (CSP) configuration allows `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'`, which defeats the purpose of CSP and creates XSS vulnerabilities.

## Location
- **File:** `src/server/middleware/security.middleware.ts`
- **Lines:** 15-19

## Code
```typescript
"script-src": ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'", "'unsafe-eval'"],
"style-src": ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'"],
```

## Impact
- ⚠️ XSS attacks can execute arbitrary JavaScript
- ⚠️ CSP protection is effectively disabled
- ⚠️ Users are vulnerable to script injection attacks
- ⚠️ Defeats the security benefit of CSP

## Recommended Fix
1. Remove `'unsafe-inline'` and `'unsafe-eval'` from CSP
2. Use nonce-based or hash-based inline scripts
3. Move all inline scripts to external files
4. Implement proper CSP with strict directives
5. Use Angular's built-in sanitization

## Example Fix
```typescript
// Generate nonce for each request
const nonce = crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('base64');

// Make the nonce available to your rendering layer (for example, via locals)
// so it can be added to <script> / <style> tags:
res.locals.cspNonce = nonce;

// Configure CSP to allow only scripts/styles with this nonce.
// NOTE: This is a simplified illustration. For Angular SSR you must also
// modify the server-side rendering pipeline to inject this nonce into the
// rendered <script> (and optionally <style>) tags. The exact integration
// depends on your SSR setup and is not shown here.

"script-src": ["'self'", `'nonce-${nonce}'`],
"style-src": ["'self'", `'nonce-${nonce}'`],
```

## Priority
🟠 **HIGH** - Fix to prevent XSS vulnerabilities

2. **`src/app/shared/services/seo.service.ts`** (lines 36, 47, 171, 193, 194, 208, 219, 221, 262, 279, 280, 285, 300, 321)

   - Hardcoded phone number: `+998-XX-XXX-XXXX`

   - Hardcoded contact information (phone, email, address, hours)

4. **`src/server.ts`** (line 138)
   - Hardcoded localhost in startup messages

5. **`src/server/db/pool.ts`** (line 61)
   - Hardcoded default database host: `localhost`

## Impact
- 🔴 Difficult to deploy to different environments (dev/staging/prod)
- 🔴 Testing is complicated and error-prone
- 🔴 Configuration changes require code changes and redeployment
- 🔴 Production/development parity issues
- 🔴 Cannot easily switch between environments

## Recommended Fix

### 1. Create Environment Configuration
```typescript
// src/config/environment.ts
export const config = {
  domain: process.env.DOMAIN || 'http://localhost:4200',
  apiUrl: process.env.API_URL || 'http://localhost:4000',
  production: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production',
  contact: {
    phone: process.env.CONTACT_PHONE,
    email: process.env.CONTACT_EMAIL,
    address: process.env.CONTACT_ADDRESS
  }
};
```

### 2. Use Environment Variables
- Create `.env.development`, `.env.production` files
- Document all required environment variables in README
- Use `dotenv` package to load environment variables
- Validate required environment variables on startup

### 3. Update Angular Environment Files
```typescript
// src/environments/environment.ts
export const environment = {
  production: false,
  apiUrl: 'http://localhost:4000',
  domain: 'http://localhost:4200'
};
```

closing_issues.title: Divide DefaultContext to Editing and Simulation implementation using factories or DI and some new classes
closing_issues.body:
`DefaultContext` directly instantiates simulation process classes, violating dependency inversion and creating tight coupling to the `sim/` package.

## Problematic code

```kotlin
// context/DefaultContext.kt imports:
import cz.vutbr.fit.interlockSim.sim.Generator
import cz.vutbr.fit.interlockSim.sim.InOutWorker
import cz.vutbr.fit.interlockSim.sim.ShuntingLoop

// Later in code:
val generator = Generator(...)
val worker = InOutWorker(...)
```

## Impact

- Context depends on concrete simulation classes (should depend on abstractions)
- Cannot test context without simulation classes
- Violates single responsibility principle
- Makes it difficult to add new simulation types

## Recommended Solutions

1. **Factory pattern:** Create `SimulationProcessFactory` interface with implementations
2. **Extend Koin DI:** Define simulation objects in Koin modules (but see constraints below)
3. **Strategy pattern:** Abstract simulation setup logic

## Constraints

- Per CLAUDE.md: `sim/` package is RESTRICTED (jDisco migration pending)
- Must coordinate with future jDisco → DSOL/Kalasim migration
- Cannot add Koin to `sim/` package yet (traffic-simulation-expert requirement)

**Complexity:** MEDIUM-HIGH - Requires careful design to align with jDisco migration strategy

**Priority:** Medium - Improves testability but doesn't block current work

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] DefaultContext does not import concrete sim/ classes
- [ ] Simulation object creation uses factory abstraction or DI
- [ ] All 662 tests pass (especially simulation tests)
- [ ] Design documented and compatible with future DSOL migration

mentioned_issues.title: Phase 3: Split DefaultContext into DefaultEditingContext and DefaultSimulationContext
mentioned_issues.body:
**Parent Issue:** #92

## Overview

Phase 3 of the Context refactoring involves splitting `DefaultContext` into two separate classes:
- `DefaultEditingContext` - Only editing operations (mutable network, no simulation)
- `DefaultSimulationContext` - Extends editing with simulation capabilities

## Context

Phase 2 (PR #95) successfully implemented the Factory pattern, decoupling DefaultContext from concrete simulation classes. However, DefaultContext still combines both editing and simulation concerns in a single class (984 lines).

## Goals

1. **Separation of Concerns**: Clearly separate editing operations from simulation operations
2. **Reduced Complexity**: Smaller, more focused classes
3. **Better Testability**: Test editing without simulation dependencies
4. **Domain Alignment**: Match the conceptual model (editing phase vs. simulation phase)

## Design

### DefaultEditingContext
```kotlin
class DefaultEditingContext(
    cols: Int,
    rows: Int
) : EditingContext {
    // All grid operations
    // All path finding
    // All graph management
    // All cell manipulation
    // NO simulation-specific fields or methods
}
```

### DefaultSimulationContext
```kotlin
class DefaultSimulationContext(
    cols: Int,
    rows: Int,
    private val processFactory: SimulationProcessFactory
) : DefaultEditingContext(cols, rows), SimulationContext {
    // Simulation-specific fields: mainProcess, workers
    // Simulation methods: run(), stop(), errorStop()
    // Uses factory for process creation
}
```

## Tasks

- [ ] Create `DefaultEditingContext` class
  - [ ] Move all editing-related code from DefaultContext
  - [ ] Remove simulation-specific fields and methods
  - [ ] Ensure no imports from sim/ package
- [ ] Create `DefaultSimulationContext` class
  - [ ] Extend DefaultEditingContext
  - [ ] Add simulation-specific fields (mainProcess, workers)
  - [ ] Implement SimulationContext interface
  - [ ] Use SimulationProcessFactory for process creation
- [ ] Update `XMLContextFactory`
  - [ ] Use DefaultSimulationContext instead of DefaultContext
  - [ ] Verify XML loading still works
- [ ] Update tests
  - [ ] Add tests for DefaultEditingContext (editing without simulation)
  - [ ] Update DefaultContext tests to use DefaultSimulationContext
  - [ ] Verify all 728 tests pass
- [ ] Documentation
  - [ ] Update CONTEXT_REFACTORING_DESIGN.md
  - [ ] Document class responsibilities in KDoc
  - [ ] Update CLAUDE.md if needed

## Backwards Compatibility

Option 1: Keep DefaultContext as deprecated alias
```kotlin
@Deprecated("Use DefaultSimulationContext")
abstract class DefaultContext(
    cols: Int, rows: Int, processFactory: SimulationProcessFactory
) : DefaultSimulationContext(cols, rows, processFactory)
```

Option 2: Remove DefaultContext entirely (breaking change)

## Complexity

**HIGH** - Large refactoring (984 lines to split), extensive testing required

## Success Criteria

- [ ] DefaultEditingContext has no simulation dependencies
- [ ] DefaultSimulationContext properly extends DefaultEditingContext
- [ ] All 728 tests pass
- [ ] No imports from sim/ package in DefaultEditingContext
- [ ] XML loading and simulation examples still work
- [ ] Documentation updated

## References

- Parent issue: #92
- Phase 2 PR: #95
- Design doc: `CONTEXT_REFACTORING_DESIGN.md`
- Factory pattern implementation: `FACTORY_PATTERN_IMPLEMENTATION.md`

mentioned_issues.title: Phase 4: Separate Static and Dynamic Properties in Domain Objects
mentioned_issues.body:
**Parent Issue:** #92

## Overview

Phase 4 of the Context refactoring involves separating static (editing-time) and dynamic (simulation-time) properties in domain objects like `Track`, `RailSwitch`, `RailSemaphore`, and `InOut`.

## Context

Currently, domain objects mix:
- **Static properties**: Track length, max speed, cell positions (set during editing, immutable during simulation)
- **Dynamic properties**: Train position, occupancy state, semaphore signals (change during simulation)

This mixing violates the conceptual model where:
- **Editing phase**: Network structure is mutable, objects have only static properties
- **Simulation phase**: Network structure is immutable, objects gain dynamic state

## Goals

1. **Conceptual Clarity**: Static vs. dynamic properties match editing vs. simulation phases
2. **Immutability**: Editing contexts cannot modify dynamic state
3. **Type Safety**: Compile-time guarantee that editing code can't access simulation state
4. **Performance**: Dynamic state can use specialized data structures optimized for simulation

## Design Proposal

### Static Objects (Editing Phase)
```kotlin
// Static properties only - set during editing
class Track(
    val length: Double,
    val maxSpeed: Double,
    val cells: List<Cell>
) {
    // No occupancy, no train reference
    // Immutable during simulation
}

class RailSemaphore(
    val position: Point,
    val direction: Direction,
    val controlledTracks: List<Track>
) {
    // No signal state
}
```

### Dynamic Objects (Simulation Phase)
```kotlin
// Dynamic properties wrap static objects
class DynamicTrack(
    val static: Track  // Delegation target
) {
    var currentOccupant: Train? = null
    var isOccupied: Boolean = false
    var reservedBy: Train? = null
    
    // Delegate static properties
    val length: Double by static::length
    val maxSpeed: Double by static::maxSpeed
}

class DynamicSemaphore(
    val static: RailSemaphore
) {
    var signalState: SignalState = SignalState.RED
    var lastStateChange: Double = 0.0
}
```

### Context Separation
```kotlin
// Editing context - works with static objects only
interface EditingContext {
    fun addTrack(track: Track)
    fun removeTrack(track: Track)
    fun getTracks(): List<Track>
    // NO access to DynamicTrack
}

// Simulation context - has both static and dynamic
interface SimulationContext : EditingContext {
    fun getDynamicTrack(static: Track): DynamicTrack
    fun getDynamicSemaphore(static: RailSemaphore): DynamicSemaphore
}
```

## User Proposal (from #92)

> For each RailSemaphore, RailSwitch, InOut, ..., Track(Block):
> - must contain only "static" properties (static from point of view of simulation, not programming)
> - must exist some Dynamic* class for dynamic properties (which is changing during simulation)
> - this dynamic class should be at first linked with its static instance by delegation (kotlin delegation?)
> - this delegate is stable base for compute equals and hashcode to be Dynamic* placed in some net

## Tasks

- [ ] **Design Phase**
  - [ ] Identify all static vs. dynamic properties for each domain object
  - [ ] Design Dynamic* wrapper classes with delegation
  - [ ] Plan migration strategy (can be gradual)
- [ ] **Implementation Phase**
  - [ ] Create DynamicTrack, DynamicRailSwitch, DynamicSemaphore, DynamicInOut
  - [ ] Use Kotlin delegation (`by` keyword) for static property access
  - [ ] Update SimulationContext to manage Dynamic* instances
  - [ ] Ensure equals/hashCode use static object (stable identity)
- [ ] **Migration Phase**
  - [ ] Update simulation code to use Dynamic* objects
  - [ ] Update editing code to use static objects only
  - [ ] Ensure EditingContext has no access to Dynamic* types
- [ ] **Testing Phase**
  - [ ] Test that editing contexts cannot access dynamic state
  - [ ] Test that simulation state changes don't affect static objects
  - [ ] Verify all 728 tests pass
  - [ ] Golden output validation (simulation results unchanged)

## Benefits

1. **Type Safety**: Compiler prevents editing code from accessing simulation state
2. **Immutability**: Network structure cannot change during simulation
3. **Clarity**: Static vs. dynamic properties are explicit in type system
4. **Testing**: Can test static structure without simulation state

## Complexity

**VERY HIGH** - Affects core domain model, requires careful migration

## Dependencies

- Depends on: Phase 3 (DefaultEditingContext / DefaultSimulationContext split)
- Blocks: Future multiplatform support (static objects can be shared, dynamic cannot)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All domain objects have separate Static and Dynamic* classes
- [ ] EditingContext works only with static objects
- [ ] SimulationContext manages Dynamic* objects
- [ ] Kotlin delegation used for static property access
- [ ] equals/hashCode based on static object
- [ ] All 728 tests pass
- [ ] Golden output matches (simulation unchanged)
- [ ] No compilation errors when editing code tries to access dynamic state

## References

- Parent issue: #92
- User proposal: #92 (comments)
- Design doc: `CONTEXT_REFACTORING_DESIGN.md` (Phase 6)

mentioned_issues.title: Simulation fails
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary of Investigation

I've completed a thorough investigation of the simulation failure. Here are the findings:

### Fixes Successfully Applied

1. ✅ **Train.kt Dynamic wrapper comparisons** - Fixed InOut entry/exit detection to use `.static` property
2. ✅ **Generator termination** - Changed `hold(random.exp(43.0))` to `hold(5.0)` for timely termination response
3. ✅ **ShuntingLoop.kt nextSemaphore comparison** - Added static reference unwrapping to avoid Dynamic wrapper identity mismatches  
4. ✅ **ShuntingLoop.kt isSetUpPath comparison** - Fixed to use static separators (identity comparison requires same object instance)

### Root Cause Identified

The simulation fails because **railway switches create duplicate track segments that share the same name but are different objects**:

- `constructPath(zA, vA, doA1, ...)` creates TWO track blocks both named "vA-around":
  - Block from `zA` to `vA` (switch entrance)
  - Block from `vA` to `doA1` (switch exit)
- Trains enter BOTH segments sequentially (`enter()` called twice with same block name)
- **Only the FIRST segment gets properly reserved** (RESERVED->OCCUPIED)
- **The SECOND segment remains FREE** (never reserved by path setup)
- This causes "Wrong state: FREE, expected: RESERVED" error

### Why Develop Branch Works

The develop branch works because:
- NO Dynamic* wrappers for tracks
- Direct state management in static SimpleTrack objects  
- Path setup and train traversal use the SAME objects
- Both track segments around switches get properly reserved

### Why Current Branch Fails

The `copilot/separate-static-and-dynamic-properties` branch introduced Dynamic* wrappers but the migration is **incomplete**:
- `DynamicTrack` class exists but is NEVER used
- Paths contain Dynamic separators but static tracks  
- Identity comparisons (`===`) fail when mixing static/Dynamic objects
- The second track segment around switches doesn't get reserved

### Recommended Solution

The issue requires architectural analysis beyond quick fixes. The branch attempted to separate static/dynamic properties but this conflicts with how ShuntingLoop reserves multiple track segments for switches. Options:

1. **Revert Dynamic track approach** - Keep only Dynamic separators (Semaphore, Switch, InOut), leave tracks static
2. **Complete Dynamic migration** - Fully implement DynamicTrack usage throughout (major refactoring)
3. **Fix switch path logic** - Ensure both track segments get reserved independently

The simulation works correctly through time ~23, then fails when the second switch segment isn't reserved. This suggests the interlocking logic needs deeper changes to handle the Dynamic wrapper architecture.
