mentioned_issues.title: feat(fast-sim): TextReporter — human-readable simulation output
mentioned_issues.body:
## Parent

Part of #413 (`:fast-sim` epic)

## Description

Implement `TextReporter` that subscribes to simulation events and prints human-readable text to stdout.

## SimulationEvent Data Class (new)

Format-agnostic event model enabling future JSON/CSV formatters:

```kotlin
data class SimulationEvent(
    val time: Double,
    val source: String,
    val type: String,     // ReportType name: TRAIN_EVENTS, NODE_EVENTS, PATH_SETTING, etc.
    val message: String
)
```

## Event Field Mapping

TextReporter receives `ContextChangeEvent` where:
- `event.propertyName` = `ReportType.name` (e.g., "TRAIN_EVENTS") → maps to `SimulationEvent.type`
- `event.newValue` = formatted string `"<simTime> <object> <message>"` (from `DefaultSimulationContext.report()` at line ~1338) → parsed into `SimulationEvent.time`, `.source`, `.message`

## TextReporter Design

Implements `ContextPropertyChangeListener`. Registered via `context.addPropertyChangeListener(reporter)` before `context.run()`.

**Output format:**
like in JVM

Summary line at end: `--- Simulation complete: <n> trains, <endTime>s sim time, <wallTime>s wall ---`

## Verbosity Flags

- **Default:** TRAIN_EVENTS + NODE_EVENTS + PATH_SETTING
- `--verbose`: adds TRAIN_CONTINUOUS (can produce thousands of lines)
- `--quiet`: summary line only

## Logging Strategy

**Research required**: Verify how kotlin-logging 7.0.3 configures log level on Kotlin/Native (no SLF4J backend). Check if `KotlinLoggingConfiguration` or equivalent API exists. Fallback options:
- Custom `KLogger` wrapper that discards below WARN
- Redirect kotlin-logging output to stderr via platform-specific native I/O
- Suppress all logging in fast-sim (set min level at initialization)

**Core requirement:** zero kotlin-logging output on stdout. TextReporter → stdout; logging → stderr.

## Tasks

- [ ] Implement `SimulationEvent` data class
- [ ] Implement `TextReporter` implementing `ContextPropertyChangeListener`
- [ ] Research kotlin-logging native log level configuration
- [ ] Implement `--verbose` / `--quiet` CLI flags
- [ ] Add summary line at simulation end
- [ ] Unit tests for event parsing and formatting

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `./fast-sim example shuntingLoop 60` produces readable event output on stdout
- [ ] Zero kotlin-logging messages on stdout
- [ ] Default output excludes TRAIN_CONTINUOUS
- [ ] `--verbose` includes TRAIN_CONTINUOUS
- [ ] `--quiet` shows only summary
- [ ] Output parseable by regex `t=[\d.]+\s+\[\w+\]\s+.+`
- [ ] Summary line includes train count and wall-clock time

## Risk Register

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| kotlin-logging stdout pollution | High | Research native log config API; fallback to custom wrapper or suppression |
| TRAIN_CONTINUOUS output flooding | Medium | Default exclude; `--verbose` opt-in |
| Event format parsing from report() | Low | Format is stable (established 2007, unchanged since) |

## LONG_TERM_GOALS Links

- **Goal 17 (Export)**: Same SimulationEvent model → CSV/Excel formatter
- **Goal 6 (Metrics)**: SimulationEvent = metrics collection foundation
- **Goal 9/10 (AI Dispatcher)**: Machine-parseable events for future agent monitoring

closing_issues.title: refactor(core): emit dedicated TRAIN_APPROVED ReportType instead of parsing "approved" keyword
closing_issues.body:
## Problem

`TextReporter.propertyChange()` counts unique trains by searching for the English word `"approved"` in the combined `source + message` string:

```kotlin
val combined = "${simEvent.source} ${simEvent.message}"
val approvedIndex = combined.indexOf("approved")
if (approvedIndex > 0) {
    trainNames.add(combined.substring(0, approvedIndex).trim())
}
```

This couples train counting to a specific English word in the simulation output. If that word is ever changed, localised, or a message happens to contain "approved" for an unrelated reason, train counting silently breaks.

## Proposed Fix

Emit a dedicated `ReportType.TRAIN_APPROVED` event from the simulation layer when a train's path request is approved, instead of inferring it by parsing free-form text. `TextReporter` would then hook on `TRAIN_APPROVED` events directly.

## Context

Introduced in PR #424 (`feature/fastSim-textReporter`). The fragility is currently mitigated by tests (`summaryCountsTrainsWithSpacesInName`) but the root cause remains.

closing_issues.title: test(fast-sim): smoke test — native vs JVM semantic parity
closing_issues.body:
## Parent

Part of #413 (`:fast-sim` epic)

## Description

Verify that native simulation produces the same results as JVM simulation.

## Critical Insight

**kDisco.Random determinism across platforms is unknown.** If Random produces different sequences on JVM vs native, train generation timing differs. Therefore: **compare structural invariants only**, not exact event times.

## Structural Invariants for shuntingLoop 60

1. At least 1 train generated (ShuntingLoop has `MAX_TRAINS = 2`; actual count depends on random timing and 60s duration — validate empirically by running JVM first)
2. All generated trains traverse network (visit track blocks)
3. All completed trains reach destination InOut
4. Simulation terminates normally (exit 0)
5. No error events
6. **Same train count on both platforms** (key parity check)

## Implementation

`@Tag("integration-test")` JVM test using `ProcessBuilder`:
1. Build/locate JVM JAR (`desktop-ui/build/libs/interlockSim.jar`) and native binary
2. Run both with `example shuntingLoop 60`, capture stdout + stderr
3. Parse events into `SimulationEvent` model
4. Compare structural invariants (order-independent for HashMap safety, #409)
5. If Random IS deterministic: also compare event times within 0.01s tolerance (conditional assertion)
6. 120s timeout per process; capture stderr on failure for diagnostics

## Risks

- **kDisco.Random divergence:** JVM vs native may produce different random sequences → different train timing
- **PlatformIdentity (#409):** HashMap iteration order may differ → event ordering divergence
- **Native hang:** kDisco simulation could hang on native → 120s timeout required

## Future Enhancement

A `--json` output flag would simplify comparison. Deferred — use text parsing for v1.

## Tasks

- [ ] Create integration test class with ProcessBuilder
- [ ] Implement SimulationEvent text parser (regex-based)
- [ ] Implement structural invariant comparison (order-independent)
- [ ] Add 120s timeout with stderr capture
- [ ] Validate test stability (10 consecutive runs)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test passes when both platforms produce structurally equivalent results
- [ ] Test fails with clear diagnostics (showing both outputs) on divergence
- [ ] Handles native binary crash gracefully (timeout + stderr capture)
- [ ] 120s timeout per process
- [ ] Stable across 10 consecutive runs (no flakiness)

## Risk Register

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Random sequence divergence | High | Structural invariants only (not exact times) |
| HashMap iteration order (#409) | Medium | Order-independent comparison |
| Native simulation hang | High | 120s timeout; capture stderr |
| JVM output format differs from TextReporter | Medium | Both parsed into SimulationEvent model |

## LONG_TERM_GOALS Links

- **Goal 9/10 (AI Dispatcher)**: Establishes trust in native simulation results
- **Goal 1 (Multi-Train)**: Parity test framework extends to multi-train scenarios

closing_issues.title: feat(fast-sim): Docker image — minimal native container
closing_issues.body:
## Parent

Part of #413 (`:fast-sim` epic)

## Description

Create `Dockerfile.fast-sim` with multi-stage build producing a minimal native container.

## Docker Configuration

```dockerfile
# Build stage
FROM debian:bookworm AS builder
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y openjdk-21-jdk git libxml2-dev libicu-dev
COPY . /build
# CRITICAL: Copy pre-built kDisco artifacts for offline build
COPY docker-kdisco/ /root/.m2/repository/cz/hovorka/kdisco/
WORKDIR /build
ENV GRADLE_OPTS="-Xmx2g"
RUN ./gradlew :fast-sim:linkReleaseExecutableLinuxX64

# Runtime stage
FROM debian:bookworm-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libxml2 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY --from=builder /build/fast-sim/build/bin/linuxX64/releaseExecutable/fast-sim.kexe /app/fast-sim
WORKDIR /app
HEALTHCHECK CMD ["./fast-sim", "--version"]
ENTRYPOINT ["./fast-sim"]
```

## Key Notes

- **docker-kdisco/ MUST be copied** to `.m2` before Gradle build (missing in original spec)
- Runtime: `debian:bookworm-slim` + `libxml2` (NOT `-dev`)
- **HEALTHCHECK** added for container orchestration
- **Image target: < 120MB** (bookworm-slim alone is ~80MB uncompressed; original 50MB target was unrealistic)
- Consider `alpine` + `musl` for < 50MB in future
- `GRADLE_OPTS="-Xmx2g"` to prevent OOM during K/N compilation
- `sim` mode: bind-mount XML files (`-v ./networks:/data:ro`)

## docker-compose.yml

```yaml
fast-sim:
  build:
    context: .
    dockerfile: Dockerfile.fast-sim
  entrypoint: ["./fast-sim"]
```

closing_issues.title: fix(fast-sim): wall-time formatting in TextReporter.printSummary uses float division
closing_issues.body:
## Problem

`TextReporter.printSummary()` formats wall time with:

```kotlin
val wallSeconds = (currentTimeMillisKMP() - startWallTime) / 1000.0
val wallFormatted = ((wallSeconds * 10).toLong() / 10.0).toString()
```

The `toLong()` truncation is correct (preserves 1 decimal place of precision), but dividing by `10.0` converts back to `Double`, reintroducing IEEE 754 representation issues. `kotlin.Double.toString()` may emit e.g. `3.1000000000000001` instead of `3.1`.

## Fix

Use pure integer arithmetic to format the tenths digit:

```kotlin
val wallMs = currentTimeMillisKMP() - startWallTime
val wallTenths = wallMs / 100        // integer tenths of seconds
val wallFormatted = "${wallTenths / 10}.${wallTenths % 10}"
```

This avoids all floating-point formatting entirely.

## Scope

`core/src/commonMain/kotlin/cz/vutbr/fit/interlockSim/sim/TextReporter.kt`, `printSummary()`.

Found during review of PR #424 (feat(fast-sim): TextReporter).

mentioned_issues.body:

This issue is implemented through 9 sequential phases:

**Complexity**: HIGH - Major architectural change affecting entire codebase

**User Clarifications** (from comments):
1. ✅ DynamicPathSeparator has static reference to NodeCell
2. ✅ Create new grid (immutable structure for simulation)
3. ✅ Preserve object identity (static is immutable base)
4. ✅ Paths in simulation must be dynamic
5. ✅ CellRenderer handles both static and dynamic
6. ✅ XML serialization for editing context only

See individual subissues for detailed task breakdowns and verification steps.

---

## Subissue Links

- **Phase 1**: #139 - Create design document with type hierarchy and transformation strategy
- **Phase 2**: #140 - Add type parameter to RailwayNetGrid interface
- **Phase 3**: #141 - Create DynamicRailSwitch, DynamicRailSemaphore, DynamicInOut wrapper classes
- **Phase 4**: #142 - Add type parameter to Context, EditingContext, SimulationContext
- **Phase 5**: #143 - Implement grid transformation from static to dynamic cells
- **Phase 6**: #144 - Update context implementations to use parameterized grids
- **Phase 7**: #145 - Update path system to store dynamic references in simulation
- **Phase 8**: #146 - Update CellRenderer to handle both static and dynamic cells
- **Phase 9**: #147 - Migrate all tests and validate acceptance criteria

---

## Original Issue Description

(Keep existing issue description below this line)
## Problem Statement

Current `RailwayNetGrid` uses a non-generic `Cell` type with no compile-time distinction between editing and simulation contexts. Simulation contexts maintain a parallel `IdentityHashMap` for dynamic wrappers, requiring explicit `context.toDynamic()` calls throughout the simulation code.

## Current Architecture

- **Non-generic interface**: `RailwayNetGrid : Iterable<Map.Entry<Point, Cell>>`
- **Editing phase**: Grid contains static cells (RailSwitch, RailSemaphore, InOut)
- **Simulation phase**: Grid remains static; dynamic wrappers managed separately via `IdentityHashMap<PathSeparator, DynamicPathSeparator>`
- **Conversion**: `SimulationContext.toDynamic()` converts static objects to dynamic wrappers on demand

See [STATIC_DYNAMIC_SEPARATION_ARCHITECTURE.md](../STATIC_DYNAMIC_SEPARATION_ARCHITECTURE.md) for complete details.

## Proposed Solution

### Type Parameterization

- **Parameterize RailwayNetGrid**: `interface RailwayNetGrid<out T : Cell>`
- **EditingContext**: Uses `RailwayNetGrid<NodeCell>` containing static cells only
- **SimulationContext**: Uses `RailwayNetGrid<DynamicPathSeparator>` containing dynamic wrappers directly
- **Context interface**: Parameterized as `Context<C : Cell>` with grid type parameter

### Grid Transformation

When transitioning from editing to simulation, grid contents are "upgraded" from static to dynamic:

```kotlin
// Editing phase
val editingContext: EditingContext // Has RailwayNetGrid<NodeCell>
editingContext.putCell(point, RailSwitch(...)) // Static cell

// Simulation phase
val simulationContext: SimulationContext // Has RailwayNetGrid<DynamicPathSeparator>
// Grid transformed: RailSwitch → DynamicRailSwitch
val cell = simulationContext.getRailWayNetGrid().getCellAt(x, y) // Returns DynamicRailSwitch
cell.setUpPath(...) // Direct access, no toDynamic() needed
```

## Potential Benefits

1. **Type safety**: Compile-time enforcement that editing contexts cannot access dynamic state
2. **Simplified simulation code**: Direct grid access without manual `toDynamic()` wrapping
3. **Code clarity**: Method signatures self-document whether they work with static or dynamic cells
4. **Eliminate IdentityHashMap**: Dynamic wrappers stored directly in grid, not separate mapping
5. **IDE support**: Better type inference and autocomplete
6. **Extensibility**: Future grid implementations can specialize on cell type

## Challenges and Considerations

- **Major architectural change**: Complete redesign of static/dynamic separation pattern
- **Grid transformation logic**: Need to "upgrade" grid contents when starting simulation
- **Backward compatibility**: Requires changes to all grid consumers and simulation code
- **Type complexity**: Adds type parameters throughout Context, factories, and GUI components
- **Testing**: All 662 tests must pass; golden output must remain identical
- **jDisco compatibility**: Must not break current jDisco simulation integration
- **Identity preservation**: Must maintain stable object identity during grid transformation

## Design Questions

1. How to handle grid transformation from `RailwayNetGrid<NodeCell>` to `RailwayNetGrid<DynamicPathSeparator>`?
2. Should transformation create new grid or mutate existing grid?
3. How to preserve object identity during transformation (for `===` comparisons)?
4. Should paths continue to store static objects or switch to dynamic?
5. Does visualization layer (CellRenderer) need to handle both static and dynamic cells?
6. How does this interact with XML serialization (save/load)?

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Design document for grid transformation strategy
- [x] Analysis of identity preservation during transformation
- [x] Prototype implementation demonstrating feasibility
- [x] All 662 tests pass with identical golden output
- [x] No performance degradation
- [x] Compatible with jDisco migration plans (LONG_TERM_GOALS.md)
- [x] Updated architecture documentation

## Constraints

- Per CLAUDE.md: `sim/` package is RESTRICTED (jDisco migration pending)
- Must coordinate with future jDisco → DSOL/Kalasim migration
- Changes must align with LONG_TERM_GOALS.md objectives

## Related

- Parent: #92
- Architecture: STATIC_DYNAMIC_SEPARATION_ARCHITECTURE.md
- Context design: CONTEXT_REFACTORING_DESIGN.md

**Complexity:** HIGH - Major architectural change affecting entire codebase
**Priority:** Medium - Improves type safety but current architecture works

mentioned_issues.title: Context Inheritance Incompatibility: SimulationContext cannot extend EditingContext
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary

`DefaultSimulationContext` currently extends `DefaultEditingContext`, but this inheritance relationship is **architecturally incompatible** with the Grid Parameterization design (#131/#139) and violates the principle that simulation contexts have **immutable network structures**.

**See full analysis:** [`docs/CONTEXT_INHERITANCE_INCOMPATIBILITY.md`](https://github.com/bedaHovorka/interlockSim/blob/feature/simulation_contect_not_extends_of_editing/docs/CONTEXT_INHERITANCE_INCOMPATIBILITY.md)

## Core Issues

1. **Type parameter conflicts**: Editing and simulation contexts require different parameterized grids (static vs. dynamic cells)
2. **Interface Segregation Principle violation**: Simulation contexts should NOT support editing operations (putCell, removeCell, moveCell)
3. **Liskov Substitution Principle concerns**: Cannot safely substitute DefaultSimulationContext for DefaultEditingContext
4. **Immutability assumptions**: Simulation network structure must be frozen at initialization time

## Current Architecture Problem

```kotlin
// CURRENT (problematic):
class DefaultSimulationContext : DefaultEditingContext, SimulationContext {
    // ❌ Inherits mutable editing operations
    // ❌ Shares grid with static cells
    // ❌ Cannot have independent grid parameterization
}
```

## Proposed Solution: Composition over Inheritance

```kotlin
// PROPOSED:
abstract class BaseContext : Context<Cell> {
    // Shared utilities
}

class DefaultEditingContext : BaseContext, EditingContext {
    private val railwayNetGrid: RailwayNetGrid<Cell>  // Static cells
    // ✅ Mutable operations: putCell, removeCell, moveCell
}

class DefaultSimulationContext : BaseContext, SimulationContext {
    private val railwayNetGrid: RailwayNetGrid<Cell>  // Dynamic wrappers
    // ✅ NO editing operations
    // ✅ Immutable network structure
}
```

## Implementation Phases (14 days)

1. **Phase 1**: Create BaseContext abstract class (2 days)
2. **Phase 2**: Refactor DefaultSimulationContext to use BaseContext (3 days)
3. **Phase 3**: Update Interface Hierarchy (2 days)
4. **Phase 4**: Parameterize Grids - Integration with #131 (5 days)
5. **Phase 5**: Documentation and Testing (2 days)

## Impact

- **Breaking Changes**: SimulationContext will no longer extend EditingContext
- **New Tests Required**: 20-30 tests for context transformation and immutability
- **Migration**: Code assuming inheritance will need updates
- **Benefits**: 
  - Clear architectural separation
  - Type-safe grid parameterization
  - Enforced immutability for simulation
  - Better alignment with SOLID principles

## Related Issues

- Parent: #92 (Context Refactoring)
- Related: #131 (Grid Parameterization), #139 (Grid Parameterization Design)
- Foundation: #98 (Context split), #100 (Static/Dynamic Separation)
- Type params: #149 (RailwayNetGrid), #151 (Context hierarchy)

## Decision Points

1. **Shared Functionality Approach**: BaseContext abstract class vs ContextHelper delegation
2. **Graph Parameterization**: Should simulation use `ExtendedUnorientedGraph<Point, DynamicTrack, Segment>`?
3. **Migration Strategy**: Big-bang refactor vs incremental
4. **Immutability Enforcement**: Compile-time only vs compile-time + runtime

## Approval Required From

- **traffic-simulation-expert** - Simulation correctness, immutability assumptions
- **kotlin-tech-lead** - Architecture, type parameterization, design patterns
- **java-senior-dev** - Legacy code compatibility, migration risks
- **railway-civil-engineer** - Domain validation, network immutability requirements

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] SimulationContext does not extend EditingContext
- [x] Both contexts extend only Context<Cell> or BaseContext
- [ ] Editing operations not available in SimulationContext interface
- [ ] Context transformation factory implemented
- [ ] Immutability enforcement in place
- [ ] All existing tests pass (662 tests)
- [ ] New tests added (20-30 for refactoring + 45-65 from #139)
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [ ] Architecture diagrams reflect new structure

---

**Document**: 828 lines of comprehensive analysis
**Sub-issue of**: #92

## Current Architecture

- **Editing phase**: Grid contains static cells (RailSwitch, RailSemaphore, InOut)
- **Simulation phase**: Grid remains static; dynamic wrappers managed separately via `IdentityHashMap<PathSeparator, DynamicPathSeparator>`
- **Conversion**: `SimulationContext.toDynamic()` converts static objects to dynamic wrappers on demand

See [STATIC_DYNAMIC_SEPARATION_ARCHITECTURE.md](../STATIC_DYNAMIC_SEPARATION_ARCHITECTURE.md) for complete details.

- **Parameterize RailwayNetGrid**: `interface RailwayNetGrid<out T : Cell>`
- **EditingContext**: Uses `RailwayNetGrid<NodeCell>` containing static cells only
- **SimulationContext**: Uses `RailwayNetGrid<DynamicPathSeparator>` containing dynamic wrappers directly
- **Context interface**: Parameterized as `Context<C : Cell>` with grid type parameter

### Grid Transformation

When transitioning from editing to simulation, grid contents are "upgraded" from static to dynamic:

```kotlin
// Editing phase
val editingContext: EditingContext // Has RailwayNetGrid<NodeCell>
editingContext.putCell(point, RailSwitch(...)) // Static cell

// Simulation phase
val simulationContext: SimulationContext // Has RailwayNetGrid<DynamicPathSeparator>
// Grid transformed: RailSwitch → DynamicRailSwitch
```

1. **Type safety**: Compile-time enforcement that editing contexts cannot access dynamic state

- **Major architectural change**: Complete redesign of static/dynamic separation pattern

- **Backward compatibility**: Requires changes to all grid consumers and simulation code

mentioned_issues.title: Context Inheritance Incompatibility: SimulationContext cannot extend EditingContext
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary

`DefaultSimulationContext` currently extends `DefaultEditingContext`, but this inheritance relationship is **architecturally incompatible** with the Grid Parameterization design (#131/#139) and violates the principle that simulation contexts have **immutable network structures**.

**See full analysis:** [`docs/CONTEXT_INHERITANCE_INCOMPATIBILITY.md`](https://github.com/bedaHovorka/interlockSim/blob/feature/simulation_contect_not_extends_of_editing/docs/CONTEXT_INHERITANCE_INCOMPATIBILITY.md)

## Core Issues

1. **Type parameter conflicts**: Editing and simulation contexts require different parameterized grids (static vs. dynamic cells)
2. **Interface Segregation Principle violation**: Simulation contexts should NOT support editing operations (putCell, removeCell, moveCell)
3. **Liskov Substitution Principle concerns**: Cannot safely substitute DefaultSimulationContext for DefaultEditingContext
4. **Immutability assumptions**: Simulation network structure must be frozen at initialization time

## Current Architecture Problem

```kotlin
// CURRENT (problematic):
class DefaultSimulationContext : DefaultEditingContext, SimulationContext {
    // ❌ Inherits mutable editing operations
    // ❌ Shares grid with static cells
    // ❌ Cannot have independent grid parameterization
}
```

## Proposed Solution: Composition over Inheritance

```kotlin
// PROPOSED:
abstract class BaseContext : Context<Cell> {
    // Shared utilities
}

class DefaultEditingContext : BaseContext, EditingContext {
    private val railwayNetGrid: RailwayNetGrid<Cell>  // Static cells
    // ✅ Mutable operations: putCell, removeCell, moveCell
}

class DefaultSimulationContext : BaseContext, SimulationContext {
    private val railwayNetGrid: RailwayNetGrid<Cell>  // Dynamic wrappers
    // ✅ NO editing operations
    // ✅ Immutable network structure
}
```

## Implementation Phases (14 days)

1. **Phase 1**: Create BaseContext abstract class (2 days)
2. **Phase 2**: Refactor DefaultSimulationContext to use BaseContext (3 days)
3. **Phase 3**: Update Interface Hierarchy (2 days)
4. **Phase 4**: Parameterize Grids - Integration with #131 (5 days)
5. **Phase 5**: Documentation and Testing (2 days)

## Impact

- **Breaking Changes**: SimulationContext will no longer extend EditingContext
- **New Tests Required**: 20-30 tests for context transformation and immutability
- **Migration**: Code assuming inheritance will need updates
- **Benefits**: 
  - Clear architectural separation
  - Type-safe grid parameterization
  - Enforced immutability for simulation
  - Better alignment with SOLID principles

- Related: #131 (Grid Parameterization), #139 (Grid Parameterization Design)

2. **Graph Parameterization**: Should simulation use `ExtendedUnorientedGraph<Point, DynamicTrack, Segment>`?
3. **Migration Strategy**: Big-bang refactor vs incremental
4. **Immutability Enforcement**: Compile-time only vs compile-time + runtime

## Description

- Avoids memory duplication and synchronization issues

- Grid management (RailwayNetGrid storage and access)
- Graph management (ExtendedUnorientedGraph storage and access)
- PropertyChangeSupport and listener management
- Configuration properties (currentMaxSpeed, currentTrackLength, currentNameString)
- Track block mappings and queries

mentioned_issues.title: Context Inheritance Incompatibility: SimulationContext cannot extend EditingContext
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary

`DefaultSimulationContext` currently extends `DefaultEditingContext`, but this inheritance relationship is **architecturally incompatible** with the Grid Parameterization design (#131/#139) and violates the principle that simulation contexts have **immutable network structures**.

**See full analysis:** [`docs/CONTEXT_INHERITANCE_INCOMPATIBILITY.md`](https://github.com/bedaHovorka/interlockSim/blob/feature/simulation_contect_not_extends_of_editing/docs/CONTEXT_INHERITANCE_INCOMPATIBILITY.md)

## Core Issues

1. **Type parameter conflicts**: Editing and simulation contexts require different parameterized grids (static vs. dynamic cells)
2. **Interface Segregation Principle violation**: Simulation contexts should NOT support editing operations (putCell, removeCell, moveCell)
3. **Liskov Substitution Principle concerns**: Cannot safely substitute DefaultSimulationContext for DefaultEditingContext
4. **Immutability assumptions**: Simulation network structure must be frozen at initialization time

## Current Architecture Problem

```kotlin
// CURRENT (problematic):
class DefaultSimulationContext : DefaultEditingContext, SimulationContext {
    // ❌ Inherits mutable editing operations
    // ❌ Shares grid with static cells
    // ❌ Cannot have independent grid parameterization
}
```

## Proposed Solution: Composition over Inheritance

```kotlin
// PROPOSED:
abstract class BaseContext : Context<Cell> {
    // Shared utilities
}

class DefaultEditingContext : BaseContext, EditingContext {
    private val railwayNetGrid: RailwayNetGrid<Cell>  // Static cells
    // ✅ Mutable operations: putCell, removeCell, moveCell
}

class DefaultSimulationContext : BaseContext, SimulationContext {
    private val railwayNetGrid: RailwayNetGrid<Cell>  // Dynamic wrappers
    // ✅ NO editing operations
    // ✅ Immutable network structure
}
```

## Implementation Phases (14 days)

1. **Phase 1**: Create BaseContext abstract class (2 days)
2. **Phase 2**: Refactor DefaultSimulationContext to use BaseContext (3 days)
3. **Phase 3**: Update Interface Hierarchy (2 days)
4. **Phase 4**: Parameterize Grids - Integration with #131 (5 days)
5. **Phase 5**: Documentation and Testing (2 days)

## Impact

- **Breaking Changes**: SimulationContext will no longer extend EditingContext
- **New Tests Required**: 20-30 tests for context transformation and immutability
- **Migration**: Code assuming inheritance will need updates
- **Benefits**: 
  - Clear architectural separation
  - Type-safe grid parameterization
  - Enforced immutability for simulation
  - Better alignment with SOLID principles

- Parent: #92 (Context Refactoring)
- Related: #131 (Grid Parameterization), #139 (Grid Parameterization Design)
- Foundation: #98 (Context split), #100 (Static/Dynamic Separation)
- Type params: #149 (RailwayNetGrid), #151 (Context hierarchy)

1. **Shared Functionality Approach**: BaseContext abstract class vs ContextHelper delegation
2. **Graph Parameterization**: Should simulation use `ExtendedUnorientedGraph<Point, DynamicTrack, Segment>`?
3. **Migration Strategy**: Big-bang refactor vs incremental
4. **Immutability Enforcement**: Compile-time only vs compile-time + runtime

- **kotlin-tech-lead** - Architecture, type parameterization, design patterns
- **java-senior-dev** - Legacy code compatibility, migration risks
- **railway-civil-engineer** - Domain validation, network immutability requirements

- [ ] Immutability enforcement in place

mentioned_issues.title: Context Inheritance Incompatibility: SimulationContext cannot extend EditingContext
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary

`DefaultSimulationContext` currently extends `DefaultEditingContext`, but this inheritance relationship is **architecturally incompatible** with the Grid Parameterization design (#131/#139) and violates the principle that simulation contexts have **immutable network structures**.

**See full analysis:** [`docs/CONTEXT_INHERITANCE_INCOMPATIBILITY.md`](https://github.com/bedaHovorka/interlockSim/blob/feature/simulation_contect_not_extends_of_editing/docs/CONTEXT_INHERITANCE_INCOMPATIBILITY.md)

## Core Issues

1. **Type parameter conflicts**: Editing and simulation contexts require different parameterized grids (static vs. dynamic cells)
2. **Interface Segregation Principle violation**: Simulation contexts should NOT support editing operations (putCell, removeCell, moveCell)
3. **Liskov Substitution Principle concerns**: Cannot safely substitute DefaultSimulationContext for DefaultEditingContext
4. **Immutability assumptions**: Simulation network structure must be frozen at initialization time

## Current Architecture Problem

```kotlin
// CURRENT (problematic):
class DefaultSimulationContext : DefaultEditingContext, SimulationContext {
    // ❌ Inherits mutable editing operations
    // ❌ Shares grid with static cells
    // ❌ Cannot have independent grid parameterization
}
```

## Proposed Solution: Composition over Inheritance

```kotlin
// PROPOSED:
abstract class BaseContext : Context<Cell> {
    // Shared utilities
}

class DefaultEditingContext : BaseContext, EditingContext {
    private val railwayNetGrid: RailwayNetGrid<Cell>  // Static cells
    // ✅ Mutable operations: putCell, removeCell, moveCell
}

class DefaultSimulationContext : BaseContext, SimulationContext {
    private val railwayNetGrid: RailwayNetGrid<Cell>  // Dynamic wrappers
    // ✅ NO editing operations
    // ✅ Immutable network structure
}
```

## Implementation Phases (14 days)

1. **Phase 1**: Create BaseContext abstract class (2 days)
2. **Phase 2**: Refactor DefaultSimulationContext to use BaseContext (3 days)
3. **Phase 3**: Update Interface Hierarchy (2 days)
4. **Phase 4**: Parameterize Grids - Integration with #131 (5 days)
5. **Phase 5**: Documentation and Testing (2 days)

## Impact

- **Breaking Changes**: SimulationContext will no longer extend EditingContext
- **New Tests Required**: 20-30 tests for context transformation and immutability
- **Migration**: Code assuming inheritance will need updates
- **Benefits**: 
  - Clear architectural separation
  - Type-safe grid parameterization
  - Enforced immutability for simulation
  - Better alignment with SOLID principles

## Related Issues

- Parent: #92 (Context Refactoring)
- Related: #131 (Grid Parameterization), #139 (Grid Parameterization Design)
- Foundation: #98 (Context split), #100 (Static/Dynamic Separation)
- Type params: #149 (RailwayNetGrid), #151 (Context hierarchy)

## Decision Points

1. **Shared Functionality Approach**: BaseContext abstract class vs ContextHelper delegation
2. **Graph Parameterization**: Should simulation use `ExtendedUnorientedGraph<Point, DynamicTrack, Segment>`?
3. **Migration Strategy**: Big-bang refactor vs incremental
4. **Immutability Enforcement**: Compile-time only vs compile-time + runtime

mentioned_issues.title: Issue #153.8: Enforce Simulation Network Immutability
mentioned_issues.body:
**Parent Issue**: #153 - Context Inheritance Incompatibility
**Phase**: 5 - Immutability Enforcement
**Priority**: MEDIUM
**Estimate**: 2 days
**Dependencies**: #164 (Issue #153.7)

## Description

Enforce that simulation contexts have immutable network structures - once initialized, the railway network cannot be modified.

## Rationale

Simulation correctness depends on static network topology. Allowing runtime modification would:
- Invalidate pre-computed paths
- Break dynamic wrapper mappings
- Cause undefined behavior in running simulations
- Violate simulation physics assumptions

## Immutability Levels

**Level 1: Compile-time (Interface Segregation)** - ✅ Already achieved by removing EditingContext from SimulationContext (Issue #153.5)

**Level 2: Runtime (Defensive Programming)** - Add runtime checks, throw `UnsupportedOperationException`

**Level 3: Data Structure (Immutable Grid)** - Wrap simulation grid in read-only view

**Recommended**: Level 1 + Level 2

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `frozen: Boolean` flag to BaseContext (default false)
- [ ] Add `freeze()` method to mark context as immutable
- [ ] Call `freeze()` in DefaultSimulationContext after initialization
- [ ] Override grid modification methods to check frozen flag
- [ ] Add tests for immutability enforcement (10-15 tests)
- [ ] Document immutability contract in SimulationContext KDoc

## Test Coverage

- Attempt to putCell on frozen context → exception
- Attempt to removeCell on frozen context → exception
- Attempt to moveCell on frozen context → exception
- Verify freeze() is idempotent
- Verify editing context remains mutable

## Acceptance Criteria

- ✅ SimulationContext network structure immutable after initialization
- ✅ Clear exception messages when modification attempted
- ✅ EditingContext remains mutable
- ✅ 10-15 immutability tests added
- ✅ Documentation updated

mentioned_issues.title: Issue #153.8.5: Expose freeze/isFrozen API in EditingContext interface
mentioned_issues.body:
**Parent Issue**: #153 - Context Inheritance Incompatibility
**Phase**: 5.5 - API Enhancement (BEFORE Phase 6 tests)
**Priority**: HIGH
**Estimate**: 0.5 days
**Dependencies**: #165 (Issue #153.8)
**Blocks**: #168 (Issue #153.9)

## Description

Expose `freeze()` and `isFrozen()` methods in the `EditingContext` interface to allow tests to verify immutability enforcement without requiring concrete type casts.

## Problem

ContextImmutabilityTest.kt.disabled contains 15 comprehensive tests but fails to compile because:
- Tests call `context.freeze()` and `context.isFrozen()` on `EditingContext` interface
- These methods exist only in `BaseContext` implementation
- Tests would need ugly casts: `(context as DefaultEditingContext).freeze()`

## Solution

Add freeze operations to `EditingContext` interface:

```kotlin
interface EditingContext : Context<Cell> {
    /**
     * Freeze this context, making the network structure immutable.
     * After freezing, editing operations will throw UnsupportedOperationException.
     * This is typically called before converting to SimulationContext.
     */
    fun freeze()
    
    /**
     * Check if this context is frozen (immutable).
     * @return true if context is frozen and modifications are not allowed
     */
    fun isFrozen(): Boolean
    
    // Existing editing operations...
    fun putCell(key: Point, cell: NodeCell)
    fun removeCell(key: Point)
    fun moveCell(from: Point, to: Point)
    fun joinCells(key1: Point, key2: Point, trackBlock: TrackBlock)
    fun removeLine(block: TrackBlock)
    // ...
}
```

## Implementation

1. **Update EditingContext.kt**
   - Add `freeze()` method declaration
   - Add `isFrozen(): Boolean` method declaration
   - Add comprehensive KDoc documentation

2. **Verify DefaultEditingContext.kt**
   - Already implements these methods via BaseContext
   - No changes needed

3. **Build and verify**
   - `./gradlew build`
   - All 837 unit tests should pass
   - No behavioral changes

## Rationale

### Why expose in interface?

1. **Clean API** - freeze() is a legitimate editing context operation
   - Users build networks in editing context
   - Users may want to freeze before manual conversion
   - Explicit freeze() clearer than implicit conversion freeze

2. **Type Safety** - works with interface references
   - No casts needed: `val context: EditingContext = ...context.freeze()`
   - Tests use interface types, not concrete implementations

3. **Minimal Changes** - just expose existing BaseContext methods
   - Implementation already exists in BaseContext
   - DefaultEditingContext inherits from BaseContext
   - Zero new code, just API exposure

4. **Test Enablement** - allows ContextImmutabilityTest.kt to compile
   - 15 tests can be re-enabled without modification
   - Tests verify immutability contract correctly

### Alternative: Why NOT cast to concrete types?

```kotlin
// BAD: Ugly casts in tests
val context = factory.createEmptyContext()
(context as DefaultEditingContext).freeze()  // ❌ Breaks abstraction
```

This approach:
- ❌ Breaks abstraction - tests depend on concrete types
- ❌ Brittle - breaks if factory returns different implementation
- ❌ Poor API design - forces users to know implementation details

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `freeze()` method added to EditingContext interface with KDoc
- [ ] `isFrozen()` method added to EditingContext interface with KDoc
- [ ] DefaultEditingContext implementation unchanged (inherits from BaseContext)
- [ ] All existing tests pass (837 unit tests, 90 integration tests)
- [ ] No behavioral changes
- [ ] Code compiles without warnings
- [ ] Ready for #168 to re-enable ContextImmutabilityTest.kt

## Files to Modify

- `src/main/kotlin/cz/vutbr/fit/interlockSim/context/EditingContext.kt` - Add method declarations

## Testing

- Existing tests cover BaseContext.freeze() implementation
- #168 will add 15 immutability tests when re-enabled
- No new tests needed in THIS issue (just API exposure)

## Success Criteria

✅ EditingContext interface has freeze/isFrozen methods
✅ Build passes: `./gradlew build`
✅ All 927 tests pass
✅ ContextImmutabilityTest.kt.disabled can be compiled (verified manually)
✅ No warnings or errors
✅ Ready for #168 to proceed

---

**Note:** This is a prerequisite for #168. Complete this BEFORE attempting to re-enable ContextImmutabilityTest.kt.

mentioned_issues.title: Context Inheritance Incompatibility: SimulationContext cannot extend EditingContext
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary

`DefaultSimulationContext` currently extends `DefaultEditingContext`, but this inheritance relationship is **architecturally incompatible** with the Grid Parameterization design (#131/#139) and violates the principle that simulation contexts have **immutable network structures**.

**See full analysis:** [`docs/CONTEXT_INHERITANCE_INCOMPATIBILITY.md`](https://github.com/bedaHovorka/interlockSim/blob/feature/simulation_contect_not_extends_of_editing/docs/CONTEXT_INHERITANCE_INCOMPATIBILITY.md)

## Core Issues

1. **Type parameter conflicts**: Editing and simulation contexts require different parameterized grids (static vs. dynamic cells)
2. **Interface Segregation Principle violation**: Simulation contexts should NOT support editing operations (putCell, removeCell, moveCell)
3. **Liskov Substitution Principle concerns**: Cannot safely substitute DefaultSimulationContext for DefaultEditingContext
4. **Immutability assumptions**: Simulation network structure must be frozen at initialization time

## Current Architecture Problem

```kotlin
// CURRENT (problematic):
class DefaultSimulationContext : DefaultEditingContext, SimulationContext {
    // ❌ Inherits mutable editing operations
    // ❌ Shares grid with static cells
    // ❌ Cannot have independent grid parameterization
}
```

## Proposed Solution: Composition over Inheritance

```kotlin
// PROPOSED:
abstract class BaseContext : Context<Cell> {
    // Shared utilities
}

class DefaultEditingContext : BaseContext, EditingContext {
    private val railwayNetGrid: RailwayNetGrid<Cell>  // Static cells
    // ✅ Mutable operations: putCell, removeCell, moveCell
}

class DefaultSimulationContext : BaseContext, SimulationContext {
    private val railwayNetGrid: RailwayNetGrid<Cell>  // Dynamic wrappers
    // ✅ NO editing operations
    // ✅ Immutable network structure
}
```

## Implementation Phases (14 days)

1. **Phase 1**: Create BaseContext abstract class (2 days)
2. **Phase 2**: Refactor DefaultSimulationContext to use BaseContext (3 days)
3. **Phase 3**: Update Interface Hierarchy (2 days)
4. **Phase 4**: Parameterize Grids - Integration with #131 (5 days)
5. **Phase 5**: Documentation and Testing (2 days)

## Impact

- **Breaking Changes**: SimulationContext will no longer extend EditingContext
- **New Tests Required**: 20-30 tests for context transformation and immutability
- **Migration**: Code assuming inheritance will need updates
- **Benefits**: 
  - Clear architectural separation
  - Type-safe grid parameterization
  - Enforced immutability for simulation
  - Better alignment with SOLID principles

## Related Issues

- Parent: #92 (Context Refactoring)
- Related: #131 (Grid Parameterization), #139 (Grid Parameterization Design)
- Foundation: #98 (Context split), #100 (Static/Dynamic Separation)
- Type params: #149 (RailwayNetGrid), #151 (Context hierarchy)

## Decision Points

1. **Shared Functionality Approach**: BaseContext abstract class vs ContextHelper delegation
2. **Graph Parameterization**: Should simulation use `ExtendedUnorientedGraph<Point, DynamicTrack, Segment>`?
3. **Migration Strategy**: Big-bang refactor vs incremental
4. **Immutability Enforcement**: Compile-time only vs compile-time + runtime

## Approval Required From

- **traffic-simulation-expert** - Simulation correctness, immutability assumptions
- **kotlin-tech-lead** - Architecture, type parameterization, design patterns
- **java-senior-dev** - Legacy code compatibility, migration risks
- **railway-civil-engineer** - Domain validation, network immutability requirements

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] SimulationContext does not extend EditingContext
- [x] Both contexts extend only Context<Cell> or BaseContext
- [ ] Editing operations not available in SimulationContext interface
- [ ] Context transformation factory implemented
- [ ] Immutability enforcement in place
- [ ] All existing tests pass (662 tests)
- [ ] New tests added (20-30 for refactoring + 45-65 from #139)
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [ ] Architecture diagrams reflect new structure

closing_issues.title: Pre-Wrap All Tracks at Initialization
closing_issues.body:
# Issue #214: Pre-Wrap All Tracks at Initialization

**Type:** Enhancement / Consistency
**Priority:** Low
**Estimate:** 1 day
**Related Issues:** #153, #100

---

## Problem Statement

The static/dynamic separation architecture creates **dynamic wrappers** for simulation objects, but the wrapping strategy is **inconsistent**:

- **PathSeparators (InOut, RailSemaphore, RailSwitch):** Wrapped **eagerly** at initialization via `GridTransformer`
- **Tracks (SimpleTrackBlock):** Wrapped **lazily** on first `toDynamic()` call

### Current Behavior

```kotlin
// PathSeparators (EAGER):
// Created during fromEditingContext() → GridTransformer.transformGrid()
val dynamicSep = context.toDynamic(railSemaphore)  // Instant lookup, wrapper already exists

// Tracks (LAZY):
// Created on-demand during first toDynamic() call
val dynamicTrack = context.toDynamic(simpleTrackBlock)  // Creates wrapper if not exists
```

**Code Location:** `DefaultSimulationContext.toDynamic()` lines ~900-950

---

## Impact Analysis

### Inconsistency
- Two different strategies for same pattern (wrapper creation)
- Developers must remember which objects are eager vs lazy
- Surprising behavior (some wrappers exist, some don't)

### Performance
- Lazy creation adds overhead on first access
- Unpredictable timing (first access slower than subsequent)
- No benefit from lazy evaluation (all tracks eventually wrapped)

### Debugging
- Some wrappers exist at `run()` start, some don't
- Memory layout changes during execution
- Harder to debug missing wrapper issues

### Memory
- Minor: Wrappers created eventually anyway
- Eager wrapping makes memory usage predictable

---

## Proposed Solution

Wrap **all tracks eagerly** during `DefaultSimulationContext.run()` initialization, matching the eager wrapping of path separators.

### Implementation

#### Step 1: Add Track Wrapper Initialization

```kotlin
// In DefaultSimulationContext class

/**
 * Initialize dynamic wrappers for all tracks.
 * Called during run() initialization to ensure all tracks have wrappers upfront.
 */
private fun initializeTrackWrappers() {
    val trackWrappers = mutableMapOf<SimpleTrackBlock, DynamicTrack>()

    // Iterate through all track blocks in the graph
    for (entry in extendedUnorientedGraph.entrySet()) {
        val trackBlock = entry.value
        if (trackBlock is SimpleTrackBlock) {
            // Create wrapper if not already exists
            if (trackBlock !in trackToDynamicMap) {
                val wrapper = DynamicTrack(trackBlock)
                trackToDynamicMap[trackBlock] = wrapper
                trackWrappers[trackBlock] = wrapper
            }
        }
    }

    logger.debug { "Initialized ${trackWrappers.size} track wrappers eagerly" }
}
```

#### Step 2: Call During Initialization

```kotlin
override fun run() {
    if (running) return

    // Existing initialization...

    // NEW: Pre-wrap all tracks (matching separator wrapping)
    initializeTrackWrappers()

    // Existing: Freeze after initialization
    freeze()

    // ... rest of run() method
}
```

#### Step 3: Simplify toDynamic()

```kotlin
// BEFORE (lazy creation):
fun toDynamic(track: SimpleTrackBlock): DynamicTrack {
    return trackToDynamicMap.getOrPut(track) {
        DynamicTrack(track)  // Create on-demand
    }
}

// AFTER (eager lookup):
fun toDynamic(track: SimpleTrackBlock): DynamicTrack {
    return trackToDynamicMap[track]
        ?: throw SimulationException(
            "Track $track has no dynamic wrapper. " +
            "This indicates initialization did not complete correctly."
        )
}
```

**Rationale:** If all tracks are wrapped at initialization, `toDynamic()` should never need to create wrappers. A missing wrapper indicates a bug.

---

## Benefits

✅ **Consistency** - All dynamic wrappers created at same time (initialization)
✅ **Predictability** - Memory layout stable after `run()` initialization
✅ **Performance** - No lazy creation overhead during simulation
✅ **Debugging** - All wrappers exist upfront (easier to inspect state)
✅ **Error detection** - Missing wrapper is immediate error, not lazy fallback

---

## Trade-offs

### Memory Overhead
- **Before:** Wrappers created on-demand (might save memory if some tracks never accessed)
- **After:** All tracks wrapped upfront

**Analysis:** In practice, all tracks are accessed during simulation, so lazy evaluation provides no real benefit.

### Initialization Time
- **Before:** Fast `run()` start, slower first track access
- **After:** Slightly slower `run()` start, instant track access

**Analysis:** Minimal impact (track wrapper creation is lightweight). Predictability outweighs minor initialization cost.

---

## Files to Modify

1. **`src/main/kotlin/cz/vutbr/fit/interlockSim/context/DefaultSimulationContext.kt`**
   - Add `initializeTrackWrappers()` method
   - Call in `run()` initialization
   - Update `toDynamic(SimpleTrackBlock)` to fail if wrapper missing

2. **Tests**
   - Verify all tracks wrapped after `run()` initialization
   - Verify `toDynamic()` throws if wrapper missing (should never happen)
   - Performance test (ensure no significant slowdown)

---

## Test Requirements

### New Unit Tests (3 tests)

1. **All tracks wrapped after initialization**
   ```kotlin
   @Test
   fun `all tracks have wrappers after run initialization`() {
       val context = createSimulationContextWithTracks()
       context.run()

       // Verify all tracks in graph have wrappers
       for (entry in context.getGraph().entrySet()) {
           val trackBlock = entry.value
           if (trackBlock is SimpleTrackBlock) {
               val wrapper = context.toDynamic(trackBlock)
               assertThat(wrapper).isNotNull()
           }
       }
   }
   ```

2. **toDynamic throws if track not wrapped**
   ```kotlin
   @Test
   fun `toDynamic throws for unwrapped track`() {
       val context = createEmptySimulationContext()
       val orphanTrack = SimpleTrackBlock(...)

       // Should throw because track not in context
       assertThrows<SimulationException> {
           context.toDynamic(orphanTrack)
       }
   }
   ```

3. **No performance regression**
   ```kotlin
   @Test
   fun `initialization time acceptable`() {
       val context = createLargeSimulationContext(100, 100)
       val start = System.currentTimeMillis()

       context.run()

       val duration = System.currentTimeMillis() - start
       assertThat(duration).isLessThan(5000)  // 5 seconds max
   }
   ```

### Existing Tests
- [ ] All 927 tests still passing
- [ ] No regressions in simulation behavior

---

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `initializeTrackWrappers()` method implemented
- [ ] Called during `run()` initialization (before freeze)
- [ ] `toDynamic(SimpleTrackBlock)` throws if wrapper missing
- [ ] All tracks wrapped after initialization
- [ ] 3 new unit tests passing
- [ ] All 927 existing tests still passing
- [ ] No significant performance regression (< 5% initialization slowdown)

---

## Alternative: Keep Lazy Wrapping

If eager wrapping proves problematic (performance, memory), document the **intentional inconsistency** instead:

```kotlin
/**
 * Dynamic wrapper strategy:
 * - PathSeparators: Eager (via GridTransformer at initialization)
 * - Tracks: Lazy (created on first toDynamic() call)
 *
 * Rationale: Tracks may be numerous and not all accessed during simulation.
 * Lazy creation saves memory for unused tracks.
 */
```

**However:** Exploration suggests all tracks are accessed, so eager wrapping is preferable.

---

**Priority Justification:** Low - Functional correctness not affected, but consistency and predictability are valuable for maintainability. Consider as polish after higher-priority issues.

**Effort:** 1 day (implementation + testing)

mentioned_issues.title: Simulation fails
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary of Investigation

I've completed a thorough investigation of the simulation failure. Here are the findings:

### Fixes Successfully Applied

1. ✅ **Train.kt Dynamic wrapper comparisons** - Fixed InOut entry/exit detection to use `.static` property
2. ✅ **Generator termination** - Changed `hold(random.exp(43.0))` to `hold(5.0)` for timely termination response
3. ✅ **ShuntingLoop.kt nextSemaphore comparison** - Added static reference unwrapping to avoid Dynamic wrapper identity mismatches  
4. ✅ **ShuntingLoop.kt isSetUpPath comparison** - Fixed to use static separators (identity comparison requires same object instance)

### Root Cause Identified

The simulation fails because **railway switches create duplicate track segments that share the same name but are different objects**:

- `constructPath(zA, vA, doA1, ...)` creates TWO track blocks both named "vA-around":
  - Block from `zA` to `vA` (switch entrance)
  - Block from `vA` to `doA1` (switch exit)
- Trains enter BOTH segments sequentially (`enter()` called twice with same block name)
- **Only the FIRST segment gets properly reserved** (RESERVED->OCCUPIED)
- **The SECOND segment remains FREE** (never reserved by path setup)
- This causes "Wrong state: FREE, expected: RESERVED" error

### Why Develop Branch Works

The develop branch works because:
- NO Dynamic* wrappers for tracks
- Direct state management in static SimpleTrack objects  
- Path setup and train traversal use the SAME objects
- Both track segments around switches get properly reserved

### Why Current Branch Fails

The `copilot/separate-static-and-dynamic-properties` branch introduced Dynamic* wrappers but the migration is **incomplete**:
- `DynamicTrack` class exists but is NEVER used
- Paths contain Dynamic separators but static tracks  
- Identity comparisons (`===`) fail when mixing static/Dynamic objects
- The second track segment around switches doesn't get reserved

### Recommended Solution

The issue requires architectural analysis beyond quick fixes. The branch attempted to separate static/dynamic properties but this conflicts with how ShuntingLoop reserves multiple track segments for switches. Options:

1. **Revert Dynamic track approach** - Keep only Dynamic separators (Semaphore, Switch, InOut), leave tracks static
2. **Complete Dynamic migration** - Fully implement DynamicTrack usage throughout (major refactoring)
3. **Fix switch path logic** - Ensure both track segments get reserved independently

closing_issues.title: HashMapGraph: Return collection views instead of copies
closing_issues.body:
## Description

Current `HashMapGraph` methods return defensive copies of collections. Consider returning unmodifiable views for better performance.

## Current Code

```kotlin
// src/main/kotlin/cz/vutbr/fit/interlockSim/util/HashMapGraph.kt:162
// EXTENSION pohled ne copii (view not copy)
```

## Motivation

**Performance:** Creating defensive copies for every collection access has O(n) overhead. Unmodifiable views would be O(1).

**Memory:** Views don't duplicate collection data.

## Examples

```kotlin
// Current (copy):
fun getNodes(): Collection<Node> = ArrayList(internalMap.keys)

// Proposed (view):
fun getNodes(): Collection<Node> = Collections.unmodifiableSet(internalMap.keys)
```

## Impact

- **Pros:** Better performance for large graphs, reduced memory usage
- **Cons:** Callers cannot modify returned collections (but they shouldn't anyway)

## Priority

Low - Current implementation is safe and correct, just not optimized

## Related

Could improve performance for Goal 2 (Automatic Path Finding) when traversing large railway networks

closing_issues.title: PlatformIdentity: JVM uses identity hash, native uses value hash — document or fix
closing_issues.body:
## Problem

`PlatformIdentity` has a semantic mismatch between platforms:
- **JVM actual:** uses `System.identityHashCode()` — identity-based (unique per object instance)
- **Native actual:** uses `hashCode()` — value-based (for data classes, two equal objects have the same hash)

This means the same object graph can produce different debug/log output depending on platform, which may cause confusion in diagnostics and tests.

## Options

1. **Document the limitation** — Add KDoc to the `expect` declaration explaining the platform difference
2. **Use `AtomicInt` counter on native** — Allocate a monotonically increasing ID per object for true identity semantics across platforms
3. **Accept the difference** — If only used for logging, document it and move on

## Context

Flagged in PR #399 code review (github-actions, 2026-03-20).

closing_issues.title: ci(fast-sim): build & test in GitHub Actions
closing_issues.body:
## Parent

Part of #413 (`:fast-sim` epic)

## Description

Add CI/CD pipeline for `:fast-sim` — build native binary, run smoke test, upload artifact.

## Recommendation

Add `fast-sim` job to existing `.github/workflows/gradle-java21.yml` (shares Gradle cache).

## Pipeline Configuration

```yaml
fast-sim:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  timeout-minutes: 30
  needs: [build]  # Share Gradle cache with JVM build
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
      with: { distribution: 'temurin', java-version: '21' }
    - run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libxml2-dev
    - name: Install kDisco to mavenLocal
      run: ... # Copy docker-kdisco/ artifacts
    - run: ./gradlew :fast-sim:linkReleaseExecutableLinuxX64
    - run: ./fast-sim --version  # Sanity check
    - name: Smoke test
      run: ... # Run #417 smoke test
    - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: fast-sim-linuxX64
        path: fast-sim/build/bin/linuxX64/releaseExecutable/fast-sim.kexe
        retention-days: 30
```

## Key Notes

- **`libxml2-dev` must be installed** on ubuntu runner (not present by default)
- **30-minute timeout** for Kotlin/Native compilation (can be slow)
- **Job ordering:** build JVM → build native → smoke test → upload artifact
- **Smoke test failure blocks PR merge**
- **Optional:** Docker image build on develop/main branches only

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `fast-sim` job to `gradle-java21.yml`
- [ ] Install `libxml2-dev` in CI step
- [ ] Copy docker-kdisco/ to mavenLocal in CI
- [ ] Build native binary
- [ ] Run smoke test (#417)
- [ ] Upload binary as 30-day artifact

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] CI builds native binary on pushes to feature/fast-sim
- [ ] Smoke test runs as PR check (blocks merge on failure)
- [ ] Binary uploaded as 30-day artifact
- [ ] Total CI time increase < 10 minutes
- [ ] libxml2-dev correctly installed on ubuntu runner

## Risk Register

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| K/N compilation slow (>15 min) | Medium | 30-min timeout; Gradle build cache |
| CI flakiness from smoke test | Medium | Structural comparison only (not timing-sensitive) |
| ubuntu-latest missing C toolchain | Low | Ubuntu has gcc by default; verify |

## LONG_TERM_GOALS Links

- **Goal 6 (Metrics)**: CI can run benchmark tracking over time
- **Goal 10 (AI Dispatcher)**: Produces deployable binary for agent infrastructure

closing_issues.title: feat(fast-sim): graceful SIGINT shutdown with partial results
closing_issues.body:
## Summary

`fast-sim` does not register a POSIX signal handler for SIGINT. Ctrl+C kills the process immediately without printing partial simulation results.

## Current Behavior

No signal handler registered in Main.kt. Process terminates abruptly on SIGINT.

## Proposed Behavior

Per the design spec (#413):
- Register POSIX `signal(SIGINT, handler)` in native Main.kt
- On SIGINT: stop simulation, print partial results via TextReporter, exit with code 130 (Unix convention)
- Ensure Koin is stopped cleanly on signal

## Context

Listed in #413 design spec as "Graceful SIGINT shutdown" but not implemented in the initial delivery. Identified during PR #421 review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] SIGINT stops the running simulation gracefully
- [ ] Partial results printed to stdout before exit
- [ ] Exit code is 130
- [ ] Koin scope cleaned up
- [ ] Test documenting the expected exit code

closing_issues.title: feat(fast-sim): ProcessBuilder-based cross-platform parity test with crash handling
closing_issues.body:
## Parent

Part of #413 (`:fast-sim` epic). Found during #417 retest.

## Problem

Issue #417 spec describes a **ProcessBuilder-based** integration test that:
- Launches JVM JAR and native binary as separate processes
- Captures stdout + stderr from both
- Compares output with structural invariants
- Has 120s timeout per process
- Handles native binary crash gracefully (timeout + stderr capture)

Current implementation uses **in-process** tests on each platform independently. This is functionally sound (10/10 stable, all invariants pass), but:
- No cross-platform output comparison in a single test
- No stderr capture on crash
- No 120s timeout (JVM: 30s/test, Native: none)
- Native hang = test runner hang (unrecoverable)

## What Works Today

- `JvmParityReferenceTest` (6 tests) — in-process JVM invariant checks ✅
- `NativeJvmParityTest` (6 tests) — in-process native invariant checks ✅
- 10/10 stability across consecutive runs ✅

## Proposed Enhancement

Add a JVM-side `@Tag("integration-test")` that uses `ProcessBuilder` to:
1. Run `java -jar interlockSim.jar example shuntingLoop 60` (capture stdout/stderr)
2. Run `fast-sim.kexe example shuntingLoop 60` (capture stdout/stderr)
3. Parse both outputs into event model
4. Compare structural invariants cross-platform
5. 120s `waitFor` timeout per process
6. On failure: print both outputs side-by-side

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Single test compares JVM and native output
- [ ] 120s timeout per process with `ProcessBuilder.waitFor()`
- [ ] stderr captured and included in failure diagnostics
- [ ] Native binary crash results in clear test failure (not hang)

## LONG_TERM_GOALS Links

- **Goal 9/10 (AI Dispatcher)**: Stronger parity guarantee for native simulation

- [ ] Handle `run_once` exit status — currently `|| true` silently records bogus metrics if the benchmark command fails; capture exit code and skip/report failed iterations
- [ ] RSS parsing robustness — use `LC_ALL=C` and `awk` directly (instead of `grep | awk`) to avoid locale-dependent failures under `set -euo pipefail`
- [ ] Use median event count for events/sec — currently uses `tail -1` (last iteration) while wall time uses median; inconsistent

## Won't Fix

- **OS check for Linux**: The native binary is `linuxX64` only — the existing preflight check already fails if the binary is missing. An explicit OS check adds no value.
- **GNU time macOS detection**: Same reasoning — Linux-only benchmark for a Linux-only binary. `/usr/bin/time` on Linux is GNU time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `benchmark.sh` passes [ShellCheck](https://www.shellcheck.net/) with no warnings
- [ ] Failed iterations are detected and excluded from stats
- [ ] All metrics use consistent aggregation (median)

closing_issues.title: DingTalk syncer cannot synchronize users in multi-level departments (only first-level departments are processed)
closing_issues.body:
When using the DingTalk syncer to import organization data, users under multi-level departments (child departments of child departments) are not synchronized.

Current behavior:

Root and first-level departments are retrieved

Users under first-level departments are synchronized

Users under deeper-level departments are missing

Total synced user count is significantly lower than actual DingTalk user count

Example:

Actual DingTalk users: ~80

Synced users: ~37

Missing users are all located in nested departments

### Source Code
Path:
`object/syncer_dingtalk.go`
Function:
```
func (p *DingtalkSyncerProvider) getDingtalkDepartments(accessToken string) ([]int64, error) {
	apiUrl := fmt.Sprintf("https://oapi.dingtalk.com/topapi/v2/department/listsub?access_token=%s",
		url.QueryEscape(accessToken))

	// Get root department (dept_id=1)
	postData := map[string]interface{}{
		"dept_id": 1,
	}

	data, err := p.postJSON(apiUrl, postData)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	var deptResp DingtalkDeptListResp
	err = json.Unmarshal(data, &deptResp)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if deptResp.Errcode != 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get departments: errcode=%d, errmsg=%s",
			deptResp.Errcode, deptResp.Errmsg)
	}

	deptIds := []int64{1} // Include root department
	for _, dept := range deptResp.Result {
		deptIds = append(deptIds, dept.DeptId)
	}

	return deptIds, nil
}
```
### Root Cause
The implementation only calls:
```
/topapi/v2/department/listsub
```
with:
```
dept_id = 1
```
This DingTalk API only returns direct sub-departments, not all nested departments.

So for a structure like:
```
Root
 ├─ Dept A
 │   ├─ Dept A-1
 │   │   └─ Dept A-1-1
 │   └─ Dept A-2
 └─ Dept B
```
Current code retrieves only:
```
[1, Dept A, Dept B]
```
But not:
```
[Dept A-1, Dept A-1-1, Dept A-2]
```
As a result:

- User synchronization only runs on the retrieved departments
- Users in deeper levels are never requested or imported

### Suggested Fix
Departments should be fetched recursively.

Example approach:
```
func (p *DingtalkSyncerProvider) getAllDepartments(accessToken string, parentDeptId int64) ([]int64, error) {
	apiUrl := fmt.Sprintf("https://oapi.dingtalk.com/topapi/v2/department/listsub?access_token=%s",
		url.QueryEscape(accessToken))

	postData := map[string]interface{}{
		"dept_id": parentDeptId,
	}

	data, err := p.postJSON(apiUrl, postData)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	var deptResp DingtalkDeptListResp
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &deptResp); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if deptResp.Errcode != 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to get departments: errcode=%d, errmsg=%s",
			deptResp.Errcode, deptResp.Errmsg)
	}

	deptIds := []int64{parentDeptId}

	for _, dept := range deptResp.Result {
		subIds, err := p.getAllDepartments(accessToken, dept.DeptId)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		deptIds = append(deptIds, subIds...)
	}

	return deptIds, nil
}
```
Entry point:
```
deptIds, err := p.getAllDepartments(accessToken, 1)
```
### Impact
- Affects all environments using the DingTalk syncer

- Occurs whenever nested departments exist

- Results in incomplete user synchronization
This is a functional bug, not a configuration issue.

closing_issues.title: The disableSSL field in email providers is confusing and causes arguably buggy behavior
closing_issues.body: If you are setting up a default SMTP email provider in casdoor, there is a field called "disableSSL" that is directly beneath the host and port fields. This field is used to override the SSL setting of the gomail SMTP dialer when it is configured. https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor/blob/f7bd70e0a3c24cfc86431fd0d9b380cac1b592c1/email/smtp.go#L34 This will cause what is essentially buggy behavior depending on the configuration. If you want to use the standard 587 port and you have disableSSL turned off (the default setting), sending an email may fail because the casdoor will override the SSL field in the gomail dialer and attempt to establish a TLS connection before [negotiating via STARTTLS](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/insights/what-is-starttls). Ironically, it fails to establish a TLS connection because you are preemptive attempting to open an TLS connection. Alternatively, if you configure the SMTP provider via the implicit TLS port 465, turning on "disableSSL" will cause emails to fail because port 465 requires TLS. ------------------------------------------------------------------ ## What should be done I think the best way to deal with this would be to remove the "disableSSL" field for the default SMTP provider. The gomail version being used in casdoor already correctly sets the SSL field based on the chosen port for SMTP. See: https://github.com/casdoor/gomail/blob/4086d90e02d7414c41ba708580c3b9fe659506a7/smtp.go#L53 This way you wouldn't need to counterintuitively turn on disableSSL in order to negotiate to TLS via STARTTLS on port 587 and you wouldn't need to worry about an unnecessary configuration option if using implicit TLS via port 465.

closing_issues.title: [Bug] Casdoor panics with "Not implemented" on Azure SQL (Forced TLS) due to outdated go-mssqldb driver
closing_issues.body:
## Describe the bug
When configuring Casdoor to use Azure SQL Database (which enforces TLS encryption by default) via the mssql driver, the Casdoor instance frequently crashes (panics) with a panic: Not implemented error.

This crash usually happens during concurrent database queries, such as loading the dashboard (/api/get-dashboard). The crash causes the frontend to receive a 503 Service Unavailable or upstream connect error (often resulting in a JSON parse error on the frontend: SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'u', "upstream c"...).

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Deploy Casdoor using the official Docker image.

2. Set the environment variables to connect to an Azure SQL database (driverName=mssql, dataSourceName=...).

3. Log in as admin.

4. Navigate to the Dashboard or trigger /api/get-dashboard.

5. Check the backend logs, and you will see the container has crashed with a panic.

## Expected behavior
Casdoor should successfully query the database and close connections gracefully without panicking.

## Logs / Stack Trace

``` Plaintext
panic: Not implemented

goroutine 635 [running]:
github.com/denisenkom/go-mssqldb.passthroughConn.SetWriteDeadline(...)
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/denisenkom/go-mssqldb@v0.9.0/net.go:167
crypto/tls.(*Conn).SetWriteDeadline(...)
	/usr/local/go/src/crypto/tls/conn.go:159
crypto/tls.(*Conn).closeNotify(0xc0009c5188)
	/usr/local/go/src/crypto/tls/conn.go:1469 +0xd0
crypto/tls.(*Conn).Close(0x0?)
	/usr/local/go/src/crypto/tls/conn.go:1439 +0x66
github.com/denisenkom/go-mssqldb.(*Conn).Close(0xc0016b3ac8?)
	/go/pkg/mod/github.com/denisenkom/go-mssqldb@v0.9.0/mssql.go:361 +0x22
database/sql.(*driverConn).finalClose.func2()
	/usr/local/go/src/database/sql/sql.go:687 +0x32
...
github.com/casdoor/casdoor/object.GetDashboard.func1(0xc0008fee00)
	/go/src/casdoor/object/get-dashboard.go:64 +0x33d
```

## Root Cause Analysis
Casdoor's go.mod currently pins github.com/denisenkom/go-mssqldb to v0.9.0.
In modern Go versions (1.16+), closing a TLS connection invokes the SetWriteDeadline method. However, v0.9.0 of this driver lacks the implementation for SetWriteDeadline in its passthroughConn wrapper, which immediately triggers the panic.

This is a known issue in the old driver repository that was fixed in later versions:
[denisenkom/go-mssqldb#639](https://github.com/denisenkom/go-mssqldb/issues/639)

## Proposed Solution
Update the database driver dependency in go.mod.
Since denisenkom/go-mssqldb has been archived by its author, the official recommendation is to migrate to the Microsoft-maintained fork: [github.com/microsoft/go-mssqldb](https://github.com/microsoft/go-mssqldb).
Updating this dependency will permanently fix the panic for all SQL Server / Azure SQL users using encrypted connections.

Given that this only requires a simple dependency update in go.mod, it should be a very quick and easy fix. I recommend prioritizing this, as it currently completely blocks all Azure SQL users from using Casdoor in production.
