closing_issues.title: [feature] [mcp-1] Implement OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728) for MCP server discovery
closing_issues.body:
#### Summary

The [MCP Authorization specification (2025-06-18)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization) **requires** MCP servers to implement [RFC 9728 - OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728). This is a **MUST** requirement. Casdoor currently does not expose this metadata, which blocks Casdoor from being used as a compliant MCP resource server or as the authorization server for third-party MCP servers.

#### Background

When an MCP client (e.g., Claude Desktop, Cursor, ChatGPT) connects to a remote MCP server, the discovery flow works as follows:

1. MCP client sends a request to the MCP server
2. MCP server returns `HTTP 401 Unauthorized` with a `WWW-Authenticate` header pointing to its Protected Resource Metadata URL
3. MCP client fetches `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` from the MCP server
4. The PRM document tells the client which authorization server(s) to use, what scopes are available, etc.
5. MCP client then fetches the authorization server metadata (RFC 8414) and begins the OAuth 2.1 flow

Casdoor currently only serves `/.well-known/openid-configuration` (via the `GetOidcDiscovery()` function in `object/oidc_discovery.go`). There is no `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` endpoint.

#### Current State in Casdoor

Casdoor's existing OIDC discovery is built around the `OidcDiscovery` struct and the `GetOidcDiscovery(host string)` function, which returns the standard OIDC metadata. The route is registered in `routers/router.go` and handled by a controller that calls this function. This existing pattern can be extended for PRM.

The current `/.well-known/openid-configuration` response looks like:

```json
{
  "issuer": "https://door.casdoor.com",
  "authorization_endpoint": "https://door.casdoor.com/login/oauth/authorize",
  "token_endpoint": "https://door.casdoor.com/api/login/oauth/access_token",
  "userinfo_endpoint": "https://door.casdoor.com/api/userinfo",
  "jwks_uri": "https://door.casdoor.com/.well-known/jwks",
  "introspection_endpoint": "https://door.casdoor.com/api/login/oauth/introspect",
  ...
}
```

There is no PRM equivalent.

#### Proposed Implementation

**1. Define a new `OauthProtectedResourceMetadata` struct in `object/` (e.g., `object/wellknown_oauth_prm.go`):**

```go
type OauthProtectedResourceMetadata struct {
    Resource                string   `json:"resource"`
    AuthorizationServers    []string `json:"authorization_servers"`
    BearerMethodsSupported  []string `json:"bearer_methods_supported,omitempty"`
    ScopesSupported         []string `json:"scopes_supported,omitempty"`
    ResourceSigningAlg      []string `json:"resource_signing_alg_values_supported,omitempty"`
    ResourceDocumentation   string   `json:"resource_documentation,omitempty"`
}

func GetOauthProtectedResourceMetadata(host string) OauthProtectedResourceMetadata {
    return OauthProtectedResourceMetadata {
        Resource:               host,
        AuthorizationServers:   []string{host}, // Casdoor is its own auth server
        BearerMethodsSupported: []string{"header"},
        ScopesSupported:        []string{"openid", "profile", "email", "read", "write"},
    }
}
```

**2. Register a new route in `routers/router.go`:**

```go
beego.Router("/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource", &controllers.RootController{}, "GET:GetOauthProtectedResourceMetadata")
```

This follows the same pattern as the existing:
```go
beego.Router("/.well-known/openid-configuration", &controllers.RootController{}, "GET:GetOidcDiscovery")
```

**3. Add `WWW-Authenticate` header to 401 responses:**

When Casdoor's MCP server endpoints (from [#4750](https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor/issues/4750)) return `HTTP 401`, the response must include:

```
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="casdoor",
  resource_metadata="https://<casdoor-host>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"
```

This should be added to the MCP transport handler.

**4. Support application-specific PRM (optional, for multi-tenant):**

Similar to how Casdoor supports `/.well-known/<app-name>/openid-configuration`, we could also support `/.well-known/<app-name>/oauth-protected-resource` where each application has its own resource identifier and potentially different scopes.

#### References

- MCP Authorization spec: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization
- RFC 9728: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728
- Related: #4750 (MCP server for Casdoor)

closing_issues.title: [feature] [mcp-2] Serve OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414)
closing_issues.body:
### Summary

Casdoor currently serves authorization server metadata only at the OpenID Connect discovery endpoint `/.well-known/openid-configuration`. It does **not** serve metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` as defined by [RFC 8414](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414). This endpoint is critical for MCP (Model Context Protocol) authorization, where MCP clients are required to attempt discovery from `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` **first**, before falling back to `/.well-known/openid-configuration`.

### Background

RFC 8414 defines `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` as the standard endpoint for **general-purpose OAuth 2.0** authorization server metadata. `/.well-known/openid-configuration` was originally defined by OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 for OIDC-specific scenarios. While the two endpoints serve nearly identical JSON payloads, they exist as separate standards:

- `/.well-known/openid-configuration` → defined by OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0
- `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` → defined by RFC 8414 for general OAuth 2.0

RFC 8414 Section 5 explicitly acknowledges the overlap and notes that both can coexist. Many IAM products (e.g., Keycloak, PingFederate, Auth0) serve both.

The [MCP Authorization specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization) defines the following discovery priority order for MCP clients:

For root issuer URLs (e.g., `https://auth.example.com`):
1. `https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` **(try first)**
2. `https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration` **(fallback)**

For issuer URLs with path components (e.g., `https://auth.example.com/tenant1`):
1. `https://auth.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/tenant1`
2. `https://auth.example.com/.well-known/openid-configuration/tenant1`

Without `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`, every MCP client connecting to Casdoor will:
1. Hit a **404** on the first discovery attempt
2. Fall back to `/.well-known/openid-configuration` and succeed

This is functionally correct but has several downsides:
- Adds unnecessary latency (one extra round-trip per client connection)
- Generates noisy 404 error logs on the Casdoor side
- May break **strict** MCP clients that do not implement the fallback (the MCP Inspector project already had a [related compatibility bug](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/issues/563))

### Current State in Casdoor

Casdoor registers only the OIDC discovery routes in its router:

```go
// routers/router.go (current)
beego.Router("/.well-known/openid-configuration", &controllers.RootController{}, "GET:GetOidcDiscovery")
beego.Router("/.well-known/:applicationName/openid-configuration", &controllers.RootController{}, "GET:GetOidcDiscovery")
```

The handler calls `object.GetOidcDiscovery(host)` which returns an `OidcDiscovery` struct. There is **no route** for `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.

The current `/.well-known/openid-configuration` response includes:

```json
{
  "issuer": "https://door.casdoor.com",
  "authorization_endpoint": "https://door.casdoor.com/login/oauth/authorize",
  "token_endpoint": "https://door.casdoor.com/api/login/oauth/access_token",
  "userinfo_endpoint": "https://door.casdoor.com/api/userinfo",
  "jwks_uri": "https://door.casdoor.com/.well-known/jwks",
  "introspection_endpoint": "https://door.casdoor.com/api/login/oauth/introspect",
  "response_types_supported": ["code", "token", "id_token", ...],
  "grant_types_supported": ["authorization_code", "implicit", "password", ...],
  "scopes_supported": ["openid", "email", "profile", "address", "phone", "offline_access"],
  ...
}
```

Note that it is also **missing** `code_challenge_methods_supported`, even though Casdoor already supports PKCE with S256. This field is important for MCP clients to confirm PKCE support before initiating the auth flow.

### Proposed Implementation

**1. Add new routes in `routers/router.go`:**

```go
// OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414)
beego.Router("/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server", &controllers.RootController{}, "GET:GetOAuthServerMetadata")
beego.Router("/.well-known/:applicationName/oauth-authorization-server", &controllers.RootController{}, "GET:GetOAuthServerMetadata")
```

**2. Implement the controller method:**

The simplest and most maintainable approach is to **reuse `GetOidcDiscovery()`** internally, since the response format is nearly identical:

```go
func (c *RootController) GetOAuthServerMetadata() {
    host := c.Ctx.Request.Host
    applicationName := c.GetString(":applicationName")
    
    // Reuse the existing OIDC discovery data
    discovery := object.GetOidcDiscovery(host, applicationName)
    
    // Build the RFC 8414 response (same fields, with OAuth 2.0 additions)
    metadata := object.BuildOAuthServerMetadata(discovery, host)
    
    c.Data["json"] = metadata
    c.ServeJSON()
}
```

**3. Add missing fields to both endpoints:**

Create a shared helper that augments the base OIDC discovery data with fields required by RFC 8414 and the MCP spec:

```go
func BuildOAuthServerMetadata(oidc OidcDiscovery, host string) map[string]interface{} {
    metadata := map[string]interface{}{
        // All existing OIDC discovery fields
        "issuer":                   oidc.Issuer,
        "authorization_endpoint":   oidc.AuthorizationEndpoint,
        "token_endpoint":           oidc.TokenEndpoint,
        "userinfo_endpoint":        oidc.UserinfoEndpoint,
        "jwks_uri":                 oidc.JwksUri,
        "introspection_endpoint":   oidc.IntrospectionEndpoint,
        "response_types_supported": oidc.ResponseTypesSupported,
        "grant_types_supported":    oidc.GrantTypesSupported,
        "scopes_supported":         oidc.ScopesSupported,
        "subject_types_supported":  oidc.SubjectTypesSupported,
        
        // Fields currently missing but needed for MCP compatibility
        "code_challenge_methods_supported": []string{"S256"},
        "token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported": []string{
            "client_secret_basic",
            "client_secret_post",
            "none", // for public clients using PKCE
        },
        
        // Will be added after DCR is implemented:
        // "registration_endpoint": host + "/api/oauth/register",
    }
    return metadata
}
```

**4. Also update `/.well-known/openid-configuration`:**

The existing `OidcDiscovery` struct should be updated to include `code_challenge_methods_supported`:

```go
type OidcDiscovery struct {
    // ... existing fields ...
    CodeChallengeMethodsSupported []string `json:"code_challenge_methods_supported"`
}
```

And set it in `GetOidcDiscovery()`:

```go
func GetOidcDiscovery(host string) OidcDiscovery {
    return OidcDiscovery{
        // ... existing fields ...
        CodeChallengeMethodsSupported: []string{"S256"},
    }
}
```

This ensures both endpoints advertise PKCE support, which Casdoor already has.

### Implementation Cost

This is a **low-effort, high-value** change:
- Add 2 new routes pointing to a new handler
- The new handler reuses `GetOidcDiscovery()` and adds a few extra fields
- Add `code_challenge_methods_supported` to the existing `OidcDiscovery` struct
- No database changes, no new dependencies

### References

- RFC 8414: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414
- RFC 8414 Section 5 (compatibility with OIDC Discovery): https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414#section-5
- MCP Authorization spec (discovery priority): https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization
- MCP Inspector compatibility issue: https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector/issues/563
- Related: #4750 (MCP server for Casdoor)

closing_issues.title: [feature] [mcp-3] Implement OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) for MCP client onboarding
closing_issues.body:
#### Summary

The MCP Authorization specification **recommends** (SHOULD) that authorization servers support [RFC 7591 - OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration Protocol](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591). This allows MCP clients (AI agents like Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, etc.) to automatically register themselves with Casdoor without manual intervention, which is essential for the MCP ecosystem to work seamlessly.

#### Background

In the MCP ecosystem, AI agents often need to connect to MCP servers they have never interacted with before. The current Casdoor workflow requires an admin to manually create an Application via the Web UI or API (`AddApplication()` in `object/application.go`), obtain a `client_id` and `client_secret`, and then configure them in the MCP client. This is not feasible for dynamic agent scenarios.

With DCR, the flow becomes:

1. MCP client discovers the authorization server metadata (RFC 8414)
2. MCP client finds the `registration_endpoint` in the metadata
3. MCP client sends a `POST /register` request with its metadata (name, redirect URIs, etc.)
4. Casdoor creates a new Application record and returns `client_id` (and optionally `client_secret`)
5. MCP client uses these credentials for subsequent OAuth 2.1 flows

#### Current State in Casdoor

Casdoor's `Application` struct in `object/application.go` already contains all the fields needed for an OAuth client:

```go
type Application struct {
    Owner       string `xorm:"varchar(100) notnull pk" json:"owner"`
    Name        string `xorm:"varchar(100) notnull pk" json:"name"`
    ClientId    string `xorm:"varchar(100)" json:"clientId"`
    ClientSecret string `xorm:"varchar(100)" json:"clientSecret"`
    RedirectUris []string `xorm:"varchar(1000)" json:"redirectUris"`
    // ...
}
```

Application creation is done via `AddApplication()`, and `client_id` / `client_secret` are generated by the `generateId()` / `generateSecret()` utility functions. These can be reused for DCR.

However, there is currently **no DCR API endpoint** and no way for an external client to create an Application programmatically without admin-level authentication.

#### Proposed Implementation

**1. Add a `/api/oauth/register` endpoint in `routers/router.go`:**

```go
beego.Router("/api/oauth/register", &controllers.OAuthController{}, "POST:DynamicClientRegister")
```

**2. Implement the `DynamicClientRegister` controller method:**

The handler should accept a standard RFC 7591 registration request:

```json
POST /api/oauth/register HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "client_name": "Claude Desktop",
  "redirect_uris": ["http://localhost:3000/callback"],
  "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
  "response_types": ["code"],
  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none",
  "application_type": "native"
}
```

And return a standard registration response:

```json
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "client_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
  "client_secret": "...",
  "client_name": "Claude Desktop",
  "redirect_uris": ["http://localhost:3000/callback"],
  "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
  "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none",
  "registration_client_uri": "https://<casdoor-host>/api/oauth/register/a1b2c3d4e5f6",
  "registration_access_token": "..."
}
```

Internally, this would:
- Create a new `Application` object under a configurable default organization (or the org inferred from context)
- Generate `client_id` and `client_secret` using existing utility functions
- Store the `redirect_uris` and `grant_types` from the request
- Set appropriate defaults (e.g., `EnablePassword: false`, `EnableCodeSignin: true`)

**3. Advertise `registration_endpoint` in OIDC Discovery:**

Update the `OidcDiscovery` struct and `GetOidcDiscovery()` to include:

```go
type OidcDiscovery struct {
    // ... existing fields ...
    RegistrationEndpoint string `json:"registration_endpoint,omitempty"`
}
```

**4. Add policy controls for DCR:**

DCR is a potential security risk if left completely open. The implementation should support configurable policies at the organization level. Possible options:

- **Open registration**: Any client can register (suitable for public MCP servers)
- **Token-gated registration**: Require an initial access token to register (suitable for private deployments)
- **Domain-restricted registration**: Only allow `redirect_uris` from approved domains
- **Disabled**: Do not allow DCR (existing behavior)

This could be a new field on the `Organization` struct:

```go
type Organization struct {
    // ... existing fields ...
    DcrPolicy string `xorm:"varchar(100)" json:"dcrPolicy"` // "open", "token", "disabled"
}
```

**5. Optionally implement RFC 7592 (Dynamic Client Registration Management):**

This adds `GET /api/oauth/register/{client_id}`, `PUT /api/oauth/register/{client_id}`, and `DELETE /api/oauth/register/{client_id}` for managing registered clients. This can be a follow-up task.

#### References

- MCP Authorization spec: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization
- RFC 7591: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591
- RFC 7592 (Management): https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7592
- Related: #4750

closing_issues.title: [feature] [mcp-4] Implement Resource Indicators for OAuth 2.0 (RFC 8707) to support token audience binding
closing_issues.body:
#### Summary

The MCP Authorization specification **requires** (MUST) that MCP clients include the `resource` parameter in authorization and token requests, and that MCP servers validate that tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience. This is defined in [RFC 8707 - Resource Indicators for OAuth 2.0](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8707). Casdoor currently does not support the `resource` parameter in its OAuth endpoints and does not bind access tokens to a specific audience/resource.

#### Background

In MCP, token audience validation is a critical security mechanism. Without it, a token obtained for one MCP server could be replayed against a different MCP server (a "confused deputy" attack). The MCP spec explicitly states:

> MCP servers MUST validate that access tokens were issued specifically for them as the intended audience, according to RFC 8707 Section 2.

The flow works like this:

1. MCP client includes `resource=https://mcp-server.example.com` in the authorization request
2. Authorization server (Casdoor) records this resource binding
3. Casdoor issues an access token with an `aud` (audience) claim set to `https://mcp-server.example.com`
4. MCP client presents this token to the MCP server
5. MCP server validates that the token's `aud` matches its own resource URI

#### Current State in Casdoor

Casdoor's authorization endpoint (`/login/oauth/authorize`) currently accepts standard OAuth parameters (`client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type`, `scope`, `state`, `code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method`) but **does not accept or process a `resource` parameter**.

The token generation logic (in `object/token.go` and related files) creates JWT tokens with claims like `iss`, `sub`, `aud`, `exp`, `iat`, etc. The `aud` claim is currently set to the `client_id` of the requesting application:

```go
// Current behavior (simplified) in token generation:
claims := jwt.MapClaims{
    "iss": issuer,
    "sub": user.Id,
    "aud": application.ClientId,  // <-- currently just the client_id
    "exp": expireTime,
    "iat": issuedAt,
    // ...
}
```

This is the standard OIDC behavior (audience = client_id), but RFC 8707 requires support for a separate `resource` parameter that explicitly identifies the target resource server.

#### Proposed Implementation

**1. Accept `resource` parameter in the authorization endpoint:**

Update the authorization handler to parse and validate the `resource` query parameter:

```go
// In the authorization endpoint handler
resource := c.Input().Get("resource")
if resource != "" {
    // Validate resource is a valid absolute URI
    if _, err := url.ParseRequestURI(resource); err != nil {
        c.ResponseError("invalid_target", "The resource parameter must be a valid URI")
        return
    }
    // Store resource in the authorization code record for later use
}
```

**2. Accept `resource` parameter in the token endpoint:**

When exchanging the authorization code for a token, also accept and validate the `resource` parameter:

```go
// In the token endpoint handler
resource := c.Input().Get("resource")
// Validate it matches the resource from the authorization request
```

**3. Bind `aud` claim to the resource:**

When the `resource` parameter is present, use it as the `aud` claim instead of (or in addition to) the `client_id`:

```go
claims := jwt.MapClaims{
    "iss": issuer,
    "sub": user.Id,
    "aud": resource,  // <-- use the resource URI when provided
    "exp": expireTime,
    "iat": issuedAt,
    "client_id": application.ClientId,  // keep client_id as a separate claim
    // ...
}
```

When `resource` is not provided, fall back to the current behavior (`aud = client_id`) for backward compatibility.

**4. Add audience validation in token introspection:**

Update the introspection endpoint (`/api/login/oauth/introspect`) to include the `aud` field in the response and support `resource` as a validation parameter:

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "sub": "user123",
  "client_id": "app-client-id",
  "aud": "https://mcp-server.example.com",
  "scope": "openid read",
  "exp": 1700000000
}
```

**5. Validate audience in the built-in MCP server:**

When Casdoor's own MCP server (from #4750) receives a token, it should validate:

```go
func validateMCPToken(tokenString string, expectedResource string) error {
    claims, err := parseAndVerifyToken(tokenString)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    
    // Validate audience matches this MCP server's resource URI
    if claims.Audience != expectedResource {
        return fmt.Errorf("token audience %q does not match expected resource %q", 
            claims.Audience, expectedResource)
    }
    return nil
}
```

#### Backward Compatibility

- When `resource` is not provided, behavior remains unchanged (`aud = client_id`)
- Existing OIDC/OAuth clients that do not use `resource` are not affected
- The `resource` parameter is purely additive

#### References

- MCP Authorization spec: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization
- RFC 8707: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8707
- Related: #4750

closing_issues.title: [feature] [mcp-5] Add Application.Category and Application.Type fields to support Agent applications (MCP, A2A)
closing_issues.body:
### Summary

Add two new fields `Category` and `Type` to the `Application` struct to distinguish between traditional applications and AI agent applications. When `Category` is `"Agent"`, the `Type` field specifies the agent protocol (e.g., `"MCP"`, `"A2A"`). When `Category` is `"Default"` (or empty for backward compatibility), the `Type` field specifies the authentication protocol (e.g., `"OIDC"`, `"OAuth"`, `"SAML"`, `"CAS"`, or empty for all). The Application edit page should dynamically show/hide fields based on `Category` and `Type` selection.

### Background

Casdoor has been adding MCP OAuth 2.1 support (PRs #5092, #5094, #5097, #5098, #5100) to serve as an authorization provider for AI agent ecosystems. As the agent ecosystem grows (MCP for agent-to-tool communication, A2A for agent-to-agent communication), Casdoor needs a way to distinguish agent applications from traditional SSO/OAuth applications within the same Application model. Rather than creating a separate entity, we reuse the existing `Application` struct and use `Category` + `Type` to drive different UI views, default behaviors, and protocol-specific logic.

### Proposed Changes

#### 1. Backend: New fields on `Application` struct

```go
type Application struct {
    // ... existing fields ...
    Category string `xorm:"varchar(20)" json:"category"`
    Type     string `xorm:"varchar(20)" json:"type"`
}
```

Valid combinations:

| Category | Type | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| `"Default"` (or `""`) | `""` (or `"All"`) | Traditional app, all protocols enabled (current behavior) |
| `"Default"` | `"OIDC"` | Traditional app, OIDC only |
| `"Default"` | `"OAuth"` | Traditional app, OAuth only |
| `"Default"` | `"SAML"` | Traditional app, SAML only |
| `"Default"` | `"CAS"` | Traditional app, CAS only |
| `"Agent"` | `"MCP"` | AI agent app using Model Context Protocol |
| `"Agent"` | `"A2A"` | AI agent app using Agent-to-Agent Protocol |

Both fields are free-form strings (not enums) for extensibility. The UI provides dropdowns but the backend does not reject unknown values.

#### 2. Backend: Default values and backward compatibility

**Existing records**: All existing Application records have `Category = ""` and `Type = ""`. Empty `Category` should be treated as `"Default"`, and empty `Type` should be treated as `"All"` (all protocols enabled). No data migration is needed.

**Built-in applications**: The built-in `app-built-in` application should explicitly set `Category: "Default"` in its init data (`object/init_data.go`).

**Init data (`init_data.json`)**: If `Category` and `Type` are omitted in init data, they default to `"Default"` and `""` respectively. Document this in the init data examples.

**API backward compatibility**: The `AddApplication` and `UpdateApplication` APIs should accept requests without `Category` or `Type` fields and treat them as default values. Existing API clients are not affected.

**DCR (Dynamic Client Registration)**: Applications created via DCR (RFC 7591, PR #5097) should default to `Category: "Agent"`, `Type: "MCP"` since DCR is primarily used by MCP clients. This can be overridden by including `category` and `type` in the DCR request metadata.

#### 3. Frontend: Application edit page dynamic fields

The Application edit page should dynamically show/hide fields based on `Category` and `Type`:

**Category selector**: A top-level selector (dropdown or radio) for `Category` (`Default` / `Agent`). Changing this resets `Type` to the first valid option for the new category.

**Type selector**: A secondary dropdown whose options depend on `Category`:
- `Category = Default`: `All`, `OIDC`, `OAuth`, `SAML`, `CAS`
- `Category = Agent`: `MCP`, `A2A`

**Fields shown for ALL categories**:
- Basic info: Name, DisplayName, Logo, HomepageUrl, Description, Organization
- OAuth core: ClientId, ClientSecret, RedirectUris, GrantTypes, TokenExpiration, RefreshTokenExpiration
- Cert selection
- Provider configuration
- Sign-up / Sign-in configuration (EnablePassword, EnableCodeSignin, etc.)

**Fields shown ONLY for `Category = Default`**:
- SAML fields: SamlReplyUrl, SamlAttributes, etc. (only when `Type` is `"SAML"` or `"All"`)
- CAS fields (only when `Type` is `"CAS"` or `"All"`)
- Form offset / CSS / custom pages that are login-page specific

**Fields shown ONLY for `Category = Agent`**:
- `Scopes` field: A custom scope editor (see Section 5 below)
- Endpoint URL (optional, for Casdoor to know the agent's MCP/A2A server URL)

**Fields hidden for `Category = Agent`**:
- SAML-related fields (SP ACS URL, SP Entity ID, Metadata XML, etc.)
- CAS-related fields
- LDAP-related fields
- Login page customization (HeaderHtml, FooterHtml, FormCss, FormOffset, etc.)

#### 4. Frontend: Application list page

Add `Category` and `Type` columns to the Application list table:

- `Category` column: Show `Default` or `Agent` with a distinguishing tag/badge
- `Type` column: Show the specific type value (e.g., `OIDC`, `MCP`, `A2A`, or `All`)
- Both columns should be filterable and sortable
- Consider using color-coded badges: e.g., blue for Default, green/purple for Agent; protocol-specific colors for Type

#### 5. Backend + Frontend: Application.Scopes field

Currently, Casdoor has no Application-level field for defining custom scopes. The supported scopes (`openid`, `profile`, `email`, `address`, `phone`) are hardcoded in `GetOidcDiscovery()` within `object/oidc_discovery.go`. This works for traditional OIDC applications but is insufficient for Agent applications, where scopes are business-specific (e.g., `files:read`, `calendar:manage`, `database:query`).

Add a new `Scopes` field:

```go
type ScopeItem struct {
    Name        string `json:"name"`        // e.g., "files:read"
    DisplayName string `json:"displayName"` // e.g., "Read Files" (shown on Consent Screen)
    Description string `json:"description"` // e.g., "Allow reading your files and documents"
}

type Application struct {
    // ... existing fields ...
    Scopes []*ScopeItem `xorm:"mediumtext" json:"scopes"`
}
```

**Frontend**: When `Category = Agent`, show a scope editor (add/remove scope items, each with name, display name, and description fields). For `Category = Default`, the scope editor can be hidden or shown as an advanced option.

**Integration with existing endpoints**:
- `GetOidcDiscovery()` and `GetOAuthServerMetadata()`: Merge the hardcoded OIDC scopes with the Application's custom `Scopes` in the `scopes_supported` field
- `GetProtectedResourceMetadata()`: Use the Application's custom `Scopes` for the `scopes_supported` field
- Consent Screen (PR #5100): Display `DisplayName` and `Description` from `ScopeItem` for each requested scope
- Token generation: Validate that requested scopes are within the Application's defined `Scopes` list (for Agent apps) or are standard OIDC scopes (for Default apps)

#### 6. Backend: Category-based default behavior differences

When `Category = Agent`, apply stricter security defaults (no new fields needed, just different logic paths):

- **PKCE**: Agent applications should enforce PKCE by default. If an Agent app receives an authorization request without `code_challenge`, return an error. For Default apps, PKCE remains optional for backward compatibility.
- **Consent**: Agent applications should default to `ConsentPolicy: "always"` (once Consent Screen PR #5100 is merged). For Default apps, consent can be skipped.
- **Token lifetime**: Consider shorter default token expiration for Agent apps (e.g., 1 hour vs 7 days). This can be implemented by checking `Category` in the token generation logic and applying different defaults when the Application's own `TokenExpiration` is not explicitly set.

### Implementation Notes

**Go variable naming**: Since `type` is a reserved keyword in Go, use `typ` as the variable name when processing the `Type` field in backend code:

```go
typ := app.Type
if typ == "" {
    typ = "All"
}
```

The JSON field name and database column name remain `type`.

**Database migration**: Both new columns have default values (`Category` defaults to `"Default"`, `Type` defaults to `""`), so xorm's `Sync2` auto-migration should handle this without manual migration scripts.

**Affected files** (estimated):
- `object/application.go`: Add `Category`, `Type`, `Scopes` fields to struct
- `object/init_data.go`: Set default values for built-in application
- `object/oidc_discovery.go`: Merge custom scopes into `scopes_supported`
- `controllers/auth.go` or related: Apply Category-based PKCE enforcement
- `web/src/ApplicationEditPage.js`: Dynamic field visibility based on Category/Type
- `web/src/ApplicationListPage.js`: Add Category/Type columns
- `web/src/locales/en/data.json`: i18n strings for new fields
- `swagger/`: Update API docs

### References

- Related PRs: #5092 (PRM), #5094 (OAuth Server Metadata), #5097 (DCR), #5098 (Resource Indicators), #5100 (Consent Screen)
- Related issue: #4750 (MCP server for Casdoor)
- MCP Authorization spec: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization
- A2A Protocol spec: https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/

closing_issues.title: [feature] Implement scope-to-tool permission mapping for MCP server authorization
closing_issues.body:
### Summary

Casdoor's built-in MCP server (#4750) currently exposes tools like `get_applications`, `add_application`, etc., but lacks a mechanism to restrict which tools a given OAuth access token can invoke based on its scopes. Once a client obtains any valid token, it can potentially call all MCP tools regardless of the scopes granted. This issue proposes a configurable scope-to-tool mapping system that enforces fine-grained access control at the MCP tool level, designed to work both for Casdoor's own MCP server and as a reusable framework for third-party MCP servers using Casdoor as their authorization provider.

### Background

The MCP Authorization specification requires that MCP servers validate access tokens and enforce scope-based permissions, but it deliberately does **not** define how scopes should map to tools — this is left to the implementation. Currently in Casdoor:

- PR #5098 (RFC 8707) enables tokens to carry `scope` claims and audience bindings
- PR #5100 (Consent Screen, WIP) will display requested scopes to users for approval
- The related Application Category/Type issue proposes an `Application.Scopes` field for custom scope definitions

However, there is no enforcement layer between "token has scope X" and "tool Y is allowed to execute." This is the missing link.

### Design Goals

1. **Immediate use**: Enforce scope-based tool access for Casdoor's own MCP server (#4750)
2. **Reusable for third-party MCP servers**: The mapping model should be generic enough that when Casdoor acts as an auth provider (or MCP Gateway in the future), third-party MCP servers can define their own scope-tool mappings within their Application configuration
3. **Casbin-ready**: The design should integrate naturally with Casbin for fine-grained, sub-tool authorization (e.g., "can call `update_user` but only for users in org X")
4. **Extensible**: Support future scenarios like wildcard scopes, hierarchical scopes, and per-tool risk levels

### Scope Naming Convention

Use the `resource:operation` pattern. This aligns with Casdoor's REST API structure and is the most common pattern in the industry (GitHub, Google, Azure all use variants of this).

For Casdoor's own MCP server, the built-in scope definitions:

| Scope | Operation | Mapped MCP Tools |
|-------|-----------|------------------|
| `application:read` | Read | `get_applications`, `get_application` |
| `application:write` | Write | `add_application`, `update_application`, `delete_application` |
| `user:read` | Read | `get_users`, `get_user` |
| `user:write` | Write | `add_user`, `update_user`, `delete_user` |
| `organization:read` | Read | `get_organizations`, `get_organization` |
| `organization:write` | Write | `add_organization`, `update_organization`, `delete_organization` |
| `permission:read` | Read | `get_permissions`, `get_permission` |
| `permission:write` | Write | `add_permission`, `update_permission`, `delete_permission` |
| `role:read` | Read | `get_roles`, `get_role` |
| `role:write` | Write | `add_role`, `update_role`, `delete_role` |
| `provider:read` | Read | `get_providers`, `get_provider` |
| `provider:write` | Write | `add_provider`, `update_provider`, `delete_provider` |
| `token:read` | Read | `get_tokens`, `get_token` |
| `token:write` | Write | `delete_token` |

Convenience aliases can also be supported:

| Alias Scope | Expands To |
|-------------|------------|
| `read` | All `*:read` scopes |
| `write` | All `*:write` scopes |
| `admin` | All scopes |

### Proposed Implementation

#### 1. Scope-Tool mapping data model

Define a `ScopeToolMapping` struct that maps a scope to one or more tool names. This is stored per-Application (in the `Application.Scopes` field proposed in the Category/Type issue), allowing each MCP server application to define its own mappings:

```go
// object/scope.go

type ScopeItem struct {
    Name        string   `json:"name"`        // e.g., "application:read"
    DisplayName string   `json:"displayName"` // e.g., "Read Applications"
    Description string   `json:"description"` // e.g., "View application configurations"
    Tools       []string `json:"tools"`       // e.g., ["get_applications", "get_application"]
}
```

This extends the `ScopeItem` proposed in the Category/Type issue by adding a `Tools` field. The `Tools` field is optional — for third-party MCP servers using Casdoor only as auth provider, they may define scopes without tool mappings (they handle enforcement themselves). For Casdoor's own MCP server, the tool mappings are used for enforcement.

#### 2. Built-in scope registry for Casdoor's MCP server

Casdoor's own MCP server should ship with a default set of scope-tool mappings. These are registered at startup and used when the MCP server application does not have custom scopes configured:

```go
// mcp/scope_registry.go

var BuiltinScopes = []ScopeItem{
    {
        Name:        "application:read",
        DisplayName: "Read Applications",
        Description: "View application list and details",
        Tools:       []string{"get_applications", "get_application"},
    },
    {
        Name:        "application:write",
        DisplayName: "Manage Applications",
        Description: "Create, update, and delete applications",
        Tools:       []string{"add_application", "update_application", "delete_application"},
    },
    // ... more scopes
}

// GetToolsForScopes returns the union of tools allowed by the given scopes
func GetToolsForScopes(grantedScopes []string, registry []ScopeItem) map[string]bool {
    allowed := make(map[string]bool)
    for _, scopeName := range grantedScopes {
        for _, item := range registry {
            if item.Name == scopeName {
                for _, tool := range item.Tools {
                    allowed[tool] = true
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return allowed
}
```

#### 3. Enforcement middleware in MCP tool handler

Add scope checking in the MCP request handler, before dispatching to the tool implementation. This is the critical enforcement point:

```go
// mcp/handler.go (pseudo-code)

func (s *McpServer) handleToolCall(ctx context.Context, req ToolCallRequest) (ToolCallResponse, error) {
    // 1. Extract and validate token (already done by auth middleware)
    claims := getClaimsFromContext(ctx)
    
    // 2. Check scope-tool permission
    grantedScopes := strings.Split(claims.Scope, " ")
    allowedTools := GetToolsForScopes(grantedScopes, s.scopeRegistry)
    
    if !allowedTools[req.ToolName] {
        return ToolCallResponse{}, &McpError{
            Code:    -32001,
            Message: fmt.Sprintf("insufficient_scope: scope required for tool '%s' is not granted", req.ToolName),
        }
    }
    
    // 3. (Optional) Fine-grained Casbin check for sub-tool authorization
    // e.g., can this user update THIS specific application?
    if !s.enforcer.Enforce(claims.Sub, req.ToolName, req.Params) {
        return ToolCallResponse{}, &McpError{
            Code:    -32001,
            Message: "forbidden: you do not have permission to perform this action on the specified resource",
        }
    }
    
    // 4. Dispatch to tool implementation
    return s.dispatchTool(ctx, req)
}
```

#### 4. Scope-aware tool listing

When an MCP client calls `tools/list`, the response should only include tools that the client's current token is authorized to use. This follows the principle of least surprise — agents should not see tools they cannot call:

```go
func (s *McpServer) handleListTools(ctx context.Context) ([]ToolDefinition, error) {
    claims := getClaimsFromContext(ctx)
    
    if claims == nil {
        // Unauthenticated: return all tools (discovery mode)
        // Or return empty list depending on policy
        return s.allTools, nil
    }
    
    grantedScopes := strings.Split(claims.Scope, " ")
    allowedTools := GetToolsForScopes(grantedScopes, s.scopeRegistry)
    
    var filtered []ToolDefinition
    for _, tool := range s.allTools {
        if allowedTools[tool.Name] {
            filtered = append(filtered, tool)
        }
    }
    return filtered, nil
}
```

#### 5. Integration with Consent Screen and PRM

**Consent Screen** (PR #5100): When displaying consent to the user, the scope descriptions from `ScopeItem.DisplayName` and `ScopeItem.Description` should be shown. The `Tools` field can optionally be displayed as "This includes access to: get_applications, get_application" for transparency.

**Protected Resource Metadata** (PR #5092): The `scopes_supported` field in `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` should be populated from the Application's defined scopes. For Casdoor's own MCP server, this comes from the built-in registry.

**OAuth Authorization Server Metadata** (PR #5094): The `scopes_supported` field in `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` should also include these scopes.

#### 6. Third-party MCP server support (Gateway scenario)

When Casdoor acts as auth provider for a third-party MCP server:

- The third-party MCP server is registered as an Application in Casdoor with `Category: "Agent"`, `Type: "MCP"`
- The admin configures custom scopes via `Application.Scopes` (with or without `Tools` mappings)
- Casdoor issues tokens with the requested scopes
- The `Tools` field in `ScopeItem` is **informational** in this case — the third-party MCP server is responsible for its own enforcement
- But if Casdoor is acting as an MCP Gateway (future), the `Tools` mappings become enforcement rules at the gateway layer

This means the same data model serves both scenarios:
- **Casdoor's own MCP server**: `Tools` field is used for enforcement
- **Third-party MCP server (auth only)**: `Tools` field is optional/informational; scope descriptions power the Consent Screen
- **MCP Gateway (future)**: `Tools` field is used for gateway-level enforcement

### Error Handling

When a tool call is denied due to insufficient scope, the MCP server should return a standard JSON-RPC error:

```json
{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 1,
    "error": {
        "code": -32001,
        "message": "insufficient_scope",
        "data": {
            "tool": "add_application",
            "required_scope": "application:write",
            "granted_scopes": ["application:read", "user:read"]
        }
    }
}
```

The MCP client can then trigger a step-up authorization flow (re-requesting with additional scopes) as described in the MCP Authorization spec.

### Backward Compatibility

- **Existing MCP server behavior**: If no scope-tool mappings are configured and the token has no scope claim, all tools remain accessible (current behavior). This ensures existing deployments are not broken.
- **Gradual adoption**: Scope enforcement is activated when `Application.Scopes` is populated with tool mappings for Casdoor's MCP server application, or when the built-in registry is loaded.
- **REST API parity**: The MCP tool permissions align with REST API permissions as stated in #4750: "the permission for MCP tool `add_application` is the same as the permission for REST API `add-application`". The scope-tool mapping formalizes this relationship.

### Future Extensions

- **Wildcard scopes**: Support patterns like `*:read` (all read scopes) or `application:*` (all operations on applications)
- **Hierarchical scopes**: Support `admin` → includes all scopes, `write` → includes corresponding `read`
- **Risk-level annotations**: Mark scopes as `low`/`medium`/`high` risk, enable policies like "high-risk scopes require MFA"
- **Dynamic tool filtering at Gateway**: When Casdoor acts as MCP Gateway, use the mappings to filter `tools/list` responses from downstream MCP servers based on the user's granted scopes
- **Audit logging**: Log every scope-checked tool call with the user, agent, tool, scope, and result (allowed/denied)

### Affected Files (estimated)

- `object/scope.go` (new): `ScopeItem` struct with `Tools` field, scope resolution functions
- `mcp/scope_registry.go` (new): Built-in scope definitions for Casdoor's MCP tools
- `mcp/handler.go`: Add scope enforcement middleware before tool dispatch
- `mcp/server.go`: Filter `tools/list` response by token scopes
- `object/application.go`: The `Scopes` field (from Category/Type issue) includes `Tools`
- `object/prm.go`: Populate `scopes_supported` from Application scopes
- `object/oidc_discovery.go`: Merge custom scopes into discovery metadata
- `web/src/ApplicationEditPage.js`: Scope editor UI with tool mapping

### References

- Related issues: #4750 (MCP server for Casdoor), Application Category/Type issue
- Related PRs: #5092 (PRM), #5094 (OAuth Server Metadata), #5098 (Resource Indicators), #5100 (Consent Screen)
- MCP Authorization spec: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization
- MCP spec on insufficient scope handling: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization#insufficient-scope-handling
- Industry patterns: GitHub OAuth scopes (`repo`, `user:email`), Google OAuth scopes (`drive.readonly`), Azure RBAC (`Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read`)

closing_issues.title: [feature] Add OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange grant (RFC 8693) support
closing_issues.body:
This feature-request proposes adding support for the OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange grant as defined in [RFC 8693](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8693.html). It enables clients to exchange a valid security token (e.g., an access token, ID token, or JWT) for a new token tailored for a different audience or scope—ideal for service‑to‑service delegation, impersonation, and token‑renewal scenarios.

Why This Matters:

Casdoor currently supports standard OAuth 2.0 grants (authorization code, client credentials, etc.) but lacks a standardized way to exchange an existing token for another token with a different audience or scope. This is a common requirement in microservices architectures, where a client (e.g., an API gateway) needs to forward requests to downstream services that expect tokens with service‑specific audiences.

closing_issues.title: Casdoor: unidentifyable record in webhook for set-password and reset-password flow
closing_issues.body: When : 1. Setting password via set-password api 2. Resetting password via forgot password flow Issues: 1. Set password does not create any webhook calls, neither does it make any entry in `records`.The same is true when we use casdoor Admin UI to set a user's password. 2. Forgot password creates a set password webhook call, but with unidentifiable data, rendering it useless. below is the sample request body. It creates records for send-verification-code and verify-code but not for set-password. It does not have user details nor org details. The "name" field also does not match to a user-id. ``` { "id": 0, "owner": "", "name": "8cec33e5-65cf-476a-bbac-51bc7e6ec68c", "createdTime": "2026-02-07T13:15:07Z", "organization": "", "clientIp": "172.67.70.233", "user": "", "method": "POST", "requestUri": "/api/set-password", "action": "set-password", "language": "en", "object": "", "response": "{status:\"ok\", msg:\"\"}", "statusCode": 200, "isTriggered": false, "extendedUser": null } ``` here is the config for the webook Expectations: 1. set-password call records the full details including the user it was set for. It should also capture the user who triggerred this operation 2. forgot-password flow should also record a the same when the password is succesfully updated. Note: there are sometimes entries in the record for set-password during forgot password flow, and that looks like the below image with data points missing: Our system is a high audit need system. So this audit functionality is crucial. We are currently at the end of development phase. We want to understand if this is a key part of Casdoor, or if casdoor is not suitable for high audit need systems? 🙇

closing_issues.title: Feature Request: Store original OAuth tokens per provider instead of single originalToken field
closing_issues.body:
Description:                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  Currently, Casdoor stores only a single originalToken and originalRefreshToken for each user, which gets overwritten whenever the user logs in via a different OAuth provider.                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  Current Behavior:                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  When a user has multiple linked OAuth accounts (e.g., GitHub + Custom provider), only the token from the most recent OAuth login is preserved:                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  {                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    "github": "103566763",                                                                                                                                                                                         
    "custom": "14076",                                                                                                                                                                                             
    "originalToken": "<token from last login>",                                                                                                                                                                    
    "originalRefreshToken": "<refresh token from last login>"                                                                                                                                                      
  }                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  If the user logged in via the Custom provider last, the GitHub token is lost, and vice versa.                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  Problem:                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  This makes it impossible to:                                                                                                                                                                                     
  1. Validate whether each linked provider's token is still valid                                                                                                                                                  
  2. Make API calls to multiple providers on behalf of the user                                                                                                                                                    
  3. Implement token refresh for all linked accounts                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  Proposed Solution:                                                                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  Store original tokens per provider, similar to how user info is stored in properties:                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  {                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    "properties": {                                                                                                                                                                                                
      "oauth_GitHub_accessToken": "...",                                                                                                                                                                           
      "oauth_GitHub_refreshToken": "...",                                                                                                                                                                          
      "oauth_Custom_accessToken": "...",                                                                                                                                                                           
      "oauth_Custom_refreshToken": "..."                                                                                                                                                                           
    }                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  }                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  Or add dedicated fields:                                                                                                                                                                                         
  {                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    "originalTokens": {                                                                                                                                                                                            
      "GitHub": { "accessToken": "...", "refreshToken": "..." },                                                                                                                                                   
      "Custom": { "accessToken": "...", "refreshToken": "..." }                                                                                                                                                    
    }                                                                                                                                                                                                              
  }                                                                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  Use Case:                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  We need to validate third-party tokens to show users which linked accounts have expired tokens and need re-authorization.

closing_issues.title: WeCom Syncer users cannot login via WeCom Provider due to missing 3rd-party ID binding
closing_issues.body: I am using the WeCom Syncer to synchronize users from WeCom to Casdoor, and the WeCom Provider for user login. My goal is to allow synced users to log in via WeCom Scan QR code directly, without enabling "Allow Sign Up" (strict user base) and without relying on Email/Phone matching (due to WeCom privacy API limitations). **Problem Description** **Synchronization Works:** The WeCom Syncer successfully imports users (Name, Avatar, etc.) from WeCom. **Binding Missing:** However, the synced users do NOT have their 3rd-party logins (specifically the WeCom binding) populated. The wecom column in the user table remains empty. **Login Fails:** When these users try to log in via WeCom Provider (Scan QR), Casdoor cannot match the incoming WeCom UserID to the existing user record because the link is missing. - Since "Allow Sign Up" is disabled, they get "User not found". - "Enable Email linking" fails because WeCom's snsapi_login / scan scope does not return the email address by default (due to 2022+ privacy policies). **Expected Behavior** The WeCom Syncer should have an option (e.g., "Auto Link to Provider") or default behavior to populate the WeCom binding column with the userid it just synced. Since the Syncer trusts the source (WeCom), it should be safe to assume the synced user is the same identity as the login user from the same WeCom CorpID.

closing_issues.title: docs(migration): 升級說明補充 MVC JSON 數字輸出成字串（WriteAsString）的行為與調整方式
closing_issues.body:
## 背景
`UseWtmJsonOptions()` 設定了 `NumberHandling = AllowReadingFromString | WriteAsString`，所以 MVC `Json()`／API 回應的數字會輸出成 JSON 字串（例如 `"0"`）。這是 upstream 長期的預設：2021-04 加入，2023-05-26 拿掉，2023-06-29 又加回去。因此 upstream **6.3.25～6.3.29** 這幾版輸出的是 JSON number，其他版本（6.3.24 以前、6.3.30 以後、6.4、6.5、10.0、fork 10.0.x）都輸出字串。

從 6.3.25～6.3.29 升級的應用，前端可能出現行為差異，例如 `if (resp.x)` 原本對 `0` 判斷為 false，改成字串 `"0"` 後變成 true。

## 範圍
只補文件，fork 的預設值不變（與 upstream 一致）。

## 待辦
- [ ] 在 `docs/migrations/` 新增說明：行為、受影響的版本範圍、恢復成數字的寫法（在 `UseWtmJsonOptions()` 之後設定 `NumberHandling = AllowReadingFromString`），以及這樣做對框架其他部分（LayUI grid、`FFResult`、cache、`CallAPI`）的影響
- [ ] 註明：若既有外部呼叫端依賴字串格式，就不要改

closing_issues.title: fix(core): 匯入時數值型日期儲存格（Excel 日期序號）無法轉成 DateTime
closing_issues.body:
## 現象（依原始碼判讀，尚未實測）
`BaseImportVM.GetCellTextValue`（OpenXML 讀取器）讀儲存格時只取 `CellValue.Text`，沒有依 `CellFormat`／`NumberFormatId` 判斷是不是日期格式。Excel 的日期儲存格是數值，內部存的是 OADate 序號（例如 45953），讀出來就是 `"45953"`；接著 `ExcelPropety.ValueValidity` 用 `DateTime.TryParse` 解析，會失敗，`Date`／`DateTime` 欄位因此被判為格式錯誤。

WTM 自己產生的匯入範本中，`DateTime` 欄位套用的是日期數字格式（`NumberFormatId = 165`，`yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`），所以使用者在範本的日期欄直接輸入日期時，也可能存成序號，同樣受影響。

## 來源
這是 upstream 10.0 分支把 NPOI 改寫成 OpenXML SDK 時引入的。fork 10.0.0.4 到 10.0.0.8 都有這段程式。6.3.27 用的是 NPOI（推測靠 NPOI 的儲存格文字轉換處理日期，未實測）。

## 做法
- 讀取數值儲存格時，查詢它的 `CellFormat` → `NumberFormatId`：內建日期格式（14–22、45–47 等），或自訂格式中的 FormatCode 含日期／時間符號（y、m、d、h、s，且不在引號或 `[...]` 內）時，用 `DateTime.FromOADate` 轉換，再輸出成可以被 `DateTime.TryParse` 解析的字串（例如 invariant 的 `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss`）。
- 文字型儲存格的日期（例如 `2026-10-22`）行為維持不變。

## 驗收條件
- [ ] 數值型日期儲存格（內建格式與自訂格式）能正確匯入 `Date`／`DateTime` 欄位
- [ ] 文字型日期、非日期數值的行為不變
- [ ] 單元測試涵蓋；E2E（#272）若有對應案例一併驗證

`BaseImportVM` 是 LayUI 與 API 匯入共用的基礎（隨 Core 發佈）。

closing_issues.title: [feature] Extend Application with reverse proxy fields (Domain, Host, SslMode, SslCert)
closing_issues.body:
### Background

To enable Casdoor to act as a reverse proxy (like Nginx), we need to extend the existing `Application` object with proxy-related fields. This is modeled after [CasWAF](https://github.com/casbin/caswaf)'s `Site` object, where Casdoor's `Application` corresponds to CasWAF's `Site`.

### Mapping: CasWAF Site → Casdoor Application

In CasWAF, a `Site` has the following proxy-related fields (see [object package](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/casbin/caswaf/object)):

```go
type Site struct {
    Domain       string   `xorm:"varchar(100)" json:"domain"`
    OtherDomains []string `xorm:"varchar(500)" json:"otherDomains"`
    Host         string   `xorm:"varchar(100)" json:"host"`
    Port         int      `json:"port"`
    SslMode      string   `xorm:"varchar(100)" json:"sslMode"`
    SslCert      string   `xorm:"varchar(100)" json:"sslCert"`
    // ...
}
```

We should add equivalent fields to Casdoor's `Application` struct.

### What to implement

1. **Add new fields to `Application`** (in `object/application.go`):
   - `Domain string` — the public-facing domain for this application (e.g., `blog.example.com`)
   - `OtherDomains []string` — additional domains that should also route to this application
   - `UpstreamHost string` — the upstream backend address to forward requests to (e.g., `localhost:8080` or `192.168.1.100`)
   - `SslMode string` — one of `"HTTP"`, `"HTTPS and HTTP"`, `"HTTPS Only"` (same as CasWAF)
   - `SslCert string` — reference to a `Cert` object name for TLS termination

2. **Update the Application edit page (frontend)**:
   - Add a new section/group in the Application edit form for "Reverse Proxy" settings
   - Show fields: Domain, OtherDomains, ProxyHost, ProxyPort, SslMode, SslCert (dropdown of existing Certs)
   - These fields should be optional — if not filled, the application works as before (pure SSO app, no proxy)

3. **Update the Application REST API**:
   - The existing `add-application`, `update-application`, `get-application` APIs should include the new fields
   - No new endpoints needed

4. **Database migration**:
   - XORM should auto-migrate the new columns. Ensure existing applications are not affected (all new fields default to empty/zero).

### Notes

- At this stage we are only adding the data model and UI. The actual proxy forwarding logic will be implemented in a separate issue.
- The field names may differ slightly from CasWAF (e.g., `ProxyHost` instead of `Host`) to avoid confusion with Casdoor's existing fields.

### References

- CasWAF Site model: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/casbin/caswaf/object#Site
- CasWAF Site docs: https://caswaf.org/docs/site/
- Casdoor Application model: https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor/blob/master/object/application.go

It's defined [here](https://github.com/casdoor/casdoor/blob/8d2290944a9d7b3dc26fbd8281010d85c52e97ec/object/ormer.go#L56) in the ormer file.

closing_issues.title: Add missing keywords support for OpenAPIReference (and JsonSchemaRefernece
closing_issues.body:
actually I went ahead and had additional discussions with both @handrews and @darrelmiller (thank you both). My understanding was wrong.
Any JSON Schema keyword can appear next to $ref, some might not be applicable (not do anything) due to their nature, some might be contradictory when appearing both in the reference and the referenced schema, in which case, it's up to the application to define what the behaviour should be.

In the case where both are present, we have a precedent of returning the reference value for annotation keywords, so being consistent here makes sense. Then the application can check the reference and the target values, and compare them, if the difference is important to the application.

Any keyword in JSON schema exposed as a property in the [IOpenAPISchema interface](https://github.com/microsoft/OpenAPI.NET/blob/7345caac686dde49e97e36b2509f9fb674c825ca/src/Microsoft.OpenApi/Models/Interfaces/IOpenApiSchema.cs#L11) as well as in the [IOpenApiSchemaMissingProperties](https://github.com/microsoft/OpenAPI.NET/blob/7345caac686dde49e97e36b2509f9fb674c825ca/src/Microsoft.OpenApi/Models/Interfaces/IOpenApiSchemaMissingProperties.cs#L13) should have:
- a corresponding setter in the JsonSchemaReference type, and serialization code to match (use x-jsonschema prefix for OAI < 3.1)
- a corresponding getter in the JsonSchemaReference type, and the deserialization code to match (use x-jsonschema prefix for OAI < 3.1)
- a corresponding setter in OpenApiSchemaReference, that maps to the reference corresponding setter
- a corresponding getter, which returns the reference value when present, otherwise the target value
- cloning and unit test code like you've started

Now, I understand this is significant work, if you want to focus on the properties you've identified first, and punt the other properties to an additional issue, let me know.

_Originally posted by @baywet in https://github.com/microsoft/OpenAPI.NET/pull/2896#discussion_r3454882031_

mentioned_issues.title: Support relative URI resolution in $dynamicRef
mentioned_issues.body:
## Problem

`$dynamicRef` values with relative URIs (e.g., `./external.yaml#node`) are not resolved. `FindDocumentByBaseUri` compares the raw string against document base URIs, so a relative reference never matches an absolute document URI.

Example:
```yaml
# Document A (baseUri: https://example.com/main.yaml)
Tree:
  properties:
    next:
      $dynamicRef: './external.yaml#node'

# Document B (baseUri: https://example.com/external.yaml)
ExternalNode:
  $dynamicAnchor: node
  type: object
```

`$dynamicRef: './external.yaml#node'` should resolve to `https://example.com/external.yaml` (Document B), but `FindDocumentByBaseUri('./external.yaml')` cannot match `https://example.com/external.yaml`.

## Proposed fix

Pass the host document's `BaseUri` to `FindDocumentByBaseUri` and resolve the relative reference via `new Uri(baseUri, documentUri)`:

```csharp
internal OpenApiDocument? FindDocumentByBaseUri(string documentUri, Uri? baseUri)
{
    var resolved = baseUri is not null 
        ? new Uri(baseUri, documentUri).ToString() 
        : documentUri;
    return _dynamicAnchorRegistryByDocument.Keys
        .Concat(_anchorRegistryByDocument.Keys)
        .Distinct()
        .FirstOrDefault(doc => doc.BaseUri?.ToString()
            .Equals(resolved, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) == true);
}
```

## Scope

- `OpenApiWorkspace.FindDocumentByBaseUri` — accept optional base URI parameter
- `OpenApiSchemaReference.Target` — pass `Reference.HostDocument.BaseUri`
- Tests — cross-document resolution with relative URIs

## Related

- #2911 — parent tracking issue for `$dynamicRef`/`$dynamicAnchor` resolution
- #2913 — initial cross-document resolution (absolute URIs only)

closing_issues.body:
## 背景
以下有已知弱點的套件，**只有升到新的 major 版本才能修補**，而且都是 Elsa 2.17（工作流程引擎）帶進來的 transitive 依賴。WTM 自己的程式碼沒有直接使用它們：
- `MailKit`／`MimeKit` 3.6.0（GHSA-9j88-vvj5-vhgr、GHSA-gmc6-fwg3-75m5、GHSA-g7hc-96xr-gvvx）：來自 `Elsa.Activities.Email`
- `AutoMapper` 12.0.0（GHSA-rvv3-g6hj-g44x）：來自 `Elsa.Core`

Elsa 2.x 已經停止維護；Elsa 2.17 是用 3.x／12.x 編譯的。如果直接強制覆蓋成新的 major 版本，執行時很可能會出現 `MissingMethodException`。

## 待評估的選項
1. 升級到 Elsa 3（變更很大，屬於 breaking，需要遷移方案）
2. 讓 Elsa 相關套件改為可選：未啟用 `EnableWorkflow` 的應用就不帶入這些依賴（可能需要拆出套件）
3. 維持現狀並記錄風險（工作流程功能本身就是可選的）

## 相容性
任何一個選項都可能影響有使用工作流程功能的下游，屬於高風險，需要維護者決定。

closing_issues.title: security(core): sanitize OSS object keys and stored file extensions
closing_issues.body:
## 問題
- `WtmOssFileHandler.Upload` 用 `subdir`／`_subDirFunc` 與用戶端檔名的副檔名組出 OSS object key，但沒有做 #11 那樣的路徑限制與副檔名清理，用戶端因此可以控制 bucket 內 key 的前綴與後綴。OSS 的 key 是扁平的，不屬於檔案系統的路徑穿越，但遇到 CDN 或 URL 正規化時可能造成問題
- `WtmFileProvider.Upload`、`WtmDataBaseFileHandler.UploadToDB` 存進 DB 的 `FileExt`，是從未清理過的用戶端檔名計算出來的，可能和磁碟上實際的副檔名不一致；demo 會用它決定 content type

## 修正方向
- OSS handler 比照本機 handler 的做法：拒絕 rooted 路徑與 `..` 片段，副檔名只接受 1–10 個 ASCII 英數字
- provider 存進 DB 的 `FileExt` 套用相同的清理規則
- 視需要限制 subdir 的字元與深度

## 相容性
一般的上傳行為不變；只有原本不正常的 key 或副檔名會改變。

mentioned_issues.title: deps: ImageSharp vulnerabilities via captcha dependency
mentioned_issues.body:
## 背景
`SixLabors.ImageSharp` 3.1.12 有 5 個弱點（3 High、2 Moderate），都在 4.1.2 修補，屬於 major 升級。它是由驗證碼套件 `DUWENINK.Captcha` 0.10.2（已是最新版）帶進來的；這個套件依賴 ImageSharp 3 與 ImageSharp.Drawing 2，目前沒有支援 ImageSharp 4 的版本。

- WTM 在 `AddDUWENINKCaptcha()` 中使用這個驗證碼套件，**LayUI 的登入頁會用到驗證碼**
- Vue3Demo 的 `FileApiController` 會直接用 ImageSharp 解碼使用者上傳的圖片，這是實際暴露在外的入口

## 待評估的選項
1. 等 `DUWENINK.Captcha` 推出支援 ImageSharp 4 的版本後再升級
2. 換成其他驗證碼實作（需要維持 LayUI 登入頁的行為不變）
3. 短期緩解：demo 上傳不接受 TIFF 等高風險格式

## 相容性
驗證碼屬於 LayUI 登入流程，任何替換都要確保 LayUI 照常可用，屬於高風險，需要維護者決定。

closing_issues.title: security(mvc): encode redirect value in SetLanguageForBlazor response
closing_issues.body:
## 背景

- [ ] 一般網址的導向行為不變（單元測試）

closing_issues.title: security(mvc): EnableWorkflow=false 時 /_WorkflowApi/* 一律回 404（含 SPA 通配路由的網站）
closing_issues.body:
## 背景
#13（PR #206）在 `EnableWorkflow=false` 時，會用 `WorkflowApiDisabledConvention` 把 `_WorkflowApiController` 從應用程式中移除。一般 MVC／LayUI 網站因此會回 404；但有 SPA 通配路由（例如 `MapFallbackToFile`，Vue3Demo 就是）的網站，會回前端首頁（200、text/html，不含資料）。不會洩漏資料，但下游驗證時結果不一致。維護者 2026-10-21 決定補一個 stub，讓結果固定是 404。

## 做法
- `EnableWorkflow=false` 時，註冊一個只處理 `_WorkflowApi/{**path}` 的 stub controller，不需要登入，所有 HTTP method 都回 404，不查詢任何資料。`EnableWorkflow=true` 時，用 convention 把 stub 移除，原本的 `_WorkflowApiController` 照常運作。
- 未登入和已登入的請求都要拿到 404。

## 驗收條件
- [ ] `EnableWorkflow=false`：不論網站有沒有 SPA 通配路由，`GET /_WorkflowApi/GetWorkflowUsers` 都回 404，登入與否都一樣
- [ ] `EnableWorkflow=true`：行為跟 #206 一樣，未登入回 401，登入後正常回傳
- [ ] 測試涵蓋 convention 的兩種情況；可行的話，用 Vue3Demo 以未登入的 curl 實測
- [ ] FORK.md 第 12 節、CHANGELOG 更新

closing_issues.title: fix(mvc): BaseCRUDVM 以伺服器端自我 HTTP 呼叫 _WorkflowApi 的 GetTimeLine／GetWorkflow
closing_issues.body:
## 背景
在修 #13（PR #206）時發現，不在該 PR 範圍內：`BaseCRUDVM` 呼叫 `_WorkflowApi` 的 `GetTimeLine`／`GetWorkflow` 時，是從伺服器端用 HTTP 呼叫自己。這兩個 action 本來就需要登入，但 `CallAPI` 只會在 `LoginUserInfo.RemoteToken` 有值時帶 `Authorization: Bearer`，不會轉送使用者的 cookie。所以在單主機、用 cookie 登入的網站上，這個呼叫很可能一直拿到 401，結果是流程時間軸或流程資訊顯示為空。這是既有行為，不是 #13 造成的。

## 待評估
- [ ] 確認啟用 workflow 的單主機網站，`BaseCRUDVM` 的這兩個呼叫實際上是否失敗（401）
- [ ] 若確認失敗，評估改成直接呼叫服務或查詢，比照 #206 對 `ApproveActivity` 的做法，不再走 HTTP 自我呼叫
- [ ] `HasMainHost`（多主機）時的行為要維持

## 範圍
只有 `EnableWorkflow=true` 時相關。BMS／BOC_WebAPI 沒有啟用 workflow，不受影響。

closing_issues.title: security(mvc): RequireAuthentication 關閉時 /v1/activities 匿名回傳全部角色與群組
closing_issues.body:
## 背景
在 #13（PR #206）的安全審查中發現，屬於既有行為。`WorkflowOptions:RequireAuthentication` 預設為 false。這時 `/v1/activities` 不需要登入，Elsa 會呼叫 `WtmApproveActivity.GetOptions`，結果會包含 `ApproveRoles`、`ApproveGroups`、`ApproveManagers` 的下拉選項。所以未登入者可以拿到**全部角色與群組的 ID 和名稱**（匿名時只有主租戶的資料）。不包含使用者帳號、姓名，也不包含主管的帳號。

只有 `EnableWorkflow=true` 時相關。BMS／BOC_WebAPI 沒有啟用 workflow，不受影響。

## 可能的做法（待維護者決定）
- (a) `GetOptions` 在 `LoginUserInfo == null` 時回傳空清單。但 `RequireAuthentication=false` 時，內部呼叫不帶登入資訊（`ResolveSelfCall`），設計器的下拉選項會變空，需要先評估。
- (b) 把啟用 workflow 但沒開 `RequireAuthentication` 時的啟動 Warning 寫得更明確，或在文件建議啟用 workflow 的網站一律開啟。
- (c) 長期：考慮讓 `RequireAuthentication` 在啟用 workflow 時預設為 true（breaking）。

## 參考位置
`src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Mvc/Helper/WtmMiddleware.cs`（處理 `/v1/activities`）、`src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core/WorkFlow/ApproveActivity.cs`（`GetOptions`）

mentioned_issues.title: security(mvc): set Secure on UI state cookies over HTTPS (CodeQL cs/web/cookie-secure-not-set)
mentioned_issues.body:
## 背景
CodeQL `cs/web/cookie-secure-not-set`（9 個告警）：以 `Response.Cookies.Append` 寫入的 UI 狀態 cookie 未設 `Secure`。皆為 upstream 原有。

| 位置 | Cookie |
|---|---|
| `Filters/FrameworkFilter.cs` L324, L339 | `divid` |
| `Helper/WtmMiddleware.cs` L73, L74 | `pagemode`, `tabmode` |
| `_FrameworkController.cs` L249, L276 | `DONOTUSEDOWNLOADING` |
| `_FrameworkController.cs` L682, L704 | 語系 cookie |
| `_WorkflowController.cs` L43 | `workflowtenant` |

登入 cookie 已設 `HttpOnly`＋`SameSite=Strict`，不在這批；以上 cookie 皆非 session 憑證。

## 提案
`new CookieOptions { Secure = Request.IsHttps }`（不強制 `Secure=true`，避免破壞純 HTTP 部署）。

## FORK.md §2 評估（此變更可能被視為改變既有行為，故先列出再動工）
- **為什麼必要**：站台同時存在 HTTP 入口時，這些 cookie 會明文傳輸；掃描工具持續回報。
- **替代方案**：(a) 強制 `Secure=true`（會破壞 HTTP 部署，不建議）；(b) 新增設定開關預設關閉（無實際效益）；(c) 維持現狀並 dismiss 告警。
- **受影響範圍**：僅 HTTPS 回應上的上述 UI cookie；反向代理終止 TLS 且未設定 forwarded headers 時 `IsHttps=false`，行為不變。
- **遷移步驟**：無。
- **回滾方式**：還原該 commit。

## 備註
- `GetExcelTemplate`（L276）的 `Domain = "/"` 不是合法網域，瀏覽器會拒收該 cookie；屬既有 bug，修正會改變行為，另案處理，本 Issue 不含。
- 需維護者確認上述評估後再實作；確認前不開 PR。

mentioned_issues.title: security(mvc): constrain code generator output paths (CodeQL cs/path-injection)
mentioned_issues.body:
## 背景
CodeQL `cs/path-injection`（67 個告警，皆在 `src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Mvc/CodeGenVM.cs`）。程式碼產生器的輸出路徑由表單欄位（`EntryDir`／`MainDir`／`Area`／`SelectedModel` 等）組成，伺服器端沒有重新計算或驗證範圍。此檔案與 upstream `dotnet10` 相同（非 fork 引入）。

## 影響範圍
- 僅 `[DebugOnly]` 的 `_CodeGenController`，即 `IsQuickDebug=true` 時才可達；`IsQuickDebug=false` 時不受影響。
- 開發期工具，生成物落在 `Controllers/ViewModels/Views/ClientApp` 等目錄。

## 修法（非 breaking）
- 伺服器端以 `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.BaseDirectory` 重算 `EntryDir`／`MainDir`，不採用 client 送回的值
- `ModelName`、`Area`、`ModuleName` 驗證為識別字；`DoGen`／`Preview`／`Gen` 也要驗證 `SelectedModel`
- 所有寫檔／建目錄集中走單一 helper，確認解析後的完整路徑位於預期根目錄之下（參考 #11 的 `IsInside`）
- 合法的 LayUI／React／Vue／Blazor 生成路徑與內容不變

## 不在此 Issue
是否把 `[DebugOnly]` 改為「IsQuickDebug 且 Development」才放行（會改變既有行為，依 FORK.md 需另案評估）。

## 驗收條件
- [ ] 非法的 ModelName／Area／ModuleName／SelectedModel／目錄輸入被拒絕
- [ ] 所有寫檔點通過範圍檢查
- [ ] LayUI 生成的檔案路徑與內容與修改前相同（有測試）
- [ ] CodeQL 對 CodeGenVM.cs 的告警數下降（PR 的 CodeQL 結果附註）

mentioned_issues.title: fix(layui): escape and correct the option-selected regex in gridcellchange
mentioned_issues.body:
## 背景
CodeQL `js/useless-regexp-character-escape`（1 個告警）：`src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Mvc/framework_layui.js` 的 `gridcellchange`（約 L1176）：

```js
new RegExp("(<option\\s*value\\s*=\\s*[\"']" + ele.value + "[\"'])\s*>", "ig")
```
字串裡的 `\s` 被解讀成 `s`，正規式實際上不比對空白，使可編輯表格下拉欄在 `<option ...  >` 帶空白時無法標記 `selected`。另外 `ele.value` 未做 regex 跳脫，含特殊字元的值會造成比對錯誤或例外。upstream 原有。

## 修法
- `\s*>` 改為 `\\s*>`
- 對 `ele.value` 做 regex 跳脫
- 只動這一個函式，不改其他 LayUI 行為

## LayUI 保護
`framework_layui.js` 屬 FORK.md §3 受保護路徑；PR 需附 LayUI 相關測試結果，並確認 diff 僅此處。

## 驗收條件
- [ ] 帶空白與含特殊字元的 option 值都能正確設定 `selected`
- [ ] LayUI 相關測試通過，diff 僅限該函式

mentioned_issues.title: chore(demo): fix toolsValidate.ts regexes (CodeQL js/redos, js/overly-large-range)

mentioned_issues.title: security(layui): ChartTagHelper 的 Scatter tooltip 與 ToChartData 未轉義圖表資料（可能的 XSS）
mentioned_issues.body:
## 背景
評估 #189 時發現（只讀過原始碼，沒有做 PoC），跟 echarts 版本無關，升級 echarts 也解決不了：
- `src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.TagHelpers.LayUI/Chart/ChartTagHelper.cs:104-109`：Scatter 的 tooltip formatter 把 `seriesName` 和 `value[3]`（也就是 `ChartData.Series`／`Category`）沒有轉義就當成 HTML 回傳。如果圖表資料含有使用者可以控制的字串（例如來自資料庫的名稱），就可能造成 DOM XSS。
- `ListExtension.ToChartData` 用字串串接組 JSON，沒有轉義 `Category`／`Series`；`framework_layui.js:1043` 再用 `JSONfns.parse` 解析。`JSONfns` 不是 repo 定義的，而是宿主網站提供的。若宿主用的是常見的 jsonfn 實作（會對 `function` 字串做 eval），就有程式碼注入的疑慮。這一點是假設，要看宿主實際使用的版本。

## 影響
`ChartTagHelper` 和 `ListExtension` 會隨 NuGet 發佈，使用 LayUI `wt:chart` 的下游可能受影響。BMS 是否有用到 `wt:chart`，需要確認。

## 待辦
- [ ] 做 PoC，確認兩條路徑實際能不能被利用
- [ ] `ToChartData` 改成用 JSON serializer 輸出，不再字串串接
- [ ] Scatter tooltip formatter 對輸出值做 HTML 轉義
- [ ] 確認 `JSONfns` 的來源，評估改用 `JSON.parse`
