closing_issues.title: Warn or error on unreachable code and unused variables at the TypeScript level
closing_issues.body: The compiler should detect and warn about unreachable code after `throw`/`return` statements and unused local variables. The Solidity compiler already warns about unused variables, but catching these at the TypeScript level would provide earlier feedback in the development cycle.

closing_issues.title: Add source maps from TypeScript to generated Solidity
closing_issues.body: When Hardhat reports a Solidity error, users need to manually map it back to their TypeScript source. Source maps linking generated Solidity line numbers back to the original TypeScript would significantly improve the debugging experience, especially for complex contracts.

closing_issues.title: Support optional constructor parameters with default values
closing_issues.body: TypeScript supports default parameter values (`constructor(supply: number = 1000000)`). This could compile to Solidity functions with overloads or default values, making contracts more flexible to deploy.

closing_issues.title: Add watch mode for the compiler (skittles compile --watch)
closing_issues.body: A `--watch` flag that recompiles on file changes would improve the developer experience. This is standard for TypeScript tooling (`tsc --watch`) and would pair well with Hardhat's test watching.

closing_issues.title: Add abi.decode TypeScript syntax with type parameters
closing_issues.body:
While `abi.decode` is listed as available, the docs don't show how to specify target types in TypeScript. Solidity's `abi.decode(data, (uint256, address))` requires type specifications. A TypeScript-friendly syntax should be documented and supported:

```typescript
const [amount, addr] = abi.decode<[number, address]>(data);
```

closing_issues.title: Support for...in loops over enum values
closing_issues.body: TypeScript's `for...in` could be used to iterate over enum values. While Solidity doesn't natively support this, the compiler could desugar it into a loop over the known enum range.

closing_issues.title: Support Map<K, V> as an alternative to Record for mappings
closing_issues.body: TypeScript developers might instinctively use `Map<K, V>` for key-value storage. Supporting `Map` as an alias for `Record` (both compiling to `mapping`) would feel more natural for some developers.

closing_issues.title: Support try/catch for external calls
closing_issues.body: Solidity supports `try/catch` for handling errors from external contract calls. This is important for composable DeFi protocols that need to gracefully handle failures in other contracts.

closing_issues.title: Support exponentiation operator (**)
closing_issues.body: TypeScript's `**` (exponentiation) operator should compile to Solidity's `**` operator. This is needed for calculations involving powers (e.g., `10 ** decimals` for token amounts with decimal scaling).

closing_issues.title: Docs and website say Node 20+ but scaffolded project requires Node 22+
closing_issues.body:
The website and Installation docs state "Node.js 20.0 or higher" as a prerequisite. However:

1. The scaffolded `package.json` has `"engines": {"node": ">=22.0.0"}`
2. Hardhat 3 (installed by `skittles init`) requires Node.js 22+
3. Running `npm run test` on Node 20 fails with `TypeError: this[#dependenciesMap].values(...).flatMap is not a function` inside Hardhat

The docs should state Node.js 22+ as the requirement, or explain the distinction (Skittles compiler = Node 20+, full workflow with Hardhat 3 = Node 22+).

closing_issues.title: --version flag shows project version (1.0.0) instead of Skittles compiler version
closing_issues.body:
## Description

Running `npx skittles --version` outputs `1.0.0`, which is the version from the project's `package.json`, not the actual installed Skittles version (`1.2.6` per `npm ls skittles`). The `--version` flag should report the Skittles compiler version so users can verify which version of the tool they're running.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `npx skittles@latest init`
2. Run `npx skittles --version`
3. Observe it says `1.0.0` instead of `1.2.6`

## Expected Behavior

Should display the Skittles package version (e.g., `1.2.6`).

closing_issues.title: feat(vox): Add VOX types, configuration, and service interfaces to Core layer
closing_issues.body:
## Description

Add all VOX v2.0 data structures, configuration, and service interfaces to the Core layer. This is the foundation for the entire VOX system.

## Context

VOX v2.0 is a static clip library system (no database). All types are simple records/enums - no EF Core entities needed.

**Spec Reference:** [vox-system-spec.md](docs/articles/vox-system-spec.md) - Architecture section

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Create `VoxClipGroup` enum (Vox, Fvox, Hgrunt)
- [ ] Create `VoxClipInfo` record (Name, Group, FileSizeBytes, DurationSeconds)
- [ ] Create `VoxPlaybackOptions` record (WordGapMs with default 50)
- [ ] Create `VoxPlaybackResult` record (Success, ErrorMessage, MatchedWords, SkippedWords, EstimatedDurationSeconds)
- [ ] Create `VoxTokenPreview` record (Tokens list, MatchedCount, SkippedCount, EstimatedDurationSeconds)
- [ ] Create `VoxTokenInfo` record (Word, HasClip, DurationSeconds)
- [ ] Create `VoxOptions` configuration class (BasePath, DefaultWordGapMs, MaxMessageWords, MaxMessageLength)
- [ ] Create `IVoxClipLibrary` interface (InitializeAsync, GetClips, GetClip, SearchClips, GetClipFilePath, GetClipCount)
- [ ] Create `IVoxConcatenationService` interface (ConcatenateAsync)
- [ ] Create `IVoxService` interface (PlayAsync, TokenizePreview)

## Technical Notes

**File locations:**
- `src/DiscordBot.Core/Enums/VoxClipGroup.cs`
- `src/DiscordBot.Core/DTOs/Vox/VoxClipInfo.cs` (and other DTOs)
- `src/DiscordBot.Core/Configuration/VoxOptions.cs`
- `src/DiscordBot.Core/Interfaces/Vox/IVoxClipLibrary.cs` (and other interfaces)

**VoxOptions:**
```csharp
public class VoxOptions
{
    public const string SectionName = "Vox";
    public string BasePath { get; set; } = "./sounds";
    public int DefaultWordGapMs { get; set; } = 50;
    public int MaxMessageWords { get; set; } = 50;
    public int MaxMessageLength { get; set; } = 500;
}
```

See spec for full interface signatures and record definitions.

## Dependencies

None - this is the first issue in the VOX v2.0 implementation.

closing_issues.title: feat(vox): Implement VoxClipLibrary singleton filesystem scanner
closing_issues.body:
## Description

Implement `VoxClipLibrary` - a singleton service that scans the filesystem at startup to build an in-memory inventory of all available audio clips across 3 groups (VOX, FVOX, HGrunt).

## Context

The clip library is the foundation of VOX v2.0. It replaces the v1.0 database-backed word bank with a simple filesystem scan. Clips are pre-built MP3 files that ship with the bot.

**Spec Reference:** [vox-system-spec.md](docs/articles/vox-system-spec.md) - Clip Library section

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Implement `VoxClipLibrary : IVoxClipLibrary`
- [ ] On `InitializeAsync()`, scan `sounds/vox/`, `sounds/fvox/`, `sounds/hgrunt/` folders
- [ ] For each `.mp3` file, extract: name (filename without extension, lowercased), file size, duration (via FFprobe)
- [ ] Store inventory in `Dictionary<VoxClipGroup, Dictionary<string, VoxClipInfo>>`
- [ ] Log clip counts per group on initialization
- [ ] `GetClips(group)` returns all clips for a group
- [ ] `GetClip(group, name)` returns single clip or null
- [ ] `SearchClips(group, query, maxResults)` returns prefix matches first, then substring matches (case-insensitive)
- [ ] `GetClipFilePath(group, name)` returns full file path
- [ ] `GetClipCount(group)` returns count
- [ ] Parallelize FFprobe duration extraction for startup performance
- [ ] Handle missing folders gracefully (log warning, continue)

## Technical Notes

**FFprobe duration extraction:**
```bash
ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format clip.mp3
```
Parse `format.duration` from JSON output.

**Search priority:** Prefix matches sorted alphabetically, then substring matches sorted alphabetically. Max 25 results by default.

**Lifetime:** Singleton - loaded once at startup, held in memory for the application lifetime.

## Dependencies

- Core types and interfaces (VOX types issue)
- FFprobe must be available in PATH

closing_issues.title: feat(vox): Implement VoxConcatenationService for FFmpeg audio joining
closing_issues.body:
## Description

Implement `VoxConcatenationService` - a singleton service that concatenates multiple MP3 clips into a single audio stream with configurable silence gaps between clips using FFmpeg.

## Context

This is the audio processing core of VOX. It takes a list of clip file paths and joins them with silence, producing a temporary audio file that can be streamed to Discord via the existing PlaybackService.

**Spec Reference:** [vox-system-spec.md](docs/articles/vox-system-spec.md) - Audio Pipeline section

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Implement `VoxConcatenationService : IVoxConcatenationService`
- [ ] `ConcatenateAsync(clipFilePaths, wordGapMs, cancellationToken)` produces a temporary audio file
- [ ] Insert silence of `wordGapMs` milliseconds between each clip
- [ ] Output format compatible with PlaybackService (PCM s16le, 48kHz, stereo preferred)
- [ ] Handle single-clip input (no silence needed)
- [ ] Clean temporary files on cancellation
- [ ] Return the path to the concatenated temporary file

## Technical Notes

**Silence gap calculation (PCM 48kHz, 16-bit, stereo):**
```
Silence bytes = gapMs * 48000 * 2 (bytes/sample) * 2 (channels) / 1000 = gapMs * 192
```

**FFmpeg approaches (choose most reliable):**

1. Concat demuxer with silence file entries
2. Filter complex with `adelay`/`apad`
3. Programmatic PCM: decode each clip, append silence bytes between segments

The simplest approach may be to decode all clips to PCM, programmatically insert silence bytes, and output the concatenated PCM.

**Lifetime:** Singleton (stateless - each call produces an independent temp file)

**Temp file management:** Use a dedicated temp directory, clean up after playback completes.

## Dependencies

- Core types and interfaces (VOX types issue)
- FFmpeg must be available in PATH

closing_issues.title: feat(vox): Implement VoxService orchestrator
closing_issues.body:
## Description

Implement `VoxService` - the main orchestrator that coordinates the full VOX pipeline: tokenize input → resolve clips → concatenate audio → play via PlaybackService.

## Context

VoxService is the central service that slash commands and API endpoints call. It ties together the clip library, concatenation service, and existing PlaybackService.

**Spec Reference:** [vox-system-spec.md](docs/articles/vox-system-spec.md) - IVoxService section

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Implement `VoxService : IVoxService`
- [ ] `PlayAsync(guildId, message, group, options, cancellationToken)`:
  - Tokenize input (split on whitespace, lowercase, strip punctuation)
  - Look up each token in `IVoxClipLibrary` for the requested group
  - Collect file paths for matched clips, track skipped words
  - Call `IVoxConcatenationService.ConcatenateAsync()` with matched clip paths
  - Create transient `Sound` object wrapping the concatenated file
  - Call `IPlaybackService.PlayAsync()` to stream to Discord
  - Clean up temporary file after playback
  - Return `VoxPlaybackResult` with matched/skipped word lists
- [ ] `TokenizePreview(message, group)`:
  - Parse message into tokens
  - Look up each token, return `VoxTokenPreview` with match status and estimated duration
  - No audio processing - preview only
- [ ] Validate message against `VoxOptions` limits (MaxMessageWords, MaxMessageLength)
- [ ] Return error if zero clips matched
- [ ] Return error if user not in voice channel (or delegate to caller)

## Technical Notes

**Tokenization rules:**
1. Split on whitespace
2. Convert to lowercase
3. Strip leading/trailing punctuation
4. Empty tokens filtered out

**Transient Sound object for PlaybackService:**
```csharp
var voxSound = new Sound
{
    Id = Guid.NewGuid(),
    GuildId = guildId,
    Name = $"vox-{DateTime.UtcNow:yyyyMMddHHmmss}",
    FileName = concatenatedFilePath,
    FileSizeBytes = new FileInfo(concatenatedFilePath).Length,
    DurationSeconds = estimatedDuration
};
```

**Lifetime:** Scoped (per-request pipeline coordination)

## Dependencies

- VoxClipLibrary implementation
- VoxConcatenationService implementation
- Existing IPlaybackService

closing_issues.body:
## Description

Implement three top-level slash commands (`/vox`, `/fvox`, `/hgrunt`) that play VOX announcements from their respective clip groups, with autocomplete suggesting available clip names as the user types.

## Context

Each command maps to one of the three Half-Life clip groups. They share the same parameters and behavior, differing only in which `VoxClipGroup` they target.

**Spec Reference:** [vox-system-spec.md](docs/articles/vox-system-spec.md) - Slash Commands section

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Create `VoxModule : InteractionModuleBase<SocketInteractionContext>`
- [ ] `/vox message:[string] gap:[int?]` - Play VOX group announcement
- [ ] `/fvox message:[string] gap:[int?]` - Play FVOX group announcement
- [ ] `/hgrunt message:[string] gap:[int?]` - Play HGrunt group announcement
- [ ] All commands use shared `PlayVoxAsync` helper method with group parameter
- [ ] `message` parameter: MaxLength 500, required
- [ ] `gap` parameter: MinValue 20, MaxValue 200, optional (defaults to VoxOptions.DefaultWordGapMs)
- [ ] Apply `[RequireGuildActive]`, `[RequireAudioEnabled]`, `[RequireVoiceChannel]`, `[RateLimit(5, 10)]`
- [ ] `DeferAsync()` before processing
- [ ] On success: ephemeral followup showing matched words and any skipped words
- [ ] On error: ephemeral followup with error message
- [ ] Implement `VoxAutocompleteHandler`:
  - Extract last word being typed from partial input
  - Search clips in the appropriate group via `IVoxClipLibrary.SearchClips()`
  - Return up to 25 suggestions with full message text preserved
  - Three derived handlers (one per group) or single handler with group resolution from command name

## Technical Notes

**Command response format:**
```
Playing: warning security breach detected in sector c
Skipped (no clip): hello, world
```

**Autocomplete handler:** When user has typed `"attention all per"`, the handler:
1. Extracts `"per"` as the last partial word
2. Searches VOX group for clips starting with `"per"` (e.g., `personnel`, `perimeter`)
3. Returns suggestions like `"attention all personnel"`, `"attention all perimeter"`

**File location:** `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Modules/VoxModule.cs`

## Dependencies

- VoxService implementation (Phase 1)
- VoxClipLibrary (for autocomplete)
- DI registration (Phase 1)

closing_issues.title: feat(vox): Parse punctuation (comma, period) as timing tokens in text entry
closing_issues.body:
## Description

When users type punctuation in the VOX text entry box, it should be automatically parsed and converted to the corresponding timing tokens/clips, which provide natural pauses in the synthesized speech.

## Punctuation Mappings

| Character | Token | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| `,` (comma) | `_comma` | Short pause between phrases |
| `.` (period) | `_period` | Longer pause at end of sentences |

## Current Behavior

Punctuation is either ignored or treated as literal text, not converted to the corresponding audio clips.

## Expected Behavior

- Typing `hello, world` should be parsed as `hello _comma world`
- Typing `hello. goodbye` should be parsed as `hello _period goodbye`
- The timing clips provide appropriate pauses matching Half-Life's sentences.txt behavior

## Implementation Notes

- Update the VOX tokenizer/parser to recognize punctuation
- Convert punctuation to corresponding timing tokens during parsing
- Ensure token preview strip displays these as tokens
- Handle edge cases (multiple punctuation, punctuation at start/end)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Commas in input text are converted to `_comma` tokens
- [ ] Periods in input text are converted to `_period` tokens
- [ ] Preview strip shows punctuation as timing tokens
- [ ] Audio playback includes the appropriate pause clips
- [ ] Works in both Portal UI and slash commands

closing_issues.title: epic(vox): VOX v2.0 - Static Clip Library System
closing_issues.body:
## Overview

VOX v2.0 - A Half-Life-style concatenated clip announcement system for Discord. Users type words, the system finds matching pre-recorded audio clips from 3 groups (VOX, FVOX, HGrunt), concatenates them with configurable gaps, and plays the result in Discord voice channels.

## Key Design Decisions (v2.0)

- **No database required** - Clip inventory built by filesystem scanning at startup, held in memory
- **3 independent clip groups** - VOX, FVOX, HGrunt with dedicated slash commands
- **Reuses existing PlaybackService** - Same audio streaming infrastructure as soundboard
- **Static clip library** - Pre-built MP3 clips ship with the bot (no TTS generation)

## Architecture

```
Bot Layer: VoxModule / FvoxModule / HgruntModule + VoxController + Portal Razor Page
Services:  IVoxService (orchestrator) → IVoxClipLibrary + IVoxConcatenationService → IPlaybackService
```

Pipeline: `User input → Tokenize → Resolve clips → Concatenate (FFmpeg) → PlaybackService → Discord`

## Specs

- [vox-system-spec.md](docs/articles/vox-system-spec.md) - System architecture and service design
- [vox-ui-spec.md](docs/articles/vox-ui-spec.md) - Portal and admin UI design
- [vox-portal.html](docs/prototypes/vox-portal.html) - Interactive portal prototype
- [vox-admin.html](docs/prototypes/vox-admin.html) - Interactive admin prototype

## Phases

### Phase 1: Core & Services
- [ ] Add VOX types, configuration, and service interfaces to Core layer
- [ ] Implement VoxClipLibrary (singleton filesystem scanner with FFprobe)
- [ ] Implement VoxConcatenationService (FFmpeg audio joining with silence gaps)
- [ ] Implement VoxService orchestrator (tokenize → resolve → concatenate → play)
- [ ] Create VOX DI registration and startup initialization

### Phase 2: Slash Commands
- [ ] Implement /vox, /fvox, /hgrunt slash commands with autocomplete

### Phase 3: Portal API & UI
- [ ] Implement Portal VOX API endpoints (clips, preview, play, stop)
- [ ] Implement Portal VOX Razor Page (layout, sidebar, group tabs)
- [ ] Implement message input with autocomplete dropdown
- [ ] Implement token preview strip (matched/skipped indicators)
- [ ] Implement clip browser grid with search and click-to-append

### Phase 4: Admin
- [ ] Implement Admin VOX page (read-only clip library + settings)

### Phase 5: Testing & Documentation
- [ ] Write unit tests for VOX services
- [ ] Write integration tests for VOX pipeline
- [ ] Update documentation and api-endpoints.md

### Phase 6: Polish
- [ ] Implement accessibility and responsive design

## Supersedes

Closes the v1.0 issue set (#1412-#1453) which was designed around TTS word generation, database entities, word bank management, and sentence builder - all removed in v2.0.

closing_issues.title: feat(vox): Implement VoxClipLibrary singleton filesystem scanner
closing_issues.body:
## Description

Implement `VoxClipLibrary` - a singleton service that scans the filesystem at startup to build an in-memory inventory of all available audio clips across 3 groups (VOX, FVOX, HGrunt).

## Context

The clip library is the foundation of VOX v2.0. It replaces the v1.0 database-backed word bank with a simple filesystem scan. Clips are pre-built MP3 files that ship with the bot.

**Spec Reference:** [vox-system-spec.md](docs/articles/vox-system-spec.md) - Clip Library section

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Implement `VoxClipLibrary : IVoxClipLibrary`
- [ ] On `InitializeAsync()`, scan `sounds/vox/`, `sounds/fvox/`, `sounds/hgrunt/` folders
- [ ] For each `.mp3` file, extract: name (filename without extension, lowercased), file size, duration (via FFprobe)
- [ ] Store inventory in `Dictionary<VoxClipGroup, Dictionary<string, VoxClipInfo>>`
- [ ] Log clip counts per group on initialization
- [ ] `GetClips(group)` returns all clips for a group
- [ ] `GetClip(group, name)` returns single clip or null
- [ ] `SearchClips(group, query, maxResults)` returns prefix matches first, then substring matches (case-insensitive)
- [ ] `GetClipFilePath(group, name)` returns full file path
- [ ] `GetClipCount(group)` returns count
- [ ] Parallelize FFprobe duration extraction for startup performance
- [ ] Handle missing folders gracefully (log warning, continue)

## Technical Notes

**FFprobe duration extraction:**
```bash
ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format clip.mp3
```
Parse `format.duration` from JSON output.

**Search priority:** Prefix matches sorted alphabetically, then substring matches sorted alphabetically. Max 25 results by default.

**Lifetime:** Singleton - loaded once at startup, held in memory for the application lifetime.

## Dependencies

- Core types and interfaces (VOX types issue)
- FFprobe must be available in PATH

closing_issues.title: feat(vox): Implement VoxConcatenationService for FFmpeg audio joining
closing_issues.body:
## Description

Implement `VoxConcatenationService` - a singleton service that concatenates multiple MP3 clips into a single audio stream with configurable silence gaps between clips using FFmpeg.

## Context

This is the audio processing core of VOX. It takes a list of clip file paths and joins them with silence, producing a temporary audio file that can be streamed to Discord via the existing PlaybackService.

**Spec Reference:** [vox-system-spec.md](docs/articles/vox-system-spec.md) - Audio Pipeline section

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Implement `VoxConcatenationService : IVoxConcatenationService`
- [ ] `ConcatenateAsync(clipFilePaths, wordGapMs, cancellationToken)` produces a temporary audio file
- [ ] Insert silence of `wordGapMs` milliseconds between each clip
- [ ] Output format compatible with PlaybackService (PCM s16le, 48kHz, stereo preferred)
- [ ] Handle single-clip input (no silence needed)
- [ ] Clean temporary files on cancellation
- [ ] Return the path to the concatenated temporary file

## Technical Notes

**Silence gap calculation (PCM 48kHz, 16-bit, stereo):**
```
Silence bytes = gapMs * 48000 * 2 (bytes/sample) * 2 (channels) / 1000 = gapMs * 192
```

**FFmpeg approaches (choose most reliable):**

1. Concat demuxer with silence file entries
2. Filter complex with `adelay`/`apad`
3. Programmatic PCM: decode each clip, append silence bytes between segments

The simplest approach may be to decode all clips to PCM, programmatically insert silence bytes, and output the concatenated PCM.

**Lifetime:** Singleton (stateless - each call produces an independent temp file)

**Temp file management:** Use a dedicated temp directory, clean up after playback completes.

## Dependencies

- Core types and interfaces (VOX types issue)
- FFmpeg must be available in PATH

closing_issues.title: feat(vox): Implement VoxService orchestrator
closing_issues.body:
## Description

Implement `VoxService` - the main orchestrator that coordinates the full VOX pipeline: tokenize input → resolve clips → concatenate audio → play via PlaybackService.

## Context

VoxService is the central service that slash commands and API endpoints call. It ties together the clip library, concatenation service, and existing PlaybackService.

**Spec Reference:** [vox-system-spec.md](docs/articles/vox-system-spec.md) - IVoxService section

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Implement `VoxService : IVoxService`
- [ ] `PlayAsync(guildId, message, group, options, cancellationToken)`:
  - Tokenize input (split on whitespace, lowercase, strip punctuation)
  - Look up each token in `IVoxClipLibrary` for the requested group
  - Collect file paths for matched clips, track skipped words
  - Call `IVoxConcatenationService.ConcatenateAsync()` with matched clip paths
  - Create transient `Sound` object wrapping the concatenated file
  - Call `IPlaybackService.PlayAsync()` to stream to Discord
  - Clean up temporary file after playback
  - Return `VoxPlaybackResult` with matched/skipped word lists
- [ ] `TokenizePreview(message, group)`:
  - Parse message into tokens
  - Look up each token, return `VoxTokenPreview` with match status and estimated duration
  - No audio processing - preview only
- [ ] Validate message against `VoxOptions` limits (MaxMessageWords, MaxMessageLength)
- [ ] Return error if zero clips matched
- [ ] Return error if user not in voice channel (or delegate to caller)

## Technical Notes

**Tokenization rules:**
1. Split on whitespace
2. Convert to lowercase
3. Strip leading/trailing punctuation
4. Empty tokens filtered out

**Transient Sound object for PlaybackService:**
```csharp
var voxSound = new Sound
{
    Id = Guid.NewGuid(),
    GuildId = guildId,
    Name = $"vox-{DateTime.UtcNow:yyyyMMddHHmmss}",
    FileName = concatenatedFilePath,
    FileSizeBytes = new FileInfo(concatenatedFilePath).Length,
    DurationSeconds = estimatedDuration
};
```

**Lifetime:** Scoped (per-request pipeline coordination)

## Dependencies

- VoxClipLibrary implementation
- VoxConcatenationService implementation
- Existing IPlaybackService

## Context

Each command maps to one of the three Half-Life clip groups. They share the same parameters and behavior, differing only in which `VoxClipGroup` they target.

- [ ] `/fvox message:[string] gap:[int?]` - Play FVOX group announcement
- [ ] `/hgrunt message:[string] gap:[int?]` - Play HGrunt group announcement
- [ ] All commands use shared `PlayVoxAsync` helper method with group parameter
- [ ] `message` parameter: MaxLength 500, required
- [ ] `gap` parameter: MinValue 20, MaxValue 200, optional (defaults to VoxOptions.DefaultWordGapMs)

closing_issues.title: fix(vox): Add guild-level audio settings check to Portal VOX controller
closing_issues.body:
## Problem

The VOX Portal API does not check guild-level audio settings (`GuildAudioSettings.AudioEnabled`) before allowing playback. This creates an inconsistency where:

- **VOX slash commands** (`/vox`, `/fvox`, `/hgrunt`) correctly enforce both global AND guild-level audio settings via the `[RequireAudioEnabled]` precondition
- **VOX Portal API** (`/api/portal/vox/play`) only checks the global `Features:AudioEnabled` setting

If a guild admin disables audio via guild settings, VOX slash commands will be blocked but portal playback will still work.

## Current Behavior

| Component | Global Audio Check | Guild-Level Check |
|-----------|-------------------|-------------------|
| VOX Slash Commands | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| VOX Portal API (`/play`) | ✅ Yes | ❌ Missing |
| VOX Portal API (clips, preview) | ❌ No | ❌ No |

## Expected Behavior

The VOX Portal should check guild-level audio settings the same way the Soundboard Portal does in `PortalSoundboardController.cs` (lines 98-110).

## Implementation

1. Inject `IGuildAudioSettingsService` into `PortalVoxController`
2. Add guild-level audio check in the `Play()` method (similar to soundboard pattern)
3. Return appropriate error response when guild audio is disabled

## References

- `PortalVoxController.cs` line 240 - current global-only check
- `PortalSoundboardController.cs` lines 98-110 - reference implementation
- `RequireAudioEnabledAttribute.cs` lines 39-42 - guild check logic

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `PortalVoxController.Play()` checks `GuildAudioSettings.AudioEnabled` before playback
- [ ] Returns user-friendly error when guild audio is disabled
- [ ] Consistent behavior between slash commands and portal API

closing_issues.title: feat(vox): Parse punctuation (comma, period) as timing tokens in text entry
closing_issues.body:
## Description

When users type punctuation in the VOX text entry box, it should be automatically parsed and converted to the corresponding timing tokens/clips, which provide natural pauses in the synthesized speech.

## Punctuation Mappings

| Character | Token | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| `,` (comma) | `_comma` | Short pause between phrases |
| `.` (period) | `_period` | Longer pause at end of sentences |

## Current Behavior

Punctuation is either ignored or treated as literal text, not converted to the corresponding audio clips.

## Expected Behavior

- Typing `hello, world` should be parsed as `hello _comma world`
- Typing `hello. goodbye` should be parsed as `hello _period goodbye`
- The timing clips provide appropriate pauses matching Half-Life's sentences.txt behavior

## Implementation Notes

- Update the VOX tokenizer/parser to recognize punctuation
- Convert punctuation to corresponding timing tokens during parsing
- Ensure token preview strip displays these as tokens
- Handle edge cases (multiple punctuation, punctuation at start/end)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Commas in input text are converted to `_comma` tokens
- [ ] Periods in input text are converted to `_period` tokens
- [ ] Preview strip shows punctuation as timing tokens
- [ ] Audio playback includes the appropriate pause clips
- [ ] Works in both Portal UI and slash commands

Phase 1 is the foundation on which all subsequent Blazor work rests. The goal is zero disruption to existing Razor Pages while wiring in Blazor Server. Key infrastructure includes: service registration, middleware pipeline, root component files, `IDbContextFactory` migration for circuit-safe DbContext usage, refactored guild authorization handlers for Blazor compatibility, a revalidating auth state provider, and a circuit-scoped IP service for audit logging.

- [ ] `SearchService.cs` and `PreviewController.cs` updated to use factory-resolved contexts
- [ ] Guild authorization handlers (`GuildAccessHandler`, `GuildAccessAuthorizationHandler`, `PortalGuildMemberAuthorizationHandler`) support resource-based auth with HttpContext fallback

- [ ] Existing Razor Pages (`/`, `/Admin/Settings`, etc.) still work unchanged

- `UseAntiforgery()` must be placed after `UseAuthorization()` in the pipeline

closing_issues.title: Migrate to IDbContextFactory for Blazor circuit-safe DbContext usage
closing_issues.body:
## Description
Replace `AddDbContext` with `AddPooledDbContextFactory` for both SQLite and PostgreSQL providers in `Infrastructure/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`. Fix the two direct DbContext consumers that are incompatible with Blazor circuits.

## Context
Blazor Server circuits can outlive a scoped lifetime. Injecting a scoped `DbContext` directly into a long-lived component causes "DbContext disposed" errors. The solution is `IDbContextFactory<BotDbContext>`, which creates a short-lived context per operation. `AddPooledDbContextFactory` also registers a scoped `DbContext` automatically via the factory, so existing Identity, repositories, and Razor Pages code continues to work without changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/DiscordBot.Infrastructure/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` updated to use `AddPooledDbContextFactory<SqliteBotDbContext>` for SQLite provider
- [ ] `src/DiscordBot.Infrastructure/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` updated to use `AddPooledDbContextFactory<PostgresBotDbContext>` for PostgreSQL provider
- [ ] `IDbContextFactory<BotDbContext>` is resolvable from DI (for Blazor components)
- [ ] Existing code that injects `BotDbContext` directly continues to work (scoped fallback via factory)
- [ ] `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Services/SearchService.cs` (line ~27) updated to resolve DbContext via factory
- [ ] `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Controllers/PreviewController.cs` (line ~24) updated to resolve DbContext via factory
- [ ] No "DbContext disposed" errors under normal operation
- [ ] All existing repository tests pass

## Technical Notes
- `AddPooledDbContextFactory` registers both the factory (`IDbContextFactory<T>`) and a scoped `DbContext<T>` -- no additional code needed for backward compat
- For PostgreSQL, the factory needs to wrap `PostgresBotDbContext` as `IDbContextFactory<BotDbContext>` if the application uses `BotDbContext` as the abstraction (adapter pattern may be needed)
- Pattern for Blazor components using the factory:
  ```csharp
  await using var ctx = await DbFactory.CreateDbContextAsync();
  var result = await ctx.Users.ToListAsync();
  ```
- `SearchService.cs` is 919 lines -- search for the DbContext injection at line 27 rather than reading the whole file
- `PreviewController.cs` DbContext injection is at line 24

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: #1633 (service registration in place)
- Part of: #1631 (Phase 1 Epic)

## Testing Requirements
- `dotnet test` passes (repository tests exercise DbContext)
- Manual: log in, navigate guild settings page (uses Identity + repositories)
- Manual: trigger a search to verify `SearchService` still works
- Manual: trigger a preview popup to verify `PreviewController` still works

## Documentation Updates
- Update `docs/articles/database-schema.md` with note on factory pattern for Blazor components

closing_issues.title: Refactor guild authorization handlers for Blazor resource-based auth
closing_issues.body:
## Description
Modify `GuildAccessHandler`, `GuildAccessAuthorizationHandler`, and `PortalGuildMemberAuthorizationHandler` to support resource-based authorization. Check `context.Resource` first (for Blazor callers), then fall back to `IHttpContextAccessor` (for Razor Pages callers).

## Context
The existing guild authorization handlers extract `guildId` from `HttpContext.Request.RouteValues`. In Blazor Server circuits, `HttpContext` is null after the initial HTTP request -- the circuit runs over WebSocket, not HTTP. This causes all guild-scoped authorization to fail in Blazor components. The fix is resource-based authorization: Blazor components pass the `guildId` as the resource when calling `AuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync(user, guildId, "GuildAccess")`, and the handlers check `context.Resource` before falling back to HttpContext route values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Authorization/GuildAccessHandler.cs` modified to check `context.Resource is ulong resourceGuildId` before falling back to HttpContext route extraction
- [ ] `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Authorization/GuildAccessAuthorizationHandler.cs` modified with same resource-first pattern
- [ ] `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Authorization/PortalGuildMemberAuthorizationHandler.cs` modified with same resource-first pattern
- [ ] Existing Razor Pages that use these handlers continue to work (HttpContext fallback path is exercised)
- [ ] Blazor component calling `AuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync(user, (ulong)guildId, "GuildAccess")` succeeds when user has access
- [ ] Authorization is denied correctly when user does not have guild access (both paths)

## Technical Notes
- Pattern for handlers:
  ```csharp
  ulong guildId;
  if (context.Resource is ulong resourceGuildId)
      guildId = resourceGuildId;
  else
  {
      // existing HttpContext route value extraction
      var httpContext = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext;
      // ...
  }
  ```
- Blazor component usage pattern:
  ```csharp
  var result = await AuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync(User, GuildId, "GuildAccess");
  ```
- This is listed as a High severity risk in the migration plan -- get it right before any Blazor page navigates to guild routes

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: #1633 (service registration, Phase 1 infrastructure)
- Part of: #1631 (Phase 1 Epic)

## Testing Requirements
- Unit test: verify handler approves with valid `context.Resource` (ulong guild ID)
- Unit test: verify handler approves via HttpContext route value (existing path)
- Unit test: verify handler denies for unauthorized guild on both paths
- Manual: navigate to a guild page in Razor Pages -- authorization must still work

## Documentation Updates

closing_issues.title: Implement RevalidatingAuthenticationStateProvider for Blazor circuits
closing_issues.body:
## Description
Create `RevalidatingAuthStateProvider.cs` in `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Components/Services/` that periodically validates user sessions every 30 minutes. Register it in DI.

## Context
Blazor Server circuits can outlive cookie expiry. A user whose auth cookie has expired would still appear authenticated inside an active circuit. `RevalidatingServerAuthenticationStateProvider` is an ASP.NET Core base class that periodically re-checks the user's validity against a stamp validator, forcing re-authentication when the session is no longer valid.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Components/Services/RevalidatingAuthStateProvider.cs` created, inheriting from `RevalidatingServerAuthenticationStateProvider`
- [ ] Revalidation interval set to 30 minutes
- [ ] `ValidateAuthenticationStateAsync` checks that the user still exists and their security stamp is valid using `IUserClaimsPrincipalFactory<ApplicationUser>` or `UserManager<ApplicationUser>`
- [ ] Provider registered in DI in `WebServiceExtensions.cs` or a dedicated Blazor services extension
- [ ] A user whose cookie has expired (simulated by clearing the cookie) is redirected to login on the next revalidation cycle
- [ ] An active, valid session is not interrupted

## Technical Notes
- Base class: `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.RevalidatingServerAuthenticationStateProvider`
- The implementation should use `IServiceScopeFactory` to create a new scope for each validation check (never inject scoped services directly into a singleton provider)
- Security stamp validation pattern:
  ```csharp
  protected override async Task<bool> ValidateAuthenticationStateAsync(
      AuthenticationState authState, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
  {
      await using var scope = ScopeFactory.CreateAsyncScope();
      var userManager = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<UserManager<ApplicationUser>>();
      return await ValidateSecurityStampAsync(userManager, authState.User);
  }
  ```
- `ValidateSecurityStampAsync` is a helper that checks `ISecurityStampValidator`

- Part of: #1631 (Phase 1 Epic)

closing_issues.title: Create circuit-scoped CircuitClientInfoService for audit logging
closing_issues.body:
## Description
Create `CircuitClientInfoService.cs` in `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Components/Services/` that captures the client IP address from the initial HTTP request and makes it available for the duration of the Blazor circuit.

## Context
Audit logging records the client IP for actions taken through the admin portal. In Razor Pages, this is straightforward via `HttpContext.Connection.RemoteIpAddress`. In Blazor Server, `HttpContext` is only available during the initial HTTP request that upgrades to a WebSocket. After the upgrade, `IHttpContextAccessor.HttpContext` is null. This service captures the IP during circuit initialization and stores it for the circuit's lifetime, so audit log entries from Blazor components still record the correct IP.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Components/Services/CircuitClientInfoService.cs` created
- [ ] Service captures `HttpContext.Connection.RemoteIpAddress` during the initial HTTP phase (via `CircuitHandler` or constructor injection with `IHttpContextAccessor`)
- [ ] Service exposes `string? ClientIpAddress` property readable throughout the circuit's lifetime
- [ ] Service registered as scoped in DI (one instance per circuit)
- [ ] Audit log entries written from Blazor components use the IP from this service
- [ ] Service gracefully handles cases where IP is unavailable (returns null, does not throw)

## Technical Notes
- Implementation options:
  1. `CircuitHandler` subclass -- `OnCircuitOpenedAsync` is called during HTTP phase; capture IP there
  2. Constructor injection with `IHttpContextAccessor` -- works if resolved during DI initialization while `HttpContext` is still available
- Prefer the `CircuitHandler` approach as it is more explicit about the lifecycle
- Register with `services.AddScoped<CircuitClientInfoService>()` and `services.AddScoped<CircuitHandler, CircuitClientInfoService>()` if using handler approach
- Consider X-Forwarded-For header handling for reverse proxy scenarios (consistent with how existing Razor Pages audit logging works)

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: #1633 (service registration, Phase 1 infrastructure)
- Part of: #1631 (Phase 1 Epic)

## Testing Requirements
- Manual: perform an audited action from a Blazor page and verify the IP appears in the audit log
- Manual: verify existing Razor Pages audit logging is unaffected

## Documentation Updates
- Update `docs/articles/audit-log-system.md` with note on IP capture for Blazor circuits

mentioned_issues.title: Epic: Phase 2 - Blazor Component Library
mentioned_issues.body:
## Description
Port all 55 shared `.cshtml` partial components to `.razor` Blazor components organized across three tiers by complexity, and create the JS interop service layer.

## Context
The portal has 55 shared components currently implemented as Razor partial views with ViewModel classes. These must be ported to Blazor before any pages can be migrated. The work is organized in tiers: Tier 1 (25 atomic/pure render components) is fully parallelizable, Tier 2 (9 interactive components) needs JS interop or C# events, and Tier 3 (22 complex/stateful components) involves SignalR or multi-component composition.

The porting pattern is consistent:
- ViewModel properties become `[Parameter]` properties in `@code {}`
- `Html.Raw(content)` becomes `@((MarkupString)content)`
- `onclick="..."` strings become `@onclick="Handler"` with `EventCallback`
- Tailwind classes are identical -- no changes needed

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 25 Tier 1 components ported to `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Components/Shared/`
- [ ] All 9 Tier 2 components ported with JS interop or C# event handling
- [ ] All 22 Tier 3 components ported with SignalR or multi-component composition
- [ ] JS interop services created in `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Components/Interop/`: `ToastInterop`, `ThemeInterop`, `ChartJsInterop`, `TimezoneInterop`, `ClipboardInterop`, `NavigationInterop`
- [ ] `blazor-chart-interop.js` created in `wwwroot/js/`
- [ ] Visual regression: each component renders identically to its Razor partial equivalent
- [ ] Toast notifications work from Blazor components via `ToastInterop`
- [ ] Chart.js renders in a test component via `ChartJsInterop` in `OnAfterRenderAsync`

## Technical Notes
- Component source files are in `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Pages/Shared/Components/`
- ViewModel source files are in `src/DiscordBot.Bot/ViewModels/Components/`
- Target location: `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Components/Shared/`
- Tier 3 complex components (e.g., VoiceChannelPanel, SignalR-dependent) should subscribe to `IDashboardEventBus` once it is available in Phase 5; for Phase 2, they may use stub/placeholder event subscriptions
- Discord IDs (ulong) must remain as strings in any JS interop calls to avoid precision loss

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: #1631 (Phase 1 Blazor Foundation complete)
- Blocks: Phase 3 Simple Pages epic

## Testing Requirements
- Side-by-side visual comparison for each ported component
- Toast interop: call `ToastInterop.ShowSuccessAsync("Test")` from a Blazor page and verify the toast appears
- Chart interop: render a bar chart with `ChartJsInterop` in a test component

## Documentation Updates
- `docs/articles/component-api.md` -- rewrite for Blazor component library parameters and usage
- `.claude/agents/web-ui-portal.md` -- update component inventory

mentioned_issues.title: Create JS interop services for Blazor components
mentioned_issues.body:
## Description
Create 6 JS interop C# service classes in `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Components/Interop/` and create `blazor-chart-interop.js` for Chart.js lifecycle management.

## Context
Blazor Server components cannot call browser APIs directly -- they use `IJSRuntime` to invoke JavaScript functions. Rather than scattering `IJSRuntime` calls throughout components, this task creates dedicated typed interop services that encapsulate the JS calls. This keeps components clean and makes the JS boundary explicit.

## Acceptance Criteria
Interop services created in `src/DiscordBot.Bot/Components/Interop/`:
- [ ] `ToastInterop.cs` -- wraps existing `toast.js`; exposes `ShowSuccessAsync(string message)`, `ShowErrorAsync(string message)`, `ShowInfoAsync(string message)`
- [ ] `ThemeInterop.cs` -- wraps existing `theme.js`; exposes `SetThemeAsync(string theme)`, `GetCurrentThemeAsync()`
- [ ] `ChartJsInterop.cs` -- wraps new `blazor-chart-interop.js`; exposes `CreateChartAsync(string canvasId, object config)`, `UpdateChartAsync(string canvasId, object data)`, `DestroyChartAsync(string canvasId)`
- [ ] `TimezoneInterop.cs` -- wraps existing `timezone.js`; exposes `GetUserTimezoneAsync()`, `FormatDateAsync(DateTime utcDate, string format)`
- [ ] `ClipboardInterop.cs` -- uses browser Clipboard API; exposes `CopyToClipboardAsync(string text)`
- [ ] `NavigationInterop.cs` -- sidebar toggle, scroll; exposes `ToggleSidebarAsync()`, `ScrollToTopAsync()`, `ScrollToElementAsync(string elementId)`

JavaScript file created in `src/DiscordBot.Bot/wwwroot/js/`:
- [ ] `blazor-chart-interop.js` -- exposes `createChart(canvasId, config)`, `updateChart(canvasId, data)`, `destroyChart(canvasId)` functions; manages Chart.js instance registry by canvas ID

All services:
- [ ] Registered in DI (Scoped or Singleton as appropriate)
- [ ] Implement `IAsyncDisposable` if they load a JS module via `IJSRuntime.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>`
- [ ] All `string` parameters for Discord IDs use string type (no numeric Discord IDs passed to JS)

## Technical Notes
- Interop pattern using module loading:
  ```csharp
  public class ToastInterop : IAsyncDisposable
  {
      private readonly Lazy<Task<IJSObjectReference>> _moduleTask;
      public ToastInterop(IJSRuntime js)
          => _moduleTask = new(() => js.InvokeAsync<IJSObjectReference>(
              "import", "/js/toast.js").AsTask());

      public async Task ShowSuccessAsync(string message) {
          var module = await _moduleTask.Value;
          await module.InvokeVoidAsync("showSuccess", message);
      }
  }
  ```
- `ChartJsInterop` must handle the `OnAfterRenderAsync` timing concern: Chart.js requires the canvas element to exist in the DOM before initialization
- `blazor-chart-interop.js` should store chart instances in a `Map` keyed by canvas ID to support `update` and `destroy` calls

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: #1631 (Phase 1 complete -- Blazor services registered)
- Part of: #1654 (Phase 2 Epic)
- Required by: #1660 (ToastContainer), #1662 (VoiceChannelPanel, charts)

## Testing Requirements
- `dotnet build` passes
- `ToastInterop.ShowSuccessAsync("Hello")` from a Blazor component displays a toast
- `ChartJsInterop.CreateChartAsync` renders a Chart.js bar chart in `OnAfterRenderAsync`
- `ClipboardInterop.CopyToClipboardAsync` copies text (manual browser test)
- `ThemeInterop.SetThemeAsync` switches theme without page reload

## Documentation Updates
- Add interop service API to `docs/articles/component-api.md`

mentioned_issues.title: Phase 4.1: Migrate simple CRUD form pages to Blazor
mentioned_issues.body:
## Description

Convert the six simple CRUD form pages to Blazor using `EditForm` and `DataAnnotationsValidator`. Each page maps directly to a create or edit operation on a single entity.

## Context

These pages are the simplest form migrations in Phase 4: each has a single model, one submit action, and no complex dependencies. Completing them first proves out the Blazor EditForm pattern before tackling more complex tabbed settings pages. Blocking sub-issue of the Phase 4 epic (#1627).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `Admin/Users/Create` migrated to `Components/Pages/Admin/Users/UserCreate.razor`
- [ ] `Admin/Users/Edit` migrated to `Components/Pages/Admin/Users/UserEdit.razor`
- [ ] `Guilds/Edit` migrated to `Components/Pages/Guilds/GuildEdit.razor`
- [ ] `Guilds/ScheduledMessages/Create` migrated to `Components/Pages/Guilds/ScheduledMessages/ScheduledMessageCreate.razor`
- [ ] `Guilds/ScheduledMessages/Edit` migrated to `Components/Pages/Guilds/ScheduledMessages/ScheduledMessageEdit.razor`
- [ ] `Guilds/Welcome` migrated to `Components/Pages/Guilds/GuildWelcome.razor`
- [ ] All forms use `EditForm` + `DataAnnotationsValidator`; validation messages appear inline
- [ ] Toast notification fires on successful save and on error
- [ ] Navigation sidebar/NavMenu links updated so pages are reachable without typing URLs
- [ ] Corresponding Razor PageModel files removed after successful migration

## Technical Notes

### Form Pattern
```razor
<EditForm Model="model" OnValidSubmit="HandleSubmit" FormName="createUser">
    <DataAnnotationsValidator />
    <ValidationSummary />
    <FormInput @bind-Value="model.Username" Label="Username" />
    <Button Type="submit">Save</Button>
</EditForm>
```

### Service Injection
Components inject services directly (e.g., `IUserManagementService`, `IGuildService`, `IScheduledMessageService`). Do NOT route through API controllers.

### Route Parameters
Pages with edit forms receive entity ID via `[Parameter]` on the `@page` directive route:
```razor
@page "/Admin/Users/{UserId:long}/Edit"
[Parameter] public long UserId { get; set; }
```

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: Phase 3 (Simple Pages) epic
- Related to: #1627 (Phase 4 epic)

## Testing Requirements
- Submit each form with valid data and verify save succeeds
- Submit each form with invalid data and verify validation messages appear
- Verify toast shows on success and on server-side error
- Verify cancel/back navigation works correctly
- Verify routes match existing URL patterns to avoid breaking bookmarks

## Documentation Updates
- No new documentation required; existing form-implementation-standards.md covers the pattern

---

## Component Library Requirements

**MANDATORY:** Use existing Blazor components from `Components/Shared/` — do NOT hand-roll HTML for functionality these components already provide. No inline `<script>` blocks — use `@onclick` handlers and `IJSRuntime` interop services from `Components/Interop/`.

**Available components (non-exhaustive):**
- **Layout:** `Alert`, `Card`, `EnhancedCard`, `DashboardWidget`, `EmptyState`, `HeroMetricCard`
- **Navigation:** `GuildBreadcrumb`, `CommandBreadcrumb`, `NavTabs`, `TabPanel`, `Pagination`, `GuildTabNavigation`
- **Forms:** `FormInput`, `FormSelect`, `FormToggle`, `AutocompleteInput`, `Button`
- **Feedback:** `Badge`, `StatusBadge`, `SeverityBadge`, `StatusIndicator`, `LoadingSpinner`, `Skeleton`
- **Interactive:** `ConfirmationModal`, `TypedConfirmationModal`, `ToastContainer`, `SortDropdown`
- **Domain:** `GuildHeader`, `CommandHeader`, `VoiceChannelPanel`, `VoiceSelector`, `SsmlPreview`
- **Interop services:** `ToastInterop`, `ChartJsInterop`, `ClipboardInterop`, `TimezoneInterop`, `ThemeInterop`, `NavigationInterop`

**Quality gates:**
1. No inline `<script>` blocks (use `@onclick` + interop services)
2. No inline `<style>` blocks with hardcoded hex colors (use Tailwind classes or CSS variables)
3. Use `<Button>` not raw `<a class="btn ...">` or hand-rolled button markup
4. Use `<Alert>` for success/error/warning messages
5. Use `<Badge>` / `<StatusBadge>` / `<SeverityBadge>` for labels
6. Use `<Card>` / `<EnhancedCard>` for content sections
7. Use `<FormInput>` / `<FormSelect>` / `<FormToggle>` in forms
8. Use `<GuildBreadcrumb>` or `<CommandBreadcrumb>` for navigation
9. Use `<Pagination>` for paginated lists
10. Reference: `GuildDetails.razor` and `FlaggedEventDetails.razor` are the gold standard — follow their patterns

**Hosting model:** Pages render inside `_BlazorHost.cshtml` which provides `_Layout.cshtml` (navbar, sidebar, all global JS). `MainLayout.razor` is just `@Body`. Do NOT add outer page chrome to Blazor pages — it is already provided by the host.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The manual construction of the `memory` configuration dictionary is a bit verbose and could be brittle. If fields are added or removed from `MemoryConfig`, this section will need to be updated manually. To make this more maintainable and dynamic, you could build this dictionary by introspecting the `MemoryConfig` model's fields. This would automatically adapt to changes in `MemoryConfig` as long as the naming convention (`episodic_*`, `semantic_*`) is followed.

```python
        # Dynamically build the nested memory dictionary
        memory_dict = {"episodic": {}, "semantic": {}}
        for field_name in self.memory.model_fields:
            value = getattr(self.memory, field_name)
            if field_name.startswith("episodic_"):
                key = field_name.removeprefix("episodic_")
                memory_dict["episodic"][key] = value
            elif field_name.startswith("semantic_"):
                key = field_name.removeprefix("semantic_")
                memory_dict["semantic"][key] = value

        config_dict = {
            'agent': {
                'name': self.name,
                'version': self.version,
                'max_iterations': self.runtime_settings.max_iterations,
                'timeout': self.runtime_settings.timeout,
            },
            'generation': self.generation.model_dump(),
            'timeouts': self.timeouts.model_dump(),
            'model': self.model.model_dump(),
            'memory': memory_dict,
            'logging': self.logging.model_dump(),
            'compliance': self.compliance.model_dump(),
        }
```

Add variables MCP tools (CRUD) + CLI
closing_issues.body:
Motivation
n8n Variables API enables storing small key/value data for workflows. Exposing it via MCP is useful for prompt/config toggles and simple state.

Public API
- POST /variables
- GET /variables
- PUT /variables/{id}
- DELETE /variables/{id}

Deliverables
- MCP tools
  - list_variables() → { data: variable[], nextCursor? }
  - create_variable({ key, value }) → variable
  - update_variable({ id, value }) → variable
  - delete_variable({ id }) → { ok: true }
- Client methods in `src/n8n-client.ts`
- CLI commands: `variables list`, `variables create --key --value`, `variables update <id> --value`, `variables delete <id>`
- README updates with examples
- Tests

Acceptance criteria
- Listing supports pagination when available
- Create requires unique key; proper error surfaced when duplicate
- Update persists value change
- Delete removes variable
- CLI returns JSON; tools return structured content

closing_issues.title: Add tags CRUD MCP tools + CLI
closing_issues.body:
Motivation
Tags are the primary way to group workflows in n8n. MCP should support creating, updating, deleting, and listing tags.

Public API
- POST /tags
- GET /tags
- GET /tags/{id}
- PUT /tags/{id}
- DELETE /tags/{id}

Deliverables
- MCP tools
  - list_tags({ limit?, cursor? }) → { data: tag[], nextCursor? }
  - get_tag({ id }) → tag
  - create_tag({ name, color? }) → tag
  - update_tag({ id, name?, color? }) → tag
  - delete_tag({ id }) → { ok: true }
- Client methods in `src/n8n-client.ts`
- CLI commands: `tags list|get|create|update|delete`
- README updates
- Tests

Acceptance criteria
- Tags CRUD round-trips correctly
- Pagination supported on list
- Errors (409 on duplicate name, 404 on missing) mapped to friendly messages
- CLI prints JSON

closing_issues.title: Switch workflow update to PUT + optional If-Match concurrency
closing_issues.body:
Motivation
Public API specifies PUT /workflows/{id}. Our client uses PATCH, which can drift or fail on some versions. Also add optional optimistic concurrency.

Public API
- PUT /workflows/{id}

Deliverables
- Change `N8nClient.updateWorkflow` to use PUT (preserve signature)
- MCP tool `update_workflow` continues to accept `{ id, workflowJson, ifMatch? }`
- If `ifMatch` provided, send `If-Match` header; surface 412 errors clearly
- Update README and tests

Acceptance criteria
- Updating a workflow works on a current n8n instance using PUT
- Optional `ifMatch` header is sent when provided; 412 precondition failure mapped to a friendly error
- No breaking change to MCP tool interface

closing_issues.title: Expose credential schema fetcher

Motivation
Let clients fetch JSON schema for a credential type to validate or drive UIs.

Public API
- GET /credentials/schema/{credentialTypeName}

Deliverables
- MCP tool `get_credential_schema({ credentialTypeName })`
- Client method
- README + tests

Acceptance criteria
- Returns JSON schema
- 404s and auth failures mapped cleanly

closing_issues.title: Incremental graph ops at MCP layer (createNode/connect/update/delete/position)
Utilities: webhookUrls + runOnce helpers
closing_issues.body:
Summary
Add convenience tools for common tasks when orchestrating workflows.

Deliverables
- MCP tools
  - webhook_urls({ workflowId, nodeId }) → { testUrl, productionUrl }
  - run_once({ workflowId, input? }) → { executionId, status }
- Client methods; CLI; README; tests

Acceptance criteria
- webhook URLs match those shown in UI (respect baseUrl env); document prereqs for Webhook node
- run_once triggers a manual execution and returns executionId/status; handle non-trigger workflows gracefully

Notes
From docs/SUGGESTIONS.md.

closing_issues.title: chore(ci): Add required checks for benchmarking
closing_issues.body:
### Description

See #5951 for full context.

We need to migrate all workflows using the `on.[event].paths` filtering to use a `files-changed` job using `dorny/paths-filter` instead. To enforce required checks we need to add a required check job at the end, which always runs and is used as the main indicator for required checks.

An example implementation is done for `tests.yml` and `api-stability.yml`, reference PR is #5893 

Use the following prompt to create a draft PR:

```text
Do the following for these variables:

[WORKFLOW_NAME] = "Benchmarking"
[WORKFLOW_KEY] = "benchmarking"
[WORKFLOW_FILE] = "benchmarking.yml"

Use the file-filters at .github/file-filters.yml and the auto-update-tools workflow .github/workflows/auto-update-tools.yml as reference on how we added a check to enforce required checks. Then create the same for the [WORKFLOW_NAME] workflow:

Requirements:
1. **Add file filter**: Create a new filter called `run_[WORKFLOW_KEY]_for_prs` in .github/file-filters.yml containing all file paths from the workflow's current `on.pull_request.paths` (if it exists, otherwise include relevant paths for that workflow)

2. **Remove the paths filter**: Remove the paths filtering from the `on.pull_request.paths` so the workflow runs always for all pull requests.

3. **Modify workflow**: Update .github/workflows/[WORKFLOW_FILE].yml to:
   - Add `files-changed` job that detects file changes using the new filter
   - Make the main job(s) conditional with `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || needs.files-changed.outputs.run_[WORKFLOW_KEY]_for_prs == 'true'` and `needs: files-changed`
   - Add `[WORKFLOW_KEY]-required-check` job at the end that validates completion using `if: always()` pattern
   - **IMPORTANT**: Do NOT change the workflow triggers (`on:`) or concurrency settings beyond removing the paths filter

4. **Follow the exact pattern**: Use the auto-update-tools implementation as the template for job structure, naming, and logic.

The goal is to make the workflow:
- Always run for schedule and workflow_dispatch events
- Run conditionally for pull requests based on file changes
- Provide a reliable required check that can be used in branch protection rules

5. In the commit message use the keyword `[skip ci]` to skip the CI
```

PROJ: GFC Website - Phase 11: "Modern Legacy" Architecture & Operational Integration
closing_issues.body:
Issue Description
Objective: Kick off the development of the new GFC public website using Next.js 14+. This phase focuses on establishing the "Modern Legacy" design system and the mandatory integration with the GFC Web App for real-time club operations (Status, News, and Calendar).

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/PHASE_11_NEW_GFC_WEBSITE/00_WEBSITE_MASTER_PLAN.md

docs/in-process/PHASE_11_NEW_GFC_WEBSITE/01_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md

docs/in-process/PHASE_11_NEW_GFC_WEBSITE/04_WEBAPP_CONTROL_INTEGRATION.md
🚀 Tasks / Checklist
1. Design System & Global Layout
 Implement the "Midnight Blue & Burnished Gold" design tokens in Tailwind CSS.
 Create the High-End Global Header:
Sticky navigation with elegant hover states.
Live Status Indicator: Pulling real-time "Open/Closed" data from the Web App API.
 Create the Standardized Footer: Contact info, Social links, and specific links for Member Login.
2. Operational "Control" Bridge
 Setup the Next.js API Routes to consume data from the GFC Web App:
/api/club-status (Live toggle).
/api/announcements (Updates/News ticker).
/api/events (Public calendar items).
 Implement ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) logic for instant site refreshes when admins update data in the Web App.
3. Announcement & News Engine
 Build the "Update Bar" component: A premium, subtle notification bar at the top of the site for urgent club news.
 Build the Homepage News Module: A visual card system that displays featured announcements posted from the Web App.
4. Hall Rental & Financial Foundations
 Create the Financial Placeholder Logic: A toggle that shows/hides the "Donate" and "Member Dues" buttons based on Web App settings.
 Setup the Public Review Submission Form: A simple, high-end form that sends user feedback to the Web App moderation queue.
5. Accessibility & Responsiveness
 Implement the Mobile Navigation "Drawer": Full-screen, sleek dark overlay.
 Setup the High-Accessibility Toggle (Drafting state): Logic to increase contrast and font scale site-wide.
🛠️ Technical Requirements
Frontend: Next.js 14 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS.
Animations: Framer Motion for subtle "Reveal" transitions.
Integration: REST API connection to the existing GFC SQL database.
SEO: Automated Sitemap.xml and Metadata generation per page.
✅ Success Criteria
The Vibe: The site loads with the premium "Midnight Blue and Gold" theme, looking significantly more professional than the previous attempt.
Operational Control: Toggling the "Club Status" in the Web App Dashboard updates the website indicator in under 5 seconds.
Data Integrity: Posting an "Alert" in the Web App News table makes the website's top update bar appear instantly.
Frictionless Mobile: The site is 100% usable on a mobile phone with large, elegant touch targets.
Notes for Developer
The #1 priority is the Operational Integration. The website should feel like a 'live reflection' of what is happening inside the club. Use Tailwind custom colors to ensure the 'Burnished Gold' accents are consistent across all components.

closing_issues.title: PROJ: GFC Studio V2 - Phase 11: Visual Component System & Drag-and-Drop Editor
closing_issues.body:
Issue Description
Objective: Transforming the Foundation shell into a functional visual editor. This phase involves building the dynamic component library, the Drag-and-Drop (D&D) engine between the Blazor sidebars and the Next.js Iframe, and the Property Inspector for visual style editing.

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/PHASE_10_STUDIO_V2_REBUILD/02_COMPONENT_LIBRARY.md

docs/in-process/PHASE_10_STUDIO_V2_REBUILD/01_STUDIO_UI_SPECIFICATIONS.md
 (Properties Panel section)
🚀 Tasks / Checklist
1. Drag-and-Drop Infrastructure
 Implement the JS Interop Bridge that handles dragging a component from the Blazor Left Panel and injecting it into the Next.js Canvas.
 Setup the Next.js Drop Zones: Create visual "insertion lines" in the preview to show exactly where a component will land.
 Implement Post-Drop Logic: Automatically generate a new SectionId in the database when a component is dropped.
2. Visual Properties Inspector (Right Panel)
 Build the Contextual Editor: The panel must change its controls based on what component is selected (e.g., Image settings for images, Text settings for headings).
 Implement Visual Controls:
Color Pickers (Syncing to CSS Variables).
Sliders for margins/padding.
Dropdowns for Font selection (Outfit vs Inter).
 Setup Real-Time Property Syncing: Every slider movement in the Right Panel must update the Iframe preview in under 100ms.
3. The "Big Four" Core Components
Implement the specific rendering logic and property sets for the four most used blocks:

 Hero Section: Support for background image selection and headline overlay.
 Rich Text Block: Full integration for multi-line text with inline styling.
 Button/CTA: Visual control over links, padding, and "Burnished Gold" variants.
 Layout Grid: A smart container that can hold other components in 2 or 3 columns.
4. Next.js Dynamic Renderer
 Create the SectionRenderer component in Next.js: It must loop through the Sections array from the database and output the correct React components.
 Implement Live State Management (Zustand or Redux): Ensure the preview reflects changes without requiring a page refresh.
🛠️ Technical Requirements
D&D Engine: dnd-kit or react-beautiful-dnd (React side) paired with Custom Blazor event triggers.
Serialization: All component properties must be saved as JSON in the SQL Sections table.
Styling: Properties must be injected as CSS Variables or Tailwind classes for maximum performance.
✅ Success Criteria
Drag-to-Build: Dragging a "Hero" from the sidebar into the canvas visually adds that section instantly.
Visual Feedback: Clicking an element in the canvas highlights it with a blue border and opens its settings.
Live Tweaking: Changing the gold color of a button in the properties panel updates the preview in real-time.
Data Persistence: After refreshing the Studio, all added components remain in their correct order with their custom settings.
Notes for Developer
Focus on the Data Loop first. If the Right Panel can successfully tell the Iframe to change a color, the rest of the components are easy. Start with the 'Hero' component as your test case.

closing_issues.title: PROJ: GFC Studio V2 - Phase 15: Content Migration, URL Scraping & Portability
closing_issues.body:
Issue Description
Objective: Implement the ingestion engine and data portability tools. This system allows the GFC Studio to scrape content from the existing live website, parse HTML files, and provide a backup/restore mechanism for all visual sections.

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/PHASE_10_STUDIO_V2_REBUILD/00_MASTER_PLAN.md
 (Migration section)

docs/in-process/PHASE_10_STUDIO_V2_REBUILD/03_DATABASE_SCHEMA.md
🚀 Tasks / Checklist
1. URL Scraping & Asset Harvesting
 Implement the URL Ingestion Engine: A tool where you paste a link (e.g., gloucesterfraternityclub.com/about) and the system fetches the raw content.
 Setup Automated Asset Extraction: Automatically find all images in the scraped HTML, download them, and place them in the Studio Media Library.
 Implement Smart Block Identification: A rule-based engine that identifies "Text Blocks," "Headings," and "Images" from the scraped HTML and converts them into editable Studio blocks.
2. HTML & File Import
 Build the HTML/JSON File Uploader: Allow users to upload old .html exports or Studio .json backups.
 Implement the "Raw Code Wrapper": For complex legacy scripts or layouts that cannot be auto-converted, automatically wrap them in a "Custom Code Component" to preserve functionality.
3. Data Portability & Backups
 Build the Full-Site Export Tool: Generate a single .gfc-bundle (ZIP) containing every page and every image for local archiving.
 Implement the Static HTML Generator: Ability to export a "frozen" version of a page as a single standalone HTML/CSS file.
 Setup Database-to-JSON Migration: A tool to move a page between different environments (e.g., from a local development computer to the live server).
4. "Redirect Manager" Validation
 Connect the Legacy Route Manager (from Phase 11): Automatically suggest a redirect whenever a page is imported from an old URL.
🛠️ Technical Requirements
Scraper Backend: Use Playwright or Puppeteer within the Web App to render and capture legacy content.
Parsing: Use HtmlAgilityPack (C# side) or Cheerio (JavaScript side) for DOM analysis.
Portability: Use standard JSON schemas to ensure that a page exported today can still be imported years from now.
✅ Success Criteria
The Scraping Win: Pasting an old GFC website URL into Studio creates a new page with all text and images already in place.
Asset Recovery: Images from the old site are automatically optimized (converted to WebP) during the import process.
Backup Peace of Mind: A director can export a "Full Site Backup" to their desktop in under 60 seconds.
Environment Sync: A page designed on one server can be exported and imported into another with 100% visual parity.
Notes for Developer
The scraper is a 'best-effort' tool—it doesn't need to reconstruct 100% of the old styling, but it MUST capture 100% of the text and images. The goal is to save the user hours of manual copy-pasting during the migration.

closing_issues.title: PROJ: GFC Studio V2 - Phase 14: Integrated Utility Suite (Form Designer, Media Library & SEO)
closing_issues.body:
Issue Description
Objective: Implement the professional-grade utility suite within GFC Studio. This includes the centralized Media Library, the visual Form Builder for rentals, and the integrated SEO and Performance scoring dashboard that ensures the site stays lightning-fast.

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/PHASE_10_STUDIO_V2_REBUILD/00_MASTER_PLAN.md

1. Centralized Media Library (Asset Manager)
 Build the Asset Browser: A dedicated modal for uploading and choosing site images.
 Implement the Auto-Optimization Pipeline:
Automatically convert JPG/PNG to WebP.
Generate 3 responsive sizes for every upload (Mobile, Tablet, Desktop).
 Setup Usage Tracking: Add a visual indicator showing "This image is used on: Home, About Us."
2. Visual Form Designer & GFC Wizards
 Build the Drag-and-Drop Form Builder: Drag text fields, email inputs, and date pickers into a form container.
 Implement "Save & Resume" Logic: Backend logic for the Hall Rental form to generate a magic link for incomplete applications.
 Setup Submission Routing: Logic to direct form entries to specific Web App tables and trigger the correct director alerts.
3. SEO & Performance Dashboard
 Build the SEO Settings Panel: Edit meta titles, descriptions, and Open Graph (social share) images per page.

Character counters for titles (Green/Yellow/Red).
"Missing Alt Text" warnings for images in the current page.

closing_issues.title: PROJ: GFC Studio V2 - Phase 10: Foundation & Core Infrastructure
closing_issues.body:
Issue Description
Objective: Establish the high-performance core infrastructure for the redesigned GFC Studio. This phase focuses on creating the "Full-Page" editing workspace in the Blazor Web App and the seamless <iframe> integration that allows the Next.js website to be manipulated visually.

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/PHASE_10_STUDIO_V2_REBUILD/00_MASTER_PLAN.md

docs/in-process/PHASE_10_STUDIO_V2_REBUILD/03_DATABASE_SCHEMA.md
🚀 Tasks / Checklist
1. Full-Page Editor Layout (Blazor Server)
 Implement the Studio Shell: A dedicated route (/admin/studio/editor) that hides all standard app navigation and sidebars to provide a 100vw/100vh workspace.
 Build the Command Top Bar (60px): Include the Page Switcher, Save buttons, and Device toggles.
 Create Collapsible Side Panels:
Left: 280px (Component Library placeholder).
Right: 320px (Properties Inspector placeholder).
2. Real-Time Preview Canvas
 Implement the Center Canvas: A specialized container that hosts an <iframe> pointing to the Next.js dev server.
 Implement Multi-Device Viewport Scaling:
Desktop (100% width).
Tablet (768px with visual device frame).
Mobile (375px with visual device frame).
 Setup the Iframe PostMessage Bridge: Establish the base JavaScript channel to send "Update" commands from Studio to the Preview.
3. Database & Versioning Foundation
 Implement the Pages, Sections, and Drafts schema as per 

03_DATABASE_SCHEMA.md
.
 Create the Page Switcher Logic: Fetch the list of editable pages from the database and populate the Studio dropdown.

closing_issues.title: PROJ: GFC Studio V2 - Phase 12: Page Management, Versioning & Publishing Workflow
closing_issues.body:
Issue Description
Objective: Implement the robust "CMS" infrastructure required to manage multiple pages, maintain a safe history of changes (Auto-save/Versioning), and handle the "Publishing" lifecycle from a private draft to the public-facing GFC website.

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/PHASE_10_STUDIO_V2_REBUILD/00_MASTER_PLAN.md

docs/in-process/PHASE_10_STUDIO_V2_REBUILD/03_DATABASE_SCHEMA.md
 (Drafts and Pages tables)
🚀 Tasks / Checklist
1. Page Dashboard & Multi-Page Support
 Implement the Page Navigator: A searchable dashboard in the Studio Top Bar to switch between "Home," "About," and "Hall Rentals."
 Build the "New Page" Flow: Logic to create a blank page or clone an existing page as a new entity in the database.
 Implement Sitemap Sync: Ensure the Page Switcher list is always alphabetized and displays the current "Live" status of each page.
2. Debounced Auto-Save & Conflict Protection
 Implement the Auto-Save Engine: Automatically save the current editor state to the Drafts table every 2 seconds after a change.
 Add Visual Indicators: Show "Saving..." and "All changes saved" status in the Top Bar to prevent user anxiety.
 Implement Locking Logic: Prevent two different administrators from editing the same page simultaneously (prevents data loss).
3. Version History & Restore
 Build the History Sidebar: List all saved "Snapshot" versions with a timestamp and the name of the director who made them.
 Implement Visual Comparison (Preview-Only): Clicking a history item renders that old version in the iframe for review before hitting "Restore."
 Implement the "Name this Version" feature: Allow users to create "milestones" (e.g., "Ready for New Year Announcement").
4. The "Publish" Lifecycle
 Build the Publishing Wizard: A safe process that copies the current Draft state into the production Sections table.
 Implement On-Demand Cache Purging: When a page is published, Studio must trigger the Next.js API to revalidate and update the live site instantly.
 Add "Unpublish" Functionality: Ability to take a page offline (returns a 404 or redirect) without deleting it from Studio.
🛠️ Technical Requirements
Data Compression: Drafts should be serialized and stored as compressed JSON in SQL for performance.
Workflow State Engine: Strictly manage the lifecycle: Draft → Published → Archived.
API Cache: Use Next.js res.revalidate() to ensure the live site reflects the new content in under 5 seconds.
✅ Success Criteria
Multi-Page Agility: A user can switch from editing the Home page to the Contact page in under 3 seconds without a full browser reload.
The Safety Net: Closing the browser and returning to Studio restores the exact last state from the Auto-save.
One-Click Live: Hitting "Publish" makes the change visible on the public URL (e.g., www.gfc.com/rentals) immediately.
Time Travel: Rolling back to a version from yesterday successfully restores all components, styles, and data accurately.
Notes for Developer
Data integrity is the absolute priority here. The 'Draft' state must never overwrite the 'Published' state until the admin explicitly clicks the green button. This creates the 'undo' safety net directors need.
