closing_issues.title: PROJ: GFC Camera Security - Phase 7: Token-Based Stream Security & URL Hardening
closing_issues.body:
Issue Description
Objective: Secure the raw video streams coming from the Video Agent. Currently, RTSP/HLS streams can be vulnerable if the URLs are exposed. This phase implements short-lived, encrypted security tokens that must be present in every request. If a token is expired or missing, the Video Agent will instantly drop the connection.

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/CAMERA_REMOTE_ACCESS_SECURITY_MASTER_PLAN.md
 (Section 7.1 - 7.5)
🚀 Tasks / Checklist
1. Secure Token Engine (StreamSecurityService)
 Token Generator: Create a service to generate cryptographically random, timed tokens (e.g., JWT or signed HMAC hashes).
 Expiry Logic: Set tokens to expire after 60 seconds of inactivity.
 Validation Bridge: Logic to share a "Secret Key" between the Web App (the generator) and the Video Agent (the validator).
2. URL Hardening & Masking
 Encrypted Paths: Instead of showing the raw camera IP, use proxied URLs like /api/video/stream/camera-01?token=X.
 Dynamic Re-validation: Ensure that if a user keeps a stream open for an hour, the app silently refreshes the security token in the background.
3. Video Agent Access Guard
 Mandatory Token Check: Update the Video Agent to reject any HLS/M3U8 request that doesn't contain a valid, unexpired token.
 IP-Locking: (Optional) Bind a stream token to the user's specific VPN IP address, preventing a session from being "hijacked" even if the token is stolen.
4. Unauthorized Access Cleanup
 Connection Murder: Implement logic to instantly terminate any active socket connection as soon as a user's session ends or their access is revoked in Phase 2.
🛠️ Technical Requirements
Token Format: Use HMAC-SHA256 for signing stream URLs to ensure they cannot be tampered with.
Latency: Token validation must happen in under 10ms to avoid buffering issues.
Protocol: Ensure compatibility with standard HLS players used in the CameraFeed component.
✅ Success Criteria
Link Expiration: Copying a video URL from the browser's developer tools and pasting it into a new window fails after 60 seconds.
Zero Leakage: The raw credentials and internal IP of the NVR are NEVER visible in the browser's network traffic.
Session Binding: A token generated for "Director A" on the VPN will not work for "Director B" on their own VPN.
Immediate Kill: When a director clicks "Stop Viewing," the Video Agent stops processing that camera's data immediately to save bandwidth.
Notes for Developer
The user should never see these tokens—this all happens 'under the hood.' The goal is to make the video URLs useless outside of the authorized Web App session.

closing_issues.title: PROJ: GFC Camera Security - Phase 5: Automated VPN Profile Generation & Key Management
closing_issues.body:
Issue Description
Objective: Implement the automated engine that generates unique, secure WireGuard VPN profiles for every authorized user. This phase focuses on the cryptographic generation of per-user keypairs, static IP address assignment within the secure subnet, and the real-time synchronization with the WireGuard server running on the club computer.

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/CAMERA_REMOTE_ACCESS_SECURITY_MASTER_PLAN.md
 (Section 5.1 - 5.5)
🚀 Tasks / Checklist
1. VPN Management Service (WireGuardManagementService)
 Profile Engine: Create the core C# service to handle the full lifecycle of a VPN user (Generate → Activate → Revoke).
 Key Generation: Implement Curve25519 cryptographic generation for unique Private and Public keys.
 Encryption at Rest: Ensure Private Keys are encrypted before being stored in the VpnProfiles table.
2. Intelligent IP Address Management (IPAM)
 Static Assignment: Logic to automatically assign the next available IP inside the 10.8.0.x range to each user.
 Collision Prevention: Implement checks to ensure no two users are assigned the same VPN IP.
 IP Recycling: Logic to mark IPs as "Available" once a profile is permanently deleted or revoked.
3. Real-Time Server Synchronization
 CLI Peer Bridge: Implement the shell commands to instantly "Live-Inject" a new user into the active WireGuard interface:
wg set wg0 peer [PublicKey] allowed-ips [AssignedIP]/32.
 Persistence: Logic to save the current server state (wg-quick save) so users remain connected after a server reboot.
4. The Profile (.conf) Generator
 Final Config Assembly: Create the logic that stitches together the user's private key, assigned IP, and the club's public endpoint into a standard .conf file.
 DNS & Handshake Tuning: Pre-configure optimized settings like PersistentKeepalive = 25 to ensure the connection stays alive on mobile devices.
🛠️ Technical Requirements
Cryptography: Use an industry-standard library (e.g., BouncyCastle or Sodium.Core) for key generation.
Storage: Private keys MUST be encrypted in the database.
CLI Execution: The Web App service must have sufficient permissions to execute wg.exe commands on the host machine.
✅ Success Criteria
One-Click Creation: Clicking "Generate Profile" in the admin dashboard successfully creates a unique keypair and assigns a static IP in under 1 second.
Valid Output: The generated .conf file can be successfully imported into any standard WireGuard client (iPhone/Android/Windows).
Live Sync: Adding a user in the Web App UI makes them visible in the server's active peer list (wg show) instantly.
Revocation Security: Revoking a user's access in the UI immediately removes their peer from the server, cutting their connection mid-stream.
Notes for Developer
This is the most sensitive phase regarding data security. Under no circumstances should a user's Private Key be logged or displayed in plain text in the Audit Logs. Once the profile window is closed, only the encrypted version remains.

closing_issues.title: PROJ: GFC Camera Security - Phase 3: Real-Time Video Monitoring & Audit Dashboard

 (Section 3.1 - 3.5)

1. Active Sessions Tracker (Real-Time)

 Metric Tracking: Display active bandwidth usage (Mbps) and connection duration for each user.
 Remote Forfeit: Implement the "Disconnect Session" button to instantly kick a user off a stream.
2. VPN Readiness & Setup Status
 User Status List: A comprehensive list of all authorized users and their current security status.
 Setup Tracking: Visual indicators for:
Never (No profile created).
Pending (Profile downloaded but not yet connected).
Complete (Successfully connected via VPN at least once).
 Action Center: Buttons to "Resend Setup Instructions" or "Reset VPN Profile."
3. The Master Access Audit Log

 Action Tags: Categorize logs into Live View, Recording Playback, Snapshot Captured, and File Downloaded.
 Export Engine: One-click export to PDF, Excel, and CSV for board reporting.
4. Security Alert Center
 Alert Triage: Create a high-priority inbox for security events such as:
Multiple failed remote login attempts.
Unusual access hours (e.g., 3:00 AM remote views).
Unexpected location detections (Geofencing alerts).
 Resolution Workflow: Ability to mark alerts as "Reviewed," "Resolved," or "Dismissed" with notes.
🛠️ Technical Requirements
Real-Time Updates: Use SignalR to push session updates to the dashboard without requiring a page refresh.
Performance: Implement server-side pagination for the Audit Log to handle thousands of historical records efficiently.
Reporting: Integrate a lightweight library (e.g., QuestPDF or ClosedXML) for report generation.

Data privacy is important—ensure that the dashboard is strictly limited to 'SuperAdmin' or 'SecurityDirector' roles. The 'Active Sessions' view should be the default tab, as it provides the most critical real-time information.

closing_issues.title: PROJ: GFC Camera Security - Phase 6: Guided "One-Click" VPN Setup Wizard
closing_issues.body:
Issue Description
Objective: Replace the technical setup process with a high-end, user-friendly "Setup Wizard." This phase builds the landing page that users see when their remote access is blocked, guiding them through installing the WireGuard app, downloading their profile, and verifying their connection in under 2 minutes.

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/CAMERA_REMOTE_ACCESS_SECURITY_MASTER_PLAN.md
 (Section 6.1 - 6.5)
🚀 Tasks / Checklist
1. The "Secure Access Required" Landing Page
 Adaptive UI: Build the page that automatically appears when a remote user attempts to view a camera without a VPN.
 Device Optimization: Ensure the wizard looks and works perfectly on iPhone, Android, and Desktop browsers.
2. The 3-Step Setup Wizard
 Step 1: App Installation: Smart buttons that detect the user's device and open the correct App Store (iOS/Play Store/Windows) for WireGuard.
 Step 2: Profile Download:
Implement the "Secure Download" button that generates the .conf file on-the-fly.
Add clear "Tap-to-Import" instructions for mobile users.
 Step 3: Connectivity Test: A "Verify My Connection" button that checks the user's current IP against the NetworkLocationService.
3. Visual Guidance & Progress Tracking
 Animated Cues: Use subtle icons and progress bars to show the user exactly where they are in the process.
 Visual Success State: Once the VPN is verified, show a "Secure Access Enabled" screen with a direct link to the cameras.
4. Automated Notifications & Email Dispatch
 Welcome Email: Logic to send a personalized "Your Secure Access is Ready" email whenever a director is granted permission.
 In-App Alerts: Show a "Setup Needed" banner on the homepage for authorized users who haven't completed their setup.
🛠️ Technical Requirements
Browser API: Use URL.createObjectURL to trigger the download of the configuration file without storing temporary files on the server.
Client Detection: Use User-Agent parsing to show the correct mobile vs. desktop instructions automatically.
Integration: Link the completion of the wizard to the LastUsedAt field in the VpnProfiles table.
✅ Success Criteria
The 2-Minute Goal: A non-technical board member can go from "Blocked" to "Watching Cameras" in under 120 seconds.
Zero Manual Entry: The user never has to type an IP address, domain, or key—everything is contained in the one-click profile download.
Smart Redirection: After a successful "Verify Connection" check, the user is automatically redirected back to the exact camera they were trying to watch.
Error Handling: If the connection test fails, the wizard provides a "Troubleshooting Guide" link instead of a generic error.
Notes for Developer
The instructions must be written for someone who has never heard the word 'VPN.' Use phrases like 'Secure Connection' and 'Security App' instead of technical jargon. Test the mobile 'Tap-to-Open' flow specifically, as this is how most directors will use the system.

closing_issues.title: PROJ: GFC Camera Security - Phase 4: Network Location Detection & Access Guard Logic
closing_issues.body:
Issue Description
Objective: Implement the intelligent "Location Detection" engine. This core security component automatically detects a user's IP address and determines if they are on the Club LAN, the Secure VPN, or the Public Internet. This logic serves as the primary gateway, blocking remote access unless the secure tunnel is active.

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/CAMERA_REMOTE_ACCESS_SECURITY_MASTER_PLAN.md
 (Section 4.1 - 4.3)
🚀 Tasks / Checklist
1. Network Location Service (NetworkLocationService)
 IP Analyzer: Create a service to extract and validate the client's IP address (handling Cloudflare's X-Forwarded-For headers).
 Subnet Logic: Implement CIDR range checking to categorize IPs into:
LAN: The physical club network (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24).
VPN: The secure WireGuard subnet (e.g., 10.8.0.0/24).
Public: Any unauthorized external connection.
2. Multi-Layer Authorization Middleware
 The "Guard" Filter: Implement a global navigation filter for all /video/* and /cameras/* routes.
 Conditional Blocking:
If LAN or VPN → Allow Access.
If Public → Block Access and redirect to the "Enable Secure Access" setup wizard.
 State Persistence: Cache the user's location status in their session to minimize database lookups.
3. Geofencing & Geo-IP Integration
 Location Enrichment: (Optional) Integration with a Geo-IP database to detect the country/state of Public connection attempts.
 Unusual Activity Detection: Flag and log "Out of State" login attempts as high-priority security alerts in the dashboard.
4. UI Feedback Systems
 Status Badge: Add a subtle indicator in the app header (e.g., "Connected via: Club WiFi" or "Connected via: Secure VPN").
 Auto-Refresh Logic: Detect if a user switches networks (e.g., moving from WiFi to Data) and instantly re-verify their access level.
🛠️ Technical Requirements
Networking: Use System.Net.IPAddress and IPNetwork2 library for efficient subnet calculations.
Middleware: Implement as a Blazor circuit handler or a custom AuthorizationHandler.
Cloudflare Support: Ensure the logic correctly identifies the original user IP, not the Cloudflare tunnel IP.
✅ Success Criteria
The Automatic Guard: A user at home who forgets to turn on their VPN is immediately blocked from viewing cameras and shown a helpful setup link.
Seamless Transition: A user who turns on their VPN can refresh the page and gain instant access without re-logging in.
LAN Priority: The system correctly recognizes a user at the club, allowing them to watch video without needing to activate the VPN.
Audit Accuracy: Every block event is logged in the VideoAccessAudit table with the specific "Public" IP address that attempted access.
Notes for Developer
The most critical part of this phase is the 'Cloudflare Header' logic. If the system incorrectly sees the Cloudflare IP instead of the User IP, everyone will be blocked. Thoroughly test the IP extraction logic in the production environment.

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/CAMERA_REMOTE_ACCESS_SECURITY_MASTER_PLAN.md
 (Section 2.1 - 2.6)

1. Remote Access Configuration (Infrastructure UI)
 Tunnel Controls: UI for entering/managing the Cloudflare Tunnel Token and Public Domain.
 VPN Networking: Controls for setting the WireGuard Listening Port (Default 51820) and the internal VPN Subnet.
 Health Status Dashboard: Real-time visual status for the Tunnel and VPN services.
2. User & Board Permission Management
 Director Expiry Engine: Implement a global "Director Access Expiry" setting with automatic revocation logic.
 Authorized User Management: Create the interface to add members who aren't directors (Maintenance/Security) with specific roles (View Only vs. Full Access).
 One-Click Revocation: Add the "Remove Access" buttons that instantly trigger the WireGuard peer remove command.
3. Security "Hardening" Toggles
Implement the toggles and backend logic for:

 Session Auto-Timeout: Force re-authentication for remote users after X minutes.
 Failed Login Protection: Automatic IP blocking after too many incorrect password attempts.

4. System Limits & "Mission Control"
 Throughput Management: Set maximum simultaneous remote viewers to prevent internet congestion.
 Quality Toggles: Define maximum bitrates for remote (VPN) vs. local (LAN) users.
 🚨 Emergency Kill Switch: Build the high-visibility "Emergency Lockdown" button that instantly disconnects all VPN users.
🛠️ Technical Requirements
UI Framework: Bootstrap 5 with Blazor components.
State Management: Use SettingsService to persist these high-security flags into the SystemSettings table.
Validation: Add strong validation for subnet ranges and port numbers to prevent accidental network lockout.
✅ Success Criteria
The Board Transition: Setting an expiry date for "Directors" automatically terminates their VPN access at the scheduled time.
Instant Lockdown: Pressing the Kill Switch triggers a background job that empties the WireGuard peer list in under 1 second.

closing_issues.title: PROJ: GFC Camera Security - Phase 1: Foundation & Infrastructure Setup
closing_issues.body:
Issue Description
Objective: Establish the core networking and security infrastructure required for the "Two-Computer" remote viewing architecture. This phase focuses on the Cloudflare Tunnel integration, WireGuard server management, and the persistent data schema for VPN profiles and audit logs.

Reference Documentation:


docs/in-process/CAMERA_REMOTE_ACCESS_SECURITY_MASTER_PLAN.md
 (Phase 1 section)

docs/in-process/PHASE_CAMERA_REMOTE_SECURITY/INDEX.md
🚀 Tasks / Checklist
1. Cloudflare Tunnel Integration
 Setup Guide: Create a detailed administrator guide with screenshots for setting up the initial Cloudflare tunnel.
 Config UI: Add a "Cloudflare Tunnel Configuration" section to the Web App Settings page.
 Health Check: Implement a background status service with a visual "Connected/Disconnected" indicator (Green/Red).
 Diagnostics: Add a "Test Connection" button that dry-runs the tunnel's responsiveness.
2. WireGuard Server Management (C# Wrapper)
 Server Setup: Prepare the Windows host server for WireGuard management via CLI.
 Management Wrapper: Create the WireGuardManagementService (C#) to wrap CLI commands for:
wg genkey / wg pubkey (Curve25519 keypair generation).
wg set peer (Adding/Removing authorized users).
wg-quick save (Config persistence).
 Template Engine: Implement the .conf configuration file generator for user profiles.
3. Database Schema Implementation
Deploy the following tables as defined in the Master Plan:

 VpnProfiles: Stores user keypairs (encrypted private keys), assigned static IPs, and revocation status.
 VpnSessions: Tracks active connection metrics (Bytes sent/received, timestamps).
 VideoAccessAudit: Logs every remote viewing event, download, and snapshot.
 SecurityAlerts: Stores automated alerts for failed logins or unusual access locations.
 SystemSettings Updates: Add columns for Tunnel Tokens, VPN Subnet ranges, and global security toggles.
4. Network Layer logic
 IP Detection: Create NetworkLocationService to distinguish between LAN (Local), VPN (WireGuard Subnet), and Public traffic.
 Access Guard: Implement the base logic to block video access if the user is detected as "Public."
🛠️ Technical Requirements
Framework: .NET 8 / Blazor Server.
Crypto: BouncyCastle or Sodium.Core for secure key derivation.
Commands: Must handle cmd / powershell execution with administrative privileges for WireGuard CLI.
Cloudflare: Use Cloudflared CLI for the tunnel daemon.

The Bridge: The Web App settings show a "Green" status when the Cloudflare tunnel is active.
Key Logic: The system can successfully generate a valid WireGuard public/private keypair and save it to the database.
Audit Trail: Manually inserting a test connection into the database triggers a "Security Alert" if set to do so.
Clean Schema: All four new database tables are created and correctly related to the Users table.
Notes for Developer
Security is paramount. Private keys must be encrypted before being stored in the VpnProfiles table using a machine-level key or AES-256. Do not implement the user-facing 'Download' UI yet—focus entirely on the 'Admin/Server' infrastructure first.

closing_issues.title: [bug]: JSONConfig sendTo jsonData attribute parser problem
closing_issues.body:
### No existing issues.

- [X] There is no existing issue for my problem.

### Describe the bug

If a data field includes a \ and is added to jsonData the string can not parsed correct. This leads to an error and throws a message in Browser.

closing_issues.title: perf: language-aware worker task distribution and --max-workers flag
closing_issues.body:
With round-robin task distribution, each parse worker loads every tree-sitter grammar it encounters. On an 8-worker, 5-language repo, that's up to 400 MB–2 GB of native grammar memory across workers.

### Problem

Round-robin distribution causes each worker to load all grammars. No CLI control over worker count.

### Solution

Sort files by language before distribution so each worker receives contiguous same-language blocks (1–2 grammars each). Add `--max-workers` CLI flag.

### Expected impact

50% less worker memory on multi-language repos. `--max-workers` gives users control on memory-constrained systems.

closing_issues.title: perf: cascade deletes and batch DELETE in source-index update path
closing_issues.body:
Per-file updates execute 3–7 individual DELETE/UPDATE statements each. At scale (hundreds of changed files), this multiplies into thousands of round-trips.

### Problem

No cascade deletes on FK constraints means manual cleanup statements per file. No batching of deletes across files.

### Solution

Add `ON DELETE SET NULL` / `ON DELETE CASCADE` to FK columns. Batch deletes using `WHERE id IN (...)` instead of per-file deletes.

### Expected impact

Reduce delete cascade from 3–7 statements per file to 1 batch statement total.

closing_issues.title: perf: pre-populate sourceCache with async I/O before LSP enrichment
closing_issues.body:
During LSP enrichment, cache misses cause synchronous `existsSync` + `readFileSync` calls per file inside the hot per-file loop.

### Problem

Synchronous file reads block the event loop during LSP enrichment when source cache misses occur.

### Solution

Pre-read uncached files in batches of 50 via `Promise.allSettled` + `fs.promises.readFile` before enrichment loops run.

### Expected impact

Avoid redundant synchronous readFileSync during enrichment. Free sourceCache memory after last consumer.

closing_issues.title: perf: parallel LSP enrichment across files
closing_issues.body:
LSP enrichment processes files sequentially — each file must complete before the next begins — leaving I/O wait time on the table even though per-file concurrency (30 hover+definition requests) is already saturated.

### Problem

No cross-file parallelism during LSP enrichment.

### Solution

Process 3 files concurrently per language server using batched `Promise.all`, and commit DB writes for the entire batch in one transaction.

### Expected impact

3–5× faster LSP enrichment stage by overlapping I/O across files.

closing_issues.title: perf: stream git blame/log output via spawn to eliminate large string buffering
closing_issues.body:
`git blame --line-porcelain` on large files can produce 10+ MB of output that is fully buffered into a string via `execFileSync` before any parsing begins. Same issue for `git log -L` in history mode.

### Problem

Peak memory spikes due to large string allocations. Parsing cannot begin until the entire subprocess completes.

### Solution

Replace `execFileSync` with `spawn` and process stdout as a stream of chunks, parsing blame porcelain output incrementally as it arrives.

### Expected impact

Reduce peak memory for blame operations on large files. Eliminate 10+ MB temporary string allocations.

mentioned_issues.title: Add tests for deletion refresh, call-edge resolution, and FTS cleanup
mentioned_issues.body:
## Problem

Several code paths lack test coverage for important behavioral contracts, making regressions easy to miss.

## Missing Tests

1. **Deleted-file refresh**: No test verifies that `update()` correctly removes DB rows (files, symbols, imports, FTS5 entries) when a previously-indexed file is deleted. Related to issues #21 (FTS5 orphans) and #22 (manual refresh deletion).

2. **Call-edge resolution**: No test verifies that `callee_id` is populated after indexing. Related to issue #18 (buildCallGraph never invoked).

3. **FTS5 cleanup on deletion**: No test verifies that `symbols_fts` entries are removed when a file is deleted via `update()`.

4. **History ingestion during incremental update**: No test verifies that commits are ingested when `update()` is called with `history: true`.

5. **Poller/watcher single-flight**: No test verifies that concurrent poll/flush cycles don't overlap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Test: indexing a file then deleting it and calling `update()` results in zero rows for that file in `files`, `symbols`, `file_imports`, `symbol_refs`, and `symbols_fts`.
- [ ] Test: after `build()`, `symbol_refs.callee_id` is non-null for refs that match a known symbol name.
- [ ] Test: after `update()` with history enabled, `commits` table has rows.
- [ ] Test: overlapping poll triggers result in serial execution.

closing_issues.title: perf: batch SCIP document transactions in 200-doc chunks
closing_issues.body:
A single `db.transaction()` wrapping thousands of SCIP documents creates a massive WAL file and serializes all INSERTs into one giant commit.

### Problem

Monolithic transaction for all SCIP documents causes excessive WAL growth and memory pressure.

### Solution

Batch into 200-document transactions for both Pass 1 (files & symbols) and Pass 2 (call/type refs).

### Expected impact

10–50× faster SCIP insertion by amortizing fsync overhead across batches instead of per-statement.

closing_issues.title: perf: optimize multi-hop dependent expansion using CTE
closing_issues.body:
Multi-hop dependent expansion (`expandCallers`, `expandImporters`, `expandSubclasses`) uses sequential per-hop queries.

### Problem

For depth=5, 5 separate database queries are executed. Each hop waits for the DB response before starting the next.

### Solution

Replace per-hop loops with single `WITH RECURSIVE` CTE queries.

### Expected impact

5 queries → 1 query. Eliminate per-hop latency accumulation.

closing_issues.title: perf: move file reads off the main thread; make processFile async
closing_issues.body:
The serial `processFile` path blocks the main thread with `fs.statSync`/`fs.readFileSync`. Workers already read source text for parsing but always clone the full string back to the main thread regardless of file size.

### Problem

Main-thread synchronous I/O blocks during file processing. Large file source strings are unnecessarily cloned via structured clone from workers.

### Solution

Make `processFile` async with `fs.promises` equivalents. Add 1 MB threshold for worker source text transfer — omit source for large files.

### Expected impact

Eliminate main-thread file I/O blocking during indexed file processing.

closing_issues.title: perf: streaming embedding text generation to reduce peak memory
closing_issues.body:
For large codebases (~50K symbols), the embedding stage builds a full `items` array of text strings for all symbols before batching, holding ~500 MB of text in memory simultaneously.

### Problem

Two-phase accumulate-then-batch approach holds all embedding text in memory at once.

### Solution

Replace with inline streaming pattern: build text per-symbol and flush into batches as they fill, retaining double-buffered I/O.

### Expected impact

Reduce peak memory by 500+ MB by never holding more than one batch of embedding text simultaneously.

mentioned_issues.title: Prevent event loop starvation in `RenderManager` when lagging
mentioned_issues.body:
**Title:** Prevent event loop starvation in `RenderManager` when lagging

**Description:**
When the render loop exceeds the frame budget (16.6ms), it executes `await asyncio.sleep(0)`. In severe lag scenarios, this creates a tight loop that may starve networking or watchdog tasks.

**File:** `src/managers/render_manager.py`

**Task:**
- Enforce a minimum sleep duration (e.g., `0.001` or `0.005`) even when lagging to ensure the event loop allows I/O tasks to run.
- Optionally log a warning if frame drops exceed a certain threshold.

**Proposed Change:**
```python
            if sleep_duration > 0:
                await asyncio.sleep(sleep_duration)
            else:
                # Force a minimum yield to prevent starvation
                next_frame_time = now  # Reset baseline
                await asyncio.sleep(0.001)
```

**Alternative:**
- Reduce target frame rate when lagging due to performance constraints?

mentioned_issues.title: Trench Run game mode
mentioned_issues.body:
This is an excellent idea. Implementing a 'perspective toggle' in a scrolling matrix game is actually a fantastic exercise in coordinate math. Because incremental rotary encoders determine relative rotational position continuously without fixed endpoints, they pair perfectly with an endlessly wrapping 8x8 matrix.
The secret to pulling off the First Person vs. Third Person toggle is realizing that the collision logic never actually changes. You always track the player's absolute position relative to the gap's absolute position. The only thing the perspective toggle changes is how you draw it on the matrix.
The Rendering Math
 * Third Person: We draw the ship at player_pos. We draw the gap at gap_pos.
 * First Person: We freeze the ship rendering at the center of the screen (e.g., matrix index 3). We then render the gap relative to the ship using the wrapped offset: (gap_pos - player_pos + 3) % 8.
Here is the complete implementation for trench_run.py:

``` Python
"""Trench Run Game Mode - Endless Sci-Fi runner for 8x8 LED Matrix."""

import asyncio
import random
from adafruit_ticks import ticks_ms, ticks_diff

from utilities.palette import Palette
from utilities import tones
from .game_mode import GameMode

class TrenchRunMode(GameMode):
    """
    Trench Run Game Mode.
    
    Features:
    - Endless vertical scrolling dodging game
    - Perspective toggle: 3rd Person (ship moves) vs 1st Person (world moves)
    - Rotary encoder controls absolute horizontal position
    - Progressive speed and difficulty
    - Synthio procedural audio
    """
    
    METADATA = {
        "id": "TRENCH_RUN",
        "name": "TRENCH RUN",
        "icon": "GAME",
        "requires": ["CORE"],
        "settings": [
            {
                "key": "difficulty",
                "label": "DIFF",
                "options": ["NORMAL", "HARD", "INSANE"],
                "default": "NORMAL"
            },
            {
                "key": "perspective",
                "label": "VIEW",
                "options": ["3RD_PERSON", "1ST_PERSON"],
                "default": "3RD_PERSON"
            }
        ]
    }

    def __init__(self, core):
        super().__init__(core, "TRENCH RUN", "Endless Space Dodger")
        
        self.player_pos = 3
        
        # Walls are stored as dicts: {'y': float, 'gap_x': int}
        self.walls = []
        
        self.base_speed = 0.04
        self.current_speed = self.base_speed
        self.gap_width = 3
        self.wall_spacing = 4.0  # Vertical space between spawned walls
        
    async def run(self):
        """Main game loop."""
        self.difficulty = self.core.data.get_setting("TRENCH_RUN", "difficulty", "NORMAL")
        self.perspective = self.core.data.get_setting("TRENCH_RUN", "perspective", "3RD_PERSON")
        
        # Unique high scores for combinations of difficulty and perspective!
        self.variant = f"{self.perspective}_{self.difficulty}"
        
        if self.difficulty == "HARD":
            self.base_speed = 0.06
            self.gap_width = 2
        elif self.difficulty == "INSANE":
            self.base_speed = 0.08
            self.gap_width = 1
            
        self.current_speed = self.base_speed
            
        self.core.display.use_standard_layout()
        await self.core.display.update_status("TRENCH RUN", f"VIEW: {self.perspective}")
        asyncio.create_task(self.core.synth.play_sequence(tones.POWER_UP, patch="SCANNER"))
        await asyncio.sleep(2.0)
        
        self.core.hid.reset_encoder(0)
        self.score = 0
        self.level = 1
        self.walls.clear()
        
        # Spawn the first wall off-screen
        self.spawn_wall(y_start=-1.0)
        
        last_tick = ticks_ms()
        game_running = True
        
        while game_running:
            now = ticks_ms()
            delta_ms = ticks_diff(now, last_tick)
            
            if delta_ms >= 16:  # ~60 FPS Target
                self.update_player()
                crashed = self.update_walls()
                
                if crashed:
                    # Explode and end game
                    self.core.matrix.fill(Palette.WHITE)
                    asyncio.create_task(self.core.synth.play_sequence(tones.GAME_OVER))
                    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
                    return await self.game_over()
                
                await self.core.display.update_status(f"SCORE: {self.score}", f"SPEED: {self.level}")
                self.render()
                
                # Engine drone that pitches up slightly as you speed up
                drone_freq = 80.0 + (self.level * 2.0)
                self.core.synth.play_note(drone_freq, "ENGINE_HUM", duration=0.05)
                
                last_tick = now
            
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)

    def spawn_wall(self, y_start=-1.0):
        """Creates a new wall segment with a gap."""
        if not self.walls:
            gap = random.randint(0, 7)
        else:
            # Prevent impossible jumps by keeping the next gap close to the last one
            last_gap = self.walls[-1]['gap_x']
            shift = random.choice([-2, -1, 0, 1, 2])
            gap = (last_gap + shift) % 8
            
        self.walls.append({'y': y_start, 'gap_x': gap})

    def update_player(self):
        """Update absolute ship position from encoder."""
        encoder_pos = self.core.hid.encoder_positions[0]
        # Keep player in infinite 0-7 wrapped space
        self.player_pos = encoder_pos % 8

    def update_walls(self):
        """Moves walls down and handles collisions. Returns True if crashed."""
        crashed = False
        walls_to_remove = []
        
        for wall in self.walls:
            old_y_int = int(wall['y'])
            wall['y'] += self.current_speed
            new_y_int = int(wall['y'])
            
            # If the wall just hit the bottom row (y=7), check collision
            if old_y_int < 7 and new_y_int >= 7:
                # Calculate the safe indices for this wall
                safe_indices = [(wall['gap_x'] + i) % 8 for i in range(self.gap_width)]
                
                if self.player_pos in safe_indices:
                    # Success!
                    self.score += 10
                    self.core.synth.play_note(880.0, "UI_SELECT", duration=0.05)
                    
                    # Speed up every 100 points
                    if self.score % 100 == 0:
                        self.level += 1
                        self.current_speed = min(self.base_speed + (self.level * 0.01), 0.25)
                else:
                    # Crash!
                    crashed = True
            
            # If wall goes completely off screen, mark for removal
            if wall['y'] > 8.0:
                walls_to_remove.append(wall)
                
        # Remove old walls
        for w in walls_to_remove:
            self.walls.remove(w)
            
        # Check if we need to spawn a new wall
        if self.walls:
            highest_wall_y = self.walls[-1]['y']
            if highest_wall_y > self.wall_spacing:
                self.spawn_wall()
                
        return crashed

    def render(self):
        """Draw the game state based on the selected perspective."""
        self.core.matrix.clear()
        
        for wall in self.walls:
            y_int = int(wall['y'])
            if 0 <= y_int < 8:
                
                if self.perspective == "3RD_PERSON":
                    render_gap = wall['gap_x']
                else: # 1ST_PERSON
                    # Shift the gap rendering so the player is effectively locked at index 3
                    render_gap = (wall['gap_x'] - self.player_pos + 3) % 8
                
                # Calculate the exact indices to leave blank
                gap_indices = [(render_gap + i) % 8 for i in range(self.gap_width)]
                
                # Draw the wall blocks (color shifts slightly as speed increases)
                wall_color = Palette.RED if self.level < 5 else Palette.PURPLE
                for x in range(8):
                    if x not in gap_indices:
                        self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(x, y_int, wall_color)
        
        # Draw the Ship
        if self.perspective == "3RD_PERSON":
            # Ship moves across the bottom row
            self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(self.player_pos, 7, Palette.CYAN)
        else:
            # Ship is anchored in the center (index 3)
            self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(3, 7, Palette.CYAN)
```

mentioned_issues.title: Create a Brick Breaker style game mode
mentioned_issues.body:
Notes from Gemini

This is a fantastic direction. To implement these features, we need to upgrade the brick storage from a simple set to a dictionary so we can track properties like type and hp (hit points).
We also get to fully leverage the SynthManager (self.core.synth) you built. Because play_sequence is an asynchronous coroutine that uses asyncio.sleep to time notes, we will use asyncio.create_task() to fire off multi-note jingles in the background without freezing the 60 FPS game loop. For simple single-note bounces, play_note is perfect as it is non-blocking and uses an auto-release task.
Here is the updated src/modes/astro_breaker.py:

```
"""Astro Breaker Game Mode - Sci-Fi Brick Breaker for 8x8 LED Matrix."""

import asyncio
import math
import random
from adafruit_ticks import ticks_ms, ticks_diff

from utilities.palette import Palette
from utilities import tones
from .game_mode import GameMode

class AstroBreakerMode(GameMode):
    """
    Astro Breaker Game Mode.
    
    Features:
    - 8x8 LED matrix playing field
    - 2-pixel wide ship shield (paddle) controlled by core rotary encoder
    - Plasma bolt (ball) with physics and angle deflection
    - Multiple Brick Types (Normal, Multi-hit, Indestructible Cores)
    - Synthio procedural audio for physical interactions
    - Fully integrated with the CoreManager High Score system
    """
    
    METADATA = {
        "id": "ASTRO_BREAKER",
        "name": "ASTRO BREAKER",
        "icon": "GAME",
        "requires": ["CORE"],
        "settings": [
            {
                "key": "difficulty",
                "label": "DIFF",
                "options": ["NORMAL", "HARD", "INSANE"],
                "default": "NORMAL"
            }
        ]
    }

    def __init__(self, core):
        super().__init__(core, "ASTRO BREAKER", "Sci-Fi Brick Breaker")
        
        self.paddle_x = 3
        self.paddle_width = 2
        
        self.ball_x = 4.0
        self.ball_y = 6.0
        self.ball_dx = 0.0
        self.ball_dy = 0.0
        
        self.base_speed = 0.10
        self.current_speed = self.base_speed
        
        self.lives = 3
        self.level = 1
        
        # Dictionary to store brick states: {(x, y): {'type': str, 'hp': int}}
        self.bricks = {}
        
    async def run(self):
        """Main game loop."""
        self.difficulty = self.core.data.get_setting("ASTRO_BREAKER", "difficulty", "NORMAL")
        self.variant = f"SOLO_{self.difficulty}"
        
        if self.difficulty == "HARD":
            self.base_speed = 0.14
        elif self.difficulty == "INSANE":
            self.base_speed = 0.18
        
        self.core.display.use_standard_layout()
        
        await self.core.display.update_status("ASTRO BREAKER", f"DIFF: {self.difficulty}")
        asyncio.create_task(self.core.synth.play_sequence(tones.POWER_UP, patch="SCANNER"))
        await asyncio.sleep(2.0)
        
        self.core.hid.reset_encoder(0)
        self.score = 0
        self.lives = 3
        self.level = 1
        
        self.generate_bricks()
        self.reset_ball()
        
        last_tick = ticks_ms()
        game_running = True
        
        while game_running:
            now = ticks_ms()
            delta_ms = ticks_diff(now, last_tick)
            
            if delta_ms >= 16:  # ~60 FPS Target
                self.update_paddle()
                life_lost = self.update_ball()
                
                if life_lost:
                    self.lives -= 1
                    if self.lives <= 0:
                        asyncio.create_task(self.core.synth.play_sequence(tones.GAME_OVER))
                        return await self.game_over()
                    else:
                        await self.core.display.update_status("HULL BREACH!", f"SHIELDS: {self.lives}")
                        asyncio.create_task(self.core.synth.play_sequence(tones.ERROR))
                        await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
                        self.reset_ball()
                
                # Check for sector clear
                if not self.bricks:
                    self.level += 1
                    self.current_speed = min(self.base_speed + (self.level * 0.02), 0.3)
                    await self.core.display.update_status("SECTOR CLEARED", f"WARPING TO SEC {self.level}")
                    asyncio.create_task(self.core.synth.play_sequence(tones.SECRET_FOUND))
                    await asyncio.sleep(2.0)
                    self.generate_bricks()
                    self.reset_ball()
                
                await self.core.display.update_status(f"SCORE: {self.score}", f"LIVES: {self.lives}  SEC: {self.level}")
                self.render()
                
                last_tick = now
            
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)

    def generate_bricks(self):
        """Spawns different brick types based on row placement."""
        self.bricks.clear()
        
        for x in range(8):
            # Row 0 (Top): 2 Core targets flanked by Tough bricks
            if x in [3, 4]:
                self.bricks[(x, 0)] = {'type': 'CORE', 'hp': 1}
            else:
                self.bricks[(x, 0)] = {'type': 'TOUGH', 'hp': 3}
                
            # Row 1: Medium bricks
            self.bricks[(x, 1)] = {'type': 'TOUGH', 'hp': 2}
            
            # Row 2: Standard debris
            self.bricks[(x, 2)] = {'type': 'NORMAL', 'hp': 1}

    def reset_ball(self):
        """Reset plasma bolt to paddle position."""
        self.ball_x = self.paddle_x + 0.5
        self.ball_y = 6.0
        
        angle = random.choice([210, 225, 240, 300, 315, 330])
        self.ball_dx = self.current_speed * math.cos(math.radians(angle))
        self.ball_dy = self.current_speed * math.sin(math.radians(angle))
        
    def update_paddle(self):
        """Update shield position from encoder."""
        encoder_pos = self.core.hid.encoder_positions[0]
        self.paddle_x = encoder_pos % 7 

    def update_ball(self):
        """Update physics and handle collisions. Returns True if ball falls off bottom."""
        self.ball_x += self.ball_dx
        self.ball_y += self.ball_dy
        
        # Wall collisions
        if self.ball_x <= 0:
            self.ball_x = 0
            self.ball_dx = abs(self.ball_dx)
            self.core.synth.play_note(300.0, "UI_SELECT", duration=0.02)
        elif self.ball_x >= 7:
            self.ball_x = 7
            self.ball_dx = -abs(self.ball_dx)
            self.core.synth.play_note(300.0, "UI_SELECT", duration=0.02)
            
        if self.ball_y <= 0:
            self.ball_y = 0
            self.ball_dy = abs(self.ball_dy)
            self.core.synth.play_note(300.0, "UI_SELECT", duration=0.02)
            
        # Paddle collision
        if self.ball_y >= 6.5 and self.ball_dy > 0:
            ball_x_int = int(self.ball_x)
            if self.paddle_x <= ball_x_int <= self.paddle_x + 1:
                self.ball_y = 6.5
                self.ball_dy = -abs(self.ball_dy)
                
                offset = self.ball_x - (self.paddle_x + 0.5)
                self.ball_dx += offset * 0.1
                
                speed = math.sqrt(self.ball_dx**2 + self.ball_dy**2)
                self.ball_dx = (self.ball_dx / speed) * self.current_speed
                self.ball_dy = (self.ball_dy / speed) * self.current_speed
                
                # Laser deflection sound
                self.core.synth.play_note(600.0, "UI_SELECT", duration=0.05)
        
        # Brick collisions
        ball_pos = (int(self.ball_x + 0.5), int(self.ball_y + 0.5))
        if ball_pos in self.bricks:
            brick = self.bricks[ball_pos]
            # Reverse Y velocity to bounce back
            self.ball_dy = -self.ball_dy
            
            if brick['type'] == 'CORE':
                # Check if this is the last brick standing (or if only cores are left)
                cores_protected = any(b['type'] != 'CORE' for b in self.bricks.values())
                
                if cores_protected:
                    # Indestructible thud
                    self.core.synth.play_note(150.0, "UI_ERROR", duration=0.1)
                else:
                    # Core destroyed!
                    del self.bricks[ball_pos]
                    self.score += 50
                    self.core.synth.play_note(1200.0, "ALARM", duration=0.1)
                    
            else: # NORMAL or TOUGH
                brick['hp'] -= 1
                if brick['hp'] <= 0:
                    del self.bricks[ball_pos]
                    self.score += 10
                    # Glass shatter / destroy sound
                    self.core.synth.play_note(880.0, "UI_SELECT", duration=0.05)
                else:
                    self.score += 2
                    # Chipping sound
                    self.core.synth.play_note(440.0, "UI_SELECT", duration=0.05)
            
        # Check for hull breach (lost life)
        if self.ball_y > 8:
            return True
            
        return False

    def render(self):
        """Draw the game state."""
        self.core.matrix.clear()
        
        # Check if cores are currently vulnerable to update their color state
        cores_protected = any(b['type'] != 'CORE' for b in self.bricks.values())
        
        # Draw Bricks
        for (bx, by), brick in self.bricks.items():
            if brick['type'] == 'CORE':
                color = Palette.RED if cores_protected else Palette.AMBER
            elif brick['type'] == 'TOUGH':
                # Fade color based on HP remaining
                if brick['hp'] >= 3:
                    color = Palette.PURPLE
                elif brick['hp'] == 2:
                    color = Palette.MAGENTA
                else:
                    color = Palette.PINK
            else:
                color = Palette.CYAN
                
            self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(bx, by, color)
            
        # Draw Paddle (Shield)
        for i in range(self.paddle_width):
            x = self.paddle_x + i
            if 0 <= x < 8:
                self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(x, 7, Palette.GREEN)
                
        # Draw Ball (Plasma Bolt)
        bx, by = int(self.ball_x + 0.5), int(self.ball_y + 0.5)
        if 0 <= bx < 8 and 0 <= by < 8:
            self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(bx, by, Palette.YELLOW)
```

Key Additions Explained:
 * The Dictionary Upgrade: self.bricks is now a dictionary mapped to the (x,y) coordinate tuple. This allows us to rapidly query any brick's state and type when the ball collides.
 * Audio Design: - I used play_note for rapid, physical actions (bounces, chipping bricks). Notice how I vary the frequency. A wall bounce is a low 300.0 Hz, while chipping a brick is 440.0 Hz, and breaking it is 880.0 Hz. This gives the player instant acoustic feedback on the game state!
   * I used tones sequences via asyncio.create_task() for game flow changes (Sector Clear, Life Lost, Bootup) without locking the ball physics.
 * Core Mechanic Check: When the ball hits a CORE brick, it instantly checks any(b['type'] != 'CORE' for b in self.bricks.values()). If True, the core emits a dull thud (UI_ERROR) and doesn't take damage. If False (all other bricks are dead), the core is vulnerable!
 * Dynamic Colors: In the render() function, the colors shift logically:
   * Tough bricks fade from PURPLE ➔ MAGENTA ➔ PINK as their HP drops.
   * Core bricks sit menacingly in RED until they are vulnerable, at which point they glow AMBER.

mentioned_issues.title: Laser path ("pipe puzzle")
mentioned_issues.body:
This is an excellent concept for the 8x8 matrix!
When translating a "Pipe Puzzle" to a low-resolution 8x8 grid, trying to visually represent curved pipes (like a T-junction or a corner) on a single pixel is nearly impossible to read.
Instead, the cleanest and most visually striking way to build this is as an Optical Data Router (a laser-deflection puzzle).
 * The Source fires a beam of data.
 * The Nodes are single-pixel "Mirrors" or "Deflectors".
 * You use the rotary encoder to move a cursor across the board, and the button to rotate the deflectors 90 degrees to bounce the data stream into the Target.
Here is the complete framework-compliant code for Data Flow. It features a procedural level generator so it is infinitely replayable, instant data-trace physics, and deep synthio integration.
The Code (src/modes/data_flow.py)
"""Data Flow Game Mode - Procedural Laser Deflection Puzzle."""

``` Python
import asyncio
import random
from adafruit_ticks import ticks_ms, ticks_diff

from utilities.palette import Palette
from utilities import tones
from .game_mode import GameMode

class DataFlowMode(GameMode):
    """
    Data Flow Game Mode.
    
    Features:
    - Procedurally generated laser-routing puzzles
    - Rotary encoder seamlessly maps 1D rotation to a 2D cursor (0-63)
    - Instant ray-casting physics to trace the data stream
    - Synthio audio for tactile cursor movement and routing
    """
    
    METADATA = {
        "id": "DATA_FLOW",
        "name": "DATA FLOW",
        "icon": "GAME", # Or "DIAL" / "FACTORY" depending on your icon lib
        "requires": ["CORE"],
        "settings": [
            {
                "key": "difficulty",
                "label": "DIFF",
                "options": ["NORMAL", "HARD"],
                "default": "NORMAL"
            }
        ]
    }

    def __init__(self, core):
        super().__init__(core, "DATA FLOW", "Optical Routing Puzzle")
        
        self.cursor_pos = 0  # 0 to 63 (maps to 8x8 grid)
        self.last_encoder_pos = 0
        self.last_btn_state = False
        
        self.source = (0, 0)
        self.target = (7, 7)
        self.mirrors = {} # dict of (x,y) -> {'type': int} (0 = '/', 1 = '\')
        self.beam_path = []
        
        self.level = 1
        self.score = 0
        
        # Colors
        self.COLOR_SOURCE = Palette.GREEN
        self.COLOR_TARGET = Palette.GOLD
        self.COLOR_MIRROR_0 = Palette.CYAN     # '/' mirror
        self.COLOR_MIRROR_1 = Palette.MAGENTA  # '\' mirror
        self.COLOR_BEAM = (80, 80, 0)          # Dim yellow data stream
        
    async def run(self):
        """Main game loop."""
        self.difficulty = self.core.data.get_setting("DATA_FLOW", "difficulty", "NORMAL")
        self.variant = f"PUZZLE_{self.difficulty}"
        
        self.core.display.use_standard_layout()
        await self.core.display.update_status("DATA FLOW", "INITIALIZING...")
        asyncio.create_task(self.core.synth.play_sequence(tones.SYSTEM_BOOT))
        await asyncio.sleep(1.5)
        
        self.core.hid.reset_encoder(0)
        self.last_encoder_pos = self.core.hid.encoder_positions[0]
        self.level = 1
        self.score = 0
        
        self.generate_level()
        self.calculate_beam()
        
        last_tick = ticks_ms()
        game_running = True
        
        while game_running:
            now = ticks_ms()
            delta_ms = ticks_diff(now, last_tick)
            
            if delta_ms >= 16:  # ~60 FPS
                self.update_cursor()
                self.handle_input()
                
                # Check Win Condition
                if self.target in self.beam_path:
                    await self.handle_victory(now)
                    # If game over was returned from victory (e.g., max levels), exit
                    if not game_running:
                        break
                
                # Render
                await self.core.display.update_status(f"ROUTER SEC: {self.level}", f"NODES: {len(self.mirrors)}")
                self.render(now)
                
                # Background ambient hum
                if random.random() < 0.05:
                    self.core.synth.play_note(60.0, "ENGINE_HUM", duration=0.1)
                
                last_tick = now
            
            await asyncio.sleep(0.01)

    # --- GAME LOGIC ---

    def update_cursor(self):
        """Map 1D encoder rotation to 2D grid position."""
        current_encoder = self.core.hid.encoder_positions[0]
        
        if current_encoder != self.last_encoder_pos:
            # Calculate delta to handle infinite scrolling smoothly
            delta = current_encoder - self.last_encoder_pos
            self.cursor_pos = (self.cursor_pos + delta) % 64
            self.last_encoder_pos = current_encoder
            
            # Ultra-short tactile click for cursor movement
            self.core.synth.play_note(1000.0, "UI_SELECT", duration=0.01)

    def handle_input(self):
        """Check for button press to rotate mirrors."""
        # Standard edge-trigger debounce
        btn_pressed = False
        if hasattr(self.core.hid, 'button_pressed'):
            current_btn = self.core.hid.button_pressed(0)
            if current_btn and not self.last_btn_state:
                btn_pressed = True
            self.last_btn_state = current_btn

        if btn_pressed:
            cx = self.cursor_pos % 8
            cy = self.cursor_pos // 8
            
            # If the cursor is over a mirror, flip it!
            if (cx, cy) in self.mirrors:
                self.mirrors[(cx, cy)]['type'] = 1 - self.mirrors[(cx, cy)]['type']
                self.core.synth.play_note(600.0, "UI_SELECT", duration=0.05) # Mechanical clack
                self.calculate_beam() # Instantly recalculate the laser path
            else:
                # Error beep for empty space
                self.core.synth.play_note(200.0, "UI_ERROR", duration=0.05)

    def calculate_beam(self):
        """Ray-casts the data stream from source through the mirrors."""
        self.beam_path.clear()
        
        x, y = self.source
        dx, dy = 1, 0  # Source always faces right
        
        # Trace up to 64 steps to prevent infinite loops if mirrors form a closed circle
        for _ in range(64):
            x += dx
            y += dy
            
            # Out of bounds
            if not (0 <= x < 8 and 0 <= y < 8):
                break
                
            self.beam_path.append((x, y))
            
            if (x, y) == self.target:
                break # Reached the end!
                
            # Hit a mirror, calculate deflection
            if (x, y) in self.mirrors:
                m_type = self.mirrors[(x, y)]['type']
                if m_type == 0:
                    # '/' Mirror: (dx, dy) becomes (-dy, -dx)
                    dx, dy = -dy, -dx
                else:
                    # '\' Mirror: (dx, dy) becomes (dy, dx)
                    dx, dy = dy, dx

    # --- LEVEL GENERATOR ---

    def generate_level(self):
        """Procedurally generate a solvable puzzle by walking backward from source."""
        base_mirrors = 3
        if self.difficulty == "HARD":
            base_mirrors = 5
            
        num_mirrors = min(base_mirrors + (self.level // 2), 12)
        
        # Try to generate a valid level up to 100 times
        for attempt in range(100):
            self.mirrors.clear()
            
            # 1. Place Source on the left wall
            x, y = 0, random.randint(1, 6)
            self.source = (x, y)
            dx, dy = 1, 0
            
            valid_path = True
            
            # 2. Walk the path and place mirrors
            for _ in range(num_mirrors):
                # Move forward 1 to 3 steps
                steps = random.randint(1, 3)
                for _ in range(steps):
                    x += dx
                    y += dy
                    if not (0 <= x < 8 and 0 <= y < 8):
                        valid_path = False
                        break
                
                if not valid_path: break
                
                # Prevent placing a mirror on the source or an existing mirror
                if (x, y) == self.source or (x, y) in self.mirrors:
                    valid_path = False
                    break
                    
                # Decide turn and mirror type
                m_type = random.choice([0, 1])
                if m_type == 0: # '/'
                    dx, dy = -dy, -dx
                else: # '\'
                    dx, dy = dy, dx
                    
                self.mirrors[(x, y)] = {'type': m_type}
                
            if valid_path:
                # 3. Final steps to place target
                steps = random.randint(1, 3)
                for _ in range(steps):
                    x += dx
                    y += dy
                    if not (0 <= x < 8 and 0 <= y < 8):
                        valid_path = False
                        break
                        
                if valid_path and (x, y) not in self.mirrors and (x, y) != self.source:
                    self.target = (x, y)
                    
                    # 4. Scramble the mirrors so the player has to solve it!
                    for pos in self.mirrors:
                        self.mirrors[pos]['type'] = random.choice([0, 1])
                    return # Success!
                    
        # Fallback if generation fails (very rare on 8x8)
        self.generate_fallback_level()

    def generate_fallback_level(self):
        """A simple hardcoded level in case procedural generation fails."""
        self.mirrors.clear()
        self.source = (0, 3)
        self.target = (7, 5)
        self.mirrors[(3, 3)] = {'type': 0}
        self.mirrors[(3, 5)] = {'type': 1}

    # --- RENDERING & SEQUENCES ---

    async def handle_victory(self, now):
        """Plays victory animation and advances level."""
        # Draw the final winning frame
        self.render(now)
        self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(self.target[0], self.target[1], Palette.WHITE)
        
        # Data success sound
        asyncio.create_task(self.core.synth.play_sequence(tones.NOTIFY_INBOX, patch="SUCCESS"))
        
        # Flash the successful path white
        for pos in self.beam_path:
            self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(pos[0], pos[1], Palette.WHITE)
            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
            
        await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
        
        self.score += (100 * self.level)
        self.level += 1
        
        self.generate_level()
        self.calculate_beam()
        self.cursor_pos = 0

    def render(self, now):
        self.core.matrix.clear()
        
        # 1. Draw Data Stream (Beam)
        for pos in self.beam_path:
            self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(pos[0], pos[1], self.COLOR_BEAM)
            
        # 2. Draw Mirrors
        for (mx, my), mirror in self.mirrors.items():
            color = self.COLOR_MIRROR_0 if mirror['type'] == 0 else self.COLOR_MIRROR_1
            self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(mx, my, color)
            
        # 3. Draw Source and Target (Pulsing)
        pulse = (now % 1000) > 500
        source_color = Palette.WHITE if pulse else self.COLOR_SOURCE
        target_color = Palette.WHITE if not pulse else self.COLOR_TARGET
        
        self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(self.source[0], self.source[1], source_color)
        self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(self.target[0], self.target[1], target_color)
        
        # 4. Draw Cursor (Rapid Blink)
        if (now % 400) > 200:
            cx = self.cursor_pos % 8
            cy = self.cursor_pos // 8
            # Invert the pixel under the cursor so it's always visible
            self.core.matrix.draw_pixel(cx, cy, Palette.WHITE)
```

The Design Decisions
 * The 1D to 2D Encoder Translation: Because the rotary encoder only outputs a single integer (e.g., 12, 13, 14...), trying to move a 2D cursor (X and Y) can be tricky. I solved this by treating the 8x8 matrix as an array of 64 pixels.
   cx = self.cursor_pos % 8
   cy = self.cursor_pos // 8
   Turning the dial to the right sweeps the cursor across the row from left to right, and wraps seamlessly down to the next row. It feels incredibly intuitive for a dial.
 * Procedural Level Generation: Instead of hardcoding puzzles, generate_level() does a random walk forward from the source, randomly placing mirrors and turning, until it drops the target. Once the valid path is proven, it scrambles all the mirror rotations. This guarantees every puzzle is 100% solvable while offering endless replayability.
 * Instant "Ray Casting": Instead of moving a slow dot across the screen, calculate_beam() instantly traces the path of the data through the mirrors every time you press the button. This allows the player to rapidly experiment and see the immediate consequences of flipping a node.
How does the laser-deflection mechanic sound compared to the original pipe-rotation concept?

mentioned_issues.title: Create custom Copilot agent in .github for unit test repair and coverage expansion
mentioned_issues.body:
Create a custom Copilot agent within the `.github` directory to focus on:

- **Automated repair of failing or flaky unit tests** (identify breakages, suggest/test fixes, and propose pull requests or summaries).
- **Automated expansion of test coverage** (identifying untested areas or files, proposing/scaffolding new tests, or suggesting missing assertions).
- Optional support for reporting or summarizing test coverage after CI builds.
- Ensure the agent is tailored for this repository's technology stack and preferred testing practices.
- Provide setup instructions and usage documentation for maintainers/contributors.

## Critical Requirements

**⚠️ This agent MUST NOT modify source code outside of test files.**

- The agent may only create or modify files in the `tests/` directory.
- If the agent identifies an actual bug in source code (e.g., in `src/`) that is causing test failures, it **MUST open an issue** rather than attempting to fix the bug directly.
- The agent should clearly document in issue descriptions:
  - Which test(s) are failing
  - What the root cause appears to be in the source code
  - Suggested fix or investigation steps
  - Reference to failing test file and line numbers

## Scope

- **Test repair**: Fix broken test logic, update mocks, adjust assertions to match corrected behavior
- **Coverage expansion**: Identify untested code paths, create new test files, add missing test cases
- **Test infrastructure**: Update test utilities, fixtures, or helpers as needed
- **Bug reporting**: Open issues when source code bugs are discovered during test analysis

## Relevant Code References

### Existing Test Infrastructure

- **Test directory**: [`tests/`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/tree/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/tests) - Contains 28+ unit tests covering utilities, managers, transport, protocol, and modes
- **Test coverage report**: [`TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/TEST_COVERAGE_REPORT.md) - Documents current test coverage and gaps
- **Example test patterns**:
  - [`tests/test_cobs.py`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/tests/test_cobs.py) - Standalone test with manual assertions
  - [`tests/test_message.py`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/tests/test_message.py) - Tests for transport layer
  - [`tests/test_audio_manager.py`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/tests/test_audio_manager.py) - Manager tests with extensive mocking
  - [`tests/test_mode_base.py`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/tests/test_mode_base.py) - Async test with pytest decorators

### CI/CD Configuration

- **Unit test workflow**: [`.github/workflows/unit-tests.yml`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/.github/workflows/unit-tests.yml) - Runs all unit tests on push/PR
- **Pytest workflow**: [`.github/workflows/pytest-tests.yml`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/.github/workflows/pytest-tests.yml) - Alternative pytest-based runner
- **Workflow documentation**: [`.github/workflows/README.md`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/.github/workflows/README.md) - Details test execution patterns

### Testing Patterns & Documentation

- **OTA Update testing**: [`docs/OTA_UPDATE.md#Testing`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/docs/OTA_UPDATE.md#L341-L381) - Documents test coverage for updater
- **Web configurator testing**: [`docs/WEB_CONFIGURATOR.md#Testing`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/docs/WEB_CONFIGURATOR.md#L430-L456) - Test patterns for web server

### Technology Stack

- **Language**: Python 3.11 (for tests), CircuitPython (for source)
- **Test frameworks**: pytest, pytest-asyncio for async tests
- **Mocking**: Extensive use of mock objects to simulate CircuitPython hardware modules
- **Async patterns**: Many managers use asyncio, tests must handle async/await

## Motivation

- Improve maintenance velocity by keeping the test suite healthy
- Expand test coverage to reduce risk of regressions and increase confidence in code changes
- Automate the tedious work of fixing broken tests while maintaining strict boundaries around source code modifications

## Deliverables

1. Custom Copilot agent configuration in `.github/copilot/` (or similar)
2. Agent instructions/prompt defining:
   - Test-only modification policy
   - Issue creation workflow for source bugs
   - Coverage analysis approach
   - Test repair strategies
3. Documentation for maintainers on how to use the agent
4. (Optional) Integration with CI to trigger agent on test failures

mentioned_issues.title: Fix ImportError: CircuitPython does not support `os.path` in WebServerManager
Implement fail-safe mode fallback to prevent infinite error loops
mentioned_issues.body:
### Description
In `CoreManager.start()`, if the current mode throws an exception during initialization, the system falls back to `self.mode = "DASHBOARD"`. If the "DASHBOARD" mode is corrupted, missing, or missing required hardware, the loop will catch the error, re-assign DASHBOARD, and fail again immediately. This causes a tight loop that locks up the system and spams the logs/audio.

### Proposed Solution
Introduce a bare-minimum `SAFE_MODE` built directly into `core_manager.py` (or a dedicated minimal file) that has zero external hardware dependencies. If `self.mode == "DASHBOARD"` fails to load, the `except` block should catch it and load `SAFE_MODE`, which simply displays "SYSTEM HALT: DASHBOARD CORRUPT" on the OLED and waits for developer intervention.

mentioned_issues.title: Refactor animation: Move and generalize logic/math to base_pixel_manager, add shape/layout state handling
mentioned_issues.body:
Currently, animation logic and math are handled separately in both `led_manager` (for straight-line LED arrays) and `matrix_manager` (for matrices such as an 8x8 grid). To enable code reuse and more advanced animations, refactor and migrate animation logic from both `led_manager` and `matrix_manager` into `base_pixel_manager`.

**Requirements:**
- Move all core animation-related logic (e.g., setting SOLID, FLASH, PULSE/BREATHE animations) and mathematical computations out of both `led_manager` and `matrix_manager`.
- Generalize and merge this logic into `base_pixel_manager` so it can be used by both and any future pixel managers.
- **Enhance `base_pixel_manager` to handle the shape/layout of its implementing subclasses**, so it can support:
    - LED strips and strings (linear/1D)
    - LED matrices (2D, e.g., x*y)
    - LED circles or custom layouts
- Facilitate the correct animation behavior depending on the shape/layout. For example, a Cylon strobe (scanner) should behave differently for a matrix than a strip or a circle.
- Provide relevant state or accessor methods within `base_pixel_manager` for shape/layout awareness (e.g., `get_shape()`, `get_dimensions()`, `get_layout_type()` or similar).
- Update implementing classes (`LEDManager`, `MatrixManager`, etc.) to declare/define their shape/layout in a way consumable by the new shared animation logic.
- Ensure existing features and animations in both managers continue to work as expected after refactor.

**Relevant code references:**
- [`matrix_manager.py`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/src/managers/matrix_manager.py):
   - `MatrixManager` specializes drawing and animating in a 2D matrix, see methods like `draw_pixel`, `_animate_slide_left`, `show_icon`.
- [`led_manager.py`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/src/managers/led_manager.py):
   - `LEDManager` handles linear/1D LED animation, see methods like `set_led`, `solid_led`, `breathe_led`, `start_cylon`.
- [`base_pixel_manager.py`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/src/managers/base_pixel_manager.py):
   - Current shared animation logic and place to relocate all math and state.

**Motivation:**
- Reduces duplicate code and consolidates animation features
- Enables unified, shape-aware animation APIs for all pixel managers
- Simplifies addition of new layouts or animation types in the future

---
**References:**
- [`docs/LED_RENDERING.md`](https://github.com/jimmydoh/jeb/blob/0007d8ae7e9bf986a71650f5729b33d673e991d1/docs/LED_RENDERING.md) for rendering architecture overview

---
**Next Steps:**
- After refactoring, update documentation and any usage examples to match the new structure.
- Ensure robust unit or integration tests cover refactored animation flows and shape/layout awareness.

mentioned_issues.title: Prevent MemoryError by chunking file uploads in WebServerManager
mentioned_issues.body:
### Description
In `web_server_manager.py`, the file upload handler accesses `content = request.body` before checking if the file size fits in available memory. Because `adafruit_httpserver` evaluates `.body` by loading the entire payload into a single contiguous bytearray, the system is highly susceptible to throwing a `MemoryError` due to heap fragmentation before the safety check even executes.

### Proposed Solution
Avoid accessing `request.body`. Instead, utilize the underlying raw socket or `request.stream` (depending on the specific `adafruit_httpserver` version being used) to stream the incoming HTTP payload in 1KB chunks directly to the SD card `with open(filepath, "wb") as f:`. This bypasses the need for a large contiguous RAM allocation.
