closing_issues.title: UX Redesign: Tab bar navigation, summary cards, contact detail sheet, and visual refresh
closing_issues.body:
## Summary

Complete visual and interaction redesign of the two primary screens (Home and Contact Detail), a new Contacts tab, plus a fundamental navigation architecture change from single-screen NavigationStack to a TabView-based layout. This issue documents every visual and interaction delta between the current implementation and the target design, organized by screen and component.

All changes apply to **both light and dark themes**. The design language updates (accent color, typography, spacing, radius) must also propagate to the **Settings view**, the **new Contacts tab**, and the **Onboarding flow** for visual consistency.

**Design accent color:** `#3D6B4F` (muted forest green) replaces the current system `AccentColor`.

### Guiding Principle

**This is a visual/layout redesign only. ALL existing features and functionality must be preserved.** No features should be added or removed — only the presentation layer changes. Snooze, custom due dates, quick-action logging, contact unavailability banners, paused state, custom breach time — all must map into the new layout.

### Terminology Reference (for implementers)

| UI Label | Entity | Property | Notes |
|----------|--------|----------|-------|
| "Frequency" filter | `Group` | `selectedGroupId` | Group entity has `frequencyDays` |
| "Group" filter | `Tag` | `selectedTagId` | Tags are user-defined groupings |
| "Manage Frequencies" (Settings) | `Group` | — | ManageGroupsView |
| "Manage Groups" (Settings) | `Tag` | — | ManageTagsView |

---

## 1. Navigation Architecture

### Current
- `ContentView.swift` renders `HomeView()` directly after onboarding
- `HomeView` uses a single `NavigationStack` with `NavigationLink` to `SettingsView` (gear icon) and `PersonDetailView` (contact row tap)
- No tab bar exists anywhere in the app
- `DeepLinkRouter` pushes onto `HomeView`'s `NavigationPath`

### Target
- Introduce `MainTabView` (or update `ContentView`) wrapping content in a `TabView` with 3 tabs:
  1. **Home** (SF Symbol: `house.fill` active / `house` inactive) — current HomeView content (always status-based sections)
  2. **Contacts** (SF Symbol: `person.2.fill` active / `person.2` inactive) — alphabetical all-contacts list (see Section 23)
  3. **Settings** (SF Symbol: `gearshape.fill` active / `gearshape` inactive) — current SettingsView, no longer navigated via gear icon
- Tab bar styling:
  - White background (light) / system dark background (dark), 1px top border
  - Active tab: accent green `#3D6B4F`, 10px bold label
  - Inactive tabs: `Color(.secondaryLabel)`, 10px bold label
  - System bottom safe area padding
- Contact detail presented as a **full-screen cover** (`.fullScreenCover`) with sheet-like visual treatment (drag handle, X button, rounded top corners, no navigation bar). This avoids sheet-stacking problems since the detail view presents 6+ nested modals (LogTouch, EditTouch, GroupPicker, TagManager, BirthdayEditor, multiple date pickers, phone/email confirmation dialogs). Sub-modals present as normal `.sheet` modals from within the fullScreenCover.
- **Sort control removed from Home.** The Home tab always shows status-based sections (Overdue / Due Soon / All Good). The alphabetical browsing experience moves to the Contacts tab. Remove `sortOption` state and name-sort rendering path from `HomeView`.
- DeepLinkRouter updated for tab selection + fullScreenCover presentation

### Files affected
- `UI/Views/ContentView.swift` — add TabView or introduce `MainTabView.swift`
- `UI/Views/Home/HomeView.swift` — remove NavigationLink to SettingsView, remove sort toggle and name-sort code path, change person navigation to fullScreenCover
- `App/DeepLinkRouter.swift` — update routing for TabView + fullScreenCover model
- `UI/ViewModels/HomeViewModel.swift` — remove `sortOption` and name-sort rendering (retained/reused for Contacts tab)
- **NEW:** `UI/Views/Contacts/ContactsListView.swift` — Contacts tab

---

## 2. Design System Updates (`DesignSystem.swift`)

### 2a. Accent Color

| Property | Current | Target |
|----------|---------|--------|
| `AccentColor.colorset` | Empty (system blue) | `#3D6B4F` light, appropriate dark variant |
| `DS.Colors.accent` | `Color.accentColor` | Inherits from updated asset catalog |

### 2b. New Color Tokens

```swift
// Summary card backgrounds (light theme values — need dark equivalents)
static let overdueCardBackground    // light: #FEF2F2 (red-50)
static let overdueCardBorder        // light: #FEE2E2 (red-100)
static let dueSoonCardBackground    // light: #FFFBEB (amber-50)
static let dueSoonCardBorder        // light: #FDE68A (amber-100)
static let allGoodCardBackground    // light: #ECFDF5 (emerald-50)
static let allGoodCardBorder        // light: #A7F3D0 (emerald-100)

// Action button colors (contact detail)
static let actionButtonBackground   // #2D3339 (dark charcoal)
static let actionButtonPressed      // #1F252B (darker charcoal)
static let actionButtonIconBg       // Color.white.opacity(0.1)

// Notes card
static let notesBackground          // light: yellow-50 at 50% opacity
static let notesBorder              // light: #FEF08A (yellow-100)

// Sheet overlay
static let sheetOverlay             // Color.black.opacity(0.4)
```

### 2c. New Typography Tokens

```swift
static let summaryNumber    // Font.system(size: 28, weight: .bold) — large status card number
static let summaryLabel     // Font.system(size: 11, weight: .bold) — uppercase tracking-wider
static let sectionHeaderMono // Font.system(size: 11, weight: .bold, design: .monospaced) — 0.15em tracking
static let tabLabel         // Font.system(size: 10, weight: .bold)
static let sheetHeroName    // Font.system(size: 24, weight: .bold) — centered detail name
static let timelineTitle    // Font.system(size: 14, weight: .bold)
static let timelineMono     // Font.system(size: 12, weight: .regular, design: .monospaced)
static let timelineNotes    // Font.system(size: 14, weight: .regular)
```

### 2d. New Radius Tokens

```swift
static let xl: CGFloat = 20
static let xxl: CGFloat = 32     // fullScreenCover top corners
static let full: CGFloat = 999   // pill/capsule shapes
```

### 2e. Dark Mode

All new color tokens must have dark mode variants:
- Summary card tint backgrounds → darker, more muted versions
- Action button charcoal → may stay same or lighten slightly
- Notes yellow tint → darker warm tint
- Timeline markers → appropriate contrast on dark backgrounds
- Use `Color(uiColor:)` with `UIColor { trait in ... }` or asset catalog named colors for automatic switching

### 2f. Theme-Aware Avatar Colors

The dark mode addendum specifies exact muted bg/text colors per avatar color. Add a static mapping in `DesignSystem.swift`:

```swift
static func avatarColors(for hex: String, scheme: ColorScheme) -> (background: Color, text: Color)
```

Light mode: use `avatarColor` hex directly as background, white text.
Dark mode: use muted variant per dark mode addendum spec.

---

## 3. Home Screen — Header

### Current
- Large title "Keep In Touch" (`DS.Typography.largeTitle` ~34px) + gear NavigationLink
- Inline status counts: `"X overdue · Y due soon · Z all good"`

### Target
- Title: "Keep in Touch" at **28px bold** — may need new token or reduce current `largeTitle`
- **Gear icon removed** (settings moves to tab bar)
- **NEW subtitle:** "Keep your people close" — 14px medium, `Color(.secondaryLabel)`
- **Status counts removed** — replaced by summary cards (Section 4)

### Files affected
- `UI/Views/Home/HomeView.swift` — `header` computed property

---

## 4. Home Screen — Summary Status Cards (NEW)

### Current
- Inline text: `statusCountText(count:label:color:)` renders colored pills

### Target
- 3-column grid of rounded cards:
  - Corner radius: 16px (`DS.Radius.lg`)
  - Light shadow: `shadow(.drop(color: .black.opacity(0.05), radius: 2, y: 1))`
  - 14px internal padding
  - **Overdue:** red tint bg, red border, large red number, "OVERDUE" uppercase label
  - **Due Soon:** amber tint bg, amber border, amber number, "DUE SOON" label
  - **All Good:** emerald tint bg, emerald border, emerald number, "ALL GOOD" label
- Number: `DS.Typography.summaryNumber`, centered
- Label: 11px bold uppercase with ~0.05em tracking, colored to match status
- Animated count changes: `.contentTransition(.numericText())`

### New component
- `StatusSummaryCard(count:, label:, numberColor:, backgroundColor:, borderColor:)` — or inline

---

## 5. Home Screen — Filters

### Current
- `FlowLayout` with sort Menu icon + frequency capsule chip + tag capsule chip
- Active state: accent-tinted background

### Target
- **Two horizontal buttons** (sort control removed — alphabetical browsing moves to Contacts tab)
- Both are equal-width buttons in an HStack (each `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`)
- Shape: `RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: DS.Radius.md)` (~10px) instead of Capsule
- Border: 1px `Color(.separator)`
- Text: 13px semibold, `Color(.secondaryLabel)`
- Labels: "Frequency: All" + caret-down, "Group: All" + caret-down
- **"Frequency: All"** — filters by `Group` entity (frequency cadence: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, etc.). Maps to `selectedGroupId` in `HomeViewModel`. This matches the existing convention where the UI label "Frequency" maps to the `Group` entity.
- **"Group: All"** — filters by `Tag` entity (user-defined groupings: Friends, Work, Family, etc.). Maps to `selectedTagId` in `HomeViewModel`. This matches the existing convention where the UI label "Groups" maps to the `Tag` entity.
- Shows selected value inline when filtered: "Frequency: Monthly", "Group: Friends"
- **Active state:** Accent green border (`#3D6B4F`) + subtle accent tint background when filter is applied. "×" clear button appears inside the button when active.
- Dropdown menu contents: "All Frequencies" / "All Groups" as first item, then all available options by name.

### Files affected
- `UI/Views/Home/HomeView.swift` — `filters`, `frequencyFilterChip`, `tagFilterChip`, remove sort menu

---

## 6. Home Screen — Contact List Sections

### Current (`ContactListSection.swift`)
- Collapsible VStack with chevron toggle
- Section header: color dot + bold subheadline title + caption count + rotating chevron

### Target
- **Retain collapse/expand behavior** — keep toggle interaction and `collapsedSections` state
- **Sticky section headers:** Use `LazyVStack(pinnedViews: [.sectionHeaders])` for sticky behavior
- **Header text restyled:** `"OVERDUE · 3"` format
  - 11px bold **monospace** uppercase with 0.15em letter-spacing (`DS.Typography.sectionHeaderMono`)
  - `Color(.secondaryLabel)` (gray-400)
  - Background: `.ultraThinMaterial` or `Color(.systemBackground).opacity(0.95)` for backdrop blur effect
- **Remove color dot** from header (color is implied by section name)
- **Keep chevron** for collapse/expand toggle (rotate on state change)
- Thin bottom border on header: 1px `Color(.systemGray6)`

### Files affected
- `UI/Views/Home/ContactListSection.swift` — header restyle
- `UI/Views/Home/HomeView.swift` — switch to `LazyVStack(pinnedViews: [.sectionHeaders])`

---

## 7. Home Screen — Contact Card (Row)

### Current (`ContactCard.swift`)
- 36px `ContactPhotoView`
- Row 1: name + inline TagPills (max 2) + `+N` overflow + StatusIndicator (dot + days)
- Row 2: metadata with clock icon + time ago + method icon + frequency + custom due date icon

### Target
- **48px avatar** circle with colored background + bold initials (use `ContactPhotoView(size: 48)`)
- **Row 1:** Name only — 15px bold (`Font.system(size: 15, weight: .bold)`) — **no inline TagPills**
- **Row 2:** `"2 weeks ago · Monthly"` — 13px medium, `Color(.secondaryLabel)` — simplified metadata
  - Format: `"{timeAgo} · {frequencyName}"`
  - If person has a `customDueDate`: append small `calendar.badge.clock` SF Symbol indicator (10pt, inline after frequency name)
  - If person is **paused**: replace entire row with `"Paused"` in `Color(.tertiaryLabel)` with moon icon
  - If person is **snoozed**: replace time-ago with `"Snoozed · {frequencyName}"` in muted color
- **Right side:**
  - **Group badge:** Small pill with 10px bold uppercase text, `Color(.systemGray5)` background, showing frequency group name (e.g., "FRIEND", "WORK")
  - **Status dot:** 8px colored circle with subtle shadow — `shadow(.drop(color: statusColor.opacity(0.3), radius: 3))`
- Row separators: 1px `Color(.systemGray6)` borders
- Full row tappable (existing `contentShape(Rectangle())`)

**Intentional display simplifications (not feature removal):**
- Tag pills removed from card → still shown in detail hero
- Days overdue number removed from card → visible via status dot color + detail view
- Touch method icon removed from card → visible in detail history
- These are display density reductions. Data and features remain accessible in the detail view.

### Files affected
- `UI/Views/Home/ContactCard.swift` — major visual rewrite
- `UI/DesignSystem.swift` — `StatusIndicator` needs "dot only" mode (8px, no text, with shadow)

### Reusable
- `ContactPhotoView` — pass larger `size` parameter

---

## 8. Home Screen — Search Bar

### Current
- Positioned at bottom of screen in the VStack
- Capsule shape, secondary background fill

### Target
- **Floating position:** Anchored above the tab bar, overlaying content
- Use `ZStack` or `.overlay(alignment: .bottom)` to position
- Shape: Capsule (rounded-full) with shadow (`shadow(.drop(color: .black.opacity(0.1), radius: 8, y: 2))`)
- Background: white (light) / dark surface (dark) with `border(Color(.systemGray5), lineWidth: 1)`
- Magnifying glass icon, "Search contacts..." placeholder
- Focus ring: 2px accent green border when focused
- Clear button: same xmark pattern
- Bottom padding: enough to clear the tab bar (~70pt from bottom safe area)
- Gradient fade above search bar for smooth content-to-search transition

### Files affected

## 17. Interaction Changes

| Interaction | Current | Target |
|-------------|---------|--------|
| Navigate to settings | Gear icon in header | Settings tab in bottom TabView |
| Open contact detail | NavigationLink push | `.fullScreenCover` with sheet-like visual |
| Dismiss contact detail | Swipe-back / back button | Drag down on handle or tap X button |
| Section collapse/expand | Tap section header | **Retained** — tap header chevron |
| Browse alphabetically | Sort toggle → Name mode on Home | Contacts tab (dedicated) |
| Sort contacts | Status/Name toggle in filter bar | **Removed** — Home always status-based |
| Search | TextField at bottom of screen | Floating capsule above tab bar (Home and Contacts tabs) |
| Filter contacts | Capsule chips + sort icon | Rounded-rect buttons, no sort icon |

- Summary card numbers: 28px light / 24px dark
- Summary card labels: status-colored light / all gray-500 dark
- Contact row padding: 14px light / 16px dark
- Avatar-to-text spacing: 14px light / 16px dark

## 20. Settings & Contacts Views

The same design language must propagate to:
- **SettingsView** (`UI/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift`) — updated accent color, typography, spacing
- **ManageGroupsView** — consistent radius, colors
- **ManageTagsView** — consistent styling
- **ContactsListView** (`UI/Views/Contacts/ContactsListView.swift`) — Alphabetical list of all tracked contacts. A-Z letter section headers. Trailing section index scrubber for quick navigation. Floating search bar (same style as Home). Reuses redesigned `ContactCard` component. Tapping a row opens `.fullScreenCover` detail. No filter buttons — browse-only. Standard empty state if no contacts tracked.
- **Onboarding flow** (`UI/Views/Onboarding/`) — All onboarding screens (WelcomeView, ContactsPermissionView, ContactPickerView, GroupsInfoView, NotificationsPermissionView, etc.) updated with new accent color (`#3D6B4F`), typography tokens, spacing, and radius tokens. No layout or flow changes — only visual consistency with the redesigned app.
- All views should feel visually cohesive with the redesigned Home and Detail screens

---

## 21. Suggested Implementation Order

1. **DS tokens:** Update `DesignSystem.swift` with all new colors (including theme-aware avatar mapping), typography, radius. Update `AccentColor.colorset`
2. **Tab bar + Contacts tab:** Introduce `MainTabView` with TabView, move Settings to own tab, build `ContactsListView` with alphabetical A-Z sections and section index scrubber. Remove sort toggle and name-sort rendering path from Home.
3. **Home header + summary cards:** Replace status counts with card grid, add subtitle, remove gear
4. **Home sections + contact card:** Sticky monospace headers (keep collapse), restyled contact rows with paused/snoozed/custom-due-date metadata states
5. **Home filters + search bar:** Restyle filters as equal-width buttons with active state, move search to floating position
6. **Contact detail fullScreenCover:** Change from push to `.fullScreenCover` with `DismissableFullScreenCover` wrapper (rounded top corners, drag handle, X button, custom drag-to-dismiss). Ensure all sub-modals present correctly. Update DeepLinkRouter.
7. **Detail hero + actions:** Center hero, 96px avatar, dark charcoal action buttons with preserved quick-log behavior, state banners, undo banners
8. **Detail notes + timeline:** Yellow notes card, vertical timeline with long-press context menu and discoverability hint
9. **Detail settings + CTA:** Restyle settings section with all items (frequency, custom due date, snooze, groups, birthday, notification time, mute, pause, remove). Fixed bottom "Log Connection" button.
10. **Dark mode audit:** Verify all new tokens in dark theme, implement structural divergences
11. **Settings/Contacts/Onboarding polish:** Propagate design language to Settings, Contacts tab, and all Onboarding screens (accent color, typography, spacing, radius — no layout changes to onboarding flow)

---

## 22. Implementation Scope Guard

To prevent scope creep, these are **explicitly out of scope**:
- New features or behaviors not in the current app
- Changes to data models, Core Data schema, or entity structs
- Changes to business logic (FrequencyCalculator, notification scheduling, PersonStatusService)
- Changes to onboarding flow *layout or step sequence* (design token propagation IS in scope — accent color, typography, spacing, radius)
- Changes to modal/sheet *content* (LogTouchModal, EditTouchModal, GroupPickerSheet, TagManagerSheet, BirthdayEditorSheet internals) — only their host presentation model changes
- Changes to SettingsView section content or SettingsViewModel logic
- Performance optimizations beyond what the redesign structurally requires (e.g., LazyVStack migration)

---

## 23. Contacts Tab — Full Spec (NEW)

### Purpose
Dedicated alphabetical browsing experience for all tracked contacts. Replaces the previous "Sort by Name" mode on Home.

### Layout
- **A-Z section headers:** Letter headers (e.g., "A", "B", "C") using `DS.Typography.sectionHeaderMono` styling (11px bold monospace uppercase, `Color(.secondaryLabel)`)
- **Contact rows:** Reuses redesigned `ContactCard` component (48px avatar, name, metadata, group badge, status dot)
- **Section index scrubber:** Trailing edge A-Z quick-scroll (using existing `SectionIndexView` component if suitable, or standard `List` with sections)
- **Floating search bar:** Same style as Home (capsule, shadow, above tab bar). Filters contacts by name.
- **No filter buttons** — browse-only
- **Empty state:** Standard `EmptyStateView` if no contacts tracked

### Navigation
- Tapping a contact opens the same `.fullScreenCover` detail view used from Home
- Search results also open detail via fullScreenCover

### Data Source
- All tracked, non-demo contacts from `HomeViewModel` or shared data source
- Sorted alphabetically by `displayName`
- Grouped by first letter of `displayName`

### Files
- **NEW:** `UI/Views/Contacts/ContactsListView.swift`

mentioned_issues.title: Add logical operators (&&, ||) to guard expressions
mentioned_issues.body:
## Description

`examples/tutorials/03_match_guards.ns` fails to parse because the grammar doesn't support `&&` (logical AND) or `||` (logical OR) operators in match guard expressions. The guard `d >= 128 && d < 512` is invalid syntax.

The grammar has comparison operators (`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=`, `==`, `!=`) but no logical connectives. Guards are currently limited to single comparisons or dimension-capture-only patterns.

## Location

- `src/grammar/neuroscript.pest` — grammar definition
- `src/grammar/ast.rs` — AST builder for value expressions
- `src/interfaces.rs:90-101` — `BinOp` enum (needs `And`, `Or` variants)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Grammar supports `&&` and `||` operators in value expressions
- [ ] AST builder handles logical operators (new `BinOp` variants: `And`, `Or`)
- [ ] Codegen emits Python `and` / `or` for logical operators
- [ ] Proper operator precedence: comparison > AND > OR
- [ ] Tutorial file parses and validates

_Migrated from internal kanban: VAL-3 / FEAT: Logical operators_

mentioned_issues.title: Variadic shape unification only checks rank, not element-wise
mentioned_issues.body:
## Description

When two shapes both contain variadic segments, unification only checks that ranks match — it doesn't perform element-wise unification of the variadic contents. This means repeated variadic bindings can accept shape mismatches silently.

For example, if `*shape` is bound to `[batch, 512]` in one context and `[batch, 256]` in another, the mismatch may not be caught.

## Location

- `src/shape/inference.rs:1041-1044` — variadic unification loop
- `src/shape/inference.rs:993-1069` — `unify_shapes_with_variadic()`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Variadic segments unified element-wise (not just rank-checked)
- [ ] `[*shape, 512]` vs `[batch, 256, 512]` correctly binds `*shape = [batch, 256]`
- [ ] Conflicting variadic bindings produce a clear error
- [ ] Test case with conflicting variadic bindings

_Migrated from internal kanban: SHAPE-NEW-2_

- `src/shape/inference.rs` — shape unification logic

## Description

251 non-test `.unwrap()` calls remain across the codebase. Most are `writeln!().unwrap()` in codegen (harmless for String buffers but poor practice) and parse-related unwraps in the AST builder.

For a language compiler, panicking on unexpected input is unacceptable — users need error messages, not stack traces. The AST builder unwraps are the real risk.

- `src/codegen/instantiation.rs` — writeln unwraps
- `src/grammar/ast.rs` — 56 parse-related unwraps

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reduce to under 50 non-test unwraps
- [ ] All `writeln!().unwrap()` in codegen replaced with `?` operator
- [ ] AST builder unwraps replaced with proper error propagation
- [ ] No panics on malformed input

mentioned_issues.title: ValidationError PartialEq: unreachable!() arm is fragile for future variants
mentioned_issues.body:
## From PR #113 review

The `_ => unreachable!()` arm in `impl PartialEq for ValidationError` is correct given the `std::mem::discriminant` guard, but if a new variant is added without a corresponding match arm, it panics at runtime instead of failing at compile time.

**Options:**
1. Revert to `_ => false` with a comment explaining the discriminant pre-check
2. Derive `PartialEq` on a span-stripped wrapper type (blocked by miette's `#[label]` requiring `Option<SourceSpan>`)

**Location:** `src/interfaces.rs` ~line 850

**Priority:** Low — functionally correct today, but a maintenance footgun.

## Scope

---

## Section 1: Navigation Architecture

### Current
- `ContentView.swift` renders `HomeView()` directly after onboarding

### Target
- Introduce `MainTabView` (or update `ContentView`) wrapping content in a `TabView` with 3 tabs:
  1. **Home** (SF Symbol: `house.fill` active / `house` inactive) — current HomeView content (always status-based sections)
  2. **Contacts** (SF Symbol: `person.2.fill` active / `person.2` inactive) — alphabetical all-contacts list (see Section 23)
  3. **Settings** (SF Symbol: `gearshape.fill` active / `gearshape` inactive) — current SettingsView, no longer navigated via gear icon
- Tab bar styling:
  - White background (light) / system dark background (dark), 1px top border
  - Active tab: accent green `#3D6B4F`, 10px bold label
  - Inactive tabs: `Color(.secondaryLabel)`, 10px bold label
  - System bottom safe area padding
- **Sort control removed from Home.** The Home tab always shows status-based sections (Overdue / Due Soon / All Good). The alphabetical browsing experience moves to the Contacts tab. Remove `sortOption` state and name-sort rendering path from `HomeView`.
- DeepLinkRouter updated for tab selection + fullScreenCover presentation

### Files affected
- `UI/Views/ContentView.swift` — add TabView or introduce `MainTabView.swift`
- `UI/Views/Home/HomeView.swift` — remove NavigationLink to SettingsView, remove sort toggle and name-sort code path
- `App/DeepLinkRouter.swift` — update routing for TabView + fullScreenCover model

### Current
- Inline text: `statusCountText(count:label:color:)` renders colored pills

### Target
- 3-column grid of rounded cards:
  - Corner radius: 16px (`DS.Radius.lg`)
  - Light shadow: `shadow(.drop(color: .black.opacity(0.05), radius: 2, y: 1))`
  - 14px internal padding
  - **Overdue:** red tint bg, red border, large red number, "OVERDUE" uppercase label
  - **Due Soon:** amber tint bg, amber border, amber number, "DUE SOON" label
  - **All Good:** emerald tint bg, emerald border, emerald number, "ALL GOOD" label
- Number: `DS.Typography.summaryNumber`, centered
- Label: 11px bold uppercase with ~0.05em tracking, colored to match status
- Animated count changes: `.contentTransition(.numericText())`

### New component
- `StatusSummaryCard(count:, label:, numberColor:, backgroundColor:, borderColor:)` — or inline

- `FlowLayout` with sort Menu icon + frequency capsule chip + tag capsule chip

mentioned_issues.title: [Epic]: Eliminate Dual Joker Framework and Migrate to Unified Trait System
mentioned_issues.body:
## Epic Overview 🎯

This epic eliminates the technical debt from maintaining two parallel joker systems and migrates balatro-rs to use only the modern trait-based joker framework. This "big bang" migration affects game engine, Python bindings, and state management.

## Current Architecture Problem

**Dual System Maintenance (80% overhead)**:
- **Old System**: 16 jokers in `Jokers` enum with callback-based `Effects`
- **New System**: Modern trait-based `Joker` trait with `JokerEffect` returns
- **Bridge Layer**: `compat.rs` maintains compatibility between systems
- **Impact**: Every joker must be implemented twice, type conflicts, testing complexity

## Migration Goals

✅ **Single JokerStateManager**: Unified state management across all jokers  
✅ **Clean Architecture**: Event-driven game engine integration  
✅ **Expanded Capabilities**: Support all 150+ planned jokers instead of just 16  
✅ **Python Compatibility**: Migrate PyO3 bindings to new API  
✅ **Performance**: Eliminate callback overhead and enable parallel processing  
✅ **Breaking Changes Accepted**: Save games and Python API will break for clean architecture  

## Work Streams

### 🔧 Core Framework Migration (15-21 story points)
- Finalize trait-based joker system
- Migrate 16 existing jokers from enum to trait implementation
- Remove compatibility layer and old Effects system

### 🏗️ Game Engine Integration (23 story points)  
- Replace callback-based Effects with event-driven JokerEngine
- Integrate JokerStateManager into Game struct
- Add performance optimizations and concurrent processing

### 🐍 Python Binding Migration (31 story points)
- Update PyO3 bindings from Jokers enum to JokerId system
- Expand API to support all 150+ jokers with metadata
- Add backwards compatibility layer with deprecation path

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Zero jokers implemented in dual system
- [ ] All 16 existing jokers migrated to trait system
- [ ] Game engine uses event-driven joker processing
- [ ] Python bindings expose new joker capabilities
- [ ] Performance improved over baseline
- [ ] All tests passing
- [ ] Documentation updated

## Architecture Benefits Post-Migration

🚀 **Performance**: Event-driven processing with parallel execution  
🧱 **Maintainability**: Single source of truth for joker logic  
🔧 **Extensibility**: Clean patterns for new jokers and state management  
🐍 **Python Power**: Rich metadata API for ML/RL applications  
📈 **Scalability**: Support for 150+ jokers with efficient state management  

## Implementation Strategy

**Big Bang Migration**: Coordinated changes across all systems simultaneously
**Parallel Development**: Multiple independent work streams
**Incremental Testing**: Validate each component as it completes
**Breaking Changes**: Accept API breaks for clean architecture

## Dependencies and Parallel Opportunities

See individual child issues for detailed dependency graphs. Key parallel streams:
- Core framework foundation can run alongside engine integration foundation
- Python binding planning can start immediately
- Documentation can be written in parallel with implementation
- Testing can validate components as they complete

- Game Engine: #[will be filled with child issue numbers]  
- Python Bindings: #[will be filled with child issue numbers]

✨ **Sparkly Organization**: Optimized for maximum parallelization and developer productivity

## Description
This epic tracks the refactoring of the monolithic Joker trait (25 methods) into 5 focused traits following the Interface Segregation Principle. This will improve code maintainability, enable better testing, and make it easier to implement new joker types.

## Problem Statement
- Single trait with 25 methods violating Interface Segregation Principle
- Forces all 150+ joker implementations to provide methods they don't use
- Difficult to test individual aspects in isolation
- High cognitive load for developers

## Solution Overview
Split into 5 focused traits with a Joker super trait for compatibility:
- `JokerIdentity` (6 methods) - Core metadata
- `JokerLifecycle` (7 methods) - State transitions  
- `JokerGameplay` (3 methods) - Game effects
- `JokerModifiers` (4 methods) - Rule modifications
- `JokerState` (5 methods) - Persistence

## Implementation Strategy
Hyper-parallel implementation across 5 days with infinite developer resources:
- **Day 1**: Foundation (3 PRs)
- **Day 2-3**: Mass migration (15+ PRs)
- **Day 4**: Testing blitz (8+ PRs)
- **Day 5**: Documentation (3 PRs)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 26+ PRs merged successfully
- [ ] All existing tests pass with no regressions
- [ ] Performance regression <1%
- [ ] All 150+ jokers migrated to new trait system
- [ ] Comprehensive unit tests for each trait
- [ ] Documentation and examples updated

## Success Metrics
- Each trait has single responsibility (max 7 methods)
- Simple jokers need only 2 trait implementations
- Unit test coverage >95% per trait
- Manual implementation approach (no derive macros)
- Joker super trait maintained permanently

mentioned_issues.title: [Enhancement]: Add Performance Benchmarks for JokerEffectProcessor
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary
Add comprehensive performance benchmarks for the JokerEffectProcessor to monitor and validate performance characteristics for RL training scenarios.

## Background
During code review of PR #205 (issue #152), it was identified that while the implementation includes performance tracking, dedicated benchmarks would help ensure optimal performance for reinforcement learning applications.

## Current State
- Processing time tracking exists but no formal benchmarks
- General game benchmarks exist but no specific effect processor benchmarks
- No performance regression detection for effect processing

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add Criterion.rs benchmarks for effect processing operations
- [ ] Benchmark `process_hand_effects` with varying joker counts (1, 5, 10, 20)
- [ ] Benchmark `process_card_effects` with different effect complexities
- [ ] Benchmark conflict resolution strategies (Sum, Max, Min, etc.)
- [ ] Benchmark retriggering scenarios with various retrigger counts
- [ ] Benchmark priority ordering with different priority distributions
- [ ] Add memory allocation profiling for effect processing
- [ ] Create baseline performance targets for CI validation
- [ ] Add benchmark comparison reports for performance tracking

## Benchmark Scenarios
1. **Basic Effect Processing**: Simple effects with minimal retriggers
2. **Complex Effect Combinations**: Multiple jokers with different effect types
3. **Heavy Retriggering**: High retrigger counts near the limit
4. **Large Joker Collections**: Performance with many jokers active
5. **Memory Allocation**: Track allocations during processing
6. **Cache Performance**: Benchmark cache hit/miss scenarios (after cache implementation)

## Performance Targets
- Single joker effect processing: < 1μs
- 10 jokers with complex effects: < 10μs
- 20 jokers with retriggering: < 50μs
- Memory allocations: < 1KB per processing operation
- Cache hit performance: < 100ns

## Files to Create/Modify
- `core/benches/effect_processor_benchmark.rs`
- Update `Cargo.toml` if needed for benchmark dependencies
- CI configuration for performance regression detection

## Benefits

closing_issues.title: conscious probe - website
closing_issues.body:
Create a small interactive web component called "NeuroFlow – Cognitive Development Probe".

Requirements:

The component displays 7 neuroscience-inspired yes/no questions.

Each question has two buttons: YES and NO.

The questions should be shown in a vertical diagnostic-style panel.

The last question (Q7) should be locked until Q1–Q6 are answered YES.

Show the status of each question using indicators:

YES → green

NO → red

unanswered → gray

locked → 🔒 icon

The UI should look minimal, scientific, and futuristic, similar to a lab diagnostic interface.

Questions to display:

Q1 – Prediction error detected?
Q2 – Internal model updated?
Q3 – Uncertainty estimated?

closing_issues.title: Automated issue report to github project
closing_issues.body:
The most straightforward, zero-user-effort approach is to **build it directly into your agent's tool calling logic**. Here's the thinking:


**The ideal flow:**
1. User expresses dissatisfaction (frustration, a bug report, "this doesn't work", etc.)
2. Your agent detects it via the system prompt instruction
3. Agent **silently calls a `create_github_issue` tool in the background**
4. Agent responds normally to the user — they never have to do anything


The user experience is just: they complain → agent helps them → issue is already filed on GitHub automatically.


**What you need to set up (one-time):**


1. **Register a GitHub tool** in your agentic framework:
```python
{
  "name": "create_github_issue",
  "description": "Silently file a GitHub issue when user expresses dissatisfaction, reports a bug, or encounters an error.",
  "input_schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "title": {"type": "string"},
      "body": {"type": "string"},
      "labels": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
    },
    "required": ["title", "body"]
  }
}
```


2. **Add this to your system prompt:**
```
If the user expresses frustration, confusion, dissatisfaction, or reports a bug or error, 
ALWAYS silently call create_github_issue with a descriptive title and body summarizing 
the problem. Do this before or while responding — never ask the user for permission.
```


3. **Implement the tool handler** with your GitHub token to hit `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`.


That's it — fully automatic, no user friction at all. The agent both helps the user *and* logs the issue in one turn.

closing_issues.title: [REFACTOR]: Centralize Configuration Precedence & Merge Strategy
closing_issues.body:
Stakeholder Type: Project Maintainer
Component/Domain: Config

As a:
Project maintainer

I want to:
Implement a single, explicit layered configuration loading & merge pipeline (defaults → file → env → CLI → post-processing) with clear override logging, validation, and predictable handling of None vs empty lists.

But:
Precedence is implicit and scattered; overrides are silent; secrets vs env order undocumented; None vs [] intent ambiguous; legacy compatibility flags previously added increased complexity.

This helps by:
Making behavior predictable, simplifying debugging, reducing regressions, enabling a --show-effective-config feature, and simplifying future configuration-related features.

Unlike:
The current ad hoc, multi-location merging with silent overrides and unclear semantics.

Refactoring Type:
Reorganize modules; Simplify complex logic.

Affected Code/Files:
- src/config/__init__.py (load_config)
- src/config/config.py (model defaults)
- src/cli/handlers.py (config usage patterns)
- Future new module: src/config/merge.py (to introduce)
- Any direct env/secret reads in Trakt integration

Current Issues:
- No central merge function
- Silent override of scan_mode, extensions
- Ambiguous None vs [] for include_statuses/extensions
- Secrets precedence (env vs files) undocumented
- No debug trace of effective config
- Legacy behavior (path list returns) already removed but not documented

Proposed Structure:
1. Add merge utility (config/merge.py) implementing ordered layering: model defaults → file config → secrets/env → CLI overrides → post_process.
2. Provide deep merge for nested objects; replace lists entirely; preserve explicit empty list override.
3. Secrets precedence: env variables override secrets files; fail fast on partial credentials.
4. Add debug logging per override: source, key, old, new.
5. Optional --show-effective-config flag to dump merged model.
6. Emit deprecation warnings only for still-supported transitional options (none expected after this refactor).
7. Unit tests for scalar override chain, list None vs [], deep merge, secrets precedence, failure on partial credentials.
8. Update docs/CONFIG.md with precedence table, examples, troubleshooting.
9. Document removal of prior backward compatibility flags (as_paths) and that legacy path-list return style is not supported.

EXPLICIT REQUIREMENT (Non-Goal / Constraint):
Backward compatibility with the old path-list return style is NOT required. Do NOT reintroduce the as_paths flag or similar shims. Breaking change accepted.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Central merge function in place and used by load_config.
- No scattered ad hoc env/CLI overrides in handlers.
- Distinct handling of None vs [] confirmed by tests.
- Debug/verbose mode logs each override.
- Secrets precedence enforced and documented; partial credentials error out early.
- Docs updated (CONFIG.md) with precedence & examples.
- --show-effective-config (if implemented) outputs final merged model.
- CI tests (make check, make test) pass.

Tasks:
- [ ] Implement config/merge.py with ordered layering.
- [ ] Refactor load_config to use merge pipeline.
- [ ] Add env+secrets loader (CVI_*, TRKT_* prefixes).
- [ ] Implement override logging (debug level).
- [ ] Add unit tests for merge behaviors.
- [ ] Add failure test for partial Trakt credentials.
- [ ] Add --show-effective-config (optional) to CLI.
- [ ] Update CONFIG.md with precedence table & examples.
- [ ] Note permanent removal of legacy path list behavior.
- [ ] Add changelog/release notes entry summarizing the refactor & breaking change.

Code of Conduct:
I agree to follow this project's Code of Conduct.

closing_issues.title: Improve Negative Test Conformance
closing_issues.body:
## Description

Currently only 1.7% (9 out of 543) of invalid 3MF files are correctly rejected. The parser is too permissive and accepts many files that violate the 3MF specification. This is a critical gap in spec compliance.

## Current State

- ✅ 100% positive test compliance (1,698/1,698 valid files parse)
- ⚠️ 1.7% negative test compliance (9/543 invalid files rejected)
- 📊 76.2% overall conformance (1,707/2,241 total tests)

The parser correctly handles all valid files but fails to reject most invalid ones.

## Expected Outcome

- Analyze negative test failures systematically
- Categorize failures by error type (using test codes from filenames)
- Implement validation rules for each category
- Achieve >90% negative test compliance
- Document any intentionally permissive behavior

## Implementation Approach

1. **Analyze failures:** Run `cargo run --example categorize_failures` to group failures by test code
2. **Understand requirements:** For each code category, review the 3MF specification to understand what should be validated
3. **Implement validators:** Add validation rules to `src/validator.rs`
4. **Track progress:** Run `cargo run --example analyze_negative_tests` to measure improvement
5. **Prioritize:** Focus on high-frequency failure categories first

## Test Files

- 543 negative test cases available in `test_suites/*/negative_test_cases/`
- Test file naming: `N_XXX_NNNN_VV.3mf` where NNNN is the test code category
- Examples already exist: `examples/categorize_failures.rs`, `examples/analyze_negative_tests.rs`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Negative test compliance improved to >90% (485+ out of 543 invalid files rejected)
- [ ] Failures categorized by test code
- [ ] Validation rules documented
- [ ] Error messages are clear and reference spec violations
- [ ] No regression in positive tests (maintain 100%)
- [ ] README updated with new conformance statistics

## References

- README.md, lines 204-206
- TESTING_QUICK_REFERENCE.md, lines 131-133
- [3MF Core Specification](https://3mf.io/specification/)
- [3MF Consortium Test Suites](https://github.com/3MFConsortium/test_suites)

## Related Issues

- #[issue for base materials validation]
- #[issue for component validation]
- #[issue for metadata validation]

## Additional Context

This is the highest priority issue as it represents the largest gap in spec compliance. Breaking it down into smaller validation tasks (one per test code category) may make implementation more manageable.

```sql
create table if not exists features_catalog (
  feature_key text primary key,
  label text,
  category text,
  description text,
  is_global boolean default false
);

create table if not exists user_feature_toggles (

  user_id uuid not null,
  feature_key text not null references features_catalog(feature_key),
  enabled boolean not null default false,
  updated_at timestamptz default now(),
  unique (user_id, feature_key)
);
```

- Architect to assign to UI/UX and backend devs as needed

- UI engineer to rebuild feature toggle board per spec above (always show full feature list, toggles, error handling, fallback mode, WebGL visual improvements as suggested)

## ⚖️ Feature Request: Manual Virtual Balance Override

### Summary
Add the ability to manually set/override the virtual balance (actual balance) directly from the dashboard, allowing users to quickly correct discrepancies or input their current bank balance.

### User Story
As a user, I want to be able to manually set my actual balance directly on the dashboard, so I can quickly reconcile my virtual budget with my real bank account without navigating to separate screens or complex reconciliation flows.

### Proposed Features

#### 🎯 Core Functionality
- **Clickable Balance Display**: Make the virtual balance clickable to edit
- **Inline Editing**: Quick input field that appears on click
- **Validation**: Ensure entered value is a valid number
- **Confirmation**: Optional confirmation dialog for large changes
- **Audit Trail**: Log manual balance adjustments for tracking

#### 🛠️ Implementation Options
1. **Inline Edit**: Click balance → input field appears → save/cancel
2. **Modal Edit**: Click balance → modal with input and explanation
3. **Quick Actions**: Preset buttons for common adjustments (+$100, -$50, etc.)

#### 🎨 UI/UX Considerations
- **Visual Feedback**: Highlight that balance is clickable (hover effect)
- **Clear Labels**: Distinguish between "calculated" vs "manually set" balance
- **Undo Option**: Allow reverting recent manual changes
- **Difference Display**: Show variance between calculated and manual balance
- **Warning States**: Alert if manual balance creates large discrepancies

#### 🔧 Technical Details
- **State Management**: Update `actualBalance` in budget store
- **Persistence**: Save manual overrides to localStorage/sync
- **Reconciliation Impact**: Consider how this affects transaction reconciliation
- **Data Integrity**: Maintain audit log of manual adjustments

### Benefits
- **Quick Corrections**: Fast way to fix balance discrepancies
- **Real-world Alignment**: Easy to match actual bank balance
- **User Control**: Direct manipulation of key financial metric
- **Reduced Friction**: No need for complex reconciliation workflows for simple adjustments

### Priority
🟡 **Medium** - Frequently requested for budget accuracy

### Related Features
- Could integrate with bank sync to auto-populate real balance
- Potential connection to reconciliation system
- Might trigger smart suggestions for discrepancy resolution

---
*This feature would significantly improve the user's ability to keep their virtual budget aligned with reality.*

## 🔴 Feature Request: Negative Virtual Balance Support

### Summary
Enable and properly handle negative virtual balance scenarios when users spend more than their available cash, allowing the unassigned cash to go negative to reflect real-world overspending situations.

### User Story
As a user, when I spend more money than I have available in my budget, I want the system to allow and properly display negative unassigned cash, so I can see that I'm overspending and need to address the deficit.

### Current Behavior Analysis
After reviewing the codebase, it appears that:
- ✅ **Negative values are technically supported** - No explicit restrictions prevent negative `unassignedCash`
- ❓ **UI handling unclear** - Need to verify how negative values display in summary cards
- ❓ **Transfer restrictions** - Some validation might prevent transfers when insufficient funds

### Proposed Enhancements

#### 🎯 Core Functionality
- **Allow Negative Unassigned Cash**: Explicitly support and encourage negative values when overspending occurs
- **Visual Indicators**: Clear styling for negative balances (red color, warning icons)
- **Overspending Alerts**: Notifications when going negative
- **Recovery Suggestions**: Smart recommendations for addressing negative balances

#### 🛠️ Technical Implementation
- **Validation Updates**: Remove/modify any restrictions preventing negative unassigned cash
- **UI Styling**: 
  ```css
  .negative-balance {
    color: #ef4444; /* red */
    font-weight: bold;
  }
  ```
- **State Management**: Ensure all stores properly handle negative values
- **Transaction Processing**: Allow transactions that push balance negative

#### 🎨 UI/UX Enhancements
- **Summary Card Styling**: Red background/border for negative unassigned cash
- **Warning Icons**: Alert triangle or similar indicator
- **Balance Display**: Show negative values clearly (-$123.45)
- **Dashboard Alerts**: Prominent notification when budget is in deficit
- **Recovery Mode**: Special UI state suggesting actions to resolve negative balance

#### 🚨 Smart Alerts & Actions
- **Threshold Warnings**: Alert before going negative
- **Recovery Suggestions**:
  - "Transfer from [envelope] to cover deficit"
  - "Reduce spending in [category]"
  - "Add income to balance budget"
- **Historical Tracking**: Track how often/long budget stays negative

### Real-World Scenarios
1. **Unexpected Expenses**: Medical bill, car repair exceeds available cash
2. **Overspending**: User spends more than allocated in categories
3. **Income Delays**: Paycheck delayed but bills still need paying
4. **Emergency Situations**: Using credit/overdraft reflected in virtual budget

### Benefits
- **Reality Alignment**: Virtual budget matches real financial situations
- **Awareness**: Users see overspending immediately
- **Planning Tool**: Helps plan recovery from deficit situations
- **Transparency**: No hidden or masked financial problems

### Priority
🟡 **Medium** - Important for real-world budget accuracy

### Technical Investigation Needed
- [ ] Test current behavior with negative values
- [ ] Identify any validation preventing negative balances
- [ ] Review envelope transfer restrictions
- [ ] Check summary card display with negative values

### Related Features
- Could trigger smart suggestions for deficit recovery
- Integration with emergency fund recommendations
- Connection to income planning features

---
*Supporting negative balances makes the virtual budget more realistic and helps users understand their true financial position.*

## 🏗️ Refactor: Rename AuthContext.jsx to authStore.js for Consistent Architecture

### Summary
Rename `src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx` to `src/stores/authStore.js` to reflect that it's actually a Zustand store, not React Context, and maintain consistency with our Zustand-based architecture.

### Background
Following the state management cleanup in #211, we have a clean Zustand-based architecture. However, there's a naming inconsistency:

- ✅ **budgetStore.js** - Pure Zustand store (correctly named)
- ❌ **AuthContext.jsx** - Actually exports a Zustand store, but named like Context API

The `AuthContext.jsx` file exports:
```javascript
export const useAuth = create((set) => ({
  // This is actually a Zustand store, not React Context
}));

export const AuthProvider = ({ children }) => {
  // This just handles auto-logout timer, not Context provision
  return <>{children}</>;
};
```

### 🎯 Proposed Changes

#### File Structure
```
src/stores/
├── budgetStore.js     ✅ (existing)
└── authStore.js       🆕 (renamed from contexts/AuthContext.jsx)
```

#### Consistent Naming
- **Before**: `AuthContext.jsx` exports `useAuth` Zustand store
- **After**: `authStore.js` exports `useAuth` Zustand store
- Keep `AuthProvider` component for auto-logout timer functionality

### 🔧 Implementation Tasks

- [ ] Move `src/contexts/AuthContext.jsx` → `src/stores/authStore.js`
- [ ] Update all import statements:
  - `import { useAuth } from "../contexts/AuthContext"`
  - `import { useAuth } from "../stores/authStore"`
- [ ] Update files that import `AuthProvider`:
  - Keep the component but import from the new location
- [ ] Clean up empty `src/contexts/` directory if no other files remain
- [ ] Update any documentation references

### 📁 Files to Update
Based on our recent refactoring, these files likely need import updates:
- `src/hooks/useAuthFlow.js`
- `src/hooks/usePasswordRotation.js` 
- `src/hooks/useDataManagement.js`
- `src/components/layout/MainLayout.jsx` (for AuthProvider)
- Any other files importing from AuthContext

### 🎨 Benefits

#### Consistency
- Both stores follow same naming pattern: `budgetStore.js`, `authStore.js`
- Clear distinction: `/stores/` for Zustand, `/contexts/` for React Context
- Easier for developers to understand the architecture

#### Clarity
- Filename reflects actual implementation (Zustand store)
- Eliminates confusion about Context API vs Zustand
- Maintains clean separation of concerns

### 🧪 Testing
- [ ] Verify all auth flows still work (login/logout/profile updates)
- [ ] Confirm auto-logout timer functionality preserved
- [ ] Check that all imports resolve correctly
- [ ] Run linting to ensure no missing imports

### Priority
🟡 **Medium** - Improves code organization and developer experience

### Related Issues
- Follows #211 state management cleanup
- Prepares for #220 TanStack Query + Dexie integration
- Part of overall architecture standardization

---
*This refactor completes the transition to a pure Zustand-based state management architecture.*

mentioned_issues.body:
## 💳 Feature Request: Comprehensive Debt Tracking System

### Summary
Add a dedicated debt tracking module to monitor loans, mortgages, bankruptcy payments, and other debt obligations with interest calculations, payment schedules, and payoff projections.

### User Story
As a user with various debt obligations (car loans, mortgets, Chapter 13 bankruptcy, credit cards), I want to track all my debts in one place with their interest rates, payment schedules, and payoff timelines, so I can make informed financial decisions and monitor my debt reduction progress.

### Core Debt Types to Support
- **🏠 Mortgages** - Fixed/variable rates, PMI, escrow
- **🚗 Auto Loans** - Standard car financing
- **💳 Credit Cards** - Revolving credit with minimum payments
- **🏛️ Bankruptcy Plans** - Chapter 13 payment plans with trustee payments
- **🎓 Student Loans** - Federal/private with various repayment plans
- **👥 Personal Loans** - Fixed-term personal debt
- **🏢 Business Loans** - Commercial debt obligations
- **📱 Other Installment Debt** - Phone financing, appliances, etc.

### 🎯 Core Features

#### Debt Management
- **Add/Edit Debts**: Create debt entries with all relevant details
- **Debt Categories**: Organize by type (secured, unsecured, priority)
- **Account Linking**: Connect to specific accounts or envelopes
- **Status Tracking**: Active, paid off, in deferment, etc.

#### Financial Details
- **Principal Balance**: Current amount owed
- **Interest Rate**: APR with compound frequency

closing_issues.title: ATOM-ISSUE-20260117-001-the-identify-regions-method-only-detects-problematic-regions
closing_issues.body:
The `_identify_regions()` method only detects problematic regions when divergence is positive \(unresolved expansion\) but fails to detect negative divergence regions \(premature closure\/over\-compression\)\, which are explicitly documented as a concern in the Wave protocol\.
View Details
📝 Patch Details ```diff diff --git a/experiments/spiral_verifier.py b/experiments/spiral_verifier.py index a7d6564..872f376 100644 --- a/experiments/spiral_verifier.py +++ b/experiments/spiral_verifier.py @@ -407,6 +407,13 @@ class CoherenceAnalyzer: "description": "Unresolved expansion detected" }) + if divergence < -self.thresholds["divergence_warning"]: + regions.append({ + "type": "negative_divergence", + "severity": "critical" if abs(divergence) > self.thresholds["divergence_critical"] else "warning", + "description": "Premature closure or over-compression detected" + }) + return regions ```
### Analysis ## Missing negative divergence detection in CoherenceAnalyzer\.\_identify\_regions\(\) **What fails\:** CoherenceAnalyzer\.\_identify\_regions\(\) detects unresolved expansion \(positive divergence\) but fails to detect premature closure or over\-compression \(negative divergence\)\, leaving incomplete coherence analysis\. **How to reproduce\:** ```python from experiments.spiral_verifier import CoherenceAnalyzer analyzer = CoherenceAnalyzer() # Content with negative divergence indicators (premature closure) content = """ Obviously this is simple. Clearly we can conclude. In summary, needless to say, it's done. Therefore, finally, finished. """ metrics = analyzer.analyze(content) print(f"Divergence: {metrics.divergence}") # Returns -0.7 (below -0.4 threshold) print(f"Regions: {metrics.regions}") # Returns empty list (BUG) ``` **Result\:** Divergence is calculated correctly as \-0\.700 \(negative value indicating over\-compression\)\, but the regions list remains empty\. No problematic region is detected or reported\. **Expected\:** Should return regions list containing a \"negative\_divergence\" region with appropriate severity level\, matching how positive divergence is handled\. **Background\:** Per Wave protocol documentation \(lines 332\-333\)\, negative divergence represents \"premature closure\, over\-compression\" which is explicitly documented as a concern\. ## Cascading Issues Analysis: Structural Patterns in Claude Code

We applied systematic architectural analysis (wave.md protocol) to 
your 100 open issues. Rather than treating them as independent bugs, 
we mapped how they cascade from shared boundary fractures.

### What We Found

Three critical architectural violations create compounding failures:

1. **Context Inheritance Assumption** (#15993, #16162, #15950, #16110)
   - Subagents spawn with zero context
   - Cascades to: 756+ logged protocol deviations, unreliable multi-agent workflows

2. **Permission Model Gaps** (#15711, #12926, #16163)
   - Allow-lists bypass at execution layer (rm -rf succeeds despite restrictions)
   - Cascades to: Data loss, security vulnerabilities, user trust erosion

3. **Session Lifecycle Fragmentation** (#4953, #14951, #13952, #15531)
   - Operations that should be atomic scatter across lifecycle
   - Cascades to: Memory leaks (120GB+), zombie processes, LSP/MCP non-functional

### The Load-Bearing Insight

Claude Code is a **coordination system** masquerading as a terminal application. 
The fractures all occur at coordination *boundaries*—where systems must hand off 
context, enforce permissions, or guarantee state consistency. Fix the boundaries, 
watch 15-20 issues cascade-resolve.

### Three Leverage Points (Minimum Viable Fixes)

We identified three strategic fixes that would cascade-resolve the highest impact:

- **UTF-8 Safe String Operations** (~10-15 LOC) → Eliminates fatal CJK crashes
- **Plugin Initialization Ordering** (~3-5 LOC reorder) → LSP/MCP ecosystem functional
- **Permission Execution-Layer Validation** (~25-35 LOC wrapper) → Bypasses impossible

### Next Steps

We've forked the repo and can implement these fixes with full verification. 
But before we do heavy lifting, we wanted to surface the structural insight and 
ask: Does this match what you're seeing? What should we be attending to that 
we might have missed?

""" metrics = analyzer.analyze(content) print(f"Divergence: {metrics.divergence}") # Returns -0.7 (below -0.4 threshold) print(f"Regions: {metrics.regions}") # Returns empty list (BUG) ``` **Result\:** Divergence is calculated correctly as \-0\.700 \(negative value indicating over\-compression\)\, but the regions list remains empty\. closing_issues.title: Implement apply_change in RootDatabase
closing_issues.body:
## Problem

The `RootDatabase::apply_change` method is currently a no-op placeholder that accepts changes but doesn't process them:

```rust
pub fn apply_change(&mut self, _change: Change) {
    // Placeholder implementation for Phase 1
    // Full implementation will come when we add FileRegistry
    // For now, we just accept changes but don't process them
    // This is sufficient for initial testing of the database structure
}
```

**Location:** `crates/graphql-db/src/lib.rs:186-191`

This means the entire incremental computation system doesn't actually respond to file changes, which defeats the purpose of using Salsa.

## Impact

- Salsa queries are never properly invalidated when files change
- The LSP can't provide real-time updates as users edit files
- Tests can't verify incremental recomputation behavior
- The "golden invariant" (editing bodies doesn't invalidate schema knowledge) can't be validated

## Tasks

- [ ] Implement `apply_change` to properly handle `files_changed` events
  - Update `FileContent` for changed files using `FileContent::set_text()`
  - Salsa will automatically invalidate dependent queries
- [ ] Implement `files_added` handling
  - Integrate with `FileRegistry` to allocate new `FileId`s
  - Create `FileContent` and `FileMetadata` for new files
  - Update `ProjectFiles` to include new files in appropriate lists
- [ ] Implement `files_removed` handling
  - Update `ProjectFiles` to remove deleted files
  - Consider cleanup/garbage collection of unused Salsa data
- [ ] Add tests that verify changes trigger proper invalidation
  - Test that modifying a file invalidates `parse()` query
  - Test that changing schema invalidates `schema_types()`
  - Test that changing operations invalidates `file_diagnostics()`
  - Test that changing bodies doesn't invalidate schema structure (golden invariant)

## Context

This is a core piece of the Salsa-based architecture. The `FileRegistry` in `graphql-ide` crate already exists and handles URI-to-FileId mapping. The `apply_change` method needs to coordinate with it.

See:
- `crates/graphql-ide/src/file_registry.rs` - URI/FileId mapping
- `crates/graphql-db/src/lib.rs:169-178` - Change struct definition
- Salsa docs on invalidation: https://salsa-rs.github.io/salsa/

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `apply_change` processes all three change types (added/changed/removed)
- [ ] Salsa queries are properly invalidated based on changes
- [ ] Tests verify incremental recomputation works correctly
- [ ] No placeholder comments remain in the implementation

mentioned_issues.title: LSP: Config reload not implemented
mentioned_issues.body:
## Description

When a `.graphqlrc.yaml` file changes, the LSP detects it but doesn't reload the configuration.

**Location:** `crates/graphql-lsp/src/server.rs:992`

```rust
FileChangeType::CREATED | FileChangeType::CHANGED => {
    tracing::info!("Config file changed for workspace: {}", workspace_uri);
    // TODO: Reload config and re-validate all documents
}
```

## Impact

- Adding a new project to `.graphqlrc.yaml` requires LSP restart
- Changing project configuration (schema paths, document patterns) uses stale data
- Newly added files matching new project patterns won't be analyzed

## Expected Behavior

When config changes are detected, the LSP should:
1. Reload the configuration file
2. Update the `configs` map
3. Re-discover files for each project
4. Rebuild `AnalysisHost` state
5. Re-validate open documents

closing_issues.title: [Feature]: Strengthen ESLint for Guardrails
closing_issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

ESLint is not strong enough in enforcing AI Guardrails for safe AI implementation.

### Proposed Solution

Enhance `eslint.config.mjs` to enforce AI guardrails: stricter TypeScript, accessibility/a11y, banned APIs/patterns, and Next.js best practices.

### Alternatives Considered

## Requirements
- Enforce `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` (use `import type`).
- Disallow `any` (except explicitly justified via `// eslint-disable-next-line` with rationale).
- Disallow `console.*` except `console.error` inside `lib/error-logging.ts` usage or in tests.
- Add `jsx-a11y` rules for headings, interactive controls, alt text, and focus management.
- Ban direct DOM mutations in React code (`document.querySelector`, `innerHTML`) except in vetted utilities.
- Disallow `fetch` in client components; prefer server functions/route handlers.
- Enforce use of `next/link` for internal navigation with descriptive text.
- Prefer `metadata` exports in `app/[lang]/**/page.tsx`.
- Integrate forbidden patterns from `docs/FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS.md`.

## Implementation Details
- Update `eslint.config.mjs`:
  - Add `plugin:jsx-a11y/recommended`.
  - Add custom rule sets:
    - `no-restricted-globals` for `document`, `window` in components.
    - `no-restricted-syntax` banning `any` and `as any` casts.
    - `no-console` with allow list.
    - `@next/next/no-html-link-for-pages` and `@next/next/no-img-element` (force `next/image` where appropriate).
    - `@typescript-eslint/no-misused-promises` for event handlers.
  - Use overrides for `app/api/**` and `scripts/**` where needed.
- Add ESLint comments examples to `docs/AI_GUARDRAILS.md` for justified exceptions.

### Feature Category

DevEx

### Priority (Your Assessment)

Medium

### Additional Context

- `pnpm lint` fails on violations introduced by the above rules.
- Overrides avoid false positives in route handlers and scripts.

Enhance `eslint.config.mjs` to enforce AI guardrails: stricter TypeScript, accessibility/a11y, banned APIs/patterns, and Next.js best practices.

### Alternatives Considered

## Requirements
- Enforce `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` (use `import type`).
- Disallow `any` (except explicitly justified via `// eslint-disable-next-line` with rationale).
- Disallow `console.*` except `console.error` inside `lib/error-logging.ts` usage or in tests.
- Add `jsx-a11y` rules for headings, interactive controls, alt text, and focus management.
- Ban direct DOM mutations in React code (`document.querySelector`, `innerHTML`) except in vetted utilities.
- Disallow `fetch` in client components; prefer server functions/route handlers.
- Enforce use of `next/link` for internal navigation with descriptive text.
- Prefer `metadata` exports in `app/[lang]/**/page.tsx`.
- Integrate forbidden patterns from `docs/FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS.md`.

## Implementation Details
- Update `eslint.config.mjs`:
  - Add `plugin:jsx-a11y/recommended`.
  - Add custom rule sets:
    - `no-restricted-globals` for `document`, `window` in components.
    - `no-restricted-syntax` banning `any` and `as any` casts.
    - `no-console` with allow list.
    - `@next/next/no-html-link-for-pages` and `@next/next/no-img-element` (force `next/image` where appropriate).
    - `@typescript-eslint/no-misused-promises` for event handlers.
  - Use overrides for `app/api/**` and `scripts/**` where needed.
- Add ESLint comments examples to `docs/AI_GUARDRAILS.md` for justified exceptions.

closing_issues.title: [Feature]: Add AI Guardrails Spec
closing_issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Without automated CI gates:
- AI-generated changes may lack tests or only pass lint by accident.
- Architectural decisions can be merged without documented rationale.
- Reviewers lack a machine-enforced checklist (a11y, SEO, error handling).
- Regressions slip through because visual/e2e/unit tests are not mandatory.
- There's no way to distinguish "AI-generated" changes for stricter review.

CI automation reduces reviewer burden and ensures every change meets standards consistently.

### Proposed Solution

## Summary
Add GitHub Actions workflows to gate AI-authored changes: require tests, guardrails adherence, rationale/ADR for architecture changes, and PR template confirmations.

### Alternatives Considered

## Requirements
- On PR:
  - Run `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:e2e`, and `pnpm test:visual` (with masks and shared utils).
  - Fail if files under `app/` or `lib/` change without accompanying tests in `test/unit/` or `test/e2e/` or `test/visual/`.
  - Require PR template checkboxes: a11y, SEO, error handling, security.
  - If label `architecture-change` present, require link to ADR in `docs/adr/`.
- Provide minimal caching (pnpm, Playwright) for speed.

## Implementation Details
- Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
  - Jobs: `lint`, `typecheck`, `unit`, `e2e`, `visual`.
  - Conditional gates: use `paths` filters and a script step to verify changed paths have tests (custom Node script in `scripts/check-pr-tests.mjs`).
  - Upload Playwright artifacts on failure.
- Update `.github/pull_request_template.md` with checkboxes and ADR link field.

### Feature Category

DevEx

### Priority (Your Assessment)

Medium - Would improve experience

### Additional Context

## Acceptance Criteria
- CI blocks merges that violate guardrails or missing tests.
- Visual tests run using masking utilities in `test/visual/utils.ts`.
- PR template renders with required confirmations.

closing_issues.title: [Feature]:  Forbidden APIs and Patterns
closing_issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

## Problem
Without explicit forbidden-list:
- AI may inadvertently bypass Turnstile, rate-limiting, or honeypot checks.
- Secrets/tokens can be hard-coded instead of using env variables.
- AI might use unsafe DOM APIs or sanitization methods not aligned with `lib/sanitize-html.ts`.
- Developers don't have a quick reference for "what not to do."

A clear "forbidden" list with alternatives is easier to scan, link in code review, and reference in lint rules.

### Proposed Solution

## Summary
Create `docs/FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS.md` enumerating APIs and patterns that AI must not use and enforce via ESLint where possible.

### Alternatives Considered

## Requirements
- List forbidden items with rationale and alternatives.
- Cross-link to ESLint rules and code examples.
- Include security-critical bans (e.g., Turnstile bypass, secrets in code).

## Implementation Details
- Add `docs/FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS.md` with entries:
  - Bypass Turnstile or `rate-limit.ts` in `/api/contact`.
  - Hard-coded secrets/API keys/tokens; use env and Next config.
  - Direct DOM mutation in components; use React state/refs.
  - Inline styles that break theme variables; use Tailwind and design tokens.
  - `any` types and unchecked `as any` casts.
  - Fetch in client components; use server functions/route handlers.
  - Custom sanitization bypassing `lib/sanitize-html.ts`.
  - Disabling a11y/SEO metadata.
- Reference enforcement via `eslint.config.mjs` changes.

### Feature Category

DevEx

### Priority (Your Assessment)

Medium

### Additional Context

- `docs/FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS.md` merged and linked in guardrails doc.
- Lint rules mapped to listed forbidden patterns.

closing_issues.title: [Feature]: Test Coverage Thresholds
closing_issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

## Problem
Without coverage thresholds:
- AI-generated code can have high pass rates but low actual test coverage.
- Regressions appear only in production or late in the user journey (e.g., masked carousel or dynamic content in visual tests).
- No automatic feedback that a feature lacks e2e/visual validation.
- Coverage reports are generated but not enforced, making them optional.

Coverage gates ensure every change is actually tested, not just syntactically correct.

### Proposed Solution

## Summary
Configure coverage gates for Vitest and ensure E2E and visual tests run with minimum coverage thresholds to enforce high-quality AI changes.

### Alternatives Considered

## Requirements
- Add Vitest coverage config (lines, branches, functions) in `vitest.config.ts`.
- Enforce minimum thresholds (e.g., 80% lines for touched packages/modules).
- Ensure `pnpm test:e2e` and `pnpm test:visual` are part of CI gates.
- Provide guidance for adding unit/e2e/visual tests when changing UI/logic.

## Implementation Details
- Update `vitest.config.ts` to enable coverage via `c8` with sensible defaults.
- Add documentation to `docs/TESTING.md` for coverage expectations and examples of writing tests using shared utilities.
- Ensure CI workflow reads thresholds and fails when not met.

### Feature Category

Developer Experience

Medium - Would improve experience

### Additional Context

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pnpm test` emits coverage reports and fails under thresholds.
- CI integrates unit/e2e/visual runs and enforces gates.

closing_issues.title: [Feature]: Runtime Guardrails
closing_issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

## Problem
Silent failures in production are hard to debug:
- Empty catch blocks swallow errors and make debugging harder.
- Unreachable code paths don't get caught until edge cases hit production.
- Without structured logging, errors are scattered and hard to aggregate.
- AI-generated code may omit error handling or logging, assuming things "just work."

Runtime assertions and centralized logging catch bugs early and provide clear error messages for debugging.

### Proposed Solution

## Summary
Introduce runtime assertions and logging wrappers to prevent silent failures and enforce expected invariants.

### Alternatives Considered

## Requirements
- Add `lib/assertions.ts` with `assertNever(value: never): never` and `invariant(condition: boolean, message: string)`.
- Encourage use via docs and lint suggestions (e.g., ban empty catch blocks; require logging).
- Ensure errors use `logError()` and error boundaries where appropriate.

## Implementation Details
- Create `lib/assertions.ts` with minimal helpers and TypeScript-friendly signatures.
- Update docs in `docs/ERROR_HANDLING.md` and `docs/AI_GUARDRAILS.md` to mandate using these assertions for unreachable states and critical invariants.
- Consider adding an ESLint rule or custom lint check to flag empty catch blocks and missing `logError()`.

### Feature Category

Developer Experience

### Priority (Your Assessment)

Low - Nice to have

### Mockups or Examples

_No response_

### Additional Context

## Acceptance Criteria
- File exists with exported helpers and is used in at least one component or utility as reference.
- Documentation updated and linked.
- Lint rules or guidance reduce silent failures.

closing_issues.title: [Docs]: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
closing_issues.body:
### Documentation Type

ADR

### Issue Description

## Problem
Without ADRs:
- Architectural decisions made by AI (or humans) lack context for future maintainers.
- Reviewers can't easily understand the reasoning behind choices, only the implementation.
- Technical debt accumulates without a record of tradeoffs or alternatives considered.
- New contributors (or future AI agents) may undo good decisions because the rationale is lost.

ADRs provide lightweight, searchable documentation that pairs decisions with consequences and alternatives.

### Location

## Summary
Introduce ADRs (`docs/adr/`) and a lightweight template to capture non-trivial decisions, especially for AI-authored changes.


### Suggested Improvement

## Requirements
- Create `docs/adr/` directory and `ADR-template.md`.
- Add guidance in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and PR template to link ADRs when making architecture-impacting changes.
- Encourage small, focused ADRs with context, decision, consequences, and alternatives.

## Implementation Details
- Add `docs/adr/ADR-template.md` with fields: Context, Decision, Status, Consequences, Alternatives, References.
- Update `.github/pull_request_template.md` with an ADR link section.
- Link ADR process from `docs/TECHNICAL_GOVERNANCE.md`.

### Severity

Medium - Missing information or unclear section

### Additional Context

## Acceptance Criteria
- ADR template in place and referenced by PR template.
- At least one sample ADR added for a recent architectural area (optional).

closing_issues.title: [Feature]: Secure Secrets Handling
closing_issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

## Problem
Secrets accidentally committed to code are:
- Hard to fully revoke (repos are often forked, cloned, and pushed to public mirrors).
- Easy for AI to introduce if not explicitly warned (hard-coded API keys, tokens, webhook URLs).
- Difficult to catch in manual review if they're long hex strings or look like normal data.
- Risky if the repo is ever made public or leaked.

Automated scanning + clear guidance prevents accidental exposure and reduces human error.

### Proposed Solution

## Summary
Prevent AI from introducing secrets into code and enforce proper environment variable usage and security practices.

### Alternatives Considered

## Requirements
- Document secrets handling in `docs/SECURITY_POLICY.md` (or link existing) and add a short guide in README.
- Add CI scan to detect committed secrets (e.g., simple regex scan) and fail PRs.
- Ensure `vercel.json` and Next.js config encourage env-based configuration.
- Forbid hard-coded tokens via ESLint rules.

## Implementation Details
- Add a lightweight Node script `scripts/scan-secrets.mjs` scanning changed files for patterns: `API_KEY`, `Bearer `, `sk-`, `ghp_`, long hex secrets, etc.
- Integrate scan into CI `ci.yml`.
- Add ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` to flag string literals matching secret-like patterns.
- Update docs to show correct `.env` usage and deployment guidance.

### Feature Category

Developer Experience

mentioned_issues.title: [Feature]: Secure Secrets Handling
mentioned_issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

## Problem
Secrets accidentally committed to code are:
- Hard to fully revoke (repos are often forked, cloned, and pushed to public mirrors).
- Easy for AI to introduce if not explicitly warned (hard-coded API keys, tokens, webhook URLs).
- Difficult to catch in manual review if they're long hex strings or look like normal data.
- Risky if the repo is ever made public or leaked.

Automated scanning + clear guidance prevents accidental exposure and reduces human error.

### Proposed Solution

## Summary
Prevent AI from introducing secrets into code and enforce proper environment variable usage and security practices.

### Alternatives Considered

## Requirements
- Document secrets handling in `docs/SECURITY_POLICY.md` (or link existing) and add a short guide in README.
- Add CI scan to detect committed secrets (e.g., simple regex scan) and fail PRs.
- Ensure `vercel.json` and Next.js config encourage env-based configuration.
- Forbid hard-coded tokens via ESLint rules.

## Implementation Details
- Add a lightweight Node script `scripts/scan-secrets.mjs` scanning changed files for patterns: `API_KEY`, `Bearer `, `sk-`, `ghp_`, long hex secrets, etc.
- Integrate scan into CI `ci.yml`.
- Add ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` to flag string literals matching secret-like patterns.
- Update docs to show correct `.env` usage and deployment guidance.

Developer Experience

Medium - Would improve experience

mentioned_issues.title: feat: T1 — "Why This Matters" intention field for tasks
mentioned_issues.body:
## Summary

Add an optional `intention` text field to tasks. When creating a task, a subtle prompt asks: "Why does this matter to you?" This connects tasks to personal meaning and increases follow-through.
